- SISTEMA: {{SISTEMA}} > System to diagram: name, purpose, and limits (what is in scope and what is out)
- NIVEL: {{NIVEL}} > Target C4 level: context (C1), containers (C2), components (C3), or several chained
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Primary audience: executive, product, technical team, audit/security
- ELEMENTOS: {{ELEMENTOS}} > Known systems, services, data stores, users, and externals ("(optional)" if the AI should infer them)
- NOTACION: {{NOTACION}} > Output: Mermaid, PlantUML (C4-PlantUML), or both (optional; default Mermaid)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The architecture of {{SISTEMA}} typically lives scattered across the team's heads, repos, and wikis, hiding dependencies, trust boundaries, and single points of failure. A clear diagram at the right C4 level replaces dozens of explanation threads: it aligns {{AUDIENCIA}}, accelerates onboarding and reviews, and leaves a versionable source of truth.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Solutions Architect expert in C4 Model (Simon Brown), UML, and system visualization for technical and business audiences.
Deliver an architecture diagram of {{SISTEMA}} at level {{NIVEL}} plus its reading. Steps:
1. Set the scope: which system is modeled, what falls inside and outside the boundary.
2. Declare {{ELEMENTOS}}: persons, systems, containers/services, and data stores; infer what is reasonable and flag [SUPUESTO].
3. Model directed relationships with verb, protocol, and direction of data flow (synchronous/asynchronous).
4. Mark trust boundaries, deployment limits, and single points of failure.
5. Add a legend that explains each shape, color, and relationship type.
6. Generate the code in {{NOTACION}} renderable without editing, plus a simplified version for a non-technical audience.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpretation: set purpose, boundary, and appropriate C4 level for {{AUDIENCIA}}; flag missing data.
Phase 2 – Inventory: list actors, systems, containers, and stores from {{ELEMENTOS}}.
Phase 3 – Relationships: connect with verb + protocol + direction; detect dependencies and failure points.
Phase 4 – Encoding: translate to {{NOTACION}} validating syntax and add legend.
Phase 5 – Dual version and close: emit the technical and the simplified version; list assumptions [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The C4 level is appropriate for {{AUDIENCIA}}; abstractions are not mixed (e.g. classes inside a C1).
- [ ] All {{ELEMENTOS}} appear; nothing is left disconnected without a relationship or purpose.
- [ ] Each relationship has verb, protocol, and direction; no ambiguous arrows.
- [ ] Trust boundaries and single points of failure are marked.
- [ ] The legend explains all notation used (shapes, colors, line types).
- [ ] The code in {{NOTACION}} renders without editing and a simplified non-technical version exists.
- [ ] Assumptions about inferred elements are flagged [SUPUESTO].
Deliverable: renderable {{NOTACION}} code block(s) + legend + simplified executive version + list of assumptions.
spec-u_visual_brand_kit_personal:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE: {{NOMBRE}} > Your name or personal brand
- VALORES: {{VALORES}} > 3 values or attributes the brand must project (e.g. "approachability, rigor, innovation")
- CANALES: {{CANALES}} > Channels with presence where the kit will be applied (e.g. "LinkedIn, presentations, newsletter") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a coherent personal brand visual kit that makes me recognizable across {{CANALES}} and that any designer can reproduce without ambiguity. My personal brand is my visual reputation: consistency, not the volume of assets, is what builds recognition. I want to project the values {{VALORES}} uniformly and accessibly.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior Brand Designer with experience in visual identity for entrepreneurs, speakers, and independent professionals.

Deliverable: documented personal brand kit with these 8 components:
1. Visual brand concept: guiding idea in one sentence and its connection to {{VALORES}}.
2. Logo or brand mark: concept, variants (primary, secondary, logomark, monochrome), protection zone and minimum size.
3. Color palette: max 5 colors (primary, secondary, neutral) with hex code and when to use each; text/background contrast WCAG AA (4.5:1).
4. Typography: 2 fonts with hierarchy (headings, body, support), reference sizes and web-safe alternatives.
5. Photographic style: what images to use, treatment (color, framing, mood) and what to avoid, with 2–3 reference descriptions.
6. Templates: minimum 3 channels from {{CANALES}} with dimensions, margins, and logo placement.
7. Do and Don't rules that prevent common application errors.
8. Summary tokens: compact table with hex codes, fonts, and sizes to copy.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Interpretation: validate NAME, VALORES, CANALES, and ADJUNTOS; if VALORES is vague, define it with questions; do not invent identity or preferences.
Phase 2 · Concept: derive the guiding idea from the 3 values before touching color or form.
Phase 3 · Visual system: define logo, palette (verifying contrast), typography, and photographic style as a coherent system, not isolated pieces.
Phase 4 · Application: produce channel templates and the tokens table; close with Do/Don't rules.
Principles: consistency over creativity; less is more (2 core colors + 2 fonts); cross-platform; document everything; accessible by default. Flag assumptions with [assumption: ...]. No prices or promises of results.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The palette has max 5 colors, each with a hex code and usage rule.
- Text/background combinations meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1).
- The 2 fonts have clear hierarchy and a web-safe alternative.
- The logo declares variants, protection zone, and minimum size.
- Templates cover at least 3 channels with concrete dimensions.
- Do/Don't rules prevent common application errors.
- Every decision connects to one of the 3 values; assumptions are flagged.
Tone: creative-professional. Audience: yourself + any collaborating designer.
Expected deliverable: complete personal brand kit (concept, logo, palette, typography, photography, templates, Do/Don't, tokens) ready to apply across all channels.
spec-u_visual_storyboard_campana:

--- S | SITUATION ---

For visually planning a content or marketing campaign before producing. The storyboard is the visual script: it organizes the big idea, the pieces, and the calendar so that no asset is produced without purpose and the narrative between channels doesn't break.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Creative Director with experience in multimedia campaign planning for consumer and B2B brands.

Campaign storyboard:
1. Creative concept: the big idea in 1 sentence (feeling or action it triggers).
2. Audience and promise: who it speaks to and what changes for that person.
3. Pieces by channel: content to produce in the native format of each channel.
4. Storyboard per piece: hook/visual + copy + CTA + mood, in order.
5. Publication calendar: which piece, when, where, with narrative tension (opening, development, close).
6. Consistency: connective thread (message, palette, tone, visual element) that unites everything into one story.
7. Measurement plan: 1–2 metrics per piece + campaign north metric.
8. Assumptions and limits: budget, team, brand maturity assumed; what is out of scope.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Big idea first: one idea, multiple executions; not many scattered ideas.
- Channel-native: adapt to the format of each channel, do not copy the same piece.
- Narrative calendar: consistency requires a calendar with an arc (opening > development > close).
- Measure what matters: engagement and conversion over raw reach.
- If a critical asset is missing (logo, brand guide, fixed date), flag it as a blocker instead of inventing it.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: storyboard + calendar + measurement plan + assumptions.
Tone: creative-strategic.
Audience: marketing/content team.
Action: close by recommending which piece to produce first and why it is the best validation point.

[checklist]
- [ ] The creative concept fits in 1 sentence and names the desired feeling or action
- [ ] Each piece is in the native format of its channel, not copied across channels
- [ ] Each storyboard piece has hook/visual + copy + CTA
- [ ] The calendar has dates, channels, and a narrative arc (opening/development/close)
- [ ] There are 1–2 metrics per piece and one campaign north metric
- [ ] Assumptions, limits, and blockers are explicit
- [ ] The first piece to produce is recommended with justification

The thumbnail is the visual pitch: you have ~0.5s to win the click against everything surrounding the content in the feed. Goal: sustained high CTR, without clickbait that breaks trust or retention.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: YouTube Creative Strategist with a track record of high-CTR thumbnails (>10%) on educational and business channels.

- Contrast against the feed > internal harmony of the thumbnail

- [ ] Contrast was evaluated against the platform's feed, not in isolation

spec-u_visual_data_viz_interactiva:
[inputs]
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} > Dataset to visualize: source, size, key columns, temporal granularity
- HISTORIA: {{HISTORIA}} > Central insight the view must reveal upon arrival (one sentence)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > (optional) Who explores: executive, analyst, general public
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > (optional) D3, Plotly, Observable, Tableau; default based on fit
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

Design an interactive data visualization where the viewer becomes an analyst: they explore, filter, and discover insights on their own. Interactivity is only justified if it reduces the cognitive cost of reaching the answer; otherwise, a static chart is superior.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Data Visualization Engineer with experience in D3.js, Plotly, and Observable for data-driven products, fluent in grammar of graphics and visual perception.

Deliver an interactive visualization spec:
1. Data-story fit: why this dataset supports this insight; biases or gaps in the data.
2. Encoding map: variable > visual channel (position, length, color, area) justified by perceptual accuracy.
3. Default view: what the user sees upon arrival; must tell the story without any interaction.
4. Interaction layers: filter, zoom, hover, drill-down; each with the insight it enables.
5. States: loading, empty, error, partial data, no results after filtering.
6. Responsive: graceful degradation from desktop to mobile; which interactions are simplified or removed.
7. Accessibility: contrast, keyboard navigation, textual alternative for the insight.
8. Technical spec: tool, data format, performance budget, maximum volume.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand (Shneiderman).
- Default view = the story: the initial view conveys the narrative without user action.
- Purposeful interaction: each control answers a specific question; if not, it is removed.
- Data honesty: no misleading axis truncation, declared aggregations, visible uncertainty.
- Performance budget: < 2 s to useful interaction; define the volume limit and the strategy (sampling, aggregation, virtualization) when exceeded.

Assumptions and limits:
- If the dataset or story is missing, ask for the minimum piece before designing; do not invent data.
- Declare a single tool and justify ruling out the others in one line.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: interactive spec + textual wireframes per breakpoint (desktop, mobile).
Tone: technical-creative, precise.
Audience: developer or designer who will implement.
Action: implement the prototype from the spec without context questions.

[checklist]
- [ ] The default view tells the main story without prior interaction
- [ ] Each interaction answers a question and adds value, not decoration
- [ ] Loading, empty, error, and no-results states are defined
- [ ] Encoding is justified by perceptual accuracy and honest with the data
- [ ] Responsive and accessible: keyboard, contrast, and textual alternative
- [ ] Spec is implementable with the chosen tool within the performance budget

--- S | SITUATION ---

I need visual educational content that teaches a complex concept in a simple and memorable way. The dual channel (text + visual) accelerates learning and improves retention compared to text alone.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Visual Instructional Designer with experience in educational content for universities and corporate programs.

Design the visual educational set for {{TEMA}} targeting {{AUDIENCIA}}:
1. Decomposition: 3–5 atomic key ideas, each teachable independently.
2. Optimal format per idea, justified: diagram, visual analogy, step-by-step process, comparison, or timeline. Include a textual description of each piece ready to execute in an image tool or by a designer (elements, on-screen text, spatial relationship).
3. Pedagogical progression: from simple to complex; each piece scaffolds on the previous one.
4. Assessment: 1 quiz-type or exercise piece that validates comprehension of the key ideas.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

- Dual coding: text + visual to reinforce memory.
- Chunking: maximum 5 ideas per piece.
- Progressive disclosure: reveal complexity gradually.
- Visual metaphor: anchor the abstract in the concrete and everyday.

Assumptions and limits: if TEMA, AUDIENCIA, or ADJUNTOS are missing, request them before executing. Do not invent source data; flag as assumption any figure not supported by {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver image descriptions, not graphic files.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: set of 3–5 visual pieces (with executable description) + 1 assessment piece + usage guide for 3 contexts.
Tone: pedagogical-visual, neutral professional English, no emojis.
Deliverable: usable in the next educational session without rework.

- [ ] The progression goes from simple to complex with explicit scaffolding
- [ ] Visual metaphors are clear, concrete, and memorable
- [ ] Each piece includes an executable description (elements + on-screen text)
- [ ] The assessment validates the declared key ideas
- [ ] The guide covers class, self-study, and social media
- [ ] Assumptions and unverified data are flagged

--- S | SITUATION ---

Low-fidelity wireframes that communicate structure, flow, and interaction without ambiguity are required. The wireframe is the digital architect's blueprint: it defines what goes where and how navigation works, before any visual decision is made. It reduces rework in design and development by locking the skeleton and states early.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior UX Designer with experience in low-fidelity wireframing for web, mobile, and SaaS (Figma, Balsamiq).

Wireframe Spec:
1. Screen inventory: purpose and entry trigger for each screen.
2. Layout per screen: zones, components, and visual hierarchy; no color or typography.
3. User flow: end-to-end navigation without dead ends; happy path + alternative branches.
4. Interactions: per actionable element, what happens on click/tap, where it leads, and what it validates.
5. States per component: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, success.
6. Responsive: desktop-to-mobile reflow, navigation collapse, content priority, assumed breakpoints.
7. Developer annotations: implementable, unambiguous.

Method:
- Structure before aesthetics: wireframe = skeleton, not visual design.
- Flow first: flow drives screens, not the other way around.
- State coverage: every component in all its states, not just the happy path.
- Actionable handoff: every annotation must be implementable exactly as written.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: descriptive wireframes per screen + flow + states + annotations.
Tone: technical-precise. Audience: UI designer or developer. Action: implement in Figma or code.

- [ ] Assumptions and boundaries declared; pending items marked

- TAREAS: {{TAREAS}} > Types of tasks you do with AI (creation, analysis, search, code, visual)
- MODELOS: {{MODELOS}} > AI models or tools you have access to
- PRESUPUESTO: {{PRESUPUESTO}} > (optional) Usage constraint or monthly budget; leave blank if not applicable
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

Using a single model for everything wastes each AI's strengths and degrades results. The goal is a workflow that routes each task to the right model (creativity, analysis, live search, code, deep reasoning) and connects the steps without losing context.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: AI Workflow Architect with experience in multi-model orchestration and LLM selection for specific tasks.

Design the multi-model workflow:
1. Inventory of {{TAREAS}} classified by type (creation, analysis, live search, code, deep reasoning, visual or documents).
2. Strengths matrix for {{MODELOS}}: for each one (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, or other available) its dominant strength and its weak point.
3. Optimal model assignment per task type, with one justification line per row.
4. Handoffs: how the output of one model passes to the next (expected format, what to clean up or reformat, receiver's input prompt).
5. Selection by intensity considering {{PRESUPUESTO}}: when a lightweight model is sufficient and when a higher-capacity one is justified. Without citing amounts.
6. Diagrammed workflow: which model at which point and the human verification checkpoint.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan. If TAREAS or MODELOS are missing, ask for them before designing.

Method:
- Right model for right job: the correct model per task, not one default for everything.
- Specialist beats generalist: leverage each model's strength.
- Usage-aware: reserve higher-capacity models for tasks that justify it.
- Pipeline: the output of one step is the clean input of the next.
- Explicit assumptions when data is missing; declare design limits.
- Edge case: define the plan if a model is unavailable or delivers low quality (fallback and reassignment).

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: diagrammed workflow + model-task matrix + handoff guide.
Tone: technical-strategic. Audience: professional who uses multiple AIs. Action: implement this week.

Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Every model-task assignment has a one-line justification
- [ ] Every handoff defines output format, cleanup, and receiver's prompt
- [ ] Intensity-based selection is resolved without citing amounts
- [ ] The edge case of an unavailable model or low-quality output is covered
- [ ] Assumptions and limits are declared
- [ ] The workflow is executable with current tools this week
spec-u_agentes_quality_rubric_outputs:
[inputs]
- TIPO_OUTPUT: {{TIPO_OUTPUT}} > Type of output to evaluate (text, analysis, presentation, code, etc.)
- ESTANDAR: {{ESTANDAR}} > Required quality level (professional, executive, publication)
- DIMENSIONES_CRITICAS: {{DIMENSIONES_CRITICAS}} > Dimensions with veto power, or "Define for me" to let the model propose
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To create a quality rubric that evaluates AI outputs consistently, objectively, and in an auditable way. Without a rubric, "looks good" is an opinion; with a rubric, it is a repeatable measurement across evaluators and over time. The risk to mitigate is drift: the same output receiving different scores depending on who or when it is evaluated.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Content QA Specialist with experience designing evaluation rubrics for LLM outputs and editorial content.

Quality rubric, adjusted for TIPO_OUTPUT and ESTANDAR:
1. Quality dimensions: accuracy, completeness, clarity, format, tone, actionability. Each operationalized with an observable descriptor (what to look at when scoring), not a vague adjective.
2. 1–10 scale per dimension with descriptors anchored at least at levels 2, 5, 8, and 10.
3. Weight per dimension summing to 100%, with explicit justification for why accuracy weighs more than format for this TIPO_OUTPUT.
4. Minimum acceptable score (approval threshold) + veto rule: if a DIMENSIONES_CRITICAS falls below its floor, it is rejected even if the weighted average passes.
5. Examples of the same case evaluated 10/10, 5/10, and 2/10, with the reason for each score per dimension.
6. Step-by-step evaluation protocol applicable in under 2 minutes per output.

Declare assumptions about: what counts as a "complete" output, how to handle non-applicable dimensions (e.g., actionability in an informational summary is excluded and weights are renormalized), and how to resolve ties at the threshold. Flag each assumption.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Measurable criteria: each dimension with an observable descriptor verifiable by a third party.
- Weighted scoring: justified weights; accuracy above format unless ESTANDAR inverts it.
- Critical veto: critical dimensions can sink an output with a good average.
- Calibration: apply the rubric to 3 reference outputs (high, medium, low) to fix anchors before real use.
- Speed: if evaluation takes more than 2 minutes, simplify dimensions or descriptors.
- Anti-drift: record scores to compare evaluations and detect inconsistency across evaluators.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: complete rubric (dimension-weight-descriptor table) + examples by level + protocol + declared assumptions.
Tone: technical.
Audience: professional who evaluates AI outputs regularly.
Action: evaluate the next 5 outputs with this rubric and record the scores.

Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Each dimension has an observable descriptor (not subjective)
- [ ] The scale is anchored at least at levels 2, 5, 8, and 10
- [ ] Weights sum to 100% and are justified for the TIPO_OUTPUT
- [ ] The threshold and critical veto rule are defined
- [ ] There are 10/5/2 examples for the same case with reason per score
- [ ] The protocol fits within 2 minutes
- [ ] Assumptions, non-applicable dimensions, and ties are resolved and flagged

Deliverable: rubric ready to use plus three sample calibrations and the anti-drift recording guide.
spec-u_stack_auditar_herramientas_person:
[inputs]
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > List of tools you use (name and, if possible, what you use it for)
- PRESUPUESTO: {{PRESUPUESTO}} > (optional) Current recurring spend on tools
- FRECUENCIA_USO: {{FRECUENCIA_USO}} > (optional) Actual frequency or context of use per tool
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To audit your tools stack and eliminate redundancies. The average professional pays for 8 tools and uses 3; the other 5 are silent waste that drains recurring spend, attention, and context-switching time.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Digital Productivity Consultant with experience in stack optimization for remote teams and independent professionals.

Stack Audit:
1. Full inventory: tool, function category, recurring cost, actual usage frequency, unique value provided.
2. Classification: essential / useful / redundant / abandoned, with the explicit criterion that places it there.
3. Overlap map: which tools cover the same function and which one wins.
4. Optimal stack: consolidate to the minimum viable; one solid tool per function over several mediocre ones.
5. Migration plan: export data, retrain habits, deactivate what is removed without losing information.
6. Estimated savings: recurring spend freed up + management hours and context-switching time recovered.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan. If inventory, spend, or actual frequency are missing, ask for them; do not assume.

Method:
- Inventory first: you cannot optimize what you do not know.
- Usage audit: actual frequency, not perceived.
- Consolidation: 1 good tool > 3 mediocre ones.
- Total cost: license + learning curve + maintenance.
- Trade-off: weigh switching cost and lock-in before recommending migration; if the risk exceeds the savings, keep it and record the assumption.

Assumptions and limits: work only with the declared tools; mark as {to_confirm} any cost or frequency you do not receive. Edge cases: unique tool with no overlap (keep), expensive tool used infrequently but critical (review plan, do not eliminate), duplicate for team vs individual (decide by function owner).

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: inventory + classification + overlap map + optimal stack + migration plan + savings.
Tone: analytical. Audience: professional or team.
Closing action: name the first redundant tool to deactivate this week and the data point that triggers the decision.

[checklist]
- [ ] All tools are inventoried with cost and frequency (or {to_confirm})
- [ ] Each tool has a classification with an explicit criterion
- [ ] Overlaps are identified with the winning tool
- [ ] The optimal stack is at least 30% smaller or justifies why not
- [ ] Each migration considers switching cost and lock-in
- [ ] Savings are quantified in recurring spend and hours
spec-u_stack_seleccionar_herramienta:
[inputs]
- NECESIDAD: {{NECESIDAD}} > What underlying problem the tool solves (the problem, not the assumed solution)
- CANDIDATAS: {{CANDIDATAS}} > Tools to compare (ideally 3–5)
- STACK_ACTUAL: {{STACK_ACTUAL}} > (optional) Tools/platforms it must integrate with
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > (optional) Hard limits: relative budget, deadline, team, compliance, on-premise
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To evaluate and select the right tool when multiple options exist. The tool decision is not technical, it is strategic: the real cost is not adopting it but changing it later. A rushed choice creates lock-in, rework, and debt. This prompt converts intuition into a traceable and reversible decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Technology Evaluator with experience selecting tools for teams and organizations.

Tool evaluation:
1. Requirements: must-haves (they disqualify if absent) vs nice-to-haves. Maximum 10, specific and verifiable, never generic.
2. Candidates: 3–5 real options. Fewer than 3 -> propose alternatives for contrast. More than 5 -> discard weak ones with explicit criteria.
3. Weighted criteria: functionality, usability, integrations with STACK_ACTUAL, support and community, scalability, maturity and discontinuation risk, total cost of ownership (learning, migration, switching cost, lock-in). Weights summing to 100, each justified.
4. Scoring: comparative table with a 1–5 score per criterion × weight. Unmet must-have = automatic disqualification, not a low score.
5. Trial plan: how to test the top 2 under real conditions (not just a demo) in one week, with concrete tasks and a measurable success criterion.
6. Decision: recommendation + 2–3 risks + signals that would require reconsideration + exit plan if it fails.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the underlying need, declare assumptions, and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Requirements-first: know what you need before comparing.
- Weighted scoring: not all criteria weigh the same; the weight is justified.
- Trial > demo: use the tool on a real task, not just watch it.
- Total cost: reason about switching cost, learning, and lock-in in relative terms, never with specific prices.
- Reversibility: prefer options with lower exit cost under uncertainty.

Assumptions and limits: if NECESIDAD, CANDIDATAS, or STACK_ACTUAL are missing, mark as an explicit assumption or ask before closing the recommendation. Do not issue a verdict with unverified must-haves.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: comparative table + weighted scoring + recommendation. Tone: analytical-pragmatic. Audience: decision-maker. Action: start the winner's trial.

[checklist]
- [ ] Requirements are specific and verifiable, separated into must-haves vs nice-to-haves
- [ ] Criterion weights sum to 100 and are justified
- [ ] Table with weighted scoring and unmet must-have marked as disqualification
- [ ] Trial plan executable in 1 week with a measurable success criterion
- [ ] Decision includes risks, reconsideration signals, and exit plan
- [ ] Explicit assumptions for each missing data point; no specific prices
spec-u_stack_integraciones_mapa:
[inputs]
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > Tools in your stack (name and, if known, plan or edition)
- FLUJOS: {{FLUJOS}} > Main workflows and, if possible, their frequency and who operates them
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To map how your tools connect with each other, detect the integration gaps causing repetitive manual work, and prioritize where to invest automation effort for the greatest return.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Integration Architect with experience designing connected tool ecosystems for operations teams.

Integration map:
1. Data flow diagram: origin, destination, and direction between tools.
2. Active integrations: what is connected and by what mechanism (native, API, middleware, manual).
3. Gaps: every copy/paste or data re-entry is a gap; estimate frequency and hours lost.
4. Opportunities: available native integrations not yet configured.
5. Viable automations: orchestrators such as Zapier, Make, or n8n, with trigger and action.
6. Prioritized implementation plan by ROI (hours saved / hours of configuration).

Assumptions and limits: flag each assumption; if the volume of a workflow is missing, estimate in a range and declare it. Note risks per integration: API limits, recurring costs, vendor dependency, single points of failure.

Edge cases: tools without a public API (propose scheduled export or RPA), integrations requiring a higher plan tier (flag the edition upgrade), workflows with sensitive data that should not leave a system (exclude or recommend direct encrypted connection).

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan. If HERRAMIENTAS or FLUJOS are incomplete or ambiguous, ask for them before proceeding.

Method:
- Data flow mapping: trace where each piece of data originates and where it ends up, end to end.
- Gap = manual transfer: quantify every re-entry by frequency and hours.
- Native > third-party: prefer native integrations when functional parity exists.
- ROI per integration: hours saved over hours of configuration; break ties by risk and reversibility.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: integration diagram + inventory + quantified gaps + prioritized plan.
Tone: practical-technical. Audience: operations team or professional.
Closing action: leave the highest-ROI integration ready to configure, with its trigger, its action, and a measurable success criterion.

[checklist]
- [ ] The diagram covers all tools and shows data direction
- [ ] Active integrations indicate their mechanism (native, API, middleware, manual)
- [ ] Each gap is quantified by frequency and hours lost
- [ ] Native opportunities and automations include a trigger and action
- [ ] The plan is prioritized by ROI and names risks per integration
- [ ] The highest-ROI integration is ready with a measurable success criterion
- [ ] Assumptions and missing data are explicitly declared
spec-u_automatizacion_ritual_productivo_:
[inputs]
- RITUAL: {{RITUAL}} > Ritual or productive routine to automate (name, frequency, and expected outcome)
- FRICCIONES: {{FRICCIONES}} > Highest friction, delay, or abandonment points in the ritual
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To convert a manual productive ritual into a semi-automated flow that reduces friction, sustains consistency, and keeps the human as the decision-maker.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Automated Ritual Designer with expertise in behavioural design and personal automation.

Semi-automated ritual:
1. Map the current ritual: steps, estimated time per step, and friction points
2. Classify each step: automatable / assistable / human-required (with justification)
3. Design a concrete trigger per automatable step (event, schedule, condition) and name the tool or mechanism
4. Define a fallback per automation: if it fails, the ritual continues manually without breaking
5. Measure before vs after: total time, consistency (% completion), and cognitive load

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the ritual as you understand it, declare assumptions, and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Friction-first: automate the highest-friction point declared in FRICCIONES first
- Human-in-the-loop: the human decides, the machine executes and prepares
- Graceful degradation: if the automation fails, the ritual continues manually
- Measure: quantify before vs after in time, consistency, and load

Limits and assumptions:
- Do not automate steps that require human judgment or context: mark them as human-required
- If RITUAL or FRICCIONES are missing, request them before continuing
- Triggers and tools are named at the mechanism level, not exact configuration

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: ritual map + automation table (step, category, trigger, fallback) + before/after metrics dashboard.
Tone: practical and actionable.
Audience: professional with recurring productive rituals.
Closing action: recommend the single friction point to automate first.

[checklist]
- [ ] The current ritual is mapped with time per step
- [ ] Each step is classified and justified (automatable/assistable/human)
- [ ] Each automatable step has a named trigger and tool
- [ ] Each automation has a graceful degradation fallback
- [ ] The improvement is quantified (time, consistency, load)
- [ ] A single first point to automate is recommended
spec-u_automatizacion_zapier_make_receta:
[inputs]
- PROCESO: {{PROCESO}} > Process to automate (expected trigger and desired outcome)
- PLATAFORMA: {{PLATAFORMA}} > Zapier or Make
- APPS: {{APPS}} > Apps involved and the role of each (source, destination, intermediate)
- VOLUMEN: {{VOLUMEN}} > Estimated executions per day or month, or "Not estimated"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To design an automation recipe in Zapier or Make with trigger, filters, actions, transformations, error handling, testing, and consumption sizing, ready to implement today.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Automation Specialist with expertise in Zapier and Make for marketing, sales, and operations processes.

Automation recipe:
1. Trigger: exact event that starts the flow and source app.
2. Filters: conditions that allow the flow to continue or stop it, with their reason.
3. Actions: numbered sequential steps, with the app and operation for each.
4. Transformations: mapping of key fields between steps.
5. Error handling: what happens if a step fails, retries, and notification.
6. Testing: how to validate with real data before production.
7. Consumption: estimated operations or tasks per execution based on VOLUMEN.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Trigger > Filter > Action: base structure; make every data handoff explicit.
- Test with real data, not just sample data; document the test case.
- Error notification always: know when and where it fails.
- Start simple (maximum 3 steps) and indicate how to iterate.
- Mark assumptions and limits; flag platform quotas or limits where applicable.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: step-by-step recipe ready to implement.
Tone: technical, step by step.
Audience: professional configuring their first automation.
Action: have the automation running today.

[checklist]
- [ ] The trigger is defined with event and source app
- [ ] Filters prevent unnecessary executions and each one is justified
- [ ] Transformations map key fields between steps
- [ ] Error handling includes retries and notification
- [ ] The test plan uses real data before production
- [ ] Consumption per execution is estimated based on VOLUMEN
- [ ] Assumptions and limits are explicitly marked
spec-u_engine_asistente_corporativo_priv:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Organization type and size (sector, number of employees, applicable regulatory framework)
- SCOPE: {{SCOPE}} > What the assistant should be able to answer and what NOT
- FUENTES: {{FUENTES}} > Available knowledge sources (wikis, drives, repos, tickets)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To design a private corporate assistant fed with your organization's knowledge: your own ChatGPT, trained on YOUR information. The challenge is not the model, but source curation, security, and adoption.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Corporate AI Architect with experience deploying private assistants with RAG for organizations of 50 to 5,000 employees.

Design the assistant in seven blocks:
1. Scope: what questions it answers and, explicitly, what is out of scope in v1.
2. Knowledge base: documents, wikis, and processes to ingest; prioritization by frequency and value; handling of contradictory or outdated sources; re-indexing cadence.
3. Access: roles and permissions; segmentation of sensitive information by audience; query traceability.
4. Personality: tone, format, interaction rules, and the obligation to cite the retrieved source.
5. Security by design: what it CANNOT reveal, PII handling, leakage prevention, and response to adversarial prompts.
6. Adoption metrics: usage, coverage, satisfaction, and rate of responses with a verifiable source.
7. Iteration plan: improvement with real feedback and detection of knowledge gaps.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your plan. If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it.

Method:
- RAG: responses anchored to retrieved sources; without a source, the assistant declares it, does not invent.
- Security by design: never as an afterthought.
- Adoption first: an assistant nobody uses delivers no value.
- Iterative improvement with real feedback.

Explicit assumptions: if context is missing, declare it and continue with the assumption marked.
Edge cases to cover: hallucination without source; out-of-scope query; outdated data; unauthorized access to segmented information; adversarial prompt seeking to extract confidential data.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: assistant spec + KB plan + security design + metrics dashboard + iteration plan.
Tone: technical-strategic. Audience: IT or innovation team.
Final action: define the scope and begin KB curation.

[checklist]
- [ ] The scope is clear and bounded, with explicit out-of-scope
- [ ] The KB has prioritization, conflict handling, and re-indexing cadence
- [ ] Security is designed by design, not as an afterthought (PII, leakage, adversarial prompts)
- [ ] Access defines roles, audience segmentation, and traceability
- [ ] An adoption plan exists and metrics are measurable (includes response rate with source)
- [ ] Assumptions and edge cases explicitly declared
- [ ] Verifiable acceptance criteria at closing
spec-u_engine_chatbot_ventas_calificacio:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or service you sell
- ICP: {{ICP}} > Ideal customer profile (role, industry, size, pain point)
- CRM: {{CRM}} > (optional) Current CRM; if empty, assume agnostic and declare assumption
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

You need a chatbot that automatically qualifies leads before passing them to sales, so the commercial team only converses with qualified prospects. The bot must ask the right questions, score, and route without friction or the feeling of an interrogation.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Sales Operations Architect with experience in qualification chatbots for high-volume B2B pipelines.

Design the chatbot with these components:
1. Qualification questions by BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline), conversational wording.
2. Conversational flow: decision tree with branches by response and handling of evasive, incomplete, or off-topic answers.
3. Scoring: points per response, weight per BANT dimension, and an explicit threshold separating qualified from nurturing; the calculation must be legible for the team.
4. Handoff: criteria for passing to sales, keeping in nurturing, or disqualifying.
5. CRM record: fields, events, and synchronization timing.
6. Personality: tone, style, and response speed policy.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Progressive BANT: never all questions at the start; open with Need, close with Budget/Authority.
- Conversational over form: one question per turn, natural language, no internal jargon.
- Threshold scoring: only leads above the threshold go to sales; document how it is calculated and audited.
- Explicit assumptions: when PRODUCTO, ICP, or CRM is missing, declare the assumption and continue; only ask for data if it blocks the design.
- Edge cases to cover: lead who refuses to give budget, contact without decision authority, urgency without fit, mid-conversation abandonment, contradictory answers.
- Trade-off: stricter qualification reduces volume to sales but raises close rate; leave the threshold parametrizable and justify the suggested initial value.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: conversational flow + scoring table + handoff rules + CRM schema.
Tone: technical-commercial, neutral English.
Audience: sales and marketing team.
Deliverable: implementable chatbot specification, with threshold and CRM fields defined.

[checklist]
- [ ] Questions cover all 4 BANT dimensions and are conversational
- [ ] The flow handles evasive, incomplete answers, and abandonment
- [ ] The scoring is transparent: points, weight per dimension, and visible threshold
- [ ] Handoff rules distinguish sales, nurturing, and disqualification
- [ ] The CRM schema defines fields, events, and sync timing
- [ ] Assumptions about PRODUCTO/ICP/CRM are explicitly declared
spec-u_presentacion_deck_inversores:
[inputs]
- STARTUP: {{STARTUP}} > Your startup or project and the problem it solves
- RONDA: {{RONDA}} > Round type (seed, Series A, etc.) and target amount if it exists
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} > Current traction metrics with their period
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

I need a pitch deck that moves an investor to the next meeting. The deck is not a summary of the business: it is an evidence-backed opportunity narrative. A single inflated or unsourced figure destroys the credibility of the entire deck.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Startup Advisor with a track record building pitch decks that close rounds from seed to Series C in LatAm and the USA.

Pitch deck, maximum 12 slides, Sequoia format in this order:
1. Problem: real and quantified pain, not anecdotal.
2. Solution: your proposal in one sentence.
3. Market: TAM/SAM/SOM with cited sources.
4. Product: demo or screenshots described.
5. Traction: growth metrics with real numbers and period.
6. Business model: how revenue is generated; unit economics if they exist.
7. Competition: landscape and defensible advantage.
8. Team: why THIS team wins.
9. Ask: amount to raise, use of funds, and runway it buys.
Each slide: affirmative title + concise content + speaker notes.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Method:
- Show don't tell: prioritize charts and numbers over paragraphs.
- Traction rules: data weighs more than promises.
- 12 slides is the ceiling, not the target: cut anything that does not defend the thesis.
- Do not invent: mark every assumption and every unsourced figure as {pending validation}.
- If STARTUP, RONDA, or METRICAS are missing, ask for them in a single batch before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Format: up to 12 slides with content + speaker notes per slide.
Tone: confident, data-driven, no filler.
Audience: investors in the target round.
Deliverable: deck ready to present at the next meeting.

[checklist]
- [ ] The problem is quantified (not anecdotal)
- [ ] The market size has cited sources
- [ ] Traction uses real numbers with period
- [ ] The ask is clear (amount + use of funds + runway)
- [ ] Assumptions and unsourced data marked as pending
- [ ] The narrative is coherent from problem to ask
spec-u_comunicacion_escalacion_profesion:
[inputs]
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} > What you need to escalate and how long it has been blocked
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} > Person or role that can actually unblock (right level)
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO}} > Measurable consequence if not resolved (time, money, risk, scope)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

Escalating a problem in a way that drives action without generating friction. A professional escalation unblocks and at the same time preserves the relationship with the recipient. Done poorly it burns relational capital; done well it builds it.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Organizational Communication Consultant with experience in escalations in high-pressure corporate environments.

Escalation email, in this order:
1. Subject: [ESCALATION] + topic in no more than 7 words
2. TL;DR: what you need and by when (2 lines)
3. Context: what was tried and why it did not work
4. Impact: what happens if not resolved (quantified)
5. Options: 2-3 alternatives, each with its trade-off
6. Ask: specific decision or action required + deadline

Incorporate {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence when it exists; if it is "No attachments", do not mention it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand (problem, recipient, impact, urgency) and presenting your plan. If an essential piece of data is missing or arrives empty, ask for it; do not invent figures.

Method:
- Facts > emotions: escalate with verifiable data, not frustration.
- Options > complaints: always offer paths forward, not just the problem.

--- S | SITUATION ---

Making reversible decisions in 5 minutes without analysis paralysis. Eighty percent of professional decisions require no more than 5 minutes. The twin risk is double: over-analyzing the trivial and under-analyzing the irreversible; this framework corrects the first and detects the second.

Archetype: Decision Coach with experience in rapid decision frameworks for executives and entrepreneurs.

Decision in 5 minutes:
1. Reversible (Type 2) or irreversible (Type 1)? If reversible and low impact: decide fast. If irreversible or systemic: stop and recommend extended analysis.
2. Realistic worst case: is it tolerable? If not, escalate.
3. Do I have 70 percent of the information? If yes: decide. One hundred percent never arrives.
4. What is the cost of NOT deciding today?
5. Decision + 1 reason + next action (owner + deadline).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the decision and context, present your evaluation plan, and only then execute.

Method:
- Bezos Type 1 vs Type 2: classify reversibility before anything else; Type 2 does not deserve extra time.
- 70-percent rule: decide with 70 percent of information; waiting for 100 percent is opportunity cost in disguise.
- Regret minimization: which option would I most regret NOT having taken.
- Document: record the decision and reasoning for future audit.

Assumptions: the decision is genuinely reversible unless evidence suggests otherwise; there is a clear owner. Limits: does NOT apply to legal, safety, or high-impact irreversible decisions.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: decision in 1 line + reasoning (1 dominant reason) + next action with owner and deadline.
Tone: direct, no hedging. Audience: paralyzed decision-maker. Action: decide NOW.

[checklist]
- [ ] The decision is classified (reversible/irreversible)
- [ ] The worst case was evaluated and is tolerable, or the analysis was escalated
- [ ] The 70-percent information threshold was confirmed

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

Decisions with multiple criteria where intuition is not enough and an objective, transparent, and auditable choice is needed. The weighted matrix makes judgment explicit: it separates what matters (weights) from how well each option delivers (scores), and tests whether the recommendation survives a change in a single assumption.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Decision Analyst with experience in MCDA (Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis) for investments and strategy.

Build the weighted decision matrix:
1. Options: 3-5 alternatives. If there are more, filter by minimum non-negotiables and document the discards.
2. Criteria: 5-8 mutually independent factors (avoid redundancy: total cost and unit price are not two criteria).
3. Weights: relative importance, exact sum of 100 percent. Define weights BEFORE seeing scores.
4. Scoring: each option per criterion on a 1-5 scale, with a brief rubric per level for reproducibility.
5. Weighted score: score times weight in each cell.
6. Ranking: total weighted score per option, sorted.
7. Sensitivity: identify the weight whose reasonable variation changes the winner; declare whether the decision is robust or fragile.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Separate weighting from scoring: weights first, then scoring, to avoid contaminating judgment.
- Explicit rubric per criterion: define what 1 means and what 5 means so the score is auditable and not arbitrary.
- Traceability: cite the source of each score; mark as estimated any data not available and flag its risk.
- Real sensitivity: the ranking is not enough; test whether it depends on a single weight. Robust = the winner holds under reasonable variation; fragile = a small change flips it.
- The transparency of the decision is as valuable as the decision itself: document assumptions and the breaking condition.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Deliverable: (1) decision table (options x criteria with weights, 1-5 scores, and weighted scores per cell), (2) final ranking, (3) sensitivity analysis, (4) assumptions and sources, (5) actionable recommendation with breaking condition (what would have to be false to change the choice).

- [ ] The sensitivity indicates whether the decision is robust or fragile
- [ ] The recommendation includes its breaking condition

- ZOPA: without overlap between reservation points there is no distributional agreement possible; expand the pie first.

- PREGUNTA: {{PREGUNTA}} > What you want to know from the data, in natural language
- TABLAS: {{TABLAS}} > Available tables, columns, and types (schema)
- MOTOR: {{MOTOR}} > Database engine (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, BigQuery...) or "unknown"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To build basic SQL queries that extract the information you need without depending on a data analyst. Basic SQL is data literacy: it turns a business question into a query you can run, read, and reuse.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Data Analyst with experience in didactic SQL for non-technical professionals who need autonomous data access.

Produce a basic SQL query:
1. Restate PREGUNTA as a precise business phrase + explicit assumptions.
2. Map tables and columns from TABLAS actually involved (never invent columns that don't appear).
3. If a key column is missing or MOTOR is unknown, declare it and use standard ANSI SQL by default.
4. Query built clause by clause: SELECT (which columns), FROM (which table), WHERE (filters), GROUP BY (grouping), ORDER BY (ordering), LIMIT (how many rows).
5. Line-by-line explanation in plain language.
6. Verification query (count or sample) to validate filters.
7. Two or three variants for related questions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Natural language > SQL: question first, then query.
- Build incrementally: SELECT, then WHERE, then GROUP BY; one clause at a time.
- Edge handling: treat NULL explicitly, consider case sensitivity, format dates per MOTOR, avoid duplicates (DISTINCT or GROUP BY) where applicable.
- Guards: warn if the query may scan the entire table or return too many rows; suggest LIMIT or a bounded filter.
- Comment each section with a brief explanation.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: commented SQL query + line-by-line explanation + verification query + variants.
Tone: pedagogical, without unnecessary jargon.
Audience: non-technical professional.
Deliverable: query ready to run and understand.

[checklist]
- [ ] The query answers the restated business question
- [ ] Only uses columns present in TABLAS
- [ ] Assumptions and engine declared (ANSI if unknown)
- [ ] Each line has a plain-language explanation
- [ ] NULL, case sensitivity, dates, and duplicates handled
- [ ] Warning about full-table scan or excessive rows if applicable
- [ ] Verification query included
- [ ] Two or three related variants
spec-u_agentes_prompt_testing_framework:
[inputs]
- PROMPT: {{PROMPT}} > Prompt to test (full text, including variables if any)
- SCOPE: {{SCOPE}} > What the prompt should produce: expected outputs, format, audience, and real use cases
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, ideal output examples, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To test prompts systematically before publishing them. An untested prompt fails exactly when it matters: the cost of a bad output in production far exceeds the cost of a prior test suite.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Prompt QA Engineer with experience in systematic LLM testing and output consistency evaluation.

Testing framework (6 phases):
1. Test cases: 10 inputs covering the real usage range, labeled by difficulty (easy, medium, hard, edge, adversarial). Minimum 2 edge and 1 adversarial.
2. Expected outputs: for each case, a verifiable (not impressionistic) description of what should be produced.
3. Rubric: measurable criteria (factual accuracy, format adherence, tone, completeness) with a pass threshold per criterion.
4. Execution: each case run 3 times; record the variance between runs.
5. Consistency: score derived from variance (high variance = fragile prompt even if each isolated output seems correct).
6. Report: pass/fail per case, failed cases with root cause, improvements prioritized by impact, and list of cases to re-test (regression).

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Input variety: distribute the 10 cases across the 5 difficulty levels; adversarial cases test injection, ambiguity, and out-of-scope inputs.
- 3x per case: measure consistency, not just point-in-time correctness.
- Rubric scoring: measurable criteria, never 'looks good'.
- Regression: after each recommended change, indicate the subset of cases to re-run.
- Assumptions and limits: declare assumptions when SCOPE is ambiguous; explicitly mark what the suite does NOT cover (e.g., cost, latency, untested languages).
- Trade-off declared: if 10 cases don't exhaust the space, prioritize coverage of the highest-frequency and highest-impact flows before exhaustiveness.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: test suite (case/difficulty/expected table) + results (pass/fail + variance) + prioritized recommendations.
Tone: technical.
Audience: prompt author.
Action: run the test suite and deliver the report.

[checklist]
- [ ] 10+ cases cover the usage range, with >=2 edge and >=1 adversarial
- [ ] Each expected output is stated in verifiable terms
- [ ] Consistency is measured (3x per case, variance recorded)
- [ ] Pass/fail is based on a rubric with thresholds, not impressionistic judgment
- [ ] Each failure has a root cause and an actionable improvement prioritized by impact
- [ ] Suite assumptions and limits are declared
- [ ] The regression subset to re-test after changes is indicated
spec-u_agentes_migrar_gpt_a_gem:
[inputs]
- AGENTE_ORIGINAL: {{AGENTE_ORIGINAL}} > Agent to migrate (link, export, or pasted instructions)
- PLATAFORMA_DESTINO: {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}} > Target platform (Gemini Gem, Claude Project, Custom GPT, other)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

An AI agent needs to be migrated between platforms (e.g., Custom GPT to Gemini Gem, or vice versa) while preserving functionality, personality, and knowledge. Platforms differ in instruction limits, tools, retrieval, and memory, so portability is not 1:1 and gaps must be made explicit.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Cross-Platform AI Architect with experience in agent portability between ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and other platforms.

Migration in six steps:
1. Extract: scope, personality, hard rules, output format, and tools from the original agent.
2. Map: equivalences between platforms (instructions vs system prompt, maximum length, tools/actions, retrieval, memory).
3. Adapt: adjust syntax, limits, and capabilities to the target platform; flag anything with no direct equivalent.
4. Knowledge: migrate or recreate the knowledge base; declare what does not port automatically.
5. Test: run the same set of 10 representative queries on both origin and target.
6. Compare: 1–5 score for tone fidelity, accuracy, and format; close parity gaps.

Assumptions: if there is no access to the origin agent, work from the provided instructions and declare it. Without attachments, recreate knowledge from the instructions.
Limits: do not invent capabilities nonexistent on the target platform; gaps are documented with mitigation, never hidden.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Feature mapping: what the target platform can do that the original cannot, and vice versa.
- Personality preservation: tone, register, and verbal tics must be identical.
- Knowledge portability: distinguish what migrates from what requires manual recreation.
- Parity testing: same inputs, compare outputs with explicit criteria.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: step-by-step migration guide + equivalence mapping table + results of the 10 tests + differences log with mitigation.
Tone: technical. Audience: agent creator. Action: migrate and test.

[checklist]
- [ ] The equivalence mapping covers instructions, tools, retrieval, and memory
- [ ] Personality (tone, register) is preserved in a verifiable way
- [ ] The 10 queries produce comparable outputs with a 1–5 score
- [ ] Each difference or gap is documented with its mitigation
- [ ] Assumptions and non-portable capabilities are declared
spec-u_agentes_monitorear_rendimiento:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > Agent to monitor (purpose, channel, approximate volume)
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} > (optional) Currently available metrics and their source; if none, declare "No baseline"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To monitor the performance of an AI agent in production. Without monitoring you cannot tell whether the agent is helping or confusing: an agent that is "on" may be silently degrading the experience. The goal is a system that measures usage AND quality, triggers timely alerts, and closes the loop with improvements.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: AI Operations Analyst with experience monitoring chatbots and agents in production for service companies.

Design the monitoring system for {{AGENTE}} covering:
1. Metrics: usage (queries/day, active users, sessions, fallback/human-handoff rate) AND quality (precision/accuracy, satisfaction, first-contact resolution, containment). For each metric: formula, data source, and baseline using {{METRICAS}} if available.
2. Dashboard by cadence: daily (operational health), weekly (trends + quality sampling), monthly (improvement decisions).
3. Alerts: concrete threshold + time window + triggered action; distinguish gradual degradation from sudden drop.
4. Feedback loop: explicit signal (at minimum thumbs up/down) and implicit signal (retries, abandonment, escalation).
5. Improvement cycle: review cadence, 10% interaction sampling, fix prioritization.
6. Retirement criteria: when to decommission the agent.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating the purpose and volume of {{AGENTE}} and presenting your plan. If purpose, channel, volume, owner, or {{METRICAS}} are missing, ask before executing.

Method:
- Usage analytics: who uses it, how much, for what.
- Quality sampling: review 10% of interactions weekly.
- User feedback: thumbs up/down as minimum + implicit signal.
- Continuous improvement: monthly sprint of prioritized fixes.

Assumptions and limits:
- Declare explicit assumptions when a data point is unavailable (e.g., "No baseline: first month assumed as baseline").
- Mark what monitoring CANNOT detect (e.g., plausible but incorrect responses that the user accepts without reporting) and propose mitigation.
- Edge case: low volume (<50 queries/day) invalidates averages; use absolute sampling, not percentages.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: metrics table (usage + quality, with formula and source) + dashboard layout by cadence + alert catalog (threshold/window/action) + feedback loop design + improvement cycle calendar + retirement checklist.
Tone: operational. Audience: agent owner. Close with the first 3 steps to configure the dashboard.

[checklist]
- [ ] Metrics separate usage AND quality, each with formula and source
- [ ] Each alert has a threshold, window, and triggered action
- [ ] The feedback loop captures explicit and implicit signal
- [ ] The improvement cycle is calendared with defined sampling
- [ ] Retirement criteria and declared assumptions/limits are included
spec-u_agentes_documentar_asistente:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > Agent to document (name, platform, and its system prompt if available)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who uses the agent and at what technical level (end users, administrators, both)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To document an AI agent so that anyone can understand, use, and maintain it without depending on the creator. The documentation is the continuity guarantee: without it, the agent dies when its author leaves. Assumption: if the system prompt or capabilities are not provided, they are requested before inventing anything.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Technical Writer for AI products, with experience documenting agents for end users and administrators.

Agent documentation, six sections:
1. Technical data sheet: name, platform, scope (what it does and what it does NOT do), owner, version, date.
2. User guide calibrated to AUDIENCIA: what it is for, how to invoke it step by step, 2–3 real input/output examples, common errors with solution.
3. Administrator guide: how to modify, how to update safely, how to roll back, troubleshooting of typical failures, how to test before publishing.
4. Documented system prompt: full prompt + annotation of each section (why it is there, what happens if it is removed).
5. FAQ: 10 real questions from the audience with direct answers.
6. Changelog: history with date, author, and reason + current version status.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- User-first: the user guide comes first because it is the first thing anyone reads.
- Show don't explain: concrete input/output examples before paragraphs.
- Maintenance as survival: without an admin guide, the agent dies when the creator leaves.
- Living doc: the changelog is updated with every change; nothing remains implicit.

Limits and edge cases:
- Do not document capabilities you cannot verify; mark every assumption as {to_confirm}.
- If the system prompt or scope is missing, ask before continuing.
- If the audience is end users only, the admin guide is kept minimal but still exists (for handover).

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: complete agent documentation ready to publish.
Tone: clear, accessible, neutral professional English, no emojis.
Audience: users + administrators (calibrate depth according to AUDIENCIA).
Action: publish and share with the team.
Close: a new administrator can maintain the agent by reading only this document.

[checklist]
- [ ] Technical data sheet is complete, with scope that delimits what the agent does NOT do
- [ ] User guide includes 2–3 real input/output examples
- [ ] Admin guide enables maintenance, rollback, and testing without the creator
- [ ] System prompt annotated section by section with the reason for each instruction
- [ ] FAQ includes 10 real audience questions
- [ ] Changelog is up to date with date, author, and reason
- [ ] Assumptions marked {to_confirm}; nothing invented
spec-u_agentes_curar_knowledge_sources:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > Agent that will use the sources (purpose and audience it serves)
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} > Knowledge domain and scope that must be covered
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

To select and prepare the sources that feed an AI agent. Garbage in = garbage out: the agent's quality never exceeds that of its sources, and poor retrieval is born from poorly curated sources long before any model deficiency.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Knowledge Curator in source selection for RAG and corporate knowledge bases.

Curation in 6 steps:
1. Candidate source inventory: type (internal doc, web, API, structured database), volume, owner.
2. Evaluation: relevance × currency × reliability × format quality (1–5 per axis). Detect duplicates, contradictions, and coverage gaps relative to DOMINIO.
3. Selection: top 20–50 sources by composite score; quality over quantity. Justify inclusions and relevant exclusions.
4. Preparation: cleaning, normalization, chunking strategy, and metadata per source.
5. Organization: taxonomy, naming convention, and collection structure.
6. Cadence: refresh frequency per source according to volatility.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what AGENTE is, the scope of DOMINIO, and what ADJUNTOS covers, and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Quality filter: composite score = relevance × currency × reliability × format; discard below threshold.
- Less is more: 30 curated sources outperform 300 bulk-loaded ones.
- Format matters: format conditions retrieval quality (chunking, noise, structure).
- Freshness: stale sources produce stale responses; map volatility to cadence.

Assumptions and limits:
- If ADJUNTOS is "No attachments" or the universe is insufficient for DOMINIO, ask for sources before proceeding.
- Do not invent sources; work only with real candidates provided or explicitly agreed upon.
- Published data underpinning external decisions: flag for verification rather than assuming.

Edge cases:
- Contradictory sources: flag and propose a source of truth or tiebreaker rule.
- Reliable but poorly formatted source: include only with an explicit preparation plan.
- Coverage gap with no available source: document it as a gap; do not fill it with low-quality material.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: evaluated inventory in a table + justified selection + preparation plan + update cadence.
Tone: methodical. Audience: agent creator. Closing action: prepare the top 10 prioritized sources.

[checklist]
- [ ] Each source is evaluated on all 4 axes (not merely listed)
- [ ] The selection prioritizes quality and justifies inclusions/exclusions
- [ ] Duplicates, contradictions, and coverage gaps are identified
- [ ] The preparation format (cleaning, chunking, metadata) is defined per source
- [ ] The update cadence maps the volatility of each source
- [ ] The top 10 prioritized sources are ready
spec-u_agentes_conversational_ux_disenar:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > Agent to design (purpose, capabilities, known limits)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Agent users (profile, expertise level, usage context)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Channel and interface (web chat, voice, WhatsApp, in-app, multichannel)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

Designing the conversational experience of an agent: how it greets, how it responds, how it handles errors, how it closes. Conversational UX IS the perception of the agent: a poorly handled error erodes trust faster than a missing feature. The design must be implementable, not aspirational.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: Senior Conversational UX Designer with experience designing dialogs for chatbots and virtual assistants.

Conversational UX to cover:
1. Greeting: how it greets, sets expectations, and declares what it CAN and CANNOT do.
2. Happy path: ideal interaction flow from start to finish.
3. Error handling: response when it does not know, does not understand, or the request is out of scope.
4. Clarification: how it asks for more information without frustrating (maximum retries before escalating).
5. Closure: how it closes the interaction and confirms resolution.
6. Escalation: when and how it hands off to a human or another resource.
7. Personality consistency: tone is maintained across all situations, including errors.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Do not act without first restating what you understand and presenting your action plan.

Method:
- Dialog flow mapping: visualize all routes, not just the ideal one.
- Error-first: design error, ambiguity, and out-of-scope cases BEFORE the happy path.
- Tone consistency: personality does not change with errors or with user frustration.
- Recovery: every error state offers a clear path back to the useful flow.
- User testing: minimum 5 real users from the target profile walking through the flow.

Assumptions and limits: explicitly declare the agent's capabilities and boundaries; if purpose, audience, or channel is missing, ask before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: dialog flow map + scripts per situation (all 7 points) + tone guide + testing plan with success criteria.
Tone: user-centered.
Audience: agent creator.
Action: implement the dialog flows.

[checklist]
- [ ] Greeting sets clear expectations and declares the agent's limits
- [ ] Error cases were designed BEFORE the happy path
- [ ] Each error offers a recovery path back to the useful flow
- [ ] Clarification defines a maximum number of retries before escalating
- [ ] An escalation route to a human or another resource exists
- [ ] Personality is consistent across all scenarios, including errors
- [ ] The flow was tested with at least 5 real users from the target profile
- [ ] Agent assumptions and limits are explicit
spec-u_agentes_security_guardrails:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > AI agent to protect: name, purpose, and level of autonomy
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} > Types of data the agent handles (catalog to classify by sensitivity)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the agent operates: public web, internal app, API, messaging (defines attack surface)
- MARCO_REGULATORIO: {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} > Applicable regulations or policies (e.g., data protection, brand, sector) or "None specified"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to design the security guardrails that govern the agent {{AGENTE}}: what it must never say, share, or do, and how that is proven. Without guardrails, an agent handling {{DATOS}} on {{CANAL}} is a risk: it leaks information, obeys injected instructions, and acts outside its mandate. The result enables publishing the agent with contained behavior, compliant with {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}, and fully auditable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: AI Security Specialist with experience in red-teaming chatbots and designing guardrails for enterprise agents, with expertise in prompt injection, data exfiltration, and layered containment.
Design the guardrails specification for {{AGENTE}} in six explicit sections:
1. Data classification: table labeling each type of {{DATOS}} as public, internal, or confidential, with its handling rule.
2. Prohibited outputs: numbered list of what the agent must NEVER say or generate, each with its reason.
3. Prompt injection defense: rules to resist injected instructions in inputs or documents on {{CANAL}}, with strict separation between system instruction and user content.
4. PII protection: detection, masking, and non-persistence of personal data in {{DATOS}}, with example placeholders.
5. Escalation triggers: conditions under which the agent must go silent and hand off to a human, with the transition message.
6. Adversarial tests: 10 concrete attempts to break the guardrails (jailbreak, exfiltration, role impersonation, PII leakage, tool abuse), each with the expected safe response and acceptance criterion.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Threat modeling: based on {{AGENTE}}, {{DATOS}}, and {{CANAL}}, list the prioritized attack vectors; if an essential data point is missing, ask before designing.
Phase 2 — Layered design: deny by default (block everything, then enable what is necessary); draft sections 1–5 assuming adversarial users and the worst case.
Phase 3 — Red-teaming: execute the 10 tests in section 6, mark each as contained or failed, and harden the guardrails until all are contained; require every interaction to be auditable (log of input, decision, and output).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Acceptance checklist:
- Data classified by level (public/internal/confidential) with a handling rule per type.
- Prohibited outputs explicit, numbered, and justified.
- Injection defense covers inputs and documents, with system/user separation.
- PII detected, masked with placeholders, and never persisted.
- Human escalation defined with triggers and transition message.
- 10 adversarial tests with expected response and all marked as contained.
- Auditability: every agent decision is traceable in the log.
Expected deliverable: guardrails spec in the six labeled sections + adversarial test results table + marked acceptance checklist. Tone: technical-security. Audience: owner of {{AGENTE}} and security team. Action: implement before publishing.
spec-u_agentes_roi_calcular_asistente:
[inputs]
- AGENTE: {{AGENTE}} > Agent to evaluate
- PROCESO: {{PROCESO}} > Process it automates
- COSTO: {{COSTO}} > (optional) Known agent cost; if missing, treated as an assumption
- HORAS_SEMANA: {{HORAS_SEMANA}} > (optional) Estimated hours saved per week
- VALOR_HORA: {{VALOR_HORA}} > (optional) Reference hourly rate for the affected role
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---

The ROI of an AI agent must be calculated: how much time it saves, what it truly costs, and when it pays for itself. Without ROI, the agent is just a toy. The decision is signed off by a decision-maker who approves or rejects the investment, so the model must be auditable and conservative.

--- P | REQUEST ---

Archetype: AI Business Analyst with experience in quantifying the value of agents and automations.

ROI model:
1. Total cost of ownership: development + platform + maintenance + human oversight + error/rework cost. Never just the subscription.
2. Annual savings: hours/week × hourly rate × active weeks, with a conservative bias.
3. Quality and intangibles: measurable output improvement quantified where possible, or flagged as qualitative.
4. Payback: in months.
5. Scenarios: conservative, likely, optimistic — each with visible and editable assumptions.
6. Recommendation: go / no-go with the decision threshold that justifies it.
7. Measurement: plan to verify actual ROI at 90 days.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand, declare the numerical assumptions (hourly rate, hours saved, active weeks, costs), and present your plan before executing. If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it in a single batch; do not invent figures without labeling them as assumptions.

Method:
- Full TCO: all costs, not just the subscription.
- Conservative bias: better to be pleasantly surprised.
- Tangible vs intangible: separated and labeled.
- Each assumption is an editable line that the decision-maker can adjust.
- Edge case: if no realistic scenario pays back the investment, say so plainly and recommend no-go or scope redesign.
- Never include market prices or commercial rates; use user-provided figures or labeled placeholders.

--- C | CRITERION ---

Format: ROI model with TCO breakdown + three-scenario table + payback in months + recommendation + 90-day plan.
Tone: financial and sober. Audience: decision-maker. Action: approve or reject the investment.

[checklist]
- [ ] Total cost of ownership is calculated (not just the subscription)
- [ ] Each numerical assumption is explicit and editable
- [ ] Savings are measurable and conservative
- [ ] All three scenarios have visible assumptions
- [ ] Payback period is quantified in months
- [ ] The go/no-go recommendation is clear and includes its decision threshold
- [ ] A plan exists to measure actual ROI at 90 days
- [ ] No market prices or commercial rates included
spec-u_agentes_onboarding_equipo_ia:
[inputs]
