1. Define players and the value net: direct rivals, substitutes, complementors, and when applicable, customers/suppliers with power, around {{DECISION_COMPETITIVA}} starting from {{JUGADORES}}.
2. Enumerate each player's set of moves, including {{MOVIMIENTO_PROPIO}} and always the option of not acting.
3. Classify the game on four axes and justify each one: simultaneous or sequential, one-shot or repeated, complete or incomplete information, zero-sum or variable-sum, per {{HORIZONTE_Y_SENALES}}.
4. Build the payoff matrix (simultaneous game) or decision tree (sequential) with relative values calibrated to {{OBJETIVO_VICTORIA}}; mark each estimated value or premise as [SUPUESTO] and make the scale explicit (ordinal or cardinal).
5. Solve: eliminate dominated strategies, identify dominant strategies and Nash equilibria; if sequential, apply backward induction; if repeated, consider retaliation and reputation strategies. Report the rival's expected best response.
6. Evaluate changing the game: credible commitments, signals, sequence changes (move first or wait), or expanding/recomposing the set of players. Verify that each lever is credible (that the rival cannot dismiss it as a bluff).
7. Recommend the most robust move, distinguish it from what is only optimal in the expected equilibrium, and list the observable triggers that would invalidate the analysis.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix {{OBJETIVO_VICTORIA}} as the payoff function and delimit the game scope (which decisions are inside and outside).
Phase 2 - Modeling: structure players, moves, and game type; represent payoffs in a matrix or tree with visible assumptions and declared scale.
Phase 3 - Resolution: apply dominance, Nash equilibrium, and backward induction; identify the equilibrium or equilibria, their stability, and whether there is multiplicity or absence of a pure equilibrium.
Phase 4 - Reconfiguration: test whether commitments, signals, or sequence changes improve your equilibrium payoff, validating the credibility of each lever.
Phase 5 - Decision: consolidate recommended move, rival's expected response, risk of irrationality or asymmetric information on the rival's side, and revision triggers.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. If an essential input is missing (players, own move, definition of winning, horizon, or signals), ask for it rather than inventing it.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The value net includes substitutes and complementors, not just direct rivals.
- [ ] Each player has their explicit set of moves, including the option of not acting.
- [ ] The game type is declared and justified on four axes (simultaneous/sequential, one-shot/repeated, information, zero-sum/variable-sum).
- [ ] A readable payoff matrix or decision tree exists, with declared scale and each estimated value marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] The resolution explicitly names dominated strategies, dominant strategies, and Nash equilibria; if sequential, backward induction is applied; if repeated, retaliation/reputation is considered.
- [ ] The rival's expected best response to the recommended move is reported.
- [ ] At least one way to change the game (commitment, signal, or sequence) is evaluated with its credibility test.
- [ ] The robust move is distinguished from what is only optimal in the expected equilibrium.
- [ ] The risk of an irrational or misinformed rival is named.
- [ ] There are explicit and observable triggers that would invalidate the analysis.
Expected deliverable: structured document with (a) game model, (b) matrix or tree with assumptions and scale, (c) equilibrium and rival's best response, (d) recommended move distinguishing robustness from expected optimality, and (e) contingency plan with observable triggers.
spec-estrategia_guerra_precios_respuesta:
[inputs]
- CATEGORIA_PRODUCTO: {{CATEGORIA_PRODUCTO}} > Category, product, or service where the price war is occurring and the relevant geography
- COMPETIDOR: {{COMPETIDOR}} > Who triggered the attack: player type, relative size, and known or inferred cost structure
- MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO: {{MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO}} > Nature of the rival's move: relative depth of the cut, scope (specific segment or total), and apparent duration (promo with expiration or permanent list price change)
- MI_POSICION_VALOR: {{MI_POSICION_VALOR}} > My value proposition, real differentiators, and current positioning against the competitor
- MARGEN_Y_EXPOSICION: {{MARGEN_Y_EXPOSICION}} > My margin cushion, customer mix (price-sensitive vs. loyal), volume at risk, and switching cost my customers face
- OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL: {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}} > What I prioritize: defend margin, defend share, protect a key account, or preserve the market's perceived value (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A competitor unleashed a price war in {{CATEGORIA_PRODUCTO}} and the organization risks reacting reflexively: matching the cut, bleeding margin, and dragging the entire category into a spiral where no one wins and perceived value is permanently eroded. The right decision is almost never to respond faster, but to respond with judgment. This prompt unlocks a deliberate response — match, ignore, or reframe — grounded in the rival's real intention and capacity, not commercial panic. The costly mistake is not losing a sale on price: it is validating a new anchor I cannot sustain or training the market to expect discounts. The deliverable goes directly to committee to align pricing, sales, and brand in a single reading.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive strategist specializing in dynamic pricing and applied game theory, with firsthand experience defending categories under discount attack without destroying their profitability or the category's value.
Deliverable: strategic response report to the price war, actionable and committee-ready. Steps:
1. Diagnose the attack: classify it as a signal (reversible gesture to discipline), tactical incursion (move limited to segment or window), or structural war (sustainable cut that rewrites the anchor); infer the real intention (gain share, clear inventory, squeeze a weak rival, set a new anchor, defend an account) and assess whether their cost structure allows them to sustain it or if it is a bluff.
2. Quantify my exposure from {{MARGEN_Y_EXPOSICION}}: volume and margin at risk, price-sensitive versus value-loyal segments, maneuvering cushion, and immediate damage versus damage if I do not respond within 1 to 2 quarters.
3. Walk the Match / Ignore / Reframe tree with the success and mistake criterion for each branch: Match is right if the rival sustains the price and the segment is worth more than the cost of matching, wrong if it validates an unsustainable price or trains toward discounting; Ignore is right if the attack is a signal or tactical and the core is loyal, wrong if it confuses paralysis with discipline; Reframe is the default with real differentiation. Recommend one branch and justify why you discard the others.
4. Design the concrete plays for the recommended branch (value reframe: bundles, guarantees, segment fencing, fighting version without cannibalizing the brand, contracts that raise switching cost; surgical match by segment or account with expiration; or ignore with explicit monitoring signals).
5. Simulate the competitor's retaliation two moves ahead (my action → counterattack → reply), flag whether a stable equilibrium or escalation exists, and fix exit or escalation conditions in advance.
6. Draft the communication plan to customers (value defense, without naming or validating the competitor) and the script for the sales force (stop the reflex to discount, with value arguments).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Board reading: separate facts from inferences about {{COMPETIDOR}} and {{MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO}}; identify what data is missing to decide and ask for it if decisive; mark each inference as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 — Intention and capacity diagnosis: cross the depth and scope of the cut against the rival's cost structure to distinguish a bluff from a sustainable war; name the rival's probable marginal cost as the limit of how far they can go.
Phase 3 — Tree decision: apply Match / Ignore / Reframe criteria against my {{MI_POSICION_VALOR}} and {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}}; make explicit the reason for discarding the non-chosen branches; consider the mixed branch (reframe on the core + surgical match only in the account or segment at risk of churn).
Phase 4 — Plays and game theory: detail the recommended branch and anticipate the rival's best response two moves ahead; identify equilibrium or escalation and define exit triggers (e.g., share recovery or margin stabilization) before acting.
Phase 5 — Communication and close: produce the messages to customers and to sales, and consolidate the committee report with a single recommendation and its logic.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The attack is classified (signal / tactical / structural) with rival intention and capacity argued from cost structure, not assumed.
- [ ] Exposure is quantified distinguishing immediate damage from 1–2 quarter damage and separating price-sensitive from value-loyal customers.
- [ ] All three branches (Match / Ignore / Reframe) have explicit success and mistake criteria; the recommendation justifies why it discards the others and considers the mixed branch.
- [ ] Plays are concrete and executable (segment, mechanism, fencing, expiration), not generic advice.
- [ ] There is a two-move retaliation simulation with an equilibrium or escalation reading and exit or escalation conditions fixed in advance.
- [ ] The communication plan defends value without naming or validating the competitor and the sales script stops reflex discounting with value arguments.
- [ ] Zero invented price figures; every assumption marked as [SUPUESTO]; no recommendation that structurally erodes the category's perceived value.
Expected deliverable: strategic price war response report with diagnosis, quantified exposure, reasoned tree decision, plays by scenario, two-move retaliation simulation, and communication plan, committee-ready.
spec-estrategia_ataque_lider_retador:
[inputs]
- MARCA_RETADORA: {{MARCA_RETADORA}} > Brand or company in challenger position that will execute the attack
- LIDER: {{LIDER}} > Market leader whose position is to be eroded
- MERCADO: {{MERCADO}} > Market, category, or geography where competition takes place
- DIFERENCIADOR: {{DIFERENCIADOR}} > Real challenger advantage (capability, agility, niche, technology, business model)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Time horizon to show traction (optional; if empty, assume 12 months as [SUPUESTO])
- RECURSOS: {{RECURSOS}} > Available challenger resources in FTE-months, team, or capacity (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A challenger brand ({{MARCA_RETADORA}}) competes against a leader ({{LIDER}}) in {{MERCADO}} with fewer resources. A frontal war of attrition favors the leader by scale, so an indirect approach is needed: flanking and selective attack on fronts where the leader cannot or will not respond. This analysis unlocks a prioritized set of moves that turns the leader's size into exploitable rigidity and the challenger's agility into an advantage, before committing commercial budget. The guiding logic: win ground where the cost of defending it is higher for the leader than the cost of yielding it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive strategist, specialist in challenger-leader dynamics, competitive role frameworks (Kotler/Singer), indirect approach (Liddell Hart), and the innovator's dilemma (Christensen).
Deliver a challenger attack plan with:
1. Leader anatomy: sources of power, structural rigidities (installed base, active contracts, channel conflict, core promise, cost structure, revenue model), and undefendable fronts without self-cannibalization.
2. Flank map: underserved or over-served segments, geographies, use occasions, channels, or service levels in {{MERCADO}} where {{LIDER}} is weak or indifferent. Distinguish real flanks (unmet needs) from mirages (markets with no demand).
3. Portfolio of 2-3 moves (flanking or selective attack) leveraging {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, each with: front, non-response mechanism (why the leader will not respond or will respond late/poorly: innovator's dilemma, margin protection, channel conflict, reputational cost), minimum resources (in FTE-months or capacity, NEVER prices), early measurable success signal, and escalation/retreat trigger threshold.
4. Sequence and contingency: order of moves to establish a beachhead and consolidate within {{HORIZONTE}}, with Plan B if the leader matches the move, launches a price retaliation, or acquires/imitates the challenger.
5. Positioning narrative that reframes a {{LIDER}} strength as a weakness, without disparaging or making defamatory comparisons.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm the challenger's competitive role and objective (share, perception, or both). Define the minimum viable victory.
Phase 2 - Leader diagnosis: identify the commitments that lock the leader in place (judo effect: using its own weight against it). List at least one commitment per source of power.
Phase 3 - Flank detection: cross unmet needs x leader weakness/indifference to locate low-counterattack fronts. Discard flanks with no real demand.
Phase 4 - Move design: define flanking (new territory) vs. selective attack (specific segment), with minimum resources, trigger metric, and decision threshold.
Phase 5 - Sequence and narrative: order moves by dependency and counterattack risk, add contingency, and close with the positioning reframe.
Flag every unverified data point as [SUPUESTO]; separate facts from inferences. If a critical input is missing ({{DIFERENCIADOR}}, {{MERCADO}}, {{LIDER}}), ask before executing. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each move attacks a front where the leader CANNOT respond without cannibalizing its core, with the non-response mechanism made explicit.
- [ ] The frontal war of attrition is explicitly avoided; the logic is one of indirect approach.
- [ ] Each move includes minimum resources (FTE-months or capacity, no prices), an early success signal, and an escalation/retreat trigger threshold.
- [ ] The proposed flanks have verified real demand, not market mirages.
- [ ] There is a sequence (what goes first, how to consolidate) and a contingency plan against imitation, price retaliation, or acquisition.
- [ ] The narrative reframes a leader strength as a weakness, without disparaging.
- [ ] Facts and assumptions are separated; assumptions carry [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: challenger strategy document with leader anatomy, validated flank map, 2-3 prioritized and sequenced moves with minimum resources, trigger metrics and contingencies, plus a positioning narrative, ready to decide commercial investment.
spec-estrategia_defensa_posicion_lider:
[inputs]
- EMPRESA: {{EMPRESA}} > Name of the market leader to defend
- CATEGORIA: {{CATEGORIA}} > Category or market where leadership is held
- CUOTA_ACTUAL: {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}} > Current market share and, if known, that of the nearest challenger
- RETADORES: {{RETADORES}} > Active and latent challengers threatening the position
- ANGULO_ATAQUE: {{ANGULO_ATAQUE}} > Challenger's dominant attack angle (price, niche, innovation, channel) (optional)
- VENTAJA_CENTRAL: {{VENTAJA_CENTRAL}} > Leader's source of advantage (brand, scale, network, technology, cost)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Planning horizon and market speed (e.g. 12-18 months, slow or disruptive market) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
{{EMPRESA}} leads the category {{CATEGORIA}} with a share of {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}}, but leadership is not self-sustaining: challengers erode flanks while the leader anchors itself in its own success. This prompt unlocks a defensive strategy that fortifies the dominant position with three coordinated lines (position, flanks, counter-offensive) and triggers that specify when to activate each one, avoiding both complacency and over-spending on defense. Guiding principle: only the true leader defends; defending when you don't lead is wasting resources.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive strategist specialized in defending market leaders, with mastery of Ries and Trout's defensive warfare doctrine (self-attack, blocking challenger moves) and Porter's five-forces model.
Deliverable: leadership defense plan for {{EMPRESA}} in {{CATEGORIA}}. Steps:
1. Characterize the leader's position: relative share against the nearest challenger, source of advantage in {{VENTAJA_CENTRAL}}, defensible moats, and exposed vulnerability points.
2. Map {{RETADORES}} (active and latent), their angle {{ANGULO_ATAQUE}}, and the specific flank they threaten; prioritize by probability and impact on share.
3. POSITION DEFENSE: core strengths to fortify and levers to raise customer switching costs without cannibalizing margin.
4. FLANK DEFENSE: segments, price tiers, or emerging niches to occupy preventively before the challenger; distinguish flanks to defend from flanks to deliberately yield.
5. COUNTER-OFFENSIVE: response when the challenger attacks the core, applying the self-attack principle to leave no free ground; include the cost of not responding.
6. Measurable ACTIVATION TRIGGERS: thresholds on {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}}, price signals, and {{RETADORES}} moves that escalate from one defense to the next, with the escalation rule made explicit.
7. Monitoring metrics, review cadence, and owner of each defensive line.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: consolidate position, advantage, and vulnerabilities; validate that {{EMPRESA}} is the true leader (if not, say so and redirect to an offensive or flanking strategy). Flag all unprovided data as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 Threat map: classify challengers by attack type and flank; prioritize by probability and impact on share within {{HORIZONTE}}.
Phase 3 Design of the three defenses: position, flanks, and counter-offensive, each with concrete actions, suggested owner, and assumed trade-off.
Phase 4 Trigger system: define quantitative thresholds, observation window, and the escalation rule between defenses; avoid ambiguous triggers.
Phase 5 Monitoring: metrics dashboard and cadence. Do not invent figures; if key data is missing, request it before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] It was verified that {{EMPRESA}} is the true leader; if not, the strategy was redirected.
- [ ] The three defensive lines (position, flanks, counter-offensive) are developed and differentiated, not merged.
- [ ] Each defense lists actionable actions with an owner, not generic principles.
- [ ] The flank defense identifies specific segments or niches to occupy preventively and distinguishes which flank to yield.
- [ ] The counter-offensive incorporates the self-attack principle and the cost of not responding.
- [ ] The triggers are quantitative, with an observation window and escalation rule, referenced to {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}} and {{RETADORES}} moves.

spec-estrategia_nicho_especializacion:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > What your company does today, main offering, and stage (early, scale, mature)
- MERCADO_ACTUAL: {{MERCADO_ACTUAL}} > Market or category where you compete and why it is perceived as saturated or generic
- CAPACIDADES_DIFERENCIALES: {{CAPACIDADES_DIFERENCIALES}} > Assets, talent, data, relationships, or knowledge where you are superior to the average
- COMPETIDORES_GENERALISTAS: {{COMPETIDORES_GENERALISTAS}} > Main broad rivals and their structural weakness against a specialist (optional)
- OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Desired outcome in 12-24 months (defensible share, margins, positioning) (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Capital, talent, geography, time, or regulatory limits that constrain which niche you can commit to (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Competing as a generalist in a saturated market erodes margins and dilutes messaging. Specializing in a defensible niche concentrates resources where depth outperforms the broad competitor's scale. This work produces a grounded niche decision and its competitive moat, unlocking a positioning that a generalist cannot replicate without cannibalizing their own model. The real value is not in "picking a segment" but in identifying the intersection where acute underserved pain coincides with a superior own capability and a structural (not circumstantial) weakness of the incumbent.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive positioning strategist, expert in job-to-be-done segmentation and in building sustainable advantage for challengers against generalist incumbents.

Deliverable: actionable niche and specialization strategy. Steps:
1. Delimit 3-4 niche candidates by crossing customer segment, acute unresolved problem, and dimension where NEGOCIO is clearly superior per CAPACIDADES_DIFERENCIALES. Each candidate must be nameable as "for [whom] who suffers [pain], we are [the only ones who] [how]".
2. Evaluate each candidate in a weighted matrix: size sufficient to sustain the business, pain intensity and frequency, structural weakness of COMPETIDORES_GENERALISTAS, right to win, and entry/exit friction. Distinguish structural weakness (they cannot close it without giving something up) from temporary weakness (they can close it with budget).
3. Recommend the winning niche with justification and build the moat, aligned with OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: specialized value proposition, non-copiable positioning message, 2-3 capabilities to deepen, and the explicit proof of why the generalist self-cannibalizes by imitating (model conflict, not a matter of will).
4. Define the resource concentration plan respecting RESTRICCIONES: what to reinforce, what to deliberately stop doing, early signals that confirm or refute the bet before committing everything, and the too-narrow niche risk with its mitigation (adjacent expansion niches and sequence).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Frame: confirm business, market, capabilities, and constraints; flag all missing data as [SUPUESTO] or ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 Generate candidates: apply job-to-be-done segmentation to find niches with underserved pain; discard broad categories disguised as niches.
Phase 3 Evaluate: score each candidate with the attractiveness and defensibility framework (Porter's focus, sustainable competitive advantage); separate preference signal.
Phase 4 Decide and fortify: choose the niche, design the moat, define validation/pivot signals, and the concentration plan with explicit trade-offs.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The niche is concrete (customer + problem + superior dimension), not a broad category or generic vertical.
- Defensibility is argued with the generalist's structural weakness, distinguished from the temporary one, not with preferences.
- The moat includes at least one element the generalist cannot copy without self-cannibalizing, with the proof of the model conflict.
- The plan explicitly names what to stop doing, not just what to add, and respects RESTRICCIONES.
- There are early validation/pivot signals before committing all resources.
- The over-specialization risk has concrete mitigation (adjacent niches and expansion sequence).
- Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; missing data requested, not invented.
Expected deliverable: document with named candidates, weighted evaluation matrix, recommended niche with justification, competitive moat (with cannibalization proof), and resource concentration plan with trade-offs, validation signals, and expansion path.
spec-estrategia_diferenciacion_costo_dua:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > Business, product, or line for which the dual strategy is designed
- CLIENTE_OBJETIVO: {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} > Segment and customer profile to be won
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > Two or three reference rivals (ideally strong differentiators in the category)
- ATRIBUTOS_VALOR: {{ATRIBUTOS_VALOR}} > Factors on which the category currently competes (optional; if missing, derive from canvas)
- PALANCAS_COSTO: {{PALANCAS_COSTO}} > Levers to lower cost without losing value (optional; e.g. automation, scale, self-service, chain reconfiguration)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to break Porter's classic trade-off for {{NEGOCIO}}: theory says one must choose between differentiation or cost leadership, and anyone attempting both gets stuck-in-the-middle. The objective is to design a deliberate dual strategy where {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} perceives clearly superior value compared to {{COMPETIDORES}} while the cost structure remains more competitive than that of rivals who only differentiate. This unlocks a defensible position: capturing share without a destructive price war or cost overruns that erode the margin. The underlying risk is not ambition but the lack of a real structural mechanism: without it, the strategy degenerates into wishful thinking and collapses at the first competitive move.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive strategist trained in the tradition of Michael Porter (generic strategies, value chain) and Blue Ocean Strategy by Kim and Mauborgne (value innovation, canvas and strategic curve).

Deliver a dual strategy report with these numbered components:
1. Current strategic canvas: segment, {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}, {{COMPETIDORES}}, and the value attributes of the category (use {{ATRIBUTOS_VALOR}} or derive them if missing).
2. Value-cost moat hypothesis: a falsifiable statement asserting why the dual position is achievable and sustainable in this specific case, including the condition that would make it false.
3. Eliminate-reduce-increase-create matrix (ERIC): which costly attributes with no perceived value to eliminate or reduce to free up cost, and which new or elevated attributes create differentiation without inflating spend. Each entry names the expected effect on cost or perceived value.
4. Sustainability mechanism: how {{PALANCAS_COSTO}} allow high value and low cost to coexist simultaneously, which value chain activity is reconfigured, why it does not collapse into stuck-in-the-middle, and why the mechanism is not trivially imitable in the short term.
5. Target value curve: description of the new value profile against {{COMPETIDORES}}, the point of greatest divergence, and name of the central value proposition.
6. Risk table (imitation, brand dilution, operational complexity, single-lever dependency, incumbent reaction) with one actionable mitigation per risk and exactly three measurable indicators with alert thresholds to measure the sustainability of the dual advantage.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: reconstruct the category and current strategic canvas; map how rivals compete today and where they spend value that the customer does not reward.
Phase 2 Value reconfiguration: apply ERIC to separate cost from perceived value; name the concrete effect of each action.
Phase 3 Dual mechanism: justify the simultaneity of both advantages with structural levers and value chain reconfiguration, not wishful thinking; declare the falsifiable hypothesis and its failure condition.
Phase 4 Tracing and fortification: draw the target value curve, name the proposition, close with risks, mitigations, and indicators.
If an essential data point is missing (segment, competitors, attributes, or levers), ask before proceeding. Flag each assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Do not invent data.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The canvas names concrete, measurable value attributes, not generic ones.
- The moat hypothesis is falsifiable: it includes the condition under which it would be false.
- The ERIC matrix has entries in all four actions and each one connects to a cost liberated or a perceived value gained.
- The sustainability mechanism explains why high value and low cost coexist without stuck-in-the-middle, which chain activity is reconfigured, and why it is not imitable in the short term; without this the report fails.
- The target value curve is distinguishable from that of {{COMPETIDORES}} and marks its point of greatest divergence.
- Each risk has one actionable mitigation; there are exactly three measurable indicators, each with an alert threshold.
- No invented data; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no mention of prices or the word free.
Expected deliverable: report structured in the six sections, ready to discuss in a strategic committee and convert into an execution plan.
spec-estrategia_ventaja_first_mover:
[inputs]
- OPORTUNIDAD: {{OPORTUNIDAD}} > Category, product, or market being evaluated for entry
- MADUREZ_MERCADO: {{MADUREZ_MERCADO}} > Market maturity and pace of technological change (stable, gradual, or abrupt)
- RECURSOS_CAPACIDADES: {{RECURSOS_CAPACIDADES}} > Own resources, differential capabilities, and execution speed
- PANORAMA_COMPETITIVO: {{PANORAMA_COMPETITIVO}} > Pioneers and current competitors and their moves
- HORIZONTE_RIESGO: {{HORIZONTE_RIESGO}} > Time horizon and risk appetite for the decision
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Deciding the entry timing for a category is one of the highest-leverage, lowest-reversibility strategic decisions: entering first can entrench a durable advantage or burn capital educating a market that someone else will harvest. The purpose is to resolve, with criteria and not intuition, whether for {{OPORTUNIDAD}} it is better to be a pioneer, fast follower, or late follower. Done well, this unlocks a defensible entry thesis, a capture plan, and a list of signals that confirm or invalidate the bet before fully committing resources. The typical costly mistake is not choosing the wrong position, but confusing a fragile pioneer advantage (awareness, being first) with a solid one (network effects, entrenched resources): this ruling exists to separate the two.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive strategist specialized in entry timing and competitive advantage dynamics, with mastery of the Lieberman and Montgomery frameworks (pioneer advantages and disadvantages) and of Suarez and Lanzolla (the pioneer's window based on market and technology dynamics).

Deliverable: an entry timing ruling (pioneer / fast follower / late follower) with thesis, conditions, invalidation signals, and capture plan.

Steps:
1. Restate the opportunity in two or three lines and declare what essential data is missing; ask for it in a single round if {{MADUREZ_MERCADO}}, {{RECURSOS_CAPACIDADES}}, or {{PANORAMA_COMPETITIVO}} arrive empty or ambiguous. Do not invent missing context.
2. Characterize the entry window based on the pace of technology and market evolution (stable, gradual, or abrupt) and derive how defensible the pioneer's position is: abrupt change erodes the advantage, stability protects it.
3. Inventory the genuinely accumulable pioneer advantages and discard the illusory ones: technological leadership and learning curve, control of scarce resources, switching costs and network effects. Rate each as solid, fragile, or nonexistent with its concrete reason.
4. Mirror-inventory the follower advantages: free-riding on market education, resolution of technological and demand uncertainty, incumbent inertia, and leap to a better curve. Rate each the same.
5. Cross both sides against {{RECURSOS_CAPACIDADES}} and {{HORIZONTE_RIESGO}} and issue a single position recommendation; name the second strongest option and why it was ruled out.
6. Define the timing thesis in one sentence, two or three observable conditions that sustain it, the early signals that would invalidate it (with the response action for each), and the capture plan for the first 12 to 18 months.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing: restate the opportunity, set missing assumptions, and characterize the entry window (technology and market stability).
Phase 2 · Advantage balance: evaluate the three sources of pioneer advantage and, in mirror, the four follower advantages, rating each by its real strength in this case, not in the abstract.
Phase 3 · Ruling: cross the balance against resources, speed, and risk appetite; issue a single position, thesis, conditions, invalidation signals with response, and 12-18 month capture plan.
Edge cases: if the market does not yet exist (category to be created), the risk of educating for someone else is maximum and the window depends on the speed of imitation; if there is already an entrenched pioneer with network effects, rule out being a late follower from the start unless there is a technological discontinuity that resets the curve.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The recommendation names a single position (pioneer, fast follower, or late follower) with a one-sentence thesis, not three lukewarm options.
- Each pioneer and follower advantage is rated solid, fragile, or nonexistent with its reason in this case, not listed in the abstract.
- The entry window is explicitly tied to the pace of technology and market change.
- The validation conditions and invalidation signals are observable and measurable, not generic; each invalidation signal carries its response action.
- The 12-18 month capture plan is actionable, sequenced, and consistent with the chosen position.
- The second strongest position and the reason for its rejection are named.
- All assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented market or share figures; no prices.
Expected deliverable: entry timing ruling with one-sentence thesis, rated advantage balance, conditions, invalidation signals with response, and 12-18 month capture plan.
spec-estrategia_inteligencia_competitiva:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION_E_INDUSTRIA: {{ORGANIZACION_E_INDUSTRIA}} > Company, sector, segment and geography where it competes
- DECISIONES_ESTRATEGICAS: {{DECISIONES_ESTRATEGICAS}} > Current decisions the system must inform (price, market entry, roadmap, positioning)
- COMPETIDORES_Y_SUSTITUTOS: {{COMPETIDORES_Y_SUSTITUTOS}} > Known direct competitors, challengers and substitutes
- CADENCIA_Y_DECISORES: {{CADENCIA_Y_DECISORES}} > Desired decision rhythm and who decides at each level
- RECURSOS_Y_FUENTES: {{RECURSOS_Y_FUENTES}} > Team, tools, budget and access to field, customers and channel (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The organization collects competitor data reactively and in a scattered way: someone sees a news item, shares it in a chat and it gets lost. There is no system that converts those signals into decisions, so the team reacts late to price moves, launches or entries by new players. Designing a recurring competitive intelligence system unlocks strategic anticipation: detecting moves before they become news, feeding price, roadmap and positioning decisions with evidence, and stopping competing while looking in the rearview mirror. The goal is not a one-off report but a living capability installed in operations, one that survives whoever built it and is maintained with effort proportional to real resources.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Director of Competitive Intelligence, with a track record of building market intelligence functions in technology and services companies, trained in the competitive intelligence discipline (KIQ, intelligence cycle, war-gaming) and in classical competitive strategy.

Deliverable: an operational blueprint of the competitive intelligence system, ready to install. Steps:
1. Derive 5 to 8 Key Intelligence Questions (KIQ) from DECISIONES_ESTRATEGICAS; each KIQ is a decision question, not a topic. Without KIQs there is no system, only collection. If more than 8 candidates come in, prioritize by decision-impact multiplied by reversibility: first what is costly to reverse.
2. Build the surveillance objective map: order COMPETIDORES_Y_SUSTITUTOS plus emerging challengers and environment signals (regulatory, technological, talent), prioritized by decision impact and rate of change. Include at least one non-obvious substitute and one potential entrant outside the known set.
3. Define the capture plan: by objective, which signals to observe, in which sources within RECURSOS_Y_FUENTES, frequency and owner; separate weak signals (early warning) from confirmed signals. Each weak signal needs at least two independent confirmations before escalating to a decision.
4. Specify the analysis engine with explicit frameworks: Five Forces for industry structure, Porter's competitor profile (goals, assumptions, current strategy, capabilities) to infer intent, and a market signals scheme to interpret moves. Describe the journey from raw data to implication for us, separating observed fact from inference, and assigning a confidence level (high/medium/low) to each inference.
5. Design the cadence and rituals adjusted to CADENCIA_Y_DECISORES: weekly signal pulse, monthly synthesis, quarterly war-game; for each ritual define input, output, decision-maker and maximum meeting time. If resources are insufficient for all three rituals, propose the minimum viable version and state what is sacrificed.
6. Define actionable dissemination: format by audience (one-line alert for executives, brief for product and commercial, deep dossier for strategy) with the trigger that emits each piece. Also define the non-emission threshold: what does NOT merit interrupting an executive.
7. Close the decision and learning loop: how to trace which decision generated each piece of intelligence, what happens with a KIQ that never drove a decision (it is retired), and how KIQs are recalibrated each quarter.
8. Set ethical and legal hygiene: only lawful and public sources; prohibited to obtain information under false pretenses, impersonation, access to confidential information from former employees or third parties, or any improper means. Include the doubt rule: when in doubt about a source, do not use it.
Close with a 30/60/90 day launch plan with a verifiable milestone per tranche and the first system owner.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the competitive situation as understood and confirm that KIQs are the real decisions; if the industry, competitors, decisions or resources are missing, ask before proceeding. Do not invent the market.
Phase 2 - Anchor to decision: for each KIQ identify which decision it unlocks, who makes it and what evidence would reverse it (action threshold). A KIQ without a decision owner does not enter the system.
Phase 3 - Design capture: map objectives to sources and owners; label each signal as weak or confirmed, assign frequency and note the cost of obtaining it relative to its decision value.
Phase 4 - Build analysis: apply Five Forces, Porter's competitor profile and market signals; convert each finding into an implication with a confidence level and a "and therefore" decision. Separate fact from inference.
Phase 5 - Install cadence and dissemination: define rituals, formats by audience and triggers; connect each deliverable to its decision-maker and set the non-emission threshold.
Phase 6 - Close the loop: define intelligence-decision traceability, retirement of inert KIQs and quarterly recalibration, and deliver the 30/60/90 launch with verifiable milestones. Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each KIQ is anchored to a concrete decision from DECISIONES_ESTRATEGICAS with an identified decision owner, not a generic monitoring topic.
- There is an explicit prioritization criterion when KIQ candidates overflow (impact by reversibility).
- The capture plan names source, frequency and owner per objective, distinguishes weak from confirmed signals and requires double confirmation before escalating.
- The objective map includes at least one non-obvious substitute and one entrant outside the known set.
- The analysis uses all three frameworks explicitly (Five Forces, competitor profile, market signals), separates fact from inference and assigns confidence level.
- Each finding ends in an actionable implication with an "and therefore" and a decision trigger.
- The cadence defines input, output, decision-maker and duration per ritual, with a minimum viable version if resources are insufficient.
- Dissemination has a format per audience, emission trigger and non-emission threshold.
- The learning loop traces intelligence toward decision, retires inert KIQs and recalibrates each quarter.
- Ethical and legal hygiene is explicit: only public and lawful sources, with the doubt rule.
- The 30/60/90 launch has a verifiable milestone per tranche and a system owner.
- Every unprovided datum is marked [SUPUESTO]; no competitors or figures are invented.
Expected deliverable: competitive intelligence system blueprint with prioritized KIQs, objective map, capture plan, analysis engine, cadence and rituals, dissemination matrix, decision-learning loop, ethical-legal note and 30/60/90 day launch plan with verifiable milestones and owner.
spec-estrategia_reposicionamiento_marca_:
[inputs]
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > Product, service or brand to reposition and the promise it communicates today
- SECTOR: {{SECTOR}} > Industry, category and geography where it competes
- SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO: {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} > Customer or segment to become relevant to again; if omitted, derive it from the diagnosis and mark it [SUPUESTO]
- COMPETIDORES_CLAVE: {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}} > 2-4 rivals the offer got trapped between and how each is positioned
- ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL: {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} > Axis on which the offer competes today and which has stopped differentiating (price, speed, reach, etc.)
- ACTIVOS_PROPIOS: {{ACTIVOS_PROPIOS}} > Capabilities, data, relationships or rights that are hard to copy and could support a new territory (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Non-negotiable limits: installed base not to lose, contracts, regulation, umbrella brand (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The positioning of {{OFERTA}} in {{SECTOR}} has lost relevance: it got trapped between {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, outmatched by perceived price on one side and by specialization on the other, and {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} no longer sees why to choose it because {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} has stopped differentiating and has become a mere entry requirement. A well-constructed strategic repositioning unlocks a defensible competitive territory, recovers choice clarity and negotiating power, and reorients product, message and proof toward a position that the dominant competitor cannot copy without betraying their own model. This deliverable feeds offer and go-to-market decisions: it is not a slogan refresh or a creative advertising exercise.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior competitive positioning strategist, with a track record of leading offer repositioning in saturated markets and mastery of positioning maps, points of parity versus difference, winnability by assets, defensibility against the rival's response and value migration.
Deliverable: strategic repositioning dossier for {{OFERTA}}. Steps:
1. Diagnose the position trap: current territory, direct rivals and their stated positioning, why it stopped being relevant and which attributes moved from differentiators to points of parity. Name the trap in one sentence.
2. Map the competitive field on 2-3 decision axes that matter to {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}; place {{OFERTA}} and {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, and reveal the contested ocean and the defensible empty territory.
3. Generate 2-3 candidate repositioning territories: segment, attribute winnable by own assets ({{ACTIVOS_PROPIOS}} if provided) and the reason why the dominant competitor cannot or would not follow there (conflict with their model, installed base or promise).
4. Recommend a territory by scoring relevance for the segment against defensibility in the face of the rival's response; draft the positioning statement: for [segment], who [need], {{OFERTA}} is [category] that [differential benefit], unlike [alternative], because [proof].
5. Define the evidence that must be true to sustain the position, the concrete changes in product, message and proof, and the transition plan that respects {{RESTRICCIONES}} and does not confuse the current customer.
6. Close with early success signals (what to measure and indicative threshold) and risks of cannibalization, brand dilution or rejection, each with mitigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: separate points of parity (what must be present to be considered) from points of difference (what drives the choice); explain why {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} migrated from one to the other; name the position trap with evidence, not in the abstract.
Phase 2 Mapping: derive the axes from real purchase criteria of the segment, not from internal attributes or product jargon; place offer and rivals; mark the contested ocean (where everyone fights) and the defensible void (relevant and underserved).
Phase 3 Options: for each territory evaluate relevance for the segment, winnability by own assets and defensibility against the competitor's foreseeable reaction; discard territories that are empty because nobody wants them (empty due to irrelevance).
Phase 4 Decision and statement: choose by relevance x defensibility; draft the complete statement and stress each part against available proof; if a part does not hold, adjust it or mark the missing evidence.
Phase 5 Activation and transition: translate into changes in offer, narrative and evidence; sequence the migration (what changes first, which signals to watch, how it is communicated to the current customer) to retain without confusing and to win the new segment.
Mark every inference without data as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent figures, market shares or prices. If OFERTA, SECTOR, COMPETIDORES_CLAVE or ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL are missing, ask before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The position trap is named in one sentence and supported with evidence, not described in the abstract.
- The map uses axes that are real purchase criteria for the segment, not internal attributes; the identified void is relevant, not merely empty.
- Each candidate territory declares the segment, an attribute winnable by own assets and why the dominant rival cannot or does not want to follow.
- The recommendation is justified by relevance x defensibility, not by aesthetic preference.
- The positioning statement follows the complete structure and each part is verifiable or has its missing evidence marked.
- Product, message and proof are aligned with the recommended territory and respect the given restrictions.
- The transition plan protects the current customer, sequences the conquest of the new one and specifies what is communicated and when.
- Success signals with metric and threshold; risks of cannibalization, brand dilution and rejection, each with mitigation.
- Each assumption is marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data, no prices or monetary figures.
Expected deliverable: dossier in neutral professional English with named diagnosis and trap, described competitive map, 2-3 compared territories, recommended territory with stressed positioning statement, activation and transition plan, and signals and risks with mitigation.
spec-estrategia_matriz_bcg_portafolio:
[inputs]
- PORTAFOLIO: {{PORTAFOLIO}} > Company or portfolio to analyze (name, sector, business model)
- UNIDADES_NEGOCIO: {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}} > List of business units or product lines to classify
- CRECIMIENTO_MERCADO: {{CRECIMIENTO_MERCADO}} > Annual market growth rate for each unit (%); if any is missing, the AI requests it
- CUOTA_RELATIVA: {{CUOTA_RELATIVA}} > Own market share and market leader's share per unit, to calculate relative share; if missing, the AI requests it
- RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA: {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}} > Constraint conditioning the allocation: available cash, focus, board mandate (optional)
- HORIZONTE_DECISION: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} > Portfolio decision horizon: 12 months, 3 years, etc. (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Deciding where to put the next unit of investment is the highest-impact and most easily mistaken corporate bet: funding dogs out of inertia, starving stars or letting question marks with potential wither. This prompt builds a rigorous BCG matrix for {{PORTAFOLIO}} to convert the set of units into a resource allocation thesis defensible to the board. It unlocks clarity on what to build, what to hold, what to harvest and what to exit, with the numerical reasoning that supports each move and honesty about where the model stops being reliable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior corporate strategist, specialist in multi-business portfolio management and the BCG growth-share matrix, with experience in capital allocation decisions at board level.

Deliverable: portfolio diagnosis with BCG classification of each unit, generic strategy by quadrant and resource allocation plan tied to real cash. Steps:
1. Restate the portfolio {{PORTAFOLIO}} and the units {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}}; confirm scope, each market definition and thresholds before executing.
2. Calculate both axes per unit: market growth (vertical, high/low threshold) from {{CRECIMIENTO_MERCADO}} and relative share (horizontal, own share / leader's share, 1.0x threshold) from {{CUOTA_RELATIVA}}. If the growth, own share or leader's share for any unit is missing, ask for it and do not classify that unit until you have it.
3. Assign each unit to a single quadrant (star, cash cow, question mark, dog) with explicit numerical reasoning.
4. Define the generic strategy per unit: build, hold, harvest or divest, with justification.
5. Flag momentum and transitions: if a unit is within ±20% of a threshold or shows a clear trend, indicate its probable quadrant within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}; the static position is misleading.
6. Diagnose the portfolio balance under {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}}: cash cows' flow toward selected stars and question marks, overweight in dogs, dependency on a single cash cow, concentration in a single star, excess of question marks dispersing investment. Quantify the balance when data allows.
7. Deliver master table by unit, resource allocation table (relative % of investment tied to available cash) and the 3 priority moves for {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: define the market of each unit explicitly and consistently (the BCG result is sensitive to this definition); set thresholds for each axis (high/low growth ~10% per year or the sector's; relative share 1.0x) and mark with [SUPUESTO] every threshold or figure estimated in the absence of data.
Phase 2 — Positioning: place each unit on the axes with its numbers; never invent shares or growth rates, ask for them. If there is no clear market leader or the market is fragmented, declare it and treat relative share as a range with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 — Classification and strategy: assign quadrant and generic strategy (build / hold / harvest / divest) per unit, plus the probable transition when applicable.
Phase 4 — Balance and moves: assess the portfolio's financial balance, contrast the required investment against the cash that {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}} allows, and prioritize 3 moves. Flag BCG model limitations (ignores synergies between units, absolute profitability and margins, and depends on how the market is defined) when they alter a recommendation, and clarify that relative share is a proxy for unit cost, not profitability.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each unit's market definition is explicit and consistent; ambiguity marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Each unit has explicit market growth and relative share (or a data request if missing); zero invented figures.
- [ ] Relative share calculated as own share / leader's share, with 1.0x threshold applied; case with no clear leader treated as a range.
- [ ] Each unit classified in a single quadrant with numerical reasoning.
- [ ] Generic strategy (build / hold / harvest / divest) justified per unit.
- [ ] Probable quadrant transition flagged for units near a threshold (±20%) or with momentum.
- [ ] Portfolio balance diagnosis under the strategic constraint, quantified when data is available.
- [ ] Resource allocation tied to the real cash the restriction allows, not to an abstract ideal.
- [ ] 3 priority moves aligned to the horizon with their portfolio logic.
- [ ] BCG model limitations flagged where they affect; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Professional English, no emojis, no prices.
Expected deliverable: master table by unit (growth, relative share, quadrant, strategy, probable transition), resource allocation table (relative % of investment tied to cash) and prioritized list of 3 moves with their portfolio logic.
spec-estrategia_matriz_ge_mckinsey:
[inputs]
- EMPRESA_Y_SECTOR: {{EMPRESA_Y_SECTOR}} > Corporation name and sector in which the portfolio competes
- UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO: {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} > List of units, divisions or lines to evaluate (minimum 2; ideally 3-8 for a legible grid)
- DATOS_MERCADO_Y_DESEMPENO: {{DATOS_MERCADO_Y_DESEMPENO}} > Per-unit data: market size and growth, relative share, margins, revenues; anything missing is marked [SUPUESTO]
- HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCION_CAPITAL: {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCION_CAPITAL}} > Planning horizon and capital ceiling or constraint to allocate
- CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS: {{CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS}} > Factors to overweight on the axes (optional; e.g. growth, profitability, regulatory risk)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The leadership team of {{EMPRESA_Y_SECTOR}} must decide where to concentrate scarce capital among {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} within {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCION_CAPITAL}}. Without a common framework, investment decisions become political or intuitive, and the units with the best internal narrative capture capital above their economic merit. The GE-McKinsey matrix translates the portfolio into a 3x3 map (Industry Attractiveness x Competitive Strength) that unlocks an evidence-based capital allocation conversation, comparable across units and defensible to a committee.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Corporate Strategy Director, expert in multi-business portfolio management and capital allocation.
Deliverable: complete GE-McKinsey matrix with auditable scoring, positioning and capital recommendations. Steps:
1. Define both axes on a 1-5 scale with bands Low (1.0-2.33), Medium (2.34-3.66), High (3.67-5.0).
2. Propose 5-7 Industry Attractiveness factors (size/growth, competitive intensity, structural margins, barriers to entry, cyclicality/regulation, technological disruption) with weights summing to 100%, adjusted to {{CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS}}.
3. Propose 5-7 Competitive Strength factors (relative share, differentiation/brand, cost position, capabilities/talent, financial health, customer loyalty) with weights summing to 100%.
4. Rate each unit in {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} factor by factor (1-5) using {{DATOS_MERCADO_Y_DESEMPENO}}, noting for each rating the datum or the [SUPUESTO] that supports it; calculate the weighted score per axis and show the complete table with the arithmetic.
5. Place each unit in one of the 9 cells according to the bands, size the bubble by revenues and assign a directive: Invest/Grow, Selectivity, or Harvest/Divest.
6. Deliver prioritized capital allocation recommendations, sequence under constraint, moves per unit, review triggers and risks/assumptions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm units, horizon and available data; declare factors and weights justifying each weighting against {{CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS}}; mark every unverified datum as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Scoring: rate factor by factor with an explicit rubric (what 1 means and what 5 means), weight and consolidate the score for each axis per unit in a traceable table.
Phase 3 - Mapping: position each unit in the 3x3 grid, interpret the cell and treat medium-diagonal positions (Selectivity) with a declared tiebreaker (dominant axis trend, momentum or risk).
Phase 4 - Decision: convert positions into capital directives, sequence investments under {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCION_CAPITAL}}, declare the sensitivity (which weight or borderline rating change would move a unit to a different cell) and expose risks.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Both axes have 5-7 factors with explicit weights summing exactly to 100%, and each weight is justified.
- [ ] Each unit shows a 1-5 rating per factor with the source or [SUPUESTO] that supports it, and a weighted score per axis with verifiable arithmetic.
- [ ] Each unit falls in one of the 9 cells according to the bands, with a bubble sized by revenues and no contradictions.
- [ ] Medium-diagonal positions have a declared tiebreaker.
- [ ] Each position translates into a directive (Invest/Grow · Selectivity · Harvest/Divest).
- [ ] The capital allocation respects {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCION_CAPITAL}}, is prioritized and includes review triggers.
- [ ] The result's sensitivity to weights and borderline ratings is declared.
- [ ] Every unverified datum is marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented figures or prices.
Expected deliverable: 3x3 GE-McKinsey matrix with scoring tables per axis, position map with revenue bubbles, directive per unit, prioritized capital allocation plan with sequence and triggers, sensitivity analysis and risk and assumption register.
spec-estrategia_parenting_advantage:
[inputs]
- GRUPO_CORPORATIVO: {{GRUPO_CORPORATIVO}} > Name and brief description of the multi-unit group under analysis; current portfolio thesis if it exists
- UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO: {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} > List of units with relative size, market, business model and declared strategic role
- MODELO_MATRIZ: {{MODELO_MATRIZ}} > Capabilities, processes, shared services, biases/heuristics and operating model of the corporate center (the "parenting"): what it does, how it decides and what it charges the portfolio
- CRITERIO_DECISION: {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} > What decision is to be enabled and over what horizon (reallocate capital, divest, merge units, redesign or reduce the center) and who sponsors it
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Portfolio thesis, non-negotiable links, untouchable units, regulatory or corporate governance limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A multi-unit group sustains a corporate parent whose cost and authority are only justified if it creates net value in its units above any alternative owner. The silent trap: a business can be profitable and still be poorly parented, because the parent extracts more value (center cost, delays, biases, constraints) than it contributes. This analysis subjects each unit to the better parent test and unlocks grounded portfolio decisions: where the parent should get more involved, parent lightly, transform its parenting model or withdraw and divest. The result avoids value destruction from a miscalibrated corporate center and guides the redesign of the parent itself.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior corporate strategist in portfolio strategy and corporate center design, with mastery of the parenting advantage framework (Goold, Campbell and Alexander).
Deliverable: corporate parenting advantage analysis with an actionable recommendation per unit and parent redesign implications. Steps:
1. Map the portfolio: each unit in UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO with relative size, market, business model and declared role.
2. Define 3 to 5 critical success factors (CSF) per unit: what it must master to win in its market.
3. Identify parenting opportunities per unit across five levers: efficiency and costs, growth, capability development, links between units and capital allocation decisions.
4. Evaluate fit on two independent axes: (a) MODELO_MATRIZ parenting against the unit's CSFs; (b) parent's biases and heuristics against real parenting opportunities. Classify each unit in ONE single of five zones: heartland (high-high), edge (partial fit, watch), value trap (destroys more than it creates), alien territory (healthy but another owner would parent better) or value wasteland (neither parent nor business thrives).
5. Estimate the net value per unit: value added minus value destroyed (center cost, decision delays, biases, imposed constraints), with backing logic. Explicitly separate the value the parent creates from the business's inherent value (better parent test).
6. Recommend per unit: get more involved, parent lightly, transform the parenting model or withdraw/divest; with rationale, alignment to CRITERIO_DECISION and a concrete first step.
7. Derive the parent design implications: capabilities, processes and center size that the resulting portfolio justifies, and what would no longer make sense to sustain.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm GRUPO_CORPORATIVO, UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO, MODELO_MATRIZ, CRITERIO_DECISION and RESTRICCIONES; declare [SUPUESTO] for every missing datum; if UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO or MODELO_MATRIZ are insufficient for the two fit axes, request them before concluding.
Phase 2 Per-unit diagnosis: execute steps 1 to 3, building CSFs and parenting opportunities unit by unit, skipping none.
Phase 3 Fit and net value: execute steps 4 and 5, placing each unit in its unique zone and separating the parent's value from the business's inherent value.
Phase 4 Decision and design: execute steps 6 and 7, ordering recommendations by impact on CRITERIO_DECISION and honoring RESTRICCIONES; mark every unresolved tension as a pending decision for the sponsor.
Edge cases: if two zones are defensible for a unit, choose the dominant one and register the second as a hypothesis to falsify; if a unit lacks data for one axis, place it provisionally and flag what datum would confirm it; if RESTRICCIONES shields a unit that the analysis flags as a value trap or alien territory, respect the shield but document the opportunity cost.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every unit in UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO receives CSFs, parenting opportunities across the five levers, a zone and a recommendation.
- [ ] Each unit falls in ONE single of the five zones, justified on BOTH fit axes.
- [ ] The net value explicitly separates the value created by the parent from the business's inherent value (better parent test).
- [ ] The value destroyed by the center (cost, delays, biases, constraints) is accounted for, not just the value added.
- [ ] Each recommendation aligns with CRITERIO_DECISION and includes rationale and a concrete first step.
- [ ] The parent design implications are consistent with the resulting portfolio and indicate what to stop sustaining.
- [ ] Every unprovided datum is marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented figures; RESTRICCIONES respected and their opportunity cost documented.
- [ ] Unresolved tensions are listed as pending decisions for the sponsor.
Expected deliverable: structured document in 7 sections with a zone and net value table per unit and an actionable recommendation per unit, ready for a portfolio decision.
spec-estrategia_asignacion_capital_porta:
[inputs]
- PRESUPUESTO_CAPITAL: {{PRESUPUESTO_CAPITAL}} > Capital available to distribute and its constraints (total, per-unit minimums/maximums, required reserve, already-committed amounts); relative (percentages) if no absolute figure is available
- UNIDADES_PORTAFOLIO: {{UNIDADES_PORTAFOLIO}} > List of businesses or initiatives with their available metrics (return, risk, current allocation, stage, capital already consumed); indicate which metrics are missing
- TESIS_ESTRATEGICA: {{TESIS_ESTRATEGICA}} > Corporate thesis and strategic priority criteria that define fit (target markets, capabilities to build, what is being abandoned)
- COSTO_DE_CAPITAL: {{COSTO_DE_CAPITAL}} > Cost of capital or return threshold (hurdle rate) against which each unit is measured; one global rate or by risk class
- HORIZONTE_Y_RIESGO: {{HORIZONTE_Y_RIESGO}} > Decision horizon and portfolio risk appetite; liquidity or concentration constraints if any
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

--- S | SITUATION ---
I must distribute a constrained capital budget across the units and initiatives of my portfolio. The challenge is not simply choosing the most profitable option, but balancing risk-adjusted return with strategic priority and producing a recommendation that can be defended before the investment committee. Good allocation concentrates capital where advantage is created and frees up resources trapped in what only consumes cash; poor allocation disperses capital and dilutes the corporate thesis. The committee will only approve if the logic is traceable: every dollar moved needs a reason tied to return or fit.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Corporate Strategy and Capital Allocation Director, with experience leading investment committees in multi-business portfolios.

Deliverable: one-page, committee-ready capital allocation recommendation. Steps:
1. Map each unit from {{UNIDADES_PORTAFOLIO}} in an attractiveness matrix (risk-adjusted return, horizon, optionality) vs. strategic fit (alignment with {{TESIS_ESTRATEGICA}}, competitive advantage, synergies).
2. Estimate the risk-adjusted return of each unit against {{COSTO_DE_CAPITAL}} using a transparent framework (ROIC vs. cost of capital, expected NPV or RAROC); state the formula used and tag each figure as [DATA] or [ASSUMPTION].
3. Assign each unit a role: Grow, Maintain, Harvest, Restructure, or Exit, with a one-line justification anchored to its position in the matrix.
4. Build the recommended allocation of {{PRESUPUESTO_CAPITAL}} respecting the total constraint, with an explicit reserve for optionality and the delta versus the current allocation; if the sum does not balance, adjust it and name the cut.
5. Apply a stress test against {{HORIZONTE_Y_RIESGO}}: identify the 2-3 decisions most sensitive to a deterioration of the base scenario and state the threshold (return drop, timeline, or liquidity) that would invalidate each.
6. Close with the allocation thesis (3-4 lines), a per-unit table (role, proposed capital, risk-adjusted return, primary risk), accepted trade-offs, and three questions to answer before approval.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm budget, units, cost of capital, and horizon; if an essential piece of data is missing, request it before continuing and do not invent it.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: position each unit in the matrix and calculate its risk-adjusted return, distinguishing [DATA] from [ASSUMPTION] and naming the formula.
Phase 3 - Roles and allocation: classify by role and propose the capital distribution with reserve and delta vs. current; break ties by strategic fit when attractiveness is equal.
Phase 4 - Stress test and close: test robustness under an adverse scenario, set break thresholds, and consolidate the one-page recommendation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each unit has an explicit role (Grow/Maintain/Harvest/Restructure/Exit) with justification anchored to the matrix.
- [ ] Every return is compared against {{COSTO_DE_CAPITAL}}, states its formula, and is tagged [DATA] or [ASSUMPTION]; no untagged invented figures; zero monetary figures absent from the input.
- [ ] The sum of proposed capital respects {{PRESUPUESTO_CAPITAL}}, includes a reserve for optionality, and explains any cut.
- [ ] The delta versus the current allocation and accepted trade-offs are shown.
- [ ] The stress test names the 2-3 most sensitive decisions with their break thresholds.
- [ ] Closes with the allocation thesis and three actionable questions for the committee.
Expected deliverable: one-page recommendation with allocation thesis, per-unit table, and committee questions, ready to present.
spec-estrategia_estrategia_diversificaci:
[inputs]
- EMPRESA_Y_NEGOCIO_CORE: {{EMPRESA_Y_NEGOCIO_CORE}} > Company, sector, and description of the core business (revenue model and competitive position)
- CAPACIDADES_DISTINTIVAS: {{CAPACIDADES_DISTINTIVAS}} > Capabilities, assets, and resources that give the core its advantage (technology, brand, channel, data, talent, negotiating power)
- OPCIONES_CANDIDATAS: {{OPCIONES_CANDIDATAS}} > Businesses or markets being considered for diversification, with their expected degree of relatedness to the core
