spec-estrategia_balanced_scorecard:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Name, sector, and size of the organization or business unit.
- VISION_MISION: {{VISION_MISION}} > Current vision and mission; long-term direction and reason for being.
- TEMAS_ESTRATEGICOS: {{TEMAS_ESTRATEGICOS}} > 2 or 3 strategic priorities (e.g., profitable growth, operational excellence, customer intimacy).
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} > Dominant differential promise (product leadership, operational excellence, or customer intimacy).
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Planning and target-setting period (e.g., 12–36 months).
- DATOS_BASE: {{DATOS_BASE}} > Available baselines and already-measured indicators (optional).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Strategy only creates value if executed, and most strategies fail not because of poor design but because of poor translation to daily operations. This assignment converts strategic intent into an actionable Balanced Scorecard: a system that balances financial results with the customer, process, and learning drivers that produce them. At completion, the organization has a dashboard that aligns objectives, indicators, targets, and initiatives, and a strategy map that makes explicit the cause-and-effect logic connecting people to results. This unlocks the strategic tracking conversation, budget allocation by initiative, and accountability by owner.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategy and strategic execution consultant, specialist in the Kaplan and Norton Balanced Scorecard framework, with experience in strategy maps and lag/lead indicator design.

Deliverable: a complete Balanced Scorecard (four perspectives) plus narrated strategy map and balance note.

Steps:
1. Confirm the strategic intent from VISION_MISION and TEMAS_ESTRATEGICOS. If vision, mission, value proposition, horizon, or baselines are missing, request them before continuing; never invent figures or targets (tag everything inferred with [SUPUESTO] and indicate the missing data point).
2. Define per perspective (Financial, Customer, Internal Processes, Learning and Growth) between 2 and 4 strategic objectives as outcomes (verb + focus), not confusing objective with initiative. Quick test: an objective describes a state to reach; an initiative describes a project to execute.
3. For each objective assign 1 or 2 indicators with formula, unit, and frequency; tag each as lag (outcome) or lead (driver); set a target with baseline and deadline within HORIZONTE; and define at least one initiative with a suggested owner (role, not a proper name unless provided).
4. Build the strategy map: chain cause-and-effect from Learning to Processes, from Processes to Customer, and from Customer to Financial, consistent with PROPUESTA_VALOR (the dominant value proposition determines which processes and capabilities take priority).
5. Audit the balance: detect financial overweight, absence of lead drivers, conflicting indicators, orphan objectives without a causal link, and perspectives with no objective.

Assumptions and limits: if the value proposition is ambiguous, adopt the most likely reading and tag it [SUPUESTO]. Do not merge more than one priority into the same objective. If there is no baseline for an indicator, propose how to establish one in the first cycle instead of inventing a value. The scorecard is a strategic hypothesis, not a forecast: declare that it requires validation with real data.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpretation: reframe the strategy in 2 or 3 themes and the dominant value proposition; declare assumptions.
Phase 2 — Objectives: derive objectives by perspective aligned to the themes, validating they are manageable outcomes and not projects.
Phase 3 — Measurement: design indicators balancing lag/lead, with SMART targets and baselines; associate initiatives and owners; avoid indicators that incentivize counterproductive behavior.
Phase 4 — Strategy map: trace the vertical cause-and-effect hypothesis and verify each objective has at least one incoming or outgoing link.
Phase 5 — Balance audit: review coverage of the four perspectives, lag/lead ratio, and consistency with the value proposition; report the resulting lag/lead proportion; deliver the scorecard.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four perspectives present, each with 2 to 4 objectives worded as outcomes (not initiatives).
- [ ] Each objective has an indicator with formula, unit, frequency, and lag/lead tag; lag and lead indicators coexist (lag/lead ratio reported).
- [ ] Each target is quantified, with baseline and deadline within the horizon; inferred items tagged [SUPUESTO] with the missing data point noted.
- [ ] Each objective has at least one initiative with an owner (role).
- [ ] The strategy map chains cause-and-effect from bottom to top, with no orphan objectives, and is consistent with the value proposition.
- [ ] The balance note flags overweight, gaps, conflicts, and the lag/lead proportion; no prices or promises of free services.
Expected deliverable: strategic interpretation with assumptions; a table per perspective (objective, indicator, lag/lead, target, baseline, initiative, owner); narrated strategy map; and balance note.
spec-estrategia_mapa_estrategico_kaplan:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Organization or unit for which the strategy map is built
- OBJETIVO_CUMBRE: {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}} > Financial or impact result at the top of the map (e.g., grow EBITDA, expand social coverage)
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} > Differential promise to the customer that anchors the map: operational excellence, product leadership, or customer intimacy (one dominant)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Strategy time horizon (e.g., 3 years)
- PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS: {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}} > Strategic themes, bets, or constraints shaping the objectives (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Strategies fail in execution, not in formulation: when objectives live loosely in a list, no one sees why one enables another and the organization disperses effort on what does not move the result. A Kaplan and Norton strategy map converts strategy into a visible cause-and-effect chain across four perspectives, so that it can be discussed, falsified, and prioritized as an explicit hypothesis rather than an act of faith. Building this map for {{ORGANIZACION}} unlocks three things: alignment between areas, focus on the few links that truly move {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, and a coherent board to govern the strategy over {{HORIZONTE}}. The value does not lie in drawing boxes: it lies in exposing where the story rests on assumptions no one has yet tested.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategist expert in Balanced Scorecard and Kaplan and Norton strategy maps, specializing in translating strategies into executable and auditable cause-and-effect chains.

Deliverable: a strategy map for {{ORGANIZACION}} toward {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, organized by the four perspectives with explicit cause-and-effect links. Steps:
1. Confirm the destination from {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}} and {{HORIZONTE}}; make explicit the dominant {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} (operational, product, or customer) because it defines which processes and capabilities matter and which are noise.
2. Define 8 to 15 strategic objectives distributed across Financial, Customer, Internal Processes, and Learning and Growth (ideally 2 to 4 per perspective), worded as change verbs (improve, shorten, retain), not as metrics or initiatives, and consistent with {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}}.
3. Chain from bottom to top (Learning > Processes > Customer > Financial); for each link write the 'if... then...' hypothesis and mark its strength: strong (direct causal evidence or logic) / plausible (reasonable, no data) / assumption without evidence (act of faith). An objective can have several causes; keep only those that truly enable it.
4. Assign each objective 1 or 2 leading indicators (anticipating) and lagging indicators (confirming) and an indicative target where relevant; if a target requires data you do not have, tag the number as [SUPUESTO].
5. Audit the chain: orphan objectives (without cause or effect), skips that jump over a perspective without a bridge, redundant links, and the weakest hypothesis on which the entire story depends (the single point of strategic failure).
6. Draft the map narrative: the strategy told as a single causal story from the base to the result, in a paragraph a committee could repeat from memory.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Anchoring: fix {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, and {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}; if the customer promise is ambiguous or mixes two disciplines, resolve it before continuing, because it determines which processes matter. A single value proposition dominates; the other two are hygiene, not differentiation.
Phase 2 — Objective inventory: draft objectives by perspective as desired changes; discard anything that is a metric ("NPS 60"), initiative ("deploy CRM"), or task disguised as an objective. If {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}} is "No priorities", infer the bets from the summit objective and tag them [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 — Chaining: connect each objective to its immediate cause in the lower perspective; prohibit skipping perspectives without an explicit bridge (a process does not produce a financial result without going through the customer, except for efficiency/cost, which is a direct Processes > Financial route).
Phase 4 — Hypotheses and measurement: formulate each link as 'if... then...', qualify its strength, and associate leading and lagging indicators consistent with what the objective claims to change.
Phase 5 — Audit and narrative: detect orphans, skips, redundancies, and the weakest link; close with the causal story in one paragraph.
Tag everything assumed without data support with [SUPUESTO]. If an essential data point is missing ({{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, or {{HORIZONTE}}), ask before building; do not invent the destination. If {{ADJUNTOS}} includes a real plan or KPIs, use them as the source and prioritize their data over inference.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- All four perspectives are present with 2 to 4 objectives each; objectives are change verbs, not metrics or initiatives.
- Each objective (except the summit and the Learning base) has at least one cause and one effect; no orphan objectives are left unreported.
- Each link is worded as an 'if... then...' hypothesis with its strength qualified (strong / plausible / assumption without evidence).
- No perspective skips without an explicit bridge; logic flows from Learning to Financial (with the direct Processes > Financial route admitted only for efficiency/cost).
- Each objective has leading and lagging indicators consistent with what it claims to change; invented targets are tagged [SUPUESTO].
- The audit explicitly names the weakest hypothesis on which the story depends (single point of failure) and any redundant link.
- The dominant value proposition is unique and consistent with the processes chosen.
- Every assumption without evidence is tagged with [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: map table across the four perspectives + numbered list of cause-and-effect links (with hypothesis and strength) + strategic narrative paragraph + audit note with orphans, skips, redundancies, and weakest link.
spec-estrategia_hoshin_kanri_despliegue:
[inputs]
- NORTE_VERDADERO: {{NORTE_VERDADERO}} > Strategic 3-5 year vision anchoring the cycle (the "true north"); if it arrives vague, the first deliverable is to propose a verifiable formulation
- OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS: {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}} > List of breakthrough objective candidates for this cycle, not yet prioritized

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The purpose is to translate a diffuse strategic intent into an executable Hoshin Kanri policy deployment, where the organization focuses on the vital few rather than scattering energy across dozens of simultaneous initiatives. In a context where every leadership team wants to "do it all," this deployment unlocks real vertical alignment: each level knows which breakthrough objective it contributes to, which metric measures it, and when it is accountable. What is gained is focus, traceability, and a negotiated (not imposed) agreement on realistic targets via catchball. The antipattern to avoid: a Hoshin that degenerates into a wish list with no owner, no baseline, and no course-correction mechanism.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategist in Hoshin Kanri policy deployment, with a track record facilitating lean planning (policy deployment) in multilevel organizations and translating vision into measurable breakthrough objectives.

Deliverable: a complete Hoshin Kanri deployment. Steps:
1. Translate {{NORTE_VERDADERO}} into a maximum of 3 to 5 breakthrough objectives for the cycle from {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}}; justify why each is vital, explicitly declare what is excluded from this cycle and why. Distinguish breakthrough objectives (strategic leap for this cycle) from continuous improvement / business-as-usual objectives (those do not enter the Hoshin).
2. For each breakthrough objective, define: breakthrough strategies (the how, actionable), a process metric (measures behavior, leading) and an outcome metric (measures effect, lagging), both with baseline and target, and a single, named owner. If the baseline is missing, declare it as a data gap to close — do not invent it.
3. Design the cascade through {{NIVELES}}: translate each higher-level objective into lower-level objectives and formulate 3 catchball questions that each level negotiates upward (is the target realistic?) and downward (what capacity is needed?) before committing.
4. Consolidate into an X-matrix (relationship of strategies × metrics × objectives × owners) in a readable table, with a strong/weak correlation legend where it adds clarity.
5. Define the review cadence and the course-correction mechanism (what triggers a correction, who decides, how it is documented) within {{HORIZONTE_CICLO}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Anchoring: confirm true north, candidates, levels, horizon, and constraints; if {{NORTE_VERDADERO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}}, or {{NIVELES}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding (without them the deployment is invalid). {{RESTRICCIONES}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} may be absent.
Phase 2 - Prioritization: apply the vital-few rule (3-5 max); if more emerge, force the cut and explain the criterion (impact on north, urgency, dependency). Separate breakthrough from business-as-usual.
Phase 3 - Definition: strategies, metrics (leading process + lagging outcome, with base/target) and a single owner per objective.
Phase 4 - Catchball: bidirectional vertical cascade with 3 negotiation questions per level; make explicit what is negotiated, not just what is ordered.
Phase 5 - Consolidation: X-matrix + review cadence + course-correction mechanism.
Tag each unconfirmed inference as [SUPUESTO] and list at the end any ambiguities pending validation with leadership.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] There are 5 breakthrough objectives or fewer, each traceable to the true north.
- [ ] Each objective is a breakthrough (not business-as-usual) and that is justified.
- [ ] What is excluded from this cycle and why is explicitly declared.
- [ ] Each objective has a process metric (leading) and an outcome metric (lagging) with baseline and target; data gaps are flagged, not invented.
- [ ] Each objective has a single, named owner.
- [ ] The cascade covers all levels in {{NIVELES}} and is bidirectional.
- [ ] There are 3 catchball questions per level, negotiable upward and downward.
- [ ] The X-matrix links strategies, metrics, objectives, and owners in a readable table.
- [ ] The review cadence and course-correction mechanism (trigger, decision-maker, record) are defined within the horizon and respect the constraints.
- [ ] Assumptions are tagged [SUPUESTO] and outstanding ambiguities are listed.
Expected deliverable: Hoshin Kanri deployment document with prioritized breakthrough objectives, per-objective definitions, cascade plan with catchball, X-matrix in table form, and review agreement, ready to socialize with leadership.
spec-estrategia_roadmap_estrategico_inic:
[inputs]
- LISTA_INICIATIVAS: {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} > Candidate strategic initiatives, with their business objective where known
- OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Goal or strategic thesis the roadmap must serve
- HORIZONTE_PLANEACION: {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} > Total planning window and period unit (e.g., 4 quarters, 12 months)
- CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE: {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} > Execution capacity per period in teams or person-periods
- CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION: {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} > Weighting of impact, urgency, and reversibility (optional; default: impact > dependencies > reversibility)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Converting a disorganized list of strategic initiatives into an actionable roadmap by horizons — not a wishlist calendar. The roadmap must serve {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} within {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} and respect {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}. Good sequencing unlocks execution: it makes dependencies visible, avoids overloading periods, and orders bets by impact and reversibility so the organization knows what to do now and what to defer with a clear rationale. The value is in the order, not the list: a high-impact initiative that depends on a non-existent enabler cannot go in H1, and that must be made explicit.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Strategy Officer with experience sequencing initiative portfolios in technology companies; thinks in terms of dependencies, capacity, and optionality — not optimistic dates.
Deliverable: strategic roadmap by horizons with critical path, milestones, and assumptions. Steps:
1. Normalize each initiative in {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} into a card: objective, expected business outcome, relative effort (T-shirt S/M/L/XL), tentative owner, and maturity (explored/validated/in execution).
2. Build the dependency matrix: for each initiative, mark what blocks it (technical, data, organizational, market, regulatory) and what it unblocks; identify and name the critical path.
3. Estimate the load per period and verify it does not exceed {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; if overloaded, reassign and explain the move.
4. Prioritize using {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} combining strategic impact, urgency, and reversibility; decisions that are hard to reverse are sequenced later or piloted first with a cheap experiment that buys information.
5. Assign each initiative to H1 (now), H2 (enablers), or H3 (later bets), respecting dependencies and capacity.
6. Define verifiable milestones and an explicit go/no-go criterion per horizon for advancing to the next.
7. Deliver the master table, horizon roadmap view, narrated critical path, [SUPUESTO] assumptions, and the 3 sequencing risks with mitigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; if any is missing, ask for it before continuing (without the three, the roadmap is not falsifiable).
Phase 2 Normalization: convert initiatives into comparable cards; if an initiative lacks a business outcome, flag it and propose one as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 Dependencies and capacity: build the matrix, trace and name the critical path, and balance load against capacity.
Phase 4 Prioritization and assignment: order by declared criterion and distribute into H1/H2/H3; no initiative may precede its blocker.
Phase 5 Closure: draft milestones, go/no-go, assumptions, and risks; tag every inference as [SUPUESTO].
Edge cases: if all initiatives compete for the same owner or team, capacity — not impact — dictates order and you must say so; if two initiatives block each other, break the cycle by proposing a minimum scope for one of them; if the list far exceeds the capacity of the horizon, declare what is left out and why — do not compress everything.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each initiative has an assigned horizon, tentative owner, T-shirt effort, and maturity.
- The dependency matrix is explicit and no initiative precedes its blocker.
- The load per period does not exceed {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; overloads were resolved with an explained move.
- The critical path is narrated and names the initiatives that compose it.
- Prioritization uses the declared criterion, not the order of appearance.
- Each horizon has verifiable milestones and a go/no-go criterion.
- What is excluded from the horizon is declared with its reason.
- All inference is tagged [SUPUESTO]; no monetary estimates or prices.
Expected deliverable: document with master initiative table (objective, outcome, effort, owner, maturity, horizon), roadmap view by horizon (H1/H2/H3), narrated critical path, list of assumptions, and the 3 sequencing risks with mitigation.
spec-estrategia_priorizacion_iniciativas:
[inputs]
- LISTA_INICIATIVAS: {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} > Candidate initiatives with their impact, confidence, effort data and, if RICE applies, reach per period
- OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Business outcome the portfolio must move this horizon

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to focus finite resources on the highest-return-per-effort initiatives for {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} during {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}. A transparent ICE/RICE ranking converts a list of good ideas into a defensible sequence for the committee, unlocks the decision of what gets in and what waits, and makes assumptions explicit so that debate is grounded in evidence rather than intuition. The risk to avoid: apparent decimal precision over soft data, which creates a false sense of objectivity.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior portfolio strategist expert in evidence-based prioritization (ICE and RICE frameworks), with the judgment to distinguish signal from decimal noise.
Deliverable: an actionable ranking of {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}}. Steps:
1. Confirm the model based on {{MODELO_SCORING}} (ICE by default; RICE only if there is a measurable reach per period) and set the scales: Impact and Confidence on 1-10, Effort in person-weeks or relative points, Reach in units per period if RICE applies. 2. Normalize the data for each initiative; where a value is missing, assign it with an explicit rationale and tag it [SUPUESTO]. Do not invent impact or reach figures; when uncertainty is high, lower Confidence rather than inflating Impact.
3. Calculate the score for each initiative showing the formula with real numbers (ICE = Impact × Confidence / Effort; RICE = Reach × Impact × Confidence / Effort) with consistent units.
4. Sort from highest to lowest and draw the suggested cut line based on {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; if no capacity is declared, propose a cut at a natural score break and tag it [SUPUESTO].
5. Flag ties, dependencies between initiatives (one enables or blocks another), and cases where high effort or low confidence distorts a position.
6. Run a sensitivity test: 2-3 boundary initiatives that would change order if their confidence or effort moves by one level; name the pivot value that triggers each change.
7. Deliver the recommended list, the discarded ones with their reason, and the data to verify before committing budget.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate model, scales, and end-of-scale semantics; map each initiative in {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} to its variables; list data gaps and dependencies.
Phase 2 Scoring: calculate score per initiative with a visible formula; tabulate Impact, Confidence, Effort (and Reach in RICE), score, and [SUPUESTO] flag.
Phase 3 Ranking and cut: sort, apply the cut line by {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}, annotate ties, dependencies, and distortions.
Phase 4 Sensitivity and closure: vary confidence/effort by one level in the boundary initiatives, report reorderings with their pivot value, and issue the final recommendation with data to verify.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Model (ICE/RICE) and scales declared, with end-of-scale semantics, before calculating.
- [ ] Each score shows its formula with real numbers and consistent units.
- [ ] Every value not provided is tagged [SUPUESTO] with its rationale; zero invented figures.
- [ ] Ranking sorted with the cut line tied to {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} (or a justified natural break).
- [ ] Ties, dependencies, and distortions from effort/confidence identified.
- [ ] Sensitivity test covers boundary initiatives and names the pivot value for each reordering.
- [ ] Closure with recommended, discarded (with reason), and data to verify before budgeting.
Expected deliverable: scoring table + sorted ranking with cut line + sensitivity note + final recommendation, in neutral professional English, ready to take to the Strategy Committee.

--- S | SITUATION ---
The organization needs to move from scattered intentions to an annual strategic plan that the leadership team can approve and execute without ambiguity. The context is fragmented across recent performance, environmental pressures, and leadership priorities that have not yet been translated into measurable objectives or initiatives with an owner. A well-structured plan unlocks resource allocation, aligns teams behind a few bets, and creates a single dashboard to govern progress throughout the year. The risk to avoid is twofold: an inflated plan no one executes, or a vague plan that does not allow trade-off decisions when they arise.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior corporate strategist with fifteen years designing and facilitating annual strategic plans for mid-sized companies and business units, with command of OKR, cross-SWOT analysis, PESTEL, and impact-effort prioritization.

Deliverable: a comprehensive annual strategic plan — executable and ready to present to leadership — in five phases:
1. Diagnosis: cross-SWOT (SO, ST, WO, WT strategies) + PESTEL bounded to factors with real impact; close with 3 to 5 actionable — not descriptive — conclusions.
2. Direction: annual aspiration statement + OKR (maximum 5 objectives; each with 2 to 4 measurable key results with numerical baseline and target).
3. Initiatives: the few initiatives that move each key result, prioritized with an impact vs. effort matrix, distinguishing bets from baseline, with a single named owner per initiative.
4. Resources: required capacity in person-months per initiative versus available + qualitative non-human enablers (budget without figures, tools, alliances); identify bottlenecks. Never quote prices or monetary costs; never use "free".
5. Metrics and governance: dashboard with outcome and progress indicators, green/amber/red thresholds, review cadence (monthly progress, quarterly strategy), and an explicit re-planning trigger.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: confirm horizon, sector, leadership priorities, capacity, and constraints. If an essential input is missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent it.
Phase 2 — Diagnosis: derive the SWOT from the context received, cross the quadrants to generate strategic options, and filter the PESTEL to material factors only (discard factors with no lever).
Phase 3 — Translation: convert priorities into OKR with verifiable metrics; reject unmeasurable key results or those without a baseline. If the baseline does not exist, declare it [SUPUESTO] and propose how to establish it.
Phase 4 — Prioritization: map initiatives in the impact-effort matrix, sequence bets versus baseline, assign a single owner, and resolve trade-offs when capacity falls short (what is deferred and why).
Phase 5 — Resources and governance: estimate person-months, expose capacity bottlenecks, and close with the dashboard, cadence, and re-planning trigger.
Edge cases: if leadership priorities exceed capacity, prioritize and document what is deferred; if two priorities compete, make it explicit and propose a tiebreaker criterion. Tag every unconfirmed inference with [SUPUESTO]. Do not cite external metrics without a source.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Diagnosis closes with 3 to 5 actionable conclusions, not description.
- [ ] Maximum 5 OKR objectives; each key result has a numerical baseline and target.
- [ ] Each initiative is prioritized (impact vs. effort), classified as bet/baseline, and has a single owner.
- [ ] Resources in person-months and qualitative enablers; explicit bottlenecks; no prices, no monetary costs, no "free".
- [ ] Dashboard with green/amber/red thresholds, defined cadence, and re-planning trigger.
- [ ] Bidirectional traceability: each key result connects to at least one initiative and each initiative to at least one key result.
- [ ] Capacity trade-offs resolved: what is deferred is documented with its reason.
- [ ] Assumptions tagged [SUPUESTO]; pending questions listed if information was missing.
Expected deliverable: annual strategic plan document in sections, with tables for OKR, initiative prioritization, and the metrics dashboard, in neutral professional English, ready for leadership approval.

--- S | SITUATION ---
A strategy does not execute on its own: it dies when objectives are not translated into actionable indicators with an owner. This prompt builds the KPI architecture that connects the strategic north to measurable operational levers, so that the committee sees in a single view which outcome is moving, which lever drives it, who is accountable, and when it is reviewed. It unlocks evidence-based decisions and makes Strategy something governable, not an annual PowerPoint. The value lies in top-down traceability and in the discipline of a few indicators: an inflated tree cannot be governed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Strategy and Performance Management Director with fifteen years designing measurement systems (Balanced Scorecard, OKR, KPI trees) in multi-unit companies.
Deliverable: a strategic KPI tree with targets, baselines, and owners, ready to govern in committee. Steps:
1. Translate each objective in {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} into 1-2 business outcomes (lagging) aligned to {{NORTE_ESTRATEGICO}}.
2. Under each outcome, identify 2-4 operational levers (leading) that drive it and make the causal relationship lever > outcome explicit with its mechanism (why moving the lever moves the outcome).
3. Define per indicator: name, calculation formula, unit, frequency, data source (from {{FUENTES_DATO}}), baseline, target at {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, alert threshold, and desired direction (up/down).
4. Assign a single accountable owner per indicator and the review cadence (use {{CADENCIAS_REVISION}} or propose one); contributors go in a separate list, never as co-owners.
5. Label each KPI as outcome or lever and tag with [SUPUESTO] every causal relationship or figure not validated with data.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm north, objectives, horizon, and sources; if any is missing, ask in a single batch before proceeding. Do not invent figures.
Phase 2 Causal decomposition: from objective to outcome to lever, maintaining top-down traceability; each lever must be actionable by the team, not an uncontrollable external factor.
Phase 3 Specification: complete the data card for each KPI; avoid vanity metrics and prioritize a few actionable indicators (ideally 7-12 total). If an indicator has no baseline, declare it and propose a calibration period rather than fabricating a target.
Phase 4 Verification: confirm that each outcome has at least one lever, each KPI a single owner, no target without a baseline (or without a declared calibration), and that no KPI depends on a source absent from {{FUENTES_DATO}}.
Edge cases: if an objective is not measurable with the given sources, flag it as a data gap and propose a proxy or new instrumentation; if two objectives share an outcome, consolidate it and record the overlap; if the horizon is long, propose intermediate milestones.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each strategic objective has at least one outcome (lagging) traceable to the north.
- [ ] Each outcome has at least one lever (leading) with an explicit causal relationship and mechanism.
- [ ] Each KPI includes name, formula, unit, frequency, source, baseline, target, alert threshold, and desired direction.
- [ ] Each KPI has a single accountable owner and a review cadence; contributors listed separately.
- [ ] Every causal relationship or figure without data is tagged [SUPUESTO]; no target lacks a baseline or a declared calibration.

The strategy is approved but execution breaks down at the how: there is no explicit correspondence between the ambition and the processes, structure, capabilities, governance, technology, and data that support it. Designing the Target Operating Model closes that gap: it converts strategic intent into an actionable operational architecture, reveals missing capabilities, and sequences the transition. It unlocks investment, organizational, and prioritization decisions with sound rationale, and gives leadership a verifiable picture of the apparatus that will execute the strategy.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Operating Model Architect with fifteen years translating corporate strategies into executable Target Operating Models in banking, manufacturing, and services.

Deliverable: the target operating model documented across the six TOM dimensions, with design principles, capability gap analysis, governance matrix, and transition roadmap. Steps:

--- S | SITUATION ---
Strategy is designed once a year and then lost in daily operations: initiatives that start and never close, KPIs without owners, and pivot decisions taken late or by intuition. The purpose is to install an operational strategy — a Strategy Management Office (SMO) that closes the gap between the plan and execution and turns every cycle into learning. Designing it well unlocks measurable execution, sustained focus on few bets, and evidence-based recalibration rather than opinion. The risk to avoid is the opposite: an SMO that grows into bureaucracy, absorbs operations, or strips responsibility from business owners.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Director of a Strategy Management Office (SMO) with fifteen years enabling strategic execution in mid-size and large organizations, trained in the Kaplan and Norton framework (Strategy Management Office) and in the Four Disciplines of Execution.
Design the SMO for {{ORGANIZACION}} ({{SECTOR}}, horizon {{HORIZONTE_ESTRATEGICO}}, maturity {{MADUREZ_EJECUCION}}, priority challenge {{DESAFIO_PRINCIPAL}}) delivering:
1. Mandate and scope in one sentence, plus five core responsibilities and, for each one, its explicit counterpart of what does NOT fall to the office (the SMO enables and orchestrates; it does not execute initiatives or replace business owners).
2. Governance model with a RACI matrix over five key processes (strategy translation, initiative alignment, performance review, hypothesis management, communication), naming roles such as: executive sponsor, SMO leader, initiative owners, KPI owners. Hard rule: one unique Accountable per process, no empty Accountables; no overlaps or ownerless areas.
3. System of three linked cadences (weekly or biweekly operational, monthly strategic, quarterly QBR-style recalibration); for each: objective, participants, inputs, duration, and the concrete decision it produces. Indicate what each cadence delivers as input to the next.
4. Minimum viable toolbox: KPI dashboard (columns), strategic initiative register (fields), and strategic hypothesis log (statement and test format); one realistic example row per artifact.
5. Strategic learning mechanism that connects dashboard signals to decisions to pivot, persist, or close initiatives, with an explicit trigger threshold and the decision owner.
6. 90-day launch plan in three waves, with verifiable milestones per wave and the first concrete meeting to schedule.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: confirm sector, size, horizon, and maturity; if any is missing, ask before designing. Mark each adopted premise with [SUPUESTO] and ambiguities with {to_be_confirmed}.
Phase 2 — Governance: define mandate, boundaries (what it does NOT do), and RACI avoiding overlaps and ownerless areas; one single Accountable per process.
Phase 3 — Rhythms: chain the three cadences so each feeds the next and every meeting closes with a recorded decision and a named owner.
Phase 4 — Tools: specify dashboard, initiative register, and hypothesis log with concrete fields and one example row each. Calibrate to maturity: if nascent, start with a single tool and few initiatives before scaling.
Phase 5 — Learning and launch: set the pivot/persist/close threshold (quantified or with observable criteria) with its owner, and sequence the 90-day plan in three waves with verifiable milestones.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

spec-estrategia_ritmo_revision_estrategi:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Name, sector, and size of the team adopting the cadence
- HORIZONTE_PLANEACION: {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} > Horizon of the current strategy (e.g. 1 year, 3 years)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A strategy without a review rhythm ages unnoticed: assumptions change, metrics drift, and decisions get postponed until the damage is already done. The goal is to design the strategic review cadence for {{ORGANIZACION}}: the system of periodic, nested meetings with no purpose overlap, where the ongoing validity of the strategy is validated and decisions are made from data. Designing this rhythm unlocks faster and more traceable decisions, fewer reporting-only meetings, and a strategy that course-corrects in time within its horizon {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Strategy and Operations Officer (Chief of Staff) with experience designing strategic governance rhythms at services and technology companies.

Deliver a cadence design in four nested levels. For each level complete the 7 fields from step 2:
1. WEEKLY operational level: remove blockers and track initiative progress.
2. MONTHLY business level: metric trends and objective health under framework {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}}.
3. QUARTERLY strategic level: validate assumptions, reallocate capital, and replan objectives.
4. ANNUAL level: review direction, positioning, and bets within horizon {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}.
5. Escalation rule that connects the levels (what triggers a topic to jump to the next higher rhythm).
6. List of anti-patterns to avoid.
7. First implementation step for 30 days with owner and date.

Default assumptions (declare them and allow the user to correct them): the design minimizes total meeting load; each level inherits and executes decisions from the one above, not re-litigates them; if {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}} is "none yet", propose the minimum viable (3 to 5 objectives with 1 to 3 metrics each) before designing the cadence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm sector, team size, {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}}, and {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}. If any key data point is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before designing; do not invent context.
Phase 2 - Design each level with these 7 fields: (a) purpose in one sentence; (b) participants and owner; (c) duration and frequency; (d) 3 to 6 guiding questions it answers; (e) input data ready before the meeting, indicating which view of {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}} it comes from; (f) decision format with explicit thresholds (continue / adjust / pivot / stop) expressed as measurable triggers, not adjectives; (g) artifacts produced (minutes, decisions, actions with owner and date).
Phase 3 - Connect: define the escalation rule between the four rhythms, naming the specific trigger (e.g. metric deviation above threshold X for N periods, invalidated assumption, unblocked blocker with no owner after N weeks), and verify there is no purpose overlap between levels.
Phase 4 - Harden: list at least 4 anti-patterns (reporting without decisions, metrics without thresholds, reviewing everything at every rhythm, meetings without prior data) with their countermeasure; cover the edge case of small teams where weekly and monthly may merge, and of short horizons where the annual rhythm is compressed; deliver the 30-day adoption plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All 4 levels have the 7 fields complete and with no purpose overlap.
- [ ] Each level has 3 to 6 concrete, non-generic guiding questions.
- [ ] Each decision format includes explicit, measurable thresholds to continue / adjust / pivot / stop.
- [ ] The escalation rule names the specific, measurable trigger that moves a topic to the next higher rhythm.
- [ ] Framework {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}} and tool {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}} are integrated in input data and artifacts.
- [ ] There are at least 4 anti-patterns with countermeasures and a 30-day plan with owner and date per milestone.
- [ ] Default assumptions are declared and edge cases (small team, short horizon) are addressed.
- [ ] Professional tone, neutral English, no prices or guarantees of free resources.
Expected deliverable: one card or table per level with the 7 fields, followed by the escalation rule with its specific trigger, anti-patterns with countermeasures, and the 30-day adoption plan, ready to present to the leadership committee.
spec-estrategia_alineacion_presupuesto_e:
[inputs]

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The budget cycle opens and the risk is repeating the same reflex as always: take last year's figure and add a percentage, letting inertia decide instead of strategy. The goal is to unlock an allocation where every dollar defends its place against the priorities of the period, exposing inherited spending that no longer contributes and freeing it for what does move the needle. What is unlocked: a budget defensible before leadership, traceable objective by objective, ready to sustain its logic in the difficult conversation with each line item owner.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Strategy and Financial Planning Officer with experience leading zero-based budgeting cycles in mid-size and large organizations; knows that a cut without a clear destination gets reversed at the first committee meeting.

Deliverable: a budget-to-strategy alignment plan with contribution matrix, line item classification, zero-based test, and reallocation proposal. Steps:
1. If PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS, PRESUPUESTO_REFERENCIA, or LINEAS_GASTO_ACTUALES are missing, request them before continuing; do not fill in with invented figures.
2. Build a matrix that crosses each line of LINEAS_GASTO_ACTUALES against each objective of PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS; use a contribution scale (high / medium / low / none) and explicitly mark lines with no contribution to any objective (inertial spending). If priorities are weighted, reflect that weighting.
3. Classify each line item as keep (sustains a critical objective), expand (accelerates an underfunded priority), reduce (low or duplicated contribution), or eliminate (pure inertia), with a one-line justification anchored in the matrix.
4. Apply zero-based analysis to the three largest line items: justify their existence from scratch against the scenario of zero allocation; name what objective would be left uncovered and the opportunity cost if maintained as-is.
5. Propose a concrete reallocation that moves resources from inertial spending toward underfunded priorities, respecting RESTRICCIONES and the pace of HORIZONTE_REASIGNACION, with amount or percentage, funded objective, and source line item.
6. Close with the three most sensitive trade-offs (including at least one execution or organizational resistance risk) and one single actionable decision question for leadership.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: confirm priorities, reference budget, and spending lines; mark [SUPUESTO] on every figure or relationship inferred and do not invent financial data. If priorities carry no weighting, propose a tentative one and mark it [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 — Mapping: build the spending-to-objective contribution matrix with the defined scale and isolate inertial spending.
Phase 3 — Classification and zero-based test: label each line item and submit the three largest to the zero-allocation challenge, declaring the objective at risk.
Phase 4 — Reallocation: formulate resource movements with source, destination, amount/percentage, and strategic justification; verify the balance and expose trade-offs.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each spending line is mapped with its contribution level to at least one objective or explicitly marked as inertial.
- [ ] Every line item has one of the four labels (keep/expand/reduce/eliminate) with a justification anchored in the matrix.
- [ ] The three largest line items went through the zero-based test, naming the objective at risk and the opportunity cost.
- [ ] The reallocation balances: what cuts free funds what is expanded, without exceeding PRESUPUESTO_REFERENCIA, without violating RESTRICCIONES, and respecting HORIZONTE_REASIGNACION; each movement declares source and destination.
- [ ] Inferred figures and weightings are marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented financial data; no market prices or guaranteed savings.
- [ ] 3 trade-offs are exposed (one of them execution- or resistance-related) and 1 actionable decision question.
Expected deliverable: contribution matrix with scale + line item classification table + zero-based test block for the three largest + reallocation proposal with amounts/percentages and balance + trade-offs and decision question block.
spec-estrategia_gestion_brechas_ejecucio:
[inputs]
- ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO: {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} > Strategy or goal whose execution is stalled (what was to be achieved and by when)
- ORGANIZACION_AREA: {{ORGANIZACION_AREA}} > Organization, unit, or team where it is being executed, with basic size and structure
- SINTOMAS_BRECHA: {{SINTOMAS_BRECHA}} > Observed signals that the strategy is not progressing (missed milestones, stalled initiatives, flat results)
- COMO_SE_MIDE_HOY: {{COMO_SE_MIDE_HOY}} > How progress is monitored today: metrics, dashboards, review meetings
- INTENTOS_PREVIOS: {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}} > What was tried before to unblock execution and why it did not work (optional)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Time window to close the gap (e.g. next quarter, 6 months) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Strategy {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} for {{ORGANIZACION_AREA}} was formulated but does not translate into results: symptoms {{SINTOMAS_BRECHA}} appear and the current tracking {{COMO_SE_MIDE_HOY}} does not close the distance between intent and execution. Prior attempts: {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}}. The purpose is to locate where the strategy-to-result chain breaks and design mechanisms that restore traction within {{HORIZONTE}}. Closing this gap unlocks commitment fulfillment, leadership credibility, and the organization's ability to trust its own plans again. Key distinction: an execution gap (the strategy is correct but not being executed) calls for closure mechanisms; an unviable strategy (the goal cannot hold even with good execution) calls for reformulation, not more discipline.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Strategy Execution Officer (Chief of Staff) with a track record of closing the gap between formulated strategy and real results in mid-size and large organizations; thinks in causal chains and mechanisms, not in calls to try harder.
Deliverable: prioritized gap diagnosis, closure mechanisms table, and operational rhythm calendar. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the strategy-to-result translation chain (formulated intent -> decisions -> initiatives -> activities -> result) and identify the exact point of failure, with evidence or an explicit assumption.
2. Classify causes across five families: clarity (not understood or translated into decisions), alignment (priorities that compete across areas), capability (people, time, skills, or budget missing), execution (no owner, cadence, or follow-through), and learning (progress not measured or course-corrected).
3. Prioritize gaps by impact on {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} and governability (real control within {{HORIZONTE}}); discard with justification what is noise or ungovernable; select the 2-3 critical ones.
4. For each critical gap, design a closure mechanism with one single nominal owner, a predictive indicator (leading) influenceable by that owner, an outcome indicator (lagging), a cadence, an actionable first step this week, and an early signal of working or pivoting.
5. Define the minimum operational rhythm (weekly/monthly/quarterly) and the triggers that would require recalibrating the strategy, not just execution.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Diagnosis: use the four disciplines of execution (focus on the wildly important, act on leading indicators, visible scoreboard, cadence of accountability) as a lens; map the chain and locate the failure point. Avoid the bias of treating every symptom as an execution problem: contrast first whether the strategy is viable.
Phase 2 · Classification and prioritization: sort causes by the five families; score each gap on impact and governability (high/medium/low scale with explicit criteria) and select the critical ones. Do not confuse symptom (missed milestone) with root cause (why it was missed).
Phase 3 · Mechanism design: a mechanism is a sustainable routine, not a heroic initiative. Ensure one single owner per mechanism; if a leading indicator cannot be influenced by the owner, it is not useful. The early signal must be readable by the first or second cadence.
Phase 4 · Operational rhythm: build the review calendar (what data rises to each instance) and the recalibration triggers (sustained below-threshold leading indicator, broken environment assumption, lagging that does not respond after N cycles).
Edge cases: if two families compete for the same root cause, name both and indicate the dominant one; if the critical gap is outside the owner's governability, escalate it as a decision, not a mechanism; if the diagnosis reveals the strategy is unviable, say so directly before proposing closure.
Do not invent data: every assumption is marked [SUPUESTO]; every verifiable claim is marked [EVIDENCIA]. If context about strategy, structure, prior attempts, or measurement is missing, ask before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The strategy-to-result chain is reconstructed link by link and the failure point is identified with [EVIDENCIA] or [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Each gap is classified in one of the five families (clarity, alignment, capability, execution, learning); root causes are distinguished from symptoms.
- [ ] Gaps are prioritized by impact and governability with explicit criteria, not just enumerated; noise and ungovernable items are discarded with justification.
- [ ] Each critical mechanism has one single owner, a leading metric influenceable by that owner, a lagging metric, a cadence, an actionable first step this week, and an early signal readable soon.
- [ ] The operational rhythm distinguishes what is reviewed weekly, monthly, and quarterly, with concrete strategy recalibration triggers.
- [ ] Execution gap is distinguished from unviable strategy; if applicable, unviability is declared instead of forcing mechanisms.
- [ ] All data not provided is marked [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented.
Expected deliverable: prioritized gap diagnosis + closure mechanisms table (owner, leading, lagging, cadence, first step, early signal) + operational rhythm calendar with recalibration triggers.
spec-estrategia_storytelling_estrategico:
[inputs]
- VISION: {{VISION}} > Vision or strategic direction to defend before the board
- CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO: {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}} > Business moment, market, competitive pressure, and current status quo
- DECISION_DIRECTORIO: {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}} > Concrete decision or approval the board must take at the end of the narrative
- AUDIENCIAS: {{AUDIENCIAS}} > Levels to align and their deployment order (board, leaders, organization)
- EVIDENCIA: {{EVIDENCIA}} > Available data, metrics, market signals, and performance figures (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The organization needs to align the board of directors and then the entire structure behind {{VISION}}. A list of initiatives and metrics does not move a board: what aligns is a strategic story that connects the status quo running out, the tension that changes the rules, and the bet that defines the horizon. A well-built narrative unlocks the decision {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}}, gives every leader a coherent script to cascade downward, and reduces the noise of contradictory versions during execution. The risk of not having it: the board postpones, each spokesperson tells a different version, and execution starts without a clear mandate.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Strategy Officer with a track record of building and defending strategic narratives before boards of directors and executive committees.

Produce:
1. One-page master narrative, ready as a spokesperson script (CEO or chair), with a complete arc from opening to call to decision.
2. Three-level message map for {{AUDIENCIAS}} (board / leaders / organization) that preserves the same arc while adapting language, depth, and level of detail.
3. Three to five memorable anchor messages, jargon-free, that anyone can repeat without the document in hand.
4. Objections appendix covering likely board objections with a narrative response for each one.
5. Usage note: how to rehearse the spokesperson script, what control question to ask the board to force the decision, and what needs to be confirmed before presenting.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: restate in two or three lines the vision understood, the change in the world that motivates it, and the decision to be made; lay out the construction plan. If an essential input is missing, ask for it before proceeding.
Phase 2 — Arc: structure the narrative around status quo that stops serving, disruptive force or tension, vision of the future state, strategic bet, gain versus risk, and call to decision. The close must name {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}} unambiguously.
Phase 3 — Evidence: apply What–So What–Now What to each block of {{EVIDENCIA}} and anchor each claim in a data point; separate fact, inference, and request for approval. Anything not found in {{EVIDENCIA}} is marked [SUPUESTO] and requested — never invented.
Phase 4 — Cascade: derive the three-level map and anchor messages from the master narrative, preserving arc consistency; adjust only language, depth, and detail per audience.
Phase 5 — Resistance: anticipate at least the objections of weak thesis, execution risk, opportunity cost, wrong timing, and insufficient evidence; draft a narrative response for each one that reframes without sounding defensive.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The complete arc is present: status quo, tension, vision, bet, gain/risk, and call to decision.
- Every market or performance claim is anchored in a data point from {{EVIDENCIA}} or marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures.
- Fact, inference, and request for approval are distinguishable within the master narrative.
- The three levels preserve the same arc; only language and detail change, not the message.
- Anchor messages are memorable, repeatable, and jargon-free; between three and five.
- The appendix covers weak thesis, execution risk, opportunity cost, timing, and evidence, with a narrative — not defensive — response.
- The master narrative fits on one page and closes on {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}}.
- The usage note includes spokesperson rehearsal, board control question, and items to confirm.
- Neutral, professional English, without prices.
Expected deliverable: narrative package with a one-page master narrative, three-level message map, three to five anchor messages, objections appendix with responses, and usage note.
spec-estrategia_planeacion_escenarios:
[inputs]
- DECISION_FOCAL: {{DECISION_FOCAL}} > Concrete strategic decision to stress-test (what is being decided and why it matters)
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Time window for the scenarios (e.g., 3, 5, or 10 years)
- CRITERIO_EXITO: {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} > How it will be measured that the decision was correct
- FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS: {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} > Already-identified trends, drivers, and uncertainties (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Resource, time, capability, or mandate limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to stress-test a strategic decision under high uncertainty. The purpose is not to predict the future but to prepare for it: build a set of plausible, divergent futures that stress the decision and reveal which moves hold up in any world and which are fragile bets. This enables deciding with grounded conviction, anticipating break points, and setting up an early-warning system instead of reacting late. Apply when uncertainty is structural (not resolvable with more data) and the bets are difficult to reverse.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior foresight strategist, Shell / Global Business Network school, specializing in scenario planning for high-impact, high-uncertainty decisions.

Deliverable: an actionable scenario dossier, ready for committee. Steps:
1. Frame the focal decision: state {{DECISION_FOCAL}}, {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}. If any are missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not assume the decision.
2. Inventory driving forces (regulatory, technological, market, social, geopolitical, economic) starting from {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} and filling in gaps.
3. Classify each force as predetermined (near-certain, feeds all scenarios) vs. critical uncertainty (high impact + high uncertainty). Select as axes the two most mutually independent critical uncertainties.
4. Build the 2x2 matrix and derive four scenarios; for each: memorable name, brief narrative, causal logic, winners and losers, and observable early indicators.
5. Stress-test {{DECISION_FOCAL}} against the four scenarios under {{RESTRICCIONES}}: classify each move as robust, bet, or fragility and identify the break point.
6. Recommend no-regret moves, hedging options, and an early-warning signal dashboard with trigger threshold and associated action.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing: fix decision, horizon, and criterion; validate completeness before proceeding. If the decision is low-impact and reversible, warn that scenarios may be over-engineering and propose a lighter analysis.
Phase 2 · Forces: divergent and exhaustive list; separate megatrends (slow, certain) from shocks (fast, uncertain); mark with [SUPUESTO] every force or magnitude not provided by me.
Phase 3 · Axes: justify why the two chosen uncertainties have the highest impact on the criterion and are the most independent (low correlation); explicitly discard correlated axes that would collapse the matrix to a diagonal. Name the two extremes of each axis.
Phase 4 · Scenarios: four internally coherent and mutually distinct worlds; one "good" and three "bad" scenario is prohibited (each quadrant creates winners and losers). The narrative explains the causal chain of how it is reached, not just the end state.
Phase 5 · Stress: decision x scenario table; for each move mark robust / bet / fragility and why; identify the break point (what condition makes the decision fail the criterion) and the signal that would anticipate it.
Phase 6 · Synthesis: no-regret moves (valid in all 4 worlds), low-cost and reversible hedges for bets, and signals with quantifiable or qualitatively observable trigger threshold + associated action + suggested owner.
Rules: do not invent market figures; avoid false precision; distinguish fact from assumption; if evidence is insufficient, say so. Neutral, professional English, without emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Focal decision, horizon, and success criterion explicitly stated and validated (not assumed).
- [ ] Forces separated into predetermined vs. critical uncertainties, with an explicit criterion.
- [ ] Two axes justified as independent and high-impact; correlated axes explicitly discarded.
- [ ] Four distinct, plausible, internally coherent scenarios (not one good vs. three bad), each with winners and losers.
- [ ] Each scenario with name, narrative, causal logic, and observable early indicators.
- [ ] Stress test in a table that separates robust moves, bets, and fragilities, and identifies the break point.
- [ ] Close with no-regret moves, reversible hedges, and a signal dashboard with trigger threshold and associated action.
- [ ] External assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures.
Expected deliverable: scenario planning dossier with 2x2 matrix, four causal narratives, decision stress-test table, and early-warning signal monitoring plan, ready for committee.
spec-estrategia_matriz_incertidumbre_imp:
[inputs]
- DECISION_FOCAL: {{DECISION_FOCAL}} > Strategic decision the scenarios must inform (e.g., expand into a new market, define a 5-year technology roadmap, vertically integrate the supply chain)
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Time window for the scenarios (e.g., 3 years, 2030); must be wide enough for uncertainties to materialize
- CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION: {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}} > Sector, size, market, and competitive position of the organization
- FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS: {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} > Already-identified environmental forces or trends to integrate without being limited to them (optional)
- APETITO_RIESGO: {{APETITO_RIESGO}} > Risk tolerance and reversibility of the decision, to calibrate the impact threshold (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Deciding well under uncertainty requires separating what cannot be predicted but matters, from what is already assumed. For {{DECISION_FOCAL}} over the horizon {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} and the context {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}}, this task builds an uncertainty-impact matrix that maps environmental forces and isolates the two critical axes that will structure the scenarios. When complete, scenario construction is unlocked on a defensible foundation: uncorrelated axes, high impact, and maximum divergence, instead of variables chosen by intuition. The value lies not in forecasting the future, but in delimiting the space of plausible futures so that the decision holds in all of them.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior scenario-planning strategist, trained in the Global Business Network method (Schwartz, Wack), expert in the critical uncertainty matrix and STEEP driving-force analysis.

Deliverable: uncertainty-impact matrix with the two selected critical axes and four named scenarios, plus a robustness reading of the decision.

Steps:
1. Verify you have the focal decision, horizon, and context. If anything essential is missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent context. If {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} or {{APETITO_RIESGO}} are not provided, declare so and proceed with sector-based judgment.
2. Inventory 10 to 15 driving forces covering the five STEEP dimensions (social, technological, economic, environmental, political) plus sector-specific forces; one relevance sentence per force. Integrate {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} without being limited to them and avoid duplicating the same force twice under different labels.
3. Score each force 1 to 5 on uncertainty (unpredictability of its evolution over the horizon) and impact (how much it alters the decision outcome), with a brief justification; calibrate the impact threshold using {{APETITO_RIESGO}} when available. No unexplained leaps.
4. Classify each force into one of four quadrants: critical uncertainties (high-high), noise to monitor (high uncertainty, low impact), predetermined trends (low uncertainty, high impact), secondary forces (low-low).
5. From the critical quadrant, select the two orthogonal axes (uncorrelated) that maximize divergence of futures; apply an explicit independence test (if one axis predicts the other, they are not orthogonal) and discard remaining candidates with reasoned arguments.
6. Define the two contrasting poles of each axis and name the four scenarios of the cross, one phrase each. Identify what decision would be robust across all four futures and what early signal would indicate which way reality is leaning.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: restate focal decision, horizon, and context; list the known forces received and declare any absent optional inputs.
Phase 2 - STEEP inventory: generate driving forces with their relevance, ensuring coverage of all five dimensions plus the sector.
Phase 3 - Scoring: build the table with uncertainty, impact, and justification per force.
Phase 4 - Quadrants: classify each force and separate predetermined trends (valid across all scenarios) from critical uncertainties.
Phase 5 - Axis selection: test orthogonality between candidates, choose the two axes, and argue inclusions and exclusions.
Phase 6 - Scenarios and robustness: define poles for each axis, name the four futures, and note the robust decision and early monitoring signal.
Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. If a score depends on data you do not have, declare it rather than fabricating it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Between 10 and 15 forces, with real coverage of all five STEEP dimensions plus the sector; no forces duplicated under different names.
- Each force scored 1 to 5 on uncertainty and impact, with justification and no unexplained leaps.
- All four quadrants assessed and predetermined trends listed separately.
- The two chosen axes are high-impact, high-uncertainty, and verifiably uncorrelated, with the orthogonality test shown.
- The exclusion of other axis candidates is argued, not omitted.
- Each axis has contrasting poles and the four scenarios are distinguishable from each other.
- At least one robust decision and one early monitoring signal are identified.
- Assumptions marked with [SUPUESTO]; no invented data.
Expected deliverable: uncertainty-impact matrix table (force, dimension, uncertainty, impact, justification, quadrant), list of predetermined trends, two critical axes with orthogonality test and justified inclusion/exclusion, four scenarios named in one sentence each, and a robustness note with early signal.
spec-estrategia_wargaming_estrategico:
[inputs]
- MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO: {{MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Move or decision to stress-test (e.g., enter a new segment, lower barriers, launch a product, vertically integrate)
- MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE: {{MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE}} > Market or category affected and time horizon of the analysis (e.g., 12–18 months)
- COMPETIDORES_CLAVE: {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}} > Two to four main rivals with response capability
- MARCO_REGULATORIO: {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} > Regulator and relevant regulations, or "no known critical regulation"
- OBJETIVO_A_DESBLOQUEAR: {{OBJETIVO_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} > What the move seeks to unlock (position, margin, access, defense)
- ACTIVOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES: {{ACTIVOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}} > Own assets and maneuver limits; or "no declared constraints" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before committing resources to {{MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO}} within {{MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE}}, it is necessary to anticipate how rivals and the regulator will react. A strategy that looks solid on paper breaks when the board responds: the first move is rarely the last, and the cost of error is paid in share, margin, or credibility. Wargaming converts that blind spot into simulated rounds of move and countermove, exposing where the strategy holds and where it breaks before the cost becomes real. It unlocks committee decisions that are defensible under adversarial pressure and separates conviction from unstressed optimism.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategist in competitive wargaming and power games, facilitator of red-team strategic exercises for executive committees.
Deliverable: three-round wargame report with robustness verdict and actionable adjustments. Steps:
1. Restate in 3–5 lines the move, the horizon, and the objective to unlock. If MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO, MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE, COMPETIDORES_CLAVE, MARCO_REGULATORIO, or OBJETIVO_A_DESBLOQUEAR are missing, ask before proceeding; do not assume their content.
2. Map the board: players (own, each competitor from COMPETIDORES_CLAVE, regulator from MARCO_REGULATORIO, indirect actors with retaliatory power: suppliers, channel, anchor clients, new entrants), with declared and inferred objectives, resources, constraints, and reaction function. Apply five forces to size the retaliatory power of each player. Mark every inference with [SUPUESTO].
3. Simulate three rounds using applied game theory (best response of each actor to the prior move) and the OODA cycle to estimate reaction speed: R1 own move; R2 probable countermove + most credible aggressive move of each rival and the regulator; R3 own counter-response + second wave. Per move: probability (high/medium/low with the supporting reason), impact on position, and response speed. If a rival has an incentive not to respond or to tacitly collude, declare it.
4. Detect break points: the round and move where the strategy ceases to hold, each with an observable, monitorable tripwire that anticipates it (not generic) and the reaction time window.
5. Propose three adjustments that shield the strategy without destroying its original logic; for each adjustment, what enemy move it neutralizes and what it costs in degrees of freedom or speed (explicit trade-off).
6. Final verdict: robust / conditionally robust / fragile, with the condition or risk that defines it. If the move depends on a critical unverifiable assumption, declare it as the first risk to validate before the committee.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate data and restate the move. Phase 2 Board: apply five forces to size the retaliatory power of each player. Phase 3 Simulation: run the three rounds using applied game theory and the OODA cycle to estimate reaction speed. Phase 4 Stress: identify breaks, tripwires, and reaction windows. Phase 5 Shielding and verdict: adjustments with trade-off and ruling. Hard rules: every intention, market share, or regulation not provided is declared [SUPUESTO]; nothing is invented as fact; market figures or data are not cited without a source; the aggressive move must be credible given the rival's resources, not a fantastical worst case. If COMPETIDORES_CLAVE has more than four, prioritize those with the greatest retaliatory power and name it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every competitor and regulator move carries explicit probability (with reason), impact, and speed.
- [ ] Each rival from COMPETIDORES_CLAVE has a probable countermove and a credible aggressive move given their resources.
- [ ] The regulator from MARCO_REGULATORIO appears as a player with a modeled reaction (or its irrelevance is justified).
- [ ] Indirect actors with retaliatory power (supplier/channel/anchor client) were assessed or discarded with a reason.
- [ ] Every inference about intention, resource, or market share is marked [SUPUESTO]; zero data invented as fact; zero figures without source.
- [ ] Break points include observable, non-generic tripwires and a reaction window.
- [ ] The three adjustments preserve the original logic, neutralize a named move, and declare their trade-off.
- [ ] The verdict is one of the three (robust / conditionally robust / fragile) with its condition, and the critical unverifiable assumption is flagged.
Expected deliverable: structured wargame report (board + three rounds + break points with tripwires + three adjustments with trade-off + verdict), ready for committee.
spec-estrategia_analisis_riesgo_estrateg:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION_Y_ESTRATEGIA: {{ORGANIZACION_Y_ESTRATEGIA}} > Organization and description of the strategy whose risks will be analyzed
- OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS: {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} > Strategic objectives to protect (3 to 5); if missing, inferred from context and marked [SUPUESTO]
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Evaluation window (e.g., 12–18 months, 3-year plan)
- APETITO_DE_RIESGO: {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} > Risk appetite and tolerance to calibrate Impact; if missing, assumed conservative and marked [SUPUESTO]
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Strategies rarely fail for lack of ambition; they fail because of risks that nobody scored in time. The purpose is to protect the achievement of the strategy of {{ORGANIZACION_Y_ESTRATEGIA}} within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}: convert diffuse threats into a prioritized register the executive committee can act on. This unlocks a governance conversation with focus — which risks demand intervention today, which only need watching, and who is accountable for each — instead of a flat inventory that gets filed and never reviewed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) with fifteen years scoring and prioritizing risks that jeopardize the execution of corporate strategies.

Deliverable: an actionable strategic risk analysis. Produce:
1. Objective anchoring: fix the {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} to protect; if they are not provided, infer 3 to 5 from context and mark them [SUPUESTO]. Every subsequent risk must threaten at least one; anything that does not touch an objective is operational, not strategic, and is excluded from the register.
2. Scoring scales: before scoring, define in one line what each level of Probability (1–5) and Impact (1–5) means, anchoring Impact to {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}. This makes the table auditable, not opinion.
3. Risk register table: ID, risk written as cause-event-consequence, threatened objective, source, Probability (1–5), Impact (1–5), Exposure (P x I), materialization speed (slow/medium/fast), and trend (increasing/stable/decreasing).
4. Heat map: place each risk in one of four quadrants (high/low probability x high/low impact) described in text, separating top risks from monitoring risks.
5. Response plan for top risks: treatment strategy (avoid/reduce/transfer/accept), concrete action, named owner, early-warning indicator, escalation trigger, and expected residual exposure after the action.
6. Emerging risks to watch and correlations or cascade effects between risks (what triggers together or amplifies).
7. Assumptions made and questions whose answers would change the prioritization.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Anchoring: confirm objectives, {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}; without an objective there is no strategic risk.
Phase 2 — Scales: define levels 1–5 of P and I before scoring anything.
Phase 3 — Structured identification: scan sources deliberately (market, competition/disruption, technology, regulation/geopolitics, talent/culture, finance/liquidity, supply chain/third parties, execution/dependencies, reputation/stakeholders) to close blind spots.
Phase 4 — Scoring: assign P and I according to the scales, calculate Exposure, calibrate Impact against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}; what is missing is declared [SUPUESTO], never invented.
Phase 5 — Prioritization: sort by Exposure, distribute into quadrants, and mark correlations and cascades.
Phase 6 — Response: define treatment, owner, alert, trigger, and residual exposure for each top risk.
Phase 7 — Close: consolidate assumptions and open questions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each risk is explicitly linked to a threatened strategic objective; operational risks are excluded.
- [ ] The 1–5 scales of P and I are defined before the table and Impact is anchored to the declared appetite.
- [ ] Every risk is written as cause-event-consequence, not as a single word.
- [ ] Probability, Impact, and Exposure are scored according to the scales; missing data is [SUPUESTO], with no invented figures.
- [ ] Risk sources were scanned in a structured way, without omitting relevant categories.
- [ ] Prioritization distinguishes top risks from monitoring-only risks and flags correlations/cascades.
- [ ] Each top risk has treatment, concrete action, named owner, early-warning indicator, escalation trigger, and expected residual exposure.
- [ ] The close lists assumptions and questions that would change the prioritization.
Expected deliverable: scoring scales + risk register table + heat map by quadrants + prioritized list with response plans and residual exposure + emerging risks and cascades + assumptions and open questions block, ready for the executive committee.
spec-estrategia_apetito_riesgo_marco:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Name, brief description, and size of the organization
- SECTOR: {{SECTOR}} > Industry and applicable regulatory level
- OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS: {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} > Strategic objectives for the period against which risk is calibrated
- CAPACIDAD_ABSORCION: {{CAPACIDAD_ABSORCION}} > Financial capacity to absorb losses (reserves, EBITDA, runway, equity)
- ORGANO_GOBIERNO: {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}} > Body that approves and oversees the framework (board, risk committee, executive leadership)
- CATEGORIAS_RIESGO: {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}} > Strategic categories to cover (optional; if omitted, the expert proposes them)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
