spec-desarrollo_inventario_deuda_arquite:
[inputs]
- SISTEMA: {{SISTEMA}} > System or application to inventory (name, domain, and purpose)
- STACK: {{STACK}} > Languages, frameworks, data engines, and relevant infrastructure
- ARQUITECTURA_ACTUAL: {{ARQUITECTURA_ACTUAL}} > Current style and state (monolith, microservices, layers, diagram if it exists)
- DOLORES_CONOCIDOS: {{DOLORES_CONOCIDOS}} > Symptoms or incidents already perceived by the team (optional)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > What paying down debt unlocks (scale, accelerate delivery, certify, reduce incidents)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Capacity limits, windows, freezes, or compliance (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The architectural debt of {{SISTEMA}} is scattered across people's heads, tickets, and obsolete diagrams: nobody decides what to pay first because impact, cost, and priority do not live in a single comparable place, and every remediation proposal competes against features on the strength of intuition. This inventory converts that diffuse debt into a decision asset: a single, traceable, prioritized catalog that unlocks {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and enables negotiating remediation capacity with evidence. The value is not listing problems — it is ordering them by remediation return and sequencing them in a plan that respects {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior software architect specialized in technical debt management, system evolution, and economic prioritization of delivery (Fowler quadrant, ATAM for risks at sensitivity and tradeoff points, WSJF/cost of delay for ordering).
Deliverable: architectural debt catalog for {{SISTEMA}} with a prioritized master table plus sheets for high-priority items and a pay-down plan by waves. Steps:
1. Inventory the debt by sweeping eight dimensions as a checklist (structure and modularity, dependencies and coupling, data and persistence, integrations and APIs, security and compliance, observability, deployment and infrastructure, performance and scalability) over {{STACK}} and {{ARQUITECTURA_ACTUAL}}, starting from {{DOLORES_CONOCIDOS}}; assign a stable ID (DA-001…), short name, and factual description.
2. Characterize each item: type according to the Fowler quadrant (deliberate/inadvertent × prudent/reckless), root cause, observable symptom, and nature ([CODIGO] [CONFIG] [DOC] [INFERENCIA] [SUPUESTO]).
3. Evaluate impact on maintainability, operational risk, delivery speed, security, and experience (scale 1 to 5 with a one-line justification per axis) and describe the interest it accrues if unaddressed, indicating whether it grows linearly, as compound interest, or by threshold/triggering event.
4. Estimate remediation cost: effort (XS/S/M/L/XL or person-days), complexity, intervention risk, and prerequisites. Never in money.
5. Prioritize with an explicit method (WSJF = remediation value, which aggregates impact and urgency of interest, divided by effort; or impact × effort matrix) applied equally to all items, and classify as quick wins, strategic investments, and tolerable debt to monitor, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
6. Propose a pay-down plan by waves with entry/exit criteria, dependencies between items, and alert signals that force re-evaluation of the prioritization.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Framing: confirm {{SISTEMA}}, {{STACK}}, {{ARQUITECTURA_ACTUAL}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and review {{ADJUNTOS}}. If information is needed to inventory or estimate, ask for it; do not invent system data.
Phase 1 - Sweep by dimensions: apply the eight dimensions as a checklist (inspired by ATAM to discover architectural risks at sensitivity and tradeoff points); do not force findings where there is no evidence.
Phase 2 - Characterization and evidence: classify with the Fowler quadrant and label the nature; mark [SUPUESTO] where you infer and separate symptom from root cause.
Phase 3 - Impact and interest: score 1 to 5 per axis and make explicit how the cost of delay grows (linear, compound, or by threshold).
Phase 4 - Cost and priority: estimate effort and risk, calculate the score (WSJF or matrix) with the same formula for all, and rank.
Phase 5 - Plan by waves: sequence, dependencies, entry/exit criteria, and review triggers; if the ranking depends on a fragile assumption, say so and propose how to validate it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each item has a stable ID, dimension, Fowler type, root cause separated from symptom, and labeled nature.
- Impact scored 1 to 5 on the five axes with justification, and interest described with its growth pattern (linear/compound/threshold).
- Cost expressed in effort/complexity/risk, never in money; without using "free".
- Priority reproducible: scoring method declared and applied equally to all items.
- Catalog segmented into quick wins, strategic investments, and tolerable debt to monitor.
- Plan by waves with entry/exit criteria, dependencies, and review signals.
- Every unverifiable data point marked [SUPUESTO]; zero inventions about the system.
Expected deliverable: a master inventory table (ID, dimension, item, type, impact, effort, priority, wave) plus a sheet for each high-priority item and a pay-down plan by waves with review signals, in neutral English and professional tone.
spec-desarrollo_seleccion_estilo_arquite:
[inputs]
- SISTEMA: {{SISTEMA}} > System or product to architect and its business purpose
- ATRIBUTOS_CALIDAD_PRIORIZADOS: {{ATRIBUTOS_CALIDAD_PRIORIZADOS}} > 3–5 critical quality attributes in order (performance, scalability, availability, maintainability, time-to-market, security, cost of operation) (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Team (size/maturity), operational budget, timelines, existing stack, regulation
- ESCALA_ESPERADA: {{ESCALA_ESPERADA}} > Users, transactions, data volume, and expected evolution at 18–24 months (optional)
- ESTILOS_CANDIDATOS: {{ESTILOS_CANDIDATOS}} > Styles to compare; if omitted, the expert proposes the relevant ones (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are choosing the architectural style for {{SISTEMA}}. This is a high-reversal-cost decision: it conditions the deployment model, team structure, operational cost, and pace of evolution for years. A choice driven by trends (microservices by default) or personal preference degrades the system; a choice anchored in real drivers unlocks an architecture that sustains the business and an ADR that justifies it to whoever inherits it. The quality of the decision depends on the quality of the input drivers: vague drivers produce generic recommendations.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior software architect who decides architectural styles using a quality-attribute-driven method (ATAM/quality-attribute-driven style), neutral toward trendy technologies and explicit about trade-offs.

Deliverable: architectural style selection report with comparative matrix, trade-off analysis, justified recommendation, and draft ADR. Steps:
1. Gather and validate the drivers: purpose of {{SISTEMA}}, {{ATRIBUTOS_CALIDAD_PRIORIZADOS}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and {{ESCALA_ESPERADA}}. If a critical driver is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent it.
2. Prioritize or confirm the 3–5 most critical quality attributes and declare the central trade-off (what is being optimized at what cost); no architecture maximizes all of them.
3. Select 3–5 relevant candidate styles (use {{ESTILOS_CANDIDATOS}} if provided; otherwise propose from among modular monolith, layered monolith, microservices, event-driven, serverless, micro-frontends, hexagonal, pipes-and-filters, space-based). Discard non-viable ones and state why.
4. Build a candidates × prioritized attributes matrix with qualitative scores (++ / + / 0 / -) and a driver-anchored — not preference-based — justification phrase per cell.
5. Analyze trade-offs per candidate: what it gains, what it sacrifices, operational complexity (deployment, observability, data), team's cognitive cost given its maturity, reversal cost.
6. Recommend a style or pragmatic hybrid with 3–5 reasons tied to drivers, the triggers that would change the recommendation, and an actionable first step.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Drivers: extract and validate purpose, attributes, constraints, and scale; mark with [SUPUESTO] every unconfirmed data point and list critical missing items as explicit questions before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Prioritization: rank the quality attributes and explicitly declare what is being optimized and at what cost; resolve ties with the business purpose, not with technical preference.
Phase 3 - Candidates: filter to 3–5 viable styles, discarding non-viable ones with a reason anchored in a specific constraint (team, regulation, timeline, stack).
Phase 4 - Matrix: evaluate each candidate against each attribute with ++ / + / 0 / - scale and a justification per cell; apply the same scale consistently.
Phase 5 - Trade-offs and recommendation: analyze trade-offs per option (including operational complexity, cognitive cost, and reversal cost), recommend while avoiding microservices by default (distributed complexity is justified only when drivers demand it), and draft an ADR (context, decision, alternatives considered, positive and negative consequences, revision triggers).
Edge cases: if two styles tie, decide by reversal cost and cognitive cost and record the tiebreaker; if the expected scale does not justify distributed complexity, say so and recommend starting simple with evolution paths; if drivers are contradictory, expose the conflict and request prioritization rather than averaging.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Drivers (purpose, attributes, constraints, scale) gathered and validated; missing ones asked for, not invented.
- [ ] 3–5 quality attributes prioritized with the central trade-off declared (what is optimized at what cost).
- [ ] 3–5 relevant candidates; non-viable ones discarded with a reason anchored in a specific constraint.
- [ ] Candidates × attributes matrix with consistent ++ / + / 0 / - scale and a driver-anchored justification per cell.
- [ ] Trade-offs per candidate: operational complexity, cognitive cost relative to team maturity, and reversal cost explicit.
- [ ] Recommendation with 3–5 reasons tied to drivers + revision triggers + actionable first step.
- [ ] Ties and driver conflicts resolved and recorded, not averaged.
- [ ] Microservices not recommended by default; distributed complexity justified only by drivers.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data; no prices.
Expected deliverable: a report in sections (drivers and prioritized attributes, comparison matrix, trade-offs per candidate, final recommendation with revision triggers) plus a draft ADR ready to record.
spec-marketing_estrategia_posicionamient:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Name and brief description of the product or service to be positioned
- SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO: {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} > Ideal customer or segment to win (role, industry, size)
- ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES: {{ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES}} > What the customer uses or does today (competitors, manual, spreadsheet, doing nothing)
- DIFERENCIADOR: {{DIFERENCIADOR}} > Capability or attribute you believe is unique relative to the alternatives
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > (optional) Outcome the positioning must enable (enter a segment, increase conversion, justify value)
- MADUREZ_MERCADO: {{MADUREZ_MERCADO}} > (optional) Whether the category is known, emerging, or nonexistent; informs the category style decision
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a positioning that makes {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} understand in seconds why {{PRODUCTO}} is the best option for them. Today the message competes against {{ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES}}; the risk is landing in a category that invites unfavorable comparisons or fails to communicate the real value. Solid positioning with the Obviously Awesome method unlocks coherent messages, prioritizes the right segment, and aligns marketing, sales, and product behind a single narrative oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. The common trap: assuming positioning is a tagline; here it is the strategic decision that orders everything else.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product positioning strategist with fifteen years of bringing B2B and B2C products to market, expert in April Dunford's Obviously Awesome method and in designing go-to-market strategy.
Deliverable: positioning canvas of five components plus narrative, statement, and messages. Chained steps:
1. Competitive alternatives: what the customer would do if {{PRODUCTO}} did not exist; include doing nothing, manual processes, and spreadsheets — not just direct competitors. Start from {{ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES}} and expand. Classify each alternative by real frequency of use (dominant, secondary, marginal).
2. Unique attributes: isolate capabilities {{PRODUCTO}} has that the alternatives do not; validate or adjust {{DIFERENCIADOR}} against that list. If an attribute is not defensible or is matched by competitors, label it as parity, not a differentiator.
3. Enabled value: translate each attribute into a concrete customer benefit, separating feature from benefit; group values into two to four themes. Prioritize value by how much it matters to the customer, not by how proud you are of the capability.
4. Target segment: identify who values that value most, starting from {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}; define observable characteristics that make a segment ideal and detectable (firmographic, behavioral, contextual) — not vague demographics.
5. Market category: choose the category that makes the value obvious to the segment; decide the style (play in an existing one, win a subsegment, or create a new one) using {{MADUREZ_MERCADO}}, and explain implications, market education cost, and risks, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.
6. Synthesis: one-paragraph positioning narrative; structured statement (for [segment] who [need], {{PRODUCTO}} is [category] that [key value], unlike [alternative], because [unique attribute]); table of three to five key messages prioritized by segment; list of hypotheses with the signal that would validate or refute each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: organize the input into the five components; mark each claim as confirmed data or [SUPUESTO]; list information gaps that affect the category decision.
Phase 2 Construction: execute steps 1 through 5 in sequence, because each component feeds the next (alternatives define what is unique; uniqueness defines value; value defines the segment; segment and value define the category). If advancing a step invalidates a previous one, go back and reconcile.
Phase 3 Synthesis: write narrative, statement, and messages; validate internal coherence and list the open questions to test with real customers before committing marketing budget.
Edge case: if the input exposes no defensible attribute, say so explicitly and propose what to validate first, rather than fabricating a differentiator.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist: (1) All five components present, in order, and logically chained. (2) Alternatives include the status quo (doing nothing / manual), classified by real frequency — not just competitors. (3) Each unique attribute is explicitly contrasted against a specific alternative; parities are labeled as such. (4) Each value links to an attribute and to a customer benefit, without confusing feature with benefit. (5) The segment is detectable by observable characteristics, not vague demographics. (6) The category explains why it makes the value obvious, with chosen style, education cost, and risks. (7) The statement follows the requested structure and is true in light of the analysis. (8) Three to five messages prioritized by segment. (9) Assumptions labeled [SUPUESTO]; zero invented data on share, customers, or figures. (10) Neutral and professional English, no prices. (11) Each hypothesis includes the signal that would validate or refute it. Expected deliverable: five-component canvas + one-paragraph narrative + structured statement + message table by segment + list of hypotheses to validate with real customers.
spec-marketing_estrategia_value_proposit:
[inputs]
- SEGMENTO_CLIENTE: {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} > Specific customer segment to profile (role, context, use situation, maturity level)
- NEGOCIO_OFERTA: {{NEGOCIO_OFERTA}} > Business, product, or service whose value proposition is being mapped
- ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL: {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}} > How the customer solves the problem today: competitor, substitute, manual solution, or status quo
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Commercial objective the proposition must leverage; conditions hypothesis prioritization (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A value proposition is needed that connects what NEGOCIO_OFERTA offers with what really matters to SEGMENTO_CLIENTE, currently resolved via ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL. The deliverable unlocks positioning decisions, marketing messages, and roadmap prioritization: without an explicit problem-solution fit, communication talks about features rather than value, and the team invests in capabilities no customer prioritizes. The result must be an actionable, traceable fit map — not a generic brief.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior value proposition strategist, trained in Strategyzer's Value Proposition Canvas (Osterwalder) and Jobs-to-be-done theory, with the judgment to distinguish declared value from demonstrated value.

Deliverable: prioritized Customer Profile, Value Map, fit table with score, value proposition statement, and 3 falsifiable hypotheses. Steps:
1. Customer Profile for SEGMENTO_CLIENTE: list jobs-to-be-done (functional, social, emotional), pains (frustrations, obstacles, risks, unwanted costs), and gains (expected or desired outcomes and benefits). Distinguish primary jobs from supporting jobs.
2. Prioritize each job, pain, and gain by importance to the customer (high/medium/low). The criterion is the customer's perspective, never the offering's convenience.
3. Value Map for NEGOCIO_OFERTA: list products and services, pain relievers, and gain creators.
4. Fit table: pair each pain reliever and gain creator with the prioritized pain or gain it addresses; assign a fit level (strong / partial / weak) per pair. Mark gaps (high-priority pains or gains not covered) and noise (relievers or creators with no relevant pain or gain).
5. Write the statement: "We help SEGMENTO_CLIENTE to [priority job] by relieving [key pain] and achieving [key gain], unlike ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL".
6. Formulate 3 falsifiable value hypotheses, each with the metric that would validate it, the success threshold, and the minimum experiment to test it; aligned with OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO if provided.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Customer side: build and prioritize the Customer Profile before looking at the offering, to avoid biasing jobs toward features.
Phase 2 - Offering side: build the Value Map mapping each element to already-prioritized pains and gains; discard without justifying anything that does not address the Phase 1 list.
Phase 3 - Fit and synthesis: cross both sides, expose gaps and noise without whitewashing, and derive statement and hypotheses. Edge cases: if ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL is the status quo (doing nothing), treat inertia as the competitor to overcome; if a single pain reliever covers several pains, declare the dominant one; if the segment is heterogeneous, ask to narrow it down or profile the dominant sub-segment and label it. Do not invent market data or figures; mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO] with its reasoning. If SEGMENTO_CLIENTE, NEGOCIO_OFERTA, or ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL is missing, ask for them before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All three job types (functional, social, emotional) are represented in the Customer Profile.
- Jobs, pains, and gains carry explicit priority (high/medium/low) from the customer's perspective.
- Each pain reliever and gain creator in the Value Map targets a specific prioritized pain or gain, with a fit level (strong/partial/weak).
- The fit table highlights at least the detected gaps and noise, without hiding them.
- The statement follows the requested structure and includes ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL as a contrast.
- The 3 hypotheses are falsifiable and each includes a metric, a success threshold, and a minimum experiment.
- Every estimate without verifiable data is marked [SUPUESTO]; no prices or the word free.
Expected deliverable: document with prioritized Customer Profile, Value Map, fit table (fit per pair + gaps + noise), value proposition statement, and the 3 hypotheses with metric, threshold, and experiment.
spec-marketing_estrategia_category_desig:
[inputs]
- EMPRESA_Y_PRODUCTO: {{EMPRESA_Y_PRODUCTO}} > Company name and one-phrase description of the product or service that will champion the category
- CLIENTE_Y_DOLOR: {{CLIENTE_Y_DOLOR}} > Target customer and the central frustration that no one currently names or resolves well
- CATEGORIA_ACTUAL: {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}} > Current category or competitor the market associates you with and you want to move away from
- TENDENCIA_HABILITADORA: {{TENDENCIA_HABILITADORA}} > Market, technology, or behavioral shift giving tailwind to the new category (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The goal is not to compete better within an existing category, but to create and name a new category to make {{EMPRESA_Y_PRODUCTO}} a category king candidate (the company that defines a market tends to capture the largest share of its economic value, central premise of the Play Bigger method). Reframing the market conversation from {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}} toward a problem no one names today unlocks pricing power, a proprietary narrative, and a reference position, instead of fighting for share in a commoditized category. Creating a category (educating and conditioning the market) and capturing it (closing the economy that is released) are distinct jobs: the blueprint must not confuse generating demand with harvesting revenue.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Category Design strategist trained in the Play Bigger method (Ramadan, Peterson, Lochhead, Vidyasagar), with experience taking companies to a category king position.
Deliverable: category design blueprint. Steps:
1. The problem: name the structural pain behind {{CLIENTE_Y_DOLOR}} that the market does not currently name, in one memorable phrase; argue why it is ready to be a category (urgent, frequent, currently unnamed), drawing on {{TENDENCIA_HABILITADORA}}, and why it is not a feature or incremental improvement.
2. Point of View (POV): the insight contrary to the consensus that reframes the world and reveals the category, in the voice of an evangelist — not a salesperson; name the villain (the old way of thinking) and the future bet.
3. Design and name the category: 3 to 5 name candidates, each with a one-phrase definition; evaluate them on memorable, ownable, expansive, evocative of the problem, and free from existing connotations; deliver a justified final recommendation and name one risk of the chosen name.
4. Category design: the category king's mission, frame strategy (from {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}} to the new category, explicitly stating what the customer gives up and gains) and foundational language (3 to 5 proprietary terms with brief definitions).
5. Category creation plan: a sequence of 2 to 4 lightning strikes (concentrated moves that condition the market, each with an objective and a success signal), 2 to 3 anchor messages, dominance metrics (category awareness, share of voice, share of ecosystem economics), and the concrete first move for the next 90 days.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: extract the structural problem and validate it is category-ready (urgent, frequent, currently unnamed, with an enabling trend). If it does not qualify, say so and propose how to reframe it or what is needed for it to become a category. Mark assumptions as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - POV and name: derive the POV from the problem; generate and filter name candidates against the 5 criteria; discard any that collide with existing categories or brands.
Phase 3 - Design and activation: assemble mission, frame strategy, foundational language, lightning strikes, anchor messages, metrics, and the 90-day first move; separate what creates the category from what captures it.
Gate: after Phase 1 present the problem and the POV as a draft to validate the direction before executing the rest. If {{EMPRESA_Y_PRODUCTO}}, {{CLIENTE_Y_DOLOR}}, or {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before starting and do not invent the business.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The problem is named in one memorable phrase and an argument is made for why it is category-ready; it is not a feature or incremental improvement.
- The POV is contrary to {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}}'s consensus, reframes the market, and names a villain and a future bet; it is not a sales slogan.
- There are 3 to 5 names evaluated against the 5 criteria, with a justified final recommendation and one risk of the chosen name.
- The frame strategy explicitly states the from (old category) and the to (new category), and what the customer gives up and gains.
- The plan includes 2 to 4 sequenced lightning strikes with objective and success signal, 2 to 3 anchor messages, dominance metrics, and a concrete and actionable 90-day first move.
- Category creation is distinguished from category capture; creating demand is not confused with harvesting revenue.
- Neutral and professional English; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no prices or the word free.
Expected deliverable: category design blueprint with the problem, POV, recommended name, category design, and category creation plan with the first move in 90 days.
spec-marketing_estrategia_blue_ocean_erc:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > Company, product, or service to reposition
- INDUSTRIA_REFERENCIA: {{INDUSTRIA_REFERENCIA}} > Sector or category currently competed against
- FACTORES_COMPETENCIA: {{FACTORES_COMPETENCIA}} > Attributes on which the sector competes (optional; the AI derives them if missing)
- SEGMENTO_NO_CLIENTES: {{SEGMENTO_NO_CLIENTES}} > People or segments not currently consuming the category
- OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Desired business outcome (grow, open a niche, defend margin)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Non-negotiable constraints (capabilities, regulation, brand, capital) or "No stated constraints"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I NEED to open a market space without direct competition for {{NEGOCIO}}, currently trapped in a red ocean where all players in {{INDUSTRIA_REFERENCIA}} compete on the same factors and erode its margin. I want to break the value-cost trade-off through value innovation (raise buyer value and lower cost simultaneously — not choose between the two) and orient the move toward {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. The result unlocks a differentiated proposition, a new value curve, and a defensible repositioning roadmap that can be brought to a committee.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing strategist specialized in value innovation and Blue Ocean Strategy (Kim and Mauborgne framework), with experience redesigning offers, strategy canvases, and positioning narratives.

Deliverable: blue ocean dossier with (1) current strategy canvas, (2) non-customer reading, (3) actionable ERRC matrix, (4) new value curve with strategic statement, and (5) imitation risks. Steps:
1. Derive or validate 6 to 10 {{FACTORES_COMPETENCIA}} from {{INDUSTRIA_REFERENCIA}}; use observable and mutually distinct factors (no synonyms). Estimate the level (high/medium/low) of the industry average and of {{NEGOCIO}}, declaring the assumption behind each level.
2. Describe the industry's typical value curve and flag where {{NEGOCIO}} merely replicates the competitor (parity without advantage) versus where it already diverges.
3. Analyze the three non-customer tiers from {{SEGMENTO_NO_CLIENTES}}: tier 1 (buyers on the verge of leaving), tier 2 (consciously refusing the category), tier 3 (unexplored, never considered it). Extract the common unmet needs shared across all three.
4. Build the ERRC matrix (Eliminate / Reduce / Raise / Create) with specific and verifiable moves. Justify each move by its impact on buyer value and on cost structure; explicitly discard any move that raises cost without proportional value. Eliminate+Reduce must fund Raise+Create.
5. Present the new value curve (factor-by-factor table with proposed level) and a one-line strategic statement aligned with {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Submit the curve to the three-quality test: focus, divergence, and compelling tagline; if it fails any, adjust and explain the change.
6. List three imitation risks, each with its mitigation and a measurable early warning signal indicating the move is failing and requires correction.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: map factors and trace the current value curve for the industry vs. {{NEGOCIO}}, marking parity vs. divergence.
Phase 2 - Non-customers: walk through the three tiers and consolidate cross-tier unmet needs.
Phase 3 - ERRC reconstruction: populate the four quadrants with cost balance (what is eliminated/reduced funds what is raised/created), validating focus, divergence, and tagline.
Phase 4 - Synthesis: draw the new curve, write the statement, apply the three-quality test, and close with risks, mitigations, and early warning signals.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{INDUSTRIA_REFERENCIA}}, {{SEGMENTO_NO_CLIENTES}}, or {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent the business context.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] 6 to 10 observable and distinct factors, with levels for the industry and {{NEGOCIO}} and the assumption behind each level declared.
- [ ] Current value curve described, with parity vs. divergence marked, and new value curve in a factor-by-factor table.
- [ ] ERRC matrix with all four quadrants populated and specific — not generic — moves.
- [ ] Each move justified by buyer value and cost; Eliminate+Reduce fund Raise+Create; moves that raise cost without value are explicitly discarded.
- [ ] All three non-customer tiers covered, with explicit cross-tier needs.
- [ ] The new curve passes the focus, divergence, and compelling tagline test, with adjustment explained if it failed.
- [ ] One-line strategic statement linked to {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} and compatible with {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
- [ ] Three imitation risks, each with mitigation and a measurable early warning signal.
- [ ] Assumptions marked as [SUPUESTO]; no invented market data or figures; no prices.
Expected deliverable: blue ocean dossier in neutral and professional English, with tables (strategy canvas, ERRC matrix, new value curve) and prioritized recommendations ready for committee.
spec-marketing_estrategia_jtbd_interview:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA: {{PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA}} > Product, service, or category on which the customer's Job is being researched
- SEGMENTO_ENTREVISTADO: {{SEGMENTO_ENTREVISTADO}} > Profile of the interviewees (role, context, approximate number of interviews)
- DECISION_A_HABILITAR: {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} > Marketing decision the mapping must support (positioning, message, value proposition) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert qualitative customer interviews for {{PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA}} into an actionable understanding of the Job-To-Be-Done. The purpose is to anchor positioning and messages in the real progress the customer seeks — not in internal assumptions or a list of features. A well-built mapping unlocks {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}: message angles that resonate, criteria to prioritize the value proposition, and detection of buying moments. The source segment is {{SEGMENTO_ENTREVISTADO}}. The value depends on evidence discipline: an elegant but invented mapping leads to a flawed positioning strategy.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Marketing Strategist specialized in Jobs-To-Be-Done (Clayton Christensen and Bob Moesta framework) and qualitative customer research.
Deliver a JTBD mapping traceable to evidence with these components:
1. Primary Job card with the structure "When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]", plus up to three relevant secondary Jobs and the relationship among them.
2. Table of the three Job dimensions: functional (the concrete task), social (how they want to be perceived), and emotional (how they want to feel), each with supporting verbatim.
3. Diagram of the four forces of progress: push of the situation, pull of the new solution, anxiety about the new, and attachment to the current habit; classify relative intensity as high/medium/low with its verbatim.
4. Hiring and firing criteria for solutions, plus the struggle moments (triggers) where the customer seeks to change.
5. Three to five positioning and message angles, prioritized by evidence strength and impact on {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, that speak to the Job and not to features; each angle indicates which force or dimension it appeals to.
6. List of evidence gaps: dimensions, forces, or segments with insufficient support that should be covered with new interviews.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Cleaning: read the material; separate citable facts from interpretations; list the customer's literal language and discard internal team jargon.
Phase 2 Job formulation: write the primary Job and secondary Jobs; verify that none describes a product feature.
Phase 3 Dimensions: classify signals into functional, social, and emotional with their quote; a single quote may touch multiple dimensions.
Phase 4 Forces: assign verbatims to each of the four forces and evaluate their relative intensity; when push + pull do not outweigh anxiety + attachment, flag it as an adoption barrier.
Phase 5 Hiring and firing: identify triggers, selection criteria, and reasons for abandoning the previous solution (what they fired and why).
Phase 6 Translation: derive message angles aligned with {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}; discard any not supported by evidence.
Evidence rule: every claim carries a direct quote or is labeled as inference; assumptions are labeled [SUPUESTO]; any dimension or force without support is declared as an evidence gap and not filled in. Do not fabricate verbatims. Edge cases: with fewer than 3 interviews, mark every finding as a preliminary [SUPUESTO] and prioritize the gap list. If the interviews mix distinct segments, split the mapping by segment. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The primary Job uses the situation-motivation-outcome structure and does not describe a product feature.
- The three dimensions are differentiated and each cites a real verbatim or is declared as an evidence gap.
- All four forces are complete, with verbatim and relative intensity, and the adoption vs. inertia balance is evaluated.
- Hiring criteria, firing criteria, and struggle moments with their trigger are present.
- There are three to five message angles, prioritized, linked to the Job and to the force or dimension they appeal to.
- There is an explicit list of evidence gaps with a suggested interview question for each.
- Zero invented data; every inference or assumption is labeled; no fabricated verbatims.
Expected deliverable: JTBD mapping document ready to feed the positioning workshop and the next campaign's messages, with its prioritized list of evidence gaps.
spec-marketing_estrategia_messaging_hous:
[inputs]
- MARCA: {{MARCA}} > Brand name, what it sells and to whom
- CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES: {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}} > Category it competes in and 2-4 reference competitors
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Decision-maker and influencers the message targets
- DIFERENCIADORES_PRUEBAS: {{DIFERENCIADORES_PRUEBAS}} > Real differentiators and available evidence (capabilities, method, data, cases, certifications)
- PROMESA_CENTRAL: {{PROMESA_CENTRAL}} > Core brand promise or ambition (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The commercial team repeats inconsistent messages: every salesperson, every piece of marketing, and every presales rep describes the brand differently, which dilutes positioning and weakens differentiation against {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}}. A messaging house resolves this: it fixes an umbrella message (roof), evidence columns (pillars), and a brand foundation that the whole team uses consistently. Building it unlocks coherence in proposals, pitch, web, and campaigns, and accelerates commercial enablement. The cost of not having it is real: longer sales cycles, proposals that buckle under objections, and differentiation perceived as interchangeable with the competition.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior brand and positioning strategist, specialist in messaging houses and B2B commercial narrative.
Deliverable: a complete, activation-ready messaging house with roof, pillars, foundation, commercial enablement table, and channel-use matrix.
Steps:
1. Synthesize the context from {{MARCA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}}, {{DIFERENCIADORES_PRUEBAS}}, and {{PROMESA_CENTRAL}}; name the category, decision-maker, influencers, and central competitive tension.
2. Draft the ROOF (umbrella message): a single, memorable phrase centered on customer value rather than product; maximum 15 words. It must be defensible (the brand can support it with evidence) and distinguishable from {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}}.
3. Define 3 or 4 PILLARS. Each pillar: short name + customer-oriented benefit statement + 2-3 concrete reasons-to-believe derived from real evidence. Pillars must be mutually exclusive and together hold up the roof.
4. Build the FOUNDATION: brand values, tone of voice, and a closing phrase that supports the house.
5. Generate the COMMERCIAL ENABLEMENT table: per pillar, one sales-opening line and one typical objection with its response.
6. Generate the CHANNEL-USE MATRIX: how the roof and pillars translate into proposal, pitch, web, and campaign without contradicting each other (what is emphasized in each channel).
7. Mark with [SUPUESTO] every inferred datum the team must validate; list at the end the critical assumptions that would change the house if proven false.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Context: distill the offer, audience, category, and competitive tension into one framing paragraph.
Phase 2 - Roof: derive the umbrella message from the intersection of core promise / dominant differentiator; test that it is defensible and not generic. Quick test: if a competitor from {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}} could sign the same phrase, rewrite it.
Phase 3 - Pillars: group differentiators into 3-4 mutually exclusive themes; for each, anchor the benefit in the customer and back it with verifiable reasons-to-believe; discard any unsupported evidence or mark it [SUPUESTO].
Phase 4 - Foundation, enablement, and channel: close with values, tone, and closing phrase; translate each pillar into a concrete sales move; and map how each channel uses the house.
Edge cases: if {{PROMESA_CENTRAL}} is empty, derive it from the dominant differentiator and mark it [SUPUESTO]. If the differentiators are weak or interchangeable, say so directly and suggest what should be validated or strengthened before activating. If two differentiators overlap, merge them into one pillar and do not invent a fourth filler pillar; three strong pillars beat four weak ones.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Roof in a single phrase, <=15 words, centered on customer value, not product, defensible with evidence and distinguishable from {{CATEGORIA_COMPETIDORES}} (a competitor would not sign it).
- [ ] 3-4 mutually exclusive pillars, each with a customer-oriented benefit, that together support the roof.
- [ ] Each pillar has 2-3 concrete reasons-to-believe; inferred ones are marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented metric, certification, or case left unmarked.
- [ ] Foundation includes values, tone of voice, and closing phrase consistent with the roof.
- [ ] Enablement table: per pillar, sales opening + objection with response.
- [ ] Channel-use matrix: proposal, pitch, web, and campaign, without contradicting each other.
- [ ] Final list of critical assumptions that would change the house if proven false.
- [ ] Neutral, professional English, no emojis; no invented unmarked data.
Expected deliverable: structured document (Framing / Roof / Pillars / Foundation / Commercial Enablement Table / Channel Matrix / Critical Assumptions) ready to distribute to the commercial team as a single script.
spec-marketing_estrategia_perceptual_map:
[inputs]
- MARCA: {{MARCA}} > Own brand to be positioned on the map
- CATEGORIA: {{CATEGORIA}} > Category or market where the brand competes
- SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO: {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} > Customer segment whose perception anchors the axes
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > List of competitors to place (real names)
- ATRIBUTOS_CLAVE: {{ATRIBUTOS_CLAVE}} > Attributes that influence the purchase decision, axis candidates
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to see the competitive field of {{CATEGORIA}} as a plane, not as a list. A two-axis perceptual map translates segment {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}'s perception into coordinates, reveals where competitors cluster, and shows where a defensible white space exists. The result unlocks a concrete decision: which positioning territory to occupy for {{MARCA}} with the least competitive friction and the most relevance to the customer. It is direct input for a brand strategy, a creative brief, or a committee session. Quality warning: a map is only valuable if the axes truly discriminate and the positions distinguish data from inference; a visually polished plane with correlated axes or invented coordinates leads to wrong decisions.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior brand positioning strategist with a track record of building perceptual maps that have redefined brand territory in contested categories.
Deliverable: a reasoned perceptual map of {{MARCA}} against {{COMPETIDORES}} with a recommendation of the territory to occupy.
Steps:
1. Select the two axes from {{ATRIBUTOS_CLAVE}}: propose 3 candidate pairs, evaluate each axis by relevance to {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} and by discriminating power across competitors, discard correlated pairs that collapse the plane into a diagonal (two attributes that always rise together are not two dimensions), and recommend the most revealing pair with your reasoning.
2. Define each axis as a 0 to 10 scale with unambiguous verbal anchors at both extremes (what 0 means, what 10 means); avoid vague anchors that prevent placing an actor.
3. Assign a coordinate (x, y) to {{MARCA}} and to each competitor, justifying the position with evidence or perception; mark [SUPUESTO] for every position inferred without confirmed data and indicate what data would confirm it.
4. Read the plane by quadrant: clusters, saturated zone, and white space with plausible demand; distinguish a gap with demand from an empty gap that nobody wants.
5. Recommend the territory to occupy: why it is defensible, what reality check validates it (brand capability or asset that supports it, not just aspiration), and what main risk threatens it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reformulate category, segment, and purpose of the map; list what is missing.
Phase 2 - Axis design: derive the 3 candidate pairs from {{ATRIBUTOS_CLAVE}}, apply the relevance + discrimination + non-correlation filter, recommend one and discard the others with reasoning.
Phase 3 - Placement: coordinate each actor with justification; separate data from [SUPUESTO] and name the data that would close each assumption.
Phase 4 - Reading: describe quadrants, density, and white space with plausible demand.
Phase 5 - Recommendation: territory, defensibility, reality check, and risk.
Edge cases: if {{COMPETIDORES}} has fewer than 3 actors, warn that the map loses discriminating power and ask for more; if {{ATRIBUTOS_CLAVE}} is empty or trivial, propose candidate attributes and ask for validation before fixing axes; if all actors fall in one quadrant, revisit the axes before drawing conclusions; if {{MARCA}} does not yet exist in the market, place it as a target position and mark it [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The two axes are relevant to the purchase and discriminate across competitors; they are not correlated, and the recommended pair is justified against the rejected ones.
- Each axis has a 0 to 10 scale with unambiguous verbal anchors at both extremes.
- Every brand has a coordinate (x, y) and justification; inferred positions carry [SUPUESTO] with the data that would confirm them.
- The white space is identified and its plausible demand is argued, not just an empty gap.
- The recommendation includes territory, defensibility, a reality check anchored in a brand asset, and a risk.
- Edge cases addressed (fewer than 3 competitors, empty attributes, single quadrant, nonexistent brand).
- No invented competitors or attributes; missing data is requested, not filled in.
- Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word free.
Expected deliverable: coordinate table (brand, x, y, justification, data/assumption) + quadrant description of the plane + paragraph recommending the territory with its reality check and risk.
spec-marketing_estrategia_north_star_met:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > Business and product to analyze (what it does, for whom)
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} > Core benefit the customer obtains
- MODELO_NEGOCIO: {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} > How it monetizes (SaaS, marketplace, e-commerce, ads, subscription)
- ETAPA_OBJETIVO: {{ETAPA_OBJETIVO}} > Company stage and priority growth objective
- DATOS_DISPONIBLES: {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} > Events, metrics, or instrumentation available today (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need ONE single metric to serve as the north star for all marketing and growth effort, avoiding scatter across vanity metrics and misalignment between teams. Defining the North Star Metric well unlocks investment prioritization, growth roadmap clarity, and a shared conversation between marketing, product, and leadership on what real value is being delivered to the customer. A poorly chosen NSM (a proxy of internal activity or vanity) misdirects budget and erodes retention; the cost of getting it wrong is strategic, not just a reporting issue.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior growth marketing strategist expert in Amplitude's North Star Metric framework (NSM Playbook: one output metric + equation of movable inputs).
Deliverable: NSM definition with its actionable input equation for marketing. Steps:
1. Classify the product in one of the three Amplitude value archetypes (Attention, Transaction, Productivity) and justify with the value proposition and business model.
2. Articulate the central value moment: the exact instant when the customer experiences the promised benefit, not the activity surrounding it.
3. Propose 2-3 NSM candidates and evaluate them in a table against the 6 Amplitude criteria (expresses customer value; represents vision/strategy; is a leading indicator of revenue; is actionable; is understandable by everyone; is measurable with existing or feasible instrumentation). Use a high/medium/low scale with one line of justification per cell.
4. Recommend ONE winning NSM with an exact operational definition: what event is counted, time window, unit of aggregation (users, accounts, sessions), and what is explicitly excluded.
5. Break down the NSM into an equation of 3-5 inputs movable by marketing, organized by the dimensions breadth, depth, frequency, and efficiency; assign to each input a concrete marketing lever and a measurable proxy.
6. Close with safeguards: vanity metrics to discard with reasoning; gaming risks of the chosen NSM with mitigation; and a health counter-indicator (retention or margin) that prevents optimizing the NSM at the expense of real value.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm value archetype and value moment from the value proposition and business model. Apply the anti-proxy test: if the NSM can rise without the customer receiving more value, it does not qualify as an NSM. If an essential datum is missing (value proposition, monetization, stage, or instrumented events), ask for it before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Candidates: generate 2-3 NSMs anchored in delivered value (not in internal activity or vanity) and build the evaluation table against the 6 criteria.
Phase 3 - Decision: select the winner, write its unambiguous operational definition, and derive the input equation with marketing levers and measurable proxies. Justify the trade-off against the second-best candidate.
Phase 4 - Safeguards: list vanity metrics to discard, gaming risks with mitigation, and the health counter-indicator. Mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and indicate what data would validate each assumption.
Edge cases: if the business is multi-sided (marketplace, ads), define whom the NSM serves and name mirror metrics by side. If the stage is pre-product-market-fit, prioritize the value criterion over the revenue criterion.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Value archetype assigned and justified (Attention/Transaction/Productivity).
- [ ] Central value moment explicit and distinguished from the surrounding activity.
- [ ] Table with 2-3 candidates evaluated against the 6 Amplitude criteria, with justification per cell.
- [ ] ONE winning NSM with operational definition (event, time window, unit of aggregation, exclusions).
- [ ] Equation of 3-5 actionable inputs, each with a marketing lever and measurable proxy.
- [ ] Vanity metrics, gaming risks, and health counter-indicator identified with mitigation.
- [ ] Trade-off against the second candidate justified.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; missing data asked, not invented.
Expected deliverable: North Star Metric document in neutral, professional English, with evaluation table, defined winning NSM, actionable input equation, and safeguards ready for marketing to use without reinterpretation.
spec-marketing_estrategia_segmentacion_s:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA: {{PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA}} > Product, service, or category to position
- MERCADO_GEOGRAFICO: {{MERCADO_GEOGRAFICO}} > Geographic market and type (B2B / B2C)
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > Main competitors to contrast on the perceptual map
- PROPUESTA_VALOR_ACTUAL: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ACTUAL}} > Current brand value proposition
- CAPACIDADES_DISTINTIVAS: {{CAPACIDADES_DISTINTIVAS}} > Capabilities, assets, or advantages that support differentiation
- PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA: {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}} > Priority focus criterion, e.g., profitability, growth, or defense (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to decide which market segments to serve and how to differentiate in each one, avoiding scattering resources on low-fit customers. A well-built Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (STP) strategy unlocks commercial focus, differentiated messages by audience, and a verifiable basis for go-to-market, pricing, and roadmap. Without it, marketing becomes generic and the brand competes on price. The recurring risk is producing a market portrait that sounds correct but commits no focus decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing strategist specialized in segmentation and positioning, with a track record building STP strategies in B2B and B2C markets.
Deliver an actionable STP strategy following these steps:
1. Segmentation: identify between 4 and 6 segments combining demographic, firmographic (if B2B), geographic, behavioral, and needs-based (jobs-to-be-done) bases. They must be mutually exclusive, exhaustive in what is relevant, and actionable. For each one define profile, estimated size, dominant need, purchase trigger, and relative willingness to pay (high/medium/low, no price figures).
2. Targeting: evaluate each segment on two axes. Attractiveness (size, growth, relative profitability, competitive intensity, barriers) and Fit with capabilities (offer alignment, sustainable differential advantage, cost to serve, channel access). Score 1 to 5 for each criterion, calculate the average per axis, and classify each segment as primary, secondary, or discarded with justification. Flag attractiveness traps (large but no fit) and fit traps (perfect alignment but marginal).
3. Positioning: for each prioritized segment draft a statement with the structure For [segment] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [differential benefit], because [verifiable reason to believe]. Add 2 to 3 points of parity and 2 to 3 points of difference; the differential benefit must be anchored in a real capability.
4. Perceptual map: define two axes that explain customer choice (avoid correlated or trivial axes), place the brand against the indicated competitors, and name the most valuable vacant space if it exists.
5. Focus decision: recommend the segment(s) to prioritize and their order of attack, declare what is deliberately left out, and state the 3 riskiest assumptions to validate along with how to validate them quickly.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm category, market, competitors, value proposition, and capabilities. If an essential datum is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent it. Mark every unverified estimate as [SUPUESTO]. If the strategic priority is given, use it to bias the focus.
Phase 2 - Segmentation: apply multiple bases and consolidate into 4 to 6 mutually exclusive, actionable segments.
Phase 3 - Prioritization: score attractiveness and fit in the matrix, calculate averages, classify, and name the traps.
Phase 4 - Positioning: draft statements, points of parity and difference, and the perceptual map with its vacant space.
Phase 5 - Close: deliver the focus decision, what is left out, and the assumptions to validate.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] 4 to 6 mutually exclusive, actionable segments with profile, size, need, trigger, and relative willingness to pay.
- [ ] Targeting matrix with criteria scored 1 to 5, average per axis, and justified primary/secondary/discarded classification.
- [ ] Attractiveness and fit traps explicitly identified.
- [ ] Positioning statement per primary segment with the complete For-is-because structure, anchored in a real capability.
- [ ] Points of parity and points of difference differentiated by segment.
- [ ] Perceptual map with two relevant discriminating axes, competitor placement, and named vacant space.
- [ ] Unverified estimates marked as [SUPUESTO]; no invented data; no price figures or the word free.
- [ ] Focus decision with order of attack, what is left out, and 3 assumptions to validate with validation method.
Expected deliverable: STP document with segment table, scored targeting matrix, positioning statements, perceptual map description, and decision block with assumptions to validate.
spec-marketing_estrategia_marketing_mix_:
[inputs]
- SERVICIO: {{SERVICIO}} > Service to position and its brief description
- SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO: {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} > Target segment and its main problem or job to be done
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} > Central value proposition that differentiates the offering
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > Reference competitors or alternatives (optional)
- MODELO_MONETIZACION: {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}} > Billing model: subscription, per project, per hour, retainer, etc.
- CANAL_DOMINANTE: {{CANAL_DOMINANTE}} > Dominant channel for service acquisition and delivery
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Designing an extended 7P marketing mix for a services offering. An incoherent mix scatters budget and dilutes positioning: the promotion's promise is not supported by the processes, or the price attribute contradicts the value proposition. Resolving this unlocks an aligned go-to-market where every lever reinforces the others and the segment, and allows prioritizing investment with criteria. Applies to B2B and B2C, professional, consultative, or digital services. Intangibles' particular challenge: the customer cannot inspect the service before buying it, so People, Processes, and Physical evidence are the levers that convert a promise into trust; neglecting them is the most common mistake relative to the classic 4Ps.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior services marketing strategist with a track record in go-to-market and positioning for intangible B2B and B2C offerings.

Deliverable: 7P marketing mix document with positioning statement, the 7Ps justified, coherence matrix, and priority moves. Steps:
1. Reformulate {{SERVICIO}} and {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} into a positioning statement (for whom, what category, what benefit, why different). This statement is the anchor; every P must be traceable to it.
2. Develop the 7Ps one by one: Product (scope, service levels, warranties, what is excluded), Price (premium/parity/penetration/perceived-value/anchoring strategy, logic of {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, value capture and billing metric, NO amounts), Place (acquisition and delivery channels according to {{CANAL_DOMINANTE}}, coverage, and why that channel serves the segment), Promotion (key messages, formats, social proof, and differentiation angles against {{COMPETIDORES}}), People (contact roles, competencies, scripts or key moments, expectation management), Processes (end-to-end delivery journey, SLAs, milestones, friction points and how to mitigate them), Physical evidence (tangibles that reduce the perceived risk of the intangible: sample deliverables, cases, certifications, dashboards, environment).
3. Justify each P against {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}; mark every datum not provided as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent figures or attributes.
4. Build a coherence matrix that crosses the 7Ps against each other; flag at least two tensions or incoherencies (e.g., premium Price against Processes with no SLA, or ambitious Promotion against People with no script) and the concrete resolution path for each.
5. Close with three priority moves for the next 90 days, actionable and sequenced, each with the P it reinforces and the expected progress signal.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Interpret): validate that {{SERVICIO}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, and {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} exist; if any is missing, ask for it before continuing and do not invent attributes or figures. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute data.
Phase 2 (Plan): fix the positioning statement as the anchor and derive from it the decisions for each P; declare the [SUPUESTO]s you will assume.
Phase 3 (Execute): write the statement, the 7Ps justified, the coherence matrix with its tensions, and the three moves.
Brand restrictions: never price figures or plans with amounts; Price is treated as strategy, billing metric, and value capture. Never the word free; use no-entry-cost, included, or complimentary. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. Do not mix brands in the same output.
Edge cases: if {{COMPETIDORES}} is empty, infer alternatives (including customer inaction) and mark it [SUPUESTO]; if {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}} is ambiguous, propose the one most coherent with the pricing strategy and justify it; if the service is very new, prioritize Physical evidence and social proof as risk reducers.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit positioning statement (for whom, what, why different) used as a traceable anchor across the 7Ps.
- [ ] The 7Ps developed, each justified against value proposition and segment.
- [ ] Price treated as strategy, billing metric, and value capture, NO monetary figures or plans.
- [ ] The word free not used; alternatives correctly applied.
- [ ] People, Processes, and Physical evidence explicitly address the reduction of intangible risk.
- [ ] Coherence matrix crossing the 7Ps with at least two tensions identified and their resolution path.
- [ ] Three priority moves for the next 90 days, actionable, sequenced, and with progress signal.
- [ ] Assumptions marked with [SUPUESTO]; neutral, professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: structured document (positioning statement + 7Ps justified + coherence matrix + 3 moves for 90 days) ready for leadership review.
spec-producto_discovery_problem_framing_:
[inputs]

- SEGMENTO_AFECTADO: {{SEGMENTO_AFECTADO}} > Who experiences the problem and in what usage context
