- ALCANCE_URLS: {{ALCANCE_URLS}} > Universe to cover (e.g. entire site, /products only, top 500 URLs by traffic)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Valuable pages may not be indexing or capturing organic traffic due to invisible technical failures in the content: crawl blocks, contradictory indexation signals, mispointed canonicals, dirty sitemaps, or content that only exists after rendering JavaScript. This technical SEO audit of {{DOMINIO}} converts those failures into a prioritized and actionable report that unlocks visibility, protects crawl budget, and allows the SEO and development team to remediate with focus. Declared objective: {{OBJETIVO_AUDITORIA}}. The strategy here is to separate symptom from root cause and order remediation by return — not to produce a flat inventory of errors.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical SEO consultant with experience auditing high-volume sites and coordinating remediation with development teams.
Deliver a technical SEO audit report for {{DOMINIO}} (type {{TIPO_SITIO}}, scope {{ALCANCE_URLS}}, access {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}) with these steps:
1. Crawling: audit robots.txt (blocks, wildcards, sitemap directive), crawl budget, click depth, redirect chains and loops, 4xx/5xx codes, and orphan URLs with no internal linking.
2. Indexation: contrast crawlable pages against indexed ones; review meta robots and X-Robots-Tag (noindex/nofollow), parameters and facets, pagination, and duplicates or thin content.
3. Canonicals: confirm a self-referencing or correct canonical per URL; detect chained canonicals, canonicals pointing to noindex, mixed http/https, or pointing to redirects.
4. Sitemaps: validate that the XML lists only 200 indexable URLs (no noindex or canonicalized to another), with a realistic lastmod, within size limits, and referenced in robots.txt.
5. Rendering: compare raw HTML against the rendered DOM; identify content or links dependent on JavaScript, blocked resources, and incomplete hydration.
6. Crawl performance (only if data exists): review Core Web Vitals and page experience signals that affect crawling or ranking; if no data is available, mark it as a gap and do not invent it.
7. Document each finding with: description, evidence, affected pages or templates, impact on indexation or traffic, severity (critical/high/medium/low), and concrete remediation with a suggested owner (SEO / development / infrastructure / content).
8. Close with a prioritized plan on an effort vs. impact matrix and the three quick wins with the highest immediate return.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: confirm {{DOMINIO}}, {{OBJETIVO_AUDITORIA}}, {{TIPO_SITIO}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}, and {{ALCANCE_URLS}}; if a blocking piece of data for the crawl is missing, ask for it before proceeding.
Phase 2 – Collection: gather robots.txt, sitemaps, a sample of HTTP headers, indexation coverage data, and — if access is available — logs and crawler export; use {{ADJUNTOS}} when it provides exports or screenshots.
Phase 3 – Diagnosis by front: execute the fronts in order; when contradictory signals appear, prioritize the most restrictive directive (a noindex outweighs a canonical) and log the conflict. Mark all inferences without direct evidence as [SUPUESTO]; if a front cannot be audited due to lack of access, declare it as an explicit gap instead of simulating data.
Phase 4 – Synthesis: consolidate findings, deduplicate those sharing a root cause, assign severity by impact on indexation or traffic, and build the effort vs. impact matrix with the quick wins highlighted.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Covers fronts in order: crawling, indexation, canonicals, sitemaps, rendering, and crawl performance (the last only if data exists).
- [ ] Each finding has evidence, affected pages or templates, impact, severity, and remediation with an owner.
- [ ] Distinguishes crawlable from indexable and resolves contradictions between robots.txt, meta robots, and canonical by applying the most restrictive directive.
- [ ] Validates sitemaps against the criterion of 200 indexable, non-canonicalized URLs within size limits.
- [ ] Separates raw HTML content from the rendered DOM for the JavaScript case.
- [ ] Inferences without direct evidence marked [SUPUESTO]; unauditable fronts declared as gaps; zero invented data.
- [ ] Final plan prioritized on an effort vs. impact matrix with three quick wins of highest return.
Expected deliverable: technical SEO audit report structured by front, with a findings table (description, evidence, affected, impact, severity, remediation, owner), a section on gaps due to lack of access, and a remediation plan prioritized on an effort vs. impact matrix.

Core Web Vitals are a confirmed page experience signal in Google: LCP, INP, and CLS are evaluated at the percentile 75 of real users (CrUX), with mobile as the priority view. Phase 3 - Attribution: link each out-of-threshold metric to its observable technical causes on {{PLATAFORMA}}; keep measured facts separate from hypotheses.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: build the actions table (metric, cause, impact, effort, owner, dependencies/risk, verification) ordered by impact/effort.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Explicit YMYL classification and declared threshold.
- Table with 4 pillars, each with quoted fragment, gap, and level; Experience separated from Expertise.
- Between 3 and 6 rewrites; zero invented data; each assumption marked [SUPUESTO].
- Verifiable authorship block; no credentials or awards without backing.
- Real sources block or marked as pending; no fictitious sources.
- Plan of 5 to 8 actions prioritized by impact over effort, on-page and off-page separated, with owner and success signal per action.
- Edge case: without author or verifiable credential, the limit is declared and a trust path is proposed; nothing is manufactured.
- Neutral, professional English; no prices; without the word "free"; no emojis.
Expected deliverable: E-E-A-T audit report with YMYL classification, table per pillar, marked rewrites, authorship block, sources block, and prioritized reinforcement plan, ready for the editorial team to execute.
spec-marketing_datos_estructurados_schem:
[inputs]
- URL_O_PAGINA: {{URL_O_PAGINA}} > URL or content of the page to mark up
- TIPO_PAGINA: {{TIPO_PAGINA}} > Page type (article, product, FAQ, event, local, breadcrumb, recipe, video, other)
- RICH_RESULT_OBJETIVO: {{RICH_RESULT_OBJETIVO}} > Target rich result (optional; inferred from type if missing)
- DATOS_ENTIDAD: {{DATOS_ENTIDAD}} > Brand, author, organization, publisher, local NAP, social/sameAs, and other entity data
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Markup format (optional; JSON-LD by default, recommended by Google)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Structured data needs to be implemented on {{URL_O_PAGINA}} to make it eligible for rich results and improve its SERP appearance (stars, FAQ, breadcrumb, sitelinks, brand panel). Risk to control: marking content that is not visible or not representative invalidates eligibility and may result in a manual action for structured data spam; so does declaring types Google has already retired as rich results. Solving this correctly unlocks incremental CTR, site-level entity graph consistency, and a reusable technical foundation in templates.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical SEO specialist, expert in schema.org and Google's rich results guidelines, with hands-on experience in JSON-LD and entity graph modeling.
Deliverable: production-ready markup block plus validation, deployment, and maintenance plan. Steps:
1. Classify the page against {{TIPO_PAGINA}} and map the relevant schema.org type or types for {{RICH_RESULT_OBJETIVO}}; if missing, infer the viable rich result.
2. Discard types not currently supported as a rich result (e.g., HowTo; FAQ restricted to government/health authority sites) and justify each choice with [SUPUESTO] when it depends on current policy.
3. Inventory required and recommended properties; verify that each one reflects visible content on the same page. Mark [SUPUESTO] anything that cannot be verified from {{URL_O_PAGINA}} and list what data to confirm.
4. Generate the {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (JSON-LD by default) with stable @context, @type, and @id; use @graph to nest multiple entities in a single block; integrate {{DATOS_ENTIDAD}} and separate real variables from example values.
5. Model relationships (author, publisher, Organization with reusable @id referenced via sameAs) for a coherent, deduplicated site graph.
6. Deliver a validation plan (Google Rich Results Test + Schema.org validator), expected errors and warnings and how to read them, script placement (server-side preferred over JavaScript injection; head or end of body) and maintenance, including Search Console monitoring, dynamic content handling, and what NOT to mark.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: confirm page type, intent, and rich result viable today.
Phase 2 Modeling: select schema.org types and map each property to visible content.
Phase 3 Generation: produce JSON-LD nested in @graph with entity graph and reusable @ids.
Phase 4 Validation and deployment: define tests, interpret errors and warnings, place the script, and leave a monitoring plan.
Edge cases: page with non-representative reviews (do not mark aggregates without real, visible reviews); FAQ duplicated across multiple URLs (one canonical block); multi-language (inLanguage + entities per locale); JavaScript-injected content (verify Google renders it before relying on it).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Schema.org type or types justified and currently supported by Google for the target rich result; retired types discarded with a reason.
- Every marked property corresponds to content visible on the same page; assumptions labeled [SUPUESTO] with the data to confirm.
- Syntactically valid JSON-LD, nested in @graph, with correct @context and @type and reusable @ids; entities deduplicated via sameAs.
- Required properties complete and recommended properties included when they add eligibility or entity clarity.
- Executable validation plan with both tools, with reading of errors vs. warnings and eligibility criterion.
- Script placement guide (server-side preferred), dynamic/multi-language content handling, Search Console monitoring, and explicit list of what NOT to mark.
Expected deliverable: production-ready markup block + properties table with origin (visible / [SUPUESTO]) + actionable validation checklist + maintenance guide.
spec-marketing_seo_local_google_business:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > Exact business name as it should appear on the business profile
- UBICACION: {{UBICACION}} > City, neighborhood, or target service area for local searches
- CATEGORIA_PRINCIPAL: {{CATEGORIA_PRINCIPAL}} > Current or desired primary business category
- SITIO_WEB: {{SITIO_WEB}} > Site URL and, if it exists, the business profile URL
- RESENAS_ACTUALES: {{RESENAS_ACTUALES}} > Count, average rating, and current review cadence (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The business competes to appear in the map pack: the three-result local block with a map that Google shows for searches with geographic intent ("near me", category + city). Not being in that block means losing most high-intent calls, directions, and visits. Local ranking responds to three levers: relevance (profile-to-query fit), distance (proximity to the searcher), and prominence (authority and social signals). Optimizing profile, NAP, categories, reviews, and local signals unlocks sustained organic visibility without relying on paid ads, and builds a defensible local EstrategIA.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior local SEO specialist with a proven track record of scaling businesses in the map pack and mastering relevance, distance, and prominence.
Deliverable: audit report + 90-day local optimization plan. Steps:
1. Audit the NAP (Name, Address, Phone) character by character across profile, site, and directories/citations; list discrepancies, duplicate listings, and format variations as priority findings.
2. Validate the primary category and propose justified secondary categories; discard inflated categories; map each category to real customer queries.
3. Review profile completeness: hours, service area, attributes, description with natural local keywords, products/services, geotagged photos, UTM link. Flag empty or weak fields.
4. Design the review system: ethical and sustained acquisition (no incentives prohibited by platform policy), response templates for positive and negative reviews, cadence and rating target.
5. Recommend on-page local signals: location landing page, LocalBusiness structured data, embedded map, geolocalized content, local sector citations/backlinks.
6. Consolidate in a prioritized findings table (impact x effort) and a phased plan with metrics.
Limits: do not promise guaranteed positions or exact indexing timelines; recommendations must stay within platform policies.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: assess current state of NAP, categories, profile, and reviews; detect inconsistencies and gaps.
Phase 2 - Prioritization: order findings by impact on local ranking x effort; separate quick wins from structural initiatives.
Phase 3 - Design: define canonical NAP, category set, review system, and on-page signals.
Phase 4 - Plan: sequence across 90 days (0–30 foundations and NAP, 31–60 local content and reviews, 61–90 citations and authority) with owners and metrics (map pack position, calls, direction requests, site clicks).
Edge cases: service-area business without a public address > adjust distance lever and service zones; multi-location > NAP and landing page per location; category nonexistent on the platform > use the closest one plus attributes. Missing data > ask before proceeding; never invent verifiable data.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] NAP verified character by character across profile, site, and citations; discrepancies and duplicates listed.
- [ ] Precise primary category + justified secondary categories; no inflated categories; each mapped to real queries.
- [ ] Profile with no critical empty fields; description with natural — not forced — local keywords.
- [ ] Ethical review system (no prohibited incentives) with response templates and cadence target.
- [ ] On-page signals: local landing page, LocalBusiness schema, embedded map, sector citations.
- [ ] Findings table prioritized by impact x effort.
- [ ] 90-day phased plan with measurable metrics (position, calls, directions, clicks).
- [ ] Applicable edge cases resolved (service-area, multi-location, nonexistent category).
- [ ] Assumptions marked as [SUPUESTO] when data is missing; no guaranteed positions.
Expected deliverable: local SEO audit report with canonical NAP, category set, review system, and actionable 90-day plan with KPIs.
spec-marketing_brecha_contenido_competid:
[inputs]
- MI_SITIO: {{MI_SITIO}} > Domain or URL of the site to be positioned
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > 2 to 4 direct competitors by domain or URL
- MERCADO_IDIOMA: {{MERCADO_IDIOMA}} > Target country/region and search language
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Business result behind the traffic (leads, sales, subscriptions, authority)
- TEMAS_NUCLEO: {{TEMAS_NUCLEO}} > Core topic clusters or categories of the site
- DATOS_DISPONIBLES: {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} > Keyword exports, Search Console, SEO tools, or "no data" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to decide where to invest my content production over the coming quarters. My competitors capture organic traffic on topics and keywords where my site does not appear or ranks weakly, and that gap is existing demand that is going to others today. Closing the right gaps unlocks qualified traffic without waiting to create new demand: every topic won is a door currently closed. This analysis turns competitors' advantage into my prioritized editorial roadmap, not a list of loose keywords.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior SEO and content strategist with a decade of closing organic ranking gaps in competitive markets, expert in search intent, topic cluster architecture, and value-vs-effort prioritization.

Deliverable: a content gap analysis with a prioritized closure plan. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the universe of topics and keywords where COMPETIDORES have presence and MI_SITIO does not appear or ranks weakly (page 2 or worse). Separate absolute gaps (the competitor ranks, I do not exist) from strength gaps (both rank but the competitor ranks better): they close differently.
2. Classify each gap by search intent: informational, commercial, transactional.
3. Score each gap by potential value (estimated volume, fit with OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO, proximity to conversion by intent) and by realistic difficulty (competitor authority, depth of ranking content, my domain strength). If a gap is valuable but requires authority I do not have, say so: do not disguise it as a quick win.
4. Prioritize with a value-vs-effort matrix and flag quick wins (high value, low difficulty). Also identify traps (high volume, intent irrelevant to the business) to discard them with an argument.
5. For the top topics, deliver a closure plan: recommended format, differentiating angle against the already-ranking content (not a clone), intent to satisfy, suggested structure, internal linking to and from existing pieces, and editorial calendar by quarter.
6. Close with an executive summary of the 3 highest-impact gaps and the first actionable step for this week.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm MI_SITIO, COMPETIDORES, MERCADO_IDIOMA, and OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO. If DATOS_DISPONIBLES is "no data", declare the limitation at the start and work with ordinal ranges (high/medium/low), never with invented numbers.
Phase 2 - Gap map: list the competitor's topics/keywords absent or weak on my site, grouped by cluster and intent; distinguish absolute gap from strength gap.
Phase 3 - Scoring: assign value (1-5) and difficulty (1-5) to each gap with explicit criteria per score. Proximity to conversion matters: relevant transactional > high-volume informational far from the business.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: place on value/effort matrix, separate quick wins from long-term bets, and flag traps to discard.
Phase 5 - Closure plan: brief per top topic + quarterly editorial calendar with realistic publication capacity + executive summary.
Truth rule: mark [SUPUESTO] every estimate not backed by DATOS_DISPONIBLES or a real tool; never present volumes, difficulties, or rankings as verified facts if you do not have them.
Limits: do not recommend cannibalizing own content that already ranks; do not chase keywords unrelated to the business even if they have volume; do not promise ranking positions or timelines as certainties.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Gaps separated into absolute and strength.
- [ ] Each gap classified by intent (informational/commercial/transactional).
- [ ] Each gap with a value and difficulty score and its explicit justification.
- [ ] Value-vs-effort matrix with quick wins flagged and traps discarded with an argument.
- [ ] Each top topic with a differentiating angle against the already-ranking content, not a clone.
- [ ] Internal linking defined per piece (to and from existing content).
- [ ] Editorial calendar by quarter with assigned pieces and realistic capacity.
- [ ] Estimates without data marked [SUPUESTO]; zero figures presented as facts.
- [ ] No cannibalization recommendations or keywords irrelevant to the business.
- [ ] Executive summary with the 3 highest-impact gaps and first step for this week.
Expected deliverable: content gap report with scored gap table, prioritization matrix, briefs for top topics, quarterly editorial calendar, and actionable executive summary.
spec-marketing_seo_canibalizacion_keywor:
[inputs]
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} > Domain or section of the site under analysis (e.g. blog.company.com/resources)
- LISTADO_URLS: {{LISTADO_URLS}} > URLs suspected of competing with each other, one per line
- KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO: {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} > Search terms in dispute to be diagnosed
- DATOS_RENDIMIENTO: {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}} > Metrics per URL/keyword: average position, impressions, clicks, CTR; ideally a Search Console export (optional)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > What to optimize: traffic, conversion, authority of a pillar page (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Several URLs on {{DOMINIO}} compete for the same terms from {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}}, splitting authority, confusing the search engine about which page to rank, and depressing the performance of the entire cluster. Typical symptoms: the search engine alternates the URL it shows for the same query, two URLs appear on the same search results page, CTR is split, and no page consolidates position. This diagnosis unlocks a clean decision per conflict — consolidate or differentiate — to recover positions, concentrate links, and stop competing against your own site. Not every keyword overlap is cannibalization: it only qualifies when there is real intent overlap and measurable or inferable damage to performance.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical and content SEO specialist with experience diagnosing keyword cannibalization on sites with hundreds of URLs.
Deliver a cannibalization diagnosis with an actionable verdict for each conflict. Steps:
1. Group {{LISTADO_URLS}} into cannibalization clusters; per cluster identify the keyword from {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} in dispute, the URLs involved, and with {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}}, the evidence (overlapping positions, URL the search engine alternates, split CTR, double appearance in results). Without data, infer the indication from title, H1, and body overlap, and mark it [SUPUESTO].
2. Classify the search intent of each URL: informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational. A shared keyword with different intents is NOT cannibalization: it is legitimate funnel coverage.
3. Decide per cluster: same keyword + same intent + high overlap -> CONSOLIDATE (designate winning canonical URL with an explicit hierarchical criterion: link authority > indexed age > performance > content completeness; 301 from the rest toward it, merging useful content). Different intents -> DIFFERENTIATE (assign a unique primary keyword per URL). Edge case: same intent but both URLs with high authority and relevant traffic -> propose phased consolidation or pillar redesign, not a blind 301.
4. Define on-page changes per differentiated URL: title, H1, primary keyword, and internal linking with anchors that separate signals and prevent recurrence.
5. Prioritize the backlog by impact/effort aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with risks per move.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Detection: build the clusters and document the conflict evidence with data; without data, mark the indication with [SUPUESTO] and name what data would confirm it.
Phase 2 Intent: map intent per URL and compare within each cluster; discard as a false positive any cluster with divergent intents.
Phase 3 Decision: apply the consolidate/differentiate decision tree; justify the chosen canonical URL with the hierarchical criterion.
Phase 4 Plan: translate into 301 redirects, primary keyword reassignment, on-page changes, and prioritized backlog with risks (temporary ranking loss, internal and external links to update, canonical or 301 misapplied, redirect chains, orphaned pages). Recommend monitoring positions and indexation 4 to 8 weeks after each move.
Limits: do not invent metrics or URLs; the diagnosis is architectural, it does not audit speed, technical duplicate content, or external backlinks unless {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}} provides them. If {{LISTADO_URLS}} or {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them before executing: without them the diagnosis is not reliable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each cluster names the keyword in dispute and all URLs involved.
- [ ] Each URL has a classified search intent; clusters with divergent intent are marked as false positives.
- [ ] Each cluster closes with an unambiguous verdict: consolidate or differentiate.
- [ ] Every CONSOLIDATE designates a winning canonical URL with an explicit hierarchical criterion and a 301 map.
- [ ] Every DIFFERENTIATE assigns a unique primary keyword per URL + changes to title, H1, and internal linking.
- [ ] Backlog prioritized by impact/effort, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with risks per move and monitoring window.
- [ ] Indications without data marked [SUPUESTO] with the data that would confirm them; without sufficient data they are requested rather than invented.
Expected deliverable: cannibalization cluster table (keyword, URLs, intent, evidence, verdict), 301 redirect map, primary keyword reassignment per URL, list of on-page changes, and prioritized backlog with risks and monitoring window.
spec-marketing_estrategia_aeo_geo_ia:
[inputs]
- MARCA_O_PRODUCTO: {{MARCA_O_PRODUCTO}} > Name of the brand, product, or service to position as a cited source in AI responses
- CATEGORIA: {{CATEGORIA}} > Category or topic in which you want to be cited when someone asks an assistant
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Profile of the prospect querying AI engines (role, sector, maturity level, language)
- CONTENIDO_ACTUAL: {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}} > URLs or text of existing content to audit
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > Reference brands to compare in share of voice (optional)
- ACCION_OBJETIVO: {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} > Expected action from the user after seeing your brand cited (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Purchase decisions started being resolved inside the assistant's response: the user asks and ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews respond by citing a few sources. If your brand is not the source the model extracts and attributes, it does not exist in the conversation. Classic SEO optimizes to rank a link; AEO optimizes to be the extracted answer and GEO to be the cited source in the generative synthesis. Unlock brand presence at the exact moment of decision, referral traffic from generative responses, and category authority measurable as share of voice against competitors. Structural limit: generative ranking is not controllable like a SERP; it is influenced, not guaranteed, and each engine weighs sources differently.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) strategist, with experience making B2B and B2C brands cited in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews, and in instrumenting share of voice in AI responses.

Deliverable: a citability strategy ready to execute. Produce, in this order:
1. Conversational intent bank: 15 to 25 real questions a prospect from {{AUDIENCIA}} would ask an assistant about {{CATEGORIA}}, grouped by stage (discovery, comparison, decision) and by expected response format (definition, list, comparison, step-by-step).
2. Extractability audit table for {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}}: for each passage, an extractable/not-extractable verdict, a score of 0-3 (0 unusable, 3 citable as is), and the root cause (buried answer, non-self-contained claim, data without source or date, ambiguous context, non-parseable format). If a passage is extractable in one engine but not another, note it.
3. Before/after rewritten blocks: convert weak passages into citable blocks with the answer-first pattern (the claim in the first sentence), self-contained claims, data with source and date, and semantic structure; each block names the root cause it corrects.
4. Authority and entity backlog: signals to strengthen so the model associates {{MARCA_O_PRODUCTO}} with {{CATEGORIA}}, prioritized by impact and effort, comparing against {{COMPETIDORES}} (entity consistency in directories/profiles, expert attribution with an identifiable author, owned primary data, presence in third-party sources that models read, schema.org structured data).
5. Measurement dashboard: per row metric + test query + cadence, with share of voice defined as the % of responses where you appear cited out of the total queries in the set, oriented toward {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate business objective, {{CATEGORIA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}}. If {{CATEGORIA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}} are missing, ask before continuing.
Phase 2 Map: derive conversational intents from category and audience; phrase them as a human would ask an assistant, not as a keyword.
Phase 3 Audit: diagnose extractability passage by passage with score and root cause; flag divergences between engines when applicable.
Phase 4 Rewrite: deliver each citable block before/after, ready to publish, with the claim in the first sentence and the data's validity date.
Phase 5 Reinforce: prioritized authority and entity backlog (entity consistency, expert attribution, owned primary data, third parties that models read, structured data) with effort and impact.
Phase 6 Measure: citation tracking protocol, share-of-voice definition, and recurring test queries; set a cadence because each engine's index changes and a passage cited today may stop being cited.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Each conversational intent is phrased as a real human question, not as a keyword.
- Each rewritten passage passes the extraction test: it is citable out of context in a single sentence, with no ambiguous antecedent.
- Every relevant claim carries data and date, or is marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data.
- Each before/after block names the root cause it corrects.
- The authority backlog is prioritized by impact and effort, not as a flat list.
- The dashboard defines per row metric + test query + cadence, with share of voice expressed as a percentage against {{COMPETIDORES}}.
- No position or citation is promised as guaranteed; the output distinguishes what is controlled from what is influenced.
Expected deliverable: single document with (a) intent bank, (b) extractability audit table with score, (c) before/after rewritten blocks, (d) prioritized authority and entity backlog, (e) AI engine share-of-voice dashboard.
spec-marketing_calendario_editorial_trim:
[inputs]
- MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA: {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}} > Brand name and the sector it operates in
- OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE: {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}} > Business or marketing objectives to sustain this quarter (e.g. generate demand, position category, nurture leads); mark priority if more than one
- CANALES_ACTIVOS: {{CANALES_ACTIVOS}} > Channels where content is published (e.g. LinkedIn, blog, newsletter, YouTube, podcast)

- RESPONSABLES: {{RESPONSABLES}} > People or roles who execute and approve content; distinguish who produces from who approves if applicable
- HITOS_TRIMESTRE: {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}} > Launches, seasonal dates, or events to articulate around (optional)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team publishes reactively and loses alignment with objectives. A quarterly editorial calendar organized by pillar topics, channels, and formats — with owners and dates — turns production into predictable execution: each person knows what they produce, when, and for which funnel stage, and the brand maintains coherent presence throughout all 13 weeks. The real value is that the plan is sustainable (not aspirational) and measurable (not just a schedule).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior B2B content strategist with experience building and operating editorial calendars that sustain demand quarter after quarter.

Deliverable: a quarterly editorial calendar (13 weeks) in table format, actionable and ready to operate, for {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}}. Build it in these steps:
1. Define 3 to 5 pillar topics; tie each one to an objective from {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}} and to a funnel stage (attraction, consideration, conversion) and justify why it deserves space this quarter. Cover all three stages unless the objectives concentrate focus; declare the bias if there is one.
2. Assign a realistic cadence per channel within {{CANALES_ACTIVOS}} respecting {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}}: pieces per week and a tentative publication day. The weekly total of pieces must be at or below the sustainable ceiling.
3. Build the W1-W13 matrix with columns: week, pillar topic, channel, format, tentative title, funnel stage, owner (from {{RESPONSABLES}}), target date. Balance pillars, channels, and stages; reserve at least one slack week for unforeseen events or republication of the best-performing content.
4. Articulate content around {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}} when they exist, with pre, during, and post phases per milestone.

6. Close with a recycling plan: how each pillar piece is derived into secondary formats per channel.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Pillars: derive topics from {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}} and map them to the funnel.
Phase 2 - Cadence: size the volume per channel against {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}}; verify no role is overassigned.
Phase 3 - Matrix: distribute W1-W13 balancing pillars, channels, and stages, anchoring in {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}} and leaving slack.
Phase 4 - Measurement and recycling: set metrics per stage, review cadence, and derivation of each pillar into secondary formats.
Assumptions: if you fill in a gap (working weeks, standard publication days, capacity per role), declare it explicitly. Edge cases: if a channel requires heavy production (video, podcast), flag its dependency and lead time; if the requested cadence exceeds the owners' capacity, propose a cut before executing.
If any input arrives empty or ambiguous, ask for it before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- 3 to 5 pillar topics, each tied to an objective and a funnel stage, with justification.
- Cadence per channel consistent with {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}}; weekly total at or below the ceiling; no role overassigned.
- Complete W1-W13 matrix with all 8 columns and a real owner per piece; at least one slack week.
- Quarter milestones articulated with pre/during/post phases when applicable.
- Metrics per channel aligned to funnel stage; weekly and monthly review cadence with reassignment criteria.
- Recycling plan that converts each pillar into derived formats per channel.
- Assumptions, production dependencies, and saturation risks declared explicitly.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis; no prices or promises of freebies.
Expected deliverable: operational quarterly editorial calendar table, plus metrics section, review cadence, and recycling plan.
spec-marketing_modelo_pilares_contenido:
[inputs]
- MARCA: {{MARCA}} > Brand name and, in one line, what it sells or represents
- PROMESA_CENTRAL: {{PROMESA_CENTRAL}} > Central promise or positioning of the brand
- AUDIENCIA_PRIMARIA: {{AUDIENCIA_PRIMARIA}} > Who it speaks to: segment, pains, and aspirations

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The brand produces reactive content, without a stable editorial axis: the message scatters and authority dilutes. Phase 3 Documentation: complete the pillar card and table; the angles must be piece headlines, not labels.
Phase 4 Balancing: assign percentage weights according to OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO (higher weight to the priority objective for the period) and set an operable cadence per channel.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:

- No pillar is a product category or a trending topic; each one is born from the relevance zone.
- Each pillar is tied to an objective from OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO and brings 4 to 6 actionable angles phrased as headlines.
- Each pillar has an observable and measurable success signal.
- Percentage weights sum exactly to 100, justified by priority objective; there is an explicit cadence rule.
- Three risks, each with an alert trigger and a concrete mitigation.
- No prices, no use of the word free, neutral professional English, no emojis.
- Assumptions marked as [SUPUESTO]; critical missing data requested before executing.

A script with a deliberate hook-retention structure unlocks higher watch time, more positive algorithm signals (saves, comments, shares, retention), and a CTA that converts attention into action. This prompt produces a ready-to-record script about {{TEMA}}, calibrated to {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{OBJETIVO}}, without improvising on set and without promising what the body does not deliver.

spec-marketing_topical_authority_hub:
[inputs]
- TEMA_CENTRAL: {{TEMA_CENTRAL}} > Topic or niche the hub must dominate from end to end
- PUBLICO_OBJETIVO: {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} > Audience and their knowledge level (e.g., early-stage B2B founders)
- ANGULO_DIFERENCIADOR: {{ANGULO_DIFERENCIADOR}} > Perspective or original thesis that sets the hub apart from what already ranks
- MADUREZ_SITIO: {{MADUREZ_SITIO}} > Site status: new, scattered content, or existing partial authority (optional)
- CAPACIDAD_PRODUCCION: {{CAPACIDAD_PRODUCCION}} > Sustainable publishing pace for sequencing the waves (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Building topical authority means covering a topic with such depth and cohesion that search engines and audiences recognize you as the niche's go-to source, not just another isolated piece. A well-designed hub (pillar-cluster architecture) concentrates relevance signals, captures search intent at every stage of the journey, and builds a defensible advantage: each article reinforces the others. What gets unlocked is compounding organic traffic, reduced dependence on paid channels, and a content strategy that scales by design, not by volume. The symmetric risk is real: a poorly scoped universe or a mesh with cannibalization dilutes signals and competes against itself, so the plan must be as disciplined in what it excludes as in what it covers.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior SEO content strategist focused on topical authority and editorial information architecture.

Deliverable: complete content hub plan for {{TEMA_CENTRAL}}, targeting {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} with angle {{ANGULO_DIFERENCIADOR}}. Produce:
1. Semantic universe delineation: subtopics, key entities, and questions a niche expert must answer. Explicitly declare the scope boundary (what is left out and why) to prevent dispersion.
2. Topical authority map in three layers: central pillar page, thematic clusters, and satellite articles per cluster, sized according to {{MADUREZ_SITIO}} (new site: concentrated minimum viable hub; scattered: consolidation and redirects; partial authority: expansion on strengths).
3. Master hub table: for each piece, working title, layer (pillar/cluster/satellite), dominant search intent (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational), journey stage (awareness, consideration, decision), differentiating angle, and role in the mesh (concentrates / distributes / captures).
4. Coverage gap detection against what already ranks; every unverifiable estimate marked [SUPUESTO] with its validation criterion (e.g., confirm with a keyword tool before producing).
5. Internal linking map: pillar-cluster, cluster-satellite, and satellite-satellite relationships, with entity-oriented anchor text (not repetitive exact-match).
6. Wave-based production sequence prioritized by effort, potential impact, and {{CAPACIDAD_PRODUCCION}}, indicating which wave enables the linking of the next one.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Delineation: set the central topic as the root entity and derive the semantic universe (subtopics and adjacent entities). Validate exhaustive coverage for an expert, not superficial coverage. If the universe exceeds what a single coherent authority can sustain, propose a scope reduction and justify it before continuing.
Phase 2 - Architecture: assign each subtopic to a layer. The pillar covers the topic in breadth; each cluster deepens a subtopic; each satellite resolves a specific intent. Avoid cannibalization between pieces competing for the same intent; when two pieces collide, declare the conflict and propose a merge or intent reassignment.
Phase 3 - Intent mapping: classify intent and journey stage per piece; verify that the hub covers the full funnel, not just the top. Flag funnel gaps (e.g., heavy awareness, no decision) as a risk.

--- S | SITUATION ---
You will design the structure of a Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram) campaign with Advantage Campaign Budget (CBO): a single budget lives at the campaign level and the algorithm allocates it in real time between ad sets toward the audience and creative combinations with the best performance. The real unit of learning is not the account but the ad set: each ad set needs sufficient signal density for the algorithm to model who to serve. A poorly built hierarchy (too many ad sets, overlapping audiences, a budget that cannot feed learning, unnecessary spend caps, edits that reset learning) fragments signals, keeps ad sets trapped in the learning phase, and drives up the cost per result. The correct structure concentrates signals, exits learning, and lets the system invest where it performs. The goal is a campaign that is ready to build and read with clear criteria — not to be improvised.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior paid media strategist specializing in Meta Ads, with experience managing campaign-level budgets (CBO/Advantage) in performance accounts and mastery of the learning phase, attribution, and audience overlap.

Deliverable: a complete, buildable CBO campaign structure. Steps:
1. Define the correct campaign objective and optimization event for META_NEGOCIO and EVENTO_CONVERSION, justifying the choice against the funnel (do not optimize an event deeper than the volume can sustain).
2. Determine the number of ad sets and the segmentation logic for each based on AUDIENCIAS, avoiding overlap that would cannibalize delivery (audiences that intersect compete in the same auction and raise costs). Start with a few broad ad sets; consolidating is preferable to multiplying. Indicate where to activate Advantage+ Audience as a signal and where to constrain it.
3. Recommend campaign-level budget using the 50x rule: each active ad set should be able to reach approximately 50 conversions of the event per week to exit the learning phase. If TICKET_PROMEDIO or NIVEL_INVERSION do not allow it, propose a higher-funnel event (e.g., initiate checkout or add to cart instead of purchase) and explain the proxy-vs-final-event trade-off.
4. Indicate whether minimum/maximum spend caps per ad set are advisable and why; by default do not use them, because they restrict the algorithm and can prevent exiting learning. Valid exception: protecting a strategic audience (e.g., retargeting) from receiving no delivery.
5. Define 3 to 5 ads per ad set with distinct creative angles (not cosmetic variations of the same message) and a consistent naming convention (campaign | ad set | creative), traceable and filterable in reports.
6. Deliver a table with the final structure (campaign, ad sets, placements, attribution window, creatives) ready for Ads Manager.
7. Specify reading rules: duration and care of the learning phase, which edits reset it and which do not, the metric that defines the winner (aligned to META_NEGOCIO, not vanity metrics), when to consolidate, and when to pause.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Validation: confirm that META_NEGOCIO, EVENTO_CONVERSION, AUDIENCIAS, TICKET_PROMEDIO, and NIVEL_INVERSION are present. Critical: the event and whether a pixel/CAPI is installed and verified; without a conversion signal, recommend a proxy objective or traffic and warn of the limitation. If a critical piece of data is missing, request it before designing.

Phase 2 - Ad sets: define quantity, segmentation, and placements (default Advantage+ placements unless there is an explicit reason to constrain, e.g., a format that underperforms in a specific placement); rule out overlaps and name the cannibalization risk.
Phase 3 - Budget: set the campaign budget coherent with learning (relative, no amounts); decide spend caps only if there is an explicit strategic reason.
Phase 4 - Creatives: 3 to 5 angles per ad set + naming convention; relate each angle to an audience pain point or motivator.
Phase 5 - Table and reading rules: build the ready-to-use table and decision rules; close with a two-week iteration plan (what to watch, what not to touch to avoid resetting learning, what to adjust).

--- S | SITUATION ---
Scaling paid media without a method burns budget: creative variants accumulate without knowing what moves the needle, and decisions are made based on team opinion or the apparent winner from the past week. This plan turns paid advertising into a learning system: each round isolates one variable, tests a falsifiable hypothesis, and promotes only winners with statistical backing. It unlocks a creative iteration machine where learning accumulates round by round and acquisition cost drops sustainably instead of depending on lucky guesses.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior creative testing strategist in paid media, with experience managing acquisition budgets on {{PLATAFORMA}} and designing experiments with statistical rigor.
Deliverable: iterative creative testing plan for the campaign "{{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}", optimized toward {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}, ready to run the first round.

1. Prioritize test variables (hook, format, message angle, offer, CTA) in a table by expected impact vs. effort; if {{VARIABLE_FOCO}} was specified, place it in the first round. Test highest impact, lowest effort first.
2. Define one variable per round, isolated from the rest, so that learning is attributable. If combinations need to be explored, explicitly declare when to move to a multivariate design and its sample cost.
3. Formulate a falsifiable hypothesis per variant: if I change X then I expect Y on {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} because W. Without the "because" there is no transferable learning.
4. Set the winner criterion before launching: primary metric, minimum detectable effect (MDE), confidence level, target power, and sample size derived from {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}. The MDE must be a business MDE, not just statistical: define what improvement justifies changing the control.
5. Define guardrail metrics to avoid false winners: one of cost/efficiency (e.g., CTR rises but CPA spikes) and one of downstream quality (e.g., initial conversion rises but retention, LTV, or lead-to-sale drops).
6. Build the iteration cadence: the valid winner becomes the control for the next round; the loser is archived with its learning. Include an early-stop protocol to halt clearly losing variants and protect budget.
7. Deliver a cumulative learning log template that turns each round into reusable knowledge (variable, hypothesis, result, decision, transferable learning).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm objective, platform, primary metric, conversion volume, and budget in investment units. If any is missing, ask before continuing.
Phase 2 - Sizing: calculate minimum sample, power, and learning window from {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}; respect the {{PLATAFORMA}} algorithm's learning phase and do not read results during it. If volume does not reach significance, warn about the risk of inconclusive tests and propose alternatives: sequential testing with correction, early signals (CTR, play-through rate, hook rate), consolidating budget into fewer variants, or raising the MDE to make the test decidable.
Phase 3 - Design: build the prioritized variable table and the test matrix (control, variant, hypothesis, primary metric, guardrail, cut criterion, early-stop rule).
Phase 4 - Cadence: define a round-by-round calendar with promotion, archiving, and creative refresh rules for fatigue, plus the log template.
Edge cases: if two variants tie within the margin of error, keep both and break the tie with a guardrail or a confirmation round; never declare a winner without an actionable difference.
Do not invent benchmarks or historical figures — mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:

- Each variant has a falsifiable hypothesis with metric, expected direction, and mechanism (the "because").
- Winner criterion set before launching: primary metric, business MDE, confidence level, target power, and sample size coherent with {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}.
