1. Objective and metrics: main metric (qualified sign-ups on waitlist + expected conversion on launch day) and 2-3 guide metrics (teaser open rate / CTR, double opt-in confirmation rate, cost per sign-up if applicable). Explicitly define what counts as a qualified sign-up.
2. Waitlist mechanics supported by {{BENEFICIO_DIFERENCIAL}}: value proposition for signing up, entry hook, fields to capture (minimum viable, justify each one), confirmation sequence (double opt-in + welcome), and a membership benefit that rewards being inside before the general public.
3. Segmentation: how to distinguish hot prospects from lukewarm ones (short survey, micro-commitment, behavioral signal) and how to treat each segment differently at close.
4. Countdown teaser calendar by channel, adjusted to {{DURACION_PRELANZAMIENTO}}: number of teasers, angle of each (problem, partial glimpse, social proof, objection handling, date reveal), the central copy piece, and a suggested asset (visual or text format).
5. Legitimate scarcity and urgency mechanisms: limited spots, early-access window for the list, visible countdown and sign-up close — each with a real, verifiable foundation. Mark the boundary between genuine scarcity and invented urgency.
6. Day-by-day schedule from kickoff to {{FECHA_SALIDA}}: what piece goes out each day, through which channel, with what call to action, and what metric is reviewed that day.
7. Contingency plan: correction levers if sign-ups are running below target at the midpoint of the campaign (hook reinforcement, additional channel, angle adjustment) — all compatible with ethical scarcity.
8. Pre-launch-day verification checklist.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Frame: set objective and metrics; if PRODUCTO, FECHA_SALIDA, AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO, BENEFICIO_DIFERENCIAL, or CANALES are missing, ask before drafting. Label every assumption with [SUPUESTO]; if DURACION_PRELANZAMIENTO is missing, assume a reasonable window and declare it.
Phase 2 - Capture: design the waitlist, its minimum fields, and the membership benefit.
Phase 3 - Segmentation: define how to qualify and split the list by intent temperature.
Phase 4 - Dosing: build the countdown teaser cadence by channel and angle, with copy and asset.
Phase 5 - Conversion: define the scarcity mechanisms, each with a verifiable foundation (no false urgency).
Phase 6 - Orchestration: assemble the day-by-day schedule, contingency plan, and closing checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The main metric defines qualified sign-up and separates real demand from empty reach.
- The waitlist has a clear value proposition, minimum justified fields, and a real membership benefit.
- Segmentation distinguishes hot from lukewarm with an observable signal, not an arbitrary label.
- Each teaser has a distinct angle, does not repeat its message, and the countdown is coherent with {{DURACION_PRELANZAMIENTO}}.
- Each scarcity mechanism has a verifiable foundation; zero invented urgency (the boundary is made explicit).
- The schedule covers every day up to {{FECHA_SALIDA}} with piece, channel, call to action, and metric.
- The contingency plan offers concrete levers without resorting to false urgency or discounts.
- No prices and no the word "free"; neutral, professional English, no emojis.
- Assumptions labeled [SUPUESTO]; missing data asked for, not invented.
Expected deliverable: ready-to-execute pre-launch sequence (objective + metrics + waitlist + segmentation + teaser calendar + scarcity plan + day-by-day schedule + contingency plan + verification checklist).
spec-marketing_plan_account_based_market:

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to concentrate marketing and sales on a bounded set of high-value accounts rather than generating scattered demand. A well-orchestrated ABM plan unlocks higher-quality pipeline, shortens the cycle on strategic accounts, and aligns both teams around the same accounts and buying groups. The plan must be executable by a small team and measurable from week one, without depending on unconfirmed budget.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior B2B account-based marketing strategist with experience orchestrating one-to-one and one-to-few campaigns between marketing and sales in complex buying cycles.

Deliver an ABM campaign plan with these numbered sections:
1. ICP and scoring: firmographic, technographic, and intent-signal criteria; weighted and replicable scoring model (weights per dimension, cut-off threshold, and tie-breaker rule) to prioritize the short list from {{NUMERO_CUENTAS}}.
2. Buying group: map of the five roles (economic decision-maker, champion, user, technical influencer, blocker) with a specific pain, likely objection, and distinct core message per role, anchored in {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}.
3. Tiering: one-to-one / one-to-few / one-to-many classification based on {{TICKET_PROMEDIO}} and account value, with personalization level, recommended coverage, and promotion or demotion criteria between tiers.
4. Orchestration: week-by-week matrix by journey stage (attraction, engagement, conversion, expansion) crossing channels (LinkedIn, email, content, events, direct sales), triggers, and sequence, sized to {{CICLO_VENTA}}.
5. Content and alignment: personalized assets per account or cluster, plus the marketing-sales model (handoff SLA, definition of an engaged account, joint review cadence).
6. Measurement: dashboard with stage-level metrics, account engagement, influenced pipeline, attribution model, and one early success signal per tier observable in the first two weeks.

Declare explicit assumptions, plan limitations, and trade-offs (coverage vs. personalization depth).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, {{NUMERO_CUENTAS}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{TICKET_PROMEDIO}}, and {{CICLO_VENTA}}; incorporate {{SENALES_INTENCION}} if available. Tag every missing or assumed data point as [SUPUESTO] and ask in a single batch before proceeding.
Phase 2 Design: derive ICP and scoring; from scoring define tiering; from tiering derive the buying group and messages per role. Maintain explicit traceability between each step.
Phase 3 Orchestrate: build the week-by-week multichannel matrix aligned to the sales cycle, with stage triggers and content assets per tier.
Phase 4 Measure and align: close with the marketing-sales SLA, metrics dashboard, attribution model, and early signal per tier.
Edge cases: a very short list (fewer than ~10) forces one-to-one; a very long list leans toward one-to-few/many and requires a stricter scoring threshold; without intent signals, substitute proxies (firmographic fit, technographic fit, industry events) and tag as [SUPUESTO]; an incomplete buying group defines the contact-discovery priority.

spec-marketing_modelo_mensaje_campana_ai:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} > Product or service being promoted in the campaign
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Target audience (segment, role, context, level of problem awareness)
- TENSION_PRINCIPAL: {{TENSION_PRINCIPAL}} > Core pain, desire, or tension driving the audience
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} > Differential benefit versus the current alternative
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Channel carrying the message (defines length, format, and tone)
- ACCION_OBJETIVO: {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} > Exact and singular action sought from the prospect
- PRUEBA_DISPONIBLE: {{PRUEBA_DISPONIBLE}} > Citable evidence (case study, data point, demo, testimonial) or "No proof"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need a campaign message that not only informs but guides the prospect step by step toward an action. The AIDA model structures that narrative across four successive mental states (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action), preventing the message from scattering or requesting action before desire has been built. Risk to neutralize: hooks that promise what the body does not deliver, blocks that invade the next block's function, and multiple calls to action that dilute conversion. A well-ordered message unlocks measurable conversion and a reusable asset for channel variants.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior direct-response advertising copywriter with mastery of persuasion psychology and channel calibration.
Deliverable: message labeled by the four AIDA blocks + publishable full-run version + two Attention hook variants. Steps:
1. Map the seven inputs; flag every missing data point as pending and declare the audience's awareness level (unaware of the problem / aware / seeking a solution / comparing options), which determines the load of each block.
2. Attention: a hook that interrupts the scroll, names the audience or their tension, and promises relevance in the first line; the promise must be fulfilled by the body.
3. Interest: data, context, or a reframe of the problem that sustains reading and connects with TENSION_PRINCIPAL; no selling yet.
4. Desire: translate PROPUESTA_VALOR into desirable and concrete outcomes, anchor PRUEBA_DISPONIBLE (or tag [SUPUESTO] if unavailable), and neutralize the main foreseeable objection.
5. Action: a single clear instruction toward ACCION_OBJETIVO, with low perceived risk and a legitimate reason to act now (no artificial pressure).
6. Calibrate length, format, and tone to CANAL; produce two hook variants with different angles (e.g. tension vs. aspiration).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate inputs, declare awareness level, and define the single core promise.
Phase 2 AIDA Build: write the four blocks in order, verifying that each fulfills its own function and does not invade the next.
Phase 3 Calibration: adjust to the channel, remove filler, ensure a single call to action, hook-body coherence, and generate the variants.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The four AIDA blocks appear, labeled and in order, each fulfilling only its own function.
- The Attention hook's promise is fulfilled by the body (no clickbait); the Desire block includes proof or [SUPUESTO] and handles one objection; the Action is singular and low-risk.
- Message calibrated to CANAL in length, format, and tone; block load coherent with the declared awareness level.
- No prices; no use of the word free; neutral professional English, no emojis.
- Every product claim is defensible; anything unconfirmed is tagged [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: message labeled by blocks + publishable full-run version + two Attention hook variants (different angles).
spec-marketing_plan_partnership_co_marke:
[inputs]

- OBJETIVO_CAMPANA: {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}} > Business objective of the joint campaign (leads, influenced pipeline, event registrations, awareness, entry into a new segment)

- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Campaign target window and desired launch date (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are planning a co-marketing campaign with a partner to activate both audience bases with shared and fair effort. A good plan unlocks access to a new and qualified audience at marginal cost, distributes asset production across two teams, and multiplies reach without doubling investment. Risks to avoid: diffuse alliances with no shared metric, unfair lead distribution, cross-contact that drives unsubscribes and spam complaints, and brand clashes. This plan leaves the alliance ready to present and execute with both teams aligned and an agreement ready to sign.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior partner marketing strategist with experience in co-branded B2B campaigns and shared demand-generation models.
Deliver an actionable co-marketing plan with these numbered sections:
1. Joint value proposition: unique alliance narrative (what problem they solve together that neither solves alone), shared target audience, co-branded message angle, and the proof or case that supports the narrative.
2. Fit and objectives: audience overlap and complementarity, SMART objective (reach, qualified leads, registrations, influenced pipeline), a single north metric, and two or three guardrail metrics (unsubscribe rate, spam complaints, coordination cost) to avoid optimizing volume at the expense of brand.
3. Audience sharing: segment each party brings, legal processing and consent basis, who sends to whom, sequencing to avoid overlap or excessive cross-contact, and handling of contacts shared across both lists.
4. Shared assets: inventory of co-branded pieces (joint landing page, webinar or event, downloadable content, email sequence, social kit, press release), owner of each asset, and brand rules for both logos, names, and mention order.
5. Responsibility sharing: RACI-style matrix for who produces, approves, and distributes each asset, with no ambiguous owner, and which channels each party brings with their estimated reach.
6. Calendar: pre-launch, launch, and sustain phases with milestones and dates relative to the target period, including the legal and brand approval window and the critical path.
7. Measurement and result sharing: definition of a shared lead, agreed attribution model, lead-sharing and handoff rules with a follow-up SLA, KPI dashboard, and joint review cadence.
8. Agreements and risks: minimum terms to document (brand use, exclusivity, data, duration, exit clause), risk register with probability, impact, and mitigation, and declared success condition and abort condition for the campaign.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm partner, business objective, audience fit, each party's assets and channels, and target period. If a key data point is missing, the partner is a direct competitor, or the audience fit does not justify the alliance, say so and ask before continuing.
Phase 2 Strategy: define the joint value proposition with its supporting proof, a single north metric with guardrails, and a SMART objective; validate that audience fit justifies the alliance.
Phase 3 Operations: build audience sharing with legal basis and sequencing, asset inventory, unambiguous RACI, phased calendar with critical path, and measurement and lead-sharing model with SLA.
Phase 4 Safeguards: close with minimum agreement terms, risk register with mitigation, and success and abort conditions.
Tag every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and separate confirmed from inferred data. Do not include prices or promises of free offerings; if you need to address investment, use relative effort and in-kind contributions. Neutral professional English.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Clear joint value proposition: articulates the value neither brand delivers alone, with supporting proof.
- A single north metric, measurable SMART objective, and guardrails protecting brand and reputation.
- Explicit audience sharing with legal basis, consent, and anti-cross-contact sequencing.
- Co-branded asset inventory with a single owner and usage rules for both logos and names.
- RACI with no ambiguous owner on any asset.
- Calendar with phases, milestones, relative dates, approval window, and critical path.
- Definition of a shared lead, attribution, sharing and handoff rules with a follow-up SLA.
- Minimum agreement terms (including exit clause) and risks with probability, impact, and mitigation.
- Declared success condition and abort condition.
- Estimates tagged [SUPUESTO]; no prices; no promises of free offerings.
Expected deliverable: co-marketing plan in neutral professional English, in actionable sections, ready to present to both teams and sign the alliance agreement.
spec-marketing_post_mortem_campana:
[inputs]
- CAMPANA: {{CAMPANA}} > Name, period, and purpose of the campaign being evaluated
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Measurable objective and targets per metric (KPI with goal value)
- RESULTADOS: {{RESULTADOS}} > Actual metrics obtained at close
- PRESUPUESTO_RECURSOS: {{PRESUPUESTO_RECURSOS}} > Investment and assigned resources (hours, team, media spend in units; no amounts if not desired)
- AUDIENCIA_CANALES: {{AUDIENCIA_CANALES}} > Target segments and executed channels
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A marketing campaign has just closed and its performance has not yet been converted into knowledge. Without a rigorous post-mortem, the team repeats costly mistakes and inadvertently discards what worked. This analysis converts the close into reusable strategy: it explains why the objective was or was not achieved and leaves actions ready so the next campaign starts from a higher baseline.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Head of Growth specializing in campaign closure and learning, with mastery of objective-vs-actual gap analysis, attribution by channel and funnel stage, and blameless retrospectives.
Deliverable: an actionable post-mortem. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the case from CAMPANA, OBJETIVO, RESULTADOS, PRESUPUESTO_RECURSOS, and AUDIENCIA_CANALES. If any critical data point is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent figures.
2. Quantify the gap per metric: achievement as a percentage and absolute value; classify each as above-target, on-target, or below-target with an explicit threshold (default: on-target = 95 to 105 percent of the goal; declare the threshold used).
3. Attribute causes by channel and by funnel stage (reach, consideration, conversion, retention); separate root cause from symptom; tag every unverifiable assumption as [SUPUESTO].
4. Distill learnings using the Keep / Adjust / Drop framework, derived from the diagnosis.
5. Prioritize by impact and effort; deliver three to five actions with a suggested owner, a measurable success signal, and a time horizon.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm data and objective; if there are gaps, request them.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: achievement table by metric and cause map by channel and funnel stage.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: Keep/Adjust/Drop block consistent with the diagnosis.
Phase 4 - Plan: prioritized actions with owner, success signal, and time horizon.
Attribution limits: if there is no control group, measurement windows overlap, or there were external factors (seasonality, platform changes, news), declare the uncertainty and do not force a single cause. Blameless tone: analyze decisions and mechanisms, not people. No prices or amounts unless they come as input.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every metric in OBJETIVO has its achievement as a percentage and absolute value, classified above/on/below-target with the declared threshold.
- [ ] Every relevant gap has a cause attributed by channel and funnel stage, with root cause distinguished from symptom.
- [ ] Unverifiable assumptions tagged [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures; attribution uncertainty declared when applicable.
- [ ] Keep/Adjust/Drop block consistent and traceable to the diagnosis.
- [ ] 3 to 5 actions prioritized by impact and effort, each with a suggested owner, a measurable success signal, and a time horizon.
- [ ] Professional, blameless tone; no prices or amounts unless provided as input.
Expected deliverable: post-mortem with achievement table by metric, cause map by channel and funnel stage, Keep/Adjust/Drop block, and prioritized action list.
spec-marketing_modelo_atribucion_multito:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision driving the attribution (e.g. reallocate budget across channels, justify upper-funnel investment, set CAC targets by channel)
- CANALES: {{CANALES}} > Active channels and touchpoints in the journey (paid search, social, email, display, organic, referrals, direct, brand)
- VENTANA_CONVERSION: {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}} > Sales cycle duration and lookback window (e.g. 30-day click, 1-day view)
- METRICA_OBJETIVO: {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} > Metric to attribute (conversions, revenue, qualified leads, pipeline)
- DATOS_DISPONIBLES: {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} > Tracking and data: cross-device, user IDs, costs per channel, conversion volume, consent/cookies (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Credit for a conversion rarely belongs to a single channel: the journey chains several touchpoints before the decision. Attributing everything to the last click undervalues the upper funnel and distorts budget; first-click commits the opposite bias. A well-chosen multitouch attribution model distributes the credit for {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} in an auditable way across {{CANALES}}, unlocking defensible investment decisions for {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}}. Attribution measures correlation of exposure; only an experiment confirms causality.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing analytics analyst, specialist in multitouch attribution and media mix, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from causality.
Deliver an actionable and auditable attribution model design:
1. Reconstruct the typical customer journey over {{CANALES}}: frequent touchpoint order, funnel role of each (discovery/consideration/decision), overlaps, and fit with {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}}.
2. Diagnose {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} and rule on whether a data-driven model is viable or a rules-based model is preferable; declare the conversion volume threshold you assume for a stable estimate and request critical missing data.
3. Compare candidate models in a table (last-touch, first-touch, linear, time decay, positional U 40-20-40, data-driven Shapley/Markov), with bias, implicit assumption, data requirements, and when appropriate; recommend one and justify the fit with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and the accepted trade-off.
4. Define the distribution rules without ambiguity: percentage per touchpoint, repeated channels, direct and brand traffic, lookback, and de-duplication.
5. Apply the model to an example journey with numbers and show the distribution of {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} by channel in a table summing to 100%.
6. Design a validation plan with an incremental experiment (geo-test or holdout) to confirm causality.
Cover edge cases: single-touchpoint journey, view-through without a click, channels that cannot be tracked, and insufficient volume for data-driven.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Mapping: order touchpoints by funnel and frequency; fix the lookback window and criterion for direct and brand sessions.
Phase 2 - Data diagnosis: evaluate cross-device, identifiers, costs, and volume; rule out data-driven if conversion volume does not reach the declared threshold for a stable estimate.
Phase 3 - Selection: contrast models against objective, cycle, and data maturity; recommend and argue the trade-off, never by default.
Phase 4 - Distribution and validation: codify the credit rules, run the numerical example, and design the incremental test with incrementality metric, minimum duration, and decision criterion.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The recommended model is justified against {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, sales cycle, and data maturity, not by default, with the trade-off explicit.
- The data diagnosis declares the assumed volume threshold and rules out data-driven if it is not reached.
- The distribution rules cover repeated channels, direct traffic, brand traffic, lookback, and de-duplication without ambiguity.
- The numerical example sums to 100% of credit and reflects the logic of the chosen model.
- Edge cases (single touchpoint, view-through, channels that cannot be tracked, insufficient volume) have explicit treatment.
- Every figure not provided by the user is tagged [SUPUESTO].
- The validation plan includes an incremental experiment with a decision criterion that tests causality, not just correlation.
- Closes with model limitations and a periodic review criterion.
Expected deliverable: document with mapped journey, data diagnosis, candidate model comparison table, recommended model justified, distribution rules, distribution table of {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} by channel, validation plan with incremental test, and limitations.
spec-marketing_dashboard_kpis_marketing:
[inputs]

- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who reads and decides (e.g., C-level, marketing lead, performance analyst) and their level of detail

--- S | SITUATION ---
A marketing KPI dashboard only creates value if it drives decisions; most fail by accumulating vanity metrics, mixing audiences in a single view, lacking a single definition per metric, and not declaring a data owner. Designing the blueprint for {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, read by {{AUDIENCIA}} over the {{MODELO_EMBUDO}} funnel and intended for {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}}, unlocks fast and traceable decisions, aligns the team on a single source of truth, and reduces reporting time in favor of analysis.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing analytics analyst with experience building decision dashboards in BI tools (Looker Studio, Power BI, Tableau) and in funnel modeling.
Deliver the complete dashboard blueprint through these steps:
1. Confirm the objective, audience, and funnel, and explain how they shape metric selection; if clarity or a critical piece of information is missing (channels, comparison baseline, tool, available granularity), ask for it; if you must proceed anyway, propose a standard and flag the assumption as [SUPUESTO].
2. Build the metric-objective tree: from {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} derive the north metric and its drivers, and filter out every KPI that does not move it.
3. Select 5 to 9 primary KPIs mapped to the funnel (acquisition, activation, conversion, retention, revenue), avoiding vanity metrics; for each KPI provide the exact formula, unit, source, update frequency, data owner, and why it moves the objective.
4. Define segments and cut dimensions over {{CANALES}} (campaign, audience, geography, device, period) and the global filters; declare the attribution rule used and its limitation.
5. Design the visual layer hierarchy: executive (3 to 5 north KPIs plus trend), tactical (breakdown by channel and campaign), diagnostic (funnel plus cohorts); for each metric indicate the correct visualization type and justify it by its analytical intent.
6. Define targets, thresholds, and alert rules per KPI (green, amber, red) and the comparison baseline ({{COMPARACION_BASE}}); indicate what action each red state triggers.
7. Close with governance: source table with data owner, single definition per metric, review cadence, and criterion for retiring or replacing a KPI.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: derive the metric-objective tree from {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and filter out every KPI that does not move it.
Phase 2 - Selection: map each KPI to a stage of the {{MODELO_EMBUDO}} funnel; discard vanity by applying the actionable-relevant-comparable criterion.
Phase 3 - Structure: order segments and layers by {{AUDIENCIA}}, from aggregate to granular; separate mixed audiences into distinct layers.
Phase 4 - Visualization: assign the chart according to analytical intent (trend, comparison, composition, distribution, detail) and the constraints of {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}}.
Phase 5 - Alerts and governance: set thresholds, comparison baseline, action per red state, and data contract.
Edge cases to resolve explicitly: incomplete or latency-affected data (downgrade frequency or flag the KPI as provisional), ambiguous multi-touch attribution (declare the rule and its bias), KPIs that contradict each other across stages (prioritize by proximity to objective), mixed audiences (do not mix in one view). State data limitations and trade-offs (e.g., executive simplicity vs. diagnostic depth).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Every KPI is mapped to a funnel stage and to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; zero vanity metrics without justification.
- Every KPI has a formula, unit, source, frequency, data owner, and a green/amber/red threshold with an action tied to red.
- There is an explicit metric-objective tree that filters out what does not move the objective.
- Layers are separated by audience and every visualization is justified by its analytical intent.
- There is a single definition per metric, a source table with a data owner, and a declared attribution rule with its limitation.
- Every assumption is tagged [SUPUESTO]; missing data is requested, not invented; edge cases and trade-offs are explicit.
Expected deliverable: actionable dashboard blueprint (metric-objective tree, catalog of 5 to 9 KPIs, segment map with attribution rule, three-layer layout with chart types, alert matrix with actions, and governance contract) ready to implement in any BI tool.
spec-marketing_calculo_cac_ltv_ratio:
[inputs]
- GASTO_ADQUISICION: {{GASTO_ADQUISICION}} > Total marketing and sales spend for the period (advertising, acquisition team salaries, agencies, tools); use accrued spend for the period, not cash basis
- CLIENTES_NUEVOS: {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}} > New customers acquired in the same period; exclude renewals and reactivations to avoid diluting CAC
- ARPA: {{ARPA}} > Average revenue per customer per period (Average Revenue Per Account); clarify whether gross or net of discounts
- MARGEN_BRUTO: {{MARGEN_BRUTO}} > Gross margin as a fraction or percentage (revenue minus cost to serve); convert to a fraction before calculating LTV
- CHURN: {{CHURN}} > Customer churn rate per period; (optional) if unavailable, provide VIDA_PROMEDIO in months
- VIDA_PROMEDIO: {{VIDA_PROMEDIO}} > (Optional) Average customer lifetime in months; only if CHURN is unavailable, for the alternative LTV method
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Reference period for normalization (monthly, quarterly, or annual)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The business needs to know whether its acquisition engine creates or destroys value before scaling growth investment. CAC, LTV, and the LTV:CAC ratio convert dispersed spend into a unit economics diagnostic: they unlock the decision to invest more, sustain, or correct, and give marketing, finance, and leadership a common language to justify budget. The fragility of the diagnostic lies not in the arithmetic but in the consistency of definitions, periods, and time units.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior unit economics and growth marketing analyst with experience in subscription and recurring-revenue models.
Deliverable: diagnostic of the three metrics with a table, verdict, and prioritized recommendations. Steps:
1. Normalize all figures to a single PERIODO and currency; convert MARGEN_BRUTO to a fraction; list missing data and ask for it if critical.
2. Calculate CAC = GASTO_ADQUISICION / CLIENTES_NUEVOS, showing the formula with the actual values.
3. Calculate LTV using the margin method = ARPA x MARGEN_BRUTO / CHURN; if CHURN is unavailable, use the alternative method LTV = ARPA x MARGEN_BRUTO x VIDA_PROMEDIO (months) and flag it.
4. Calculate the LTV:CAC ratio and the CAC payback period = CAC / (ARPA x MARGEN_BRUTO) in months.
5. Interpret each result against benchmarks and issue a health verdict.
6. Propose three prioritized levers to improve the ratio (lower CAC, raise MARGEN_BRUTO, reduce CHURN, or increase ARPA), each with its expected effect on the ratio.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Normalization: align period and currency; convert margin to a fraction; flag with [SUPUESTO] any estimated value; never invent figures.
Phase 2 CAC Calculation: apply the formula and show the numerical workings; note if GASTO_ADQUISICION mixes fixed costs that distort the period.
Phase 3 LTV Calculation: apply the margin method; document the method used and its limitations (linear churn assumed, no time-value-of-money discount).
Phase 4 Ratio and Payback: calculate the ratio and interpret against benchmarks (ratio < 1 destroys value; 1 to 3 is tight; ~3 is healthy; >> 3 may indicate underinvestment by growing too slowly). Validate that the time units for CHURN, ARPA, and payback are consistent (payback < 12 months is comfortable).
Edge cases: CLIENTES_NUEVOS = 0 -> CAC is undefined, report it and ask for a period with acquisitions; CHURN = 0 or near zero -> LTV tends to infinity, cap at an explicit horizon (e.g., 36 months) and flag it; MARGEN_BRUTO negative -> LTV does not apply and the engine loses money per unit, scaling destroys it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All figures normalized to the same PERIODO and currency; MARGEN_BRUTO in fraction form; time units consistent across churn, ARPA, and payback.
- [ ] CAC, LTV, ratio, and payback show an explicit formula with the actual numbers.
- [ ] LTV method declared (margin or alternative by average lifetime) with its limitations and assumptions (linearity, horizon, no time discount).
- [ ] Edge cases checked (customers = 0, churn = 0, negative margin) and resolved or flagged.
- [ ] Every estimated value tagged [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures.
- [ ] Health verdict interpreted against the cited benchmarks, not in the abstract.
- [ ] Three prioritized, actionable recommendations, each with its expected effect on the ratio.
Expected deliverable: table (metric | formula | result | reading) + verdict in one sentence + three prioritized recommendations + the highest-leverage question about which data point to refine.
spec-marketing_analisis_cohortes_retenci:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product, app, or service whose users are being analyzed
- GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE: {{GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE}} > Unit for grouping by entry date (weekly or monthly)
- EVENTO_ACTIVO: {{EVENTO_ACTIVO}} > Event that defines a user as active in a period (login, purchase, session, key action)
- TIPO_RETENCION: {{TIPO_RETENCION}} > Measurement criterion: N-day (active exactly on period N), unbounded (active on N or after), or rolling (active within a rolling window)
- HORIZONTE_PERIODOS: {{HORIZONTE_PERIODOS}} > Number of subsequent periods to measure per cohort
- SEGMENTO_O_CANAL: {{SEGMENTO_O_CANAL}} > Dimension for comparing cohorts: acquisition channel, plan, geography, or segment (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to understand the true health of retention by separating signal from growth noise. Grouping users by entry date and comparing their curves over time makes it possible to distinguish whether the product improves cohort over cohort, where value is lost, and whether product or acquisition changes moved the needle. The analysis unlocks investment decisions in onboarding, channels, and retention, and feeds LTV projections more honest than a global churn rate, which hides the mix of new and mature cohorts. An imprecise reading leads to overinvesting in acquisition when the problem is early retention, or vice versa.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior retention and growth analyst, expert in product analytics and cohort matrix interpretation for marketing and product teams.
Deliverable: cohort and retention curve report. Steps:
1. Define precisely the cohort unit (GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE), the EVENTO_ACTIVO that counts as retention, and the TIPO_RETENCION applied; specify period 0 (entry) and the window of each period; declare every assumption as [SUPUESTO].
2. Build the cohort matrix: rows = cohort by entry date, columns = periods 0..HORIZONTE_PERIODOS since entry, cells = retention percentage over each cohort's size. Report the size (n) of each cohort and exclude or flag cells from recent cohorts that have not yet matured the period, to avoid survivorship bias. Flag cohorts with small n as low confidence.
3. Plot the superimposed retention curves per cohort; identify the retention floor (plateau), the period at which it stabilizes, the magnitude of early churn (drop from period 0 to 1), and the slope of subsequent decay.
4. Compare cohorts against SEGMENTO_O_CANAL and over time: flag which ones improve or worsen, distinguish true improvement from a mix effect (more traffic from a low-retention channel depresses the average without any cohort worsening), and correlate breakpoints with known launches, campaigns, or channel changes without asserting causality.
5. Close with 3 to 5 recommendations prioritized by expected impact on the curve, distinguishing early-churn interventions from sustained-decay interventions, each with the lever, the metric it would move, and how to validate it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpretation: restate the objective, confirm definitions of active user, cohort unit, and retention type, and list missing data (including the data cut-off date).
Phase 2 Structure: build the matrix, normalize to percentage over each cohort's size, isolate immature cells, and annotate n per cohort.
Phase 3 Reading: derive curves, floor, early churn, decay slope, and segment/channel comparatives, separating signal from noise and mix from true improvement.
Phase 4 Synthesis: translate findings into prioritized recommendations with the lever, the metric, and the test that would confirm the effect.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] EVENTO_ACTIVO, GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE, TIPO_RETENCION, and period 0 defined without ambiguity.
- [ ] Matrix in percentage over each cohort's size, with n reported and immature cells excluded or flagged (no survivorship bias).
- [ ] Superimposed curves with retention floor, stabilization period, and decay slope identified.
- [ ] Early churn quantified and separated from sustained decay.
- [ ] Cohort/time comparison that distinguishes true improvement from mix effect and correlates with known events without asserting causality.
- [ ] Cohorts with small n flagged as low confidence.
- [ ] Assumptions tagged [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures; every figure supported by data.
- [ ] 3 to 5 recommendations prioritized by impact on the curve, each with a lever, a metric, and a validation method.
Expected deliverable: report with cohort matrix, description of curves and floor, business reading (signal vs. noise, mix vs. true improvement), and prioritized recommendations, ready to review with marketing and product teams.
spec-marketing_plan_medicion_kpi_tree:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Business objective to measure and its time horizon
- METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA: {{METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA}} > Candidate north metric or central value hypothesis (optional)
- MODELO_NEGOCIO: {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} > Business model and value proposition (what it sells, to whom, how it earns)
- ETAPAS_FUNNEL: {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} > Relevant funnel or lifecycle stages (acquisition, activation, retention, etc.)
- FUENTES_DATOS: {{FUENTES_DATOS}} > Available data sources and analytics tools
- MADUREZ_MEDICION: {{MADUREZ_MEDICION}} > Current measurement maturity level (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need a measurement plan that connects {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} to actionable metrics, not a loose dashboard of vanity figures. The purpose is to trace an auditable causal chain from instrumentable activity to business value: every team should know which driver it moves, how it is calculated, and which event the data comes from. Completing this unlocks a meaningful dashboard, performance conversations based on levers (not symptoms), and a clear instrumentation roadmap for the data team. Risk to avoid: a visually appealing tree that cannot be instrumented, or metrics the team cannot move.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Head of Marketing Analytics with experience building measurement plans and KPI trees (north-star metric, driver trees, input-output models) in digital businesses.

Deliver a complete, auditable measurement plan with KPI tree:
1. North metric: define 1 north-star aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, its formula, why it measures value delivered to the customer and not just activity, and 1-2 health counter-metrics to prevent gaming. Validate or reject {{METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA}} with an explicit argument.
2. KPI Tree: decompose the north-star into level-1 KPIs with an explicit equation (sum, product, or funnel) and each KPI into level-2 drivers actionable by an owner. Present it as an indented hierarchy showing the mathematical relationship between each level; maximum 3 levels to keep it operable.
3. Metric cards: for each north-star, KPI, and driver provide name, one-sentence definition, exact formula, unit, time granularity, cut dimensions, data source, owner, and target/threshold with baseline.
4. Instrumentation plan: list events and properties to capture to feed the drivers according to {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, mark existing vs. to-instrument, define an event naming convention, and deliver the event -> driver -> KPI -> north-star map plus a data quality validation plan (completeness, freshness, consistency).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - North: anchor the north-star to customer value according to {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}; validate that it is not vanity using the counter-metric test (if raising the north-star could deteriorate the experience or economics, add the counter-metric that monitors it).
Phase 2 - Decomposition: derive levels only with explicit mathematical relationships; a driver is valid only if a team can move it directly. Use {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} as the skeleton when the model is funnel-based. Flag whether the contribution of each branch is high/medium/low to prioritize.
Phase 3 - Operationalization: complete each card; any inferred figure, baseline, or target is tagged [SUPUESTO] with the assumption stated. Do not invent industry benchmarks; if needed, ask for them. If {{MADUREZ_MEDICION}} is low, prioritize already-instrumentable drivers and flag those that depend on new capture.
Phase 4 - Instrumentation: map each driver to >= 1 event; no driver is left without an event. Define consistent naming (object_action, snake_case) and data quality validation rules. Flag capture dependencies that block measuring a driver.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Single north-star, with formula and centered on value delivered, not activity; {{METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA}} evaluated with an argument.
- Each tree level exposes its explicit mathematical relationship to the level above; maximum 3 levels.
- Every driver is an actionable lever with an assigned owner.
- Every metric (north-star, KPI, driver) has a complete card: definition, formula, unit, granularity, dimensions, source, owner, target/baseline.
- Every driver is covered by at least one instrumented event and appears in the event -> driver -> KPI -> north-star map.
- Event naming convention defined and data quality validation plan (completeness, freshness, consistency) included.
- Every inferred figure tagged [SUPUESTO]; no invented benchmarks.
- If {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}}, or {{FUENTES_DATOS}} are missing, they are asked for before executing.
Expected deliverable: measurement plan document with north-star section, indented KPI tree, metric card table, event instrumentation table, and event -> north-star traceability map.
spec-marketing_diseno_ab_test_significan:
[inputs]
- HIPOTESIS_O_CAMBIO: {{HIPOTESIS_O_CAMBIO}} > Specific decision or change to test (e.g., new CTA, new landing page, email subject line)
- METRICA_PRIMARIA: {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} > Primary metric and randomization unit (e.g., conversion rate per unique visitor)
- TASA_BASE: {{TASA_BASE}} > Current value of the primary metric in the control (e.g., 3.2%)
- MDE: {{MDE}} > Minimum detectable effect that justifies the business decision, absolute or relative (e.g., +0.5pp or +15% relative)
- VOLUMEN_DISPONIBLE: {{VOLUMEN_DISPONIBLE}} > Available traffic or volume per period to split across variants (e.g., 8,000 visitors/week)
- ALFA_Y_POTENCIA: {{ALFA_Y_POTENCIA}} > Significance level and power (optional; default alpha 0.05 two-tailed, power 0.80)
- NUM_VARIANTES: {{NUM_VARIANTES}} > Number of variants including control (optional; default 2 = A/B)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a marketing decision into a statistically defensible A/B experiment. Not to launch blindly: to know upfront how much sample is required, what effect can be detected, how long it will run, and under what rule a winner is declared. This unlocks evidence-based decisions, avoids false positives from peeking, and protects the budget from iterations that do not move the needle. The resulting plan must be handed off to a growth team or loaded into an experimentation tool and executed without reinterpretation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing experimentation and applied statistics expert (CRO/growth), with command of proportion hypothesis tests, power calculations, and experiment design.
Deliver an A/B test plan with these numbered components:
1. Explicit, falsifiable null and alternative hypotheses; primary metric with its randomization unit; maximum 2-3 secondary or guardrail metrics, of which at least one must be a business health metric that must not degrade (e.g., revenue per session, churn rate, latency).
2. Sample size per variant from TASA_BASE, MDE, alpha, and power; show the two-proportion test formula and total n. If NUM_VARIANTES > 2, calculate n for the most demanding contrast and apply a multiple comparison correction.
3. Estimated duration in days using VOLUMEN_DISPONIBLE, rounded up to full weekly cycles to neutralize intra-week seasonality. If duration exceeds 4-6 weeks, warn about cookie/session contamination risk and propose a lever (reduce variants, raise MDE, or increase traffic).
4. Pre-registered decision criterion in a table: condition that declares a winner, inconclusive condition, and stopping rule (no peeking before reaching n; if continuous monitoring is required, declare a sequential test upfront with its adjusted threshold).
5. Assumptions and threats to validity: one vs. two tails, multiple comparison correction, peeking risk, novelty/primacy effect, sampling representativeness, unit interference (SUTVA), and assignment balance check (sample ratio mismatch).
Close with a one-line summary per component for operational handoff.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm the randomization unit and primary metric; validate that TASA_BASE and MDE are on the same basis (absolute or relative) and are coherent; verify that the primary metric is a proportion (if it is continuous or a count, declare that the two-proportion test does not apply and ask for the correct method).
Phase 2 - Parameters: fix alpha and power (default alpha 0.05 two-tailed, power 0.80 if not specified) and justify the MDE in business terms (what decision does that effect enable).
Phase 3 - Calculation: estimate n per variant with the two-proportion formula, derive total n (x NUM_VARIANTES) and duration in days and weeks; show the numerical substitution step by step.
Phase 4 - Decision: draft the criteria table, the stopping rule, and the test invalidation conditions.
Rules: if TASA_BASE, MDE, VOLUMEN_DISPONIBLE, alpha, or power are missing, ask for them specifically before calculating; do not invent figures; flag every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and every derived value with its visible formula.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit, falsifiable null and alternative hypotheses.
- [ ] Primary metric with defined randomization unit; secondary/guardrail metrics limited to 2-3 with at least one business health metric.
- [ ] Validated that the primary metric is a proportion before applying the two-proportion test.
- [ ] n per variant and total n with visible, reproducible formula and numerical substitution.
- [ ] Alpha, power, and MDE declared and justified; one vs. two tails specified.
- [ ] Multiple comparison correction applied if NUM_VARIANTES > 2.
- [ ] Duration in days and weeks, rounded to full weekly cycles; warning issued if it exceeds 4-6 weeks.
- [ ] Decision table with winner / inconclusive / stopping rule without peeking.
- [ ] Threats to validity listed (multiple comparisons, novelty, sampling, SUTVA, sample ratio mismatch).
- [ ] No invented figures; estimates tagged [SUPUESTO]; missing data requested.
Expected deliverable: a self-contained A/B experiment plan with a sample/duration table, decision table, and one-line summary per component, ready to hand off to a team or load into an experimentation tool.
spec-marketing_marketing_mix_modeling:
[inputs]
- MARCA_O_CATEGORIA: {{MARCA_O_CATEGORIA}} > Brand, product, or category whose sales are being modeled
- CANALES: {{CANALES}} > Investment channels to evaluate (e.g., TV, search, paid social, display, OOH, promotions)
- GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL: {{GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL}} > Series frequency (weekly or monthly)
- HORIZONTE_HISTORICO: {{HORIZONTE_HISTORICO}} > Period covered by the data (e.g., Jan-2023 to Dec-2025)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision the model enables (e.g., reallocate investment, justify TV)
- PRESUPUESTO_ACTUAL: {{PRESUPUESTO_ACTUAL}} > Current investment distribution by channel (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Marketing investment decisions often rely on last-click metrics that over-credit bottom-funnel channels and ignore lagged and brand effects. An econometric Marketing Mix Model (MMM) estimates the incremental contribution of each channel to the sales of {{MARCA_O_CATEGORIA}}, controlling for exogenous factors, to reallocate budget based on evidence rather than inertia. Unlocks: justifying investment to finance, detecting saturated or underinvested channels, and building a media StrategyIA based on real marginal ROI for {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Unlike digital attribution, MMM captures offline media, cross-channel halo effects, and brand carryover that last-click cannot see.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing science econometrician, expert in MMM, time series, and media response curves, with the judgment to distinguish spurious correlation from causal effect and to communicate uncertainty without glossing over it.

Deliverable: a documented MMM for {{CANALES}} with granularity {{GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL}} over {{HORIZONTE_HISTORICO}}, producing incremental contribution, marginal ROI, and a reallocation plan. Steps:
1. Diagnose the data: granularity, series length, and channel coverage; validate whether {{HORIZONTE_HISTORICO}} is sufficient for inference (ideally 2+ years; <18 months degrades confidence and is declared as a limit).
2. Define exogenous control variables (seasonality, price, distribution, promotions, macro trend, events, competitive pressure) to avoid inflating media contribution.
3. Specify per-channel transformations: adstock (carryover) and saturation (Hill or log) with the range of decay rates to test; justify priors by channel type (high decay for TV/brand, low for search).
4. Set up the regression that decomposes sales into baseline plus channel contribution; report coefficients, significance, expected sign, and confidence intervals.
5. Validate: adjusted R2, MAPE, VIF, autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson), and temporal stability (rolling/holdout); discard the model if there are unjustified counterintuitive signs or VIF indicating severe collinearity.
6. Decompose into contribution (volume and percentage) and marginal ROI; flag saturated and underinvested channels against {{PRESUPUESTO_ACTUAL}}.
7. Recommend reallocation toward the highest marginal ROI until marginal returns are equalized, with scenarios (conservative, base, aggressive), assumptions, and a validation plan (geo-test or lift) to confirm.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm objective, channels, and time window; list the required columns (date, sales, spend by channel, price, distribution, promotions, events, competition).
Phase 2 - Data: diagnose completeness and quality; any missing figure is declared [SUPUESTO] and no numerical results are invented. Flag multicollinearity risks when channels move together.
Phase 3 - Specification: fix controls, adstock, and saturation; justify functional form (log-log multiplicative or transformed additive) and explain why.
Phase 4 - Estimation and validation: run the conceptual model, report fit and diagnostics, and iterate if signs are implausible.
Phase 5 - Business interpretation: translate coefficients into contribution, marginal ROI, and prioritized reallocation with scenarios, assumptions, and a validation plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Includes exogenous control variables; media contribution does not absorb seasonality, price, or distribution.
- [ ] Each channel has explicit adstock and saturation, with a decay rate range and priors justified by channel type.
- [ ] The model reports coefficients, significance, intervals, adjusted R2, MAPE, and VIF; signs are plausible or are justified.
- [ ] Sales are decomposed into baseline plus channel contribution, summing to the total.
- [ ] Every figure not derived from real data provided is tagged [SUPUESTO]; no invented numbers.
- [ ] Marginal ROI distinguishes saturated from underinvested channels and supports reallocation until marginal returns are equalized.
- [ ] Limits are declared (no strict causality without experiments, sensitivity to collinearity, degradation from short window) and an experimental validation plan is included.
Expected deliverable: contribution and marginal ROI table by channel, sales decomposition (baseline vs. media), model validity diagnosis, and prioritized reallocation plan with scenarios, assumptions, and next confirmation experiment.
spec-marketing_plan_tagueo_utm_taxonomia:
[inputs]
- MARCA: {{MARCA}} > Brand or business unit for which the campaign taxonomy is defined.
- CANALES: {{CANALES}} > Active channels and platforms that will generate tagged traffic (e.g., paid social, search, email, display, affiliates).
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Time scheme for encoding campaigns (e.g., quarter 2026-q3, month 2026-07).
- PLATAFORMA_MEDICION: {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}} > Destination where UTMs are consumed (e.g., GA4, BI platform, CRM).
- CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS: {{CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS}} > Prior rules or naming conventions to preserve or migrate (optional).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
UTM fragmentation is the silent root cause of unreliable marketing reports: the same channel appears as "facebook", "FB", and "Meta", campaigns are named manually, and attribution becomes impossible to audit. Defining a canonical convention and a governed taxonomy for {{MARCA}} unlocks end-to-end traceability, cross-period comparability, and investment decisions based on clean data in {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}. Without a standard, the cost is not merely aesthetic: attribution models are contaminated, report rows are duplicated, and the team's confidence in the numbers erodes.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior marketing analytics specialist and campaign data governance expert, with experience consolidating traceability across measurement stacks and paid acquisition platforms.
Deliver a UTM tagging plan and campaign taxonomy through these steps:
1. Define the convention for the five canonical parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term): purpose, controlled vocabulary of permitted values derived from {{CANALES}}, one valid example per parameter, and the mandatory/optional rule (which is required, which is optional, and why).
2. Set the non-negotiable format rules: always lowercase, hyphen as the only separator, no spaces, no accents or special characters; and the utm_campaign encoding pattern as [{{PERIODO}}]-[initiative]-[channel]-[geo], with a maximum length rule and what to do when a component does not apply (explicit placeholder, never empty).
3. Build the medium-source mapping table that blocks invalid combinations and collapses synonyms to a single canonical value (e.g., fb, facebook, meta -> facebook).
4. Deliver the governance matrix: role that creates UTMs, central registry prior to publication, validation method, and a construction tool that prevents manual tagging, respecting {{CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS}} or documenting why they are being migrated.
5. Define the migration strategy for already-published URLs and redirect handling to avoid breaking the historical record or attribution continuity in {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}.
6. Close with a pre-publication validation checklist, 3 to 5 frequent anti-patterns with their corrections, and verifiable acceptance criteria.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm {{MARCA}}, {{CANALES}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}, and {{CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS}}; tag as [SUPUESTO] any data not provided and state the limits of the scope.
Phase 2 Convention: write the dictionary of the five parameters with their controlled vocabulary and mandatory/optional rules.
Phase 3 Rules and mapping: formalize the canonical format, the utm_campaign pattern, and the medium-source table.
Phase 4 Governance and migration: define roles, registry, validation, error-prevention tool, and strategy for live URLs.
Phase 5 Control: produce the checklist, anti-patterns, and acceptance criteria; deliver everything in tables ready for operation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The five UTM parameters have purpose, controlled vocabulary, a valid example, and a mandatory/optional rule.
- Format rules are explicit, non-negotiable, and verifiable (lowercase, hyphen, no accents or spaces).
- The utm_campaign pattern is deterministic, reproducible across periods, and resolves non-applicable components without leaving empty values.
- The medium-source table blocks invalid combinations and unifies synonyms to a canonical value.
- The governance matrix assigns a responsible role, central registry, and an error-prevention construction tool.
- There is a migration strategy for published URLs that preserves the historical record of {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}.
- There is a pre-publication checklist, 3 to 5 anti-patterns with corrections, and verifiable acceptance criteria.
- Neutral, professional English, no emojis; assumptions tagged [SUPUESTO]; inherited conventions preserved or migration justified.
Expected deliverable: operational document with parameter dictionary, format rules, medium-source mapping table, governance matrix, migration strategy, checklist, anti-patterns, and acceptance criteria, ready to adopt as a tagging standard.
spec-marketing_analisis_funnel_conversio:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_FUNNEL: {{NOMBRE_FUNNEL}} > Name or type of funnel to analyze (e.g., web acquisition, SQL-to-close, onboarding)
- ETAPAS_Y_CONTEOS: {{ETAPAS_Y_CONTEOS}} > Ordered list of stages with their record counts, from entry to final conversion
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Time window of the data (e.g., April 2026, last 90 days)
- UNIDAD_CONTEO: {{UNIDAD_CONTEO}} > What each count represents: unique people, sessions, opportunities, or events (optional; if missing, unique people is assumed and tagged [SUPUESTO])
- BENCHMARK_REFERENCIA: {{BENCHMARK_REFERENCIA}} > Reference rates by stage or industry (optional; if missing, typical industry ranges are used, tagged [SUPUESTO])
- META_CONVERSION: {{META_CONVERSION}} > End-to-end conversion target to reach (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A funnel loses prospects at every transition and the key decision is where to intervene first. Knowing precisely the step-by-step rate, the cumulative rate, and the gap against a benchmark unlocks prioritizing the highest-return stage before investing effort or budget. Building an AARRR metrics tree (Dave McClure's pirate model: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) unlocks evidence-based prioritization: a north-star metric at the top, five stages with their primary metric, actionable drivers below, and dashboard-ready instrumentation. This turns opinion discussions into traceable decisions about {{PRODUCTO}}.

1. Acquisition: primary metric (qualified new users, cost of acquisition by channel, visit-to-registration rate), drivers (channel, message, landing friction), and events to instrument. Separate volume from quality: a high-volume, low-subsequent-activation channel is a trap, not a success.

4. Referral: viral coefficient (K-factor), invitation rate, acceptance rate, NPS as a proxy for willingness to recommend. Flag whether virality is a real lever for the product or just noise; if it does not apply, say so and do not inflate it.

[inputs]

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A single-point retention number (e.g., "D30 retention = 22%") hides the real diagnosis: two products with the same final figure can have opposite health depending on the SHAPE of the curve. A curve that flattens at an asymptote above zero reveals a core with a formed habit (retentive PMF); one that continuously decays toward zero retains no one even if it looks the same today. Reading the shape by cohort unlocks the right decision: if the problem is EARLY ACTIVATION, invest in onboarding and value promise; if it is SUSTAINED RETENTION, invest in habit and recurring value. Confusing the two burns quarters on the wrong lever. Three recurring reading errors: confusing user retention with account retention; mixing cohorts from channels with different intent (organic vs. paid) into a single average; and reading immature cohorts (with few observed periods) as if they were conclusive.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior Head of Product Analytics, specialist in retention curves for digital products, with the judgment to distinguish activation from retention and to read cohorts as a time series.
Deliverable: product health diagnosis based on the shape of the curve by cohort, with prioritized levers. Steps:
1. Validate minimum inputs: PRODUCTO with its expected frequency, EVENTO_RETENCION as a value-bearing action (not just a login), CADENCIA matching that frequency, and DATOS_COHORTES with cohort size. If any is missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent figures.
2. Reconstruct the retention table (rows = acquisition cohort; columns = CADENCIA). Declare whether retention is classic (returns in the exact period) or range-based (returns at any point up to the period); do not mix them.
3. Classify the shape of each curve (smile, flattening at a positive asymptote, decay to zero, late leakage), justifying with its inflection points, not with the final number.
4. Separate the diagnosis into two layers and indicate which dominates: (a) early activation (initial drop D0–D1) vs. (b) sustained retention (slope and height of the asymptote).
5. Compare cohorts with each other: higher flattening in recent cohorts = improvement; lower = degradation (review acquisition channel, product regression, or addressable market saturation). Mark immature cohorts as inconclusive.
6. Deliver a shape-per-cohort summary table, dominant diagnosis, 2–3 causal hypotheses prioritized by expected impact, and the recommended lever per hypothesis, anchored to PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate that CADENCIA and EVENTO_RETENCION correspond to the natural usage frequency of PRODUCTO; a poorly chosen cadence distorts the reading. Confirm whether the unit is user or account.
Phase 2 Shape reading: locate the first inflection point (activation drop) and the asymptote (or its absence); name the pattern per cohort.
Phase 3 Attribution: assign the weight of the problem between early activation and sustained retention with evidence from the curve points.
Phase 4 Inter-cohort comparison: order cohorts by maturity and detect a trend of improvement or degradation; mark immature cohorts as inconclusive and separate cohorts from heterogeneous channels if the data allows it.
Phase 5 Synthesis: prioritize hypotheses by expected impact and assign a lever; for each lever propose a verification metric and the expected signal in the next cohort. Mark every inference without sufficient data as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent figures.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

- The diagnosis explicitly declares whether early activation or sustained retention dominates.
- The inter-cohort comparison concludes improvement, degradation, or stability, with immature cohorts marked as inconclusive.
- There are 2–3 causal hypotheses prioritized by impact, each with its actionable lever and verification metric.
- Every inference without sufficient data carries [SUPUESTO]; no figure was invented.
- The entire diagnosis responds to PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO.
Expected deliverable: brief report with shape-per-cohort summary table + dominant diagnosis (activation vs. retention) + 2–3 prioritized hypotheses with lever and verification metric, ready to decide the investment for the next cycle.
