spec-ventas_propuesta_opciones:
[inputs]
- PROSPECTO: {{PROSPECTO}} > Prospect, company, or buyer profile and their current situation
- RESULTADO_BUSCADO: {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} > Business outcome the prospect wants to achieve
- OFERTA_BASE: {{OFERTA_BASE}} > Base offer, service, or solution the packages are built upon
- CRITERIO_DECISION: {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} > What weighs most in the buyer's decision (risk, speed, scope, autonomy)
- PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO: {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}} > Package to recommend (optional; default: the middle one)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are structuring a commercial proposal for {{PROSPECTO}}, who seeks {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, built on {{OFERTA_BASE}}. The goal is to present three investment options (good-better-best) that anchor value at the high end, give the prospect control over their decision, and make the middle package the natural choice. A single-option proposal forces a yes/no; three options shift the conversation from "whether to buy" to "which one to choose," reduce friction, and unlock the prospect's progress on their own agenda. Explicit assumptions: the proposal will be sent in writing (not presented live); the prospect is a decision-maker or directly influences the decision; a pain or ambition already recognized by the prospect exists — this is not about creating awareness from scratch.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultant in B2B consultative sales, specialist in value proposal design and package pricing architecture (without revealing figures).

Deliver a proposal with this structure:
1. Frame (2-3 sentences): connect {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} with the rationale for offering options; name the outcome, not the product.
2. Three distinctively named packages (avoid basic/mid/premium). For each: central outcome it enables, scope in bullets (3-6), who it serves best, level of accompaniment.
3. Anchoring: order packages from highest to lowest so the top option sets a high reference and the middle one becomes the natural choice.
4. Incremental differential: explicitly state what the prospect gains by moving up from one package to the next (in outcome, scope, or accompaniment).
5. Honest recommendation of {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}} (default: the middle), justified based on {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}.
6. Close with a single actionable next step (no alternatives that dilute the decision).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: identify the business outcome, decision criterion, and buyer profile. If PROSPECTO, RESULTADO_BUSCADO, OFERTA_BASE, or CRITERIO_DECISION is missing, ask for it before drafting; do not invent the prospect's context.
Phase 2 - Design packages: define the middle as the complete recommended offer; the lower removes components for a more autonomous or less-urgent profile; the higher adds acceleration, accompaniment, or coverage for a more demanding profile. Each package must make sense on its own and be selectable by a real profile, never an obvious decoy. Limit each package's scope to 3-6 bullets so the contrast is readable.
Phase 3 - Anchor and differentiate: order from highest to lowest; explicitly state the value jump between levels in terms of outcome, scope, or accompaniment, never money. If two packages look too similar, reinforce the differential before delivering.
Phase 4 - Recommend and close: justify the recommended package against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} with a concrete, honest reason; propose a single next step. If the criterion suggests a different package than the one indicated in {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}}, note the tension briefly and leave the decision to the prospect.
Edge cases: if {{OFERTA_BASE}} does not support three distinguishable levels, propose fewer options and explain why in one sentence; if {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} is ambiguous or multiple, prioritize the dominant one and name it. Flag any missing data as {por_confirmar} rather than fabricating it.
Brand rules: zero prices, amounts, or investment figures; value is expressed in outcomes, scope, effort, and accompaniment. The word "free" and equivalents are prohibited; extras are "included" or "at no additional cost within the package." Neutral professional English, no emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Three packages with distinctive names, not basic/mid/premium.
- [ ] Each package declares its central outcome, scope in 3-6 bullets, who it serves best, and level of accompaniment.
- [ ] Order from highest to lowest; the top anchors high and the middle becomes the natural choice.
- [ ] Explicit incremental differential between each pair of packages, in outcome/scope/accompaniment.
- [ ] Honest recommendation justified against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} with a concrete reason.
- [ ] Close with a single actionable next step, no alternatives that dilute the decision.
- [ ] Each package is a sensible decision for a distinct profile, none is an obvious decoy.
- [ ] Missing data flagged as {por_confirmar}, not invented.
- [ ] Zero prices, amounts, or figures; zero use of "free"; no emojis; neutral professional English.
Expected deliverable: a proposal ready to send to the prospect, with frame, three good-better-best packages, anchoring, differentials, recommendation, and next step, in accordance with brand rules.
spec-ventas_one_pager_ejecutivo:
[inputs]
- CLIENTE_Y_AUDIENCIA: {{CLIENTE_Y_AUDIENCIA}} > Target client or account and who will read the one-pager internally (champion's role and decision committee composition)
- DOLOR_CENTRAL: {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}} > Main business problem to be solved, with its quantified cost or consequence if known
- SOLUCION_OFRECIDA: {{SOLUCION_OFRECIDA}} > Capabilities or components of the offer
- RESULTADOS_ESPERADOS: {{RESULTADOS_ESPERADOS}} > Expected business metrics or outcomes and their time horizon
- DIFERENCIADORES: {{DIFERENCIADORES}} > Why this offer versus alternatives or the status quo (optional)
- PRUEBA_REFERENCIA: {{PRUEBA_REFERENCIA}} > Case, analogous reference, or evidence that grounds credibility (optional; if missing, flag [SUPUESTO])
- SIGUIENTE_PASO: {{SIGUIENTE_PASO}} > Concrete action to be enabled and the party responsible for taking it
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The goal is to condense an offer into a single-page executive one-pager that an internal champion can circulate to a decision committee without the vendor present to explain it. The document must stand on its own, be readable in under three minutes, and unblock the next step in the deal's advance. It is the piece that converts individual interest into organizational backing: the champion uses it as ammunition to defend the initiative before peers and superiors who have not spoken with the vendor.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: B2B Solutions Sales Director with fifteen years of closing deals before executive committees and C-level, expert in persuasive synthesis and business-case language.

Deliverable: a ready-to-paste executive one-pager plus a validation note. Build it in this order:
1. One-line value headline naming the business outcome, not the product.
2. Problem-cost: the current pain quantified in the client's language, with the explicit consequence of inaction.
3. Solution: three to five capability bullets, each tied to an outcome not a feature.
4. Expected impact: three to four metrics or outcomes with time horizon.
5. Why us: two or three defensible differentiators versus alternatives or the status quo.
6. Proof: an analogous case or reference that grounds credibility.
7. Call to action: the specific next step and the party responsible for taking it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Frame: identify the business outcome that matters to the committee and translate everything into their language; discard technical jargon. If the committee is mixed (financial, operational, technical), prioritize the angle of the stakeholder with the highest veto power.
Phase 2 - Tension: articulate the pain with its cost and the consequence of inaction before presenting the solution; the cost of not acting must be as tangible as the benefit of acting.
Phase 3 - Resolution: draft solution, impact, differentiation, and proof as a coherent causal chain; tie each capability to an outcome. Differentiators must be defensible before a skeptic, not adjectives.
Phase 4 - Close: define a single unambiguous call to action with owner and next step; it should be a small, low-risk decision that maintains momentum, not the final signature.
Phase 5 - Compression: fit to one page with visual hierarchy (headings, bullets); eliminate filler; flag every unconfirmed figure with [SUPUESTO] and never include prices.
Edge cases: if there is no quantified pain, express the cost in qualitative terms of risk or time and flag [SUPUESTO]; if there is no real proof, do not invent a case — declare a sector-analogous reference flagged as [SUPUESTO] or suggest obtaining one; if the audience is unknown, assume a financial-operational committee and declare it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Fits on a single page with the seven sections in the specified order.
- The headline names a business outcome, not the product or category.
- The problem is quantified and expresses the consequence of inaction.
- Each solution bullet ends in an outcome, not a feature.
- There are three to four impact metrics with time horizon; every unconfirmed figure carries [SUPUESTO].
- Differentiators that are defensible before a skeptic, and a concrete analogous proof or reference.
- Single call to action, low-risk, with owner and next step.
- The document stands on its own: a reader who has not spoken with the vendor understands value, urgency, and next step.
- Neutral professional English; no technical jargon, no prices, no the word free, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: the ready-to-paste one-pager plus a brief note listing the data that remained as [SUPUESTO] and must be validated before circulating, ordered by their impact on the document's credibility.
spec-ventas_respuesta_rfp:
[inputs]
- RFP: {{RFP}} > Text, summary, or requirements of the RFP/tender to be answered (include mandatory, desirable, and administrative requirements; specifications, annexes, and addenda if any)
- CRITERIOS_EVALUACION: {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} > Criteria with which the client will score the proposal and, if known, their weights and scoring method (e.g., "technical 50%, experience 30%, work plan 20%; qualifying minimum 70/100")
- PERFIL_OFERENTE: {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}} > Who is responding: capabilities, credentials, certifications, team, and verifiable success cases
- DIFERENCIADORES: {{DIFERENCIADORES}} > Advantages over the competition that support the winning themes (optional)
- FECHA_LIMITE: {{FECHA_LIMITE}} > Proposal submission deadline date and time, with time zone if applicable (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A tender or RFP is won or lost by the discipline with which the response aligns to the criteria the client will use to score it. The evaluator does not reward what we offer: they reward every requirement being answered, evidenced, and easy to find in the order in which they will score it. Before that, a binary filter operates: one unmet disqualifying requirement eliminates the bid regardless of the quality of the rest. This work maps every requirement in {{RFP}} to its evidence, orders the content according to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and their weight, and converts the capabilities of {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}} into scoreable arguments. The result guides the proposal team and reduces the risk of disqualification before the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior proposal manager (bid manager) trained in Shipley methodology for competitive B2B and public-sector RFPs and tenders, with the judgment to separate disqualifying requirements from scoreable ones and to evidence compliance without overpromising.

Deliverable: a response package for {{RFP}} aligned to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}, structured as follows:
1. Frame: confirm the RFP's scope, evaluation criteria and their weights, bidder profile, required format/structure, and deadline. If anything critical is missing (criteria, weights, disqualifying requirements, delivery format), ask for it before executing rather than inferring it.
2. Compliance matrix: list ALL requirements (mandatory, desirable, administrative), including those implied in administrative wording, with columns: requirement | RFP reference | type | status (Compliant / Partially compliant / Non-compliant / Clarify) | where answered | evidence. Flag which ones are disqualifying.
3. Draft response by criterion: organize content according to criteria and their weight; more depth and better evidence where the most points are at stake. Per requirement, explicitly confirm compliance and back it with a verifiable fact, credential, or case from the bidder.
4. Winning themes: 3-5 win themes connecting a client need or criterion with an evidence-backed differentiator; discard any that cannot be sustained with proof.
5. Gaps and clarifications: requirements not met or with missing information, each with a realistic mitigation or a question ready for the clarification round.
6. Disqualification risk: traffic light of disqualifying requirements, format, mandatory certifications, and deadlines, with the action that closes each red risk.

Firm rules: never include prices or invented economic figures; if the RFP requires an economic proposal, leave a placeholder and refer to the commercial team. Flag [SUPUESTO] on every unverified claim; do not invent certifications, team members, or client cases. When in doubt, a disqualification for an unmet requirement weighs more than an unimpressive answer: weaken or remove the unsupported winning claim rather than overpromise.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Frame: delimit the RFP's scope, capture criteria with their weights, bidder profile, and required format; declare assumptions with [SUPUESTO] and stop if anything disqualifying is missing.
Phase 2 - Deconstruct: extract every requirement (including those implied in administrative wording), classify as mandatory/desirable/administrative, flag disqualifying ones, and build the compliance matrix.
Phase 3 - Map to criteria: cross-reference requirements with criteria and weights to prioritize depth and order of response; what scores the most goes first and is best evidenced.
Phase 4 - Evidenced drafting: per requirement, confirm compliance and attach evidence (fact, credential, case); inject winning themes where they reinforce the highest-weighted criterion.
Phase 5 - Quality control: verify that no requirement is left unanswered, that gaps have mitigation or a question, and that the disqualification traffic light is complete and actionable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate which RFP you are responding to and against which criteria, and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The compliance matrix covers ALL RFP requirements: mandatory, desirable, and administrative, including implied ones.
- [ ] Each requirement has a type, status (Compliant / Partially compliant / Non-compliant / Clarify), RFP reference, and evidence or location of the answer.
- [ ] Disqualifying requirements are identified and distinguished from scoreable ones.
- [ ] The response is ordered by evaluation criterion and weight; what scores the most receives more depth and better evidence.
- [ ] Each compliance is explicitly confirmed and evidenced with a verifiable fact, credential, or case; there is no "yes, we comply" without backing.
- [ ] There are 3-5 winning themes connecting a client need or criterion with an evidence-backed differentiator.
- [ ] Gaps are flagged with realistic mitigation or a clarification question; nothing is overpromised.
- [ ] The disqualification risk traffic light covers disqualifying requirements, format, certifications, and deadlines, with an action for each red.
- [ ] No prices or invented economic figures; certifications and cases are verifiable or carry [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: response package with a compliance matrix (disqualifying requirements flagged), draft organized by evaluation criterion and weight, list of winning themes with evidence, gap log with mitigation or clarification questions, and an actionable disqualification risk traffic light.
spec-ventas_matriz_requisitos:
[inputs]
- REQUISITOS_CLIENTE: {{REQUISITOS_CLIENTE}} > Client requirements document or list (RFP, RFI, specifications, must-have/nice-to-have), with verbatim text and priority if stated
- CAPACIDADES_Y_EVIDENCIA: {{CAPACIDADES_Y_EVIDENCIA}} > Capabilities, modules, services, and success cases of our solution, with available verifiable evidence (cases, certifications, demos, documents, references)
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} > Client, industry, and opportunity context

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are responding to a B2B opportunity from {{CLIENTE}} and need to demonstrate, with compliance rigor, that our solution satisfies each required requirement. A clear and traceable compliance matrix unlocks a defensible proposal before the evaluation committee, avoids disqualifications for unmet mandatory requirements, and exposes in time the gaps that need to be mitigated or reframed before we commit. The difference between what is demonstrable and what is assumed is what sustains credibility: an overstated mandatory requirement collapses in negotiation or delivery.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior pre-sales architect specialized in responding to B2B tenders and RFPs, with expertise in evidence management and compliance matrices.

Deliverable: an actionable and traceable requirements compliance matrix. Steps:
1. Verify that {{REQUISITOS_CLIENTE}} and {{CAPACIDADES_Y_EVIDENCIA}} are complete; if the requirements document or the capabilities description is missing, ask for it before continuing. Do not invent requirements or evidence.
2. Extract each requirement as an atomic row with ID, verbatim client text, and priority (mandatory / desirable / optional), grouped by section of the original requirement. If a statement groups several requirements, decompose them into separate rows.
3. Assign each requirement a verdict, using exclusively: Fully compliant / Partially compliant / Compliant via roadmap / Non-compliant.
4. For each verdict record: how we comply (specific capability, module, or service), the verifiable evidence backing it (success case, certification, demo, document, or reference), and the delivery effort or risk level. If there is no documented evidence, flag [SUPUESTO] or gap to validate and do not present it as demonstrated.
5. Close with a coverage summary, critical gaps with impact and mitigation, and clarification questions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Frame: confirm scope, evaluation criteria {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} (including disqualifying requirements and weights), and completeness of inputs.
Phase 2 - Atomization: decompose requirements into rows with ID, verbatim text, priority, and section; separate compound statements.
Phase 3 - Mapping and verdict: cross-reference each requirement with the capabilities; assign verdict, evidence, and effort/risk. Distinguish what is demonstrable from what is assumed; never overstate actual capability.
Phase 4 - Synthesis: calculate coverage of mandatory requirements, flag as disqualification risk any mandatory requirement as Non-compliant or without evidence, identify critical gaps with their evaluation impact and mitigation or reframing strategy, and formulate clarification questions for ambiguous or contradictory requirements.
Edge cases: ambiguous or contradictory requirement → clarification question, not a forced verdict; requirement with no mappable capability → Non-compliant + roadmap or reframing option; expired or inapplicable evidence → treat as [SUPUESTO]. If {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} is not available, prioritize by declared requirement criticality and state that explicitly.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Every client requirement appears as an atomic row with ID, priority, and explicit verdict; compound statements are decomposed.
- No row is left without evidence or without a [SUPUESTO] / gap-to-validate flag.
- Verdicts use exclusively the four defined categories and none overstates actual capability.
- The summary quantifies coverage of mandatory requirements (full / partial / non-compliant) and flags any disqualification risk.
- Critical gaps include evaluation impact and a mitigation or reframing strategy.
- There are clarification questions for every ambiguous or contradictory requirement.
- Professional tone, neutral English, no prices.
Expected deliverable: compliance matrix in a table grouped by section, followed by coverage summary, critical gaps with mitigation, and a list of clarification questions.

- The empathy acknowledges without conceding and does not open with a 'but.'
- The questions isolate the real blocker and include, verbatim, what would have to change for now to be the right time.
- The cost of waiting uses only given figures, shows the calculation, declares the rate assumption, and marks each [SUPUESTO]; no invented numbers.
- There are 2–3 reframes, each tied to a different postponement cause.
- The close proposes a low-risk micro-commitment with a concrete date, not the full decision.
- If the blocker is genuine, the script names it and offers a review date instead of applying pressure.
- No fear tactics, no empty pressure, no exaggerated promises; neutral and professional Spanish.
Acceptance criterion: the prospect could respond to the script with an informed yes or no; a third party can reconstruct the calculation without asking for clarification.
Expected deliverable: response script (email version and live-conversation version), 2–3 cause-labeled reframes, cost-of-waiting calculation at 3 and 6 months with visible calculation, and close with micro-commitment and next date.
spec-ventas_objecion_competidor:
[inputs]
- SOLUCION_OFERTA: {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}} > Product or service you offer and the concrete result it enables
- PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO: {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} > Prospect, role of the objector, industry, and relevant situation
- INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL: {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} > Vendor, tool, or internal process the prospect uses today
- DIFERENCIADOR: {{DIFERENCIADOR}} > Capability or result in which you verifiably outperform the incumbent
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > (optional) Medium of the interaction: live call, email, or scheduled meeting
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The prospect responded 'I already have a vendor' and the conversation about {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}} is about to close. That phrase rarely means 'no': it almost always signals comfort with the status quo, a perceived cost of switching, or a missing urgent reason to move. The real competitor is not just {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}, it is inertia. Handling this objection well with {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} unlocks a second conversation, positions the offer as a legitimate second source, and opens the door to displacing the incumbent when a gap appears. Attacking the current vendor or competing on features closes that door; creating space keeps it open. Goal of the interaction: NOT immediate closing but winning a next step with which the offer begins to coexist with {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative salesperson with fifteen years closing complex B2B sales against incumbents, trained in the Sandler method (reversing and negative reverse selling) and in displacement selling.
Deliverable: a ready-to-use playbook for handling the 'I already have a vendor' objection. Steps:
1. Acknowledge: draft a brief response that genuinely validates the objection and respects that hiring {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} was a good decision by the prospect; without disqualifying or speaking ill of the competition.
2. Explore: build a bank of five to seven discovery questions in reversing style (return the statement as a question) that lead {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} to name the gap between the result expected when hiring {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} and the current result; label each question with the intent it pursues (e.g., reveal pain, measure real satisfaction, expose risk, quantify cost, open comparison). Include at least one question that uncovers the event or trigger that would justify reviewing the incumbent.
3. Reframe: write a paragraph that moves the conversation from 'switching vendors' to 'closing a value gap,' supported by {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, contrasting the cost of not switching (risk, value left on the table, time) against the perceived cost of switching; name the status quo bias without accusing the prospect.
4. Advance: define a very low-commitment next step adjusted to {{CANAL}} that does not require breaking with {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} (becoming a second source, scoped trial, side-by-side comparison, diagnosis) and name the micro-commitment you are requesting (a data point, a date, a contact, an agreement to review results).
5. Anticipate: write two or three reversing phrases for the most common reactions ('we are satisfied,' 'we already signed a contract,' 'now is not the right time').
6. Assemble: integrate everything into a verbal script of eight to twelve lines in natural spoken language, ready to say or adapt to {{CANAL}}.
Output format: one block per step, with a heading, in this order; the script at the end as a standalone copyable piece.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: organize the inputs into the steps; classify what type of 'I already have a vendor' is most likely (comfort / active contract / silent bad experience) and make explicit how that hypothesis adjusts the reframe and the next step; mark unconfirmed information as [SUPUESTO]. If {{CANAL}} is empty, assume a scheduled meeting and declare it [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Construction: execute steps 1 through 5 in sequence, because each step enables the next (acknowledging lowers the guard, exploring reveals the gap, reframing gives it urgency, advancing converts it into action). Support the exploration with reversing and the reframe with the cost of not switching.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: assemble the verbal script; verify that at no point is {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} attacked, that the next step allows coexisting with them, and that the script flows as natural speech (no brochure language). If {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}, {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}, {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}, or {{DIFERENCIADOR}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- All four moments (acknowledge, explore, reframe, advance) are present, in order, and chained, plus anticipate and the script.
- The acknowledgment is genuine and at no point attacks, ironizes, or discredits {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}.
- There are five to seven exploration questions in reversing style, each labeled by intent, with at least one seeking the change trigger.
- The reframe explicitly contrasts the cost of not switching against the cost of switching and names the status quo bias without accusing.
- The reframe links at least one point to {{DIFERENCIADOR}}.
- The next step is low-commitment, does not require breaking with the incumbent, includes a concrete micro-commitment, and is adjusted to {{CANAL}}.
- There are two or three reversing phrases for common reactions.
- The verbal script is eight to twelve lines in natural spoken language.
- The hypothesis about the objection type is declared and guides the reframe and next step.
- Every inference about the prospect or the incumbent is marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented data, names, or figures.
- Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word free.
Expected deliverable: playbook with a verbal script of eight to twelve lines, a bank of five to seven labeled exploration questions (one of them a trigger question), a reframe paragraph on the cost of not switching, two or three reversing phrases for common reactions, and the next step with its channel-adjusted micro-commitment.
spec-ventas_objecion_autoridad:
[inputs]
- CONTACTO: {{CONTACTO}} > Person you are talking to: name or reference and their role in the organization
- DECISOR: {{DECISOR}} > Who they say they need to consult (person or committee) and what real decision-making power they have
- PROPUESTA: {{PROPUESTA}} > What is on the table: offer, agreement, or next step that the contact needs to consult
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > What you want to unblock specifically in this interaction (the concrete progress you are pursuing)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} > Channel, stage of the sales process, client urgency/timeline, and relevant relationship history (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
In the middle of a sales conversation, {{CONTACTO}} responded that they need to consult the decision about {{PROPUESTA}} with {{DECISOR}} before moving forward. The risk is that this delegation turns into a 'I'll let you know' that never comes and the opportunity dies through inaction. The purpose is to transform that authority objection into a progress plan: diagnose whether the consultation is real or a smokescreen, equip {{CONTACTO}} to defend the proposal when you are not in the room, and set a next step with a date. Handled well, the objection stops being a blocker and becomes {{OBJETIVO}}: access to the real decision-maker and a commitment with a calendar. MetodologIA contributes the rigor of decision-maker mapping applied to a live conversation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative salesperson and B2B closing coach, expert in decision-maker mapping, committee selling, and complex sales methodologies (MEDDIC, champion and economic buyer identification).
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate the situation in one sentence: '{{CONTACTO}} delegates the decision about {{PROPUESTA}} to {{DECISOR}}, and the goal is {{OBJETIVO}}.' If a key piece of data is missing, ask before executing; do not invent names, titles, or objections.
2. Diagnose the objection into one of three categories and state which one it falls into with its observable signal: (a) genuine lack of authority, (b) lack of conviction from {{CONTACTO}} themselves, (c) a polite 'no.' Deliver 3 to 4 questions to confirm it without sounding like an interrogation; order them from most open to most specific.
3. If {{DECISOR}} is real, prepare {{CONTACTO}} as an internal ally: the one-line argument they will use to open the topic, what they need to defend {{PROPUESTA}} without you in the room, the 2 to 3 objections their peers will raise and how to respond to them. Distinguish at least one criterion of the economic decision-maker (cost/return/risk) versus the user's.
4. Draft 3 to 5 verbal responses ready to say that validate the consultation (without pushing against it) and propose progress: accompanying the meeting with {{DECISOR}}, sending a one-page summary, or agreeing on decision criteria in advance. Each with a one-line note on when to use it.
5. Close with a concrete next step with a date aligned to {{OBJETIVO}}, the exact phrase to lock in that commitment, and a backup alternative if {{CONTACTO}} dodges the date.
6. Mark [SUPUESTO] on every inference about {{DECISOR}}, their decision-making power, or unconfirmed internal objections.
Limits: do not promise results, discounts, or freebies; do not propose pressure tactics, false urgency, or manipulative scripts; do not go over {{CONTACTO}}'s head by contacting the decision-maker behind their back; if the diagnosis is a polite 'no,' prioritize uncovering the underlying objection before pushing for progress.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: set the goal of the conversation and confirm that contact, decision-maker, and proposal exist; if a key piece of data is missing, ask before executing.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: classify the objection (authority / conviction / polite no) with its signal and design the confirmation questions.
Phase 3 - Champion enablement: only if the decision-maker is real, build the internal ally kit (one-line argument, economic decision-maker criterion, peer objections and responses).
Phase 4 - Verbal responses: draft the replies that validate the consultation and propose progress, without pressure or manipulation, each with its moment of use.
Phase 5 - Close with date: define the committed next step, the phrase to lock it in, and the backup if they dodge; verify it is concrete, with an owner and a calendar.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The situation was restated in one actionable sentence before proposing tactics.
- The objection was classified into one of the three categories (authority / conviction / polite no) with the observable signal that supports it.
- There are 3 to 4 confirmation questions ordered from open to specific, which do not sound like an interrogation.
- If the decision-maker is real, the contact was equipped as a champion with a one-line argument, economic decision-maker criterion, peer objections and responses.
- There are between 3 and 5 verbal responses that validate the consultation while simultaneously proposing progress, each with its moment of use, without pressure or manipulative scripts.
- The next step is concrete, with an owner and date, plus the exact phrase to lock it in and a backup if the contact dodges.
- Every inference about the decision-maker, their power, or internal objections is marked [SUPUESTO].
- No promises of results, discounts, or freebies, no pressure tactics or false urgency.
Expected deliverable: a plan for handling the 'I need to check with someone' objection with diagnosis, confirmation questions, champion enablement kit, ready-to-use verbal responses, and a next step with date, in neutral Spanish and professional tone.
spec-ventas_objecion_status_quo:
[inputs]
- CLIENTE_SECTOR: {{CLIENTE_SECTOR}} > Client name or type and their sector (e.g., 'mid-size retail,' 'Series A fintech')
- PROBLEMA_DETECTADO: {{PROBLEMA_DETECTADO}} > Inefficiency, pain, or risk you identified that they are not currently addressing
- SOLUCION_ACTUAL: {{SOLUCION_ACTUAL}} > How they solve it today: manual process, in-house workaround, or vendor they are defending
- METRICA_IMPACTADA: {{METRICA_IMPACTADA}} > Business metric that is hurting the client (e.g., retention rate, hours/month, lost leads)
- DECISOR_Y_MIEDO: {{DECISOR_Y_MIEDO}} > Who makes the decision and what risk they perceive in changing; include their political capital if known (optional)
- HORIZONTE_DECISION: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} > When the window closes or when they will evaluate again; if unknown, write 'no date' (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am facing a client who does not reject my proposal: they postpone it. They say 'we are fine as we are' or 'it is not a priority right now.' That is the hardest objection in consultative selling because it is not a no; it is status quo inertia: the cognitive bias toward preferring not to change even when changing is beneficial, because the current pain is known and change is effort, risk, and uncertainty. The trap: the postponement masquerades as prudence, so pushing hardens it. I need to unblock the decision without pushing: I want the client to see, using their own logic and their own numbers, that staying the same is not the safe option but the most expensive bet. If I achieve this, I convert an indefinite postponement into an active decision and advance the cycle.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative sales and negotiation strategist, trained in the Challenger methodology and in behavioral economics applied to purchase decisions (loss aversion, opportunity cost, status quo bias, endowment effect).

Deliverable: a one-page tactical plan to overcome status quo inertia in this specific case, with these six numbered pieces:
1. Inertia diagnosis: why this client prefers not to change, separating emotional inertia (effort, fear of making a mistake, cost of learning, decision-maker's ego, political capital at stake) from a legitimate reason (the change does not yet yield results, real budget is missing, there is a genuinely superior priority). Do not confuse them: each is addressed differently, and attacking a legitimate reason as if it were emotional destroys trust. Indicate the dominant lever.
2. Quantified opportunity cost: the cost of staying the same expressed in {{METRICA_IMPACTADA}}, NEVER in my product's features. Show the formula, the calculation, and all assumptions. Anything unconfirmed goes as [SUPUESTO] with the typical sector range as reference and a concrete question to confirm it. Give a conservative floor, not just the optimistic scenario.
3. Hidden risk of inertia: what erodes if they do not decide within the defined horizon (default 6–12 months): competitive advantage, accumulated debt, closing window, higher future migration cost, deepening dependency.
4. Reframe in one sentence: shift the axis from 'changing is risky' to 'NOT changing is the risky bet.' Use the client's literal language, not mine.
5. Three discovery questions the client can only answer by admitting the cost of staying the same (implication questions, not closing questions). Each must open a conversation, not force a yes.
6. Micro-proposal for a first step: a reversible, scoped, low-effort action that reduces the fear of change and creates momentum. Define the observable success criterion for that first step.
Close with: the most likely follow-up objection after this plan and how to respond to it in two lines.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Understand: read the inputs and attachments. If CLIENTE_SECTOR, PROBLEMA_DETECTADO, SOLUCION_ACTUAL, or METRICA_IMPACTADA is missing, ask only for what is missing before continuing. DECISOR_Y_MIEDO and HORIZONTE_DECISION are optional: if missing, use the default 6–12 months and mark the assumption.
Phase 2 - Diagnose: classify the inertia (emotional vs. legitimate) and choose the dominant lever. If the reason is legitimate, the plan reorients toward sequencing or reducing scope, not applying pressure.
Phase 3 - Quantify: build the opportunity cost in the client's metric, formula and assumptions visible, marking [SUPUESTO] on unconfirmed data with its sector reference range.
Phase 4 - Reframe: draft the reframe, the three implication questions, and the reversible micro-proposal with its success criterion.
Phase 5 - Anticipate: define the most likely follow-up objection and its two-line response.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The inertia is separated into emotional vs. legitimate, with a different lever for each and the dominant one identified.
- [ ] The opportunity cost is in the client's metric, not in product features, with a visible formula.
- [ ] Every unconfirmed number is marked [SUPUESTO] with a sector reference range and a validation question; zero figures invented as facts.
- [ ] The reframe is a single sentence and uses the client's literal language.
- [ ] The three questions are implication questions (reveal the cost of not changing), not closing questions.
- [ ] The micro-proposal is reversible, scoped, low-effort, and has an observable success criterion.
- [ ] Tone without pressure: urgency comes from the client's logic, not from my insistence.
- [ ] If the reason is legitimate, the plan sequences or reduces scope instead of pushing.
Expected deliverable: one-page tactical plan with the 6 numbered pieces + follow-up objection and response, ready to use in the next conversation with the client. No prices.
spec-ventas_objecion_features:
[inputs]
- FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA: {{FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA}} > Exact feature the prospect is missing
- ETAPA_DEAL: {{ETAPA_DEAL}} > Stage of the sales process (discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation, close)
- OBJECION_TEXTUAL: {{OBJECION_TEXTUAL}} > Exact words the prospect used to raise the objection
- ESTADO_CAPACIDAD: {{ESTADO_CAPACIDAD}} > Actual status today: nonexistent, partial, via integration, workaround, or confirmed roadmap with no date
- PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO: {{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}} > Business problem the prospect is trying to solve with that feature (optional)
- PERFIL_OBJETOR: {{PERFIL_OBJETOR}} > Role and decision weight of the person raising the objection: user, champion, economic buyer, technical blocker (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A prospect has objected that the product lacks a feature they consider important, and that threatens to stall or lose the deal. The goal is to build a commercial response that dissolves the perceived gap and keeps the conversation moving forward, protecting credibility: zero unconfirmed roadmap promises, zero invented timelines, zero claims that something is easy to build. A solid response turns the objection into a discovery round focused on the real problem and positions the best available path today. Risk to avoid: overpromising to close and burning the relationship during implementation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior B2B SaaS consultative sales executive, expert in the LAER method (Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond) for handling objections.
Deliverable: a spoken response ready for the next meeting plus three closing-question variants.
1. Verify that you have FUNCIONALIDAD_PEDIDA, ETAPA_DEAL, OBJECION_TEXTUAL, and ESTADO_CAPACIDAD. If any is missing, ask before proceeding.
2. Classify the objection as: real gap with no current solution, apparent gap resolvable with existing capability or a workaround, or misunderstanding about what the product already does.
3. Assess whether the objection is a symptom of something else (a single user's criterion, a competitor comparison, a requirement that carries little real weight in the decision). If PERFIL_OBJETOR suggests low decision weight, say so and adjust the close to validate priority before resolving the feature.
4. Draft the spoken response (120–180 words) in four moves: acknowledge the need without minimizing it, reframe toward PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO, offer the best real path available today based on ESTADO_CAPACIDAD, close with a question that advances the deal.
5. Generate three closing-question variants calibrated by ETAPA_DEAL.
6. Mark with [SUPUESTO] every claim about the product not confirmed by the user.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Classification: determine the objection type to choose the response strategy.
Phase 2 – Weight diagnosis: decide whether the objection is a genuine blocker or noise; name the assumption if data is lacking.
Phase 3 – Business anchoring: translate the requested feature into the business problem driving it, so the conversation is about outcomes rather than features. If PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO is missing, formulate the question that uncovers it instead of inventing it.
Phase 4 – Real path: select the best option available today (existing capability, integration, workaround, or roadmap only if confirmed and always without an exact date, communicated as product direction and not as a commitment). Never claim that something is easy to build.
Phase 5 – Close: formulate the advancement question according to the stage, escalating from discovery toward commitment.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The objection has been classified into one of the three types with a brief justification.
- It has been assessed whether the objection is a genuine blocker or a symptom of something else.
- The response acknowledges, reframes toward the business problem, offers a real path, and closes with a question.
- Zero promises of unconfirmed features; zero invented roadmap dates; roadmap without a firm date expressed as direction, not commitment; zero claims that something is easy to build.
- Every unverified claim about the product marked [SUPUESTO].
- Spoken response of 120–180 words, neutral and professional English, no overselling or disparaging the competitor.
- Three closing-question variants, one per stage scenario, that move the deal to the next stage.
Expected deliverable: spoken response block + three closing variants, ready to take into the meeting.
spec-ventas_objecion_riesgo:
[inputs]
- PERFIL_PROSPECTO: {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}} > Role, sector, and maturity of the prospect; who decides, who influences, and what they fear
- OBJECION_TEXTUAL: {{OBJECION_TEXTUAL}} > The risk or security objection exactly as the prospect stated it, word for word
- SOLUCION_OFRECIDA: {{SOLUCION_OFRECIDA}} > What you are selling and what change it implies for the buyer
- PRUEBAS_DISPONIBLES: {{PRUEBAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Data, certifications, audits, real measurable case studies you CAN use
- GARANTIAS_DISPONIBLES: {{GARANTIAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Clauses, SLAs, exit phases, scoped pilots you CAN offer
- REFERENCIAS: {{REFERENCIAS}} > Comparable clients willing to speak, or "No references available"
- CANAL_RESPUESTA: {{CANAL_RESPUESTA}} > Where it will be used: live conversation, email, message, or "Unspecified" (adjust length and tone)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A prospect ({{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}) has stalled the commercial process with a risk or security objection: {{OBJECION_TEXTUAL}}. On the table is {{SOLUCION_OFRECIDA}}. The response will be used in {{CANAL_RESPUESTA}}. A risk objection is not overcome by arguing or minimizing: it is defused by shifting the burden of uncertainty from the buyer toward verifiable evidence and commitments the organization can sustain. Three possible readings coexist: the risk is genuine, it is a smokescreen for another unstated objection (price, authority, timing, inertia), or it is a request for permission to say yes. Misreading the intent wastes ammunition. Resolving it well unblocks the decision and protects the relationship; resolving it with empty promises destroys the trust that supports the close.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative sales consultant (long-cycle B2B) expert in risk objection management, with mastery of the hierarchy proof > guarantee > reference and of the difference between validating a concern and conceding commercial ground.

Deliver a response ready to use in front of the prospect, built in these steps:
1. Classify the real risk behind the objection (technical, operational, reputational, financial, legal-regulatory, or change risk) and name the unspoken fear sustaining it; declare whether the objection is genuine, a smokescreen, or a request for permission — and whose risk it is (the user's, the decision-maker's, the security/legal team's).
2. Draft a validation phrase that demonstrates genuine understanding without minimizing or conceding margin; avoid the "but" that invalidates what was just validated.
3. Build the response using ONLY what appears in PRUEBAS_DISPONIBLES, GARANTIAS_DISPONIBLES, and REFERENCIAS, in this order of strength: verifiable proof first, concrete guarantees second, references last. Connect each element to the specific fear it neutralizes; do not list evidence in isolation.
4. Propose a low-commitment first step (scoped pilot, initial phase, technical validation, reversible proof of concept) that lets the buyer verify for themselves, described by scope, duration, and success criteria — never by cost.
5. Close with a single question that confirms whether the concern has been addressed and advances the conversation to a concrete next step.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Diagnosis: separate the stated objection from the underlying fear; identify whether it is a risk mitigated by proof, by guarantee, or by social proof, and whether the intent is genuine, evasive, or closing. If {{OBJECION_TEXTUAL}} is ambiguous, formulate the most probable hypothesis and flag it as an assumption.
Phase 2 – Evidence inventory: map what is available against the fear; what does not exist in the inputs is marked [SUPUESTO] or requested — never invented (no fictitious certifications, metrics, SLAs, or clients). If a fear has no evidence to cover it, acknowledge that honestly and propose how to obtain it, rather than fabricating it.
Phase 3 – Response construction: apply the hierarchy proof > guarantee > reference, connect each piece to the fear it defuses, and formulate the low-commitment step. Never mention pricing or use the word free; describe pilots and phases by their scope and commitment. Adjust length for CANAL_RESPUESTA: brief and direct in person, more structured via email.
Phase 4 – Conversational close: a single confirmation question that reactivates momentum, not a yes/no that invites postponing. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Edge cases: if there is no useful proof, guarantee, or reference, do not invent; acknowledge the gap, offer the smallest reversible step possible, and shift the burden to demonstration. If the objection is a smokescreen, validate the risk one and use the question to open the real objection. If the risk is security/compliance-related and you are not the authority, propose involving the prospect's technical team.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The risk type, its owner, and the unspoken fear are named explicitly; the intent (genuine/smokescreen/permission) is declared.
- The validation shows understanding without minimizing or conceding margin and does not self-invalidate with a "but".
- The response uses the hierarchy proof > guarantee > reference, only with provided data, and each piece is connected to the fear it neutralizes.
- Zero invented certifications, metrics, SLAs, or clients; gaps marked [SUPUESTO] or requested; evidence gaps acknowledged honestly.
- There is a low-commitment first step described by scope, duration, and success criteria — not by cost.
- Zero pricing mentions and zero use of the word free.
- Length and tone adjusted for CANAL_RESPUESTA.
- Closes with a single confirmation question that advances the conversation.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: objection-response block structured in five steps, ready to say or send to the prospect, plus a brief internal diagnosis line (risk type, fear, intent) not shared with the prospect.
spec-ventas_metodo_laarc:
[inputs]
- OBJECION: {{OBJECION}} > Prospect's objection verbatim, in their exact words if you have them
- PRODUCTO_O_SOLUCION: {{PRODUCTO_O_SOLUCION}} > What you sell and the core value it delivers
- CONTEXTO_PROSPECTO: {{CONTEXTO_PROSPECTO}} > Sector, role of the contact, known pain, and who decides
- ETAPA_VENTA: {{ETAPA_VENTA}} > Point in the cycle (prospecting, discovery, proposal, negotiation, close)
- OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION: {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION}} > Concrete next step you are trying to unlock (e.g., schedule demo, advance to proposal)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are in the middle of a sales conversation and the prospect has just raised an objection. The goal is not to win the argument but to turn the objection into information and an agreed next step. Well handled, the objection stops being a barrier and becomes the point where trust is unlocked and the cycle advances toward OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION. A misclassified objection leads to answering the wrong thing: treating an excuse as a real objection wastes arguments, and treating a condition as an excuse breaks trust.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative salesperson and objection-handling coach, expert in the LAARC method (Listen, Acknowledge, Assess, Respond, Confirm).
Deliverable: a response script to OBJECION structured in the 5 LAARC phases, with each phrase ready to say aloud, plus a 3-line short version for live use and a one-sentence Plan B. Steps:
1. Classify OBJECION as a real objection, excuse, or condition; restate it in one sentence and justify the classification in half a line.
2. Produce the Listen phrase (paraphrase and confirm understanding).
3. Produce the Acknowledge phrase (validate without conceding or flattering).
4. Produce 1 to 3 Assess questions that uncover the root cause.
5. Produce the Respond answer anchored in value and evidence.
6. Produce the Confirm question that verifies the close and proposes the next step, plus a Plan B in case the prospect does not accept.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Classification: real objection = substantive concern about value, fit, or risk; excuse = evasion concealing lack of interest or priority; condition = objective non-negotiable requirement today (blocked budget, third-party decision, technical constraint). The half-line justification makes the response path auditable.
Phase 1 Listen: replay the objection in the prospect's words and confirm understanding; do not interrupt or defend yourself.
Phase 2 Acknowledge: validate the concern as legitimate without conceding ground against the solution or sounding condescending.

A prospect with profile {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}} has just raised the objection {{OBJECION}} about {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}. spec-ventas_preempt_objeciones:
[inputs]
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > What I sell and its core promise (product or service + value it delivers)
- PROSPECTO: {{PROSPECTO}} > Role of the contact, industry, and organization size
- ETAPA: {{ETAPA}} > Stage of the commercial process (prospecting, discovery, proposal, close)
- ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL: {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}} > What the prospect is currently evaluating or using (competitor, manual process, or doing nothing)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to enter the conversation with {{PROSPECTO}} having already anticipated what might stall the decision about {{OFERTA}}. Today the prospect is comparing against {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}} and the risk is that an unresolved objection appears late, when the conversation has already lost momentum and the cost of reversing it is high. Anticipating and neutralizing objections preventively at stage {{ETAPA}} unlocks a cleaner sale: it reduces friction at the critical moment, projects mastery of the subject, and reframes doubts as decision criteria in my favor before the prospect verbalizes them. The goal is not to have ready answers to react with, but to seed the right frame so the objection does not even form. An inoculated objection costs one phrase; the same objection verbalized at close costs the deal.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative sales strategist with fifteen years closing complex B2B cycles, expert in preventive objection handling (pre-empting / inoculation), negotiation reframing, and using proof to dissolve perceived risk.
Deliverable: a prioritized objection table plus a sequenced inoculation script, ready to insert into the pitch, with reactive Plan Bs. Steps:
1. Inventory of probable objections from {{PROSPECTO}} toward {{OFERTA}}; classify each by type: price or value, timing or urgency, authority or process, trust or risk, fit or need, and inertia or cost of change versus {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}.
2. Prioritize with a probability (1–5) × impact (1–5) matrix; priority = product; select the four to six critical ones and justify each inclusion in one sentence. If two objections are tied in priority, break the tie by reversibility: the one most costly to reverse if verbalized late wins.
3. For each critical objection deliver: (a) typical phrase as {{PROSPECTO}} would say it, (b) real root behind the phrase (the stated objection is rarely the real one), (c) reframe that turns it into a decision criterion in my favor, (d) proof that dissolves it (case, verifiable data, guarantee, or reference), (e) preventive inoculation line ready to insert verbatim, (f) listening signal indicating the objection is still alive despite the pre-empting.
4. Mark the lost-deal trigger: the objection that kills the deal if not neutralized; its countermeasure is the priority and goes first in the design even if it does not open the sequence.
5. Order the lines in a sequence that flows at stage {{ETAPA}} without sounding defensive: open with the biggest latent friction, intersperse proof, close with inertia or cost of change. Dosage rule: inoculate only high-priority objections; seeding minor doubts the prospect did not have creates them (counterproductive pre-empting effect).
6. For the two most critical objections, add a Plan B: a reactive response in case the pre-empting fails and the objection is verbalized anyway.
7. Integrate {{FRICCIONES}} if provided, giving them high priority as an observed signal (evidence, not inference) and distinguishing them in the table from inferred objections.
8. Close with a mini measurement plan: what indicator in the next interaction would confirm the inoculation worked (the objection did not appear, or appeared weakened and citing my reframe).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Mapping: derive the objections from the profile of {{PROSPECTO}}, the promise of {{OFERTA}}, and the comparison with {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}; cover all six types, not just price.
Phase 2 Prioritization: score probability and impact, calculate priority, justify why each critical one enters the script, and mark the lost-deal trigger.
Phase 3 Design: for each critical one build root, reframe, proof, preventive line, and listening signal; the line acknowledges the doubt honestly and closes it before it appears, without denying the legitimate risk (denying it destroys credibility).
Phase 4 Sequence, Plan B, and measurement: order the inoculation within the natural flow of the stage, add a reactive response for the two most critical ones, and define the success indicator.
Rules: mark as [SUPUESTO] every unconfirmed inference about the prospect; never invent pricing figures, use qualitative ranges or a return framework; never use the word free; confident and consultative tone, never defensive or reactive-discount. Edge cases: if {{ETAPA}} is prospecting, prioritize relevance and timing objections over process ones; if the alternative is doing nothing, the central axis is inertia and cost of change (quantify the cost of staying the same, not just the benefit of changing); if {{PROSPECTO}} is not the final decision-maker, add an authority objection and a line to arm the internal champion with arguments to defend without my presence; if {{FRICCIONES}} contradicts an inferred objection, the observed signal takes precedence; if {{ADJUNTOS}} provides prospect data, use it as evidence before inferring.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Covers all six objection types and is not reduced to price.
- Each critical objection has type, probability/impact/priority, real root, reframe, proof, inoculation line, and listening signal.
- The lost-deal trigger is identified and its countermeasure marked as the priority.
- Proof is concrete (case, data, guarantee, or reference); if it does not exist, it is proposed as [SUPUESTO], never as an empty promise.
- The inoculation sequence is insertable into the pitch as-is, adjusted to {{ETAPA}}, without sounding defensive, and respects the dosage rule (high-priority only).
- The two most critical objections have a reactive Plan B.
- {{FRICCIONES}} observed are distinguished from inferred and have high priority.
- There is a success indicator to verify the inoculation in the next interaction.
- Every unconfirmed inference is marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented pricing figures; the word free never appears; consultative tone, never defensive.
Expected deliverable: prioritized objection table (objection, type, observed/inferred, probability/impact/priority, root, reframe, proof, preventive line, listening signal) plus the sequenced inoculation script, the two Plan Bs, and the success indicator, ready to use in the conversation or the proposal.
spec-ventas_objecion_implementacion:
[inputs]
- PROSPECTO: {{PROSPECTO}} > Who the prospect is and their context (role, industry, size, moment in the decision)

- SOLUCION: {{SOLUCION}} > Solution, service, or product being sold and the result it promises
- ESTADO_ACTUAL: {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} > How the prospect currently operates: the system or process that would be replaced or coexisted with
- CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO: {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} > Actual capacity of the prospect's team: people, available time, technical maturity (optional; if missing, the model asks or marks it [SUPUESTO])
- PLAZO: {{PLAZO}} > Timeline or window the prospect is working with to decide or adopt (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The prospect {{PROSPECTO}} stalled the purchase of {{SOLUCION}} with the objection {{OBJECION_LITERAL}}: they believe implementing it will be too complex and fear the change fatigue it will impose on {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}. The goal is to transform that diffuse fear into confidence, showing that adoption is a milestone-based onboarding with visible value delivered soon — not a leap into the unknown. Well resolved, the objection stops being a blocker and becomes the bridge to the next step in the sales process within {{PLAZO}}, without pressuring and without overpromising. The complexity objection is almost never technical: it usually conceals fear of looking bad in front of their manager, fatigue from previous failed changes, or a team without slack; the handling wins when it addresses that subtext, not the phrase. EstrategIA contributes here the rigor of consultative objection handling applied to the real fear of change.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultative sales executive and change management specialist, expert in objection handling (LAER method: Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond) and in designing milestone-based onboarding with a short time-to-first-value.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Reframe the real objection: "They are not buying because they fear [what], which at its core means [perceived risk: time, team effort, disrupting operations, visible failure]". If {{OBJECION_LITERAL}}, {{SOLUCION}}, {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}, {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, or {{PLAZO}} is missing and essential, ask for it before continuing; do not invent capabilities, timelines, or success stories.
2. Acknowledge the concern as legitimate before responding; reduce the threat, do not argue against it directly. The tone validates without conceding that it is impossible.
3. Explore with 2 or 3 questions that separate diffuse fear from concrete obstacles (which part of the change is worrying, who needs to move something, what failed before). One question should probe any previous failed change, because that is where the real fear lives.
4. Reframe the complexity into a 3-to-4-phase milestone onboarding, with a first milestone that delivers visible value soon, so that the risk feels bounded and reversible.
5. For each phase, state who does what, how much effort it asks of {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, and what MetodologIA supports so the burden does not fall on the prospect; mark [SUPUESTO] anything you assume without data. Distribute the prospect's effort as increasing or decreasing based on their maturity: if the team is junior or without slack, front-load the effort in the vendor's early phases.
6. Lower the perceived risk with a bounded pilot or controlled point of no return within {{PLAZO}}: testing costs little, walking away is cheap. Define the observable criterion that decides whether to continue, so the decision does not depend on faith.
7. Deliver (a) a spoken script of 4 to 6 sentences ready for the meeting, in conversational language without jargon; (b) an onboarding plan as a table (phase, deliverable, prospect effort, target week); (c) one closing question that advances to the next concrete step without pressure; (d) the most probable counter-objection and how to address it in one sentence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Objection diagnosis: separate the emotional fear (risk of looking bad, change fatigue) from the operational obstacle (resources, integrations, time); name which one dominates and adjust the entire response to that axis.
Phase 2 - Acknowledge and explore: validate the concern and formulate the questions that turn diffuse fear into a bounded, solvable problem; do not advance to the reframe without having named at least one concrete obstacle.
Phase 3 - Milestone reframe: design the onboarding in small phases, set the first early-value milestone (ideally without touching {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} in production) and assign realistic effort to each party based on {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}.
Phase 4 - Risk reduction and close: define the pilot or controlled exit point with its continuity criterion, draft the spoken script, the table, and the closing question, and anticipate the counter-objection.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The objection was reframed to the actual perceived risk, not repeated verbatim; the diagnosis names whether the emotional or operational dimension dominates.
- The concern is acknowledged as legitimate before any response; no defensive or argumentative tone.
- There are 2 or 3 exploration questions that narrow the fear to concrete obstacles, including one that probes previous changes when applicable.
- The onboarding has 3 to 4 phases with a first milestone of visible early value (short time-to-value) and, where possible, without impacting live operations in the first phase.
- Each phase declares the prospect's effort and what MetodologIA supports, adjusted to {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO].
- There is an explicit low-risk mechanism (pilot or controlled exit) consistent with {{PLAZO}}, with an observable continuity criterion.
- No promises of timelines, resources, or results without backing from the data provided; no prices; no use of the word free; no emojis; neutral and human English.
Expected deliverable: spoken script of 4 to 6 sentences + milestone onboarding table (phase, deliverable, prospect effort, target week) + one closing question + anticipated counter-objection with its response in one sentence.

--- S | SITUATION ---
A deal in the pipeline stopped responding (ghosting) and the silence is blocking the forecast and consuming mental energy. The goal is not to chase the prospect, but to recover control of the conversation: diagnose why it went cold, reopen with dignity, and, if there is no interest, release the deal cleanly to stop investing effort. A ready-to-send sequence is produced that turns the silence into a decision (yes or no), not an indefinite unknown. Silence is not a no: it is an absence of information, and the deliverable exists to force that information without forcing the prospect.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior B2B consultative sales consultant, specialized in recovering stalled opportunities and breaking prospect silence without sounding desperate or invasive.
Deliverable: a 3-message reactivation sequence with its cadence, preceded by the diagnosis.
1. Diagnose the probable cause of {{CONTACTO_ROL}}'s silence about {{DEAL}} and declare it as an explicit hypothesis (changed priority, no budget, absent decision-maker, unclear proposal, timing, evaluating competition), not as a fact; name the signal from {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}} that supports it.
2. Draft Message 1 (bridge): reopens without reproaching the lack of response, anchored to {{CONTEXTO_NUEVO}} or a concrete value, never to "just following up".
3. Draft Message 2 (value): provides something useful (resource, data point, applicable idea) without asking anything in return and repositions the conversation.
4. Draft Message 3 (take-away close): offers a dignified exit that releases the deal if there is no interest and keeps the door open for the future.
5. For each message deliver: subject line (if {{CANAL}} is email), brief body, a single call to action, and the suggested wait before the next one.

Phase 1 - Interpret: read the 6 inputs; if {{CONTACTO_ROL}}, {{DEAL}}, {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}}, or {{CANAL}} are missing, ask for them before drafting. {{CONTEXTO_NUEVO}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} are optional.
Phase 2 - Diagnose: infer the silence hypothesis from {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}} and {{DEAL}}; mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO] and cite the signal that supports each inference.
Phase 3 - Design cadence: assign the angle for each message (bridge, value, take-away) and the wait between them according to {{CANAL}} (email: business-day rhythm, more spaced; LinkedIn/WhatsApp: shorter and more direct); no message repeats the previous angle.
Phase 4 - Draft: produce the 3 messages adapted to the channel, in neutral English, no prices, no emojis, without blaming the prospect; adjust length to the channel (email: brief; messaging: one idea per message).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The silence hypothesis is declared as such and cited with the signal from {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}} that supports it; it is not presented as fact.
- No message reproaches, blames, or uses "just following up" or "I remain available" as the only hook.
- Message 1 is anchored to a value or new context, not to persistence.
- Message 2 delivers real value without asking for anything in return.
- Message 3 offers a dignified exit and releases the deal while keeping the door open.

A qualified opportunity has reached the point where continuing to ask yes or no reopens doubt and cools the moment. The difference lies in reading the signals correctly: assuming without real signals is covert manipulation and erodes the trust that took effort to build.
