spec-datos_etl_backfill_historico:
[inputs]
- TABLA_OBJETIVO: {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}} > Destination table or dataset to reprocess (name, layer, and engine, e.g. silver.ventas_diarias in a lakehouse)
- VENTANA_HISTORICA: {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}} > Date range or partitions to reprocess (from-to, inclusive/exclusive)
- GRANO_LOTE: {{GRANO_LOTE}} > Grain of each batch (daily partition, monthly, or by key/range)
- FUENTE_ORIGEN: {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}} > System or pipeline that feeds the table (source of truth for parity)
- RESTRICCIONES_COSTO: {{RESTRICCIONES_COSTO}} > Capacity, concurrency, and permitted time window limits
- REGLA_VALIDACION: {{REGLA_VALIDACION}} > Per-batch acceptance criterion (counts, checksums, expected parity)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Reprocessing historical data in {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}} over the window {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}} is required without degrading the production service or breaking downstream consumers. A poorly planned backfill triggers compute cost, generates duplicates, contaminates live incremental loads, and leaves silent gaps discovered only weeks later. A controlled plan unlocks traceability and the ability to resume after a failure: historical logic correction, new column fill, and lost data recovery. The backfill reason is not cosmetic: logic correction typically requires full rewrite by partition, while a new column fill may be resolved with a scoped update — and each case changes the write strategy.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specializing in large-scale reprocessing pipelines, with mastery of idempotency, partitioning, late-arriving data, and cost control on modern data platforms.
Deliver an executable and resumable backfill plan with these numbered components:
1. Framing and reason: scope, natural deduplication key, downstream dependencies (materialized views, derived tables, dashboards, models), and backfill reason — because it determines the write strategy.
2. Batching strategy by {{GRANO_LOTE}} and order that respects downstream dependencies (oldest to most recent unless the dependency requires another order), with a pilot batch to size before the full sweep to calibrate real cost and duration.
3. Idempotency: safe write technique (merge/upsert by natural key, delete-insert by partition, or versioned snapshot) that avoids duplicates and orphan rows on retries; justify the choice by engine and table pattern.
4. Cost and concurrency control within {{RESTRICCIONES_COSTO}}: batch size, maximum parallelism, low-load time window, throttling, and spending cap in consumed capacity; declare the effect on live incremental loads and how to avoid lock contention.
5. Incremental batch-by-batch validation against {{REGLA_VALIDACION}}: expected vs actual counts, checksums over key columns, parity with {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, gap and duplicate detection, and handling of late-arriving data or source reprocessing during the backfill.
6. Per-batch stop gates and rollback on deviations, with explicit tolerance threshold per metric and isolation that prevents contaminating already-validated batches.
7. Numbered runbook with persistent checkpoint, idempotent resumption (without reprocessing already-validated batches), progress log, and consumer communication plan before/during/after.
8. Final reconciliation: zero gaps and zero duplicates over the full window, aggregated parity against {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, and formal closure criterion.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm scope, reason, natural key, and downstream dependencies; mark anything not provided as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent volumes or schemas.
Phase 2 Design: define batching, order, idempotency, and cost/concurrency control; size a pilot batch before the full sweep and extrapolate cost/duration.
Phase 3 Validation: specify per-batch tests, late-arriving data handling, and stop/rollback gates against {{REGLA_VALIDACION}}.
Phase 4 Delivery: consolidate the resumable runbook with checkpoints and final reconciliation of the full window.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The backfill reason is declared and justifies the chosen write strategy.
- [ ] Batch order respects downstream dependencies and processes oldest to most recent unless justified.
- [ ] Writing is idempotent: re-running a batch does not generate duplicates or orphan rows.
- [ ] A pilot batch is sized before the full sweep, with extrapolated cost/duration.
- [ ] Batch size, parallelism, and time window fit within {{RESTRICCIONES_COSTO}} with a declared spending cap and without contaminating live incremental loads.
- [ ] Each batch has automated validation against {{REGLA_VALIDACION}} (counts, checksums, parity, gaps, duplicates) and a stop gate with threshold.
- [ ] Late-arriving data and source reprocessing during the backfill are addressed.
- [ ] A persistent checkpoint exists and resumption does not reprocess already-validated batches.
- [ ] Final reconciliation confirms zero gaps and zero duplicates in {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}} with aggregated parity against {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented volumes or schemas.
Expected deliverable: backfill plan in per-batch table (range, order, dependency, validation, gate) plus numbered executable runbook, consumer communication plan, and final reconciliation section.
spec-datos_etl_streaming_vs_batch:
[inputs]
- CASO_DE_USO: {{CASO_DE_USO}} > What is being ingested and how the data is consumed (e.g., fraud dashboard, daily sales report, feeding a recommendation model)
- SLA_LATENCIA: {{SLA_LATENCIA}} > Target data freshness and the consequence of arriving late (e.g., sub-second, minutes, once a day)
- VOLUMEN_Y_PERFIL: {{VOLUMEN_Y_PERFIL}} > Events or records per second/hour, flow pattern (constant, bursts, seasonal), and record size
- GARANTIAS_DATOS: {{GARANTIAS_DATOS}} > Loss tolerance (at-least-once / exactly-once), ordering importance, and handling of late-arriving data
- RESTRICCION_COSTO_EQUIPO: {{RESTRICCION_COSTO_EQUIPO}} > (optional) Infrastructure limits, operational budget, team maturity, and on-call capacity
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Choosing incorrectly between batch and streaming is one of the most expensive decisions in data engineering: unnecessary streaming burdens the team with always-on infrastructure, state management, failure recovery, and on-call that the business never asked for; batch where the business needed freshness delivers decisions too late. The dominant cost is almost never building the pipeline, but operating it sustainably. This decision unlocks an ingestion architecture sized to the real SLA — not to trends — and a pilot with clear success criteria before committing talent and infrastructure.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specialized in ingestion architectures and data platforms, with hands-on experience operating batch and streaming pipelines in production.
Deliverable: an ingestion architecture recommendation (batch, streaming, or micro-batch) justified axis by axis, with a reference pattern and validation plan. Steps:
1. Restate the case {{CASO_DE_USO}} in one sentence and list missing or ambiguous data as questions; if {{SLA_LATENCIA}}, {{VOLUMEN_Y_PERFIL}}, or {{GARANTIAS_DATOS}} are unclear, stop and ask before recommending, because these are the axes that most shift the decision.
2. Score the four axes (High/Medium/Low) with justification: Latency (required vs. desired freshness, cost of arriving late), Volume and profile (throughput, bursts, record size), Cost and operational complexity (always-on infrastructure, state, recovery, and on-call vs. scheduled jobs, talent, and monitoring), and Guarantees and ordering (at-least-once vs. exactly-once, ordering, late-arriving data). Explicitly flag any axes in conflict (e.g., High latency with exactly-once guarantees raises cost non-linearly).
3. Issue the recommendation (batch / streaming / micro-batch) with its honest counter-argument: under what conditions would this same choice be a mistake.
4. Propose a concrete reference pattern and name components by their function, not by brand, unless requested: batch = scheduled-job orchestrator plus analytical store; streaming = event broker plus stream-processing engine with windowing and state management; micro-batch = middle ground when minute-level freshness is sufficient. If the source is transactional, evaluate CDC. Avoid dual architectures (Lambda) unless the case demands it, due to the cost of maintaining two paths.
5. Define three measurable criteria to validate the decision in a pilot (e.g., observed p95 latency against the SLA, infrastructure cost per million events, estimated weekly operational effort).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate the case and the four axes with the values received; mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO] and gaps as questions. Do not invent throughput, latency, or cost figures.
Phase 2 - Evaluation: apply the four-axis matrix; the governing rule is to choose the simplest option that meets the latency SLA and the required guarantees. On a tie, decide by lower sustained operational cost and smaller state surface area.
Phase 3 - Recommendation and validation: decide, present the counter-argument, establish the reference pattern and the three measurable pilot criteria, each with a success threshold.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The four axes (latency, volume, cost/complexity, guarantees/ordering) are scored with explicit justification.
- [ ] Axes that conflict with each other are flagged (e.g., High latency + exactly-once).
- [ ] The recommendation includes its honest counter-argument (when it would be a mistake).
- [ ] The reference pattern names components by function and fits the declared SLA and volume; CDC was evaluated if the source is transactional.
- [ ] The three validation criteria are measurable, observable in a pilot, and each has a success threshold.
- [ ] No figures were invented: missing data was asked for or marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] The simplest option that meets the SLA prevails; streaming is not recommended for its own sake, and dual architectures are not proposed without justification.
Expected deliverable: brief document with a table of the four scored axes, recommendation with counter-argument, reference pattern, and a three-criteria validation plan with thresholds.
spec-datos_etl_esquema_evolucion:
[inputs]
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > System or source table whose schema is evolving (e.g., "checkout events, Kafka topic orders.v1")
- MOTOR_INGESTION: {{MOTOR_INGESTION}} > Pipeline engine (e.g., Spark Structured Streaming, dbt, Fivetran, Flink, Kafka Connect)
- FORMATO_DATOS: {{FORMATO_DATOS}} > Serialization format at source and destination (e.g., Avro at source, Parquet/Iceberg at destination)
- DESTINO: {{DESTINO}} > Target layer and technology (e.g., Iceberg lakehouse, Snowflake warehouse, bronze/silver layer)
- POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD: {{POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD}} > Desired policy (backward, forward, full, or transitive) and critical consumers to protect
- CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS: {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} > List of changes to evaluate: new columns, renames, type changes (optional; if missing, the AI requests the schema diff before classifying)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A source feeding an ingestion pipeline is about to change its schema and the team needs to absorb new columns, renames, and type changes without breaking downstream consumers or blindly reprocessing history. The goal is to unlock continuous source changes with data contract discipline that makes evolution predictable, versioned, and auditable — avoiding silent corrupt load incidents and accumulated schema debt.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specialized in ingestion platforms and data contracts, with expertise in Avro/Protobuf schema evolution rules, schema registry, and bronze/silver/gold modeling.
Deliverable: an actionable, versioned schema evolution strategy for {{FUENTE}} on {{MOTOR_INGESTION}} ({{FORMATO_DATOS}} to {{DESTINO}}), under policy {{POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD}}. Steps:
1. Classify each change in {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} as backward-compatible, forward-compatible, or breaking by applying Avro/Protobuf rules; declare for each what it breaks and which consumer it affects. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any inference about consumers, volumetrics, or undeclared environment.
2. Define handling rules by type: new columns with an explicit default and absence tolerance; renames via alias/field mapping instead of DROP+ADD (which loses data and resets lineage); type changes distinguishing safe promotions (int to long, int to string, adding a union member) from unsafe conversions (string to int, narrowing, precision change) that require a shadow column and controlled backfill.
3. Draft the versioned data contract: a concrete example schema, responsible owner, semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (MAJOR=breaking, MINOR=additive compatible, PATCH=metadata), compatibility policy, and a dated deprecation window for retired fields.
4. Design verifiable enforcement: validation against the schema registry in CI and at runtime, a dead-letter quarantine for records that violate the contract with its reprocessing criterion, and drift detection between the actual source schema and the declared contract.
5. Deliver the version promotion runbook and the reversible rollback plan, with dual-write/dual-read intermediate states and the cutover criterion when applicable.
Edge cases to cover: field changing from nullable to required; field reordering in positional formats; enum with a new value an old consumer does not recognize; timezone or unit change in a field without renaming it (a semantic change invisible to the schema). State the trade-off between adoption speed and safety for each relevant decision (e.g., dual-write doubles temporary storage but eliminates the inconsistency window).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate source, engine, format, destination, policy, and consumers to protect; list what is missing. If {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} is empty or the schema diff is absent, ask for it before classifying; do not invent the content of the change.
Phase 2 - Plan: present the plan (classification > rules > contract > enforcement > runbook) and assumptions before generating artifacts.
Phase 3 - Execute: produce the classification tables, the versioned data contract (with a concrete schema), the enforcement design, and the runbook with rollback.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The three change types (new columns, renames, type changes) each have an explicit rule and a concrete schema example.
- [ ] Each change is classified as backward/forward/breaking with justification per Avro/Protobuf rules and specifies which consumer it breaks.
- [ ] Renames are resolved with alias/mapping, never with DROP+ADD that loses data or lineage.
- [ ] Type changes distinguish safe promotions from unsafe conversions (shadow column/backfill).
- [ ] The contract declares schema, owner, semantic version with its bumping rule, compatibility policy, and a dated deprecation window.
- [ ] Verifiable enforcement exists: schema registry (CI and runtime), dead-letter quarantine with reprocessing criterion, and drift detection.
- [ ] The runbook includes promotion steps and a reversible rollback plan with dual-write/dual-read states and a cutover criterion.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases (nullable to required, positional reordering, new enum value, semantic unit/TZ change) are addressed or explicitly discarded with a reason.
- [ ] Any inference about consumers or undeclared environment is marked [SUPUESTO], and speed vs. safety trade-offs are made explicit.
Expected deliverable: document with classification tables and rules, a versioned data contract example, the enforcement design, and a promotion + rollback runbook, ready for the contract owner's review.
spec-datos_etl_normalizar_json_anidado:
[inputs]
- JSON_FUENTE: {{JSON_FUENTE}} > JSON document to normalize: a representative sample or schema, with enough records to detect structural variations (optional fields, mixed types, empty vs. absent arrays)
- MOTOR_DESTINO: {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} > Target engine or dialect that determines the DDL, flattening function, and UPSERT options (PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, SQL Server, SQLite) (optional, default: portable ANSI SQL with per-engine notes)
- CLAVE_PRIMARIA: {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} > Field or combination from the JSON that stably identifies each root record; if absent or not unique/non-null, a deterministic surrogate key is generated (optional)
- ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS: {{ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS}} > How to handle arrays: normalized child table (default), bridge table for arrays of scalars, or denormalize to columns only if cardinality is fixed and low (optional, default: normalized child table)
- CONVENCION_NOMBRES: {{CONVENCION_NOMBRES}} > Table and column naming convention: snake_case with path separator, entity prefix, singular/plural, engine length limit (optional, default: snake_case with underscore as path separator)
- MODO_CARGA: {{MODO_CARGA}} > Load strategy: full reload, incremental UPSERT (merge key), or append-only with batch stamp; determines idempotency and reconciliation (optional, default: incremental UPSERT)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have data in {{JSON_FUENTE}} with nested objects and arrays that a relational engine cannot query directly with plain SQL. I need to unpack them into a relational, normalized, traceable, and repeatably loadable tabular model for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}. Flattening and normalization (Codd normal forms up to 3NF) convert nested paths into columns, arrays into parent-child 1:N relationships governed by primary and foreign keys, and produce an indexable, queryable schema. A good model unlocks analytical queries without parse-time overhead, reliable joins, referential integrity, efficient partitioning, idempotent loads, and an auditable lineage between source and store. The real challenge is not just flattening: it is handling schema variability across records, type ambiguities, and load repeatability without duplicating or losing rows.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specialized in relational modeling and semi-structured data transformation, with practice in JSON flattening, normalization (Codd normal forms), and each engine's native functions (JSON_TABLE, lateral flatten, UNNEST, OPENJSON).

Deliverable: a complete relational tabular model derived from {{JSON_FUENTE}}, with its DDL, transformation logic, lineage, and load plan. Steps:
1. Profile the structure: traverse {{JSON_FUENTE}} and build a path tree; for each node declare its type (object, array of objects, array of scalars, array of arrays, scalar), cardinality, nullability, and depth; report schema inconsistencies across records: optional fields, mixed types on the same path, JSON null vs. absent key, empty vs. absent arrays, numbers encoded as strings, booleans as 0/1/"true", and dates with heterogeneous formats or timezones.
2. Partition into tables: flatten each 1:1 object into columns of the same table using path notation and {{CONVENCION_NOMBRES}}; convert each array of objects into a 1:N child table; resolve arrays of scalars per {{ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS}}; decompose each array of arrays into successive levels of child tables. Respect the engine's identifier length limit.
3. Define keys: use {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} as the root entity key only if it is stable, non-null, and unique in the sample; otherwise generate a deterministic surrogate derived from the business identity (not the whole document, so reprocessing does not change it); propagate the parent foreign key to each child; keep the array position index as part of the child key when order matters; declare the merge key that will make the load idempotent.
4. Normalize to 3NF: eliminate repeating groups (1NF), partial dependencies (2NF), and transitive dependencies (3NF); flag points where denormalization is appropriate for query patterns and justify it with the trade-off (faster reads vs. risk of update anomaly).
5. Map types: infer the SQL type for each column (integer, decimal with precision and scale, text, boolean, date/time with or without timezone in ISO 8601, native JSON for irreducible residuals) according to {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}; define the NULL policy (absent key and JSON null map to NULL unless a contrary rule applies); flag ambiguous ones.
6. Deliver: CREATE TABLE DDL per table with PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, and CHECK; transformation logic to populate the tables (native SQL for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} or pseudocode if portable) consistent with {{MODO_CARGA}} and idempotent; a textual entity-relationship diagram; a lineage map linking each path in {{JSON_FUENTE}} to its destination column; and reconciliation queries comparing row counts and control sums between source and destination to detect losses or duplicates.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Profiling: inventory of paths, types, cardinalities, depth, and schema anomalies from the sample.
Phase 2 Logical design: entity tree, table decisions, and identification of 1:1, 1:N, and N:N (bridge) relationships.
Phase 3 Physical design: keys (natural or deterministic surrogate), merge keys, types, constraints, and 3NF normalization with notes on deliberate denormalization.
Phase 4 Materialization: DDL, idempotent transformation logic per {{MODO_CARGA}}, entity-relationship diagram, lineage map, and reconciliation queries. Any type, cardinality, or key inference not confirmed by {{JSON_FUENTE}} is marked [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every path in the JSON appears exactly once in the lineage map, mapped to a column or explicitly discarded with a reason.
- Every table has a primary key; every child table has its parent's foreign key and preserves array order when applicable; each child has its merge key declared.
- No array of objects was flattened to columns (avoids repeating groups); no repeated entity was left duplicated without separation; arrays of arrays are decomposed, not collapsed.
- The model satisfies 3NF or documents and justifies each deliberate deviation by query pattern with its trade-off.
- Each column has a valid SQL type in {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} with a defined NULL policy; absent key and JSON null are distinguished if the business requires it; inferences without evidence are marked [SUPUESTO].
- The DDL is executable in {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}; the transformation logic is idempotent per {{MODO_CARGA}} (re-running does not duplicate or lose rows) and produces the expected rows from {{JSON_FUENTE}}.
- The reconciliation queries balance row counts and control sums between source and destination.
Expected deliverable: profiling tree with anomalies, set of tables with DDL (PK/FK/UNIQUE/CHECK), idempotent transformation logic populating each table, textual entity-relationship diagram, path-to-column lineage map, reconciliation queries, and list of assumptions.
spec-datos_etl_arquitectura_medallion:
[inputs]
- MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE: {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} > Lakehouse engine and table format (e.g., Databricks Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg on Spark, Snowflake, BigQuery)
- DOMINIOS_DATOS: {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} > Domains or sources to model and their load type: batch, CDC, or streaming (e.g., daily batch sales, CDC customers, streaming web events)
- SLA_FRESCURA: {{SLA_FRESCURA}} > Maximum acceptable latency per layer (e.g., bronze near real-time, silver 1h, gold daily)
- HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION: {{HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION}} > Orchestrator and quality tool (e.g., Airflow + dbt + Great Expectations) (optional)
- POLITICA_CALIDAD: {{POLITICA_CALIDAD}} > How to handle records that fail a gate: quarantine, hard reject, or alert and continue; with who receives the alert if applicable (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Structuring the medallion architecture of a lakehouse so that each layer has unambiguous responsibilities and data promotion across bronze, silver, and gold is predictable, auditable, and reproducible. Purpose: unlock reliable analytical consumption by avoiding three costly anti-patterns: business logic leaking into bronze (breaks reprocessing), silver accumulating duplicates (corrupts metrics), and gold serving data without quality guarantees (erodes trust). The result is an architecture contract that a data team implements directly on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} for the domains {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, with freshness {{SLA_FRESCURA}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specialized in lakehouse architectures and the medallion pattern, with experience in data quality contracts and data governance.
Deliverable: an actionable medallion architecture contract. Components:
1. Per-layer table (bronze, silver, gold): purpose, owner, physical format, granularity, retention, and schema policy (schema-on-read vs. enforced). No overlapping responsibilities.
2. Promotion rules bronze->silver and silver->gold: applied transformations, deduplication, dimensional and fact conforming, null handling, and business rules per hop. Declare what does NOT happen in each layer (no business logic in bronze; no presentation aggregation in silver).
3. Quality gate matrix per layer: schema validation, referential integrity, freshness (per SLA_FRESCURA), completeness, and uniqueness; each gate with its trigger threshold and action on failure per POLITICA_CALIDAD (quarantine / reject / alert). If HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION is specified, express each gate as an assertion implementable in it.
4. Engineering guarantees per layer: load idempotency, reprocessing and backfill strategy, schema evolution handling (new column, type change, rename), partitioning and sorting, anchored to real mechanisms of MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE (MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE).
5. Lineage model: cross-layer traceability and minimum metadata per table (source, ingestion timestamp, schema version, run id, control hash) allowing a gold record to be traced back to bronze.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE, DOMINIOS_DATOS (with load type: batch/CDC/streaming), SLA_FRESCURA, HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION, and POLITICA_CALIDAD. If an essential piece of data is missing, request it; anything unconfirmed is marked [SUPUESTO]. Do not assert engine capabilities (MERGE, time travel, schema enforcement) without certainty: declare them [SUPUESTO] to validate.
Phase 2 - Design layers: define the per-layer table anchored to the real engine capabilities.
Phase 3 - Define promotions and gates: specify transformations, deduplication, and validations per hop, mapping each gate to its threshold and action on failure.
Phase 4 - Close engineering and lineage: idempotency, reprocessing, schema evolution, partitioning, metadata, and traceability.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The three layers have purpose, owner, format, granularity, retention, and schema policy, with no overlapping responsibilities.
- Each promotion rule explicitly declares what is done and what is NOT done in that layer.
- Bronze preserves raw immutable data; no business rule is applied before silver.
- Each quality gate has a trigger threshold and a concrete action on failure consistent with POLITICA_CALIDAD; if HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION was provided, the gate is expressible as an assertion in it.
- Idempotency, reprocessing, and schema evolution are resolved with engine mechanisms (MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE), not generic claims.
- The lineage allows tracing a gold record back to its origin in bronze.
- Late-arriving data and historical partition reprocessing are handled without duplication.
- Unverified engine capabilities are marked [SUPUESTO]; no prices or invented data.
Expected deliverable: medallion architecture contract document with per-layer table, promotion rules table, quality gate matrix with thresholds and actions, per-layer engineering guarantees, and lineage model, ready to implement on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}}.
spec-datos_etl_costo_optimizacion:
[inputs]
- PIPELINE: {{PIPELINE}} > Name and one-line description of the pipeline to optimize (purpose, layers, consumption outputs)
- PLATAFORMA_MOTOR: {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} > Cloud and query/transformation engine (columnar store, engine on data lake, orchestrator) and billing model if known (by bytes scanned, by slots/compute-hours, by storage and tier)
