>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist: table sorted descending with value, percentage of total, and cumulative percentage; UMBRAL_CORTE cutoff quantified (how many categories and what fraction of the universe); vital few named one by one; concentration metric reported (% of effect in the top 20%); explicit concentrated-vs-flat verdict; COLUMNA_VALOR validated as additive and comparable; nulls, negatives, and the "Other" residual handled without hiding them; biases declared; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented figures. Expected deliverable: Pareto table + named list of the vital group + decision paragraph stating what to attack first, what to leave in the tail, and why, ready to allocate effort for the period.
spec-datos_eda_funnel_dropoff:
[inputs]
- ETAPAS_FUNNEL: {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} > Funnel stages in order (e.g.: visit > signup > cart > checkout > purchase)
- VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA: {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}} > Unique users or events reaching each stage, aligned to the order above
- PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO: {{PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO}} > Date range and segment (channel, device, geography) the data covers
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > North-star metric or outcome to improve (e.g.: increase purchases, reduce checkout abandonment)
- BENCHMARK_CONVERSION: {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} > Conversion target or reference to compare against (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to decide where to focus my conversion funnel optimization effort. Without a clear diagnosis, the team invests in low-impact improvements on stages that are not the real bottleneck. A rigorous stage-by-stage analysis unlocks one decision: which single transition, if improved, moves the north-star metric the most, and what to test first. The business objective is {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} over the period and segment {{PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product and data analyst, specialized in conversion rate optimization (CRO) and funnel analysis, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from causation and prioritize by impact over effort.

Deliverable: a funnel diagnosis with prioritized hypotheses. Steps:
1. Build the funnel table from {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} and {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}: for each stage show users entering, stage-to-stage conversion (step N+1 / step N), cumulative conversion (step N / first stage), and users lost in absolute terms at each transition.
2. Identify the largest drop-off point. Explicitly declare whether you are prioritizing by the highest drop percentage or by the highest absolute volume of users lost, and why; when both criteria disagree, present both readings and recommend based on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.
3. Compare against {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} if provided, flagging stages below the reference; if there is no benchmark, say so and do not invent a target.
4. Formulate 3 to 5 improvement hypotheses for the critical drop-off, ordered by impact-to-effort ratio. Each must include: probable causal mechanism, validation method (A/B test, cohort analysis, segmentation, instrumentation review), and expected impact on conversion (range, not an exact figure).
5. Close with a data-quality note covering measurement risks (double counting, unfired events, attribution window, bot traffic, mixed segments, non-representative period) that qualify the conclusions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Input validation: confirm that each stage in {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} has its volume in {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}} and that the sequence is monotonically decreasing. If a stage, its volume, or the period is unclear, do not invent figures — request them before calculating. If a stage grows relative to the previous one, stop and flag a possible double count, out-of-order stage, or user re-entry before continuing. Flag any assumption with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Quantification: calculate conversions and absolute losses; show the formula for each column exactly once. Round with judgment and keep the unit (users vs. events) consistent throughout.
Phase 3 - Diagnosis: locate the critical drop-off and justify the prioritization criterion; explicitly name the winning transition (the one that moves the north-star metric the most if improved).
Phase 4 - Hypotheses and validation: derive hypotheses treated as explanations to be falsified, never as confirmed causes; for each one define what evidence would confirm or refute it.
Phase 5 - Safeguard: issue the data-quality note before closing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Complete funnel table: entries, stage-to-stage conversion, cumulative conversion, and absolute users lost per transition.
- [ ] Formulas for each column stated explicitly and arithmetic consistent with {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}; unit (users vs. events) uniform.
- [ ] Coherence validated: decreasing sequence; any growth or jump flagged as an anomaly before diagnosing.
- [ ] Largest drop-off identified with declared criterion (percentage vs. volume), discrepancies shown, and winning transition named.
- [ ] 3 to 5 hypotheses, each with causal mechanism, validation method, and expected impact, ordered by impact/effort.
- [ ] Hypotheses presented as explanations to validate with their falsification criterion; correlation not presented as causation.
- [ ] Missing figures requested, never invented; assumptions flagged [SUPUESTO]; non-existent benchmark not invented.
- [ ] Data-quality note with at least three measurement risks and their effect on the conclusions.
Expected deliverable: funnel table + diagnostic paragraph on the critical drop-off with the winning transition + prioritized list of 3 to 5 hypotheses + data-quality note.
spec-datos_storytelling_pregunta_a_insig:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_FUENTE: {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} > Table, chart, resolved query, or list of already-calculated findings to be distilled
- DECISION_A_HABILITAR: {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} > The concrete decision the insight must enable (e.g., where to invest the quarter's budget)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the insight and their level (e.g., executive committee, product lead, commercial team)
- METRICA_CLAVE: {{METRICA_CLAVE}} > The business metric at stake (e.g., cancellation rate, margin per order, conversion)
- LINEA_BASE: {{LINEA_BASE}} > Reference against which the finding is compared (prior period, target, control segment) (optional)
- HORIZONTE_DECISION: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} > When the decision must be made (e.g., this week, before quarter close); calibrates the urgency of the recommendation (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A completed analysis moves no one on its own: a table or chart is raw material, not a decision. The recipient ({{AUDIENCIA}}) does not need to see all the figures, they need to know what to do with them. This prompt converts {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} into an actionable insight that enables {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} and holds up when someone in the room asks "so what." It unlocks the shift from reporting data to driving decisions — which is where analytics generates value. The risk to neutralize is twofold: the inflated insight (claims more than the source supports) and the inert insight (true but with no actionable consequence).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and business storyteller, experienced in presenting findings to executive committees and translating metrics into defensible decisions.

Deliverable: an actionable insight structured from {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}, ready to open a meeting or an email. Produce, in this order:
1. Central claim: a single sentence with the main finding in business language, not metrics language: what changed in {{METRICA_CLAVE}}, by how much, against {{LINEA_BASE}}, and in what period.
2. The 'so what': why that claim matters to {{AUDIENCIA}}; what is gained or lost if no one acts.
3. Business implication: the cascading effect on revenue, cost, risk, customer experience, or operational capacity, with approximate magnitude only when the data supports it.
4. Recommendation: one concrete, prioritized action in service of {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, with a suggested owner, time horizon (aligned to {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} when provided), and a verifiable first step.
5. Confidence and monitoring: confidence level (high/medium/low) with its reason (sample size, data quality, presence of {{LINEA_BASE}}, possible causation vs. correlation), key assumptions flagged [SUPUESTO], and the single metric to monitor to confirm or refute the decision with its alarm threshold.
6. One-sentence headline: condensed version ready to head a slide or an email subject line.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: identify in {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} the dominant finding (highest magnitude, highest relevance to {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}) and separate observed fact from interpretation. Discard secondary findings that do not move the decision. If {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}, {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} is missing, ask for it before continuing.
Phase 2 - Structure with the Pyramid: apply the Minto principle (conclusion first, evidence after). The central claim leads; the so-what, implication, and recommendation support it. Every comparison states its {{LINEA_BASE}}; if there is no baseline, say so and lower the confidence.
Phase 3 - Test the 'so what': submit the claim to the so-what test. If it does not produce a real business consequence, reformulate it or demote it to context data. Flag every estimated figure or assumption with [SUPUESTO]; never invent numbers not in the source. Distinguish correlation from causation and do not present one as the other.
Phase 4 - Act and calibrate: derive the prioritized recommendation, assign honest confidence, and define the single monitoring metric with its threshold. Condense everything into the one-sentence headline.
Edge case: if {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} only allows description and not decision (ambiguous data, no baseline, insufficient sample), state this explicitly instead of forcing an insight, and indicate which missing data would close {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The central claim is a single sentence, in business language, and states magnitude, period, and {{LINEA_BASE}}.
- The 'so what' expresses a real consequence for {{AUDIENCIA}}, not a restatement of the data.
- The recommendation is concrete, prioritized, with an owner, time horizon, and verifiable first step, and serves {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}.
- Fact and interpretation are separated; correlation and causation are not confused; every estimate carries [SUPUESTO]; no figures are absent from {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}.
- The confidence level has an explicit reason and there is exactly one monitoring metric with a threshold.
- The one-sentence headline is self-contained and defensible.
- If the source does not allow a decision, the output states this and names the missing data instead of inflating the insight.
Expected deliverable: a 6-block actionable insight, dense and without filler, that passes the so-what test and allows {{AUDIENCIA}} to make {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} with evidence.
spec-datos_storytelling_estructura_scqa:
[inputs]
- TEMA_REPORTE: {{TEMA_REPORTE}} > Topic and scope of the data report (e.g., quarterly churn, acquisition funnel, campaign performance)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who decides upon reading it (role and level: executive committee, VP of Product, board) and what they care about
- HALLAZGOS_DATOS: {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}} > Available results, metrics, and figures (numbers, periods, segments, comparisons, source)
- DECISION_O_ACCION: {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} > Decision or action the report must enable or unlock
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > (optional) Expected final format (one-page memo, slide script, executive summary); default: one-page executive memo
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert the findings from {{TEMA_REPORTE}} into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA}} understands in minutes and uses for {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}. Today the data arrives as tables and charts without a narrative thread: the risk is that the conclusion gets buried under figures, the committee does not see why to act, or a decision is made based on the wrong metric. Structuring the report with the SCQA framework from Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle unlocks a narrative where the thesis comes first, the evidence supports it in an orderly fashion, and every visual pushes toward the decision rather than just describing the variable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data and executive communication analyst with fifteen years translating analytical results into committee decisions, expert in the SCQA framework from Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle.
Deliverable: an executive report in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with a thesis title, SCQA opening, pyramid body, actionable recommendation, and decision-oriented visual titles. Steps:
1. SITUATION: one or two sentences of the stable context that {{AUDIENCIA}} already accepts about {{TEMA_REPORTE}} (baseline, current target, status quo), neutral and consensual.
2. COMPLICATION: the change, tension, or anomaly that breaks that stability, anchored in a concrete data point from {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}}; this is where urgency comes from.
3. QUESTION: the single question that complication triggers in {{AUDIENCIA}}, specific and answerable with the data.
4. ANSWER: the thesis that answers the question as the main idea, first; below it, in pyramid form, the arguments that support it.
5. PYRAMID: MECE arguments (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive), ordered by relevance to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}, each with its quantified finding.
6. CLOSE: one actionable recommendation with a suggested owner and time horizon, and a decision-oriented title for each chart or table (state the insight, not the variable).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm TEMA_REPORTE, AUDIENCIA, HALLAZGOS_DATOS, and DECISION_O_ACCION; if a key figure or the baseline context is missing, ask before proceeding (one variable at a time).
Phase 2 - SCQA skeleton: sketch S, C, Q, and the R-thesis in a single line each; validate that C quantifies the tension and that Q has a unique answer.
Phase 3 - Evidence pyramid: group HALLAZGOS_DATOS under the thesis in MECE arguments ordered by weight; flag every inference as [SUPUESTO], separate correlation from causation, and name the source of each figure.
Phase 4 - Executive drafting: assemble the thesis title, opening, body, recommendation, and visual titles in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}; quantify impact in the unit that matters to AUDIENCIA.
Phase 5 - Verification: confirm a single main message, zero invented figures, overlaps or gaps in the pyramid resolved, and every visual pushes to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}.
Edge cases: if the data does not support a single thesis, declare the uncertainty and propose the missing data point; if the complication does not yet have a solid figure, flag it [SUPUESTO] and try to confirm it; if AUDIENCIA mixes levels, prioritize the highest-ranking decision-maker.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] SITUATION states stable, consensual context without thesis or judgment.
- [ ] COMPLICATION breaks the stability and is anchored in a real quantified data point from HALLAZGOS_DATOS (or flagged [SUPUESTO] if not).
- [ ] QUESTION is unique, specific, and answerable with the available data.
- [ ] ANSWER is the thesis and comes first (top-down), not at the end.
- [ ] Pyramid arguments are MECE and ordered by relevance to DECISION_O_ACCION.
- [ ] Each argument has a quantified finding with its source; every inference is flagged [SUPUESTO]; correlation is not confused with causation.
- [ ] There is a single main message; no figures were invented.
- [ ] Each visual title communicates the decision-oriented insight, not the variable.
- [ ] Recommendation has an owner and time horizon; no prices; neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: executive report in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with a thesis title, one-paragraph SCQA opening, pyramid body (2-4 arguments with data and source), actionable recommendation with owner and time horizon, and one decision-oriented title per visual.
spec-datos_storytelling_piramide_minto:
[inputs]
- HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS: {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} > Key findings and figures from the analysis (metrics, variations, periods, sources)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the narrative and their level (executive committee, area lead, board)
- DECISION_OBJETIVO: {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} > Concrete decision the narrative must enable
- LOGICA_AGRUPACION: {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} > (optional) Argument-ordering logic: deductive, inductive, or by relevance. If omitted, choose based on the audience and justify
- ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE: {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}} > (optional) Recommended action, owner, and time horizon
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A data analysis only generates a decision when told top-down: conclusion first, evidence after. Building the narrative with the Minto Pyramid and SCQA ensures that {{AUDIENCIA}} understands the what-to-do in the first 30 seconds and makes {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} without going through the data in reverse order. This reduces clarification meetings and turns the finding into action. The frequent error this prompt avoids: burying the conclusion under the method, opening with the methodology, or presenting lists of data without a single idea to govern them.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and executive storyteller, expert in the Minto Pyramid (Barbara Minto), the MECE principle, and the SCQA structure, with practice communicating to decision-making committees.
Deliverable: a top-down data-based narrative. Steps:
1. Draft the SCQA: Situation (stable, known context), Complication (what breaks it), Question (the one that triggers the analysis), Answer (the conclusion).
2. Distill ONE governing idea (governing thought): actionable, measurable, answering the Question in a single sentence.
3. Group 2 to 4 supporting arguments that satisfy MECE: mutually exclusive (no overlap) and collectively exhaustive (no gaps against the governing idea).
4. Order the arguments according to {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} (deductive, inductive, or by relevance) and declare the logic used and why it fits {{AUDIENCIA}}.
5. Under each argument, anchor evidence from {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} with figure, unit, period, and source. If a data point does not exist, flag it [SUPUESTO] or ask for it; never invent it. If two figures contradict each other, surface the tension instead of averaging.
6. Close with the implication ("and therefore") and the action according to {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}}, with owner and time horizon. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as the primary source of figures when available.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: draft the SCQA and validate that the Question and Answer are consistent with {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}.
Phase 2 - Peak: formulate the governing idea and discard it if it is not actionable or measurable.
Phase 3 - MECE structure: define the arguments, test for absence of overlap and gaps, order by {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}}.
Phase 4 - Evidence: anchor each figure to its argument with traceability (figure/unit/period/source); flag gaps [SUPUESTO] and data conflicts as open tensions.
Phase 5 - Narrative: draft the 5-7 sentence opening script and the MECE test per argument.
Phase 6 - Critical close: declare what decision is now enabled and the main risk of acting on the narrative as-is.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] SCQA in 4 lines, with Question and Answer aligned to {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}.
- [ ] A single governing idea, actionable and measurable (not descriptive or multi-topic).
- [ ] 2-4 arguments that pass the double MECE test (exclusive and exhaustive), with the ordering logic declared and justified.
- [ ] Each piece of evidence has figure, unit, period, and source; gaps flagged [SUPUESTO]; conflicts surfaced as tensions; zero invented numbers.
- [ ] Close with implication, action (owner + time horizon), decision enabled, and main risk.
Edge cases: insufficient data for a MECE branch → declare the gap and ask for it; mixed audience → prioritize the highest decision-making level; if {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} is not provided → choose one and justify.
Expected deliverable: (1) SCQA in 4 lines; (2) pyramid in indented text (governing idea > arguments > evidence); (3) narrative script of 5-7 sentences to open; (4) MECE test in one line per argument; (5) one line for decision enabled + main risk.
spec-datos_storytelling_audiencia_ejecut:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_TECNICO: {{ANALISIS_TECNICO}} > Source technical result: model output, dashboard, query, study, or report to translate
- DECISION_EN_JUEGO: {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} > Concrete decision this message must enable or unlock in the committee
- AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL: {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}} > Roles present and their dominant priority (CEO/growth, CFO/cost-risk, COO/operations)
- METRICA_NEGOCIO: {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}} > Business metric in which the impact must be expressed (revenue, cost, risk, time, customers)
- CIFRAS_REFERENCIA: {{CIFRAS_REFERENCIA}} > Base figures to quantify the impact (optional; anything not provided is flagged [SUPUESTO])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A solid technical analysis loses its value when it reaches the executive committee in the language of method rather than the language of decision. C-level has minutes, not pages, and acts on impact in {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}}, not on confidence intervals or model metrics. Translating ANALISIS_TECNICO into a narrative that enables DECISION_EN_JUEGO unlocks approval, aligns the committee, and turns data into action. A poor translation buries months of analytical work or, worse, induces a decision based on misunderstood figures.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Lead data analyst and executive communication consultant, with a track record presenting quantitative findings to steering committees and translating statistical complexity into business decisions.
Deliverable: a complete executive message ready to present. Steps:
1. Isolate the single decision DECISION_EN_JUEGO must unlock; if it is ambiguous or missing, ask before continuing. Do not proceed with multiple mixed decisions.
2. Draft a one-sentence headline that expresses the finding in terms of METRICA_NEGOCIO, never in statistical language.
3. Translate each metric from ANALISIS_TECNICO to its executive equivalent using CIFRAS_REFERENCIA; declare the conversion formula in half a line and flag [SUPUESTO] on every figure not provided. Give a range (floor-ceiling) when uncertainty is material.
4. Order the message in a pyramid (Minto): conclusion and recommendation first, 2 or 3 reasons next, methodological detail compressed into a single backup line at the end.
5. Anticipate 3 to 5 questions from AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL (data reliability, cost of acting, risk of not acting, discarded alternatives, impact horizon) with a brief, prepared, and defensible answer.
6. Close with an actionable recommendation and the concrete next step asked of the committee, with owner and timeline when the information allows.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: extract from ANALISIS_TECNICO the dominant finding and link it to DECISION_EN_JUEGO; discard whatever does not move the decision.
Phase 2 - Translate: apply the "metric to impact" principle; each unavoidable technical term is explained in half a line. Quantify using CIFRAS_REFERENCIA, declare the conversion, and flag assumptions.
Phase 3 - Structure: organize in an inverted pyramid according to the priority of AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL (growth, cost-risk, or operations lead the angle).
Phase 4 - Shield: build the block of anticipated questions with defensible answers; never defend a figure you cannot sustain.
Phase 5 - Close: formulate the recommendation and next step with owner and timeline when applicable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The headline is in terms of METRICA_NEGOCIO, without statistical jargon.
- [ ] The conclusion and recommendation appear before any methodological detail.
- [ ] Each technical finding has its quantified business-impact equivalent, with the conversion declared.
- [ ] Every figure not provided in CIFRAS_REFERENCIA is flagged [SUPUESTO] and verified data is distinguished from assumptions.
- [ ] The block anticipates between 3 and 5 real committee questions with a brief, defensible answer.
- [ ] Methodological detail does not exceed one backup line.
- [ ] Closes with an actionable recommendation and one concrete next step (owner/timeline when applicable).
- [ ] The message angle reflects the dominant priority of AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL.
Edge cases: if ANALISIS_TECNICO is inconclusive, say so explicitly and recommend the lowest-cost next action (more data, bounded test) instead of forcing a conclusion. If CIFRAS_REFERENCIA contradicts the analysis, flag the conflict before quantifying.
Expected deliverable: headline + executive paragraph (at most 5 lines) + 3 translated findings + block of anticipated questions with answers + final recommendation with next step. Neutral and professional English.
spec-datos_storytelling_titulo_accionabl:
[inputs]
- GRAFICO: {{GRAFICO}} > Chart type and variables it displays (e.g., sales bar chart by quarter, monthly churn line chart, price-volume scatter plot)
- INSIGHT: {{INSIGHT}} > Pattern, contrast, change, or anomaly that matters to communicate (optional; if missing, the model infers it and marks it as proposed)
- DATOS_CLAVE: {{DATOS_CLAVE}} > Actual figures, direction, or magnitude from the chart to support the title (without this, the model invents no numbers; period and unit when applicable)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who reads the chart, their level (executive, operational, technical) and what matters to them for deciding
- ACCION: {{ACCION}} > Decision or step the chart should trigger (approve, halt, reallocate, investigate, maintain)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the chart lives (executive slide, dashboard, report, email) to calibrate length and tone (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A chart title is the most-read spot and often the only thing the audience processes, yet it is routinely wasted as a descriptive label ("Sales by Quarter") that merely names the axes and forces the reader to discover on their own what to think. The goal is to convert the title of {{GRAFICO}} into an actionable statement that communicates {{INSIGHT}} directly and pushes {{AUDIENCIA}} toward {{ACCION}}, adapted for {{CANAL}}. This unlocks faster reading, shorter meetings, and better-framed decisions, because the message travels with the chart even when shared without context. EstrategIA contributes the rigor of one chart = one idea, asserting only what {{DATOS_CLAVE}} supports.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and data storytelling expert, trained in Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic's approach (Storytelling with Data), the one chart = one idea principle, and the design of titles as takeaways.
Deliver, in this order:
1. Restatement in one sentence of {{GRAFICO}} + main idea from {{INSIGHT}}; if any essential piece is missing (chart, insight, key data, audience, or action), ask for it before continuing and do not invent figures.
2. Diagnosis of the current title if provided: classify it as descriptive, neutral, or actionable and explain in one line the cost of a descriptive one (cognitive load, risk of misinterpretation).
3. Isolation of the single insight relevant to {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{ACCION}}; if there are multiple ideas, choose one and set the rest aside (one chart = one idea), suggesting whether the others deserve their own chart.
4. Three actionable titles as complete statements: declare the finding (not the dimension), include magnitude or direction from {{DATOS_CLAVE}} when available, and point toward {{ACCION}}; figures without backing are marked [SUPUESTO]. Keep length suitable for {{CANAL}} (one-line readable titles).
5. For each title: angle (urgency, opportunity, reassurance, alert), level of assertion (describing the change vs. explicit recommendation), and when to use it.
6. Recommended winning title with a one-line justification + suggested subtitle or annotation that holds the remaining context (period, source, assumption) without overloading the title.
7. List of anti-patterns: empty superlatives, judgments without data, jargon, unproven causality (correlation presented as cause), and claiming more than {{DATOS_CLAVE}} supports.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: identify the single idea that serves {{AUDIENCIA}}'s decision and discard secondary ones.
Phase 2 - Extraction: derive from {{DATOS_CLAVE}} the magnitude, direction, and comparison that will give the title strength, without adding data not provided; separate observed from inferred.
Phase 3 - Writing: write subject-verb-finding statements, testing different angles and verifying that each passes the "so what" test (answers why it matters and which decision it leads to).
Phase 4 - Curation: choose the winner based on fit to {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ACCION}}, and {{CANAL}}; vet against anti-patterns and confirm no figure lacks backing.
Edge cases: if {{INSIGHT}} contradicts a prior title, flag it; if {{DATOS_CLAVE}} does not support any strong statement, offer the most honest title available and declare the limitation; if multiple insights carry equal weight, recommend splitting into separate charts.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each title is a complete statement (subject + verb + finding), not an axis label.
- [ ] The title communicates a single idea, aligned with {{ACCION}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}.
- [ ] Every figure comes from {{DATOS_CLAVE}}; anything inferred carries [SUPUESTO]; no invented numbers or causality.
- [ ] Each title passes the "so what" test and fits the length of {{CANAL}}.
- [ ] No prices, no the word free, no emojis; neutral and professional English.
- [ ] Diagnosis of the prior title (if any), 3 alternatives with angle and assertion level, 1 justified winner, suggested subtitle, and list of anti-patterns were all delivered.
Expected deliverable: ready-to-paste block with the diagnosis, the 3 angle-labeled alternatives, the final recommendation with subtitle/annotation, and the list of what to avoid.
spec-datos_storytelling_resumen_una_pagi:
[inputs]
- PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO: {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} > Business question or decision that originated the analysis (e.g., "Should we raise the price of the Pro plan by 15% in July?")
- HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS: {{HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS}} > Findings and results already obtained with their figures, ready to synthesize (e.g., "churn rose from 4% to 6.5% in Q2; 70% of cancellations cite price; NPS of detractors dropped 12 points")
- AUDIENCIA_DECISION: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} > Who will read the one-pager and exactly what they decide (e.g., "product committee, decides whether to approve the price increase in July")
- FUENTE_PERIODO: {{FUENTE_PERIODO}} > Data origin, period, and coverage for the method note (e.g., "subscriptions data warehouse, Jan-Jun 2026, 12,400 active accounts")
- RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA: {{RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA}} > Recommendation or hypothesis already in mind, to refine or contrast (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a completed analysis and need it to travel: the decision-maker will not open twenty slides or the spreadsheet — they will read one page or nothing. A well-built one-pager applies the inverted pyramid — answer first, evidence second — and prioritizes by relevance to the decision, so that in two minutes the reader knows what happened, what it means, and what to do. This unlocks the decision without context-setting meetings, aligns those who were not in the analysis, and converts analytical work into action. The one-pager does NOT reopen the analysis or add new calculations: it synthesizes and prioritizes what was already obtained. Two failure modes to avoid: burying the conclusion under method (the reader gives up before reaching it) and stacking figures without implications (the reader does not know what to do with them). Frequent edge case: findings in tension — one points to acting, another to waiting; hiding it erodes trust, naming it builds it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and data storyteller, expert in executive communication, inverted pyramid, and design of one-page decision-oriented summaries.

Produce a self-contained, scannable one-pager with these components, in this order:
1. Answer headline: a single declarative sentence that delivers the conclusion (not the topic) and answers PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO. If the evidence does not allow a definitive answer, the headline declares the confidence level or condition (e.g., "yes, but only for monthly plans").
2. Main message: two or three lines synthesizing the what and the why, calibrated for AUDIENCIA_DECISION (their level, language, and decision lever).
3. Key findings: three to five, selected from HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS by relevance to the decision; each with its figure and its business implication (the "and therefore"). If a finding contradicts the direction of the recommendation, include it instead of omitting it.
4. Actionable recommendation: what to do, with owner or next step, drawing from RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA if provided (to refine or contrast against the evidence, not to validate uncritically); include the risk or cost of inaction when applicable.
5. Method note: source, period, and coverage from FUENTE_PERIODO, plus assumptions and limitations that condition the reading (sample bias, missing data, short time window).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: fix the question, the audience, and the single decision the one-pager must unlock; write the answer headline as a conclusion, not a title.
Phase 2 — Hierarchy: order results by relevance to that decision, keep only three to five findings and discard the rest; for each, pair the figure with its implication (what changes for the business). Do not present an estimate as a measurement; mark [SUPUESTO] for every inference; do not invent or round figures not in HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS. If two findings are in tension, name it explicitly.
Phase 3 — Recommendation: derive the actionable next step with owner and, if applicable, the cost of inaction; keep it traceable to the findings (each recommendation is backed by at least one listed finding) and consistent with the headline's confidence level.
Phase 4 — Method audit and fit to one page: declare source, period, coverage, assumptions, and limitations; trim so the whole thing fits visually on one page and is readable without opening the original analysis. If an essential piece is missing (the exact decision, a key figure, or the source), ask for it before writing instead of inventing it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The headline is a declarative sentence with the conclusion and answers PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO; it does not name the topic; if evidence is partial, it declares confidence or condition.
- There are three to five findings, each with figure and implication; none without its "and therefore".
- Every inference is marked [SUPUESTO]; no figure was invented or rounded without basis; no estimate is presented as a measurement.
- Findings in tension with the recommendation are named instead of omitted.
- The recommendation is actionable, has an owner or next step, is traceable to the listed findings, and is consistent with the headline's confidence level.
- The method note declares source, period, coverage, assumptions, and limitations.
- The whole thing fits on one page, is scannable (headlines and bullets, not long paragraphs), and is self-contained (readable without the original analysis).
- If an essential piece was missing, it was asked before executing; nothing was filled in with invention.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a one-pager in five blocks (answer headline, main message, three to five key findings with figure and implication, actionable recommendation with owner, method note) that fits on one page and is read in two minutes.
spec-datos_storytelling_manejo_incertidu:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION: {{ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION}} > Analysis performed and the central recommendation to communicate
- INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS: {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}} > Confidence intervals, scenario ranges, or margins of error for key estimates
- SUPUESTOS_CLAVE: {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}} > Assumptions on which the analysis rests (data, model, context)
- LIMITACIONES_DATOS: {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}} > Known limitations: sample bias, temporal coverage, quality, missing variables
- AUDIENCIA_DECISORA: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} > Who receives the narrative and decides (role, level of data fluency)
- DECISION_EN_JUEGO: {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} > Concrete decision the recommendation aims to enable, with its time horizon and reversibility if known
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A solid analysis loses its power in two opposite ways: it is presented as absolute certainty and reality disproves it, destroying credibility; or it drowns in disclaimers and no one dares to decide, wasting the work. The goal is to convert {{ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION}}, with its {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}}, {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}}, and {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}}, into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} can use to make {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} with calibrated confidence. Communicating uncertainty honestly protects the analyst and improves the decision: it unlocks moving forward while knowing exactly what bet is being made, with what evidence, and under what condition it would be revisited. Calibration is the asset: declared confidence must match the actual strength of the data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data scientist specializing in uncertainty communication and executive decision support, with mastery of statistical inference and calibrated narrative.
Deliver a narrative ready to present, structured as follows:
1. Single-sentence headline: the recommendation and its calibrated confidence level.
2. Three separate columns or blocks: "What we know" (evidence with its source), "What we assume" (each assumption labeled [SUPUESTO] with sensitivity high/medium/low if it fails), "What we do not know" (acknowledged gaps).
3. Reading of each interval from {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}} translated into practical consequence for {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}: what the low, central, and high extremes imply — what changes the action, not just the number.
4. Limitations map: how each element of {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}} bounds the reading, with direction of bias (overestimates/underestimates) when known and its impact on the recommendation.
5. Actionable close: recommended action, quantitative threshold that would trigger or reverse it, and the data or experiment that most reduces uncertainty (highest informational value per cost).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Calibration: classify each claim as evidence / assumption / gap; assign consistent probabilistic language (virtually certain, likely, plausible, unlikely) coherent with the actual strength of the data. Use the same scale throughout the text.
Phase 2 - Translation: convert each statistical range into decision language, showing what changes for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} at each extreme (low, central, high), not just the value.
Phase 3 - Structured honesty: expose limitations with direction and impact, without burying the recommendation or inflating caution. Prioritize high-sensitivity assumptions: if one fails and changes the recommendation, it should appear first.
Phase 4 - Close: define quantitative action/reversal threshold and the next measurement of highest informational value.
Adjust density and technicality to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}'s level. Do not invent figures: if a range or assumption is missing, mark it [SUPUESTO] or ask for it. Maintain internal consistency: headline confidence = evidence strength minus assumption fragility.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Opens with recommendation + calibrated confidence in a single sentence.
- Visibly separates what we know / assume / do not know; each assumption carries [SUPUESTO] and its sensitivity.
- Each interval is translated into practical consequence for the decision (low / central / high extreme), showing what changes the action.
- Limitations appear with direction of bias and impact on the recommendation.
- Uses calibrated and consistent probabilistic language; zero false certainties and zero paralyzing caution.
- Closes with action, quantitative reversal threshold, and the data of highest informational value.
- Internal consistency: declared confidence matches the evidence net of assumption fragility.
- Zero invented figures; gaps marked explicitly.
Expected deliverable: uncertainty narrative ready to present to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}, sustaining confidence in the recommendation while being transparent about its limits and making clear under what condition it would be revisited.
spec-datos_storytelling_anti_chartjunk:
[inputs]
- GRAFICO: {{GRAFICO}} > Chart to audit: attached image/screenshot or textual description (type, axes, series, colors, decorations)
- MENSAJE_CLAVE: {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} > The single idea the chart must convey at first glance
- AUDIENCIA_MEDIO: {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} > Who will see it and where (e.g., executive committee on a slide, operational dashboard, printed report)
- DATO_PROTAGONISTA: {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}} > Series, bar, or point that must stand out above the rest
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Brand, palette, tool, or accessibility limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A chart loaded with decorations forces the reader to work to find the data and dilutes the decision it should trigger. Cleaning it under Tufte's principles turns a noisy visualization into a visual argument understood in seconds: it unlocks a piece ready to support a decision for {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}, where attention is scarce and every drop of ink must earn its place. Assumption: the underlying data is correct; this task optimizes the representation, it does not audit the source. If the data itself is wrong, it is flagged but not corrected here.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data visualization specialist trained in Edward Tufte's work (data-ink ratio, chartjunk, redundant ink, graphical integrity, small multiples).
Redesign {{GRAFICO}} to eliminate chartjunk and reinforce {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}, highlighting {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}. Steps:
1. Confirm the single message the chart must communicate; if {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} is ambiguous or missing, ask for it before proceeding. Do not invent data not present in {{GRAFICO}}.
2. Inventory chartjunk: heavy gridlines, backgrounds and shading, 3D effects, gradients, unnecessary borders, decorative icons, redundant legends, excess decimal places, unjustified dual axes, and moire patterns.
3. Classify each element as data-ink, redundant-ink, or non-data-ink and qualitatively estimate the current data-ink ratio (high/medium/low with justification).
4. Propose the redesign element by element with the suppress-eliminate-highlight hierarchy: what to eliminate, what to suppress to background gray, and what to highlight with a single emphasis color on {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}; replace the legend with direct labeling when applicable and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
5. Evaluate whether the chart type is appropriate for {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}; if a simpler form (bar, line, table, slopegraph) communicates better, propose it with the explicit trade-off.
6. Deliver: before-vs-after representation in text/ASCII, prioritized change table with the rationale for each change citing the Tufte principle that justifies it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix the single message, the audience, and the medium; without a clear message, no audit takes place.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: go through the chart marking each ink mark as data, redundant, or non-data; name each chartjunk item with its category.
Phase 3 - Redesign: apply the suppress-eliminate-highlight hierarchy; one emphasis color only, direct labeling, honest scales (no truncated axes that distort), sufficient contrast for accessibility.
Phase 4 - Justification: link each change to a Tufte principle and verify that the message survives with less ink.
Edge cases: if there are multiple competing messages, prioritize one and propose separating the rest into small multiples. If {{RESTRICCIONES}} requires keeping a chartjunk element (brand), suppress it to the minimum and record the concession. If the brand palette prevents a single legible emphasis color, propose an alternative and name the conflict.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The single message is stated and guides the entire redesign.
- [ ] All identified chartjunk was eliminated or suppressed, not merely flagged.
- [ ] The data-ink ratio clearly improves between before and after.
- [ ] There is a single visual focus and {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}} is unambiguously the protagonist.
- [ ] Each change cites the Tufte principle that backs it.
- [ ] Scales and proportions preserve graphical integrity (no distortion or misleading truncated axes).
- [ ] Whether the chart type is optimal for the message was evaluated.
- [ ] The result respects {{RESTRICCIONES}}, is legible, and is actionable for {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}.
Expected deliverable: before-vs-after chart block, prioritized change table (element - action - Tufte principle), and a closing line with the message the cleaned chart now communicates effortlessly.
spec-datos_storytelling_narrativa_para_n:
[inputs]
- HALLAZGO: {{HALLAZGO}} > Analytical result to explain with its exact figure (e.g., "the model predicts 7% churn", "A/B test raised conversion by 1.8 points")
- FUENTE_METODO: {{FUENTE_METODO}} > Where the number comes from: model, hypothesis test, metric, or dashboard, with its interval, p-value, sample size, or period if available
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the explanation and what matters to them (e.g., commercial committee, board of directors, operations team)
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > What decision or action the finding enables, and who makes it
- NIVEL_TECNICO: {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} > Audience's familiarity with data: none, basic, or intermediate (defines how much each term is explained)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Output format: email, spokesperson script, or single slide (adjusts length and density). If omitted, assume single slide
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An analytical finding only creates value when the decision-maker understands it and acts. Here {{HALLAZGO}}, coming from {{FUENTE_METODO}}, is translated into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA}} (technical level: {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}) can understand, remember, and use to enable {{DECISION}}, optimized for {{CANAL}}. The goal is to close the gap between the rigor of the analysis and the business action without diluting either: not a decorated datum nor an exaggerated conclusion.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior data analyst specializing in data storytelling and executive communication, with mastery of the Minto Pyramid (conclusion first) and the SCQA arc (situation-complication-question-answer).
Deliverable: a narrative ready to present or send, with these six numbered blocks:
1. Headline: a single sentence with the "so what" of the finding in business language, without statistical jargon.
2. Context: one or two sentences on why it mattered to measure this and what was at stake.
3. Translated finding: the number explained with a concrete everyday analogy that makes the magnitude tangible (e.g., a probability as "out of every 100, 7"); any technical term is explained in plain language the first time according to {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}.
4. Scale: a comparison or reference point that gives dimension (against prior period, declared target, or what would be expected by chance).
5. Confidence: how sure we are in human language, how solid the evidence is (sample, period), and what could change the conclusion, without raw formulas.
6. Recommendation: the concrete action the finding supports to enable {{DECISION}}, with the next step for the decision-maker.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: extract from {{HALLAZGO}} and {{FUENTE_METODO}} the number, its nature (prediction, difference, correlation, trend), and its uncertainty (interval, p-value, sample, period). Classify {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} to set the ceiling for technical language allowed.
Phase 2 - Plan: choose the analogy and comparison most faithful to the actual magnitude before writing; verify that they do not introduce distortion, false causality, or false precision. Define which terms need a gloss and adjust the length to {{CANAL}}.
Phase 3 - Execute: write the six blocks applying the translation rules: never assert causality if there is only correlation; separate statistical significance from practical relevance; round to the precision the audience can act on; use only figures present in {{HALLAZGO}}; mark all data not provided as [SUPUESTO]; if the sample, period, or uncertainty are weak, declare it in the confidence block instead of hiding it. If {{HALLAZGO}}, {{FUENTE_METODO}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} with {{DECISION}} is missing, request it before writing.
Edge cases: if {{FUENTE_METODO}} provides no uncertainty, state it explicitly in confidence and do not invent it; if the finding does not clearly support an action, offer the most defensible recommendation and name the missing data; if {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} is none, eliminate all terms and leave only the analogy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The headline communicates the business "so what" without a single statistical jargon word.
- [ ] The analogy is concrete, everyday, and faithful to the actual magnitude of the number, neither exaggerating nor minimizing it.
- [ ] The comparison gives actionable scale (against period, target, or chance).
- [ ] No technical term appears without explanation at {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}'s level.
- [ ] Causality is not asserted where there is only correlation; significance and practical relevance are distinguished.
- [ ] Every figure comes from {{HALLAZGO}}; assumed items are marked [SUPUESTO]; strength and confidence limit are in human language.
- [ ] The recommendation connects directly to {{DECISION}} and indicates the next step for the decision-maker.
- [ ] Length and density fit {{CANAL}}.
Expected deliverable: six-block numbered narrative, ready to paste into email, spokesperson script, or slide, in neutral and professional English, no emojis.
spec-datos_calidad_dimensiones_evaluacio:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name, schema, or sample of the dataset to evaluate (table, file, view; columns and types if known; approximate record volume)
- COLUMNAS_CRITICAS: {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}} > Business-critical fields that carry more weight in the evaluation (e.g. customer_id, email, amount, date)
- REGLAS_NEGOCIO: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} > Rules and valid domains (e.g. amount >= 0, valid email format, status in {active, inactive}, FK to catalog)
- FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION: {{FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION}} > Expected cadence and freshness window for measuring timeliness (e.g. daily, data no older than 24h)
- UMBRALES: {{UMBRALES}} > Target threshold per dimension and weights for the global score (optional; if missing, propose standard values and mark them [SUPUESTO])
- FUENTE_VERDAD: {{FUENTE_VERDAD}} > Validated reference against which to measure accuracy (e.g. master system, audited sample) or "No source of truth" to activate the declared proxy
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Business decisions, models, and reports are built on {{DATASET}}; defective data propagates errors to every downstream consumer and the cost of detecting them grows with each hop. This evaluation produces a measurable and auditable per-dimension baseline, enables prioritizing remediation by impact before operationalizing the data, and leaves reusable rules as a quality contract for continuous monitoring.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality and data governance engineer, with expertise in the DAMA-DMBOK framework and data profiling techniques.
Deliverable: quality report with scorecard, prioritized findings, and remediation plan. Steps:
1. Confirm schema, COLUMNAS_CRITICAS, REGLAS_NEGOCIO, FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION, and FUENTE_VERDAD; if anything is missing, ask before proceeding. Do not infer the data structure.
2. For each of the six dimensions (completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness) define what it measures in this dataset; distinguish validity (syntactic conformance to the domain) from accuracy (correspondence with reality).
3. Propose per dimension a metric with an explicit formula (numerator/denominator or logical condition) and the executable verification rule (regex, range, unique key, referential integrity, freshness window). State the calculation granularity (column, record, or dataset).
4. Assign an acceptance threshold per UMBRALES (or [SUPUESTO] standard) and calculate a 0-100 score per dimension, weighting COLUMNAS_CRITICAS more heavily.
5. Calculate the weighted global score (weights must sum to 100%) and build the scorecard with green/yellow/red traffic light against the threshold.
6. Prioritize findings by impact x severity and deliver a remediation plan with probable root cause, suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for continuous monitoring.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpretation: restate the dataset, scope, and received parameters; list gaps and assumptions [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 Planning: present the dimension > metric > formula > rule > threshold > weight matrix before calculating; confirm weights sum to 100%.
Phase 3 Execution: apply or describe profiling, calculate scores, weight the global, write findings and plan.
Accuracy note: accuracy is measured against FUENTE_VERDAD or a validated sample; if none exists, declare it [SUPUESTO] and use a proxy (e.g. rule-conformance rate) without claiming actual accuracy.
Edge cases: empty dataset or non-representative sample (declare the limitation, do not extrapolate); columns with intentionally valid nulls (do not penalize as missing); conflicting rules (escalate, do not choose silently); dimension not applicable to the dataset (mark N/A with justification and re-normalize weights).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All six dimensions covered (or marked N/A with justification), each with a contextual definition, metric, formula, and executable rule.
- [ ] Validity and accuracy explicitly differentiated; format conformance is not confused with correspondence with reality.
- [ ] Every formula is reproducible (numerator/denominator or explicit condition) with stated granularity; no score without a method.
- [ ] Thresholds declared; global weights sum to 100%; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Accuracy not claimed without a source of truth; if none, declared proxy is used.
- [ ] Findings prioritized by impact x severity, with affected column, estimated records, and probable root cause.
- [ ] Remediation plan with suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for continuous monitoring.
Expected deliverable: report with (a) matrix of the 6 dimensions, (b) scorecard with per-dimension and weighted global score with traffic light, (c) prioritized findings table, (d) actionable remediation plan.
spec-datos_calidad_reglas_validacion:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name and purpose of the dataset or table to validate on every load
- ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS: {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} > List of columns with their expected type and whether they allow nulls
- CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES: {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} > Primary key, unique keys, and foreign-key relationships to other tables
- REGLAS_NEGOCIO: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} > Valid ranges, closed domains, and format patterns required by the business
- TOLERANCIA_FALLOS: {{TOLERANCIA_FALLOS}} > Acceptable threshold of failed rows per family and what to do when exceeded (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Every load of {{DATASET}} is the last gate before data feeds downstream tables, models, and dashboards. Without explicit assertions, a type change, an out-of-range value, a key duplicate, an orphan foreign key, or a silent volume drop propagate without warning and are discovered late, when a report is already wrong and trust is already broken. An executable rule catalog on every ingestion turns quality into a verifiable contract: the pipeline fails fast and visibly, and stops depending on manual reviews.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer with experience in assertion engines (Great Expectations, Soda Core, dbt tests) and data contracts.
Deliver a validation rule catalog for {{DATASET}}, organized by the five canonical families plus a cross-cutting one:
1. Type and nulls: one assertion per column in {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} verifying the expected type and null rule.
2. Range and domain: assertions for min/max, closed domains, and conditional rules derived from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}.
3. Format: patterns (regex or mask) for fixed-structure fields per {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}.
4. Uniqueness: primary key, unique keys, and unique combinations declared in {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}}.
5. References: referential integrity of every foreign key in {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} toward its parent table, detecting orphans.
6. Cross-cutting (when they provide a signal): freshness (maximum load recency), volume (row count within an expected range), and distribution (null proportion or deviation of a key metric against its historical baseline).
For each rule deliver a row with: name, affected column or relationship, one-line objective, deterministic and evaluable logical assertion expression, severity (blocking, warning, informational), responsible owner, failure-row tolerance threshold from {{TOLERANCIA_FALLOS}}, and failure action (reject load, row quarantine, log). Mark any assumption as [SUPUESTO] (e.g. time zone of date fields, null vs empty semantics, expected load frequency). If {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} or {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} are missing or ambiguous, request the information before generating rules; do not invent field names. NEVER include prices.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Mapping: reconstruct the column, type, key, and relationship inventory; list the gaps that prevent writing a rule and the assumptions made to continue.
Phase 2 - Design: write rules family by family, deriving each assertion from a specific type, range, pattern, uniqueness, reference, or cross-cutting check; assign severity, owner, threshold, and action. Severity trade-off: blocking only if failure corrupts downstream consumers; warning if it degrades without breaking; informational for monitoring. Cover edge cases: slowly changing dimensions, late-arriving data, null vs empty string, duplicates from idempotent reprocessing, and foreign keys to tables not yet loaded.
Phase 3 - Orchestration: order execution (structure before content: type and uniqueness first, then range/format, then references, finally cross-cutting) and define the run report (rule, evaluated rows, failed rows, failure %, triggered severity, and overall load verdict) plus the remediation playbook by action.
Phase 4 - Verification: review the catalog against the Phase C checklist before delivering.

spec-datos_calidad_profiling_anomalias:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Tabular dataset to profile (file, table, or sample) and its schema or data dictionary if available
- COLUMNA_TIEMPO: {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}} > Date or partition column for analyzing null concentration and drift (optional)

- REGLAS_DOMINIO: {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} > Known ranges, valid categories, formats, and column-level constraints (optional)
- CLAVE_PRIMARIA: {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} > Column or combination that should be unique (optional)
- USO_DESTINO: {{USO_DESTINO}} > Downstream analytical use that calibrates severity (report, model, dashboard)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dataset enters an analytical flow and no one knows if it is trustworthy until a decision goes wrong. Profiling it before use turns an opaque file into a quantified risk map: it prevents decisions on broken data and lays the foundation for continuous monitoring. The goal is a report that a team can act on today and automate tomorrow, calibrated to the intended use {{USO_DESTINO}}. A single undetected wrong figure propagates downstream and erodes trust in the entire flow; the cost of not profiling is invisible until it is already too late.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data observability, and drift detection in production pipelines.
Deliverable: a quality report for {{DATASET}} with a prioritized remediation plan. Steps:
1. Per-column inventory: inferred type, cardinality, null percentage, value sample; flag ambiguous types and separate structural quality (schema, types, uniqueness) from semantic quality (domain, inter-column coherence).
2. Unexpected nulls: nulls by column and by value of {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}}; detect disguised nulls (empty string, spaces, 'NA', 'null', '0', sentinels like 9999 or 1900-01-01) and partition concentrations that reveal ingestion failures.
3. Out-of-domain values: contrast each column against {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} (ranges, categories, formats, lengths) and verify uniqueness of {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}}; list violations with count and examples. If there are no rules, infer candidates from the data and mark them [SUPUESTO].
4. Distribution drift: compare current vs {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} per column; numerics with changes in mean, median, standard deviation, and percentiles plus KS; categoricals with chi-square or PSI; declare threshold and separate volume drift (more/fewer rows) from shape drift (same mass, different distribution).
5. Anomalous patterns: exact and near-duplicates, impossible column combinations, outliers (IQR or robust z-score via MAD), trend breaks, and daily volumes outside range.
6. For each finding: column or rule, symptom, quantified magnitude, severity (critical/high/medium/low) by impact on {{USO_DESTINO}}, probable cause, and concrete remediation (correction, quarantine, or acceptance with a note).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 Framing: confirm DATASET and schema; if COLUMNA_TIEMPO, PERIODO_REFERENCIA, REGLAS_DOMINIO, or CLAVE_PRIMARIA are missing, ask for them in a short list before calculating and state which analyses remain limited without them. Phase 1 Base profiling (steps 1-3). Phase 2 Temporal comparison and drift (step 4). Phase 3 Anomalies (step 5). Phase 4 Synthesis: summary table ordered by severity, fitness verdict, and checks to automate. State the method and threshold of every statistic; mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO]; do not report values that do not come from DATASET. If DATASET is only a sample, declare that cardinality and drift are indicative, not conclusive.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Covers all four families: unexpected nulls, drift, out-of-domain values, and anomalous patterns.
- Each finding includes a quantified magnitude (count or percentage), severity justified by impact on {{USO_DESTINO}}, and concrete remediation with a clear action (correct, quarantine, or accept with a note).
- Each statistic declares its method and threshold (KS, chi-square/PSI, IQR/MAD).
- Detects disguised nulls and sentinels, not just NaN; separates structural from semantic quality.
- Every figure comes from DATASET; assumptions are [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented.
- If a key input was missing, the report declares which analyses were out of scope.
Expected deliverable: report with per-column inventory, findings by family, summary table ordered by severity, fitness verdict for analytical use, and list of recurring checks to automate for continuous monitoring.
spec-datos_calidad_limpieza_estandarizac:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name and description of the dataset to clean (table, file, source, and approximate row/column volume)
- USO_ANALITICO: {{USO_ANALITICO}} > Destination of the clean data (report, model, dashboard, warehouse load); determines the severity of each rule

- CLAVE_NEGOCIO: {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}} > Column(s) identifying a unique record, basis for detecting duplicates (optional)
- POLITICA_NULOS: {{POLITICA_NULOS}} > Default preference for nulls (drop row, impute, or flag 'Unknown') (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, existing profile, data sample, data dictionary, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dataset with inconsistent formats, poorly inferred types, untreated nulls, and duplicate categories poisons any downstream analysis: it aggregates incorrectly, biases models, and breaks trust in the dashboard. The goal is to produce an auditable cleaning and standardization plan, not a blind script: every transformation must be explainable, justifiable, and reversible. This unlocks a reliable data delivery with clear lineage and verifiable acceptance criteria, reducing rework and data disputes. The plan always operates on a copy: the original source is never overwritten.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data governance, and reproducible pipelines.
Deliverable: a traceable cleaning and standardization plan for DATASET oriented to USO_ANALITICO. Steps:
1. Profile and report findings: rows/columns, detected vs expected type, null % per column, cardinality, duplicates, ranges, and outliers. If ADJUNTOS does not include a profile, state the exact query or command to run instead of inventing figures; mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO].
2. Format normalization: dates to ISO 8601 with explicit time zone; numbers with consistent decimal/thousands separator; text with trim, casing, and encoding (including invisible spaces and non-printable characters).
3. Type correction: detect columns with wrong type (number/date/boolean stored as text), define the casting rule and handling of values that fail (to null, to quarantine, or row rejection); preserve leading zeros in codes.
4. Null handling per column: decide to drop row, impute (mean/median/mode/constant), or flag 'Unknown', justified against USO_ANALITICO and respecting POLITICA_NULOS when applicable; declare the bias each imputation introduces (imputation for a predictive model differs from that for an accounting report).
5. Category unification: group variants (casing, accents, abbreviations, typos) to a canonical value via an explicit mapping table in COLUMNAS_CRITICAS; define a default rule for unmapped new variants.
6. Deduplication: use CLAVE_NEGOCIO, define the survival criterion for the winning record, tiebreaking, and what to do with conflicts; verify that referential integrity with other tables is not broken.
7. Final validation: verifiable acceptance rules (post-conditions) confirming the cleaning met its objective.
For EACH rule deliver: affected column, transformation, justification, risk if applied incorrectly, and reversion procedure.
Limits: treat PII under minimization and use placeholders in examples; if a rule eliminates more rows than a reasonable threshold, flag it as a decision requiring human approval instead of applying it silently.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Profile and diagnose: quantify the current state before proposing changes; never transform blindly.
Phase 2 - Design traceable rules: one rule per problem, ordered by dependencies (format and type before nulls, nulls before dedup, dedup before validation), each with justification and reversion.
Phase 3 - Define validation and deliver: before/after table, reproducible and idempotent change log (execution order + affected counts), and acceptance rules.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Real profile reported or exact query stated; zero invented figures (assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]).
- [ ] All six fronts covered: formats, types, nulls, categories, duplicates, validation.
- [ ] Every rule has column, transformation, justification, risk, and reversion.
- [ ] Dates with explicit time zone; failed casts with a defined destination (null/quarantine/rejection).
- [ ] Null decisions justified against USO_ANALITICO with declared bias, not made by default.
- [ ] Explicit category mapping table with a canonical value per group and a rule for new variants.
- [ ] Survival criterion and referential integrity of deduplication defined without ambiguity.
- [ ] Verifiable acceptance rules (boolean or measurable).
- [ ] Execution order respects dependencies, is idempotent and reproducible; high row loss flagged for approval.
Expected deliverable: plan document with (a) profiling report, (b) traceable rule catalog grouped by the six fronts, (c) category mapping table, (d) before/after table, (e) ordered and idempotent change log, and (f) acceptance rules.
spec-datos_calidad_deduplicacion_matchin:
[inputs]
- TIPO_ENTIDAD: {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} > Entity to deduplicate (customers, suppliers, products, patients)
- ATRIBUTOS_MATCH: {{ATRIBUTOS_MATCH}} > Available comparison attributes (name, tax/document ID, email, phone, address)
- FUENTES_Y_CONFIABILIDAD: {{FUENTES_Y_CONFIABILIDAD}} > Source systems and their relative reliability + recency, for survival rules
- TOLERANCIA_ERROR: {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}} > Case priority: precision (avoid erroneous merges) or recall (leave no duplicates behind); ideally with the relative cost of each error type
- MUESTRA_REGISTROS: {{MUESTRA_REGISTROS}} > Row sample or schema with types (optional; without it they are requested before setting weights)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dataset of {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} accumulates duplicates of the same entity captured across different channels and moments: spelling variations, abbreviations, accents, typos, garbage values ('N/A', '00000000', default birthdays), and missing fields inflate the unique-entity count, degrade segmentation, duplicate communications, and break reports. Resolving entities into an auditable golden record unlocks a reliable single view, decisions on clean data, and traceability of every merge back to its source records.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer specialized in entity resolution / record linkage, with expertise in deterministic and probabilistic matching, multi-pass blocking, clustering by transitive closure, and survival rules.

Deliverable: the complete and executable design of a deduplication and matching pipeline for {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}}, with every decision justified and traceable. Steps:
1. Profile {{ATRIBUTOS_MATCH}}: completeness, cardinality, and discriminating power of each attribute; detect garbage/placeholder values that should not score; define normalization rules (case-folding, strip accents/punctuation, phones to canonical E.164 format, address parsing, tokenization, explicit null handling).
2. Design blocking: blocking keys that reduce the NxN space to manageable blocks; use more than one blocking pass when a single criterion would miss legitimate pairs; justify the exhaustiveness/cost trade-off with the estimated reduction factor.
3. Define exact matching: field combinations that give immediate deterministic match (e.g. valid tax ID + equal).
4. Define fuzzy matching: named metric per attribute (Jaro-Winkler/Levenshtein for names, Jaccard/cosine token similarity for addresses, exact for dates/ids), weighted score, and two thresholds (auto-match and gray zone for human review) calibrated per {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}} and, if known, the relative cost of false positive vs false negative.
5. Group pairs into same-entity clusters (transitive closure) and mitigate over-merging with an explicit safeguard (cluster size limit, intra-cluster coherence on strong attributes, or collective resolution).
6. Set survival and merge rules per attribute using {{FUENTES_Y_CONFIABILIDAD}} (reliability + recency + completeness), preserving source IDs as lineage of the golden record and recording which rule decided each value.
7. Validate with metrics (precision, recall, F1, false positive/negative counts on a labeled sample), edge cases, and a manual sampling plan for the gray zone; define an incremental reprocessing strategy for new records.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Framing: if {{MUESTRA_REGISTROS}} or the schema are not available, ask for them before setting weights; do not invent thresholds without domain evidence (mark any tentative value as [SUPUESTO] conditioned on the sample).
Phase 1 - Profiling, garbage value detection, and normalization of {{ATRIBUTOS_MATCH}}.
Phase 2 - Blocking and indexing (one or more passes).
Phase 3 - Exact matching (deterministic rules).
Phase 4 - Fuzzy matching (metrics, weight table, two thresholds).
Phase 5 - Clustering by transitive closure and over-merging control.
Phase 6 - Survival, merge, and golden record lineage.
Phase 7 - Validation: metrics on labeled sample, gray zone sampling plan, and incremental reprocessing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every attribute in {{ATRIBUTOS_MATCH}} has an explicit normalization rule, evaluated discriminating power, and defined treatment of garbage/null values.
- [ ] Blocking names concrete keys, uses multiple passes when appropriate, and justifies the exhaustiveness/cost trade-off with a reduction factor.
- [ ] Exact and fuzzy matching rules separated; named metric per attribute (Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, token-based).
- [ ] Weight table and two thresholds (auto-match and gray zone) consistent with {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}} and, if applicable, the relative cost of each error type.
- [ ] Clustering uses transitive closure and declares a concrete safeguard against over-merging.
- [ ] Survival rules per attribute traceable to {{FUENTES_Y_CONFIABILIDAD}}; the golden record preserves source IDs and records which rule decided each value.
- [ ] Validation plan with precision, recall, F1, false positive/negative counts, manual gray zone sampling, and incremental reprocessing.
- [ ] Edge cases treated (branches of the same client, homonyms, corporate mergers, name/address changes).
- [ ] No invented thresholds: values without evidence marked [SUPUESTO] and conditioned on the sample.
Expected deliverable: pipeline design document + weight/threshold table + pseudocode or SQL/Python for the key stages (normalization, blocking, scoring, merge) + per-attribute survival rules + validation plan with metrics + edge cases list and assumed trade-offs.
spec-datos_calidad_scorecard_kpis:

--- S | SITUATION ---
The organization needs to measure and govern the data quality of the {{DOMINIO}} domain in an objective, reproducible, and auditable way. Today decisions are made on datasets whose reliability is not quantified, which generates rework, inconsistent reports, and eroded trust in information. A scorecard with KPIs by dimension, clear thresholds, a weighted index, and a monitoring dashboard unlocks early detection of degradation, assigns explicit accountability by domain, and turns data quality into a manageable indicator rather than a perception.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality architect and information governance specialist, with hands-on experience in DAMA-DMBOK and in operating data quality programs on production datasets.
Deliverable: data quality scorecard for {{DATASETS_CRITICOS}} in the {{DOMINIO}} domain, with KPI definitions, acceptance thresholds, weighted index, and dashboard schema, ready to implement. Steps:
1. Confirm datasets, business keys, source of truth per dataset, and freshness SLAs {{SLA_FRESCURA}}.
2. Per dataset, derive KPIs across the six DAMA dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness.

- Thresholds use three coherent traffic-light bands, and every threshold without a user-defined target is marked [SUPUESTO] with its recalibration criterion.
