spec-liderazgo_conflicto_conversacion_no:
[inputs]
- RECLAMO_ORIGINAL: {{RECLAMO_ORIGINAL}} > The complaint or grievance as you would say it today, in your own words and with your emotional charge
- RELACION_OTRA_PERSONA: {{RELACION_OTRA_PERSONA}} > Who they are and what role they have relative to you (direct report, peer, manager, internal client)
- RESULTADO_BUSCADO: {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} > What you want to change or agree on by the end of the conversation
- TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL: {{TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL}} > How tense the bond is today (cold, tense, open, in declared conflict)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where you will deliver the message: face to face, call, or written text (optional)
- HISTORIAL_PREVIO: {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}} > Whether you have discussed the topic before and how it ended, or "First time" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A complaint said as a judgment ("you're always late", "you don't care about the team") triggers the other person's defenses and kills the conversation before it starts. Marshall Rosenberg's nonviolent communication unlocks dialogue by separating fact from interpretation and need from demand, so the other person can listen without feeling attacked. Reframing the complaint before speaking turns a collision into a negotiation of needs and protects the long-term bond. The power asymmetry (manager, direct report, client) and the temperature of the bond change how direct the request can be without reading as a threat.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior nonviolent communication facilitator trained in Marshall Rosenberg's model, with experience mediating conflicts in work teams.
Deliverable: a CNV reframing kit for the complaint, ready to take into the conversation. Steps:
1. Diagnose the original complaint: mark the judgments, labels, generalizations ("always", "never", "again"), and concealed demands it carries. Name the conversational cost of each (what probable defensive reaction it triggers).
2. Translate into the four components: Observation (verifiable, datable fact without evaluation), Feeling (real emotion, not a pseudo-feeling that hides judgment), Need (universal human need, not a strategy or solution, without naming the other person), Request (concrete, present tense, positive, achievable, answerable with yes or no; different from a demand because it admits no without penalty).
3. Draft a 3-to-5-sentence opening script in first person, adapted to the indicated channel, that the person can say or send as is. If the channel is written text, close with an open question that invites a response.
4. Offer two reformulations of the script calibrated to emotional temperature: one warmer (cold bond or declared conflict) and one more direct (open bond), without reverting to the original complaint.
5. Anticipate three probable defensive responses from the other person (counterattack, denial of the fact, justification) and how to sustain the conversation with empathic listening without abandoning the need or falling back into judgment.
6. Close with the observable success signal of the conversation (what concrete agreement marks it as achieved) and an actionable plan B if no agreement is reached in the first round (e.g., ask for time, escalate with a neutral third party, agree to revisit on a date).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: read the complaint and the inputs; identify the fact buried under the judgment and the need buried under the reproach. Consider HISTORIAL_PREVIO to avoid repeating a frame that already failed.
Phase 2 Plan: present in one line the candidate observation, feeling, need, and request, and confirm assumptions marked with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 Execute: produce the full kit (diagnosis with cost, four components, script, two reformulations, three defensive responses, success signal + plan B) with no filler.
Do not invent facts not in the complaint; if you need a missing piece of data for the observation (what happened, when, with whom), ask for it or mark it [SUPUESTO]. Adjust the directness of the request to the power asymmetry with the other person.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The observation contains no evaluation, label, or the word "always"/"never"; it is datable or located in a concrete event.
- The feeling is a genuine emotion, not a pseudo-feeling ("ignored", "manipulated", "pressured", "not valued" are prohibited because they hide a judgment about the other person).
- The need is universal, does not name the other person or a concrete solution, and is not a disguised strategy.
- The request is actionable, present tense, positive, answerable with a clear yes or no, and admits no without becoming a demand.
- The script is in first person, without accusatory "you", fits the indicated channel, and respects the power asymmetry.
- The two reformulations change tone by temperature without reverting to the original complaint.
- Each defensive response comes with a reply that validates the other person (empathic listening) and reaffirms the need without conceding to judgment.
- The success signal is observable and the plan B is actionable without escalating the conflict.
Expected deliverable: CNV reframing kit with diagnosis (with conversational cost), the four components, opening script, two temperature variants, three objection-handling responses, and success signal + plan B, ready to take into the conversation.
spec-liderazgo_conflicto_acuerdos_trabaj:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team name, function and size, modality (on-site, remote, hybrid), and seniority or stage (newly formed, mature, reorganized, post-conflict)
- FRICCION_RECURRENTE: {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}} > Recurring irritants and conflicts, with concrete examples and frequency if known (e.g., "meetings that start 10 min late, 3 out of 5", "decisions reopened during the week", "PRs unreviewed for more than 2 days", "chat interruptions during focus blocks")
- CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO: {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} > How the team works today: ceremonies and their cadence, time zones and overlap window, tools (chat, board, repos), active SLAs and cross-role handoffs that constrain the agreements
- NUMERO_ACUERDOS: {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} > Target number of agreements, between 5 and 8; use 6 if not specified (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Company policies, non-negotiable norms, contractual SLAs, or topics outside the team's scope that the agreements cannot contradict or replace (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team has accumulated recurring friction (unproductive meetings, decisions that get reopened, failing handoffs, focus interruptions, feedback that never arrives) and that friction is escalating to interpersonal conflict and burnout. I need to convert those irritants into co-created working agreements: observable behavioral norms that the team gives itself to reduce friction before it becomes conflict. A good set of agreements unlocks shorter meetings, decisions that hold, fewer escalations to the leader, and a shared language for calling out friction in the moment without it feeling like a personal attack. I distinguish two planes that the output must not mix: the team agreement (what the team chooses and can change) and the company policy (what is given and non-negotiable).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team facilitator and agile team coach, expert in team chartering (Diana Larsen, Lyssa Adkins), in Liberating Structures for co-creation (1-2-4-All, 15% Solutions, TRIZ), and in converting recurring irritants into actionable agreements.

Produce three deliverables:
1. Friction diagnosis: group the irritants from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}} into categories (communication, meetings, decision-making, quality and handoffs, availability and focus, feedback and conflict), name the probable cause of each without blaming individuals (point to the system, not the person), and prioritize those generating the most conflict using an explicit impact x frequency criterion.
2. Working agreements table ({{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} agreements), with columns: agreement (first-person plural and observable behavior, verifiable by a third party), irritant it resolves, signal of non-compliance, who calls it out in the moment (rotating role or anyone on the team, never the leader alone), and team-agreed consequence (restorative, not punitive). Close with a meta-agreement on how the team signals friction without it feeling personal.
3. Facilitation guide for the ratification session (60 to 90 minutes) and a retrospective review block.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: classify the irritants, infer their probable root cause, and prioritize by conflict impact x frequency; mark as [SUPUESTO] anything without evidence and ask a concrete question that would confirm or rule it out.
Phase 2 - Co-creation: convert each priority irritant into an observable agreement ("We respond to direct mentions within 4 business hours"), not a vague intention ("communicate better"); each agreement must pass the third-party test (an external observer would know without ambiguity whether it was met); respect {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} (do not propose an SLA impossible for the time-zone overlap) and do not contradict {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
Phase 3 - Operationalization: for each agreement define the signal of non-compliance, who calls it out, and the team-agreed consequence (restorative, not a sanction); avoid consequences that punish the individual or that the leader must enforce.
Phase 4 - Sustainability: define where the agreements are made visible (pinned channel, board, team README), how they are ratified and edited in the session (consent, not forced unanimity), and the criterion for keeping, adjusting, or retiring each agreement in the retrospective (e.g., retire if it stopped being an irritant for 3 cycles).
Edge cases: if friction has already escalated to active interpersonal conflict, note that agreements prevent but do not resolve live conflict and recommend addressing it separately; if the number of irritants exceeds {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}}, prioritize and leave the rest in a backlog for the next review; if a proposed irritant clashes with {{RESTRICCIONES}}, flag the conflict and reframe the agreement within what is permitted.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each agreement is in first-person plural and describes observable behavior verifiable by a third party (passes the third-party test), not a good intention.
- [ ] Each agreement traces back to a real irritant from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}; nothing invented, gaps go as [SUPUESTO] with the question that would close them.
- [ ] The set respects {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} (5 to 8), does not contradict {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and does not mix team agreement with company policy.
- [ ] Each agreement has a signal of non-compliance, who calls it out (not just the leader), and a restorative non-punitive consequence agreed by the team.
- [ ] The format allows the team to ratify or edit each agreement; none is presented as a rule imposed by the leader; the diagnosis points to the system, does not blame individuals.
- [ ] The set prioritizes by an explicit impact x frequency criterion and includes a meta-agreement on how to signal friction without it feeling personal.
- [ ] The guide includes a timed agenda, ratification and live-editing mechanics, and a retrospective review block with criteria for keeping, adjusting, or retiring.
Expected deliverable: categorized and prioritized friction diagnosis, working agreements table ready to ratify, and a facilitation guide for the session with its review block, in neutral, professional English, without emojis.
spec-liderazgo_conflicto_silos_entre_are:
[inputs]
- AREA_A: {{AREA_A}} > First area in conflict (name, function, who leads it)
- AREA_B: {{AREA_B}} > Second area in conflict (name, function, who leads it)
- SINTOMAS_CONFLICTO: {{SINTOMAS_CONFLICTO}} > How it manifests today: rework, blockages, escalations, cross-blame, missed deadlines
- DETONANTES: {{DETONANTES}} > Specific situations or handoffs that trigger the clashes
- OBJETIVOS_POR_AREA: {{OBJETIVOS_POR_AREA}} > What goals/indicators each area pursues separately today (and whether they clash)
- INTENTOS_FALLIDOS: {{INTENTOS_FALLIDOS}} > Previous solutions that were tried and did not work, and why (optional)
- HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCIONES: {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCIONES}} > Intervention timeline, available authority to decide, resource or policy limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Two areas that depend on each other are in chronic friction and that is stalling shared work: slow handoffs, rework, escalations, and relationship burnout. The goal is to design an executable alignment intervention that converts the clash into collaboration with clear interfaces. What gets unlocked: a verifiable shared objective of mutual gain, cross-area working rules that reduce predictable friction, and a follow-up that detects relapses before they escalate again. Friction between areas is almost never about bad intent from individuals: it is usually a poorly designed system (opposing incentives, blurry boundaries, scarce resources) that puts reasonable people in collision. Available inputs: {{AREA_A}}, {{AREA_B}}, {{SINTOMAS_CONFLICTO}}, {{DETONANTES}}, {{OBJETIVOS_POR_AREA}}, {{INTENTOS_FALLIDOS}}, {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior organizational alignment facilitator, specialist in productive conflict between teams (Lencioni's trust and healthy conflict framework) and in interface and team interaction design (Team Topologies).
Deliverable: an alignment intervention between {{AREA_A}} and {{AREA_B}}, structured as follows:
1. Root cause diagnosis: distinguish task conflict (what/how to do the work) from relationship conflict (people/trust) and name the structural incentive sustaining the friction (opposing objectives, boundary ambiguity, scarce resources, information or power asymmetry). Estimate the approximate cost of not acting (time lost, rework, deadline risk) without inventing figures: if there is no data, express it as a range or as [SUPUESTO].
2. Shared objective: state a single measurable goal, with a time horizon and unit of measurement, that can only be achieved if both areas win together (not the sum of their separate goals); list 2-3 success indicators and, when possible, a shared indicator neither area controls alone.
3. Interface map: for each critical handoff define expected input, committed output, single owner, agreed response time, and acceptance criteria; label the interaction type (temporary collaboration, stable service, or facilitation) and note which handoffs should be simplified or eliminated.
4. Working agreement: interaction rules, level-by-level escalation path with a deadline at each level, and a decision mechanism when there is disagreement (who decides, with what criterion, and in how much time). Include what happens when one party breaches the agreement.
5. Alignment session: 90-minute agenda with a concrete objective and the facilitator's role per block; include how to open the agreements without reopening the blame fight and how emotional overflows are handled.
6. 30/60/90-day follow-up plan: metrics, review cadence, single follow-up owner, and at least one early relapse signal per milestone with its predefined response.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the conflict in a neutral phrase (without assigning blame) and validate the inputs; if a critical piece of data is missing (symptoms, triggers, area objectives, or authority to decide), ask before moving forward. Mark every inference as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Diagnose: separate task conflict vs. relationship conflict and locate the structural incentive; prioritize root cause over symptoms. Review {{INTENTOS_FALLIDOS}} to avoid repeating what has already failed and name why it failed.
Phase 3 - Design: draft the shared objective, then the interface map and the working agreement; ensure each rule attacks a real trigger from {{DETONANTES}} and respects the real authority of {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}.
Phase 4 - Operationalize: build the 90-minute agenda and the 30/60/90 plan with metrics, owner, and relapse signals.
Phase 5 - Verify against the CRITERIA before delivering and declare the risks of the intervention itself.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The diagnosis explicitly distinguishes task conflict from relationship conflict and names a concrete structural incentive, with cost of not acting (real figure, range, or [SUPUESTO]).
- The shared objective is unique, measurable, with a time horizon and unit of measurement, and is only achievable with mutual gain (not the sum of separate goals).
- Each handoff in the map has all 5 fields: input, output, single owner, response time, and acceptance criteria, plus the interaction type.
- The working agreement includes an escalation path with deadlines, a decision mechanism for disagreements, and a response for non-compliance.
- The 90-minute agenda has time totals per block and each block has an objective and a facilitator role.
- The 30/60/90 plan includes metrics, a single follow-up owner, and at least one early relapse signal per milestone with its response.
- Each rule in the agreement can be traced back to a real trigger from {{DETONANTES}} or a symptom from {{SINTOMAS_CONFLICTO}}.
- The authority and limits of {{HORIZONTE_Y_RESTRICCIONES}} are respected: nothing in the plan requires decision-making power that does not exist.
- No inference is presented as fact: every assumption is marked [SUPUESTO].
- Neutral language, without assigning blame to any individual or area; the risks of the intervention itself are declared.
Expected deliverable: alignment intervention document between {{AREA_A}} and {{AREA_B}}, with the 6 sections ready to present to both leaders and execute, plus a risks note for the intervention.
spec-liderazgo_conflicto_personalidad_di:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR_ROL: {{COLABORADOR_ROL}} > Role or relationship of the collaborator to the person you lead (e.g., direct report, peer, team specialist); determines how much formal authority you have over the agreements
- COMPORTAMIENTOS_OBSERVADOS: {{COMPORTAMIENTOS_OBSERVADOS}} > Concrete, observable actions that generate friction (what was said or done, in what situation), not personality labels
- IMPACTO_CONCRETO: {{IMPACTO_CONCRETO}} > Measurable effect on the work, deadlines, other people, or team climate
- FRECUENCIA_Y_DURACION: {{FRECUENCIA_Y_DURACION}} > How often it occurs and since when
- INTENTOS_PREVIOS: {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}} > What you have tried before and with what result (optional)
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} > The specific behavioral change you are seeking after the conversation
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You lead a team and a collaborator's conduct is generating friction: tensions in meetings, colleagues who avoid them, or work that falls behind. Most leaders react by labeling the person ("they are difficult", "they are toxic"), which escalates the conflict, invites litigation, and changes nothing. This prompt converts a vague complaint into a factual, actionable case: verifiable facts, a well-designed 1:1 conversation, and measurable agreements. It unlocks correcting the behavior while protecting the relationship, the person's dignity, and team cohesion. Limit: this dossier prepares a feedback and behavioral improvement conversation between the leader and the collaborator; it does not replace a formal disciplinary process, a harassment investigation, or legal-employment counsel. If {{COMPORTAMIENTOS_OBSERVADOS}} includes discrimination, harassment, threats, or illegal conduct, mark it as outside the scope of the 1:1 and refer to Human Resources or the formal channel.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior leadership coach specializing in difficult conversations and team dynamics, with command of the SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) model from the Center for Creative Leadership and the principles of Crucial Conversations.

Deliverable: a handling dossier for collaborator {{COLABORADOR_ROL}}. Steps:
1. Separate facts from interpretations: take {{COMPORTAMIENTOS_OBSERVADOS}} and classify each claim as documented observable behavior or as my inference; mark inferences with [SUPUESTO]. If a claim mixes fact and interpretation, separate them into two lines.
2. Restate each behavior as concrete behavior + context + impact, using {{IMPACTO_CONCRETO}} and {{FRECUENCIA_Y_DURACION}}. No adjective about the person is allowed; describe what is seen, not who the person is. Where possible, anchor each behavior to a specific date or situation so it is defensible.
3. Draft the script for a private 1:1 conversation using the SBI model: an opening that lowers defensiveness and declares the intent (to improve, not to sanction), a factual presentation of the behavior and its impact, open questions to understand the collaborator's perspective and possible non-visible causes, and a close oriented toward agreements, aligned with {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}. Include 2 backup transitions in case the person shuts down or overflows emotionally.
4. Propose 2 or 3 verifiable behavioral agreements: each with an observable success signal, a review date, and who verifies. Distinguish what is negotiable from what is non-negotiable.
5. Anticipate 3 likely reactions (denial, justification, emotional counterattack) and deliver a calm response for each that keeps the focus on the behavior and not on the person, without conceding the fact or escalating the tone.
6. Close with a follow-up and escalation note: what to document after the conversation, how to give recognition if there is improvement, and under what objective condition (agreements not met by the review date) to escalate to Human Resources or a formal body.

Consider these factors: formal power varies depending on {{COLABORADOR_ROL}} (with a peer, agreements are mutual commitments, not instructions); if {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}} shows recurrence, increase formality and maintain a written record; use data from {{ADJUNTOS}} only if it provides verifiable evidence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: if {{COMPORTAMIENTOS_OBSERVADOS}}, {{IMPACTO_CONCRETO}}, {{FRECUENCIA_Y_DURACION}}, or {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} are empty or insufficient for a concrete script, ask for them before drafting. Do not invent facts about the case or the collaborator's motivations.
Phase 2 Plan: clean up facts vs. interpretations and map each behavior to its impact; present this map and the script structure for validation.
Phase 3 Execute: produce the full dossier (separation of facts, SBI restatement, 1:1 script, verifiable agreements, reaction handling, follow-up and escalation note).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each claim in the case is classified as observable fact or as inference ([SUPUESTO]); mixed claims were separated.
- [ ] No phrase labels the collaborator's personality; every description is behavior + context + impact, anchored to a situation or date when possible.
- [ ] The script follows the SBI sequence and includes an opening with a declaration of intent, open questions, a close with agreements, and 2 backup transitions.
- [ ] There are 2 or 3 agreements, each with an observable success signal, a review date, and who verifies; negotiable is distinguished from non-negotiable.
- [ ] The 3 anticipated reactions have a calm response focused on the behavior, without conceding the fact.
- [ ] The follow-up note defines what to document and the objective condition for escalation to Human Resources.
- [ ] Behaviors that may constitute harassment/discrimination/illegal conduct were marked out of scope and referred.
- [ ] No fact in the case was invented; gaps were asked about, not filled in.
Expected deliverable: a dossier in sections (1. Facts vs. interpretations, 2. Factual restatement, 3. 1:1 SBI script, 4. Verifiable agreements, 5. Reaction handling, 6. Follow-up and escalation) ready to bring to the conversation.
spec-liderazgo_conflicto_post_incidente_:
[inputs]
- INCIDENTE: {{INCIDENTE}} > What happened, in one or two sentences: the shared error, when it occurred, and how it was detected
- PERSONAS_INVOLUCRADAS: {{PERSONAS_INVOLUCRADAS}} > Who was involved and their role; use initials or aliases if sensitive
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO}} > Consequence and severity: who was affected, magnitude, whether it is still active
- ESTADO_CONFIANZA: {{ESTADO_CONFIANZA}} > Team climate: tension, accusations, silence, fear of speaking up, someone who self-blames
- DURACION_REUNION: {{DURACION_REUNION}} > Time available for the conversation (e.g., 45 min, 90 min)
- RESULTADO_BUSCADO: {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} > What must be resolved by the end (optional; if empty, assume learning + countermeasures + restored trust)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have just experienced an incident involving a shared error among several team members, and the conversation to review it may degenerate into a blame search. I need to conduct a blameless analysis that separates the system from the person, lowers the tension, extracts the real learning, and leaves verifiable countermeasures. What gets unlocked: a retrospective that instead of eroding trust rebuilds it, converts the error into process improvement, and reduces the probability of recurrence without anyone being marked.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior facilitator of engineering culture and psychological safety, with experience conducting SRE-style blameless post-mortems and applying Just Culture (distinction between human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior) and the principle of local rationality (people acted reasonably with the information available at the time).

Deliverable: a complete blameless conversation script ready to run. Steps:
1. If critical context is missing (INCIDENTE, IMPACTO, ESTADO_CONFIANZA, or DURACION_REUNION empty or ambiguous), ask for it in a single round of questions before moving forward.
2. Draft a 60-to-90-second opening frame that sets the blameless premise: reasonable decisions made with available information are analyzed, not the people; the goal is to learn, not to judge.
3. Build a neutral timeline that separates into two columns what is observable (what happened, with time if applicable) from what is interpreted (what we assumed it meant at the time).
4. Generate a battery of questions that redirect from "who failed" to "what in the system allowed it": contributing factors, signals that were missed, assumptions that were not met, defenses that were absent, time pressure, or context.
5. Write a script for the 2 or 3 most likely tense moments (a direct accusation, a defensive person, an uncomfortable silence, or a second person who self-blames) with verbatim phrases to redirect without shaming anyone.
6. Propose a set of actionable countermeasures with an owner, date, and verification signal, separating system fixes from behavioral changes, and discarding effort-only countermeasures ("be more careful") as non-verifiable.
7. Close with a script that rebuilds trust and leaves an explicit group commitment, plus a follow-up plan (who verifies countermeasures and when).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the incident, the people, the impact, and the trust state as you understand them; mark any assumption with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Plan: present the conversation structure mapped to the available time (DURACION_REUNION) in blocks with assigned minutes; if RESULTADO_BUSCADO is empty, assume learning + countermeasures + restored trust and declare it.
Phase 3 - Execute: produce the 7 deliverable pieces in order, in neutral, professional English, with verbatim phrases usable as-is.
Tone rules: never attribute intent or bad faith; every causal claim is expressed as a system hypothesis, not a judgment. Distinguish error (system), at-risk behavior (coaching), and reckless behavior (exceptional, outside the blameless framework) without accusing. Avoid the "five whys" reflex that lands on a person: each "why" must point to a system condition.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The opening frame explicitly establishes the blameless premise and can be read in 60 to 90 seconds.
- [ ] The timeline separates observable facts from interpretations in distinct columns.
- [ ] No question starts with "who"; all point to the system, the signals, the assumptions, or the defenses.
- [ ] The tense-moments script includes verbatim phrases that redirect without shaming anyone, and includes the case of the second person who self-blames.
- [ ] Each countermeasure has an owner, a date, and a verification signal, is classified as a system fix or behavioral change, and none is an unverifiable effort-only measure.
- [ ] The close includes an explicit commitment, a trust-rebuilding gesture, and a follow-up plan (who verifies and when).
- [ ] Zero attribution of intent or bad faith; at-risk and reckless behavior distinguished without accusing; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] The agenda fits within DURACION_REUNION with minutes per block.
Expected deliverable: complete 7-piece blameless script, in professional English, ready to run the meeting without additional editing.
spec-liderazgo_conflicto_disenso_product:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The specific high-impact decision the team must make
- CLIMA_ACTUAL: {{CLIMA_ACTUAL}} > Level of trust and how the team disagrees today: silence, false harmony, personal clashes, perceived retaliation
- TAMANO_EQUIPO: {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} > Number of participants and roles or hierarchy present (who decides, who influences, who executes)
- PLAZO: {{PLAZO}} > When the decision must be made (one meeting, several days, one week)
- OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS: {{OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS}} > Disagreements or reservations already expressed or latent (optional; if empty, infer and mark as [SUPUESTO])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team must make decision {{DECISION}} and disagreement can either improve it or destroy the relationship. Most teams fall into one of two failures: groupthink (Janis), where apparent harmony suppresses valid objections and no one wants to be the killjoy, or personalized conflict, where disagreeing is experienced as an attack and people stay silent for fear of retaliation (psychological safety deficit, Edmondson). Both produce the same damage: blind spots that only reveal themselves when it is already too late and costly. Designing dissent in advance converts disagreement into an asset: better decisions, fewer blind spots, intact relationships. Dissent is not spontaneous in most teams; it is a structure that is installed. What gets unlocked is a more robust decision and a team that learns to disagree without breaking apart.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team decision facilitator, expert in productive dissent, psychological safety (Amy Edmondson), groupthink (Irving Janis), and red team / devil's advocate practices from strategic intelligence.
Deliverable: a tailored productive dissent mechanism, ready to use from the next meeting. Produce:
1. Framing: restate the decision at stake, the participants and their hierarchy, and what is actually in dispute vs. what is emotional or process noise.
2. Dominant risk diagnosis based on {{CLIMA_ACTUAL}}: groupthink and false harmony, or already personalized conflict. Support with at least two observable signals from the climate; if both risks coexist, name which one the mechanism attacks first.
3. Selection and justification of ONE mechanism from: rotating devil's advocate, formal red team, mandatory dissent before approval, prior silent writing, or pre-mortem, considering {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} and {{PLAZO}}; explain why that one and why you discard at least two alternatives (size, hierarchy, and available time criterion). Heuristic: silent writing and pre-mortem work best when there is strong hierarchy or silence; rotating devil's advocate and red team when there is time and a critical mass of participants; mandatory dissent when the deadline is short and at least one objection must be guaranteed.
4. Step-by-step operational script: who does what, in what order, with suggested times per block, conversation rules, how to separate the idea from the person (attack the argument, not who holds it), and how to close with a clear decision made and an owner assigned.
5. Library of verbatim phrases for three moments (opening the dissent, disagreeing without attacking, closing without anyone losing face) and at least three traps to avoid (theatrical dissent, silent retaliation, endless debate), each trap with its concrete countermeasure.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: separate the real decision from the noise; name the participants and their hierarchy. If {{DECISION}}, {{CLIMA_ACTUAL}}, {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}}, or {{PLAZO}} is missing, ask for it before moving forward.
Phase 2 Diagnosis: classify the dominant risk with observable signals; integrate {{OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS}} if present or, if empty, infer the most likely ones and mark them as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 Design: choose the mechanism based on risk, size, hierarchy, and timeline; justify the choice and the discarding of at least two alternatives.
Phase 4 Operation: draft the actionable script with times and the phrase library with its traps and countermeasures.
Close: list the assumptions that conditioned the design and an observable success signal for the first meeting (e.g., at least one substantive objection expressed aloud without personal friction).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The chosen mechanism corresponds to the diagnosed risk (anti-groupthink vs. depersonalizing conflict), is not generic, and the discarding of at least two alternatives is justified.
- The script says who, what, in what order, with suggested times and explicit rules for separating idea from person.
- There is a closing mechanism with a decision made and an owner assigned (avoids endless debate).
- The phrase library includes verbatim phrases for the three situations and names at least three traps, each with a countermeasure.
- The assumptions that condition the design are made explicit and there is an observable success signal.
- Neutral, professional English, without prices, actionable from the next meeting.
Expected deliverable: document structured in the 5 sections of the request, with assumptions and success signal at the close, ready to execute in the team's next meeting.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_definir_valores:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_EQUIPO: {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} > Name and brief purpose of the team whose culture is being codified
- VALORES_BORRADOR: {{VALORES_BORRADOR}} > Current values or draft to translate (list of 3 to 6 values; if none exist, the expert proposes them from context and marks them [SUPUESTO])
- TENSIONES_REALES: {{TENSIONES_REALES}} > Recent conflicts or decisions where culture was put to the test (feed trade-offs and uncomfortable pairs)
- ADMIRADO_Y_RECHAZADO: {{ADMIRADO_Y_RECHAZADO}} > Specific behaviors that are admired and rejected within the team
- TAMANO_Y_MADUREZ: {{TAMANO_Y_MADUREZ}} > Team size and stage (startup, scaling, mature) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Values written as abstract adjectives (excellence, respect, innovation) do not change behaviors: each person interprets them differently and nobody knows what to do differently on Monday. Codifying values as observable do and don't behaviors, in the style of the Netflix culture deck, unlocks consistent decisions without supervision, faster onboarding, objective feedback based on behavior rather than personality, and a culture that can be evaluated and defended in moments of tension. The opposite risk is an aspirational manifesto that nobody uses: that is why each value must be anchored in real tensions and lived trade-offs, not in intentions. The deliverable is the behavioral contract that converts poster culture into operations.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader and organizational culture designer, expert in behavioral values and the Netflix culture deck approach.
Produce a behavioral and verifiable values manifesto. Steps:
1. Distill each value into a single-sentence definition that answers "what does this mean in real work," eliminating every adjective that has no behavior behind it.
2. For each value, write 3 to 5 pairs "Looks like (do) / Does not look like (don't)" as actions observable by a third party, not intentions or feelings; include at least one pair that stings (a valued behavior that most teams avoid in practice).
3. For each value, define an anchor question for difficult decisions and a real trade-off example where that value wins over another value in the same manifesto, naming the value that yields.
4. For each value, define 1 to 2 observable behavioral signals that reveal whether the value is alive or dead, plus a team retrospective question.
5. Close with an executive summary: each value in one line and the 3 cultural tensions the manifesto resolves.
Edge cases: if more than 6 values are declared, cut to the 5–6 most distinctive and explain the cut; if two values overlap, merge them or define their boundary; if no real tensions are provided, mark the manifesto as hypothetical and warn that without lived conflicts the pairs cannot be validated.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Distillation: convert adjectives into verifiable operational meaning.
Phase 2 Behaviors: derive the observable do/don't pairs, forcing at least one uncomfortable pair per value.
Phase 3 Anchors: formulate the anchor question and the explicit trade-off between values, naming which one yields.
Phase 4 Verification: define alive/dead signals and retrospective question; assemble the per-value table and the executive summary; review the checklist before delivering.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If NOMBRE_EQUIPO, VALORES_BORRADOR, TENSIONES_REALES, or ADMIRADO_Y_RECHAZADO are missing, ask for them in a single block and do not invent them.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each value has a single-sentence definition without hollow adjectives.
- [ ] Each value has 3 to 5 do/don't pairs observable by a third party (not intentions or feelings).
- [ ] Each value includes at least one uncomfortable pair that most teams avoid.
- [ ] Each value has an anchor question and a real trade-off where it wins over another value, naming the one that yields.
- [ ] Each value has 1 to 2 alive/dead signals and a retrospective question.
- [ ] Values between 3 and 6; overlaps resolved; manifesto marked hypothetical if real tensions are missing.
- [ ] Inferred data marked [SUPUESTO]; missing items asked before executing.
- [ ] Neutral and professional English, without emojis, without motivational-poster language.
Expected deliverable: values manifesto with one table per value (definition, do/don't pairs, anchor question and trade-off, alive/dead signals and retro question) plus an executive summary, ready to present to the team and use in onboarding and feedback. Close with three calibration questions for refining the manifesto with the team.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_seguridad_psicolo:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team size, roles, and tenure (e.g., 9 people, engineering, mix of senior and junior)
- MODALIDAD: {{MODALIDAD}} > In-person, remote, or hybrid, and meeting rhythm
- SINTOMAS: {{SINTOMAS}} > Warning signs that concern you (silence in meetings, hidden errors, turnover, avoided conflict)
- HISTORIA_RECIENTE: {{HISTORIA_RECIENTE}} > Recent reorganizations, layoffs, conflicts, or leadership changes, or "No recent events"
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > What you want to unlock (more useful dissent, early problem reporting, more initiative)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Climate survey results, 1:1 notes, meeting minutes, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You lead a team and suspect people are not speaking candidly: they stay silent in meetings, hide errors until they blow up, don't ask for help, or don't contradict the leader. That is costly: problems are detected late, the best ideas never surface, and learning is slowed. Psychological safety — the shared belief that the team is a safe space for taking interpersonal risks — is, according to Amy Edmondson's research, one of the most robust predictors of team learning and performance. It is not the same as comfort: high performance lives in the learning zone, where high safety combines with high standards. Diagnosing it and raising it deliberately unlocks early problem reporting, useful dissent, and more initiative, without sacrificing the standard.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational psychologist specializing in psychological safety and high-performance team culture, with direct mastery of Amy Edmondson's framework and scale and of the safety × challenge matrix (comfort, apathy, anxiety, and learning zones).

Deliverable: a psychological safety diagnosis of the team and an actionable elevation plan. Produce, in this order:
1. Mini-diagnostic: 7 Edmondson-style scale items (including the reversed items about fear of punishment for errors and difficulty asking for help) for self-assessment on a 1 to 7 scale. Explain how to administer it anonymously, how to reverse the score on negative items, how to read the mean and dispersion (a healthy mean that hides polarized subgroups is a false alarm), and interpretive benchmarks.
2. Signal reading: 6 to 8 observable behavioral signals that betray low psychological safety, each contrasted with its healthy counterpart.
3. Elevation plan: 5 to 8 leadership actions prioritized by impact and effort. For each one: concrete leader behavior, frequency or timing of use, signal that it is working, and the Edmondson lever it activates (framing work as a learning problem, modeling one's own fallibility and curiosity, actively inviting participation). All three levers must be covered.
4. Three literal and brief opening phrases for the next meeting that genuinely invite dissent and early problem reporting.
5. Two common mistakes that confuse psychological safety with lowering standards, and how to avoid them.
6. 30-day plan: three milestones and a re-measurement metric to verify the change without self-deception.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: restate the received context and declare pending assumptions. If critical diagnostic information is missing (team composition, modality and rhythm, specific symptoms, recent history, leader behavior when someone disagrees or reports an error), ask for it in a brief list before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: build the mini-questionnaire and interpretation guide; cross-reference symptoms and attachments with the behavioral signals for an initial hypothesis of the current level and its position on the safety × challenge matrix.
Phase 3 - Design: prioritize actions by impact and effort, anchored in the three levers; draft the opening phrases, the two mistakes to avoid, and the 30-day plan.
Phase 4 - Verification: confirm that each action is observable and measurable, that the diagnosis explicitly distinguishes psychological safety from comfort and complacency, that the re-measurement does not incentivize complacent responses, and that no team data was invented (assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO]).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The mini-diagnostic has 7 items faithful to the Edmondson framework, includes reversed items, and explains anonymous administration, score reversal, reading of mean + dispersion, and interpretive benchmarks.
- [ ] The behavioral signals are observable, not judgments; each one is contrasted with its healthy counterpart.
- [ ] Each action in the plan includes concrete behavior + frequency + success signal, and maps to one of the three levers; all three levers are covered.
- [ ] The three opening phrases are literal, brief, and sound credible when spoken aloud.
- [ ] The deliverable explicitly distinguishes psychological safety from comfort or from lowering standards (safety × challenge matrix named).
- [ ] The 30-day plan has three milestones and a re-measurement metric not susceptible to complacent responses.
- [ ] Every data point not provided is marked [SUPUESTO]; zero inventions about the team.
- [ ] Neutral and professional English, without emojis.
Expected deliverable: structured document in 6 blocks (mini-diagnostic, signals, prioritized plan, opening phrases, mistakes to avoid, 30-day plan) ready for the leader to apply in their next cycle of meetings and 1:1s.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_team_charter:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_EQUIPO: {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} > Team name and main function
- TAMANO_EQUIPO: {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} > Number of members and roles represented
- MISION_PROVISIONAL: {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} > Draft of why the team exists (optional; if missing, it is co-created)
- CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL: {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}} > Area, neighboring teams, stage, and relevant constraints
- DECISIONES_TIPICAS: {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} > Recurring decisions or those that currently generate friction
- NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS: {{NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS}} > Working frictions to resolve: meetings, response times, disagreements (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team without an explicit agreement on its mission, scope, roles, and decision-making process pays the cost in diffuse meetings, decisions that are redone, and conflicts that escalate late. Building the team charter of {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} converts implicit assumptions into a visible contract: it unlocks faster decisions, clear boundaries with neighboring teams, and immediate onboarding of new members. This is not a filing document: it is the team's operational strategy, living and revisable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior high-performance team facilitator, with mastery of the Drexler-Sibbet Team Performance Model, RACI/DACI matrices, and working agreement design.

Deliverable: a team charter for {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} ready to review and sign with the team in one session, in seven blocks:
1. Mission and purpose: why it exists, whom it serves, what change it produces; start from {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} if it exists, removing hollow jargon.
2. Scope: what is inside and what is OUTSIDE the scope; explicit boundaries (inputs and deliverables) with neighboring teams according to {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}.
3. Objectives and metrics: 3 to 5 outcomes, each with an observable success signal and, where it exists, a baseline; no objectives without a metric.
4. Roles and responsibilities: RACI matrix by work type, covering the {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} members; a single Approver per decision, no orphan roles.
5. Decision model: for each item in {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}}, define what the team decides, who decides, with what mechanism (consensus, consultative, or delegated), and how, to whom, and within what timeframe it escalates.
6. Norms and working agreements: meetings, channels, response times, handling of disagreements, and definition of done; resolve {{NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS}} first; each norm verifiable, not abstract.
7. Review cadence: how often the charter is reviewed, who is its named custodian, and what triggers an early review (reorganization, member joining/leaving, recurring conflict).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the mission, context, and typical decisions in your own words. If NOMBRE_EQUIPO, TAMANO_EQUIPO, CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL, or DECISIONES_TIPICAS are missing, ask for them before drafting; do not invent team members, metrics, or neighboring teams. Mark unconfirmed items with [SUPUESTO] and list the gaps instead of filling them in. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide data.
Phase 2 - Plan: present an outline of the seven blocks and the data you will use in each; flag pending gaps.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the charter. Each objective carries a success signal; each decision in {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} carries a decision-maker, mechanism, and escalation path with timeframe; each norm is verifiable. Close with the review cadence, the custodian, and a brief facilitation note for adoption in the team session.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Mission answers why it exists, whom it serves, and what change it produces, without hollow jargon.
- [ ] Scope explicitly declares what is OUTSIDE scope and the boundaries (inputs/deliverables) with neighboring teams.
- [ ] There are 3 to 5 objectives, each with an observable success signal; baseline is named where it exists.
- [ ] The RACI matrix has no two Approvers for the same decision and no orphan roles, and covers the {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} members.
- [ ] Each decision in {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} has a decision-maker, mechanism, and escalation path with timeframe.
- [ ] Norms are verifiable (response time, definition of done) and not abstract mottos; {{NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS}} are resolved.
- [ ] There is a review cadence, a named custodian, and an early-review trigger.
- [ ] Assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO]; missing data was requested, not invented.
- [ ] Closes with a facilitation note for adoption in the session.
Expected deliverable: team charter for {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} in seven blocks, in clear and actionable English, ready to be reviewed and signed by the team in one session.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_rituales_equipo:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_EQUIPO: {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} > Team name or function (e.g., "product cell", "support area")
- VALORES_CLAVE: {{VALORES_CLAVE}} > 3 to 5 values to be reinforced and made visible
- TAMANO_EQUIPO: {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} > Number of people and composition (roles, seniority)
- MODALIDAD: {{MODALIDAD}} > In-person, remote, or hybrid; time zones if applicable
- RITUALES_ACTUALES: {{RITUALES_ACTUALES}} > Ceremonies that already exist today (dailies, demos, retros) or "none"
- DOLOR_CULTURAL: {{DOLOR_CULTURAL}} > Specific cultural problem to correct (e.g., "silos", "work goes unrecognized", "empty meetings")
- MADUREZ_LIDERAZGO: {{MADUREZ_LIDERAZGO}} > Leadership support and cadence discipline today (high, medium, low) or "no data"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team's declared values die when they live on a poster and not in the routine. This task converts the values of {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} into observable behaviors, anchoring them to specific ceremonies (kickoffs, demos, retros, recognitions, celebrations) that repeat in cadence. What is unlocked: a ritual system that a {{MODALIDAD}} team can adopt next week, with ready-made scripts and signals for detecting when a ritual becomes theater and needs to be reformed or retired. Design premise: a real ritual costs attention; fewer well-sustained rituals beat a saturated calendar that nobody respects.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Team leader and organizational culture designer, with experience building rituals that sustain high-performance teams in in-person, remote, and hybrid environments.

Deliverable: an actionable team ritual system. Steps:
1. Map each value in {{VALORES_CLAVE}} to an observable behavior (verb + object + frequency, not adjective) and to the type of ritual that triggers it: kickoff, progress, learning, recognition.
2. For each ritual define: purpose in one sentence; cadence and duration (timebox); facilitator and how the role rotates; minimum step-by-step script; opening gesture or question that anchors the value; participation mode according to {{MODALIDAD}} (synchronous, asynchronous, or mixed, with a fair time window for time zones).
3. For each ritual, declare the signal that it is still alive versus the signal that it has become theater, and the attention cost (people × minutes) it consumes.
4. Reuse or reform what exists in {{RITUALES_ACTUALES}} before creating new rituals; do not duplicate ceremonies or add a ritual where reforming one is enough.
5. Design a unique founding ritual to name the values WITH the team (not for the team) and a quarterly pruning mechanism with an explicit criterion for retiring dead rituals.
6. Close with the three most likely traps given {{DOLOR_CULTURAL}} and their prevention: the mandatory ceremony nobody wants, the recognition that only rewards heroism (and punishes sustained pace), and the celebration that ignores those who were not present or in another time zone.

Limits: do not propose more new rituals than values; do not exceed a reasonable attention budget for {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}}; do not prescribe rituals that require a higher level of {{MADUREZ_LIDERAZGO}} than what is available without flagging the risk.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reading: validate team, values, size, modality, current rituals, cultural pain point, and leadership maturity. If something is missing or ambiguous, ask; do not invent. If values exceed five, propose prioritizing.
Phase 2 - Translation: for each value, observable behavior + ritual that activates it. If you assume data not provided, mark it [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 - Design: complete the card for each ritual (purpose, cadence, duration, rotating facilitation, script, opening, mode per modality, alive/theater signal, attention cost), reusing what exists.
Phase 4 - System: founding ritual + quarterly pruning mechanism with retirement criterion + consolidated calendar with total weekly attention cost.
Phase 5 - Risks: three traps contextualized to {{DOLOR_CULTURAL}} and their prevention, plus the indicator that would warn when the trap is occurring.
Use recognized frameworks of team culture and rituals (agile ceremonies, working agreements, prime directive retrospectives). Neutral and professional English.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each value in {{VALORES_CLAVE}} is mapped to an observable behavior (verb + object + frequency), not to an abstract phrase.
- [ ] There is at least one ritual per type: kickoff, progress, learning, recognition.
- [ ] Each ritual includes purpose, cadence, duration, rotating facilitator, step-by-step script, opening, and attention cost.
- [ ] Each ritual declares its alive signal versus its theater signal.
- [ ] {{RITUALES_ACTUALES}} is reused or reformed before creating new rituals; no duplicates and no more new rituals than values.
- [ ] The design respects {{MODALIDAD}} (participation mode, asynchrony, and time zones if remote or hybrid).
- [ ] Includes a unique founding ritual and a quarterly pruning mechanism with an explicit retirement criterion.
- [ ] The three traps are tied to {{DOLOR_CULTURAL}} with concrete prevention and a warning indicator.
- [ ] The consolidated calendar declares the total weekly attention cost and is adoptable next week.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data.
Expected deliverable: document with value-behavior-ritual table, a card per ritual, the founding ritual, the quarterly pruning mechanism, and a consolidated calendar with attention cost, adoptable next week.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_reconocimiento_si:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team size, composition, and context (e.g., "14 people, distributed engineering across 3 time zones, remote")
- VALORES: {{VALORES}} > 3 to 5 values or observable behaviors to reinforce (e.g., "proactive collaboration, customer focus, shared learning")
- PROBLEMA_CULTURAL: {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}} > What motivates the system and how the lack of recognition looks today (e.g., "quiet work goes unnoticed and only failures are seen")
- CANALES: {{CANALES}} > Tools and spaces where the team already works (e.g., "Slack, weekly team meeting on Mondays")
- CADENCIA: {{CADENCIA}} > Target recognition frequency and visibility ritual frequency (e.g., "continuous in channel, weekly summary")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team leader wants to install a peer-to-peer recognition system that is frequent, specific, and anchored to values — not an annual award or vague praise. Well-designed peer-to-peer recognition reinforces desired behaviors at the moment they occur, distributes the sense of belonging, and makes visible the work that would otherwise go unnoticed. Good design unlocks observable and sustainable culture; bad design degenerates into an empty ritual, a popularity contest, or a bias toward the most visible people. The system must operate without material budget (this is not a rewards program) and respect differences in personality and time zone. The goal is to deliver an operating system ready to launch, measurable, and sustainable without depending on initial novelty.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior culture and people experience designer who has implemented peer recognition programs in knowledge teams, fluent in behavior design and engagement metrics.
Deliver, in this order:
1. Design principle of the system and how it avoids the four classic anti-patterns, neutralizing each with a concrete mechanism: vague recognition (neutralized by the observable behavior template), hierarchical or only top-down recognition (neutralized by peer-to-peer symmetry), sporadic recognition (neutralized by cadence and low effort), and transactional or material-reward-linked recognition (neutralized by anchoring to meaning, not prize).
2. Value-anchoring scheme for {{VALORES}}: for each value or observable behavior, a pair of examples "this yes recognizes / this does not recognize" to calibrate the criterion and prevent recognition from rewarding apparent effort, seniority, or social proximity instead of aligned behavior.
3. Operational mechanism over {{CANALES}}: recognition message format with a four-field template (to whom, what specific behavior, which value it embodies, what impact it had), frequency according to {{CADENCIA}}, and at least two low-friction levers for sending it (e.g., shortcut or command, light reminder, pinned example). Include how it works asynchronously if the team crosses time zones.
4. Visibility rituals that make recognition public without turning it into a contest (meeting opening, dedicated wall or channel, periodic summary), explaining the anti-contest mechanism of each one (e.g., rotation, no ranking or public count of who receives most).
5. 30-60-90 day launch plan, indicating who models the behavior first, adoption milestones per phase, and how responsibility is transferred from the leader to the team so it does not depend on a single person.
6. Health metrics for the system (participation rate, sender distribution to detect concentration in few people, per-person coverage to avoid people being forgotten, perceived link to values), their data source and review cadence, plus warning signals of an empty ritual.
7. Antifragility mechanisms to sustain it when novelty fades, including what to do if participation drops or the system starts to show bias.
Mark what you assume as [SUPUESTO]. Explicitly cover edge cases: remote multi-timezone team, leaders or founders who over-emit and overshadow others, introverted or low-profile people who are never named, and the risk that recognition is perceived as an obligation or a chore. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{VALORES}}, {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}}, {{CANALES}}, or {{CADENCIA}} are missing, ask for them in a single round before executing.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: restate team, values, cultural problem, channels, and cadence; name the anti-pattern that most threatens this team and why.
Phase 2 Design: define the principle, value-anchoring scheme with yes/no examples, and operational mechanism with a low-effort template.
Phase 3 Activation: design visibility rituals with their anti-contest mechanism and the 30-60-90 plan with who models first and the responsibility transfer.
Phase 4 Sustainability: define metrics with data source and cadence, warning signals, and antifragility mechanisms; cover edge cases; close with a launch checklist and the first step of the week.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The four anti-patterns (vague, hierarchical, sporadic, transactional) are named and each neutralized with a concrete, traceable mechanism in the design.
- Each value in {{VALORES}} has "this yes / this no" examples that allow unambiguous calibration and distinguish aligned behavior from apparent effort or social proximity.
- The message template includes the four fields: to whom, specific behavior, value it embodies, impact; with at least two low-friction levers and asynchronous support if applicable.
- The visibility rituals demonstrate how they avoid the contest effect (no ranking or public count of receivers).
- The 30-60-90 plan names who models first, milestones per phase, and how responsibility is transferred away from the leader.
- Metrics include sender distribution and per-person coverage, not just total volume, with data source and review cadence.
- There are at least two empty-ritual warning signals and two antifragility mechanisms with corrective action.
- Edge cases (multi-timezone, over-emitters, forgotten introverts, perception of obligation) are explicitly addressed.
- No material budget or monetary rewards in the design. Neutral and professional English, without emojis, without prices or the word "free".
Expected deliverable: an actionable document with a peer-to-peer recognition system (principle, value anchoring, operational mechanism, rituals, 30-60-90 plan, metrics and antifragility), covering edge cases, closed with a launch checklist and the first step of this week.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_equipo_remoto_per:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team size and nature (e.g., 9 engineers across 3 countries, 24/7 support, newly formed product squad, team with eroded trust after a reorganization)
- SINTOMAS: {{SINTOMAS}} > Observable signs of low belonging (e.g., cameras off, silence in channels, rising turnover, declining engagement survey, finding out about decisions late)
- ZONAS_HORARIAS: {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} > Time-zone spread and overlap window (e.g., UTC-5 to UTC+2, 3-hour common window; or no real overlap)
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > Available collaboration stack (e.g., Slack, Notion, video calls; clarify if there is NO in-person time or budget for physical events)
- OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA: {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}} > Target outcome with a horizon (e.g., raise perceived inclusion in the survey within 90 days; reduce voluntary turnover) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Physical distance in {{EQUIPO}} is eroding the human fabric: people deliver on tasks but build no bond, voice, or shared identity, as shown by {{SINTOMAS}}. Designing a deliberate belonging system unlocks retention, spontaneous collaboration, and psychological safety, replacing the accidental connection of the office with intentional practices that scale across {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} with {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, without depending on one person's charisma or falling into performative wellness. The system must hold even when the facilitator changes.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Organizational culture leader for remote and distributed teams, with experience in psychological safety (Amy Edmondson's framework), team ritual design, and the distinction between belonging (bond, inclusion, identity) and mere social activity.
Deliverable: an actionable belonging system, organized as follows:
1. Gap diagnosis from {{SINTOMAS}}, separating lack of social connection, lack of inclusion in decisions, and lack of collective identity; integrate {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence if available.
2. Map of the three belonging levels to address: interpersonal bond, inclusion, and collective identity, with the current and target state of each.
3. Portfolio of practices by level and cadence moment (recurring synchronous, asynchronous, one-off events). Each practice with: description, frequency, facilitator (rotating where applicable), duration, and the belonging signal it activates; respecting {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} and {{HERRAMIENTAS}}.
4. Explicit norms that make inclusion structural: speaking turns, default documentation (asynchronous decisions accessible to all time zones), a fair time-zone rule, recognition of contributions.
5. Indicators (qualitative and quantitative) tied to {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}, with a threshold or alarm signal per indicator and a review cadence.
6. 30-60-90 day implementation sequence + most likely adoption risks with their mitigations.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: classify {{SINTOMAS}} across the three belonging levels, distinguish cause from symptom, and name missing assumptions as [SUPUESTO]. If {{EQUIPO}} is new with no shared history, prioritize bond and identity; if trust is eroded, prioritize inclusion and psychological safety before asking for social vulnerability.
Phase 2 - Design: build the portfolio crossing level x cadence moment; prioritize low time-cost, high relationship-return practices; apply the fair time-zone rule by rotating scheduling discomfort among people and recording who bears it. If there is no real overlap window, default first to asynchronous practices.
Phase 3 - Governance: draft the norms, define the minimum set of indicators with their thresholds and review frequency, and lay out the 30-60-90 sequence with risks and mitigations.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each practice covers the five fields: description, frequency, facilitator, duration, and belonging signal.
- The portfolio touches all three levels (bond, inclusion, identity) and all three moments (synchronous, asynchronous, one-off); no critical cell is left empty without justification.
- Inclusion is structural (norms), not dependent on the leader's charisma; the system survives a facilitator change.
- Respects {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} (without always imposing the same slot on the same people) and runs only with {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; if a capability is missing, it is stated explicitly.
- Avoids performative wellness: each practice has a purpose tied to a level and respects time limits; nothing forces anyone to expose their private life.
- The design distinguishes the new-team case from the eroded-trust case.
- Observable indicators with thresholds or alarm signals, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: a belonging system document with diagnosis by level, current-vs-target-state map, practice portfolio table, list of structural norms, indicator panel with thresholds and cadence, and a 30-60-90 implementation sequence with risks and mitigations.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_diversidad_inclus:
[inputs]
- TIPO_EQUIPO: {{TIPO_EQUIPO}} > Team nature, size, and composition, including seniority mix if known (e.g., 8 people, multidisciplinary engineering, 3 senior / 5 junior, all reporting to the same leader)
- REUNIONES_RECURRENTES: {{REUNIONES_RECURRENTES}} > Recurring meetings and their format (e.g., 15-min daily, 60-min weekly planning, bi-weekly retro); mark which are decision meetings
- MODALIDAD: {{MODALIDAD}} > In-person, remote, or hybrid; time zones and languages involved (e.g., hybrid, UTC-5 to UTC+1, meetings in Spanish with 2 people working in their second language)
- DECISIONES_TIPICAS: {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} > Type of decisions where every voice should count (e.g., backlog prioritization, work assignment, goal-setting)
- TENSION_ACTUAL: {{TENSION_ACTUAL}} > Exclusion symptom you already observe (optional) (e.g., always the same 3 people talk; junior people stay silent; remote participants don't interrupt)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader wants every voice to count in the team's daily operations — not as a speech or a one-off event, but embedded in the meetings and decisions that already happen every week. The silent risk is that the same people dominate the airtime, that junior, remote, or second-language voices fade out, and that decisions reflect only those who speak loudest. Solving this unlocks better decisions (more real perspectives at the table), higher retention and engagement, and a culture where inclusion is an observable behavior rather than a poster on the wall.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team culture facilitator and organizational design specialist, expert in behavioral inclusion and psychological safety applied to daily operations.

Deliver, in this order:
1. Voice-gap diagnosis: identify the moments in the meeting and decision cycle where voices are currently lost in the given context (opening, speaking-time distribution, deliberation, decision, closing, and follow-up). For each gap, name who loses voice and through what mechanism.
2. Set of 6 to 8 micro-practices: for each one specify (a) exact moment of application, (b) verbatim activation script or phrase ready to use, (c) time it consumes, (d) observable signal that it is working, and (e) the failure mode it prevents.
3. Modality adjustments: adapt the set to the declared modality (in-person, remote, hybrid), addressing time zones and languages; note what changes and why.
4. 4-week adoption routine: introduce one practice at a time, specifying what to measure each week and how to decide whether to keep, adjust, or drop it.
5. Antidote to the performative: a simple mechanism to detect when a practice has become an empty ritual and how to correct it.
6. Limits and edge cases: name when a practice does NOT apply or could cause harm (teams in crisis, open conflict, extreme power asymmetry) and the alternative.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm TIPO_EQUIPO, REUNIONES_RECURRENTES, MODALIDAD, and DECISIONES_TIPICAS; if TENSION_ACTUAL is empty, infer the most likely gaps and mark them as [SUPUESTO]. Distinguish inclusion (every voice shapes the outcome) from mere speaking turns: the goal is real influence on the decision, not just microphone time.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: map the meeting-decision cycle against Tim Clark's four stages of inclusion (belonging, learning, contributing, challenging the status quo) and locate where each stage breaks down; cross with psychological safety (Edmondson) to distinguish silence from fear versus silence from disengagement.
Phase 3 - Practice design: derive micro-practices grounded in psychological safety and inclusive meeting design (rounds, write before you speak, rotating facilitator and devil's advocate roles, disagree-and-commit decisions, asynchronous capture of absent voices). Each practice low-friction, immediately actionable, no new tools.
Phase 4 - Adoption and control: order practices by impact-over-effort for the 4-week routine; define the weekly metric and the signal that a practice has become performative. Prioritize a single new practice per week to avoid overload.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each micro-practice states exact moment, verbatim activation script, time, signal of effectiveness, and failure mode prevented.
- [ ] The set has between 6 and 8 practices, all actionable tomorrow without new tools.
- [ ] The diagnosis maps explicitly to the four stages of inclusion and to psychological safety, and names who loses voice and through what mechanism.
- [ ] Modality adjustments are specific to the declared MODALIDAD, not generic, and include time zones and languages.
- [ ] The 4-week routine introduces a single practice per week with a tracking metric and a keep/adjust/drop criterion.
- [ ] The performative antidote is concrete and enables dropping or correcting a practice.
- [ ] Limits and edge cases are named where a practice does not apply or could cause harm.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented data about the team.
Expected deliverable: a 1-to-2-page operational inclusion system, with a micro-practices table (moment / script / time / signal / failure mode), a 4-week adoption plan, and a self-correction mechanism, ready to present to the team.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_team_health_check:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team name, size, and role (e.g., 7-person product squad, payments engineering)
- CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO: {{CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO}} > Frequency (monthly/quarterly) and whether it is the first measurement or there is a prior baseline
- DIMENSIONES: {{DIMENSIONES}} > Dimensions to assess, or "suggest standard set" to use the base Spotify model
- VOTOS: {{VOTOS}} > Votes per dimension with traffic light and trend, or "pending session" if voting has not happened yet (optional)
- RETO_OBSERVADO: {{RETO_OBSERVADO}} > Symptom or dysfunction that prompted the health check (e.g., turnover, rework, slow releases) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are running a team health check under the Spotify model (Kniberg and Lindwall's Squad Health Check) for {{EQUIPO}}, with cadence and moment {{CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO}}. The purpose is to detect dysfunctions early, while they are still cheap to fix, before they become turnover, rework, at-risk releases, or eroded trust. The per-dimension traffic light makes the current state visible and the trend makes direction visible: a green dimension that is getting worse can be more urgent than a red one that is improving. The outcome unlocks a focused team conversation and an action plan with owners, separating what the team controls from what must be escalated to the organization. The health check is a perception thermometer, not a hard metric: it guides the conversation rather than replacing it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team health facilitator and agile coach, with experience running dimension-based health checks with traffic lights and trend readings for product and engineering teams.

Produce two deliverables:

Deliverable 1 - Facilitation kit:
1. Confirm or propose 8 to 11 dimensions based on {{DIMENSIONES}}; if the standard set is requested, use the base Spotify model (Delivering Value, Ease of Release, Code or Work Quality, Fun, Learning, Clear Mission, Organizational Support, Autonomy, Sustainable Pace, Process Health, Mutual Trust).
2. For each dimension, write the positive statement (green anchor) and the negative statement (red anchor), with yellow as the intermediate state; phrase them in the present tense, as observable behaviors specific to the context of {{EQUIPO}}.
3. Define the protocol: individual anonymous vote first (to avoid anchoring bias and hierarchy effect), then open discussion; how to record the trend (improving / stable / worsening) relative to the previous measurement; and framing rules (suggested timebox, who facilitates, which dimension is discussed first).

Deliverable 2 - Report:
4. Using {{VOTOS}}, consolidate a Dimension | Traffic Light | Trend matrix. When there is strong vote dispersion on a dimension, flag it as a misalignment signal that warrants conversation — do not flatten it into a plain average.
5. Identify 2-3 priority focus areas (red, or yellow trending downward) and justify why, connecting them to {{RETO_OBSERVADO}} where applicable.
6. Separate what the team can resolve from what requires organizational escalation, naming for the latter who to escalate to (role, not person).
7. Propose 3-5 actions, each with a suggested owner (role) and review date; prioritize a few high-impact actions over a long list.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: validate {{EQUIPO}}, {{CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO}}, and {{RETO_OBSERVADO}}; set the dimension list and a psychologically safe purpose (it belongs to the team, it is not individual evaluation). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context.
Phase 2 - Kit design: write green/red anchors per dimension and the voting, framing, and trend protocol.
Phase 3 - Consolidation: only if {{VOTOS}} contains data, build the matrix; anything missing stays as [PENDIENTE] — no invented data. If {{VOTOS}} is "pending session," deliver only Deliverable 1 and leave Deliverable 2 as a template ready to fill in after the session.
Phase 4 - Prioritization and actions: derive focus areas, separate team vs. escalation, and list actions with owner and date.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Between 8 and 11 dimensions, each with coherent positive and negative anchors consistent with the traffic light, observable, and in the present tense.
- Explicit protocol of anonymous vote first + discussion, with framing (timebox, facilitator, order) and trend capture relative to the previous measurement.
- Dimension | Traffic Light | Trend matrix built only from real {{VOTOS}}; missing items marked [PENDIENTE], zero invented votes; strong dispersion flagged as a signal.
- 2-3 priority focus areas justified, applying the rule that a yellow trending downward can outweigh a stable red, connected to {{RETO_OBSERVADO}} where applicable.
- Clear separation of team-resolvable vs. organizational-escalation items, with the role to escalate to named.
- 3-5 actions, each with a suggested owner (role) and review date; few and high-impact.
- Professional, neutral, and psychologically safe tone; no individual performance evaluation; no votes attributed to individuals.
- If VOTOS is pending, deliver kit + report template — no invented data.
Expected deliverable: health check facilitation kit + consolidated report (or template if no votes) with the traffic-light-and-trend matrix, priority focus areas, and a 3-to-5-action plan with owner and date.
spec-liderazgo_cultura_disfunciones_lenc:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_EQUIPO: {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} > Team to diagnose (e.g., executive committee, product squad)
- TAMANO_Y_ROLES: {{TAMANO_Y_ROLES}} > Number of members and key roles
- ANTIGUEDAD_EQUIPO: {{ANTIGUEDAD_EQUIPO}} > Time working together in the current composition
- SINTOMAS_OBSERVADOS: {{SINTOMAS_OBSERVADOS}} > Concrete behaviors, phrases, and facts that motivate the diagnosis
- DINAMICA_REUNIONES: {{DINAMICA_REUNIONES}} > How debate, decisions, and follow-up happen in meetings
