- [ ] Skill and will evaluated separately, each high/low with cited evidence and listed signals.
- [ ] Inferences marked [SUPUESTO]; missing data requested, not invented; axes with weak evidence declared with lower confidence.
- [ ] Quadrant and style (Direct/Develop/Motivate/Delegate) match the matrix logic; border cases resolved toward the more conservative style with justification.
- [ ] Style translated into concrete do and stop-doing behaviors, contextualized to the task.
- [ ] Risk of the wrong style warned for this specific case.
- [ ] Explicit reminder: diagnosis per task and moment, not a label of the person; includes re-evaluation trigger.
- [ ] Plan with opening, 3 to 5 open questions, agreements, cadence, and observable signal of movement.
- [ ] Professional tone centered on behaviors and evidence, without character judgments; no prices or promises of free service.
Expected deliverable: one-page Skill-Will diagnosis with skill axis, will axis, quadrant and style with confidence level, usage warning, conversation plan with follow-up, and re-evaluation trigger.
spec-liderazgo_coaching_sucesion_rol:
[inputs]
- ROL_CRITICO: {{ROL_CRITICO}} > Name and level of the key role to safeguard (e.g. Data Architecture Lead)
- TITULAR_ACTUAL: {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}} > Person currently in the role, tenure, and departure probability or signals
- CANDIDATOS: {{CANDIDATOS}} > Potential internal successors with their current role; "Not identified" if none yet
- CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO: {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}} > Area, team size, priorities, critical dependencies, and relevant constraints
- HORIZONTE_SUCESION: {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}} > Target window to have a ready successor (e.g. 12-18 months)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A key role concentrates knowledge, relationships, and decisions held by a single person: if they leave without a prepared replacement, the team is exposed (high bus factor). The goal is to anticipate that departure, identify and prepare successors, and turn the continuity risk into a manageable development roadmap. A solid plan unlocks retention of critical knowledge, promotion decisions defensible before HR and the sponsor, and peace of mind in the event of an unexpected departure. Distinguish two urgencies: probable short-term departure (prioritize coverage and transfer) vs. preventive safeguarding (prioritize pipeline and development).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Director of Talent and Organizational Development with fifteen years of safeguarding continuity in critical roles and designing succession pipelines.
Deliver a succession plan for {{ROL_CRITICO}} (incumbent {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}}, context {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, candidates {{CANDIDATOS}}, horizon {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}, evidence {{ADJUNTOS}}) with these numbered components:
1. Criticality profile and bus factor: unique responsibilities, undocumented tacit knowledge, internal and external relationships the incumbent holds, decisions or systems only the incumbent operates, and impact and time window in which their absence becomes critical. Classify continuity risk as high / medium / low with justification.
2. Successor map: each candidate placed in a performance-by-potential matrix (9-box) with their availability classification (ready now / 1-2 years / 3+ years) and recommendation on an external path if the internal pipeline does not cover the horizon. If {{CANDIDATOS}} = "Not identified", declare the gap and propose how to build the pipeline.
3. Gap analysis for the 2-3 most viable successors: technical, leadership, and business exposure gaps, separating what can be closed through development from what only requires experience in the role.
4. Development plan per priority candidate: concrete actions (stretch assignment, shadowing the incumbent, knowledge transfer, mentoring, training), owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones within {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}.
5. Critical knowledge transfer plan (what to document, what to pair-program or shadow, what to systematize) and residual risks if the departure happens before a ready successor is in place, each with mitigation and escalation trigger; close with an interim coverage contingency plan and review checkpoints with HR and the area sponsor.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Criticality: decompose the role; if information on responsibilities, systems, or relationships is missing, ask for it in a single round before continuing.
Phase 2 - Pipeline: apply the 9-box model (performance x potential) and the availability classification; do not force candidates where there are none, recommend the external path and the continuity cost of having no pipeline.
Phase 3 - Gaps: contrast each successor against the criticality profile from Phase 1; distinguish development gap (closable through action) vs. experience gap (only closable in the role).
Phase 4 - Development and transfer: translate each closable gap into an action with owner, horizon, and progress signal; sequence milestones; document tacit knowledge transfer, residual risks, and interim coverage.
Edge cases: incumbent with imminent departure (< 3 months) -> prioritize transfer and interim coverage over long-term development. Single candidate -> declare concentration risk and recommend a backup. No candidates -> the deliverable is a pipeline-building plan + external path, not an empty map.
Do not invent names, metrics, or performance evaluations: mark any inference as [SUPUESTO]. Treat people with care: use roles and placeholders, do not expose personal judgments. Neutral and professional English.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The criticality profile names concrete tacit knowledge and relationships, not generic ones, and classifies risk as high / medium / low with justification.
- Each candidate has a 9-box position and an explicit availability classification; if there are no candidates, there is a pipeline-building plan + external path.
- Gaps separate what can be closed through development from what requires real experience in the role.
- Each development action has an owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones.
- There is a knowledge transfer plan, residual risks with mitigation and trigger, interim coverage contingency, and review checkpoints with HR and the sponsor.
- Zero invented names or metrics; every inference marked [SUPUESTO]; people information treated as sensitive; neutral English without emojis.
Expected deliverable: a succession plan structured in five blocks, ready to review with HR and the area sponsor, that reduces the bus factor of the role to an actionable and manageable development roadmap.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_evaluacion_anua:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO: {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}} > Name or identifier and role of the person being reviewed (can be anonymized, e.g. "Senior Data Analyst")
- PERIODO_EVALUADO: {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} > Cycle covered by the review (e.g. "Fiscal Year 2025, Q1-Q4"); defines the start of Q1
- EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS: {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}} > Facts, achievements, metrics, and dates throughout the cycle; ideally one or more per quarter
- AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS: {{AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS}} > Behaviors or results to develop that have already been observed (optional)
- CRITERIOS_EVALUACION: {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} > Competencies, values, or objectives from the formal framework; if there is a rating scale, indicate the levels (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are the leader responsible for closing the performance cycle for a team member and you need a balanced annual review, ready for a face-to-face conversation. The central risk is recency bias: overweighting what happened in the last few weeks and forgetting the rest of the year. A review well-anchored in dated evidence and balanced between achievements and development unlocks a fair conversation, defensible calibration decisions, and a credible growth plan for the next cycle. A biased or evidence-free review erodes trust, exposes to legal or equity bias, and demotivates.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader with experience in talent management, performance calibration, and developmental feedback.
Deliverable: a structured annual performance review for {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}} in {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}}, based on {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}}, {{AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS}}, and {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}. Steps:
1. Build a timeline of evidence by quarter (Q1-Q4); mark any quarter without data as an evidence gap (do not fill in).
2. Draft a minimum of three achievements using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model, each with a concrete example, date, and observable metric or result; distribute achievements across quarters.
3. Draft two or three development areas using the same SBI model, framed as actionable behaviors (not personality traits), each with a suggested verifiable action and, where applicable, concrete support or resource.
4. Close with an overall rating aligned to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} (mapping achievements/areas to each competency or criterion), two or three SMART objectives for the next cycle, and a calibration note confirming coverage of all four quarters and explicitly stating how recency bias was mitigated.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Temporal mapping: place each fact in its quarter using the declared start of Q1; detect late-period concentrations that reveal recency bias and flag imbalances.
Phase 2 - Achievements: apply SBI with dated evidence and observable results; balance across quarters and separate verifiable fact from interpretation.
Phase 3 - Development: translate observations into specific behaviors and verifiable improvement actions; developmental tone, not punitive.
Phase 4 - Close and calibration: synthesize overall rating, SMART objectives, and a per-quarter coverage note; declare assumptions and gaps.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
Edge cases: if evidence covers fewer than four quarters, declare gaps and do NOT invent; if an observation sounds like a personality trait, reframe it as a behavior; if {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} is not provided, use generic axes (results, collaboration, quality, initiative) and mark it [SUPUESTO]; if there is a sensitive incident, describe it as behavior and impact without accusatory language.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four quarters (Q1-Q4) are represented; evidence gaps are declared, not invented.
- [ ] At least three achievements and two or three development areas, all in SBI format.
- [ ] Each achievement has a concrete example, date, and observable metric or result.
- [ ] Development areas describe actionable behaviors, never personality traits, and each brings a verifiable action (and support where applicable).
- [ ] Overall rating coherent with {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and mapped to its competencies; next-cycle objectives in SMART format.
- [ ] Calibration note confirms temporal coverage and explicitly states how recency bias was mitigated.
- [ ] Verifiable fact separated from interpretation; professional, specific, and respectful tone in neutral English; no invented data (inferences marked [SUPUESTO]).
Expected deliverable: annual review document with sections Timeline, Achievements, Development areas, Overall rating and objectives, and Calibration note, ready for the close conversation.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_autoevaluacion_:
[inputs]
- ROL_Y_NIVEL: {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}} > Job title, seniority level, and area; calibrates the expectations against which the role is measured
- PERIODO_EVALUADO: {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} > Cycle covered by the self-evaluation (fiscal year, semester, quarter)
- OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS: {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}} > Objectives, OKRs, goals, or formal competencies against which you are evaluated
- LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA: {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} > Candidate achievements, metrics, verifiable sources, and your specific role in each one
- FORMATO_EMPRESA: {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}} > Format, length, rating scale, and tone required by the process (optional)
- FEEDBACK_PREVIO: {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} > Feedback from previous cycles, pending commitments, or areas flagged by your manager (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to write your performance self-evaluation for the period {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} in the role {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}}. A strong self-evaluation is not the most flattering or the most modest: it is the most credible. If you exaggerate, you lose credibility with your evaluator and undermine your real achievements; if you understate yourself, you leave contributions unrecognized that deserve visibility and compensation. A calibrated, evidence-based self-evaluation unlocks fairer career conversations, supports promotion or salary decisions, and builds a reliable record of your trajectory. The difference between a forgettable draft and one that moves the needle almost always comes down to three disciplines: every claim anchored to data, every achievement distinguished from the collective outcome, every gap named with its plan. This prompt gets you there without inflating or inventing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior performance and talent development coach, with experience designing evaluation cycles (including peer calibration scales and committees) and training professionals to document their work in a fair, verifiable, and development-oriented way.

Deliverable: a structured and calibrated self-evaluation draft, ready to review and paste into the company format. Steps:
1. Reframe the received context (role, period, objectives, format, prior feedback) and confirm assumptions before drafting.
2. For each item in {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}}, gather the associated achievements from {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} and convert them from vague statements to evidence-based statements (what I did, what result it produced, what data or source supports it).
3. Explicitly separate the team's result from your personally verifiable contribution in each achievement.
4. Calibrate the tone: flag where the draft exaggerates without data to support it and where it undervalues a real achievement, and adjust to a defensible middle ground before a skeptical evaluator.
5. Address goals without clear evidence honestly: declare partial progress or non-fulfillment with its root cause, without embellishment.
6. Write honest improvement areas, each with the concrete action plan you have already started or will start, connecting with {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} when it exists.
7. Close with learnings and growth from the period, tied to the trajectory and to the expectations of the next level of the role.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reframe context and objectives; if achievements, evidence, or key objectives are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Structure each achievement with STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) and use precise contribution language (I led / I coordinated / I contributed / the team achieved) to separate individual contribution from collective achievement.
Phase 2 - Conversion to evidence: for each objective, transform vague statements into statements anchored to a metric or source; flag as [SUPUESTO] or pending confirmation any data not provided, without inventing it or rounding figures upward.
Phase 3 - Tone calibration: detect exaggerations (claim without data), understatements (real achievement undervalued), and improper attributions (team achievement presented as one's own); adjust to a defensible point.
Phase 4 - Final drafting: assemble the draft with the agreed sections, align length and scale to {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}}, and list at the end the data pending confirmation and the credibility risks detected.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every relevant achievement has a metric, source, or concrete evidence; no data was invented or inflated.
- [ ] Personal contribution is clearly separated from the team's result in each achievement.
- [ ] The tone is calibrated: no inflated claims, no undervaluing of real achievements, no attributing collective achievements to oneself.
- [ ] Unmet or partially met goals are declared with their root cause — they are not omitted.
- [ ] Improvement areas are honest and each one includes a concrete action plan; prior feedback is linked when it exists.
- [ ] Missing data is flagged as pending confirmation, not completed with undeclared assumptions.
- [ ] The draft respects {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}} in structure, length, scale, and tone.
Expected deliverable: self-evaluation draft (4-to-6-line executive summary, achievements by objective, partially met or unmet goals, improvement areas with plan, learnings), followed by a list of data pending confirmation and the credibility risks detected.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_calibracion_ses:
[inputs]
- CICLO_Y_ESCALA: {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}} > Evaluated period and rating scale with its meaning (e.g. 1-5, or categories such as Below/Meets/Exceeds); include whether the scale forces a target distribution or is open
- POBLACION: {{POBLACION}} > People to calibrate grouped by level or role family; count, involved managers, and whether there are comparable subgroups
- RATINGS_PROPUESTOS: {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}} > Preliminary rating per person and proposing manager; ideally with the prior cycle's rating if available
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Achievements, metrics, feedback, and dates supporting each rating; indicate the source (self-evaluation, manager, peers, system data)
- TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES: {{TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES}} > Session duration, facilitator, and attending managers (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You will prepare a calibration session among managers who review ratings for people at the same level or role family. The purpose is to level the standard across teams and protect the cycle's fairness: a well-prepared calibration reduces disputes, sustains compensation and promotion decisions before an audit, and prevents a rating from being decided by impression rather than evidence. Good preparation unlocks a shorter, less defensive meeting, with sensitive cases already mapped and difficult questions already drafted in neutral tone.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior performance calibration facilitator with experience in people analytics and fair evaluation process design. Stance: judge the quality of the evidence supporting each rating — never the person being evaluated or the manager's judgment.
Deliverable: a session preparation package. Steps:
1. Reframe the cycle {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}}, the scale with its meaning, and the {{POBLACION}} to be calibrated; list information gaps and declare whether the scale allows free distribution or imposes a target.
2. Build the distribution of {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}} by manager and flag deviations suggesting systemic leniency or severity, comparing each manager against the group, without forcing a normal curve. Distinguish a real deviation from a small sample (a manager with few evaluees may deviate by chance): mark it as a weak signal.
3. For each flagged case, classify {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} as: full-cycle performance vs. isolated recent event (recency); individual merit vs. halo from a single project or historical reputation. Also note, when the signal appears, contrast bias (rating influenced by comparison with a nearby peer) and affinity/similarity bias.
4. Draft 2-3 neutral challenge questions per flagged case, directed at the proposing manager, requiring observable and dated evidence — not impressions or personality traits.
5. Deliver a timed agenda, case review order (from highest to lowest bias risk), and a tiebreaker protocol for when managers disagree (criterion, decision-maker, how it is recorded).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm scale, population, and rules; if {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}}, {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}}, or {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding. {{TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} are optional: if missing, assume defaults and flag them [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Detection: analyze distribution by manager (leniency/severity, with a weak signal flag if the sample is small) and per case cross-reference evidence against dates (recency) and against a single dominant attribute (halo). Flag each finding with the presumed bias, its evidence signal, and a confidence level (high/medium/low).
Phase 3 - Challenge preparation: draft neutral questions, the case card, and the agenda. Do not invent data about individuals; anything not provided goes as [SUPUESTO]. In shareable outputs use codes (P-01, M-A) instead of names to preserve functional anonymity.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit reframing of the cycle, scale (with meaning and free/target type), and population; gaps listed.
- [ ] Distribution by manager presented; leniency/severity flagged without imposing a forced curve; small samples marked as weak signal.
- [ ] Each flagged case distinguishes recency (dates) and halo (single attribute), with contrast/affinity noted when applicable, its evidence signal, and confidence level.
- [ ] Challenge questions are neutral, centered on observable and dated evidence — not on judgments about the person or personality traits.
- [ ] Timed agenda + bias-risk order + actionable tiebreaker protocol (criterion, decision-maker, record).
- [ ] Zero invented data; assumptions flagged [SUPUESTO]; functional anonymity with codes in shareable outputs; neutral professional English.
Expected deliverable: preparation document with (a) distribution table by manager, (b) card per flagged case with bias, classified evidence, and confidence level, (c) challenge question bank, (d) agenda and tiebreaker protocol.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_matriz_9box:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > List of team members with, for each one: name or alias, recent results against goals, observable behavior examples, and potential signals
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Performance window to evaluate (6 to 12 months recommended to avoid recency bias)
- OBJETIVOS: {{OBJETIVOS}} > Goals or objectives against which performance is measured
- DEFINICION_POTENCIAL: {{DEFINICION_POTENCIAL}} > What potential means in this context: agile learning, role ambition, adaptability, capacity to take on greater scope (optional; if missing, the AI proposes a definition and asks for confirmation)
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > What the calibration is for: development plans, succession, challenge assignments, career conversations (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader needs an honest and actionable read of their team to decide on development, retention, and challenge assignments. The 9-box matrix (Performance x Potential Grid, popularized by McKinsey and GE) crosses current performance against growth potential in a 9-cell grid and converts diffuse impressions into a structured, evidence-based conversation. When applied well, it unlocks differentiated development plans, identifies successors and flight risks, and exposes biases before they contaminate career decisions. When applied poorly, it labels people and justifies layoffs: this prompt prevents that use. Assumption: the leader has direct contact with the team and data from at least one cycle; if not, the output will be explicitly provisional.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Talent and Organizational Development Director with experience facilitating 9-box calibration sessions in people committees.

Deliverable: a calibrated placement of the team on the 9-box matrix with differentiated actions per quadrant. Steps:
1. Align criteria: define the performance axis as sustained results against OBJETIVOS during PERIODO (not an isolated spike or personal affinity) and the potential axis according to DEFINICION_POTENCIAL (demonstrated capacity to take on greater scope, not tenure or charisma). Declare that both axes require observable evidence and set the minimum evidence threshold.
2. Verify data sufficiency per person in EQUIPO; if evidence is missing for one axis, mark the placement as provisional and indicate the missing data instead of inventing it.
3. Build the 9-box matrix placing each person in their box with one line of evidence-based justification; flag border cases between two boxes.
4. For each occupied quadrant, provide its reading and 2 to 3 differentiated, concrete actions aligned with PROPOSITO.
5. Issue calibration alerts (biases, border cases, risk concentrations) and open questions before irreversible decisions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: set operational definitions for both axes and the minimum evidence threshold.
Phase 2 - Data cleaning: review EQUIPO person by person, separating facts from impressions and flagging gaps; discard data outside PERIODO to mitigate recency bias.
Phase 3 - Placement: assign each person to one of the 9 boxes (low/medium/high performance x low/medium/high potential) with justification; flag anyone on the border between two boxes and explain why.
Phase 4 - Action by quadrant: translate each occupied box into a reading + actions. Reference guide: high performance + high potential (star) = retention, succession, stretch; high potential + medium or low performance (enigma or new to role) = focused development and expectation clarity; high performance + medium or low potential (solid, reliable expert) = recognition, retention, and technical deepening; low potential and low performance (at risk) = improvement plan with a deadline and an honest conversation. Labels are a reading, not a verdict.
Phase 5 - Calibration and close: list probable biases (halo, recency, leniency, contrast, affinity), risk concentrations (flight of several stars, succession gap, overload on a single person), and open questions.
Edge cases: team of one person (the matrix loses comparative power — declare it); everyone in the same box (review criteria, possible leniency or poorly calibrated standard); data only for one axis (place provisionally on that axis, ask for the other).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each person placed in a single primary box, with justification by evidence (not impression).
- [ ] Placements with insufficient data marked as provisional, with the missing data explicit.
- [ ] Both axes operationally defined and evidence threshold set before placing anyone.
- [ ] Each occupied quadrant has a reading + 2 to 3 differentiated, concrete actions aligned with PROPOSITO.
- [ ] Actions distinguish development, retention, career conversation, and improvement plan according to the box.
- [ ] Section on biases, border cases, and risk concentrations present.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases (single-person team, concentration in one box, axis without data) addressed when they occur.
- [ ] No person labeled as expendable; no termination automatically derived from the 9-box.
- [ ] Open questions listed before irreversible decisions.
Expected deliverable: 9-box matrix placed by evidence + differentiated actions per quadrant + calibration alerts + open questions, in professional English.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_pip_plan_mejora:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR_ROL: {{COLABORADOR_ROL}} > Role, level, and approximate tenure of the employee (without a real name if anonymization is preferred)
- BRECHAS_DESEMPENO: {{BRECHAS_DESEMPENO}} > Observed gaps as concrete facts (what, when, impact) — not personality judgments
- EXPECTATIVAS_OBJETIVO: {{EXPECTATIVAS_OBJETIVO}} > Expected standard for the role against which performance is measured
- DURACION_PLAZO: {{DURACION_PLAZO}} > Plan horizon (e.g. 30, 60, or 90 days) and start date
- SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE: {{SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE}} > Real support resources: mentoring, training, workload reassignment, tools, time
- CONTEXTO_PREVIO: {{CONTEXTO_PREVIO}} > (optional) Feedback already delivered, background, legal or HR constraints
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An employee is operating below the role standard and the situation requires formal intervention. A well-designed PIP converts a difficult conversation into a structured and fair opportunity: it provides clarity on what needs to change, the support to achieve it, and transparent evaluation rules. Doing it well protects the person (a real opportunity, dignified treatment), the leader (a defensible and consistent decision), and the organization (a traceable process before HR). A vague, punitive, or unsupported PIP destroys trust and creates employment liability. The goal is a plan that any third party would evaluate the same way given the same data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with a track record in performance management and HR coordination, experienced in defensible, symmetric, and dignity-centered improvement plans.
Design a complete PIP and deliver, in this order:
1. Purpose framing in 3-4 sentences: respectful, improvement-oriented, with no punitive language.
2. Gap table: one row per gap, with columns Observed gap (fact) | SMART expectation | Compliance indicator | Evidence to be reviewed | Associated support.
3. Support plan: what the organization offers (mentoring, training, resources, workload adjustments) and follow-up cadence (frequency and format of check-ins).
4. Timeline: start date, intermediate check-ins with date and focus, and closing date, aligned with the given timeframe.
5. Closing criteria: a list of SUCCESS criteria and a list of EXIT criteria, symmetric, with numeric or binary thresholds (not adjectives), evaluable by a third party.
6. Opening script: a sober 6-to-8-line draft for the initial conversation.
7. Evidence log: a brief template for recording at each check-in the date, progress per expectation, and next steps.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: reframe the role, gaps, and standard; separate facts from judgments; if a gap is written as a personality judgment, ask for it to be rewritten as an observable fact (what happened, when, what impact) before including it; flag with [SUPUESTO] any missing data and ask for critical ones before proceeding; do not invent background information or facts about the person.
Phase 2 - Plan: structure the PIP (framing, gaps-to-expectations, support, timeline, criteria, script, log) and present the outline for validation.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft all 7 deliverables; verify that every expectation is SMART, that every success/exit criterion is measurable and symmetric, that no gap is left without an expectation, indicator, evidence, or support, and that the timeline is respected; close by reminding to validate with HR and, if applicable, with employment legal counsel before communicating to the employee.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each gap is stated as an observable fact, not a personality judgment.
- [ ] Each expectation meets SMART criteria (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound).
- [ ] Each gap has an expectation, indicator, evidence, and associated support (no gaps).
- [ ] Success and exit criteria are symmetric, with numeric or binary thresholds evaluable by a third party.
- [ ] The timeline respects the given period and includes at least one intermediate check-in with a defined focus.
- [ ] The support is concrete and realistic, derived from what was declared available (not vague promises).
- [ ] The evidence log allows each check-in to be documented in a traceable way.
- [ ] Professional and human tone; zero punitive or intimidating language.
- [ ] Assumptions flagged [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented about the person or their background.
- [ ] Reminder to validate with HR and, if applicable, with employment legal counsel before communicating.
Expected deliverable: a PIP document ready to review with HR and discuss with the employee, with framing, gap table, support plan, timeline, symmetric closing criteria, opening script, and evidence log.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_conversacion_ca:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_ROL: {{NOMBRE_ROL}} > Name or role of the person receiving the rating (e.g. "senior analyst on the data team")
- RATING: {{RATING}} > Rating being delivered and, if applicable, the one the person expected (e.g. "Partially Meets, expected Exceeds")
- MOTIVO_RATING: {{MOTIVO_RATING}} > Central reason and observable evidence supporting the rating (dated facts and examples, not judgments)
- FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER: {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}} > What you genuinely value about the person and what is not in question
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} > How you want the person to feel at the end of the conversation (optional)
- HISTORIAL: {{HISTORIAL}} > Prior conversations, warnings, or signals given before this cycle (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am going to conduct a performance evaluation conversation in which I deliver to {{NOMBRE_ROL}} the rating {{RATING}}, lower than expected. The central reason is {{MOTIVO_RATING}} and I want to preserve {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}}. A poorly conducted conversation burns trust, triggers a defensive reaction, and leaves the person without a path to improvement; a well-conducted one sustains the relationship, makes the message irrefutable, and opens an actionable path forward. What gets unlocked: clarity on the rating, preserved dignity, and an improvement plan the person can own.
Assumptions: the rating decision is already closed and is not renegotiated in the room; the conversation is 1:1 and private; there is a formal performance cycle backing the process. If any of these do not apply, declare it and adjust.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior manager and performance coach with experience conducting high-impact feedback conversations, trained in separating observable behavior from identity and in holding emotions without renegotiating the message.
Deliver a conversation script ready to rehearse plus a reaction management kit. Steps:
1. Opening (2-3 sentences): name the purpose without suspense or preamble; frame the conversation as honest and forward-oriented.
2. Rating delivery: communicate {{RATING}} directly and support {{MOTIVO_RATING}} with two or three specific, observable, dated examples, separating the person's behavior from who they are.
3. Recognition: integrate {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}} as a firm fact, not as a buffer or sandwich technique that dilutes the message.
4. Listening space: include phrases to invite a reaction, hold the silence (3-5 seconds), and validate the emotion without conceding on the rating.
5. Forward reframe: define two or three concrete, measurable, dated actions, and the support the manager commits to providing.
6. Closing: confirm mutual understanding (not forced agreement) and set the follow-up.
7. Reaction kit: anticipate denial, anger, and emotional breakdown with a model response for each.
8. Trap phrases: list two or three formulations to avoid (relativizing the message, blaming the system or third parties, promising what cannot be controlled) with their alternatives.
9. 30-day follow-up plan with verifiable milestones.
Align the script with {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} when it exists and consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: validate that {{MOTIVO_RATING}} is supported by observable facts; if it is based on judgments or {{HISTORIAL}} of prior signals is missing, ask for the missing evidence before drafting. If there were no prior signals, state it transparently: it is data that changes the tone, not something to hide.
Phase 2 - Structure: apply the sequence purpose > evidence > listening > path, keeping behavior and identity separate and a single central message undiluted.
Phase 3 - Rehearsal: draft the script in spoken language, brief, without HR jargon; mark with brackets the moments of pause and listening.
Phase 4 - Stress test: subject the script to the three probable reactions and adjust the model responses so they validate the emotion without reopening the rating negotiation.
Edge cases: if the person asks to change the rating in the room, redirect to the formal process without promising a review; if they cry or shut down, offer a brief pause without canceling the message; if the conversation escalates to hostility, set a respectful limit and propose resuming.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The opening names the purpose in the first 30 seconds, without suspense.
- [ ] The rating is delivered directly and supported with 2-3 specific, observable, dated examples — not judgments.
- [ ] Behavior and identity are kept separate throughout the script.
- [ ] The recognition is genuine and does not function as a buffer or sandwich.
- [ ] There is an explicit listening space with phrases to hold silence and emotion.
- [ ] The forward actions are concrete, measurable, and dated.
- [ ] The kit covers denial, anger, and emotional breakdown with responses that do not renegotiate the rating.
- [ ] Trap phrases are listed with their alternatives.
- [ ] The 30-day plan has verifiable milestones.
- [ ] Edge cases (request to change the rating, emotional shutdown, hostility) have a planned response.
- [ ] Dignified and respectful tone without diluting clarity.
Expected deliverable: rehearsable conversation script (opening, delivery, listening, reframe, closing) + three-reaction management kit + list of trap phrases with alternatives + 30-day follow-up plan with verifiable milestones.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_separar_desempe:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Name or alias and current role of the person to evaluate
- RESULTADOS_PERIODO: {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} > Verifiable goals, metrics, and milestones for the current period
- COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS: {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}} > Observed behaviors: learning, aspiration, handling ambiguity, influence
- ROL_OBJETIVO: {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} > Higher role or level the person could aspire to
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Potential evaluation window, e.g. 12-24 months (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to calibrate a team member before a people committee. The costliest error in performance evaluation is collapsing two distinct questions into a single score: "what was delivered" (performance, a verifiable backward look) and "how far they can go" (potential, a forward-looking bet). Conflating them causes two classic failures: promoting a high performer with no runway until they reach their level of incompetence, and discarding a high-potential person because of a weak period. Two biases amplify the error: recency (over-weighting the last event) and halo (letting one axis contaminate the other). Separating both axes with evidence unlocks defensible promotion, development, and retention decisions.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with fifteen years calibrating talent in people committees, expert in the nine-box talent matrix (9-box: performance x potential).

Deliverable: a calibration card for a team member with a separate classification per axis, placement in the matrix, and a differentiated action plan. Guiding principle: one period is not a destiny, and a strong period does not prove potential; data overrules impressions. Steps:
1. Evaluate CURRENT PERFORMANCE using only facts from the period (goals met or not, quality, consistency, measurable impact). Classify as low / solid / outstanding with at least two concrete pieces of evidence per assigned level.
2. Evaluate POTENTIAL using prospective signals distinct from the period's result: agile learning, aspiration and ambition, handling of ambiguity and growing complexity, influence beyond the role. Classify as low / medium / high against ROL_OBJETIVO. Mark every inference not supported by an observed behavior with [SUPUESTO].
3. Declare a confidence level (high / medium / low) per axis based on evidence sufficiency; if insufficient to classify, say so instead of forcing the score.
4. Place the person in the 9-box matrix (performance x potential) and name the cell.
5. Explain the typical risk of misreading that quadrant (over-promotion, abandoning potential, over-investing in a stagnant performer) and flag if recency or halo bias may have skewed your reading.
6. Deliver 3 differentiated development or management actions appropriate to the cell, each with an owner and a timeline.
7. Close with a calibration question the leader must be able to answer with data before the committee.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Input verification: if RESULTADOS_PERIODO, COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS, or ROL_OBJETIVO is missing, ask for it before classifying; do not invent evidence or fill gaps with impressions.
Phase 1 - Performance axis: tabulate facts from the period, assign level, cite evidence, set confidence.
Phase 2 - Potential axis: tabulate prospective signals, assign level, separate fact from inference with [SUPUESTO], set confidence. Do not reuse a performance data point as a potential signal without justification.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: place in matrix, name cell, expose misreading risk, audit recency and halo biases, derive 3 differentiated actions with owner and timeline.
Phase 4 - Calibration: formulate the closing question answerable with data.
Edge case: if the period was atypical (role change, leave, reorganization), note it as an explicit mitigating factor before assigning the performance score.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Both axes were evaluated separately, without the period's result contaminating the potential reading.
- [ ] Each assigned level has at least two concrete pieces of evidence from the period or observed behaviors.
- [ ] Every inference without an observed behavior is marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invented evidence.
- [ ] Each axis declares a confidence level; low confidence is named instead of forcing the score.
- [ ] The 9-box cell is named and its misreading risk explained, with recency and halo audit.
- [ ] The 3 actions are differentiated, consistent with the cell, and each has an owner and a timeline.
- [ ] The calibration question is answerable with data, not with opinion.
Expected deliverable: calibration card ready for the people committee, with axis classification, confidence level per axis, named cell, risk, 3 actions with owner and timeline, and a closing question.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_documentar_evid:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team size and composition (number of people, roles, seniority, location/remote)
- CICLO_EVALUACION: {{CICLO_EVALUACION}} > Cycle length and dates (semi-annual, annual, target evaluation date) and whether there is a cross-leader calibration
- COMPETENCIAS_OBJETIVOS: {{COMPETENCIAS_OBJETIVOS}} > Competencies, values, or objectives being evaluated (rubric or levels if they exist)
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > Available tools for recording (notes, spreadsheet, HR system, task manager, messaging)
- CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Realistic time and frequency the leader can dedicate to recording
- FUENTES_ADICIONALES: {{FUENTES_ADICIONALES}} > Whether collaborators, peers, or internal clients will contribute their own evidence (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Performance evaluations typically fail because of a memory problem, not a criteria problem: the leader remembers the last few weeks clearly and forgets achievements and incidents from the rest of the cycle (recency bias), which produces conversations that feel unfair and hard to defend. The purpose is to build the continuous capture infrastructure that documents observable, dated facts throughout the entire cycle so that by the time the evaluation arrives, the conversation rests on traceable evidence. This unlocks fair and defensible evaluations, specific real-time feedback, and promotion or calibration decisions grounded in facts. Limit: the system captures evidence; it does not replace the conversation or the leader's judgment.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader and people manager, expert in performance management and evidence-based evaluations.
Deliverable: a continuous evidence capture system consisting of (1) an evidence log template with defined fields and a completed example, (2) a sustainable recording cadence, and (3) the structure of a per-person evidence dossier for the evaluation conversation. NOT an annual evaluation form or an individual improvement plan.
Steps:
1. Define what constitutes useful evidence: an observable, dated fact — not a judgment or a personality label. Include the contrast of a poor entry vs. a good entry.
2. Deliver the log template in STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with fields: date, person, situation, observed behavior, impact, linked competency or objective, source, link, and data confidence level. Include a fully completed example row.
3. Propose the capture cadence: a brief periodic routine plus immediate recording of significant events, with concrete triggers.
4. Define how to incorporate and cross-reference multiple sources (collaborator self-evidence, peers, internal clients), separating data from interpretation and recording both versions when they diverge.
5. Explain how to synthesize the log into a per-person dossier, grouped by competency or objective, with a trend signal and a gap check (competencies without evidence or under-recorded people).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Record design: set the useful-evidence criterion (observable, dated, attributable) and produce the STAR log template with an example.
Phase 2 - Capture cadence: design the sustainable routine based on the declared time, with triggers that balance achievements and incidents to avoid both recency bias and negativity bias; include an anti-pattern to avoid (recording only when something goes wrong).
Phase 3 - Multiple sources: integrate self-evidence and peer and internal-client feedback, with rules for cross-referencing versions and separating the observable from the interpreted; privacy note on what is recorded and how it is communicated to the team.
Phase 4 - Synthesis for the evaluation: convert the accumulated evidence into a per-person dossier, grouped by competency or objective, with visible trend and gap coverage.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every log entry is an observable, dated fact — never a personality judgment; the poor vs. good entry contrast is present.
- The template uses STAR format, includes a data confidence level, and links each piece of evidence to an evaluable competency or objective; a fully completed example row is included.
- The cadence is sustainable for the time declared in CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE and balances positive and improvement evidence (mitigates recency and negativity bias); the anti-pattern to avoid is declared.
- Multiple sources are integrated with an explicit rule for separating data from interpretation and for recording divergent versions.
- The final dossier is grouped by competency or objective, shows a trend across the cycle, and includes a gap check.
- Assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO]; no team or cycle data is invented; if an essential piece of information is missing it is requested before executing.
- Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no invented figures.
Expected deliverable: log template with fields and a completed example, recording cadence with triggers and anti-pattern, and per-person evidence dossier structure — all actionable starting next week.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_promocion_caso:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Name or identifier of the person to promote and a summary of their role
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Level or title they currently hold
- NIVEL_OBJETIVO: {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} > Level or title they are nominated for
- RUBRICA_NIVEL_OBJETIVO: {{RUBRICA_NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} > Formal competencies and expectations of the target level (if no formal rubric exists, indicate this and they will be inferred from the role marked [SUPUESTO])
- LOGROS_CON_METRICAS: {{LOGROS_CON_METRICAS}} > Achievements with measurable result, impact scope, and period
- FEEDBACK_STAKEHOLDERS: {{FEEDBACK_STAKEHOLDERS}} > Feedback from peers, internal clients, and leaders, including any known detractor (optional)
- TIEMPO_EN_ROL: {{TIEMPO_EN_ROL}} > Time in current role and in the organization (optional)
- PAR_DE_REFERENCIA: {{PAR_DE_REFERENCIA}} > Peer already at the target level for equity comparison, or "No reference" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to take the promotion case for a team member to the calibration committee. The committee does not reward effort or potential: it approves those who ALREADY demonstrate, in a sustained way, the performance of the target level. A dossier built on impact evidence and with objections anticipated unlocks a fast and defensible decision, reduces evaluator bias, and protects process equity. A dossier based on opinions collapses at the first hard question. The risk to avoid is twofold: overselling a weak case (costs credibility before the committee) or underselling a solid one (unfairly stalls the person).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior HR Business Partner, specialist in talent management, level rubrics, and calibration committee facilitation.
Deliver a promotion dossier with these six sections, in this order:
1. One-sentence thesis: why the team member ALREADY operates at the target level — not why they would get there.
2. Rubric mapping against the target level: one row per expected competency with concrete evidence (project, measurable result, impact scope, period). Mark as BRECHA every competency without solid evidence, and as [SUPUESTO] every inference not backed by a provided fact.
3. Level differential: three to five examples showing scope, autonomy, or influence belonging to the higher level and not the current one; explicitly name what current-level behavior has been surpassed.
4. Objection anticipation: table of likely committee objection + evidence-based response. Cover at least: time in role, lack of cross-area visibility, a detractor, comparison with a peer, and performance sustainability (one stellar quarter is not a pattern).
5. Gap-closure plan: if the committee asks to wait a cycle, verifiable milestones with dates and a success signal for each real gap.
6. Case readiness verdict: READY FOR COMMITTEE / READY WITH MINOR GAPS / NOT READY, with one line justifying it based on how many competencies are demonstrated vs. in gap.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate who is being promoted, from and to which level, and what evidence is available.
Phase 2 - Data gap: identify what is missing (rubric, achievements with metrics, feedback, time in role, reference peer) and ask for it. Do not invent figures, achievements, or feedback; anything not provided is marked [SUPUESTO] or as a gap.
Phase 3 - Mapping: cross each target-level competency against the evidence; separate the demonstrated from the aspirational and from what is merely repeated from the current level.
Phase 4 - Argumentation: draft the thesis, differential, and objection responses always anchored in facts, not opinion; if the core evidence does not sustain the thesis, say so plainly.
Phase 5 - Plan and verdict: define verifiable milestones only for real gaps and issue the readiness verdict.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The thesis states ALREADY demonstrated performance at the target level, not future potential.
- [ ] Every competency in the rubric has evidence with metrics and period, or is marked BRECHA.
- [ ] The level differential distinguishes scope/autonomy/influence of the higher level from the current one and names what has been surpassed.
- [ ] Every likely objection has a response grounded in provided evidence, not opinion; time in role, cross-area visibility, a detractor, peer comparison, and sustainability are covered.
- [ ] No figure, achievement, or feedback was invented; missing items are marked [SUPUESTO] or as a gap.
- [ ] The gap-closure plan has verifiable milestones with dates and a success signal.
- [ ] The readiness verdict is consistent with the ratio of demonstrated vs. gap competencies.
Expected deliverable: promotion dossier in six sections, ready to present to the calibration committee, with rubric mapping and objection tables, and an explicit readiness verdict.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_decision_desvin:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_O_ROL_PERSONA: {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_PERSONA}} > Person to be terminated, by role or internal name (e.g. "junior analyst on the data team")
- BRECHA_DESEMPENO: {{BRECHA_DESEMPENO}} > What was expected vs. what was observed, with concrete examples, metrics, and period
- HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP: {{HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP}} > Prior feedback given, improvement plan applied, deadlines and outcomes (or "no formal plan")
- MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL: {{MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL}} > Country/jurisdiction, contract type, tenure, and known restrictions (to be validated by an expert)
- COMPOSICION_EQUIPO: {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} > Team size, closeness to the person, and workload the team absorbs
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader must decide and execute a performance-based termination. The risk is not only legal: a poorly prepared exit humiliates the person, fractures the team's trust, and leaves the leader exposed. A well-prepared exit protects the dignity of the departing person, the morale of those who stay, and the legitimacy of the decision. This prompt turns one of the most difficult conversations in leadership into a defensible, humane, and clear process: decision tested, conversation scripted, team cared for. It does not replace legal counsel or the organization's internal policy.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with experience in performance evaluation, due process, and conducting exit conversations; combines human management judgment with legal-emotional sensitivity, without substituting formal legal counsel.
Deliver three blocks in this order:
1. DECISION PROOF. Evaluate the strength of the departure against four pillars: clearly communicated expectations, documented feedback, real opportunity to improve with deadlines, and consistency against comparable cases. For each pillar: status (solid / weak / absent), supporting evidence, and what is missing. Close with a readiness verdict: READY TO EXECUTE / CLOSE GAPS FIRST / HALT, with the minimum actions that would change the verdict. Mark every inferred gap with [SUPUESTO] and declare what must be closed before proceeding.
2. CLOSING CONVERSATION SCRIPT. Logistics first (who conducts it, when, where, HR or witness presence, bounded duration). Then the script: direct opening without preamble; core message in clear, non-humiliating language; supporting facts; practical terms (effective date, function handover, access removal, support); dignity protection and respectful close. Append prepared responses for five reactions: denial, anger, emotional breakdown, negotiation ("give me another chance"), and silence.
3. TEAM MESSAGE. What to communicate and what to withhold for confidentiality; how to name the departure without exposing the person; how to contain the anxiety of those remaining; how to redistribute work in a transparent and explicitly temporary way, with a review checkpoint.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm jurisdiction, tenure, history, and team composition; if {{MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL}} or {{HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP}} are incomplete, ask for them before drafting and warn that legal validation is the responsibility of an expert.
Phase 2 - Proof: apply the four due-process pillars, back each status with evidence, issue the readiness verdict, and flag fragilities with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 - Script: draft the logistics, script, and responses to the five reactions; tone: firm, brief, no euphemisms that confuse, no judgments that humiliate; no promises you cannot keep.
Phase 4 - Team: define the message, the confidentiality line, and the temporary redistribution with a review checkpoint.
Edge cases: if the proof yields HALT, propose the remediation path (formal PIP) first rather than the exit. If there are signals of retaliation, discrimination, medical leave, pregnancy, or protected status, stop and refer to a legal/HR expert. Do not invent policies, labor regulations, or case facts; any decisive data point not provided is either requested or marked [SUPUESTO].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four due-process pillars evaluated with status, evidence, and explicit gaps.
- [ ] Readiness verdict issued (ready / close gaps / halt) with actions that would change it.
- [ ] Every assumption marked [SUPUESTO]; no case facts, policies, or regulations invented.
- [ ] Script with logistics, direct opening, non-humiliating core message, facts, practical terms, and dignified close.
- [ ] Prepared responses for denial, anger, emotional breakdown, negotiation, and silence.
- [ ] Team message separates the communicable from the confidential and resolves the temporary redistribution with a review checkpoint.
- [ ] Reminder to validate legal aspects with an expert and signals that require stopping (protected status, medical leave, retaliation).
- [ ] Tone professional, direct, no empty euphemisms, no moral judgments.
Expected deliverable: operational document in three blocks (decision proof + conversation script + team communication plan) ready for the leader to use when preparing and conducting the termination.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_compensacion_co:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Person receiving the communication and their context: role, tenure, level/band, recent relationship with their performance, and flight risk if applicable
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The exact compensation decision to communicate: salary adjustment (amount or percentage), bonus, or no raise this cycle; include effective date if applicable
- DESEMPENO: {{DESEMPENO}} > Concrete achievements and behaviors from the period that support the decision (verifiable facts, not impressions); note gaps if any
- MERCADO_POLITICA: {{MERCADO_POLITICA}} > Where the compensation falls against the market or internal band and what policy/budget rule applies this cycle (optional; anything missing is marked [SUPUESTO], never invented)
- PROXIMOS_PASOS: {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} > What can and cannot be offered going forward: dated reviews, measurable criteria, development actions, budget or policy limits
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The leader must communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} the decision {{DECISION}}, and needs the conversation to sustain motivation and trust rather than erode them. The purpose is to turn a sensitive piece of news into an honest and defensible message: a well-communicated compensation decision explicitly connects pay with real performance, with the market, and with policy, and leaves the person with clarity about where they stand and what depends on them. What this unlocks is retention through trust (not through avoided surprise), a relationship that holds even through a "no" this cycle, and a leader protected from the empty-promise trap that comes due in the next cycle. What is at stake if done poorly: a key person leaving without warning, a broken equity precedent that contaminates the team, or a verbal commitment that becomes an enforceable debt. MetodologIA brings the rigor of anchoring an emotional conversation in verifiable evidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader, expert in Total Rewards philosophy, pay-for-performance models, salary bands and pay equity, and conducting difficult compensation conversations.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate the decision in one sentence: "Communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} that {{DECISION}}, because [reason anchored in performance / market / policy]".
2. Classify the case into one scenario: (a) positive adjustment, (b) adjustment smaller than expected or none despite strong performance, (c) no adjustment due to insufficient performance or budget/policy constraint; adapt tone and order to the scenario and declare which scenario you chose and why.
3. Build the message on three separate anchors drawn from {{DESEMPENO}} and {{MERCADO_POLITICA}}: PERFORMANCE (facts from the period), MARKET (position against a reference or band), POLICY/BUDGET (cycle rule); explicitly distinguish what depends on the person from what does not. Mark [SUPUESTO] every figure, percentile, or rule not provided; do not invent data.
4. Draft the conversation script: opening with the decision in the first sentences, the rationale across the three anchors, explicit space for reaction and questions (with a suggested open question), close with next steps. Use direct language, no euphemisms that dilute the message.
5. From {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}, separate verifiable commitments (dated review, measurable criteria, development actions) from empty promises to avoid; rewrite every fragile promise as a conditional, measurable commitment (format: if [observable condition] by [date], then [concrete action]).
6. Anticipate 3 to 5 likely objections or reactions (include at least: comparison with a peer, resignation threat, request to revisit the decision now) with a brief, empathetic, and firm response for each that does not cede indefensible ground or breach third-party confidentiality.
7. Close with a preparation checklist for the leader: data to have on hand, what NOT to say (including comparisons with teammates and promises without backing), how to document the conversation, and who to escalate to if there is an equity/legal signal.
Stop signal: if the decision appears to violate internal equity, contradict current policy, or touch legal or confidentiality ground, declare it before proceeding and recommend validating with HR/legal.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix the decision in one sentence and validate that the person, the exact decision, the period's performance, and a market/policy reference are present; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing and do not invent figures or rules.
Phase 2 - Classification: place the case in one of the three scenarios and derive tone and message order from that (in (a) recognition precedes the amount; in (b) and (c) the decision comes first and context follows, without preamble).
Phase 3 - Triple anchor: draft performance, market, and policy separately, declaring what the person controls and what they do not, and marking [SUPUESTO] everything unverified.
Phase 4 - Script: structure the direct opening, the rationale, the listening space, and the close, using language that does not dilute the message.
Phase 5 - Next steps and robustness: convert fragile promises into conditional, measurable commitments, anticipate objections, run the equity/legal check, and assemble the preparation checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The decision was restated in one sentence with its primary reason before drafting the script.
- The case is classified into one of the three scenarios, with justification, and tone and order adapt to it.
- The message explicitly separates the three anchors: performance (facts), market (position), and policy/budget (rule), and distinguishes the controllable from the uncontrollable.
- Every market figure, percentile, or policy rule not provided is marked [SUPUESTO]; no data was invented.
- The script opens with the decision in the first sentences, includes space for reaction with at least one open question, and uses no euphemisms that dilute the message.
- Next steps distinguish verifiable commitments from empty promises; every fragile promise was rewritten as a conditional, measurable commitment.
- There are 3 to 5 anticipated objections, each with an empathetic and firm response that does not cede indefensible ground or breach third-party confidentiality.
- The preparation checklist includes data to have on hand, what NOT to say, how to document, and who to escalate to.
- If there was an equity, policy, or legal signal, it was declared as a stop before proceeding.
Expected deliverable: compensation conversation script by scenario + triple anchor (performance/market/policy) + verifiable next steps, bank of 3 to 5 objections, and preparation checklist, in neutral, professional English, warm and direct tone, no empty promises.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_feedback_contin:
