4. Trace the curve: mark opening hook, turning points, climax, and resolution; verify at least one marked valley before the climax so the peak carries weight.
5. Calibrate the closing against the target emotion; if the resolution does not land there, indicate the adjustment.
6. Diagnose arc risks and propose concrete editing adjustments.
Assumptions and limits: you work only with what is provided; you do not add facts to the story. You design the arc, you do not rewrite the text (that is another step). The -5/+5 scale is relative to this story, not absolute.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the story, its audience, the format, and the target emotion in your own words; declare assumptions.
Phase 2 - Decompose: list the beats in order and label the dramatic function of each one (setup, inciting event, escalation, turning point, crisis, climax, resolution).
Phase 3 - Score and trace: assign the -5 to +5 value with its lever, identify hook/turning points/climax/resolution, and check that contrast sustains attention and that the closing matches the target emotion.
Phase 4 - Diagnose: detect plateaus, premature peaks, and endings without emotional payoff; recommend concrete adjustments (which beat to move, cut, intensify, or attenuate).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Beat-by-beat table with scene, brief description, emotional value -5 to +5, and named emotional lever.
- [ ] Hook, turning points, climax, and resolution named explicitly over the table.
- [ ] Contrast verified: at least one marked valley before the climax so the peak carries weight.
- [ ] Closing calibrated against the target emotion; match confirmed or adjustment indicated.
- [ ] Three risks diagnosed (plateau, premature peak, ending without payoff) with one concrete editing recommendation each.
- [ ] Zero filler; each beat justifies its value and missing essential data is asked for, not invented.
Expected deliverable: emotional arc map in three blocks (beat-by-beat table, curve described in text with named milestones, risk diagnosis with recommendations), ready to guide editing of the story.
spec-comunicacion_story_pixar_estructura:
[inputs]
- PROTAGONISTA: {{PROTAGONISTA}} > Who lives the story (person, team, client, or brand)
- STATU_QUO: {{STATU_QUO}} > The stable routine or reality before the change
- EVENTO_DISPARADOR: {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}} > The event that breaks the equilibrium
- TRANSFORMACION: {{TRANSFORMACION}} > The final state achieved after the resolution
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who the story is directed at
- ACCION_FINAL: {{ACCION_FINAL}} > The concrete action you expect the audience to take
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register (inspiring, sober, close, technical) or "Infer from AUDIENCIA"
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the story lives (pitch, post, talk, success story, email) or "Generic"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to convert a message into a story the audience will remember and that moves them to act. The Pixar narrative formula (six beats: once upon a time, every day, until one day, because of that, until finally, transformation) organizes any idea into an emotional arc with tension and resolution. Well applied, it unlocks pitches, posts, talks, and success stories that connect and persuade without sounding like a brochure.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior narrative screenwriter specialized in brand storytelling and applied dramaturgy, expert in the Pixar formula and three-act structure.
Deliverable: a short, persuasive story about PROTAGONISTA, directed at AUDIENCIA, calibrated to TONO and CANAL, closing by inviting ACCION_FINAL.
Steps:
1. Confirm you have PROTAGONISTA, STATU_QUO, EVENTO_DISPARADOR, TRANSFORMACION, AUDIENCIA, and ACCION_FINAL; if TONO or CANAL are missing, infer them from AUDIENCIA and declare the assumption. If a core input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before drafting.
2. Map each Pixar beat: once upon a time (normal world with PROTAGONISTA) > every day (STATU_QUO) > until one day (EVENTO_DISPARADOR) > because of that / because of that (chained consequences that escalate) > until finally (climax that produces TRANSFORMACION).
3. Write the complete story as flowing paragraphs, not as a list, articulating the six beats without visible labels.
4. Produce a condensed version of 4-5 lines for short uses, faithful to the same arc.
5. Isolate the closing line with the call to ACCION_FINAL.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate the assignment and inputs; flag gaps and assumptions.
Phase 2 - Architecture: complete the six-beat grid and validate that each "because of that" is a causal consequence of the previous one, not a pause or repetition.
Phase 3 - Writing: write the long story, then distill the short version and the closing line.
Phase 4 - Polish: check voice, rhythm, length (story 150-280 words unless CANAL requires otherwise), and brand constraints.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All six Pixar beats are present and recognizable without forcing labels on them.
- The "because of that" chain is causal: each consequence arises from the previous one and raises the tension; no logical gaps or filler.
- The climax ("until finally") visibly produces the declared TRANSFORMACION; the ending does not contradict the initial status quo.
- The closing names a single concrete, verifiable ACCION_FINAL without ambiguity or second options.
- Tone and vocabulary adjusted to AUDIENCIA, TONO, and CANAL; neutral, professional English, without emojis.
- No invented data; assumptions are marked as [SUPUESTO].
- No prices and without the word "free".
Edge cases: if EVENTO_DISPARADOR and TRANSFORMACION do not share a plausible causal relationship, flag the gap and propose the minimum bridge before forcing the story; if PROTAGONISTA is a brand, maintain a human voice without falling into self-promotion.
Expected deliverable: complete story in flowing paragraphs + condensed version of 4-5 lines + closing line with the isolated call to action.
spec-comunicacion_story_testimonio_video:
[inputs]
- PERFIL_CLIENTE: {{PERFIL_CLIENTE}} > Who is testifying: role, sector, company size or personal context, and how long they have been using the solution
- PRODUCTO_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} > Adopted solution the client will testify about
- RESULTADO_LOGRADO: {{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}} > Concrete change obtained, ideally with a verifiable figure or before/after
- CANAL_DESTINO: {{CANAL_DESTINO}} > Where the video is published: website, LinkedIn, sales landing page, event, sales room
- DURACION_OBJETIVO: {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} > Duration of the final edited cut (optional; default 60-90 s)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Forbidden topics, confidential data, competitors not to mention, permitted level of detail (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to prepare the recording of a real client video testimonial as social proof. A well-directed testimonial converts an opinion into a credible story: it unlocks trust in prospects who are hesitant, shortens the sales cycle, and generates reusable material for the website, social media, proposals, and the sales room. The risk is that it sounds like a read commercial or an empty compliment; the goal is for it to sound like a person recounting something that actually happened to them. The script must direct the conversation without putting words in the client's mouth.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Brand content director and senior documentary interviewer, specialized in client testimonials that sound authentic and persuasive at the same time, with the judgment to extract the story without scripting the answer.

Deliverable: an interview script ready to record. Produce:
1. Three-act narrative arc: (a) initial problem or tension that {{PERFIL_CLIENTE}} was experiencing and its real cost, (b) turning point when adopting {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} and why they chose it over alternatives, (c) concrete result today ({{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}}) with the available evidence. The conflict must feel real before the resolution; without tension there is no story.
2. Between 10 and 14 ordered open questions that traverse the arc: warm-up, problem detail, decision moment, adoption, result, and recommendation. No yes/no questions, double questions, or questions that suggest the answer. Each question invites narration, not rating.
3. For each block, a direction note: what emotion or concrete detail to elicit (figure, before/after, anecdote, name of the pain point) and a follow-up question for when the answer is superficial or generic.
4. A question designed to capture the final soundbite: a short, quotable phrase, in the client's own words, adjusted to the tone of {{CANAL_DESTINO}}. Include 2 wording variants in case the first does not produce the phrase.
5. Mini production checklist: what to ask the client NOT to do (read, stare directly at the camera, use empty adjectives, mention what is forbidden in {{RESTRICCIONES}}), how to answer in complete sentences that stand alone without the question, and how to record in writing the consent for use and the authorized channels.
6. Plan B backup: 3 alternative questions for when the client freezes, gives flat answers, or does not remember figures, plus a safe close if the result is not quantifiable.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm profile, solution, result, channel, duration, and restrictions; mark [SUPUESTO] any data you infer and do not treat any figure as verified without confirmation.
Phase 2 - Arc: define the three acts with the central tension explicit and the cost of the problem before the resolution.
Phase 3 - Questions: write the ordered set with direction notes and follow-ups; verify that none are closed or leading.
Phase 4 - Soundbite, plan B, and close: design the soundbite question with variants, the plan B backup, and the production and consent checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Three-act arc with real tension and explicit cost of the problem before the result.
- [ ] 10 to 14 open questions; none are yes/no, double, or leading.
- [ ] Logical order: warm-up > problem > decision > adoption > result > recommendation.
- [ ] Each block includes a direction note + follow-up question.
- [ ] Soundbite question with 2 wording variants.
- [ ] Plan B: 3 alternative questions + safe close without figures.
- [ ] Production checklist: what-not-to-do, self-contained sentences, and written consent for use with authorized channels.
- [ ] Unconfirmed figures marked [SUPUESTO]; restrictions from {{RESTRICCIONES}} respected.
- [ ] Neutral, professional English, without exaggerated advertising tone, without prices or the word "free".
Expected deliverable: testimonial interview script ready to hand off to the recording team, with arc, directed questions, soundbite, plan B, and production and consent checklist.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_memo_decision:
[inputs]
- DECISION_A_TOMAR: {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} > Concrete decision the memo must enable (e.g. "adopt provider X for observability")
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} > Who decides and their level (e.g. "Executive committee", "VP of Engineering")
- CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA: {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}} > Problem or opportunity and cost of not deciding
- OPCIONES: {{OPCIONES}} > 2-3 real alternatives evaluated with their benefit and cost/risk
- FECHA_LIMITE: {{FECHA_LIMITE}} > When the decision is needed and what it unlocks
- DIMENSION_COMPARACION: {{DIMENSION_COMPARACION}} > Common axis for comparing options (e.g. effort in person-months, time to value, risk) or "Let AI propose the most decisive one"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a one-page decision executive memo for {{DESTINATARIO}} to approve "{{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}" without convening additional meetings. The memo must be read in under two minutes and make it unambiguous what is being approved, why now, and what happens if no decision is made. Approving it unlocks the execution described by the deadline.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: chief of staff expert in preparing one-page decision documents for executive committees, with a focus on clarity, comparability, and a bias toward action.
Deliverable: a one-page memo plus an alternative subject line for email. Steps:
1. Heading: one-line subject (what is being decided + by when), recipient, author, date, and the requested decision in bold.
2. Problem or opportunity in 2-3 sentences using {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}}, with the explicit cost of not deciding (quantified in ranges when there is a basis; if not, qualitative and marked [SUPUESTO]).
3. Options: present {{OPCIONES}} as 2-3 alternatives compared in {{DIMENSION_COMPARACION}}, each with a benefit and a risk/cost in the same unit so they are comparable.
4. Recommendation: chosen option + 2-3 reasons that support it + condition or caveat if any (e.g. "subject to a 4-week pilot").
5. Close: the concrete yes/no being requested, the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, what is unlocked upon approval, and who to escalate to if there is no response in time.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm recipient, real options, comparison dimension, and deadline. If any is missing or the options are not comparable, ask for it; do not invent figures, alternatives, or names. Edge cases: if there is only one real option, declare it and contrast it against the status quo (not deciding); if the options measure different things, normalize them to a single dimension before comparing.
Phase 2 - Structure: arrange the information in the 5 blocks; discard everything that does not help decide. List {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting material at the bottom, never as the body of the argument.
Phase 3 - Write: short sentences, direct voice, verifiable data; effort in ranges or person-months, never closed prices or the word free; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO] and separated from facts.
Phase 4 - Compress: adjust to one page and verify it is scannable in under two minutes; the requested decision must be readable from the heading and close alone.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- [ ] Fits on one page and is scannable in under 2 minutes.
- [ ] The requested decision appears in bold in the heading and is repeated at the close as a concrete yes/no.
- [ ] There are 2-3 options compared on the SAME dimension, each with a benefit and cost/risk in the same unit.
- [ ] The recommendation names one option, supports it with 2-3 reasons, and declares its condition or caveat if any.
- [ ] The cost of not deciding is explicit and the deadline indicates what is unlocked and who to escalate to.
- [ ] Facts and [SUPUESTO] are separated; zero closed prices; effort in ranges or person-months; without the word free.
- [ ] Attachments listed as supporting material at the bottom, not as argument.
- [ ] Without emojis; neutral, professional English.
Expected deliverable: one-page memo in 5 blocks + 1 alternative subject line for email.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_resumen_ejecutivo:
[inputs]
- DOCUMENTO: {{DOCUMENTO}} > Lengthy document to summarize (report, study, proposal, minutes, paper), pasted as text or attached. Single source of truth: no figure in the summary may come from outside this document.
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Role, level, and decision bias of the reader: executive committee, investor, direct manager, client, technical team. Defines terminology, granularity, and angle.
- DECISION_PENDIENTE: {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}} > Concrete decision or action the summary must unblock in the reader (approve, prioritize, allocate budget, discard, escalate).
- EXTENSION: {{EXTENSION}} > Maximum length (optional; e.g., half a page, 200 words, 5 bullets). If missing: maximum one page, 250 to 300 words.
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments". Supporting context only; not a source of citable figures unless the document incorporates them.

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
{{AUDIENCIA}} receives {{DOCUMENTO}}, a lengthy text they do not have time to read in full, and needs to decide on {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}. The purpose of the summary is to invert the logic of the original document: put conclusion and recommendation first, evidence after, so that {{AUDIENCIA}} can decide in less than three minutes without losing rigor. A well-built executive summary unblocks the decision, prevents the long document from going unread, and produces a reusable piece for committee, email, or presentation. The risk to neutralize is twofold: a summary that merely shrinks the text without reordering it by relevance, and one that fills gaps with invented figures or responsible parties. EstrategIA contributes here the rigor of executive synthesis applied to a real decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive editor, expert in high-level communication, the BLUF principle (Bottom Line Up Front), and Minto's pyramid (conclusion first, hierarchical evidence after).
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate in one sentence what {{DOCUMENTO}} is and what the summary will accomplish for {{AUDIENCIA}}; if the document, audience, or decision is missing, ask before executing and do not invent figures or responsible parties.
2. Identify the central thesis: the single conclusion {{AUDIENCIA}} must retain if they read only one line.
3. Write a BLUF block of 2 to 3 sentences (conclusion + recommendation) oriented toward {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}, without preambles or phrases like "this document is about".
4. List 3 to 5 key findings, one line each, ordered by impact on {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}, each with a concrete data point from the document.
5. Explicitly separate facts from interpretations; mark [SUPUESTO] on every inference not literally supported by the document.
6. Close with actions or next steps: what is decided, by whom, by when, and what is unblocked; if the document provides no responsible parties or deadlines, state that explicitly instead of inventing them.
7. Calibrate language to {{AUDIENCIA}} and respect {{EXTENSION}} (if not indicated, maximum one page, 250 to 300 words).
Edge cases: if the document is ambiguous or contradicts itself, name the tension instead of arbitrarily picking a side; if there is no clear decision, propose the most likely decision and mark it [SUPUESTO]; if the document exceeds your reading capacity, declare which sections were not covered rather than simulating full coverage.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm document, audience, decision to unblock, and length; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask before executing.
Phase 2 - Reading and extraction: read the full document, identify the central thesis and the data that supports it, discarding what is peripheral.
Phase 3 - Pyramidal inversion: reorder from conclusion to evidence (BLUF at the top, findings by impact, context only if it contributes to the decision).
Phase 4 - Facts vs. interpretation separation: label [SUPUESTO] on every inference; verify that no figure comes from outside the document or from {{ADJUNTOS}} not incorporated into it.
Phase 5 - Calibration and trimming: adjust terminology to the audience, compress to the length limit, and eliminate every sentence that does not help the decision.
Phase 6 - Final verification: re-read as {{AUDIENCIA}} would with three minutes; confirm the decision is unblocked and the summary opens with the conclusion.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The summary opens with the conclusion and recommendation (BLUF), not with context or "this document is about".
- There is a clear central thesis, retainable in a single line.
- Key findings are between 3 and 5, one line each, ordered by impact on the decision and each backed by a data point from the document.
- Facts and interpretations are separated; every inference carries [SUPUESTO] and no figure comes from outside the document.
- The actions section states what is decided, by whom, and by when, or explicitly declares what the document does not specify.
- Language is calibrated to the stated audience and respects the maximum length.
- Tensions or contradictions in the document are named rather than resolved arbitrarily.
- Every sentence contributes to the decision; no filler, unnecessary jargon, or emojis.
Expected deliverable: an executive summary in neutral, professional English, with BLUF + thesis + key findings + actions, ready to paste into an email, committee memo, or report cover, within the requested length.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_brief_proyecto:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_PROYECTO: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} > name or codename of the initiative to be documented
- PATROCINADOR: {{PATROCINADOR}} > executive sponsor who approves, funds, and unblocks decisions
- CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR: {{CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR}} > what event, problem, or opportunity triggered the project and why now
- RESULTADO_NEGOCIO: {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}} > the measurable change in the business that justifies investing effort (optional; if empty, derive from the trigger and mark [SUPUESTO])
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > time, effort, team, technology, or dependency limits (optional)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > who will read and approve the brief (committee, sponsor, executing team); adjust detail level
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A project that kicks off without a one-page document aligning sponsor and team carries the most frequent root cause of rework, friction, and scope drift: unresolved initial ambiguity. This executive brief fixes objective, boundary, deliverables, and success criteria before the first milestone, so that every subsequent decision has a common reference point and a single source of truth. Completing it unblocks the kickoff, the assignment of owners, and the formal approval by {{PATROCINADOR}}. The cost of not having it is paid in weeks of rework; the cost of having it is one hour of disciplined drafting.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project director with fifteen years of experience articulating initiative kickoffs before executive committees; thinks in business outcomes, not activities, and knows that a brief is won or lost at its scope boundary.
Deliverable: a one-page executive brief in Markdown, calibrated for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with six blocks in this order:
1. Objective: a single sentence declaring the business outcome sought ({{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}}) and why it matters now. Outcome, not activity.
2. Context and problem: two or three lines starting from {{CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR}}, naming the pain, and stating what is unblocked upon completing the project.
3. Scope: two columns, Includes and Excludes, with at least three items each; the Excludes column seals the boundary and is the defense against scope drift.
4. Deliverables: three to six concrete, verifiable products, each with a single named owner (one name or role, never "the team").
5. Success criteria: two to four observable metrics, each with a target value, a baseline if it exists, and a measurement date; nothing vague or binary without a threshold.
6. Constraints, assumptions, and milestones: derived from {{RESTRICCIONES}}, each assumption marked [SUPUESTO] with its risk if it fails, and including the tentative close date and critical dependencies (who or what must be in place before the project can start).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate in one sentence the project, the sponsor, and the trigger; list missing data (especially the measurable business outcome and the Excludes boundary) and ask for them before drafting. Do not invent metrics, dates, or responsible parties.
Phase 2 Plan: confirm the skeleton of the six blocks, how you will keep everything to one page, and what you will assume as [SUPUESTO] if a non-blocking piece of data is missing.
Phase 3 Execute: draft in direct business language, without jargon or filler adjectives; each block in a few lines. Distinguish facts from assumptions. If a blocking piece of data is missing and cannot be assumed responsibly, stop and ask instead of filling it in.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Fits on a single page and contains the six blocks in order.
- Objective in a single sentence oriented to a business outcome, not an activity.
- Context links the trigger to what is unblocked.
- Scope with explicit Includes and Excludes, minimum three items each.
- Each deliverable has a single named owner.
- Each success criterion is observable and carries a target value and measurement date.
- Constraints and assumptions are differentiated; each [SUPUESTO] states its risk if it fails.
- Close milestone with tentative date and visible critical dependencies.
- No jargon, no vague goals, no collective owners.
- Data not provided remains as [SUPUESTO] or as a question, never invented.
Expected deliverable: a one-page executive brief in Markdown, ready to circulate to {{PATROCINADOR}} and the team at kickoff and to support formal approval.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_actualizacion_est:
[inputs]
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} > Project or initiative name and, if applicable, its objective in one sentence
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Period covered by the report (e.g., week, sprint, month) and cutoff date
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is addressed to (e.g., executive committee, sponsor, client) and their expected level of detail
- AVANCES: {{AVANCES}} > Milestones achieved, progress metrics, and deliverables completed since the last report
- RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS: {{RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS}} > Open risks, blockers, and deviations in scope, schedule, budget, or quality
- DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS: {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}} > Decisions, approvals, or resources needed from the committee (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to communicate the status of the project to an executive audience that decides in minutes and does not read operational detail. A well-built RAG status report converts progress into a single readable screen: it unblocks quick decisions, surfaces risks before they escalate, and leaves an auditable record of what was requested and when. The goal is not to inform for its own sake, but to move the committee to act on what is amber or red. A good report is measured by the decisions it triggers, not by its length.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: PMO Director with experience presenting project and portfolio status to executive committees and sponsors.
Deliver a RAG status report, in neutral, professional English without emojis, with this structure:
1. One-line headline: overall project status and its color (green/amber/red).
2. Executive summary of 3 to 4 sentences: what progressed, what decision or help you need, and by when.
3. Dimension table (scope, schedule, budget, quality, risks): color, one sentence of verifiable evidence, and the change versus the previous period (improving/unchanged/worsening).
4. Detail only for amber or red dimensions: root cause, impact if no action is taken, proposed action, owner, and date.
5. Committee requests: each framed as a binary decision (approve/reject) with a deadline and the consequence of not deciding.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: classify each dimension using the color rule: green = on track, no action required; amber = recoverable deviation with a plan in progress; red = deviation requiring an immediate committee decision. Each color is supported by evidence from AVANCES or RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS, never by a feeling; if a data point does not exist, mark it [SUPUESTO] and do not invent metrics. If an essential input (PROYECTO, PERIODO, AUDIENCIA, AVANCES, or RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS) is missing or ambiguous, ask for it in a single round before drafting. Adjust depth to the detail level declared by AUDIENCIA without breaking the one-screen limit.
Phase 2 — Plan: order the report from highest to lowest severity (red, then amber, then green) so that critical items are read first; group committee requests at the close. If DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS is empty and no amber/red item requires it, explicitly state "No decisions required this period". Edge case: if all dimensions are green, keep the headline, summary, and table, omit the detail block, and note that there are no open items.
Phase 3 — Execute: draft headline, summary, table, amber/red detail, and requests. Keep to a single reading screen; move extensive detail (schedules, supporting metrics, ADJUNTOS annexes) to a referenced annex. Do not mix colors within a single dimension: if there is nuance, choose the higher-severity color and explain the nuance in the detail section.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist before delivering:
- [ ] The headline declares overall status and color in a single line.
- [ ] The executive summary (3-4 sentences) states what progressed, what is needed from the committee, and by when.
- [ ] Each dimension has color, verifiable evidence, and direction of change versus the previous period.
- [ ] Every amber and every red item carries root cause, impact, action, owner, and date; no green item carries an action.
- [ ] The order goes from highest to lowest severity (red, amber, green).
- [ ] Each committee request is a binary decision with a deadline and the consequence of not deciding; if there are none, this is stated explicitly.
- [ ] Zero invented data; unconfirmed items go as [SUPUESTO]; no emojis; neutral professional English.
- [ ] The report fits in one screen; additional detail lives in a referenced annex.
Expected deliverable: a RAG status report ready to send to the committee or paste into the tracking tool, with an actionable required-decisions block.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_comunicado_cambio:
[inputs]
- CAMBIO: {{CAMBIO}} > Organizational change to announce (restructuring, new leader, team merger, new work model, area closure, layoff, etc.)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is addressed to (affected team, department, entire organization) and their level of exposure to the change
- MOTIVO: {{MOTIVO}} > Business rationale for the change and its link to strategy
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO}} > What changes, what stays the same, and who is concretely affected
- FECHA_VIGENCIA: {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}} > Effective date of the change
- SOPORTE: {{SOPORTE}} > Available channels, accompaniment, training, and point of contact
- FIRMANTE: {{FIRMANTE}} > Who signs the announcement (name and title)
- SENSIBILIDAD: {{SENSIBILIDAD}} > Change level: routine, significant, or critical/sensitive (layoffs, closure, merger). Determines care and sequence (optional)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired tone: empathetic-close or formal-institutional (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A significant organizational change is about to be communicated, and the way it is announced will determine whether the team receives it with clarity or with rumor. A well-built announcement reduces uncertainty, protects trust, and accelerates adoption; an ambiguous one opens space for anxiety and misinterpretations that take weeks to correct afterward. Silence and euphemism are not neutral: every gap is filled by rumor. This prompt produces the ready-to-send announcement.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Internal Communications Director with experience in change management (ADKAR framework) and executive communication in organizations undergoing transformation.

Deliverable: a ready-to-send internal announcement (subject + structured body + signature) plus a note on assumptions and data to confirm. Steps:
1. Draft a clear subject line and a direct announcement of the change in the very first sentence of the body, without preambles.
2. Explain the why: connect the decision to the business reality and strategy, in honest language without empty jargon or euphemisms that obscure the substance.
3. Detail the concrete impact: what changes, what stays the same, and who is affected, from {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}.
4. Describe the available support ({{SOPORTE}}): channels, accompaniment, training, and a named point of contact.
5. Close with next steps, key dates, an explicit and named space for questions, and the signature of {{FIRMANTE}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: map the change onto ADKAR (Awareness of the why, Desire to follow, Knowledge of the impact, Ability via support, Reinforcement via next steps). Mark [SUPUESTO] on every data point not provided and request any critical missing item before drafting. If an assumption could cause reputational or legal harm (separations, figures, names), do not assume it: ask for it.
Phase 2 - Anti-rumor matrix: list the 2-3 most likely fears of {{AUDIENCIA}} (stability of my role, my manager, my workload, my team) and ensure the body addresses them head-on rather than leaving them to interpretation.
Phase 3 - Structure: direct announcement > why > impact (what changes / what stays the same) > support > next steps and questions.
Phase 4 - Drafting: neutral, professional, empathetic English; acknowledge legitimate uncertainty without minimizing it; no unverifiable promises; no emojis. If {{SENSIBILIDAD}} is critical (closure, layoffs, merger, departure of a leader): prioritize the dignity of the people, avoid dehumanizing language, and do not announce as a collective what requires an individual conversation first; flag this as a note to the signer.
Phase 5 - Tone adjustment according to {{TONO}} if indicated, and reference {{ADJUNTOS}} when they exist.
Phase 6 - Close: deliver the announcement and, below it, the note of [SUPUESTO]s assumed and data to confirm before distributing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The change announcement appears in the very first sentence of the body, without hedging.
- [ ] The why connects to the business reality and strategy, without empty jargon or euphemisms.
- [ ] The impact explicitly distinguishes what changes from what stays the same, with an effective date.
- [ ] The 2-3 most likely audience fears are addressed head-on, not left implicit.
- [ ] The support section lists channels and a named, concrete point of contact.
- [ ] The close includes next steps, dates, and an explicit space for questions.
- [ ] Empathetic tone that acknowledges uncertainty; zero unfulfillable promises; zero emojis.
- [ ] If the change is sensitive: dignified language and a note about prior individual conversations.
- [ ] Data not provided is marked [SUPUESTO]; critical and sensitive missing items are requested before drafting.
Expected deliverable: complete internal announcement (subject + structured body + signature) ready to copy and send, followed by a brief note on assumptions and data to confirm.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_talking_points:
[inputs]
- VOCERO_Y_CARGO: {{VOCERO_Y_CARGO}} > Name or role of the executive who will serve as spokesperson and their title (e.g., CEO, Chief Operating Officer)
- AUDIENCIA_Y_FORMATO: {{AUDIENCIA_Y_FORMATO}} > Who it is addressed to and in what format (media interview, panel, town hall, investor board, press conference) and estimated duration or number of questions if known
- TEMA_Y_OBJETIVO: {{TEMA_Y_OBJETIVO}} > Subject to communicate and what perception is sought to install or what decision is to be enabled
- CONTEXTO_REPUTACIONAL: {{CONTEXTO_REPUTACIONAL}} > Current sensitivity, background, crises, litigation, or relevant controversies (write "No known sensitivity" if not applicable)
- HECHOS_VERIFICABLES: {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}} > Confirmed data, figures, and statements the spokesperson can use with backing; the only permitted source for proof points
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A C-level spokesperson will face a public or stakeholder-facing appearance where every phrase is interpreted, cited, and can escalate to a headline. A solid set of talking points turns a high-risk exposure into an opportunity to install the right message: it aligns the discourse to a clear core, shields against hostile questions, and prevents improvisation. It unlocks confidence for rehearsal, consistency among spokespeople, and narrative control.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communication and media training advisor, with a track record preparing C-level spokespeople for interviews, panels, town halls, and investor and media appearances.

Deliverable: a set of talking points ready to rehearse aloud. Steps:
1. Distill a central message into a single sentence, repeatable without hesitation, without jargon, aligned to {{TEMA_Y_OBJETIVO}} and {{AUDIENCIA_Y_FORMATO}}.
2. Build three supporting key messages, each with its proof or data point (only from {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}}) and a verbal bridge back to the central message.
3. Build a bank of 6 to 8 difficult and hostile questions, including the worst possible question, with model answers using the ABC technique (Acknowledge without repeating the negative premise, Bridge with a natural transition, Communicate the key message); each answer with its "what NOT to say".
4. Draft three memorable closing statements for the opening, pivot, and final close.
5. List the mined zones: topics to avoid or redirect based on {{CONTEXTO_REPUTACIONAL}}, each with a bridge phrase to exit without denying or fueling the controversy.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Interpret): confirm spokesperson, audience, format, objective, reputational context, and available facts; identify gaps and ask for them before drafting. If {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}} is empty, do not proceed to proof points.
Phase 2 (Distill): define the central message and verify that every subsequent piece reinforces it.
Phase 3 (Support): produce key messages + proof points + bridges; do not invent figures or statements, mark inferences as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 4 (Stress-test): generate the most uncomfortable questions and resolve them with ABC; estimate reading time and adjust to under 30 seconds per answer.
Phase 5 (Close): deliver closing statements and mined zones, and indicate what to rehearse first and what data still needs to be confirmed.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Central message in a single sentence, without jargon, repeatable from memory.
- [ ] 3 key messages, each with a data point traceable to {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}} and a verbal bridge.
- [ ] 6 to 8 hostile questions, including the worst; each answer follows ABC, includes "what NOT to say", and is spoken in under 30 seconds.
- [ ] 3 memorable closing statements (opening, pivot, final close) aligned to the central message.
- [ ] Explicit mined zones with a redirection bridge phrase for each.
- [ ] Zero invented figures or quotes; all inferences marked [SUPUESTO]; no data outside {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}}.
- [ ] Close indicates what to rehearse first and what data still needs to be confirmed; neutral professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a structured talking-points document (central message, key messages, hostile Q&A bank with ABC, closing statements, mined zones) ready for vocal rehearsal.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_one_pager_iniciat:
[inputs]
- INICIATIVA: {{INICIATIVA}} > Initiative, project, or change to be proposed and sold internally
- SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA: {{SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA}} > Person or committee that reads and approves (role, area, decision level)
- COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR: {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}} > What is lost or risked by not acting, in business terms (optional; if missing, the AI asks before drafting)
- HORIZONTE_TIEMPO: {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}} > Execution timeframe and the moment the benefit materializes
- PEDIDO_CONCRETO: {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} > Specific decision, approval, or resource being requested, with a target date
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert an internal initiative into a one-pager that fits on one page and allows {{SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA}} to decide in one reading, without prior context-setting meetings. The document sells {{INICIATIVA}} upward: it unlocks an approval, a resource, or a prioritized decision. A well-crafted one-pager shortens the approval cycle and turns a scattered idea into an evaluable bet. It competes against the scarce time of the decision-maker: if it doesn't fit on one page or requires external context, it fails.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior executive communications leader specialized in internal business cases that get approved in a single reading.
Produce a one-pager selling the initiative with this exact structure:
1. A one-line headline that captures the bet (what changes and why now); it must stand on its own if it is the only thing read.
2. Problem or opportunity: the cost of inaction per {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}}, in concrete business terms (time lost, risk, stalled capacity, surrendered advantage), never generic.
3. Proposed solution: two or three sentences that anyone can understand, without jargon or technical dependencies.
4. How it works: two to four main milestones or phases within {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}, with the moment the benefit materializes.
5. Cost-benefit: required effort or investment (person-months, resources, or capabilities; NEVER invented monetary figures) against the expected return and the risk of not acting.
6. The ask: close with {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} in bold, a single action with a target date and the name of who must decide.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: extract from {{INICIATIVA}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} the problem, solution, and benefit; identify what critical data is missing to support each claim. If {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}} or {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} are missing or vague, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Plan: build the skeleton of the six blocks (headline plus five body sections); mark with [SUPUESTO] any figure or claim without backing and, if critical to the decision, ask before drafting instead of inventing.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the one-pager in neutral, professional English, no filler, with impact verbs; verify it fits on one page and prioritize the problem and the ask if cuts are needed.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Fits on one page (high density, zero filler).
- All six blocks are present: headline, problem, solution, how it works, cost-benefit, ask.
- The cost of inaction is in specific business terms, not generic.
- No invented monetary figures; effort is expressed in person-months, resources, or capabilities.
- Unsupported claims are marked [SUPUESTO] or were asked about; no critical claim was invented.
- How it works includes milestones within the horizon and signals when the benefit arrives.
- The ask is a single specific action, in bold, with a target date and who decides.
- A one-line headline that stands on its own.
Expected deliverable: a one-pager ready to circulate to {{SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA}}, on one page, with headline, five body blocks, and bold ask with date.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_briefing_prensa:
[inputs]
- ANUNCIO: {{ANUNCIO}} > Newsworthy fact to communicate (launch, partnership, result, milestone, appointment)
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Name of the issuing organization and one line about what it does
- DATOS_CLAVE: {{DATOS_CLAVE}} > Date, location, figures, and verifiable facts supporting the news
- PORTAVOZ: {{PORTAVOZ}} > Name and title of the person signing the verbatim quote
- AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS: {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS}} > Target media or audiences (business, tech, regional press)
- EMBARGO: {{EMBARGO}} > "Immediate release" or date and time of embargo lift
- CONTACTO_PRENSA: {{CONTACTO_PRENSA}} > Name, email, and phone of the press contact
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The organization needs to announce a fact to media and achieve coverage without appearing promotional. A well-crafted press release allows a journalist to publish the story with minimal rewriting: a reusable newsworthy headline, a lead that answers everything in the first paragraph, and a quote that adds a human voice. The journalist decides in seconds whether there is a story; if the text sounds like a brochure, it gets discarded. A good press release unlocks media presence, credibility with third parties, and a reusable asset for the website, social media, and the press room.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: journalist and senior media relations specialist, skilled in the inverted pyramid and with editorial judgment to distinguish news from self-promotion.
Deliverable: a complete, distributable press release in structured plain text. Steps:
1. Confirm that you have the date, location, figures, spokesperson name and title, and press contact; if anything essential is missing, ask before drafting and never invent it. Mark with [SUPUESTO] everything you assume.
2. Header: embargo line per EMBARGO (FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE or EMBARGOED UNTIL date and time) and dateline (location, date) at the start of the lead.
3. Subheadline + newsworthy headline of at most 12 words, focused on the fact, not the brand; optional one-line subtitle adding the second most relevant data point.
4. Inverted-pyramid lead: first paragraph answering the five Ws (what, who, when, where, why) in two or three sentences.
5. Two or three body paragraphs in inverted pyramid order, from the most important data to secondary context, incorporating DATOS_CLAVE; each material figure with its source or reference.
6. One verbatim quote attributed to PORTAVOZ that adds vision or meaning without repeating already-stated data; an optional second quote only if there is a relevant partner or third party.
7. Close: "About ORGANIZACION" paragraph, press contact block, and attachments boilerplate per ADJUNTOS.
8. Final distribution note: recipients within AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS, suggested email subject line, and missing assets.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: define the news angle (what changes for the reader) and discard anything that only serves the brand. If the fact is not news, say so and propose a stronger angle.
Phase 2 - Hierarchy: order the facts by descending relevance; dispensable information goes last and must be cuttable without breaking the meaning (inverted pyramid rule).
Phase 3 - Drafting: third person, short sentences, verifiable, neutral and professional English, without superlatives or empty adjectives; expand acronyms on first use; figures with source; mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 4 - Quote: draft a statement that sounds like a real person and adds meaning, vision, or commitment — not filler or repeated data.
Phase 5 - Closing and review against the checklist; add the distribution note.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Embargo line in header consistent with EMBARGO; dateline (location, date) at the start of the lead.
- [ ] Headline of at most 12 words, newsworthy, not promotional.
- [ ] Lead answers the five Ws in the first paragraph.
- [ ] Body in verifiable inverted pyramid order; each material figure with a source; zero invented data ([SUPUESTO] where information is missing).
- [ ] Verbatim quote attributed with name and title, adds vision and does not repeat data.
- [ ] "About" paragraph + press contact block + complete attachments reference.
- [ ] Third person, neutral and professional English, acronyms expanded, without empty superlatives or promotional language.
- [ ] Distribution note: recipients, suggested email subject line, and missing assets.
Edge cases: if the fact is not newsworthy, propose an alternate angle; if the quote only repeats figures, rewrite it with vision; if a data point from the five Ws is missing, ask for it and do not publish an incomplete release.
Expected deliverable: a press release ready to send to media, in structured plain text, reusable for the press room and social media, with a distribution note.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_carta_inversionis:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Organization signing the letter and its stage (e.g. Series A startup, family business, fund, scale-up)
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Period the update covers (quarter, half-year, or year) and, if applicable, the comparison period
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Recipient: equity investors, board of directors, LPs, or strategic partners; their level of familiarity and prior information
- LOGROS: {{LOGROS}} > 2 to 4 achievements for the period, each with its verifiable metric or milestone
- DESAFIOS: {{DESAFIOS}} > 1 to 3 challenges or below-expectation results, with cause and response plan
- VISION: {{VISION}} > Vision or focus for the next period: bets and how progress will be measured
- FIRMANTE: {{FIRMANTE}} > Who signs (role and name) and co-signer if applicable; "To be confirmed" if unknown
- TONO_ESPECIAL: {{TONO_ESPECIAL}} > Sensitivity of the moment (round in progress, pivot, bad news, partner exit) or "Standard"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An organization must send its investors or stakeholders a periodic business update. The purpose is to sustain trust through transparency: a letter that balances achievements, challenges, and vision, addressed to those who entrusted their capital or backing. A solid letter reduces reader uncertainty, sets the narrative before rumor does, leaves a written record of how the business is governed, and builds the credibility that enables the next cycle of support. Doing it poorly — hiding the bad, inflating the good, or burying bad news in technical jargon — erodes the relationship that sustains the organization and is paid for dearly in the next round or vote.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior Director of Investor Relations, experienced in drafting shareholder and stakeholder letters in the style of annual shareholder letters, trained in the candor principle (address the reader as an absent partner; report the good and the bad with equal rigor; explain the business, not just the numbers).

Deliverable: the complete letter, ready to send, with these steps:
1. Verify that ORGANIZACION, PERIODO, AUDIENCIA, LOGROS, DESAFIOS, and VISION are present; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting. FIRMANTE and TONO_ESPECIAL are optional; if missing, assume signatory to be confirmed and standard tone. Do not invent metrics, figures, or milestones.
2. Define the central message of the period in one sentence, anchoring the whole letter.
3. Draft the opening: acknowledge the reader as a partner and state the central message; if TONO_ESPECIAL indicates bad news, name it upfront — do not bury it.
4. Achievements section: each with its evidence or metric, explaining why it matters for the long-term thesis — not just what happened.
5. Challenges section: name them without euphemisms, with root cause and the concrete corrective action underway, with responsible party or timeline when the data exists.
6. Vision section: focus for the next period, bets, and how progress will be measured; connect each bet to an already-cited achievement or challenge.
7. Closing: reaffirm the commitment, thank for the trust, and indicate the next contact point or report if the data exists.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpretation: confirm organization, period, audience, and inputs; flag gaps; detect the sensitive moment via TONO_ESPECIAL.
Phase 2 — Message architecture: fix the central message and the achievements/challenges/vision balance before writing prose; verify that each achievement has a metric and each challenge has an action.
Phase 3 — Drafting: develop the sections in an adult-to-adult tone; each unsupported data point is marked [SUPUESTO]; without empty jargon or superlatives lacking evidence.
Phase 4 — Candor check: verify that no challenge has been softened, no achievement inflated, no figure invented, and no bad news buried; confirm zero prices and zero return projections.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Central message explicit in one sentence in the opening.
- [ ] Achievements with a verifiable metric or milestone and their relevance to the thesis, not just a description.
- [ ] Challenges named without euphemisms, each with root cause and a concrete corrective action.
- [ ] Vision with focus, bets, and a measurable progress criterion, connected to cited achievements or challenges.
- [ ] Bad news (if TONO_ESPECIAL indicates it) declared upfront, not buried.
- [ ] Professional, sober, adult-to-adult tone; neutral and professional English; no emojis.
- [ ] Zero prices, return projections, or invented figures; all assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Real balance between achievements and challenges (not a good-news letter).
Edge cases: if there is only bad news, maintain candor without alarmism and prioritize the response plan; if the audience is the board of directors, raise the level of governance detail; if metrics are missing for an achievement, report it qualitatively and mark it [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: a letter to investors or stakeholders ready to send, with opening, Achievements, Challenges, Vision, and closing, faithful to the provided data.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_mensaje_crisis:
[inputs]
- INCIDENTE: {{INCIDENTE}} > What happened, when, and who is affected, in one or two sentences
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Message recipients (customers, employees, press, regulators, affected users); if there are several, indicate the primary
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Medium and format for release (press release, email, LinkedIn post, press statement, internal message, SMS/push)
- HECHOS_CONFIRMADOS: {{HECHOS_CONFIRMADOS}} > Data verified as of now; unconfirmed items are marked separately
- ACCIONES_INMEDIATAS: {{ACCIONES_INMEDIATAS}} > What has already been done to contain the damage and protect those affected
- VOCERO: {{VOCERO}} > Name and title of the visible responsible party who signs
- SEVERIDAD: {{SEVERIDAD}} > Impact level: low / medium / high / risk to life (optional; default medium)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Target register (calm-warm, institutional-firm, technical-transparent) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A crisis is won or lost in the first hours. I need a message ready to publish that stops the uncertainty spiral: one that acknowledges what happened honestly, demonstrates the situation is under control, reports only verified facts, and commits to concrete actions with a visible responsible party. The goal is to protect those affected first and reputation second, avoiding the two fatal errors: the silence that reads as concealment and the speculation that gets disproved the next day. The message must scale with severity: the greater the risk, the earlier protection of those affected is stated and the more sober the language.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: crisis communications director with experience leading responses to high-reputational-impact incidents, trained in emergency risk communication protocols (CERC) and executive spokesmanship under pressure.
Deliverable: a publishable crisis message for {{CANAL}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, signed by {{VOCERO}}, calibrated to {{SEVERIDAD}}.
Steps:
1. Restate incident {{INCIDENTE}} in one neutral, verifiable sentence; validate with the user before drafting.
2. Draft the ACKNOWLEDGMENT block: name the fact without minimizing or speculating, with explicit empathy toward those affected; do not start by defending yourself or attributing blame externally.
3. Draft the CONTAINMENT block: translate {{ACCIONES_INMEDIATAS}} into evidence of control and protection of those affected; prioritize what reduces harm over what protects image.
4. Draft the INFORMATION block: present only {{HECHOS_CONFIRMADOS}}; visibly separate what is still under investigation; never fill in figures or causes.
5. Draft the COMMITMENT block: next steps, responsible party, exact date and time of the next update, and an operational contact channel.
6. Close with a unique spokesperson line (a short, repeatable anchor phrase) and the signature of {{VOCERO}}.
7. Mark all unverified data as [POR CONFIRMAR]. Avoid admitting legal liability or fault before the investigation: use language of care, not litigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the incident and the primary audience; list missing data in ONE single grouped question (what, when, who is affected, what is known with certainty, what has been done, who signs, which channel, what severity).
Phase 2 - Plan: present the skeleton of the four blocks (Acknowledge, Contain, Inform, Commit) and the proposed spokesperson line; wait for validation if there are critical open data points or high severity.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the full message adjusted to the length and format of {{CANAL}} and to {{SEVERIDAD}}, in neutral and professional English, {{TONO}} calm tone conveying control without coldness, no emojis or unnecessary technical jargon.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four blocks are present and in order: acknowledge, contain, inform, commit.
- [ ] Acknowledgment without minimizing or speculating; explicit empathy toward those affected; does not start by defending itself or blaming third parties.
- [ ] Zero invented data; all unverified information marked [POR CONFIRMAR]; what is under investigation visibly separated from what is confirmed.
- [ ] No admission of fault or legal liability before the investigation; language of care, not litigation.
- [ ] Commitment includes a visible responsible party, exact date and time of the next update, and an operational contact channel.
- [ ] Unique spokesperson line, short and repeatable; signature of {{VOCERO}}.
- [ ] Length, format, and register adjusted to {{CANAL}} and {{SEVERIDAD}}; calm, professional tone, no emojis.
- [ ] Neutral and professional English, without empty corporate jargon or promises that cannot be sustained.
Expected deliverable: a final publishable crisis message, with the four labeled blocks, spokesperson line, and signature, ready to copy and distribute via the indicated channel.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_acta_reunion:
[inputs]
- TEMA_REUNION: {{TEMA_REUNION}} > Topic or central objective of the meeting to document
- FECHA: {{FECHA}} > Date of the session (and time if relevant)
- ASISTENTES: {{ASISTENTES}} > Attendees and absentees with their role or area
- NOTAS_CRUDAS: {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} > Raw notes or transcript of what was discussed
- PROXIMA_REUNION: {{PROXIMA_REUNION}} > Date and focus of the next meeting (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to transform raw notes or a transcript into navigable, reliable minutes. Purpose: so that anyone, including someone who did not attend, reads the minutes in thirty seconds and understands what was decided, who is responsible for each action, and with what deadline. Clear minutes unlock execution without follow-up meetings, leave a trail of agreements, and protect everyone from ambiguity and misunderstandings. Minutes are a governance record: their value depends on separating what was decided from what was discussed and on asserting nothing that the notes do not support.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: executive facilitator and senior minutes secretary, practiced in meeting governance, drafting actionable minutes, and tracking agreements (decision-action-pending, DACI/RACI accountability).
Produce structured, navigable minutes from {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}}, in this order:
1. Three-line executive summary at the top: what was discussed, the main decision, and the next milestone.
2. Header: {{TEMA_REUNION}}, {{FECHA}}, session objective, and attendees/absentees with their role per {{ASISTENTES}}.
3. Decisions: numbered list of closed agreements, each in one unambiguous sentence with minimum context for the why; do not mix unresolved proposals with firm decisions; mark as conditional every decision subject to a condition and state the condition.
4. Actions: table with columns for action, responsible party, deadline, and status, one row per concrete, verifiable commitment.
5. Open items and next steps: open or deferred topics, risks or blockers, dependencies between actions, and the date and focus of the next meeting per {{PROXIMA_REUNION}}.
Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} when a decision or action is supported by an attachment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpretation: read {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} and {{ASISTENTES}}, separate facts from inferences, and group what was discussed into closed decisions, actions, and open items; classify each item by its actual status, not its intent.
Phase 2 — Structure: build the minutes in the order summary, header, decisions, actions, open items; each decision in one sentence, each action with a single responsible party and a deadline.
Phase 3 — Truth discipline: do not invent names, figures, dates, or agreements; mark [SUPUESTO] for every inference not made explicit; leave To be confirmed for any missing responsible party or deadline, no orphaned actions. Edge cases: shared responsibility → one responsible party and the others as support; decision that contradicts a prior one mentioned → flag it and note the contradiction; meeting with no closed decisions → state it explicitly instead of fabricating one. If critical data (notes, date, or attendees) is missing, ask for it in a brief list before drafting.
Phase 4 — Polish: neutral and professional English, no emojis, short sentences, scannable in thirty seconds; no metadiscourse.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Three-line executive summary present at the top and readable in thirty seconds.
- Each decision is closed, numbered, and drafted in one unambiguous sentence; conditional decisions state their condition.
- Firm decisions are never mixed with unresolved proposals; items discussed without closure go to open items.
- Every action has a single responsible party and deadline, or is marked To be confirmed; no orphaned actions; shared responsibility resolved with secondary support.
- Zero invented data: names, figures, and dates come from the notes; inferences marked [SUPUESTO]; contradictions flagged.
- Open items and next meeting section included; risks, blockers, and dependencies recorded.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis, scannable structure; attachments referenced where they support an agreement.
Expected deliverable: minutes ready to circulate, with executive summary, header, numbered decisions, action table with responsible party and deadline, and an open items and next steps block.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_resumen_bloi:
[inputs]
- MENSAJE_ORIGINAL: {{MENSAJE_ORIGINAL}} > Draft, notes, or raw information to be synthesized in BLUF format
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Recipient and their hierarchical level (e.g., executive committee, sponsor, client, technical peer)
- ACCION_ESPERADA: {{ACCION_ESPERADA}} > What the recipient must decide, approve, or do after reading
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Delivery medium: email, chat message, status note, memo (optional)
- NIVEL_URGENCIA: {{NIVEL_URGENCIA}} > Urgency and expected response timeframe (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The recipient is a decision-maker with little time and many messages competing for their attention. They must grasp the conclusion or request within the first few seconds to decide whether to act, delegate, or defer. A message that buries the conclusion under context gets deferred, misread, or left unanswered. Applying BLUF unlocks faster responses, decisions without clarification meetings, and the perception of the author as a high-caliber communicator.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive writer in tactical communication for senior leadership, trained in the BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front) doctrine from military and strategic consulting practice.
Deliverable: BLUF-style subject line + message rewritten in BLUF format, paste-ready.
1. Identify the single outcome AUDIENCIA needs to know or the ACCION_ESPERADA they must take.
2. Write a standalone opening line of no more than 25 words that delivers that conclusion, decision, or request without prior context.
3. Build below it, in short scannable blocks: minimum essential context, supporting evidence in descending order of importance, and a closing with concrete action, owner, and deadline if applicable.
4. Adjust length and format to CANAL and NIVEL_URGENCIA (chat = ultra-short; email/memo = blocks with headers).
5. Generate a subject line that previews the conclusion and survives mobile truncation (ideally <=60 characters).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: extract from MENSAJE_ORIGINAL the central conclusion, distinguishing it from context and filler; mark anything missing as [SUPUESTO] or ask for it. Never invent figures, dates, or commitments that support the decision.
Phase 2 — Plan: define the BLUF opening sentence and the descending order of the supporting blocks (most decisive first).
Phase 3 — Execute: draft the message, strip preamble, filler courtesy, and any data that does not support the conclusion; verify that the opening line is understood in isolation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The opening line delivers the conclusion, decision, or request and is understood without reading the rest.
- Opening of no more than 25 words, standalone.
- Supporting content in short, scannable blocks in descending order of importance.
- The closing names the action, owner, and deadline where applicable.
- Zero preamble, filler, or courtesy phrases; every line contributes.
- Inferred data marked [SUPUESTO]; zero invention of critical data.
- Format consistent with CANAL and NIVEL_URGENCIA; subject line previews the conclusion.
- Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word "free".
- Deliverable: BLUF-style subject line + paste-ready BLUF message.

Edge cases: if CANAL is chat, deliver a single BLUF sentence with no subject line. If ACCION_ESPERADA cannot be inferred, ask for it before drafting. If MENSAJE_ORIGINAL contains multiple conclusions, choose the most decisive one for AUDIENCIA and subordinate the rest.
spec-comunicacion_doc_readme_proyecto:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_PROYECTO: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} > Project/repository name and, if applicable, its one-liner
- DESCRIPCION_PROPOSITO: {{DESCRIPCION_PROPOSITO}} > What it is, what problem it solves, and why it exists
- PUBLICO_OBJETIVO: {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} > Who it serves (e.g., "backend devs", "data analysts", "CLI users")
- STACK_PRERREQUISITOS: {{STACK_PRERREQUISITOS}} > Language, runtime, package manager, system dependencies, accounts/keys, and minimum versions
- COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE: {{COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE}} > Exact commands to clone, install, and start; separate local/production if applicable
- CASO_USO_PRINCIPAL: {{CASO_USO_PRINCIPAL}} > The flow to show in the quickstart to confirm it works, with its observable output
- CONFIGURACION: {{CONFIGURACION}} > Environment variables or config file: name, purpose, and default ("(optional)" if not applicable)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A project without a usable README forces every new person to interrupt the team to understand what {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} is, how to install it, and how to start it; knowledge lives in people's heads and chats, and every onboarding costs repeated, error-prone hours. An onboarding-oriented README turns that cost into an asset: it takes {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} from zero to a first visible result without assistance, reduces time-to-first-commit, lowers the contribution barrier, and becomes the project's versionable source of truth. The success criterion is not whether the README is complete, but whether an outsider can achieve the first result following only what is written.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical writer specializing in developer experience and open-source documentation, with mastery of Standard Readme and the Diataxis model (tutorial focus).
Deliver the complete README for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} in Markdown, inside a code block, ready to paste at the repo root. Required sections in order:
1. Header: title + a sentence summarizing {{DESCRIPCION_PROPOSITO}} for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, followed by key features as a list.
2. Prerequisites: derive from {{STACK_PRERREQUISITOS}} specific minimum versions, system dependencies, and required accounts/keys.
3. Installation: numbered steps with exact, copyable commands from {{COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE}}; separate local/production if applicable.
4. Quickstart (under 5 minutes): shortest startup command for {{CASO_USO_PRINCIPAL}} + the literal expected output to confirm success.
5. Basic usage: one or two real, copyable examples with their result.
6. Repo structure: brief map of key folders and their role.
7. Configuration: table from {{CONFIGURACION}} with variable, purpose, and default value.
8. Troubleshooting: 3 to 5 common errors in symptom > cause > solution format.
9. Closing: how to contribute, license, and where to get help.
Assumptions and limits: do not invent commands, versions, paths, or variable names outside what is provided; if a critical data point is missing, mark it as {pending: <what is missing>} in its exact location and list it at the end. A quickstart without a verifiable expected output is defective.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpretation: identify the audience, language, package manager, startup command, and expected observable result; mark any unprovided data as pending.
Phase 2 — Installation path: order prerequisites and installation as a linear sequence with no gaps or hidden assumptions; every command runs as written.
Phase 3 — Verifiable quickstart: write the shortest startup that produces observable output and transcribe that expected output literally.
Phase 4 — Usage, structure, and configuration: write copyable examples with their result and the variables table.
Phase 5 — Resilience and closing: anticipate frequent errors with cause and actionable solution; close with contribution, license, and support; consolidate the pending list.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The first sentence answers what it is, what problem it solves, and for whom, without internal jargon.
- [ ] Prerequisites list specific minimum versions, not "latest version".
- [ ] All commands are copyable and exact; none invented outside {{COMANDOS_INSTALACION_ARRANQUE}}.
- [ ] The quickstart starts in under 5 minutes and shows the literal expected output to verify success.
- [ ] There is at least one usage example with its result.
- [ ] The {{CONFIGURACION}} table covers name, purpose, and default for each variable.
- [ ] Troubleshooting has 3 to 5 entries with symptom, cause, and actionable solution.
- [ ] Each missing data point is marked as {pending: ...} and listed at the end, not invented.
- [ ] The entire README is inside a copyable Markdown code block.
Expected deliverable: README.md in Markdown with header, prerequisites, installation, verifiable quickstart, usage, structure, configuration table, troubleshooting, and closing (contribution/license/support), plus the list of pending items if any.
spec-comunicacion_doc_guia_usuario:
[inputs]
- TAREA: {{TAREA}} > Specific task the reader must complete, expressed as an objective (e.g., "export a monthly report to PDF")
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product, app, or tool where the task is performed, with version if applicable
- NIVEL_LECTOR: {{NIVEL_LECTOR}} > Reader profile and experience (e.g., "new user with no technical background", "administrator")
- CANAL_PUBLICACION: {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}} > Where the guide will be published (help center, internal manual, knowledge base, README)
- ENTORNO: {{ENTORNO}} > (optional) Platform, operating system, browser, or target device; if omitted, draft without assuming a platform and mark every environment dependency [confirmar]
- PROBLEMAS_FRECUENTES: {{PROBLEMAS_FRECUENTES}} > (optional) Typical errors or blockers to cover in "If something goes wrong"; if omitted, infer them from the task and mark them [confirmar]
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A reader of level {{NIVEL_LECTOR}} needs to complete the task {{TAREA}} in {{PRODUCTO}} and opens a guide expecting to succeed without assistance, in one attempt, without frustration. A well-built task-oriented guide unlocks user autonomy, reduces support tickets, and raises product adoption. The result will be published in {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}. Reliability constraint: a guide with an invented control or incorrect path destroys trust and generates more support load than it prevents; therefore, whenever a data point is not provided, it is marked [confirmar] instead of guessed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical writer specializing in task-oriented documentation, trained in the Diataxis framework (how-to guide quadrant) and minimalist UX writing principles.
Deliver a step-by-step user guide with this structure:
1. Task-oriented title ("How to + verb + object" format) and an opening sentence stating what the reader will accomplish and when to use this guide.
2. Prerequisites: list of accounts, permissions, data, tools, or knowledge needed before starting; each prerequisite worded so the reader can verify it themselves.
3. Numbered steps: each step begins with an imperative verb, covers a single observable action, indicates where it occurs (screen, menu, or control), and describes the intermediate result visible upon completion. Mark warnings and shortcuts distinctly ("Warning:" / "Shortcut:") and only where they reduce error or effort.
4. Expected result: concrete final state and how to verify the task was completed correctly.
5. If something goes wrong: 2 or 3 common problems taken from {{PROBLEMAS_FRECUENTES}} (if empty, infer from {{TAREA}}), each with observable symptom, probable cause, and actionable solution.
Limits: a how-to guide assumes the reader already knows what they want to do; do not explain concepts or the product's rationale (that is explanation, another Diataxis quadrant). Do not cover tasks other than {{TAREA}}; if prerequisites are tasks in themselves, link them as prerequisites rather than developing them.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: confirm task, product and version, reader level, channel, and {{ENTORNO}}; define scope (where the guide starts and ends) and a single verifiable objective. If scope is ambiguous, declare the adopted assumption at the start.
Phase 2 — Inventory: list prerequisites and enumerate atomic actions in real execution order; group or split steps so each is a single user decision. Identify points where a reader of level {{NIVEL_LECTOR}} might make mistakes or get stuck.
Phase 3 — Drafting: write each step with imperative verb + location + intermediate result; insert warnings and shortcuts only where they reduce error or effort. Keep one action per step and one named control per action.
Phase 4 — Closing and verification: draft the verifiable expected result and the common problems section; check that no control names or paths are invented, marking as [confirmar] every unprovided data point, and confirm that each step from 1 to N has an observable intermediate result.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Title in "How to + verb + object" format and opening that declares the accomplishment and when to use the guide.
- [ ] Complete, reader-verifiable prerequisites before step 1.
- [ ] Each step: one imperative verb, one action, explicit location, and observable intermediate result.
- [ ] Step order = actual execution sequence; no step depends on a later action.
- [ ] Warnings and shortcuts marked distinctly and placed where they contribute.
- [ ] Expected result describes the final state and how to verify it.
- [ ] "If something goes wrong" section with 2–3 problems, each with symptom, cause, and solution.
- [ ] Scope respected: no concepts explained, no tasks other than {{TAREA}} developed.
- [ ] Neutral, professional English, formal register, no unnecessary technical jargon.
- [ ] Zero invented button names, paths, or behaviors; every missing data point marked [confirmar].
Expected deliverable: user guide ready to publish in {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}, copyable without editing except for [confirmar] fields.
spec-comunicacion_doc_faq_estructurada:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}} > Product, service, or feature the FAQ documents and its purpose in one line
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Target reader and their level (new customer, technical user, buyer evaluating, etc.)
- PREGUNTAS_REALES: {{PREGUNTAS_REALES}} > Questions or doubts the team receives today (tickets, sales, support); the base for intent classification
- ENLACES_DISPONIBLES: {{ENLACES_DISPONIBLES}} > Existing support resources with their URL or path and type (guide, documentation, form, dashboard) (optional)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the FAQ lives (help center, landing page, onboarding, internal knowledge base) to adjust tone and depth (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A flat FAQ mixes questions from someone just exploring with those from someone trying to fix a failure, and forces the reader to read everything to find one answer. Structuring it by search intent ensures each reader lands in their block, resolves on the first try, and does not open a ticket. The result unlocks real self-service: fewer repeated queries, content reusable in help centers and onboarding flows, and a base that scales as new questions emerge.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior support content architect and search intent expert, with experience in self-service knowledge bases.
