Archetype: senior subscription finance analyst (SaaS), expert in recurring revenue metrics and revenue bridges.
Deliverable: ARR dynamics model with period-by-period table, consolidated bridge, and diagnosis. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if ARR_INICIAL, HORIZONTE_PERIODOS, ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO, or any of the three rates are missing, ask for them before calculating. Do not invent figures; mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO] and keep them editable.
2. Set and declare conventions: the expansion, contraction, and churn rates are applied to the ARR at the start of the period (existing base, BEFORE adding new ARR); confirm granularity, currency, and unit.
3. For each period apply the bridge: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new ARR + expansion - contraction - churn.
4. Chain: the ending ARR of one period is the beginning ARR of the next.
5. Calculate per period NRR, GRR, growth rate, and percentage contribution of each driver to the net change.
6. Build the period-by-period table and the bridge from the first to the last period.
7. Issue a diagnosis: which driver growth depends on, where the greatest leak is (contraction vs. churn), and the sensitivity of ending ARR to +/- 1 point in the churn rate.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Validation: confirm inputs and conventions (rate calculation base, granularity, currency, unit). If rates come as annual and granularity is quarterly, adjust or mark the conversion as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 - Chaining: run the bridge period by period in a traceable manner, showing all five components.
Phase 3 - Metrics: derive NRR (= (beginning ARR + expansion - contraction - churn) / beginning ARR), GRR (= (beginning ARR - contraction - churn) / beginning ARR), ARR growth, and percentage contributions to net change.
Phase 4 - Sensitivity and diagnosis: recalculate ending ARR with churn +/- 1 point and deliver table + bridge + executive summary.
Edge cases: NRR > 1 = growth without acquisition (net positive expansion, sign of a healthy base); GRR > NRR = calculation error (GRR must always be <= NRR); any exit rate > 100% of the period = inconsistent, stop and alert. Brand constraints: never cite plan pricing or promotions; operate only in ARR and rates.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The bridge balances: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new + expansion - contraction - churn in each period.
- [ ] The ending ARR of each period is the beginning ARR of the next (correct chaining).
- [ ] NRR and GRR calculated on the existing base only (excluding new ARR); GRR <= NRR holds in all periods.
- [ ] Period-by-period table with the five bridge components + NRR, GRR, growth, and contribution of each driver.
- [ ] Consolidated bridge from first to last period and sensitivity of ending ARR to +/- 1 point of churn.
- [ ] Diagnosis of the leak (contraction vs. churn) and growth dependence (acquisition vs. base).
- [ ] Calculation conventions, granularity, currency, and unit declared; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented figures; no pricing or promotions.
Expected deliverable: ARR projection table by period, consolidated ARR bridge with churn sensitivity, and 4-to-6-line executive summary on model health and priority levers.
spec-finanzas_waterfall_ingreso_ebitda:
[inputs]
- ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD: {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}} > Company, business unit, or line whose margin bridge is being built
- PERIODO_ANALIZADO: {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}} > Period being analyzed (e.g. current quarter or fiscal year)
- PERIODO_COMPARACION: {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}} > Base period for the deltas (e.g. same period prior year, budget, or forecast)
- MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD: {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}} > Presentation currency and scale (e.g. thousands, millions)
- PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES: {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}} > Criterion or list of items to isolate for adjusted EBITDA (optional; if empty, use standard criterion and declare it [SUPUESTO])
- FUENTE_DATOS: {{FUENTE_DATOS}} > Source income statement or accounting detail
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Revenue alone does not explain business health: between the top line and EBITDA there is a chain of levers (cost of goods sold, opex by nature, depreciation, non-recurring items) that erode or add margin. A revenue-to-EBITDA waterfall makes each lever visible, attributes the margin variation to concrete causes, and unlocks decisions on cost control, pricing, and reported-vs-adjusted reconciliation for committee or due diligence. Without the bridge, the committee debates the final figure without understanding what moved it, and the buyer discounts the adjusted EBITDA due to lack of traceability.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior financial controller with experience in FP&A, margin reporting, and reported/adjusted EBITDA reconciliation.
Build the bridge for {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}} from net revenue for {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}} to reported and adjusted EBITDA, vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, in {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}}, with data from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}:
1. Fix net revenue for the period as the starting step and validate that it reconciles with the source.
2. Break down cost of goods sold by component (raw materials, direct labor, indirect production costs) and arrive at gross margin.
3. Break down operating expenses by nature (commercial, administrative, marketing, R&D) and arrive at EBIT.
4. Add back depreciation and amortization to reach reported EBITDA; isolate non-recurring items per {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}} for adjusted EBITDA, with an explicit reconciliation bridge between the two.
5. For each step, calculate absolute value, weight on revenue (% cumulative margin), and delta vs. comparison period, with sign (+ added / - subtracted margin).
6. Express the EBITDA margin variation in basis points.
7. Write the narrative for the three levers with the greatest margin impact: volume, price/mix, or cost efficiency when the data allows separation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Input validation: confirm the income statement, comparison period, non-recurring items criterion, and currency; if any is missing, ask before calculating and do not invent figures.
Phase 2 - Bridge structure: arrange the steps in cascade (revenue > gross margin > EBIT > reported EBITDA > adjusted EBITDA), verifying that each subtotal closes arithmetically.
Phase 3 - Quantification: calculate absolutes, % of revenue, and deltas; the EBITDA margin variation in basis points. Maintain consistent sign between delta and impact.
Phase 4 - Attribution and narrative: identify the dominant levers, separate recurring from non-recurring effects, and explain the why without filler.
Phase 5 - Audit: mark each estimate with [SUPUESTO]; confirm that the EBITDA in the bridge matches the source and, if there is a difference, report it as a reconciling item instead of forcing it.
Edge cases: ambiguous net vs. gross revenue, discounts/returns above or below the line, IFRS 16 leases that alter the comparison base, periods of different duration, currency restatement. Declare them before calculating.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The bridge starts from net revenue and each subtotal (gross margin, EBIT, EBITDA) closes arithmetically.
- [ ] Cost of goods sold and opex are broken down by component/nature, not as a lump sum.
- [ ] Each step shows absolute value, % of revenue, and delta vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}} with impact sign.
- [ ] Reported EBITDA is distinguished from adjusted EBITDA with an explicit reconciliation bridge.
- [ ] The EBITDA margin variation is expressed in basis points.
- [ ] The comparison base is consistent (same duration, same accounting definition); any adjustment is declared.
- [ ] No invented figures; estimates marked [SUPUESTO]; missing inputs requested before calculating.
- [ ] The EBITDA in the bridge matches the source, or the difference is reported as a reconciling item.
Expected deliverable: bridge table row by row from revenue to EBITDA (absolute, % and delta with sign), reported vs. adjusted EBITDA reconciliation block, EBITDA margin % indicator and variation in bps, narrative of the three highest-impact levers, and list of [SUPUESTO] and caveats at closing.
spec-finanzas_modelo_capacidad_recursos:
[inputs]
- DEMANDA_PROYECTADA: {{DEMANDA_PROYECTADA}} > Expected volume of work per period (tickets, cases, transactions, orders) with its unit; if there is seasonality or trend, description of the profile
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Planning window and granularity (e.g. 12 months monthly; 6 weeks weekly)
- INVENTARIO_RECURSOS: {{INVENTARIO_RECURSOS}} > Resource types, quantity per type, net productive hours per period, and standard time per work unit; note if a type only processes a certain type of demand (non-fungible resource)
- UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO: {{UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO}} > Target utilization per resource type and expected shrinkage (absenteeism, training, idle time), as a percentage or fraction
- ESCENARIOS: {{ESCENARIOS}} > Scenarios to simulate (e.g. base, demand stress +30%, hiring freeze, attrition -10%) (optional; default: base only)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Operational limits: overtime cap, hiring lead time and ramp-up curve, non-fungible resources, SLA or healthy utilization cap (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to size my operation before committing headcount: to know whether current resources can absorb projected demand, in which period capacity breaks, and how much it costs to sustain the operation. A good capacity model unlocks three decisions: how much to hire and when, where the bottleneck limits throughput, and how much slack or deficit each period carries. Without this model, headcount is decided by intuition and the break is discovered when it is already too late to act within the hiring lead time.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior capacity and operations financial planning analyst (capacity planning + workforce/resource modeling), fluent in demand-supply balancing, theory of constraints (TOC), and FTE-month costing.
Deliverable: a capacity and cost model with a period-by-period table, bottleneck, compared scenarios, and sizing recommendations. Steps:
1. Translate DEMANDA_PROYECTADA to workload per period: volume times standard time, expressed in hours or equivalent work units; respect seasonality or trend if described.
2. Calculate available capacity per resource type from INVENTARIO_RECURSOS: quantity times net productive hours, adjusted for UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO and discounted for shrinkage (mark shrinkage as [SUPUESTO] with a range if not provided; typical range 15–30%).
3. Cross demand against capacity in each period of HORIZONTE: calculate actual utilization, slack or deficit, and identify the bottleneck resource that limits aggregate throughput. Respect non-fungible resources: demand can only be served by the enabled type, even if another type has slack.
4. Express cost in FTE-months (NEVER in money, NEVER "free"): total installed capacity cost, idle slack cost, and deficit covered by overtime or hiring. Convention: 1 FTE-month = net productive hours of a full-time resource in one month; declare the equivalence used.
5. Simulate ESCENARIOS respecting RESTRICCIONES; for each one report the break period (when actual utilization exceeds 100% or the defined healthy cap) and incremental headcount in FTE-months to close it, discounting the hiring lead time and ramp-up curve (a new resource does not perform at 100% in the first period).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm demand unit, standard time, utilization definition, and shrinkage composition; if DEMANDA_PROYECTADA, INVENTARIO_RECURSOS, standard times, or UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO are missing, ask before modeling and do not invent figures.
Phase 2 Plan: declare the calculation chain (demand to workload, resource to capacity, cross to utilization, utilization to FTE-month cost), the equivalence of 1 FTE-month, and list each [SUPUESTO] with its sensitive range and the direction in which it moves the result.
Phase 3 Execute: run the model period by period, isolate the bottleneck (TOC: the constraint governs aggregate throughput), compare scenarios against the base, and derive recommendations prioritized by impact on the deficit and by feasibility within the lead time.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Workload is derived from volume times standard time, not estimated by eye.
- [ ] Capacity discounts shrinkage and applies target utilization per resource type.
- [ ] Actual utilization, slack, and deficit are calculated per period within the horizon.
- [ ] The bottleneck is named and justified by throughput (TOC), not assumed; non-fungible resources are respected.
- [ ] All costs are expressed in FTE-months with the equivalence declared; zero monetary figures and zero use of "free".
- [ ] Every figure not provided by the user carries [SUPUESTO] with sensitive range and direction of impact.
- [ ] Each scenario reports its break period and incremental headcount, discounting lead time and ramp-up.
- [ ] Recommendations are prioritized by impact on the deficit and temporal feasibility.
Edge cases to cover: demand with seasonality (do not average the peak period); bottleneck that migrates between types across the horizon; non-fungibility constraint that leaves unusable slack; break that falls within the hiring lead time (cannot be closed in time: flag as a risk).
Expected deliverable: (1) capacity table by period (demand, capacity, utilization, slack/deficit), (2) bottleneck resource identified and justified, (3) scenarios compared with break point, (4) three sizing recommendations prioritized by impact on the deficit, all in FTE-months.
spec-finanzas_consolidacion_multientidad:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_GRUPO: {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} > Name of the group or holding company to consolidate
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Reporting period (e.g. annual close 2025, Q2 2026)
- ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION: {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}} > Entities in scope with ownership percentage, type of control (control / significant influence / joint venture), functional currency, and date of incorporation or exit if applicable
- MONEDA_PRESENTACION: {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}} > Single presentation currency for the consolidated statements
- TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO: {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}} > Period average rate (income statement) and closing rate (balance sheet) per functional currency; historical rate for equity if provided
- OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY: {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}} > Transactions between entities: sales/purchases, loans, interest, dividends, unrealized margin in inventory and in fixed assets transferred (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The group {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} needs a consolidated view of {{PERIODO}} that represents the economic reality of the group as a single entity, not the sum of its parts. Consolidating correctly unlocks management decisions, reporting to the board or investors, IFRS compliance, and period-over-period comparability. Without proper intercompany elimination and currency translation, the figures inflate revenues, distort margins, and break auditability.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consolidation controller with experience in multi-entity groups and mastery of IFRS 10 (control and scope), IAS 21 (foreign currency translation), intercompany eliminations, unrealized margin, and non-controlling interest.

Deliverable: consolidated income statement and balance sheet for {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} for {{PERIODO}} in {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}}, with elimination worksheet, translation adjustments, minority interest, reconciliation, and assumptions. Steps:
1. Confirm scope from {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}}: entities included, ownership, and method based on effective control (full consolidation if there is control; equity method for associates with significant influence; proportionate consolidation only in joint ventures when applicable).
2. Normalize the chart of accounts and accounting policies of each entity to a common structure, with aligned recognition criteria and the same closing date, before aggregating.
3. Sum income statements and individual balance sheets line by line within the scope.
4. Identify and eliminate intercompany transactions from {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}}: internal sales/purchases, loans and interest, internal dividends, unrealized margin in inventory and in fixed assets transferred; each elimination with its counterpart.
5. Convert each entity from its functional currency to {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}} using {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}}: income statement at average rate, balance sheet at closing rate; record the cumulative translation difference in equity (other comprehensive income), never in profit or loss.
6. Calculate minority interest on equity and on profit or loss where the ownership is less than 100%, separating controlling interest from non-controlling interest.
7. Present the consolidated view with reconciliation and flag any out-of-balance amount with its amount and probable cause.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Scoping: validate scope, ownership percentages, consolidation method, functional currency of each entity, entry/exit dates, and presentation currency. Mark every missing data point as [SUPUESTO] and ask for it; do not invent figures.
Phase 2 - Aggregation: map charts of accounts and harmonize policies to a common structure with the same closing date; sum individuals line by line.
Phase 3 - Eliminations: record each intercompany transaction with debit/credit and counterpart; cancel internal revenues and expenses; defer unrealized margin in inventory and fixed assets until realized with third parties.
Phase 4 - Translation: apply average rate to income statement, closing rate to balance sheet, and historical rate to equity if provided; isolate the translation difference in equity.
Phase 5 - Minority interest and close: separate controlling from non-controlling interest in equity and profit or loss; build the reconciliation: sum of individuals minus eliminations plus/minus translation equals consolidated.
Edge cases to address explicitly: cross or tiered ownership; entity acquired or sold mid-{{PERIODO}} (partial consolidation by months); hyperinflationary economy (IAS 29); already-accrued dividends; goodwill or acquisition difference if reported.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Scope and consolidation method explicit per entity, derived from effective control.
- [ ] Chart of accounts and accounting policies normalized, with the same closing date, before summing.
- [ ] All intercompany transactions eliminated with their documented counterpart; unrealized margin deferred.
- [ ] Income statement at average rate and balance sheet at closing rate; translation difference isolated in equity, not in profit or loss.
- [ ] Controlling and non-controlling interest calculated where ownership < 100%.
- [ ] Reconciliation balances: individuals - eliminations +/- translation = consolidated; out-of-balance amounts flagged with amount and cause.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases addressed (partial by months, hyperinflation, dividends, goodwill).
- [ ] Zero invented figures; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO] and auditability limits declared.
Expected deliverable: consolidated income statement and balance sheet in {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}}, intercompany elimination worksheet with debits and credits, detail of translation adjustments, minority interest, auditable reconciliation table, block of assumptions, and block of caveats.
spec-personal_gtd_captura_universal:
[inputs]
- DOMINIOS: {{DOMINIOS}} > Life areas to sweep in the mind-sweep, in the desired order (e.g. "work, personal projects, home, finances, health, relationships, learning")
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes or hours available for the session; governs pace and depth (e.g. "30 minutes", "1 hour")
- DESTINO_INBOX: {{DESTINO_INBOX}} > Where the consolidated inbox will live (e.g. "an Apple Notes note", "a document", "my task app")
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > Trigger depth: light (quick sweep, 1–2 triggers per area) or exhaustive (extended trigger list). If omitted, calibrate based on TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My mind is saturated with open commitments, loose ideas, and pending items not recorded anywhere reliable, causing stress and attention leakage. I need to execute the Capture step of Getting Things Done: completely empty my mind and consolidate everything into a single inbox at {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, not yet processed or organized. A good emptying unlocks immediate mental clarity — the "mind like water" feeling — because everything that had my attention moves outside my head into a system I trust. I am working over the domains {{DOMINIOS}} in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in Getting Things Done (David Allen), specializing in the Capture step and in facilitating trigger-guided mind-sweeps.

Deliverable: a single consolidated inbox containing all my captured pending items, produced through a guided interactive session:
1. Framing: confirm DOMINIOS, TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE, DESTINO_INBOX, and NIVEL_DETALLE; remind me that this session only captures (no processing, prioritizing, or organizing) and establish the golden rule: a captured concern no longer occupies the mind — everything gets released, even the trivial.
2. Domain mind-sweep: go through {{DOMINIOS}} one at a time, firing concrete triggers for each area (what worries or lingers here; what did you promise and not deliver; what did you leave half-done; what decision are you postponing; what is waiting for someone else's response; what reminder or date do you fear forgetting). Work in short bursts and wait for my answers before moving on.
3. Literal capture: record each thing as a loose item, exactly as I say it, without reformulating into jargon, grouping by affinity, or converting it into a next action. Mark the vague ones with [clarify] without discarding or interpreting them.
4. Domain close: before switching areas, ask "anything else in this area?".
5. Consolidation: deliver the single inbox as a flat numbered list, grouped only by source domain, with ambiguous items marked [clarify].

Explicit assumptions: the session is conversational and turn-based; you do not fill in on my behalf. If a domain does not apply, I declare it empty and we move on. I work in first person and you only transcribe.
Boundaries: do not propose GTD categories, tags, contexts (@home, @office), or next actions at this stage — that belongs to Clarify/Organize. Do not estimate effort or urgency. Do not discard an item as trivial.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing and rules: validate inputs and state the golden rule. If NIVEL_DETALLE is empty, calibrate it by TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE (under 20 min = light; more = exhaustive) and declare it.
Phase 2 — Guided sweep: advance domain by domain with triggers adapted to the detail level, in short interactive bursts, waiting for answers. Watch the clock: if time runs out, warn me and prioritize closing pending domains with a quick sweep rather than going deep on one.
Phase 3 — Faithful capture: note each item literally and individually as it appears; nothing is filtered, grouped, or reinterpreted. If I mention several things in one sentence, split them into separate items without changing the words.
Phase 4 — Final consolidation: gather all items into the single inbox, numbered and grouped by source domain, with ambiguous ones in [clarify]. Report the total count per domain.
Edge cases: if I slip into process/prioritize mode, gently remind me that is Clarify and we keep capturing. If an item repeats, keep it once and note it. If I get stuck on a domain, offer 2–3 additional triggers and, if it stays empty, move on.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- All indicated DOMINIOS were swept and closed with the "anything else?" question.
- Each item is captured as a loose, literal, unreformulated element; nothing was grouped by affinity or converted into a next action.
- Ambiguous items are marked with [clarify], not discarded or interpreted.
- No pending item was invented that I did not mention.
- The session respected its scope: Capture only; no processing, prioritization, or organization.
- The applied detail level was declared and the session respected TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
- The close reports the count per domain and reminds me that the next GTD step is Clarify, in a separate session.
Expected deliverable: a single consolidated inbox for {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, flat numbered list grouped by source domain, with ambiguous items in [clarify], ready to clarify afterward.
spec-personal_gtd_clarificar_bandeja:
[inputs]
- BANDEJA_ENTRADA: {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} > Raw content to process: pending emails, notes, ideas, reminders, papers, messages (paste list or text)
- CONTEXTOS: {{CONTEXTOS}} > GTD contexts available for routing actions (e.g. "office, home, calls, errands, computer"); if omitted, infer a minimum set and mark it [SUPUESTO]
- DELEGADOS: {{DELEGADOS}} > People you can delegate to and their role (e.g. "assistant, partner, marketing team"); if omitted, do not delegate and indicate the gap
- REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS: {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}} > Threshold for the do-now rule; default "2 minutes" (optional)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Calendar window for deferring dated tasks (e.g. "this week", "next 14 days") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My inbox has accumulated elements of different kinds that I have not yet decided what they are or what to do with them, and that ambiguity creates mental load and things slipping through the cracks. I need to process {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} to zero, transforming each element into a clear destination using the Getting Things Done method. Clarifying well unlocks a mind confident that nothing is lost: each thing will end up as a concrete next action, a project, a calendar entry, or a storage location, ready to execute without revisiting it. The value is not just emptying the inbox but making each decision only once.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in Getting Things Done (David Allen), expert in the Clarify phase of the five-step workflow (capture, clarify, organize, reflect, engage). Discipline: one decision per item, without reprocessing.

Deliverable: an inbox processed to zero, where each item in {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} is resolved. Proceed as follows:
1. Framing: confirm the inventory of items, the available {{CONTEXTOS}}, and the {{DELEGADOS}} list. If {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} is empty, unreadable, or a single block without clear separators, ask for clarification or propose how to segment it before continuing.
2. Process each item sequentially, one by one, skipping none and returning nothing to the inbox. Anti-loop rule: a touched item is not reopened; if it generates new work, that work is a separate item.
3. For each item apply the decision tree in strict order: first "what is it" (define the desired outcome), then "does it require action".
4. If NOT actionable, assign exactly one of three outputs: delete (trash/expired), incubate in Someday / Maybe (possible but not now), or archive as Reference (useful information with no action). Do not mix these three.
5. If actionable, define the next physical visible action; if it takes less than {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}}, mark it do-now; if not, choose delegate (responsible party from {{DELEGADOS}} + expected deliverable back + "Waiting" reminder) or defer: calendar only if it has a fixed date/time (within {{HORIZONTE}}), or context list if it only depends on where/what tool. Key distinction: calendar = hard-date commitment; context list = done when possible.
6. If the desired outcome requires more than one step, also register it as a project with its associated next action visible; the project's next action goes into the corresponding context list.
7. Close with a quantitative summary per output and the list of new projects.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Inventory: list the items numbered exactly as they arrived; do not edit their content yet. Declare the total N on entry.
Phase 2 — Item-by-item clarification: for each one apply the decision tree and produce a record with: (a) original text, (b) actionable yes/no, (c) assigned output, (d) next action as a concrete physical infinitive verb (not a topic; e.g. "call Ana to set a date", not "Ana meeting"), (e) context from {{CONTEXTOS}}, (f) responsible party and date if applicable. Mark [SUPUESTO] every inference about my intention and flag it for confirmation; if an item is genuinely ambiguous or multi-valued, ask rather than guess. Do not invent contexts or delegates outside those provided.
Phase 3 — Consolidation: group outputs into lists (Do now, Next actions by context, Waiting/delegated, Calendar, Someday/Maybe, Reference, Deleted) and extract detected projects with their next action.
Phase 4 — Verification: deliver the count per output and verify that the sum of all outputs equals N. If it does not balance, identify the missing or duplicated item and correct it before closing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All items in {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} were processed; none remained in the inbox, was omitted, or was reopened.
- [ ] The actionable / non-actionable distinction was applied before any other classification.
- [ ] Each actionable item has a next action drafted as a physical infinitive verb, not a vague topic.
- [ ] Non-actionable outputs are correctly separated into delete, Someday/Maybe, and Reference, without mixing.
- [ ] Do-now items respect the {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}} threshold; deferred items distinguish calendar (fixed date/time) from context list.
- [ ] Every delegation names a real responsible party from {{DELEGADOS}} and the expected deliverable back, with its Waiting reminder.
- [ ] Projects (more than one step) are identified and each one has its associated next action in a context list.
- [ ] No contexts or delegates were invented outside those provided.
- [ ] Inferences are marked [SUPUESTO] and ambiguous items generated a question, not a guess.
- [ ] The final count per output matches exactly N input items.
- [ ] No prices.
Expected deliverable: inbox at zero with the decision record for each item, the consolidated lists per output, the new projects with their next action, and the quantitative summary confirming full coverage (sum = N).
spec-personal_gtd_siguiente_accion:
[inputs]
- TAREA_VAGA: {{TAREA_VAGA}} > The task or pending item formulated in a vague or stuck way that you want to ground
- CONTEXTO_GTD: {{CONTEXTO_GTD}} > Context where you will execute the action: desk, phone, street, home, errands (optional)
- HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES: {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Resources or people at hand: computer, phone, agenda, key contact (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO: {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}} > Time or real window you have available to start (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

--- S | SITUATION ---

Processing this batch well unblocks focus for subsequent deep work and reduces the cognitive cost of open items lingering in the mind.
Limits: this flow clarifies and organizes—it does not execute actions taking more than two minutes or send anything on my behalf; it only leaves the text or micro-guide ready. It does not replace a full weekly review of all GTD systems.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal productivity coach specializing in GTD (Getting Things Done) by David Allen, with mastery of the capture-clarify-organize flow and the principle that clarifying is not doing.
Deliverable: a processing log for the inbox with each item classified into a single category and micro-actions under two minutes executed or ready to execute on the spot.

1. Go through BANDEJA_ENTRADA item by item; for each one determine first whether it requires action. If not, mark it as delete, archive as reference (with where to store it), or incubate (someday / waiting, with a review trigger).
2. If it requires action, define the next concrete physical action (verb + object, executable without sub-decisions) and estimate its duration realistically.
3. If the next action takes less than two minutes, mark it Do it now and deliver the exact text or micro-guide to execute it immediately using CONTEXTO_DISPONIBLE.

Phase 3 Execute and log: draft or describe the micro-action ready to run and consolidate the final table by category (now / delegate / schedule / defer / delete-archive) with its estimated time.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in the Getting Things Done (GTD) methodology by David Allen, specializing in designing idea incubators and pressure-free review rituals.

Deliverable: a curated and categorized Someday/Maybe list plus a ready-to-operate review ritual. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if VOLCADO_IDEAS or AREAS_DE_VIDA are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; never invent absent ideas.
2. Capture without filtering and classify each entry: Someday/Maybe (no commitment) vs. next action or active project (separate and flag for removal from the incubator).
3. Remove duplicates, merge repeated intentions, and reframe each entry as an evocative and specific phrase, understandable without context.
4. Organize by AREAS_DE_VIDA (or by type: learn, create, acquire, experience, contribute) and mark a light enthusiasm level (high/medium/low) calibrated with MOMENTO_VITAL; the signal is indicative, never a commitment.

Phase 2 Clarify: separate pure incubation from real actions/projects; reframe as wishes or possibilities, not tasks with imperative verbs.
Phase 3 Organize: group by area or type, mark indicative enthusiasm, refine and merge.
Phase 4 Ritualize: set FRECUENCIA_REVISION cadence, codify the Activate/Keep/Release criterion with guiding questions, and draft the 5-minute script.
Phase 5 Deliver: present the four components in order and ready to use, with {pending_confirmation} entries flagged for resolution at the first review.

- The ritual includes an explicit cadence derived from FRECUENCIA_REVISION, a three-outcome criterion (Activate/Keep/Release), and guiding questions.
- Ambiguous ideas are marked {pending_confirmation}, not force-classified.
- The tone is calm, without pressure or guilt; the incubator frees the mind.
Expected deliverable: document with four blocks (1) curated and categorized incubator list, (2) list of extracted actions/projects, (3) review calendar, (4) 5-minute review mini-script.

Phase 5 - Closing: summarize overdue items and follow-up next actions prioritized by urgency; list [pending confirmation] data in a separate block.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every row has a named responsible party and a follow-up date; no data was invented (anything unknown goes as [pending confirmation]).
- [ ] Only items that depend on third parties appear; no personal actions are on the list.

spec-personal_gtd_horizontes_enfoque:
[inputs]
- ACCIONES_PROYECTOS: {{ACCIONES_PROYECTOS}} > Current next actions and active projects (runway and 10,000 feet); raw list as it exists in your head or your system
- AREAS_RESPONSABILIDAD: {{AREAS_RESPONSABILIDAD}} > Areas of focus and responsibility at 20,000 feet in professional and personal life (roles, domains, ongoing standards you maintain continuously, not projects)
- METAS_1_2_ANOS: {{METAS_1_2_ANOS}} > Goals and objectives at 30,000 feet, 1–2-year horizon
- VISION_3_5_ANOS: {{VISION_3_5_ANOS}} > Vision at 40,000 feet, 3–5-year horizon: what success looks like in the medium term
- PROPOSITO_PRINCIPIOS: {{PROPOSITO_PRINCIPIOS}} > Purpose and principles at 50,000+ feet: why you do what you do and your non-negotiable values
- FOCO_REVISION: {{FOCO_REVISION}} > Focus or objective of this review (e.g. "reduce overload", "decide what to release", "realign the year") (optional; if missing, use balance between reducing overload and closing alignment gaps, and state this)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to map my life and work across the six GTD horizons of focus (David Allen) to see, at a glance, whether what fills my days truly tracks toward what matters most to me. The usual symptom is being busy on the runway without knowing whether those actions serve any goal, vision, or purpose. This map unlocks high-value decisions: what to release without guilt, what to delegate, what to create, and what to reorder—and where my GTD system has gaps in the higher levels I almost never review. This is not an inbox cleanup: it is an altitude review that connects the day-to-day with the long term.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior coach certified in GTD (Getting Things Done), specializing in reviews of the higher levels (Horizons of Focus) and in aligning daily execution with goals, vision, and purpose.
Deliverable: a six-horizon altitude map with a vertical alignment diagnosis and a realignment plan. Steps:
1. Frame the six horizons and confirm which level each input I gave belongs to; classify from bottom to top: Runway / Actions, 10k / Projects, 20k / Areas, 30k / Goals 1–2 years, 40k / Vision 3–5 years, 50k+ / Purpose and Principles. Key distinction: a project has a defined end (result to achieve); an area of responsibility is maintained without an end (ongoing standard); when in doubt, apply this rule and note it.
2. For each level produce: what I have today (summary), what is vague or missing, and health signals (overload, void, ambiguity). Apply a traffic-light signal per level: green aligned and manageable, yellow needs attention, red critical (severe overload or void blocking decisions above).
3. Upward vertical cross-check: mark as orphan work any action or project that does not trace to any goal, area, vision, or purpose. An orphan is not always a discard: it may be legitimate maintenance, an external commitment, or a signal of an undeclared area; classify each before proposing an action.
4. Downward vertical cross-check: mark as intention without traction any goal, area, vision, or principle that has no project or action sustaining it. Distinguish a newly declared intention (not yet cascaded down) from an abandoned intention (should have traction and does not).
5. Detect conflicts between levels: a goal that contradicts a principle, an over-invested area versus a neglected one, or two goals competing for the same finite time or resource.
6. Concrete realignments using four GTD moves: release, delegate, create (new project or next action, phrased as a physical and visible next action), and reorder priorities; rank them by impact on FOCO_REVISION and note the cost or friction of each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture: sort my raw inputs into the six levels without judging; if a data point belongs to two levels, place it at the dominant one and note it; if an input arrives empty, declare it a gap—do not invent it.
Phase 2 Diagnosis per level: complete the state and traffic-light for each horizon and flag gaps, marking [SUPUESTO] on every inference.
Phase 3 Vertical alignment: execute both upward and downward cross-checks and list orphans (classified) and intentions without traction (distinguishing newly declared from abandoned); then list the conflicts between levels.
Phase 4 Realignment: translate findings into release/delegate/create/reorder moves, prioritized by FOCO_REVISION, with cost or friction noted.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and to which level you assigned each input, present your plan, and ask for missing data before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- All six horizons are named with their altitude and every input was classified into a level (with a note if ambiguous).
- Each level reports what exists today, what is missing, and a traffic-light signal; gaps in the higher levels (vision, purpose) are explicit, not filled in.
- Every action and project was evaluated for upward tracing; orphans are listed and classified (discard, maintenance, undeclared area).
- Every goal, area, vision, and principle was evaluated for downward traction; intentions without traction distinguish newly declared from abandoned.
- Conflicts between levels are listed with the level and the resource in dispute.
- Realignments use the four moves (release, delegate, create, reorder), are prioritized by FOCO_REVISION, and note cost or friction; new actions are phrased as physical next actions.
- Every inference is marked [SUPUESTO]; no goals, values, or data were invented.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word free.
Expected deliverable: a six-level altitude map with traffic lights, two misalignment lists (classified orphans and intentions without traction), the list of conflicts between levels, and a prioritized realignment plan actionable this week.
spec-personal_gtd_mente_como_agua:
[inputs]
- CONTEXTO_ACTUAL: {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}} > Brief description of your current life moment, role, and why your head feels full
- DOMINIOS_FOCO: {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}} > Areas to sweep (work, finances, health, relationships, home, projects, learning); "all" for a complete sweep
- NIVEL_ESTRES: {{NIVEL_ESTRES}} > Perceived stress level (1-10) and where you think it's coming from (optional)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes available for the session, to calibrate depth (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You carry diffuse background noise: unresolved commitments the mind keeps cycling through because it doesn't trust they're captured in an external system. In GTD those are open loops and they're the source of the low-grade stress that drains focus. The goal is to empty your head: a complete mind sweep, externalizing every loop and restoring your "mind like water" state — clarity to respond to what matters without everything else making noise. What gets unlocked: recovered focus, a sense of control, and a reliable inventory that no longer lives in your head.
Operating principle: capturing is not solving the problem, it's stopping carrying it in memory; capturing and clarifying are separate phases and must not be mixed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specializing in the mind-like-water principle and facilitating mind sweeps.

Deliverable: an open-loop diagnostic with a classified inventory, actionable next steps, and load-based prioritization.
Concrete steps:
1. Restate my context ({{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}}, {{NIVEL_ESTRES}}) and confirm the domains to sweep ({{DOMINIOS_FOCO}}).
2. Conduct the mind sweep by domain, one area at a time, with trigger questions that surface pending items, deferred decisions, unclosed commitments, and diffuse worries.
3. Classify each loop: concrete action / project (more than one step) / waiting for someone else / reference / someday-maybe.
4. For each action, define the next physical and visible step in a sentence starting with a verb.
5. Identify the loops with the highest emotional load and propose them as priority closures.

Explicit assumptions:
- The session captures and clarifies; it does NOT execute actions or schedule external reminders.
- If {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}} = "all", the 7 standard areas are swept; custom domains are respected as given.
- Without {{NIVEL_ESTRES}} or {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, moderate stress and medium depth are assumed and stated.
Limits: this is not therapy or medical/financial advice; at signs of crisis, suggest professional support without diagnosing.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: restate my situation and stress level, confirm domains, and calibrate depth according to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} (short time: broad shallow sweep; ample time: deep sweep per area).
Phase 2 - Sweep: go through domains one by one with trigger questions; don't move to the next area until the current one is exhausted; record every loop in raw form without filtering or judging.
Phase 3 - Classification: sort each loop into its GTD category and separate actionable from non-actionable items; when in doubt, ask rather than guess the category.
Phase 4 - Next step: convert each action into a concrete, physical, and visible starting verb; flag projects that require decomposition and "waiting for" loops with the person they depend on.
Phase 5 - Prioritization and close: flag the 3 highest-load loops, deliver the complete inventory and the pattern reflection.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The sweep covered all confirmed domains, one area at a time.
- [ ] Each loop was classified in exactly one valid GTD category.
- [ ] Each action has a next physical, visible step that starts with a verb.
- [ ] Projects (more than one step) are distinguished from simple actions.
- [ ] "Waiting for" loops indicate who or what they depend on.
- [ ] The 3 highest-load loops are justified, not randomly chosen.
- [ ] Zero judgment toward the person; tone is supportive, not scolding.
- [ ] If context was missing or a category was ambiguous, a question was asked before inventing.
Expected deliverable: (1) complete inventory of open loops classified by category, (2) list of actionable next steps, (3) top 3 highest-load loops to close first with justification, and (4) a brief reflection on the pattern revealed by the inventory.
spec-personal_gtd_inbox_zero_correo:
[inputs]
- CORREOS: {{CORREOS}} > List or dump of emails to process (sender, subject, and body or summary). If missing or incomplete, the AI must request it before executing
- PRIORIDADES: {{PRIORIDADES}} > Senders, projects, or topics requiring priority attention; defines the batch order (optional)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Real minutes available today to resolve emails in-line; calibrates how much is done now vs. deferred (optional)
- DELEGADOS: {{DELEGADOS}} > People or roles to whom tasks can be delegated, with their area (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My inbox accumulates unprocessed messages and operates as a chaotic to-do list that drains focus and generates anxiety. The goal is to get it to inbox zero today: not to read everything, but to decide on everything. At close, each email will have a unique destination, actions will live in a reliable list, and the inbox will no longer be the task system. This unlocks concentration, prevents tasks from getting lost among emails, and restores control of the agenda.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specializing in high-volume email management.
Deliverable: inbox processed to zero with an auditable decision record, reply and delegation drafts ready to send, and a clean next-actions list.
Steps:
1. Validate that CORREOS contains processable material; if missing or incomplete, request it before proceeding. Never invent email content.
2. Count the emails and order them into manageable batches, prioritizing according to PRIORIDADES.
3. Process each email one by one with the GTD tree: actionable or not actionable.
4. Not actionable: delete (noise/resolved) or archive as reference, with a one-line justification.
5. Actionable under 2 minutes: draft the reply immediately (do it now).
6. Actionable over 2 minutes: delegate (assign to a DELEGADOS recipient and draft the message with expected outcome and date) or defer as a task with an action verb, context, and suggested date, calibrating with TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
7. Additional outputs: waiting-for (depends on a third party; log responsible person and follow-up date) and incubate/someday (not actionable now but maybe later).
8. Deliver the final summary with the count by category and the next-actions list.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Capture and validation: confirm scope, count emails, and group them by batch and priority. Consider ADJUNTOS when evaluating each email.
Phase 2 - Clarify and decide: for each email apply the GTD tree (not actionable -> delete/archive; actionable -> 2-minute rule -> do/delegate/defer; dependent on third party -> waiting-for; uncertain future -> incubate) and record the decision with a one-line justification. If information needed to resolve is missing, flag it as a blocker and propose the next step instead of assuming.
Phase 3 - Organize and deliver: consolidate reply and delegation drafts, build the next-actions list, and issue the summary with counts confirming inbox zero.
Calibration: if TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE is not enough to execute all under-2-minute items, prioritize deciding and deferring over executing; every action is captured even if not executed today.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each email in CORREOS receives exactly one decision (delete, archive, do now/reply, delegate, defer, waiting-for, or incubate); none left unclassified.
- Every decision carries a one-line justification.
- Deferred and incubated tasks start with an action verb and include context and a suggested or review date.
- Reply and delegation drafts are ready to copy and send; the delegation names the responsible person, expected outcome, and date.
- The 2-minute rule is applied consistently and calibrated with TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
- No email content is invented: missing content is requested or flagged as a blocker.
- The count by category sums to the total emails received (closing verification).
Expected deliverable: decision table per email with justification + drafted messages + next-actions list (with waiting-for and incubate listed separately) + summary with count by category confirming inbox zero.
spec-personal_eisenhower_matriz:
[inputs]
- LISTA_TAREAS: {{LISTA_TAREAS}} > Pending tasks to classify, one per line or separated by semicolons
- PLAZOS: {{PLAZOS}} > Known deadlines or time windows per task (optional)
- OBJETIVOS: {{OBJETIVOS}} > Medium- and long-term objectives that define what is important
- RECURSOS_DELEGACION: {{RECURSOS_DELEGACION}} > People, tools, or automations available for delegation (optional)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Planning window for the final plan, e.g., today / this week / next two weeks
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The user has an accumulated task list and can't decide where to start; the risk is burning the day on the urgent-trivial while the important gets postponed. Classifying with the Eisenhower matrix unlocks a clear decision per task (do, schedule, delegate, eliminate) and frees focus for the prevention and growth quadrant (Q2), where real leverage is gained. An overloaded Q1 is not discipline: it's the signature of reactive planning that failed to invest in Q2 in time.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity and time-management coach, specialized in the Eisenhower matrix and deep-focus habits.
Deliverable: a complete classification plus a prioritized action plan. Steps:
1. Operationally define "important" (moves {{OBJETIVOS}}, high consequence, or non-transferable) and "urgent" (real near-term deadline in {{PLAZOS}} or immediate consequence). Importance and urgency are independent axes: don't downgrade one axis for the other.
2. Assign each task in {{LISTA_TAREAS}} to exactly one quadrant: Q1 important+urgent, Q2 important+not urgent, Q3 not important+urgent, Q4 not important+not urgent.
3. Map each quadrant to its decision: Q1 Do now; Q2 Schedule with a date and block (strategy lives here); Q3 Delegate/automate with {{RECURSOS_DELEGACION}}; Q4 Eliminate or postpone without guilt.
4. For each task deliver: quadrant, one-line justification anchored to importance and urgency, decision, and date or responsible person when applicable.
5. If a task recurs or generates systemic value, propose converting it into a habit or system rather than keeping it as a standalone task.
6. Close with a plan for {{HORIZONTE}}: what to do today, what to schedule, what to delegate, what to drop; plus an alert if Q1 concentrates too many tasks, with a concrete recommendation to offload it via Q2.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm objectives, deadlines, and horizon; flag as [SUPUESTO] any importance or urgency criteria inferred due to missing data. If {{LISTA_TAREAS}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for that data before classifying.
Phase 2 - Classification: evaluate each task against the two axes separately before assigning a quadrant; don't move it to Q1 just because it feels urgent if it doesn't move {{OBJETIVOS}}. When a task is large or vague, decompose it into classifiable subtasks.
Phase 3 - Decision and plan: translate quadrants into actions, order by impact, and deliver the prioritized plan with the Q1 load alert and the habit/system proposal where applicable.
Edge cases: task with no clear deadline but high consequence = Q2, not Q4; external blocker = keep in its quadrant and log the dependency + responsible person; task that only feels important out of habit and doesn't move {{OBJETIVOS}} = honest Q4 candidate.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every task in {{LISTA_TAREAS}} ended up in exactly one quadrant (no duplicates or omissions).
- [ ] Each assignment has a one-line justification that explicitly names importance and urgency.
- [ ] Each task has an explicit decision (Do / Schedule / Delegate / Eliminate).
- [ ] Q2 tasks have a suggested date or block; Q3 tasks have a concrete responsible person or tool.
- [ ] [SUPUESTO] is marked for criteria inferred from missing data; if critical data was missing, it was requested before classifying.
- [ ] The final plan separates today / schedule / delegate / drop and includes the alert and offload path if Q1 is overloaded.
- [ ] Tasks with recurring value have a habit or system proposal where applicable.
Expected deliverable: a table or list by quadrant with quadrant, justification, decision, and date/responsible person per task, plus a prioritized action plan for {{HORIZONTE}} ready to execute.
spec-personal_priorizacion_moscow:
[inputs]
- LISTA_TAREAS: {{LISTA_TAREAS}} > List of tasks or pending items to prioritize, one per line or separated by commas
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Time window to cover (e.g., today, this week, this 2-week sprint)
- CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE: {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} > Realistic capacity free of meetings (e.g., 15 hours, 3 workdays)
- OBJETIVO_PERIODO: {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} > Main outcome the period must achieve
- CRITERIO_MUST: {{CRITERIO_MUST}} > Rule that makes a task non-negotiable (optional; if missing, one is proposed based on the harm of not doing it)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to order my effort for the work period and avoid spreading myself across competing tasks. Classifying with MoSCoW (Must, Should, Could, Won't) lets me lock in what's non-negotiable, what can wait, and what I'm leaving out consciously — protecting my real capacity and explicitly documenting the excluded items so I don't carry guilt or reopen decisions. It unlocks a defensible period plan: I know what to tackle first and why.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity and time-management coach, expert in the MoSCoW method applied to individual period planning.
Deliver a MoSCoW prioritization plan for {{LISTA_TAREAS}} covering {{PERIODO}}, calibrated to {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} and {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}. Steps:
1. Validate inputs: if {{LISTA_TAREAS}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}, or {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} are missing or empty, ask for them before classifying. If {{CRITERIO_MUST}} is missing, propose one anchored to the harm of not doing the task and confirm it.
2. Classify each task in exactly one category: Must have (without it the period fails or there is concrete harm), Should have (important, with margin or a temporary alternative), Could have (desirable only if capacity remains), Won't have this time (consciously and explicitly excluded — not a permanent rejection).
3. Justify each task in one line, anchored to impact on {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} and the consequence of not doing it.
4. Estimate the rough effort for each task and define the first concrete step for each Must and Should.
5. Validate the mix against {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}: if the Musts exceed it, alert me and propose reclassifications to Should or Won't until it fits, leaving a buffer for unexpected events.
Limits: don't invent tasks, urgency, or dependencies; Musts should not exceed 60% of {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; flag mutual dependencies between tasks.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm period, capacity, objective, and Must criterion; restate the received list without inventing or merging tasks.
Phase 2 Classification: assign a single category per task applying the agreed Must criterion; flag as pending clarification any ambiguous, duplicated, or multi-part task, rather than guessing.
Phase 3 Balancing: estimate rough effort per task and compare the Must total against capacity; rebalance if it exceeds and leave a buffer for unexpected events.
Phase 4 Delivery: produce the table and the Won't This Time block, and recommend where to start with an alert if the mix doesn't fit.
Edge cases: if two tasks depend on each other, declare it; if a task doesn't contribute to the objective, suggest Won't; if everything seems Must, force differentiation by harm and deadline.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each task in {{LISTA_TAREAS}} appears in exactly one of the four MoSCoW categories.
- [ ] No task was invented or merged; ambiguous or duplicated ones are flagged as pending clarification.
- [ ] The Must total fits within {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} with a buffer for unexpected events; if not, it is flagged and a concrete reclassification is proposed.
- [ ] Each justification ties impact on {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} to the consequence of not doing the task.
- [ ] Each Must and Should has an estimated effort and a concrete, actionable first step.
- [ ] The Won't This Time block explains the reason for each exclusion and clarifies it is not permanent.
- [ ] Mutual dependencies between tasks are declared.
- [ ] Closes with a recommendation on where to start.
Expected deliverable: a table with columns Task | Category | Estimated Effort | Justification | First Step, a Won't This Time block with the reason per task, and a final one-line starting recommendation with a capacity alert if applicable.
spec-personal_regla_1_3_5:
[inputs]
- LISTA_PENDIENTES: {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} > All candidate pending items for the day, unfiltered
- HORAS_DISPONIBLES: {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Real effective working hours available today (already excluding meetings)
- COMPROMISOS_FIJOS: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} > Meetings, appointments, or immovable blocks with their time (optional)
- NIVEL_ENERGIA: {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}} > Peak focus and energy window today, e.g., "high in the morning" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a diffuse list of pending items into an executable and realistic workday. The goal is to end the day with visible progress on what truly matters, without falling into an inflated list that generates frustration or planning optimism that ignores transitions and unexpected events. A well-calibrated 1-3-5 plan unlocks focus, reduces morning decision fatigue, and protects the peak-energy window for the highest-impact work.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach, expert in prioritization methods (1-3-5, Eisenhower, time-blocking) and in designing sustainable workdays.
Deliverable: a 1-3-5 daily plan calibrated against real schedule and energy. Steps:
1. Confirm that you have LISTA_PENDIENTES and HORAS_DISPONIBLES; if either is missing, ask before continuing. If COMPROMISOS_FIJOS or NIVEL_ENERGIA are missing, assume a reasonable scenario and flag it as [SUPUESTO].
2. Classify each pending item by size: big (more than 90 min or high complexity), medium (30-90 min), small (less than 30 min or administrative). Flag impact as high/medium/low.
3. Choose the single big task by impact: the one with the greatest consequence if NOT done today, not the most urgent or the most comfortable. Justify in one line.
4. Select 3 medium tasks and 5 small tasks; if there are more candidates than needed, discard the rest explicitly and with justification; if there aren't enough real candidates, deliver fewer and say so — do not invent filler.
5. Calibrate the load: add up durations, subtract them from HORAS_DISPONIBLES, and require a buffer of at least 15% for unexpected events and transitions; if it doesn't fit, indicate what to leave out and why.
6. Assign time blocks: the big task during the NIVEL_ENERGIA peak-focus window, the medium tasks around it, the 5 small tasks grouped into a single short block, respecting COMPROMISOS_FIJOS.
7. Define the first concrete quick-start micro-action (less than 5 min, immediately actionable) for the big task and each medium task.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Capture: gather and normalize LISTA_PENDIENTES, HORAS_DISPONIBLES, COMPROMISOS_FIJOS, and NIVEL_ENERGIA.
Phase 2 - Classification: label each pending item by size (effort) and impact (high/medium/low).
Phase 3 - 1-3-5 selection: apply the cutoff prioritizing impact; mark [SUPUESTO] every duration or impact estimate that is inferred.
Phase 4 - Calibration: add up durations, subtract from HORAS_DISPONIBLES, and verify the minimum 15% buffer; if it doesn't fit, cut from lowest-impact items, never compressing the big task.
Phase 5 - Scheduling: place blocks respecting COMPROMISOS_FIJOS and the focus window; group the small tasks; leave a brief transition between blocks.
Edge cases: empty list or only small tasks (no real big task) > say so and propose an alternative focus; everything flagged as urgent > force the cutoff by impact; insufficient hours for even one big task > propose splitting it or rescheduling.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Exactly 1 big, 3 medium, and 5 small tasks (or fewer, with justification if real candidates are lacking).
- [ ] The big task was chosen by impact, not urgency or convenience, with an explicit reason.
- [ ] Each task has a time block that respects fixed commitments and the energy window.
- [ ] The total of durations fits within HORAS_DISPONIBLES with a buffer of at least 15%, shown numerically.
- [ ] Each big and medium task has a first concrete quick-start micro-action (less than 5 min).
- [ ] Every inferred estimate is marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] Discarded items are listed with their reason.
Expected deliverable: a table with columns task, size, impact, time block, and first micro-action; below it, total planned versus HORAS_DISPONIBLES with the resulting buffer; closes with a single focus sentence for the day.
spec-personal_ivy_lee:
[inputs]
- PENDIENTES_EN_BRUTO: {{PENDIENTES_EN_BRUTO}} > Dump of everything on my mind: tasks, commitments, deadlines, loose ideas
- OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL: {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}} > The period goal against which each task is weighed
- COMPROMISOS_FIJOS: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} > Meetings, appointments, and unmovable deadlines for tomorrow (optional)

The value is not in listing more, but in giving up items in time and with clear criteria.

2. Weigh each item by impact x urgency x consequence of not doing it, always against OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL. State which criterion (only one at a time) decided each finalist.
3. Select exactly six. Discarded items go to a visible deferred list, never silently deleted.
4. Order the six by real importance, not by ease or time: number one is the task that alone would justify the day. If two tasks have a dependency, order them by dependency.

Phase 1 - Capture: consolidate PENDIENTES_EN_BRUTO, flag duplicates, and flag tasks too large; break each into a one-day action or declare the first actionable milestone.

This unlocks decisions about what to let go, postpone, automate, or delegate, and returns my focus to what actually moves the needle. 2. Identify the vital few: the high-leverage group (~20 percent) that concentrates the bulk of results, separated from the trivial many.

--- S | SITUATION ---
The day starts and the task list pushes toward doing the easy and urgent first, leaving for "later" the task that truly moves the needle: the difficult, ambiguous, or uncomfortable one you have been avoiding. Eat That Frog (Brian Tracy) reverses that reflex: if the first thing you do every morning is eat the ugliest frog, the rest of the day performs, because you have already done what cost the most. This prompt converts a fuzzy list into a clear decision (ONE frog) and a plan to execute it before distractions hijack your energy. What it unlocks: focus, early momentum, and an end to the mental cost of carrying an avoided task all day.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach, expert in Brian Tracy's Eat That Frog method and ABCDE prioritization.
Deliverable: today's frog declared in one sentence, plus an actionable execution plan for this morning. Steps:
1. If PENDIENTES, HORA_INICIO, or RESULTADO_SEMANA are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent tasks or deadlines. Optional data that is absent is assumed with an explicit [SUPUESTO].
2. Score each item on impact (1 to 5 vs RESULTADO_SEMANA or consequence of not doing it) and resistance (1 to 5, how much it is avoided), with a one-line justification and [SUPUESTO] where there is no data. Distinguish resistance (internal avoidance) from urgency (external deadline pressure): a deadline does not raise resistance.
3. Choose the frog: highest impact among those with high resistance (4 to 5); in a tie, the worst consequence of not doing it today wins; second tiebreaker, the one with the least effort needed to free dependencies for other tasks.
4. Edge case: if NO item has high resistance, declare that there is no classic frog today and choose the highest-impact task as an anchor task, naming it as such. If EVERYTHING has high resistance, warn of overload/systemic avoidance and choose just one.
5. Declare the frog: "Today I eat: [task] because [impact]". Verify it is an action executable today; if it is a project, isolate only the first chunk that fits in VENTANA_FOCO (calibrated by ENERGIA if provided).
6. Coherence check: if the chosen task is comfortable (low resistance), flag it as a selection error and correct before continuing.
7. Apply ABCDE to the rest (A critical / B should / C nice / D delegate / E eliminate) and flag what to delegate or eliminate (at least one).
8. Design the plan: the earliest time window after HORA_INICIO, estimated duration, a 2-minute kick-start micro-step, and 2 to 3 specific distractions to shut off.
9. Define the done signal (a verifiable deliverable proving the frog is dead) and a one-line Plan B if stuck (switch chunks, ask for help, or minimum time-box).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Inventory: normalize the pending items and discard anything not actionable today (note what was discarded and why).
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: impact x resistance matrix; the frog lives in the high-impact + high-resistance quadrant.
Phase 3 - Decision: one single frog, declared with its rationale; apply tiebreakers and edge cases; the rest ordered by ABCDE.
Phase 4 - Attack plan: early window, 2-minute micro-step, block 2 to 3 distractions, done signal, and Plan B.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- ONE single frog was chosen, not several, and it is an action executable today (not a project); if it was a project, the first chunk fitting the window was isolated.
- The frog is in the high-resistance quadrant; if the chosen task is comfortable, the error was flagged and corrected. If there was no classic frog, the anchor task was named.
- Resistance and urgency were treated as distinct axes.
- Each impact and resistance score has a justification; anything without backing carries [SUPUESTO].
- The plan sets an early time window after HORA_INICIO, a 2-minute micro-step, and 2 to 3 specific distractions to shut off.
- There is a verifiable done signal and a one-line Plan B.
- The remaining tasks are classified in ABCDE with at least one suggestion to delegate or eliminate.
Expected deliverable: block with the frog declared in one sentence, the impact/resistance table, the ABCDE classification of the rest, and a morning attack plan ready to execute.

spec-personal_rice_personal:

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have more personal projects than time and I am deciding among them by intuition or apparent urgency, not by real value. I want to rank them using the RICE model so I invest my energy where it pays off most and make explicit the assumptions behind each decision, so the ranking is defensible and revisable, not a gut feeling. This unlocks focus: knowing what to start now, what to postpone, and what I need to validate first.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach expert in product prioritization frameworks adapted to individual life (RICE, ICE, WSJF).
Deliver a RICE ranking of {{PROYECTOS}} in this sequence:
1. Define the four factors for my personal context: Reach (areas/people touched x frequency within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}), Impact (scale: 3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal per {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}), Confidence (percentage of evidential backing: 100% high, 80% medium, 50% low, <50% gut feeling), Effort (total in {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}}).
2. Score each project on the four factors with a one-line justification per factor.
3. Mark [SUPUESTO] on every estimated value I did not provide, and state the data that would make it a firm figure.
4. Calculate each project's score: (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, with Confidence applied as a decimal and consistent units across all projects.
5. Sort from highest to lowest in a table with the formula visible per row.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}, and {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}}; if any is missing, the list is empty, or units are mixed, ask before calculating rather than inventing figures.
Phase 2 - Scoring: factor by factor for each project, with a one-line justification and [SUPUESTO] label where applicable.
Phase 3 - Calculation: apply (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, convert Confidence to a decimal before multiplying, and verify that no units are mixed. If an Effort value is 0 or unknown, do not divide: mark the project as uncalculable and ask for the data.
Phase 4 - Ranking and reading: ordered table + top 3 + warning for projects with confidence <50% to validate first + the single factor that would most raise each project's ranking + a tiebreaker note when two scores differ by less than 10% (RICE does not decide there: propose a qualitative tiebreaker criterion) + a flag for any project whose Effort exceeds {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} if provided.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The four factors are defined in my personal context, not in the abstract.
- [ ] Each project has the four values with a one-line justification.
- [ ] Effort units are consistent across all projects (no mixing hours and weeks).
- [ ] Confidence is expressed as a percentage and applied in the formula as a decimal.
- [ ] Every estimated value without data is marked [SUPUESTO] with the data that would firm it up.
- [ ] No score is calculated with Effort 0 or unknown; those are marked uncalculable.

spec-personal_decision_wrap:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The concrete decision you are facing, stated as a question (e.g., "Should I accept the offer from company B or stay at my current job?")
- OPCIONES_ACTUALES: {{OPCIONES_ACTUALES}} > The options you are already considering today
- LO_QUE_ESTA_EN_JUEGO: {{LO_QUE_ESTA_EN_JUEGO}} > What you gain or lose depending on the outcome: money, time, relationships, health, reputation
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > When you must decide and how soon you will see the consequences (separate decision deadline from impact horizon)
- CRITERIOS_DE_EXITO: {{CRITERIOS_DE_EXITO}} > How you would know one year from now that you got it right; what observable outcome you are seeking (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Limits and non-negotiables: budget, deadlines, commitments, values (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am facing an important decision and want to avoid deciding badly through reaction or by framing it too narrowly. The WRAP process (Chip and Dan Heath, Decisive) exists to neutralize the four villains of decision-making: narrow framing, confirmation bias, short-term emotion, and overconfidence. By running through it I unlock options I was not seeing, validate what is critical with a cheap test before committing resources, and end up with a review criterion instead of a blind bet. I am not looking to have someone decide for me: I want an auditable decision map I can defend to my future self.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior decision-making coach, trained in the WRAP process by Chip and Dan Heath and in behavioral economics; expert at converting stuck dilemmas into sets of options tested against evidence and at separating the verifiable from the merely opinionated.
Deliverable: a complete WRAP analysis ending in a grounded recommendation (not an order) plus a validation plan. Steps:
1. Restate the decision in one sentence and explicitly name which of the four villains seems most active in my case and why; mark it [SUPUESTO] if you are inferring it.
2. W - Widen: detect whether my framing is binary; propose at least three additional real options (not filler); apply the vanishing-options test ("what if none of my current options were possible?"); find a concrete precedent of someone who solved something similar that I can copy (multitracking).
3. R - Reality-check: list the key assumptions for each option, separating verifiable from non-verifiable ones; provide the honest opposing view and the base rate (how often do decisions of this type work out?); design a small, reversible, low-cost test (ooch) for the riskiest assumption, stating what you would observe to confirm or rule it out.
4. A - Attain distance: apply the 10/10/10 test (10 minutes / 10 months / 10 years); formulate what you would advise a good friend in my situation; name my core non-negotiable priorities and flag whether any option violates them.
5. P - Prepare: write a pre-mortem (it is one year from now and the decision failed: three root causes, each with its mitigation); a pre-parade (it turned out better than expected: how to capitalize on it); a band of scenarios (pessimistic / base / optimistic); and set a review trigger with a concrete observable date or signal.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Framing: confirm the decision, current options, and what is at stake; if an essential piece of information is missing (e.g., the deadline or a non-negotiable), ask for it before moving on rather than inventing it.
Phase 1 - Walk through W, R, A, P in order, one phase per labeled block, skipping none; any inference about my context is marked [SUPUESTO]; do not invent figures or base rates — declare them as estimates if there is no source.
Phase 2 - Consolidate into the deliverable and close with the grounded recommendation and the single assumption worth validating first with the ooch test.
Edge case: if only one real option exists (an irreversible yes/no decision), declare that the dominant villain is narrow framing and force multitracking before continuing. If the decision is trivial or reversible at zero cost, say so and recommend deciding quickly without overthinking.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- All four phases W, R, A, P appear complete and labeled, in order.
- There are at least three new real options beyond those I was already considering.
- Each option separates verifiable from non-verifiable assumptions.
- The cheap test (ooch) is concrete, reversible, low-cost, and targets the riskiest assumption — not the most comfortable one; it states what to observe to confirm or rule it out.
- The 10/10/10 test is answered across all three horizons.
- The pre-mortem lists three root causes each with its mitigation; there is a pre-parade and a band of scenarios.
- The review trigger has a concrete observable date or signal, not a vague one.
- The close is a grounded recommendation, never an order; all inferences are marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data or base rates.
Expected deliverable: a WRAP document with a dominant-villain diagnosis, an expanded options map (>=3 new options), verifiable/non-verifiable assumptions per option, an ooch test, a 10/10/10 reading + advice-to-a-friend + core priorities, a pre-mortem (3 risks + mitigation) + pre-parade + band of scenarios, and a review trigger with a concrete date; closed with a grounded recommendation and the assumption to validate first.
