--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist (acceptance criteria):
- [ ] The tiny version genuinely takes <30s and does not depend on high motivation or prior preparation.
- [ ] The recipe uses the literal formula "After [routine], I will [tiny habit]" with a daily, specific prompt that has a crisp end.
- [ ] The celebration is immediate (within 3s), genuine, and consistent with ESTILO_CELEBRACION; an alternative is provided if the first one feels uncomfortable.
- [ ] The 3-step growth ladder advances by achieved automaticity (not by dates) and unambiguously targets META_FINAL.
- [ ] 2 concrete obstacles are anticipated with actionable adjustments (anchor redesign or further reduction, not 'try harder').
- [ ] Assumptions and limits declared; referral to a professional if the habit is sensitive.
- [ ] If key data were missing, they were asked before delivering.
Expected deliverable: (1) recipe table (tiny habit | prompt/anchor | celebration); (2) 3-step growth ladder with the automaticity criterion that triggers each step up; (3) list of 2 obstacles with their adjustment; (4) first-week script (what to do each day D1–D7) with a day-7 self-assessment of 3 questions: I did it without an external reminder, it took <30s, I felt the celebration; and the decision rule for moving up, staying, or scaling down a step.
spec-personal_diseno_entorno:
[inputs]
- HABITO_DESEADO: {{HABITO_DESEADO}} > Habit to install, as an observable behavior (e.g., read 10 min, drink water, walk 20 min)
- HABITO_A_REDUCIR: {{HABITO_A_REDUCIR}} > Habit to reduce and its acceptable threshold (e.g., social media to under 30 min/day)
- ENTORNOS: {{ENTORNOS}} > Physical and digital spaces where they occur (desk, kitchen, phone, bedroom, browser)
- SENAL_DISPARADOR: {{SENAL_DISPARADOR}} > Cue, moment, or emotion that precedes each habit (time, place, state, prior habit)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Limits to respect: no buying, no moving furniture, housemates, remote work (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Willpower is a depletable resource; the environment determines most default behaviors. Redesigning the physical and digital space turns the desired habit into the path of least resistance and makes the habit to reduce costly, without relying on daily motivation. Guiding principle: behavior is a function of making the good thing obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying, and making the unwanted thing invisible, difficult, and unsatisfying. By the end there will be an environment redesign plan executable today, with no indispensable purchases, and an observable indicator to verify in seven days whether the environment has started working in your favor.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior behavior designer specializing in choice architecture and habit formation (B.J. Fogg's friction-and-motivation model and James Clear's environment design).
Deliverable: layered environment redesign plan. Steps:
1. Friction map: for HABITO_DESEADO and HABITO_A_REDUCIR, break down current steps from the trigger and estimate seconds or number of decisions per step; mark the highest-friction step.
2. Five friction-reduction interventions for HABITO_DESEADO: bring the cue closer to the point of use, leave the object visible and ready, reduce to one step (two-minute rule), pre-commit the night before, anchor to an existing habit (stacking).
3. Five friction-increase interventions for HABITO_A_REDUCIR: hide or unplug the trigger, add steps or delays, remove the app from the home screen and log out, social or commitment friction, separate device or account.
4. Concrete redesign for each ENTORNO in ENTORNOS: exact object placement and recommended digital configuration (location, visibility, notifications, access).
5. Single-change rule to start today (highest impact, lowest effort) plus an observable, measurable seven-day indicator with a success threshold and a plan B if it doesn't move the needle.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Diagnosis: confirm HABITO_DESEADO, HABITO_A_REDUCIR, ENTORNOS, and SENAL_DISPARADOR; if any is missing or the trigger is vague, ask before continuing. Do not invent routines; mark every inference about the current routine with [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 – Friction map: break each habit down into steps from the trigger and quantify the cost per step (seconds or decisions).
Phase 3 – Interventions: design the five reduction and five increase interventions, respecting RESTRICCIONES and prioritizing free and reversible options; if an intervention conflicts with a housemate or work setup, offer a variant.
Phase 4 – Redesign by environment: translate interventions into concrete physical placement and digital configuration per environment; flag conflicts between environments (e.g., phone used for both the desired and the unwanted habit).
Phase 5 – Activation and verification: define the single-change rule and the seven-day indicator with threshold and plan B.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each habit has a friction map with estimated cost per step and the highest-friction step identified.
- Five reduction and five increase interventions, all actionable today and tied to a step in the map.
- Redesign covers all declared ENTORNOS, physical and digital, with concrete placement and configuration.
- No intervention requires an indispensable purchase; RESTRICCIONES respected and conflicts with housemates or work resolved.
- Inferences about the routine marked [SUPUESTO]; the plan does not depend on motivation or willpower.
- Single-change rule is clear (high impact, low effort) and the seven-day indicator is observable, measurable, with a success threshold and a plan B.
Expected deliverable: environment redesign document with friction map per habit, ten prioritized interventions, plan by environment, starting rule, and seven-day verification indicator.
spec-personal_recompensa_habito:
[inputs]
- HABITO: {{HABITO}} > The behavior you want to consolidate, described as a concrete, repeatable action (e.g., "meditate for 5 minutes", "write 200 words"). If it arrives vague ("exercise"), ask or propose a measurable version.
- SENAL_DISPARADORA: {{SENAL_DISPARADORA}} > The trigger that should start the routine: time, place, prior event, or emotional state ("(optional)" if you don't have one yet and want help defining it; in that case, propose an anchor tied to an already-established habit).
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} > Where and when the habit occurs, and constraints present (at home in the morning, at the office, short on time, family around, no privacy). These constraints filter which rewards are viable.
- FUENTE_MOTIVACION: {{FUENTE_MOTIVACION}} > What type of gratification moves you most: sensory, social, seeing progress, feeling closure or achievement ("(optional)" if you want the system to infer it from your answers and declare it as an assumption).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am trying to consolidate a habit but it is not sticking: I do it for a few days and then it fades when motivation drops. The probable cause is an incomplete behavioral loop: the cue and the routine exist, but the reward that closes the cycle is delayed or intangible, so the brain does not mark the behavior as desirable and never builds the craving that makes the habit automatic. Closing that loop with an immediate reward converts discipline into attraction: it stops depending on willpower and starts sustaining itself. What gets unlocked is a habit that persists without conscious effort and a reusable design pattern for future habits. Scope: this method applies to low-friction, daily-repetition habits; habits involving clinical dependency, real physical pain, or structural barriers (no time, no access) require environment redesign before reward design, and that should be flagged, not forced.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior behavioral designer specializing in habit formation, trained in the habit loop model (cue-routine-reward) and in behavior design through immediate positive reinforcement.
Deliverable: a system of immediate rewards for my habit, plus a one-week protocol to test it. Steps:
1. Reformulate my habit into its three components: cue (what triggers it), routine (the action), and current reward, flagging whether the reward today is absent, delayed, or intangible. If the cue arrives as (optional), propose it anchored to an already-established habit.
2. Diagnose why the loop is not closing: identify whether the gratification arrives too late to associate with the routine, or is so abstract the brain does not register it. If the real blockage is friction or context (not reward), say so explicitly and recommend adjusting the environment first.
3. Propose 4 to 6 immediate candidate rewards, each deliverable within 60 seconds of completing the routine, none contradicting the purpose of the habit (coherence rule: do not reward the habit with something that sabotages it) and none that escalates tolerance or becomes a costly obligation (sustainability rule). Prioritize rewards viable within my context constraints.
4. Classify each reward by type (sensory, social, visible progress, ritual closure) and intensity (low/medium/high), and indicate which best fits my motivation source. If the source was given as (optional), infer it from my answers and declare the assumption.
5. Define a concrete celebration trigger: the exact gesture, phrase, or action that marks the closing of the loop the instant the routine ends, and explain why that gesture is immediate and emotionally positive.
6. Deliver a 7-day protocol with the chosen reward, daily application instructions, an observable automaticity measurement signal to know whether the habit is starting to feel automatic, and a contingency plan: what to do if I skip a day (without mentally breaking the streak) and how to fade the reward once the habit sustains itself.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Loop mapping: break the habit into cue, routine, and current reward; explicitly name the broken link. Declare assumptions taken about context and mark unconfirmed items as {to_confirm}.
Phase 2 – Generation and filtering: generate immediate reward candidates; discard those that arrive late, are intangible, contradict the purpose, or are not sustainable; keep only those that meet the 60-second rule, the coherence rule, and the sustainability rule. Document one line per discarded candidate and why.
Phase 3 – Selection and ritualization: choose the reward with the best motivational and contextual fit, design its celebration trigger, and package the 7-day protocol with its measurement signal and contingency plan.
Edge case: if fewer than 4 viable candidates remain after filtering, say so, explain which constraint caused it, and propose how to relax it or change the context rather than inventing weak rewards.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The habit is broken into cue, routine, and reward, with the broken link named.
- [ ] The diagnosis distinguishes a delayed reward from an intangible reward, and flags whether the real blockage is friction or context.
- [ ] There are between 4 and 6 candidate rewards, all deliverable within 60 seconds; if fewer than 4 were viable, it is explained why.
- [ ] No reward contradicts the purpose of the habit (coherence) or escalates tolerance or obligation (sustainability), verified one by one.
- [ ] Each reward is classified by type and intensity and linked to my motivation source (declared as an assumption if inferred).
- [ ] The celebration trigger is a concrete, observable gesture, not a vague intention.
- [ ] The 7-day protocol includes an observable automaticity measurement signal, a plan for a skipped day, and a reward-fading plan.
- [ ] Context assumptions are declared and unconfirmed items are marked {to_confirm}.
Expected deliverable: a document with (a) the mapped loop, (b) the table of 4–6 classified rewards (with the discarded ones and their reason), (c) the chosen reward with its concrete celebration trigger, and (d) the 7-day protocol with its measurement signal and contingency plan.
spec-personal_recuperar_habito_roto:
[inputs]
- HABITO: {{HABITO}} > Habit you want to resume (e.g., run 3 times a week, meditate 10 min, write every morning)
- TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION: {{TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION}} > How long ago the streak broke (e.g., 5 days, 3 weeks, almost a month)
- DISPARADOR_RECAIDA: {{DISPARADOR_RECAIDA}} > What you think triggered the interruption (e.g., a trip, a stressful week, lost motivation)
- MOTIVACION: {{MOTIVACION}} > Why returning to this habit matters to you (the identity or outcome you are seeking)
- DISPONIBILIDAD_DIARIA: {{DISPONIBILIDAD_DIARIA}} > (optional) Realistic time you can dedicate today and in the coming days
- HISTORIAL_RACHAS: {{HISTORIAL_RACHAS}} > (optional) Previous times you broke and resumed this habit; helps distinguish a one-off failure from a pattern
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You broke a streak of {{HABITO}} {{TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION}} ago and guilt threatens to turn a one-time failure into permanent abandonment. The goal is NOT to recover the lost volume or punish yourself, but to return to the behavior today and safeguard the system so that a future failure never becomes two in a row. What gets unlocked: you recover the identity ("I am someone who does this") with the lowest possible friction and leave with a plan that survives future relapses. Guiding principle: the never-miss-twice rule. Key insight: what erodes a habit is not the isolated failure but the guilt spiral that follows it; this is why self-compassion predicts resumption better than willpower.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior habit-formation and habit-recovery coach, trained in applied behavioral science (atomic habits, implementation intentions, and self-compassion as a predictor of resumption).
Deliver an actionable return plan in these numbered steps:
1. Guilt-free reframing: separate the objective fact from the judgment narrative and state the never-miss-twice rule as the guiding compass for the session.
2. Trigger diagnosis: analyze {{DISPARADOR_RECAIDA}} using the antecedent-behavior-consequence (ABC) framework to find the real cause, not the surface one. Classify it as a one-off trigger (extraordinary context that has already passed) or recurring pattern (use {{HISTORIAL_RACHAS}} if available); the design changes depending on the case.
3. Minimum viable return: define the smallest version of {{HABITO}} executable today in under two minutes, prioritizing recovering the identity over volume. Give the exact version for today, not a range.
4. Environment safeguard: write an implementation intention (when X happens, I will do Y in place Z) and remove one concrete friction from the environment, adjusted to {{DISPONIBILIDAD_DIARIA}}. If the diagnosis revealed a recurring pattern, the safeguard must attack that antecedent, not just the one from this episode.
5. Future relapse protocol: specify what you will do the next day you fail to guarantee you will not fail twice in a row, and include an early warning signal of risk (the first observable hint that you are on your way to failing) so you can intervene beforehand.
6. Closing commitment: a single line, measurable, with a 24-hour deadline.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Reframing: neutralize guilt and set the principle. Phase 2 Diagnosis: ABC on the relapse + one-off vs. pattern classification. Phase 3 Minimum viable design: reduce until almost-ridiculous, exact version for today. Phase 4 Environment safeguard: implementation intention + friction reduction aligned to the real antecedent. Phase 5 No-double-failure plan with early warning signal + measurable commitment. Stay direct, warm, and without moralizing; no appeals to willpower or "get motivated." Edge cases: if {{TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION}} is very long (weeks or more), do not assume the habit is still active: treat the return as a restart from scratch, not as picking up where you left off. If the habit itself seems harmful or no longer serves {{MOTIVACION}}, say so and propose revisiting it before blindly resuming. If a piece of data is ambiguous, mark the assumption as [SUPUESTO] and continue, or ask if it blocks the plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The reframing separates fact from narrative and explicitly cites the never-miss-twice rule.
- The diagnosis uses antecedent-behavior-consequence, points to the real cause, and classifies the trigger as one-off or pattern.
- The minimum viable return is a single version executable today in under two minutes and prioritizes identity over volume.
- The implementation intention has a when-then-where format, attacks the real antecedent, and one concrete friction is removed.
- The no-double-failure protocol is specific and operational (not a good intention) and includes an early warning signal of risk.
- The final commitment is a single line, measurable, and has a 24-hour deadline.
- Zero guilt, zero appeals to willpower, zero vague promises.
Expected deliverable: habit return plan in 6 numbered blocks, ready to execute today, with a 24-hour commitment at the close.
spec-personal_revision_habitos_mensual:
[inputs]
- LISTA_HABITOS: {{LISTA_HABITOS}} > Habits you tried to maintain this month with their target frequency (e.g., "meditate 10 min daily; run 3x/week")
- REGISTRO_CUMPLIMIENTO: {{REGISTRO_CUMPLIMIENTO}} > Actual compliance per habit as a percentage or number of days, even if estimated
- RESULTADOS_OBJETIVO: {{RESULTADOS_OBJETIVO}} > Life outcome each habit was meant to serve (e.g., "sleep better", "advance the project")
- FRICCIONES_DEL_MES: {{FRICCIONES_DEL_MES}} > Frictions, trips, illness, or events that affected consistency (optional)
- CAPACIDAD_PROXIMO_MES: {{CAPACIDAD_PROXIMO_MES}} > Realistic number of habits to sustain next month (optional; if missing, assume the lower of the number of Keep+Recalibrate habits and mark [SUPUESTO])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
End of month: you need to decide with evidence which habits to keep, recalibrate, pause, or eliminate, rather than dragging an inflated system along by inertia. A rigorous review turns a month of data into a lighter, more sustainable system, frees energy trapped in habits that are not delivering, and prevents total abandonment from overload. The bias to overcome: reading low consistency as a character flaw when it is almost always a design problem (high friction, absent cue, or poorly calibrated ambition).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior behavior-change and habit-design coach, with mastery of the habit loop (cue, craving, response, reward) and Fogg's behavior model (B=MAP: Motivation, Ability, Prompt).

Deliverable: an actionable monthly review. Steps:
1. Inventory: list each habit from LISTA_HABITOS with its target frequency and compliance rate from REGISTRO_CUMPLIMIENTO. Normalize to a comparable percentage (days completed / days targeted).
2. B=MAP diagnosis: for each habit, explain why it was or was not completed by naming the dominant bottleneck (motivation, ability/friction, or prompt) and, if applicable, the secondary one. Cross-reference with FRICCIONES_DEL_MES to separate structural design failures from circumstantial ones (a single trip does not condemn a habit).
3. Classification: assign each habit to Keep (high compliance and serves an active outcome), Recalibrate (active outcome but design fails), Pause (active outcome, capacity absent this month), or Eliminate (obsolete or duplicate outcome). Explicit criterion tied to compliance and the RESULTADOS_OBJETIVO it serves.
4. Overload: detect habits competing for the same cue, time of day, or energy reserve; name each collision. If the system exceeds CAPACIDAD_PROXIMO_MES, propose a prioritized cutback by impact-on-outcome / maintenance-cost ratio.
5. Recalibration: build the next month's system within capacity. Define each habit by a concrete cue (anchored to an existing anchor habit or moment), a minimum viable size (2-minute version to overcome friction), and a binary tracking metric.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Measure: tabulate compliance per habit. Phase 2 Diagnose: apply B=MAP to each one, without attributing anything to "lack of discipline." Phase 3 Decide: classify with explicit criteria. Phase 4 Lighten: resolve overload and cue collisions. Phase 5 Redesign: deliver the recalibrated system. Edge cases: if only one data point exists (no compliance data), work on design and declare the limit; if the entire system is <40% compliant, suspect global overload before going habit by habit; if two habits serve the same outcome, evaluate merging them. Mark every piece of data not provided as [SUPUESTO] or ask before continuing; do not invent the log.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each habit has a normalized compliance rate and a B=MAP diagnosis with the dominant bottleneck named.
- [ ] The diagnosis separates design failures from circumstantial failures by cross-referencing FRICCIONES_DEL_MES.
- [ ] Each habit is classified (Keep/Recalibrate/Pause/Eliminate) with an explicit criterion, not by preference.
- [ ] Each decision is tied to the RESULTADOS_OBJETIVO the habit serves; obsolete or duplicate outcomes are named.
- [ ] Overload and cue collisions are evaluated; the final system respects CAPACIDAD_PROXIMO_MES.
- [ ] Each recalibrated habit has a concrete anchored cue, a minimum viable size, and a binary metric.
- [ ] Missing data marked [SUPUESTO] or requested; zero invented log.
- [ ] No generic motivational advice: every recommendation tied to a habit and its cause.
Expected deliverable: decision table per habit (habit · compliance · B=MAP bottleneck · classification · criterion) + next month's recalibrated system (cue · minimum size · metric) + the three highest-impact levers.
spec-personal_zettelkasten_nota:
[inputs]
- IDEA_CRUDA: {{IDEA_CRUDA}} > Idea, insight, or reading excerpt recently captured that you want to convert into a permanent note
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Origin of the idea: book and author, paper, conversation, or "original" if it is your own thought
- NOTAS_EXISTENTES: {{NOTAS_EXISTENTES}} > Titles or IDs of notes already present in your network to link to (optional; if empty, tentative neighboring concepts are proposed)
- AREA_DE_INTERES: {{AREA_DE_INTERES}} > Research line, topic, or project this note should serve (optional)
- TIPO_NOTA: {{TIPO_NOTA}} > "permanent" (default) or "fleeting" if it is still an immature capture you only want to prepare for maturing (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A Zettelkasten network only generates value when each note is atomic, written in your own words, and connected to others through meaningful links; literal captures with no links accumulate as dead archive. Properly distilling this IDEA_CRUDA into a permanent note unlocks unexpected connections between AREA_DE_INTERES and notes you already have, the foundation of thinking that writes for you over time. Explicit limit: the quality of links depends on the fidelity of NOTAS_EXISTENTES; if input is sparse, neighboring concepts are marked tentative and no IDs are invented.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal knowledge management specialist, trained in Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten method and in Sonke Ahrens' principles ("How to Take Smart Notes": atomicity, autonomy, original formulation, deliberate linking).
Deliver ONE paste-ready note. Steps:
1. Identify the single concept of IDEA_CRUDA in one sentence; if there are two or more mixed ideas, separate them, note the fragmentation, and propose one note per idea (atomicity).
2. Rewrite the idea as a self-contained prose statement in your own words, without copying literally from FUENTE, understandable without external context.
3. Draft a declarative title that expresses the complete assertion (not a topic label): it should read as a thesis.
4. Propose 2 to 4 links toward NOTAS_EXISTENTES; for each link write a line justifying the relationship with a verb (continues / contradicts / exemplifies / generalizes / qualifies). If NOTAS_EXISTENTES is empty, propose plausible neighboring concepts and mark them [tentative]; never invent IDs that look real.
5. Close with an open question that keeps the note alive, connected to AREA_DE_INTERES.
6. Include the reference to FUENTE on a line at the bottom.
Type decision: if TIPO_NOTA is "fleeting" or the idea is subjective, anecdotal, or unverifiable, mark it as a fleeting note, drop the requirement for a closed thesis, and suggest what criterion it must meet to graduate to permanent.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 Validate inputs: if IDEA_CRUDA or FUENTE are missing, or if the idea is too vague to distill, ask in a single batch before drafting.
Phase 1 Distill: isolate the core of IDEA_CRUDA and verify atomicity (one note = one idea).
Phase 2 Reformulate: translate into your own voice; verify the body is understandable without opening the source.
Phase 3 Link: search for neighbors in NOTAS_EXISTENTES and justify each connection with a relation verb; discard redundant links (two that contribute the same nexus).
Phase 4 Open: formulate the living question and anchor the note to AREA_DE_INTERES.
Assumed trade-off: when in doubt between over-atomizing or under-atomizing, prioritize one clear note over several weak ones, leaving branches as tentative links.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The note contains ONE single idea (atomic); extra ideas were separated into their own notes with a fragmentation notice.
- [ ] The body is in your own words, with no literal copy from FUENTE, and is self-contained (understandable without opening the source).
- [ ] The title is declarative (a thesis), not a topic label.
- [ ] There are 2 to 4 links, each with a relation verb that justifies WHY it connects; no redundant links.
- [ ] Links without a real note are marked [tentative] and no IDs were invented.
- [ ] There is an open question aligned with AREA_DE_INTERES.
- [ ] The reference to FUENTE appears at the bottom.
- [ ] If the idea was fleeting or unverifiable, it was marked as such with a graduation criterion.
Expected deliverable: note block with declarative title, atomic body, list of justified links, source reference, and open question, ready to paste into your note-taking system.
spec-personal_para_organizacion_archivos:
[inputs]
- INVENTARIO_ACTUAL: {{INVENTARIO_ACTUAL}} > List of main folders, documents, and notes you want to organize
- CONTEXTO_PERSONAL: {{CONTEXTO_PERSONAL}} > Your role, life, or work, to correctly interpret what is actionable for you
- OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS: {{OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS}} > Goals with closing dates you are pursuing now; basis for identifying Projects
- HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO: {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}} > Where the system lives (Notion, Drive, Obsidian, Finder, other) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You have accumulated and scattered folders, documents, and notes, organized by topic or with no order, which makes it slow to find what matters and dilutes actionable items among dead reference. Tiago Forte's PARA method classifies everything by actionability, not topic: how soon you need to act on something decides where it lives. Reorganizing this way unlocks a navigable system where items that demand action (Projects, Areas) are separated from those that are only consulted (Resources, Archive). This migration map feeds your weekly review and your ability to find any file in seconds.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal knowledge management specialist, with years of applying Tiago Forte's PARA method to reorganize chaotic digital systems by actionability.
Deliverable: a PARA migration map in a table, a pending-decisions section, and a maintenance guide, classifying each element into Projects, Areas, Resources, or Archive. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if INVENTARIO_ACTUAL, CONTEXTO_PERSONAL, or OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before moving forward; never invent folders or assume the situation.
2. Classify each element using the actionability test in strict order, stopping at the first that applies: goal with closing date, Project; ongoing standard with no end, Area; useful reference with no action now, Resource; inactive in all three, Archive.
3. Build the migration table with element, category, destination path, and reason in one line, with Projects first.
4. Isolate ambiguous items, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates for the user's decision, and deliver the maintenance guide.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Inventory: gather and group the elements of INVENTARIO_ACTUAL; resolve ambiguities by asking, not inferring. Mark [SUPUESTO] any data inferred without confirmation.
Phase 2 Classification by actionability: apply the test to each element in the order Project, Area, Resource, Archive. A Project always has a goal and an end (falls to Archive or to its Area when closed); an Area is sustained with no date; a Resource is only consulted; Archive is inactive from the three. Edge rules: what fits two goes to the more actionable category; the same topic can be split (active part to Project, reference to Resource); avoid catch-all Areas: if a folder mixes multiple purposes, split it; do not classify by topic (a marketing PDF can be Project, Resource, or Archive depending on when you need it). Justify each decision in one line with the test that determined it.
Phase 3 Map and maintenance: sort the table with Projects at the top; separate a pending-decisions section for ambiguous items, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates; close with three maintenance steps that include the weekly review of Projects to move completed ones to Archive and an Inbox to process new items before they scatter.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each element is in a single category, decided by actionability and not by topic.
- The four categories respect their canonical definition: Project with goal and date, Area with no end, Resource with no action now, Archive inactive.
- Each assignment has its reason in one line (the test that decided it) and inferred data carries [SUPUESTO].
- Projects appear first; ambiguous items, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates are isolated for the user's decision, without forcing a classification.
- The maintenance guide is executable and includes the weekly review of Projects and an Inbox for new items.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis; no prices; without the word "free".
Expected deliverable: PARA migration table (element, category, destination path, reason) with Projects at the top, a pending-decisions section, and a three-step maintenance guide; close with one line on what additional data would make the map even more precise.
spec-personal_notas_cornell:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Subject or title of the material to process (e.g. "Krebs Cycle", "Monetary policy")
- MATERIAL_FUENTE: {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} > Content to convert: class transcript, reading text, raw notes, video summary, or meeting notes
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > Desired granularity: overview (key ideas only), standard (ideas plus supporting data), or exhaustive (nuances, examples, and exceptions)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > (optional) What the notes will be used for: exam, periodic review, teaching others. If empty: general review
- NUM_PREGUNTAS: {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} > (optional) Number of active review questions to generate (default 5)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to transform {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} on {{TEMA}} into notes that actually serve for studying, not into a text dump I never reread. The Cornell method (Walter Pauk, Cornell University) divides the page into three zones that force active processing: Notes (capture), Cues (retrieval prompts), and Summary (consolidation). Well-crafted Cornell notes unlock self-assessment by covering the notes column, efficient spaced repetition, and long-term retention oriented toward {{OBJETIVO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior study techniques and active learning specialist, expert in the Cornell method and in the cognitive science of memory (active recall, spaced repetition).
Deliverable: complete Cornell notes with level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}. Steps:
1. Identify the thematic blocks of the material and order them in logical sequence (not necessarily the original's).
2. Draft the Notes Zone (right column): ideas in telegraphic phrases, hierarchy through indentation, without literal copying, preserving key data, figures, and examples.
3. Derive the Cues Zone (left column): one review question or keyword hook per notes block, aligned in the same row.
4. Write the Summary (bottom): 2 to 3 sentences with the central idea in your own words.
5. Generate {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} active review questions with their brief answer for self-assessment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Comprehension: read {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}; detect thesis, subtopics, and relationships. Do not invent content absent from the source.
Phase 2 Refinement: eliminate redundancy and filler; condense into telegraphic phrases preserving precision, data, and examples.
Phase 3 Cornell Structure: build the Cues | Notes table aligning each cue with its block; adjust density to {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}.
Phase 4 Synthesis and review: draft the summary and design the active recall questions, avoiding questions answerable with just yes or no; cover comprehension and application, not just literal memory.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what material you will process, its topic, and the goal; state level and number of questions; present the plan before executing. If TEMA, MATERIAL_FUENTE, or NIVEL_DETALLE are missing, ask for them; if optional data is missing, assume general review and 5 questions and say so.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All three zones present: Cues | Notes table, Summary, Review.
- [ ] Each row of the table aligns a cue with its corresponding notes block.
- [ ] Notes in telegraphic phrases with hierarchy, without literal copying from the source.
- [ ] Cues formulated as questions or hooks that enable self-assessment by covering the notes.
- [ ] Summary of 2 to 3 sentences with the central idea in your own words.
- [ ] {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} active review questions, each with a brief answer; none answerable with just yes or no.
- [ ] Density consistent with {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}; zero invented data (mark [SUPUESTO] if a connection is inferred but not explicit).
- [ ] Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Edge cases: very short or disorganized material > ask for or reorder into minimum viable blocks; material in another language > notes in English unless technical terms are preserved; source with questionable figures > mark [SUPUESTO] and do not extrapolate.
Expected deliverable: Cornell notes block in Markdown ready to paste into a digital notebook, with two-column table + Summary + Review.
spec-personal_notas_progresivas:
[inputs]
- TEXTO_FUENTE: {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} > Text to distill (article, paper, chapter, transcript, or raw notes)
- OBJETIVO_NOTA: {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} > Why you are saving this note and what future decision or work it should feed
- USO_FUTURO: {{USO_FUTURO}} > What your future self will be looking for when re-opening it (optional; default: remember the thesis and key data)
- INCLUIR_METAFORA: {{INCLUIR_METAFORA}} > Whether to add Layer 4 with a metaphor-line or memorable headline: yes / no (optional; default yes)
- PROFUNDIDAD_MAX: {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}} > Desired final layer: 3 or 4 (optional; default 4 if INCLUIR_METAFORA=yes, otherwise 3)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You save valuable texts but when you re-read them months later you start from zero: you do not remember why you marked them or what was important. Progressive Summarization (Tiago Forte) inverts the cost: you spend a little distillation effort today so that each future re-read costs almost no attention. A well-distilled note lets your future self decide in seconds whether to go deeper or move on, and enables quick re-reads, reuse in your own writing, and reliable on-demand retrieval.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal knowledge management (PKM) specialist, expert in Tiago Forte's Progressive Summarization method and in layer-by-layer distillation for reusable note systems.
Deliverable: {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} distilled into cumulative layers, ready for future re-reading according to {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and {{USO_FUTURO}}, up to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}. Steps:
1. Layer 0 - Base: keep the source text intact and verifiable; do not edit or reinterpret it; preserve quotes, figures, names, and references exactly.
2. Layer 1 - Bold: bold only the sentences carrying the central argument (~20% of the text).
3. Layer 2 - Highlight: within what is already bolded, highlight only the indispensable (~20% of Layer 1).
4. Layer 3 - Summary: draft a 3-to-5-bullet executive summary in your own words from what was highlighted.
5. Layer 4 - Metaphor (according to {{INCLUIR_METAFORA}} and {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}): if applicable, add a metaphor-line or memorable headline that makes it recognizable at a glance.
6. Close with a label per layer indicating its compression level and mark SUPUESTO on any personal inference.
Edge cases: if {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} is very short or already condensed, say so and propose skipping Layer 1 or 2 rather than over-highlighting; if multi-topic, group highlighting by topic; if in another language, distill in that language and translate only Layer 3.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Comprehension: read {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} in full, identify thesis, supporting evidence, and digressions; use {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and {{USO_FUTURO}} as a relevance filter.
Phase 2 - Ascending distillation: apply Layer 1 on Layer 0, Layer 2 on Layer 1, and Layer 3 on Layer 2, respecting the compression caps at each step to avoid over-highlighting.
Phase 3 - Recognition and verification: if applicable, formulate Layer 4; verify that each layer is readable in isolation, faithful to the source, and traceable to the layer below.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The layers present (up to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}) are labeled with their compression level.
- [ ] Layer 1 marks ~20% of the text and Layer 2 ~20% of Layer 1: no over-highlighting.
- [ ] Layer 2 is readable and coherent when read alone; Layer 3 uses your own words without distorting the thesis.
- [ ] Each layer builds strictly on the one below (cumulative, not parallel) and is traceable to it.
- [ ] Layer 0 preserves quotes, figures, and names exactly; all personal inference is marked SUPUESTO; nothing outside the source.
- [ ] The note responds to {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and serves {{USO_FUTURO}}; applicable edge cases were resolved explicitly.
Expected deliverable: note distilled in layers (Layer 0 to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}), reusable, that a future self can scan from top to bottom and go deeper only as needed.
spec-personal_notas_literarias:
[inputs]
- FRAGMENTO: {{FRAGMENTO}} > Read text to be converted into notes: literal quote, copied paragraph, or summary of the passage
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Work identification: author, title, year, and type (book, paper, article, essay, transcribed podcast)
- LOCALIZADOR: {{LOCALIZADOR}} > Exact location within the source to verify the quote (page, chapter, section, timestamp, or paragraph)
- FOCO_DE_LECTURA: {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} > Question, project, or topic guiding what is worth extracting from the excerpt (optional; if missing, the most relevant from the excerpt itself is extracted)
- DESTINO_DE_NOTAS: {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}} > System where the notes will live to adjust title and link format (e.g. Obsidian, Notion, paper Zettelkasten) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
{{FRAGMENTO}} will be converted into literature notes under the smart notes method (Sonke Ahrens, How to Take Smart Notes) and Zettelkasten. A literature note faithfully captures what an external source says with its quote, context, and reference, and remains strictly separate from the own note (permanent), where the person reformulates the idea in their own words and connects it to their thinking. Doing this step well unlocks a reliable knowledge system: months later each note stands on its own, each quote is verifiable against the original source, and what the author said is never confused with what you thought yourself, avoiding accidental plagiarism and false attributions.
Explicit assumptions: the excerpt may arrive incomplete, badly copied, or mixed with the reader's own notes; the system assumes good faith but does not fill in data on its own. Limit: it does not access the original work, only operates on what is provided; any data not present is missing, not inferable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Academic librarian and senior personal knowledge manager, expert in smart notes (Sonke Ahrens) and Zettelkasten, rigorous about attribution and source verifiability.
Deliverable: one to three literature notes, each paired with its own note, ready to archive in {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}. Steps:
1. Restate in one sentence what {{FRAGMENTO}} is about and declare which data from {{FUENTE}} and {{LOCALIZADOR}} are complete and which are missing; if the minimum reference needed to cite is missing (author + work + locator), request it and stop.
2. Extract one to three literature notes aligned with {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} (atomic: one idea per note); each note carries: (a) literal quote in quotation marks or faithful paraphrase labeled as paraphrase, (b) precise reference (author, work, locator), (c) one context line situating the excerpt within the source's argument.
3. Under each literature note write the own note, separate and labeled: what you understood in your own words, why it matters according to {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}}, what idea or reading it connects to, and what question it leaves open.
4. Assign each note an assertion title (not a topic) and two or three tentative tags or links to integrate it into {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Anchoring: identify the excerpt's thesis and the completeness of the reference; without minimum reference, no notes are generated.
Phase 2 - Faithful capture: rigorously separate source voice (labeled quote or paraphrase) from own voice; never attribute to the source what it does not say; all external context or inference is marked as [SUPUESTO]; if the excerpt already mixes the reader's comments, isolate them and do NOT cite them as source.
Phase 3 - Elaboration: draft the own note in your own language with connections; one assertion title per note; tentative tags or links.
Phase 4 - Verification: verify that each quote is verifiable against {{LOCALIZADOR}}, that no own note disguises itself as a quote, and that each note stands on its own outside of context.
Edge cases: (a) very long or multi-topic excerpt -> divide into atomic notes, one idea per note, not exceeding three; if it exceeds, prioritize by {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} and note what was deferred. (b) quote in another language -> keep the original and offer a translation labeled as your own. (c) locator absent or ambiguous -> provisional literature note marked {pending_locator}, not considered verified. (d) paraphrase received as if it were a quote -> label it as paraphrase, never with quotation marks.
Accepted trade-off: when in doubt between fidelity and fluency, fidelity to the source wins even if the note is less polished.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist (acceptance criteria):
- Each literature note has a quote or faithful paraphrase + reference (author, work, locator) + context line.
- The own note is separate and labeled; it is never mixed with the source's voice nor attributes statements to it that it does not make.
- Each note is atomic: a single idea per note.
- All inference or external context is marked as [SUPUESTO]; no pages, years, or quotes are invented; absent data is declared missing or {pending_confirmation}.
- Each title is an assertion, not a topic; there are 2-3 tentative tags or links per note.
- Each note is self-contained outside of context and each quote is verifiable against the source.
Expected deliverable: block of 1 to 3 pairs (literature note + own note) with titles, references, and tags, ready to paste into {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}, plus a closing note with any missing or pending-confirmation source data if applicable.
spec-personal_mapa_conocimiento:
[inputs]
- TEMA_CENTRAL: {{TEMA_CENTRAL}} > Topic or central idea to map (e.g., photosynthesis, time management, neural networks)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Purpose of the map: studying for an exam, preparing a class, organizing a project, etc.
- PROFUNDIDAD: {{PROFUNDIDAD}} > Level of detail: introductory, intermediate, or advanced
- NUM_RAMAS: {{NUM_RAMAS}} > Desired number of main branches, between 4 and 7 (optional; by default the AI decides)
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Additional delivery syntax: Markmap, Mermaid mindmap, or indented list (optional; by default indented list only)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a scattered topic into a visual structure that lets me see the forest and the trees at the same time. A well-built radial mind map externalizes the hierarchy and relationships of a topic, reduces cognitive load, and accelerates review: once I have the map, I can study, teach, or plan around it without rereading everything from scratch. Topic to map: {{TEMA_CENTRAL}}. Purpose: {{OBJETIVO}}. Requested depth: {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, they are the primary source of content.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: expert facilitator in mind mapping and knowledge management, trained in Tony Buzan's mind map technique (central idea, branches, keywords, hierarchy and radial association) and in MECE structuring (mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive categories).
Deliverable: a mind map of the topic, as an indented list by level plus a cross-links section and a review questions section. Steps:
1. Distil the topic into ONE clear and concise central idea (1 to 5 words).
2. Derive {{NUM_RAMAS}} main branches (between 4 and 7) covering the major dimensions of the topic, MECE, each with a word or short phrase.
3. Expand each branch into second-level sub-branches and, where it adds value, a third level, with keywords rather than long phrases and depth adjusted to {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.
4. Identify at least two cross-links between concepts from different branches and explain each one's relationship in one line.
5. Draft 3 to 5 review questions, aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}, that the map allows answering from memory.
6. If {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} indicates Markmap or Mermaid, also deliver the map in that syntax in addition to the indented list.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm central idea, scope, and depth. If the topic is too broad for the requested detail, propose narrowing it and wait for a response before mapping. If there are attachments, use them as the source; if not, work with general knowledge and mark what was inferred.
Phase 2 - Radial structure: fix the main branches before detailing, verifying with the MECE test that they do not overlap (exclusive) and cover the topic (exhaustive).
Phase 3 - Deepening: open sub-branches with keywords, maintaining balance between branches (avoid one giant branch and others that are empty) and limiting to 2-3 levels to preserve readability.
Phase 4 - Association: trace the cross-links with their rationale and formulate review questions anchored to the objective.
Phase 5 - Format: deliver the indented list and, if applicable, the {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} code block with valid syntax that reproduces exactly the same hierarchy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- A single central idea, concise (1 to 5 words) and faithful to the topic.
- Between 4 and 7 main branches that pass the MECE test: no overlap and covering the topic.
- Clean hierarchy of 2 to 3 levels with keywords, not paragraphs, and balance between branches.
- Depth of sub-branches consistent with {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.
- At least 2 cross-links between different branches, each with its relationship in one line.
- 3 to 5 review questions aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.
- No invented data; every inference is marked [SUPUESTO]; if there were attachments, content is grounded in them.
- If Markmap or Mermaid was requested, the syntax is valid and reproduces the same hierarchy as the list.
Expected deliverable: mind map as an indented list by level + cross-links section + review questions section (and Markmap/Mermaid code block if requested).
spec-personal_outline_estructurado:
[inputs]
- IDEAS_EN_BRUTO: {{IDEAS_EN_BRUTO}} > List of loose ideas, notes, or fragments to structure, as they are, without prior order
- OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO: {{OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO}} > What the final document must achieve and the thesis or message to defend
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who will read or hear it and their level of context on the topic
- FORMATO_FINAL: {{FORMATO_FINAL}} > Target format: essay, report, article, talk, thread, script
- PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA: {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA}} > Maximum number of nesting levels (optional; default four)
- ORDEN_PREFERIDO: {{ORDEN_PREFERIDO}} > Desired pillar ordering logic: importance, chronological, problem-solution, deductive (optional; default whichever best serves the thesis)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have loose ideas on a topic and need to see their logical skeleton before drafting. Writing without structure produces texts that repeat points, leave argument gaps, and mix assertions with examples. A solid hierarchical outline unblocks drafting: it converts the chaos of notes into a navigable tree where every branch is justified, and it allows detecting logical flaws when fixing them costs minutes rather than hours of rewriting.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior non-fiction editor and information architect with fifteen years structuring documents and presentations before drafting.
Deliverable: a hierarchical outline of nested levels that clarifies the logic of IDEAS_EN_BRUTO before writing a single line, according to OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO, AUDIENCIA, and FORMATO_FINAL.
1. Refine IDEAS_EN_BRUTO: group related ideas, merge duplicates, and separate main assertions from evidence or supporting examples.
2. Formulate a single governing idea (level zero) that the document must defend, in one sentence, aligned with OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO.
3. Build the outline with nested decimal numbering (1, 1.1, 1.1.1) without exceeding PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA; each level 1 is a pillar supporting the governing idea. Order pillars according to ORDEN_PREFERIDO.
4. Write one logical line per level-1 pillar explaining why it supports the governing idea.
5. Issue a control block with the gaps, overlaps, and assumptions detected.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1, framing: if IDEAS_EN_BRUTO, OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO, AUDIENCIA, or FORMATO_FINAL are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent ideas not contributed. Adapt granularity to FORMATO_FINAL (a thread tolerates fewer levels than a report) and language to the AUDIENCIA's level of context.
Phase 2, refinement: group, merge duplicates, and distinguish assertion from evidence. If a loose idea does not fit any pillar, do not force it: record it as a candidate for [HUECO] or a justified discard.
Phase 3, hierarchy (Minto Pyramid + MECE): governing idea at the top, supporting branches below. Children of the same parent must be mutually exclusive (no overlap) and collectively exhaustive (together they cover the parent without gaps), with grammatical parallelism between siblings. Every branch must have at least two children or none: never an orphan sub-point. If a parent naturally generates only one child, reconsider the split or absorb the child into the parent.
Phase 4, control: mark [HUECO] for what no child covers of the parent, [SOLAPE] for siblings that overlap, and [SUPUESTO] for every inference of yours that fills a logical gap. If there are none, state it explicitly. Do not draft the final text: only the structure.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- A single governing idea at level zero, in one sentence, aligned with OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO.
- Consistent nested decimal numbering; depth within PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA.
- Pillars ordered according to ORDEN_PREFERIDO or, failing that, the order that best serves the thesis.
- MECE siblings: no overlaps and no gaps relative to the parent; grammatical parallelism between them.
- No branch with a single orphan child.
- Assertions separated from evidence and examples; zero invented ideas outside IDEAS_EN_BRUTO.
- One logical line per level-1 pillar.
- Granularity consistent with FORMATO_FINAL and language adjusted to AUDIENCIA.
- Control block present with [HUECO], [SOLAPE], and [SUPUESTO], or an explicit statement that there are none.
- No drafted text: structure only.
Expected deliverable: governing idea + complete numbered outline + logical lines per pillar + control block.
spec-personal_segundo_cerebro_captura:
[inputs]
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Raw content to process: article, video or meeting transcript, highlights, or loose idea
- PROYECTO_ACTIVO: {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}} > Live project or objective where this note should be useful (provides relevance criterion and final connection)
- DESTINO_PARA: {{DESTINO_PARA}} > Tentative PARA location: Project, Area, Resource, or Archive (optional; if missing, the model proposes one and justifies it)

- NIVEL_DESTILADO: {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}} > Depth of progressive summary: highlights only, highlights plus bullets, or essence in one sentence (optional; default highlights plus bullets)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Valuable information is lost when consumed without processing: it ends up in tabs, dead highlights, and notes that are never reread. Processing {{FUENTE}} with the Building a Second Brain CODE flow converts it into a retrievable asset that feeds {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}. The result is a note that my future self understands in seconds and reuses without returning to the original source.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal knowledge manager, specialist in Tiago Forte's Building a Second Brain method and its CODE flow (Capture, Organize, Distil, Express).
Deliverable: a CODE note structured in four layers, plus suggested title and next step. Steps:
1. Capture: extract from {{FUENTE}} only what resonates, surprises, serves {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, or is personally useful; quote key ideas preserving the author's voice, without transcribing everything.
2. Organize: classify the note by actionability using {{DESTINO_PARA}} (Project = actionable now; Area = ongoing responsibility; Resource = topic of interest; Archive = inactive) and justify the choice by where I will use it, not by topic.
3. Distil: apply progressive summarization in layers up to {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}}: first highlight the sentences worth rereading, then an executive summary of 3 to 5 bullets with the essence.
4. Express: produce {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} connecting the idea to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, ready to use without reopening the source.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture > resonance criterion, not exhaustiveness; preserve the author's voice in quoted content; separate verbatim quotation from paraphrase.
Phase 2 Organize > decide by actionability (where I will use it), not by topic; a single primary PARA location; if torn between Project and Area, Project wins when there is a deliverable with a date or expected outcome.
Phase 3 Distil > opaque-to-transparent layers; each layer must be readable without reading the previous one; do not introduce ideas that are not in the capture.
Phase 4 Express > orient toward the deliverable; every element must be executable or reusable; explicit connection to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}.
Edge cases: if {{FUENTE}} is very extensive, prioritize by relevance to the project and declare what was left out; if nothing resonates, say so and propose Archive instead of forcing value; if {{ADJUNTOS}} contradicts the text, flag the conflict and do not resolve it silently.
Limits: do not invent data, figures, or attributions; mark all own inferences with [SUPUESTO]. If {{FUENTE}}, {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, or {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before processing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The capture filters by resonance and relevance to the project, does not copy the whole source, and distinguishes quotation from paraphrase.
- The PARA classification is a single, primary one, justified by actionability and not by topic.
- The distillation has layers: highlights first, then a 3-to-5-bullet summary readable on its own, and essence in one sentence if {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}} requires it.
- The deliverable fulfills {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} and explicitly connects to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, usable without reopening the source.
- All inferences are marked [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented is presented as data from the source; conflicts with {{ADJUNTOS}} are flagged.
- Closes with suggested note title and a concrete next step.
Expected deliverable: CODE note in four layers (cited capture, justified PARA, layered distillation, expressed deliverable) plus suggested title line and next step.
spec-personal_indice_notas:
[inputs]
- INVENTARIO_NOTAS: {{INVENTARIO_NOTAS}} > List of existing notes (titles; ideally with tags, folder, date, or status). Accepts raw dump, app export, or table
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > Notes app (Obsidian, Notion, Logseq, Apple Notes, plain text, or other) that defines link syntax
