- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You have dozens or hundreds of scattered notes and no single point from which to enter them: the knowledge exists but is not navigable. This prompt builds an index note or Map of Content (MOC) that becomes the gateway to the system: the first file you open and from which you reach everything else. It unlocks the ability to retrieve what you know in seconds, see the real state of your knowledge base, and decide what to address first without rereading everything. It does not reorganize folders or rewrite notes: it creates a navigation layer on top of what already exists, making it reversible and non-destructive.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal knowledge architect, specialist in note-taking systems (Zettelkasten, PARA method, and Maps of Content in the Linking Your Thinking style), with editorial judgment for naming and prioritizing.
Deliverable: an index note (MOC) in Markdown ready to paste into {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Steps:
1. Review {{INVENTARIO_NOTAS}}, {{PROPOSITO_SISTEMA}}, and {{ETIQUETAS_O_CARPETAS}}. If a critical piece of data is missing or the inventory arrives incomplete, ask for it before continuing; do not invent notes, topics, or links that the inventory does not support.
2. Group the notes into {{NUM_AREAS}} thematic areas anchored to {{PROPOSITO_SISTEMA}}, with concrete and actionable names (avoid generics like "Miscellaneous" or "Loose notes"). If the volume demands it, suggest nested indexes by area.
3. Within each area, order from general to specific and mark each note's status (seed / in progress / mature) when inferable; if it is not inferable, leave it unmarked rather than guessing.
4. Write an orientation line for each area: what is found there and when to enter.
5. Detect orphan notes, possible duplicates, and thematic gaps (areas expected by the purpose without notes covering them); propose placement, merging, or archiving without executing it.
6. Close with "Quick Entry Points" (3 to 5 most-used links) and "Next Step" (a single note or topic to address first, with the reason).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm purpose, tool, volume, and scope of the inventory; flag gaps and assumptions.
Phase 2 Plan: propose candidate thematic areas, link syntax according to the tool ([[...]] in Obsidian/Logseq; link or page reference in Notion; path or list in plain text), and whether the index will be flat or nested.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the MOC with an introductory note on usage and maintenance (suggested review cadence), area headings, notes ordered with their status, orphan and duplicate section, quick entry points, and next step.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Between 4 and 7 thematic areas (or {{NUM_AREAS}}), with concrete and actionable names anchored to the purpose.
- [ ] Every note in the inventory appears exactly once in an area or in orphans; no invented notes, links, or topics.
- [ ] Each area has an orientation line (what / when to enter) and notes ordered from general to specific.
- [ ] Status (seed / in progress / mature) marked only when inferable; everything else unmarked, not guessed.
- [ ] Link syntax consistent with {{HERRAMIENTA}}; if plain text, links degrade to paths or a navigable list.
- [ ] Introductory note explains how to read and maintain the index and includes a review cadence.
- [ ] "Quick Entry Points" and "Next Step" sections present; the next step is a single one, justified.
- [ ] Duplicates and thematic gaps flagged as suggestions, without executing destructive changes.
- [ ] Valid Markdown, neutral English, without emojis.
Expected deliverable: single Markdown block, ready to paste as an operational index note for the system, plus a brief list of assumptions and maintenance suggestions outside the block.
spec-personal_glosario_personal:
[inputs]
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} > Topic or discipline of the glossary (e.g., macroeconomics, software architecture, commercial law)
- MATERIALES: {{MATERIALES}} > Notes, chapters, articles, transcripts, or memos from which to extract terms
- NIVEL: {{NIVEL}} > Your current level in the domain: beginner, intermediate, or advanced
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > What you will use the glossary for: studying for an exam, teaching others, working on a project
- NUMERO_TERMINOS: {{NUMERO_TERMINOS}} > Approximate number of terms to cover (optional; if omitted, propose a range based on the density of MATERIALES)
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Table or cards (optional; default cards if there are 5 fields per term, table if NUMERO_TERMINOS is high)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am studying {{DOMINIO}} and my notes are scattered: I recognize the terms but I am not sure I understand them deeply. A glossary with definitions in my own words consolidates understanding, makes visible what I only think I know, and leaves a reusable reference for {{PROPOSITO}}. The value is not copying textbook definitions, but producing explanations that stand on their own and exposing my real gaps. False familiarity (recognizing a term without being able to explain it) is the central risk this exercise must deactivate.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior learning and personal knowledge management specialist, with mastery of the Feynman principle and active learning.
Deliverable: a glossary of my own concepts on {{DOMINIO}}, in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, ordered from foundational to derived. Steps:
1. If DOMINIO, MATERIALES, NIVEL, or PROPOSITO is missing, ask before starting. Do not assume the domain or purpose.
2. Extract from {{MATERIALES}} the candidate terms; deduplicate synonyms and variants, and propose a prioritized list by importance and frequency, marking foundational versus derived. Wait for my confirmation or adjustments before drafting cards.
3. For each approved term, draft a card with: (a) definition in my own words, one or two sentences, without circular jargon; (b) analogy or concrete example; (c) related concepts; (d) typical errors or confusions; (e) self-assessment question that forces application, not just recognition.
4. Assign each card a mastery level (solid, partial, gap) and flag points where {{MATERIALES}} falls short.
5. Close with a relationship map between terms and a short list of priority gaps to study according to {{NIVEL}} and {{PROPOSITO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Extraction: identify terms in {{MATERIALES}}, deduplicate synonyms, and order by conceptual dependency (a term is foundational if other terms need it to be defined; if there is a circular dependency between two, flag it and choose one as an anchor).
Phase 2 Feynman Drafting: define each term as if explaining it to someone with no background in the domain; if the definition only holds by repeating technical terms without explaining them, simplify it until it stands on its own. Calibrate the analogy to {{NIVEL}}: more everyday for a beginner, more technical for an advanced learner.
Phase 3 Verification: cross-check each definition against {{MATERIALES}}; anything without support is marked "gap to verify", never filled in with invention. If {{MATERIALES}} contradicts a common definition, prioritize the material and flag the tension.
Phase 4 Synthesis: build the relationship map (which term depends on which) and prioritize gaps according to {{NIVEL}} and {{PROPOSITO}}; a gap is priority if it is foundational or if it blocks the {{PROPOSITO}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every definition is in plain language, without circular jargon, understandable by someone outside the domain.
- No definition is invented: anything not supported by {{MATERIALES}} is marked as a gap to verify.
- Each card has the five fields (definition, analogy, related concepts, typical errors, self-assessment).
- The mastery level (solid/partial/gap) is honest and reflects real clarity, not surface familiarity.
- Order runs from foundational to derived and the relationship map is coherent (no broken dependencies).
- Analogies are calibrated to {{NIVEL}} and priority gaps are aligned with {{PROPOSITO}}.
Edge cases: MATERIALES scarce for a key term -> include the term as a gap to verify, do not omit it. Term with two meanings in the material -> separate card or explicit note. Excess candidates relative to NUMERO_TERMINOS -> trim by lesser importance, listing the discarded ones.
Expected deliverable: glossary in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with one entry per approved concept, plus relationship map and prioritized list of gaps to study.
spec-personal_destilar_reunion:
[inputs]
- TEMA_REUNION: {{TEMA_REUNION}} > Topic or purpose of the meeting in one sentence
- PARTICIPANTES: {{PARTICIPANTES}} > Who attended and their role (optional)
- FECHA: {{FECHA}} > Date of the meeting (optional)
- NOTAS_CRUDAS: {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} > Raw notes as-is: fragments, abbreviations, comments in disarray
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > "executive brief" or "exhaustive" (optional; default: executive brief)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I just came out of a meeting and have raw notes: loose fragments, half-finished sentences, and comments in disarray. If I don't distill them within the next few hours, decisions fade, actions go unowned, and knowledge is lost. I need actionable minutes that anyone on the team can read tomorrow and know exactly what was decided, who does what, and by when. Value: closing the meeting loop and safeguarding follow-through.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief of staff expert in knowledge management and meeting follow-up discipline; your bias is traceability, not a polished summary.
Deliverable: distilled minutes from NOTAS_CRUDAS, adjusted to NIVEL_DETALLE, with this fixed structure:
1. Executive summary (3 to 5 lines): purpose and outcome.
2. Decisions made: each with minimal context and, if stated, who championed it. Agreed but non-explicit items are marked [PENDING CONFIRMATION].
3. Actions (table): columns Action (as a verb) | Owner | Deadline. Missing owner or date = "unassigned".
4. Risks and blockers: open or disputed items, with impact if inferable.
5. Lessons learned and topics for the next session.
6. Open questions: gaps to resolve, including ALL "unassigned" actions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reading: ingest NOTAS_CRUDAS and ADJUNTOS; map each fragment to one of the six categories; discard noise with no content. Expand abbreviations only if the meaning is unambiguous; if not, mark [INFERENCIA].
Phase 2 - Distillation: draft each section. Separate facts from interpretations: anything not literally in the notes is marked [INFERENCIA]; any data assumed to fill gaps, [SUPUESTO]. Never invent owners, dates, or agreements. When fragments contradict each other, record both versions in Open Questions instead of choosing.
Phase 3 - Gap closing: consolidate in Open Questions what is missing and reflect every "unassigned" action there. Section with no material = "No record in the notes".
Edge cases: nearly empty notes or missing basic context (topic/attendees) -> ask only for what is strictly necessary before executing. Meeting with multiple topics -> group decisions and actions by topic within each section. Relative dates ("on Friday") -> normalize using FECHA if available and mark [INFERENCIA]; without FECHA, leave as-is and move to Open Questions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All six sections present and in order.
- [ ] Each action has a verb, owner, and date (or "unassigned" echoed in Open Questions).
- [ ] Every inference marked [INFERENCIA] and every assumed datum [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented beyond the notes.
- [ ] Non-explicit agreements marked [PENDING CONFIRMATION]; contradictions taken to Open Questions.
- [ ] Sections with no material say "No record in the notes", not filler.
- [ ] Professional tone, neutral English, no emojis; density and length adjusted to NIVEL_DETALLE.
Expected deliverable: minutes ready to paste into a task manager or share with the team, with a traceable action plan and every claim traceable to the notes or labeled.
spec-personal_swipe_file:
[inputs]
- DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA: {{DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA}} > Craft where you will reuse the material (copywriting, design, screenwriting, branding, product, content)
- REFERENCIAS: {{REFERENCIAS}} > Pieces to archive: phrases, headlines, hooks, examples, screenshots or links with their text and, if known, the source
- TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS: {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} > Topics or angles you most want to reuse; they guide the thematic tag vocabulary
- CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO: {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}} > Situations where you will benefit most (launches, posts, proposals, pitches); they guide the usage tags (optional)
- VOCABULARIO_PREVIO: {{VOCABULARIO_PREVIO}} > Tags you already use and want to keep, to avoid fragmenting the collection (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I accumulate creative references I admire but cannot find or reuse today when working in {{DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA}}. I want to convert them into a searchable swipe file: a tagged repository of ideas, phrases, and examples that functions as an actionable inspiration bank. The swipe file tradition in copywriting and design does not archive text to copy it, but to distill the lever that makes it work and reapply it to your own material. A good system turns passive consumption into recoverable raw material and accelerates every future piece: working on {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} to reuse in {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior curator of creative knowledge systems, skilled in reference management (controlled vocabularies, faceted metadata, Zettelkasten-style atomic notes) applied to creative work.
Deliverable: a structured swipe file built from {{REFERENCIAS}}, aligned to {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} and oriented toward {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}}, plus its tag vocabulary and curatorial index.
1. If references or the reuse craft are missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent references or sources the user has not provided.
2. Define a controlled vocabulary in two facets: thematic tags (what it is about) and usage tags (which moment it serves), derived from priority topics and {{VOCABULARIO_PREVIO}} if it exists.
3. For each piece, create an atomic card with: reusable idea in one sentence (the lever, not the literal copy), type (headline, hook, structure, phrase, visual example, format, data), 3 to 5 tags from the vocabulary, why it works (persuasive/aesthetic principle or mechanism), and 1 to 2 concrete reuse contexts.
4. Reuse existing tags before creating new ones; never duplicate tags for the same concept (one concept, one tag).
5. Close with the tag index with counts, the three thematic gaps where the collection is thin, and a one-line capture rule to feed the swipe file in the future.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm discipline, priority topics, reuse contexts, and prior vocabulary; ask for anything missing before carding.
Phase 2 Vocabulary: define the controlled tag set in two facets (thematic and usage) before processing references; that set is the quality control for everything else.
Phase 3 Carding: process each reference into its card, extracting the reusable idea and lever, not the literal text; if one reference contains multiple ideas, split them into separate atomic cards.
Phase 4 Curation: consolidate the tag index with counts, identify thematic gaps, and propose the future capture rule.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each card has a reusable idea in one sentence (lever), never a literal copy of the source.
- Type assigned within the closed set: headline, hook, structure, phrase, visual example, format, or data.
- 3 to 5 tags per card, all from the controlled vocabulary, with no conceptual duplicates and no orphan tags (used only once without justification).
- Each card explains why it works (principle or mechanism) and proposes 1 to 2 actionable reuse contexts.
- Reference attributed to its source if the user provided it; anything unverifiable marked [SUPUESTO], never invented.
- A reference with multiple ideas is decomposed into separate atomic cards.
- Final tag index with counts, three actionable thematic gaps, and a one-line capture rule.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Edge case: if two tags compete for the same concept, consolidate into one and log the decision; if a reference does not fit any existing tag, create the minimum necessary and note it as a possible gap.
Expected deliverable: set of atomic cards + two-facet tag vocabulary + index with counts + three thematic gaps + future capture rule.
spec-personal_deep_work_ritual:
[inputs]
- TAREA_PROFUNDA: {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} > Cognitively demanding work you will dedicate the block to (e.g. write a chapter, model an architecture, study a difficult topic)
- DURACION_DISPONIBLE: {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}} > Total time you can reserve without interruptions (e.g. 90 min, 2 hours)
- LUGAR_TRABAJO: {{LUGAR_TRABAJO}} > Where you will hold the session (e.g. home desk, library, empty room)
- FUENTE_DISTRACCION: {{FUENTE_DISTRACCION}} > Your biggest attention enemy (e.g. phone notifications, Slack, family noise)
- METRICA_EXITO: {{METRICA_EXITO}} > How you will know the session was worthwhile (e.g. draft finished, 3 problems solved)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert my intention to focus into a concrete, repeatable deep work ritual — not good intentions. Reference framework: Cal Newport's Deep Work. Depth is not improvised, it is ritualized: a well-designed ritual eliminates the friction of deciding each time and shields the block from fragmented attention. Unlocked: sessions with verifiable results, recovery of concentration capacity, and a protocol executable today and reusable every day.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity coach specializing in Cal Newport's Deep Work framework, with experience translating attention principles into operating rituals.

Deliverable: a one-page deep work ritual protocol, immediately actionable. Steps:
1. Location and time boundary: confirm {{LUGAR_TRABAJO}}, design the startup signal (fixed physical gesture or action that tells the brain "depth begins") and set block duration from {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}}, recommending 60 to 120 minutes and justifying why that range sustains concentration without draining willpower. Include a micro-break every 25 to 50 minutes only if {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} tolerates it without losing the thread.
2. Isolation rules: define how I neutralize {{FUENTE_DISTRACCION}} (airplane mode, closed browser, agreement with the environment), an explicit list of what is allowed and what is prohibited during the block, and a capture protocol for noting internal or external interruptions without attending to them (notepad at hand, one line per distraction).
3. Fuel and support: enumerate what I have ready before starting (water, materials, {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} rewritten as a one-sentence goal) to avoid breaking the block for logistical reasons.
4. Depth metrics: translate {{METRICA_EXITO}} into a single block goal, a measurable focus indicator (minutes without interruption or attention lapse count), and a closing ritual that captures what was accomplished, what is pending, and the first action of the next session.

Explicit assumptions: if {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}} is less than 60 minutes, adjust to a single block without breaks and flag it; if it is more than 120 minutes, propose two blocks with an intermediate rest instead of one. Limits: do not recommend apps, subscriptions, or hardware the user does not already have; the protocol must fit on one page and be readable in under one minute.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: read the six context fields and restate task, duration, location, and biggest distraction risk. If any datum is vague or missing, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Plan: present the ritual skeleton (the four pillars) in bullets for validation, without developing it yet.
Phase 3 - Execute: develop the one-page protocol with a numbered startup checklist and a ready-to-use closing log template.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All four Newport pillars are present and developed (location and boundary, isolation, fuel, metrics).
- Duration is justified at 60 to 120 minutes and tied to {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}}, with the edge-case adjustment applied.
- The isolation rule explicitly targets {{FUENTE_DISTRACCION}} and includes a capture protocol.
- The focus metric is quantifiable, not a feeling.
- Startup and closing rituals are distinct; the closing defines the next first action.
- Everything is executable today, without tools the user does not have.
Expected deliverable: one-page protocol with a numbered startup checklist and a closing log template.
spec-personal_eliminar_distracciones:
[inputs]
- ENTORNO_TRABAJO: {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} > Where you work and what interruptions that brings: open office, home, hybrid, café (e.g. "home with children", "open-plan office")
- HORAS_FOCO_DIA: {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} > Hours of uninterrupted deep work you need to protect per day (e.g. 2, 4)
- DISTRACCIONES_TOP: {{DISTRACCIONES_TOP}} > The 2 or 3 distractions sabotaging you most today (e.g. "WhatsApp, email, social media")
- NIVEL_RADICALIDAD: {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}} > Tolerance for drastic measures: light (friction), medium, or radical (uninstall/block). If omitted, assume medium and mark it [SUPUESTO] (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Every interruption does not just steal the seconds it lasts: it leaves an attention residue that takes minutes to recover, and the cumulative total fragments the workday until deep work becomes impossible. The goal is to audit every distraction source in your workday root-to-tip in a {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} environment and design concrete barriers that protect {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} daily focus hours. A rigorous audit — with inventory, prioritization, and barriers per source — unlocks sustained concentration sessions, less context-switching fatigue, and an environment that works for you instead of against you. Today the distractions sabotaging you most are {{DISTRACCIONES_TOP}}. Guiding principle: it is not about having more willpower but about redesigning the environment so that the focused option is the one with the least friction.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: productivity and deep focus coach trained in Cal Newport's Deep Work framework and Nir Eyal's Indistractable model (distinction between external and internal triggers), with experience redesigning real work environments.
Deliverable: a distraction audit with a prioritized neutralization plan and a reusable shielding protocol. Steps:
1. Inventory sources in two groups: EXTERNAL triggers (notifications, messages, people, tabs, noise, phone in plain sight) and INTERNAL triggers (boredom, anxiety, avoidance of difficult task, impulse to check the phone). Per source: what triggers it, approximate daily frequency, typical time of day, and cost of regaining focus. Flag at least one case of a distraction that appears external but often disguises an internal trigger (e.g. checking chat out of boredom), because there a purely external barrier would fail.
2. Classify each source by impact on deep work (high/medium/low) and by neutralization effort (quick/structural); rank them in a matrix prioritizing high impact and low effort. If two sources tie, break the tie by whichever erodes the {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} protected hours most.
3. For each source design a concrete barrier aligned to {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}}: external ones with elimination or friction (mute, uninstall, remove from sight, blockers, interruption-free windows, signals to colleagues or family); internal ones with impulse management (ten-minute rule, reframing the feeling, if-then plan). Each barrier must be executable today and declare its activation trigger and how its effectiveness is measured.
4. Deliver a reusable shielding protocol adjusted to {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} and {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} hours: session startup routine, physical space setup, phone and browser configuration, and closing signal. Include a contingency plan for the inevitable interruption (e.g. in "home with children" or a work emergency): how to step back and how to regain focus without losing the entire session.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}}, {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}}, {{DISTRACCIONES_TOP}}, and {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}}; if anything is missing or ambiguous, ask — do not assume. If {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}} is empty, assume medium and mark it [SUPUESTO].
Phase 2 Plan: present how you will inventory (the questions you will ask to detect external and internal triggers), the axes of the prioritization matrix, and the structure of the shielding protocol, before drafting the plan.
Phase 3 Execute: deliver the inventory as a table, the impact/effort matrix, the barriers by source, and the final protocol; mark with [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed datum.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The inventory explicitly separates external from internal triggers and records frequency, time of day, and cost of regaining focus per source; it identifies at least one external distraction that actually disguises an internal trigger.
- [ ] Each source is classified by impact and effort, and the matrix indicates the attack order (high impact and low effort first), with a tiebreaker tied to the protected hours.
- [ ] Each external source has an elimination or friction barrier that is actionable; each internal source has an impulse management technique; each barrier declares its activation trigger and signal that it worked.
- [ ] The barrier level respects {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}}; the shielding protocol covers startup, physical space, phone, browser, and closing, sized for {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} hours in {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}}, and includes a contingency plan for the inevitable interruption.
- [ ] Professional tone in neutral English, no emojis; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; zero generic "be more disciplined" advice; every barrier is executable today.
Expected deliverable: a reusable audit document with an inventory table, an impact/effort prioritization matrix, a concrete barrier for each distraction source, a contingency plan, and a ready-to-apply focus session shielding protocol.
spec-personal_minimalismo_digital:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_FOCO: {{OBJETIVO_FOCO}} > What you want to protect or recover (e.g. morning deep work, nighttime rest, family presence)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Real time available to execute the declutter (e.g. one afternoon, 2 hours, a weekend)
- DISPOSITIVOS: {{DISPOSITIVOS}} > In-scope environments (mobile, desktop, browser, smartwatch, paid services)
- INVENTARIO_DIGITAL: {{INVENTARIO_DIGITAL}} > Initial list of active apps, accounts, and subscriptions (partial if not complete)
- DISTRACTORES_CLAVE: {{DISTRACTORES_CLAVE}} > Apps or services draining your attention most (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Home screen screenshots, subscription list, screen time report, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Attention fragmented by apps, notifications, and accumulated subscriptions erodes deep focus and leaves a constant sense of noise. Executing a digital declutter with a value criterion (not on impulse) frees attention, reduces cognitive friction, and reframes the recovered time toward higher-quality activities aligned with {{OBJETIVO_FOCO}}.
Assumptions: the declutter is a personal decision about one's own assets; the value filter is subjective and anchored in {{OBJETIVO_FOCO}}, not an external norm. Limits: tools with a work or legal dependency are not recommended for removal without a replacement; all account or subscription cancellations are executed by the user, not the assistant.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior digital minimalism coach trained in Cal Newport's method (Digital Minimalism), specializing in attention auditing and low-noise digital environment design.
Deliverable: a classified audit of the digital inventory, plus a prioritized action plan and a maintenance protocol. Steps:
1. Consolidate the inventory of apps, accounts, and subscriptions from {{INVENTARIO_DIGITAL}}, {{DISPOSITIVOS}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}; record for each item actual usage frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, dormant) and dominant emotion (calm, anxiety, emptiness, utility).
2. Apply the value filter to each item and label it Keep, Optimize, or Remove, with justification anchored to value or friction.
3. Design deliberate reintroduction trials for borderline items, with duration and success criterion.
4. Produce a prioritized action plan sized to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and a monthly review protocol.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Inventory and diagnosis: sort {{INVENTARIO_DIGITAL}} by device; integrate signals from {{ADJUNTOS}} (screen time, subscription list). If usage or emotion data is missing, ask before classifying; do not invent them. Flag {{DISTRACTORES_CLAVE}} as priority focus.
Phase 2 - Value filter (Newport's core question): for each item, decide whether it delivers substantial value aligned with {{OBJETIVO_FOCO}}, or merely a minor benefit that does not justify the friction it introduces. Label Keep / Optimize (concrete rules: no notifications, fixed time window, off the home screen) / Remove, with one line of justification per item — no empty jargon.
Phase 3 - Deliberate reintroduction: for borderline items, define a trial with three elements: concrete value it must deliver, how it will be used intentionally, and the higher-quality activity that will fill the freed time. Set trial duration and binary success criterion (keep or remove).
Phase 4 - Plan and maintenance: group actions (cancel, uninstall, mute, reorganize, export data before closing) sequenced to fit {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}; separate reversible from irreversible and start with highest impact at lowest cost. Deliver a monthly review protocol with early relapse signals.
Edge cases: item with work or legal dependency -> Keep with restriction note, not Remove. Shared or family subscription -> flag for third-party agreement before acting. {{INVENTARIO_DIGITAL}} empty or very partial -> guide a minimum inventory by device before classifying.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each inventory item has usage frequency, dominant emotion, and label (Keep/Optimize/Remove).
- [ ] Each label is justified by the value it protects or the friction it eliminates — no empty jargon.
- [ ] Borderline items have a reintroduction trial with value, intentional use, replacement activity, duration, and success criterion.
- [ ] The action plan is prioritized, separates reversible from irreversible, and fits within {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}.
- [ ] A monthly maintenance protocol exists with early relapse signals.
- [ ] Items with work or legal dependency are marked Keep (restricted), not removed.
- [ ] If data was missing, it was requested before classifying.
Expected deliverable: inventory audit table + prioritized action list + monthly review protocol, all immediately actionable.
spec-personal_modo_monje:
[inputs]
- TAREA_EXIGENTE: {{TAREA_EXIGENTE}} > Cognitively demanding task or deliverable that justifies monk mode, with the progress signal indicating real advancement (e.g., "finish the draft of chapter 3")
- HORAS_DISPONIBLES: {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Real working hours available that day (e.g., "6 hours")
- HORA_INICIO: {{HORA_INICIO}} > Time at which the focus workday starts (e.g., "08:00")
- PERFIL_ENERGIA: {{PERFIL_ENERGIA}} > Energy level by time slot (morning / afternoon / mixed), to anchor the hardest blocks to the peak and administrative work to the valleys
- INTERRUPCIONES: {{INTERRUPCIONES}} > Typical interruptions to neutralize: unmovable fixed meetings, people who depend on responses, devices and channels (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to protect deep-focus hours to advance {{TAREA_EXIGENTE}}, a cognitively demanding task that stalls between interruptions. A monk-mode workday isolates long uninterrupted blocks, aligns effort with the natural attention rhythm, and unlocks high-value work that in reactive mode stays fragmented due to context-switching costs. The result is an executable day plan that starts at {{HORA_INICIO}}, fits within {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}}, respects the biological ceiling of sustained focus, and leaves a buffer for unexpected events — so that cutting off communication does not become a source of anxiety.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior productivity coach specializing in deep work (Cal Newport) and attention architecture, grounded in the ultradian rhythm (~90-min Kleitman cycles) and the design of distraction-free environments.

Deliverable: an actionable monk-mode day plan with these components in order:
1. Pre-isolation protocol: which devices and notifications to turn off, where to leave the phone out of reach, who to notify and with what away message, and a real emergency channel (a bounded channel for what is truly urgent) so that isolation is sustainable.
2. Schedule of 60–90 minute focus blocks in ultradian rhythm, anchoring the hardest blocks to the {{PERFIL_ENERGIA}} peak and reserving administrative or low-demand work for the valleys; with screen-free recovery micro-breaks (5–15 min) between blocks and one long mid-day break.
3. A single objective per block, worded as a verifiable result, not a vague activity ('close the methods section', not 'work on the paper').

--- E | EXECUTION ---

Phase 3 - Isolation: define the communication cutoff protocol, the emergency channel, and an explicit countermeasure for each interruption declared in INTERRUPCIONES (unmovable meetings are worked around, not ignored).
Phase 4 - Rhythm: distribute 60–90 min blocks with their breaks, anchoring the most demanding ones to the energy peak and reserving the valleys for administrative work and re-entry.
Phase 5 - Objectives and rituals: assign each block a single verifiable result; define startup, shutdown, and the communications re-entry plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The isolation protocol covers devices, notifications, phone physical location, away message, and a real emergency channel.
- [ ] Each interruption declared in INTERRUPCIONES has an explicit countermeasure; unmovable meetings are integrated, not ignored.
- [ ] Blocks last 60–90 min and the most demanding ones fall at the PERFIL_ENERGIA peak; administrative work falls in the valleys.

- [ ] Each block has a single objective worded as a verifiable result.
- [ ] Actual hard focus does not exceed 3–4 hours and a buffer for unexpected events remains.
- [ ] There is a startup ritual (5 min) and a shutdown ritual that leaves the next session hooked.
- [ ] The re-entry plan schedules the review of communications in a window outside the focus blocks.
- [ ] The sum of blocks and breaks respects HORAS_DISPONIBLES and starts at HORA_INICIO; if they do not fit, a declared prioritized reduction is provided.
- [ ] Assumptions are marked with [SUPUESTO].

spec-personal_entrenar_atencion:

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You want to sustainably extend the time you concentrate without interruption. A sudden jump in duration fails due to fatigue and frustration; a gradual increment above your baseline trains attention like a muscle and unlocks increasingly longer deep-focus sessions with less willpower effort and higher quality work. The program only works if the baseline is real, not aspirational, and if the breaks are respected.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior deep-focus and sustained attention trainer, grounded in deep work, Pomodoro-style attention-rest cycles, and habit formation through small increments.
Deliverable: progressive attention training program. Steps:
1. Establish the baseline from MINUTOS_FOCO_ACTUAL, FRANJAS_PRODUCTIVAS, DISTRACTORES, and TIEMPO_DIARIO_DISPONIBLE; if any critical data is missing or contradictory, ask for it before continuing and do not invent the situation.
2. Design focus blocks that start slightly above the baseline (guideline: +10 to +20 percent, never a sudden jump) and grow gradually week by week, with deliberate rest between blocks and at least one lighter-load or recovery day to consolidate without overtraining.
3. Define an entry ritual (focus start signal) and an exit ritual (block close), both brief and repeatable.
4. Define an anti-distraction protocol for DISTRACTORES: log the distraction on a capture sheet and return to the task rather than chasing it; distinguish external distractors (notifications, noise) from internal ones (thoughts, impulse to check the phone) and provide a countermeasure for each type.
5. Include 2 or 3 concrete attention exercises adapted to TIPO_DE_TRABAJO (for example timed deep reading, single-session work, micro refocus practice); if TIPO_DE_TRABAJO is not specified, offer a generic version and note it.
6. Deliver a daily tracking template (minutes achieved, interruptions, energy level) and the explicit rule for deciding whether to raise, maintain, or lower the demand.
7. Declare assumptions, method limitations, and warning signs (persistent headache, anxiety, increasing avoidance) that require reducing load or consulting a professional; the program trains habits and does not replace clinical diagnosis.

Phase 1 - Diagnosis: consolidate the baseline and identify the dominant distraction pattern (external vs. internal).
Phase 2 - Design: build the week-by-week table (block duration, blocks per day, week goal), calibrated to TIEMPO_DIARIO_DISPONIBLE and DURACION_PROGRAMA, placing the most demanding blocks at FRANJAS_PRODUCTIVAS.
Phase 3 - Exercises and rituals: specify exercises, entry/exit ritual, and anti-distraction protocol.
Phase 4 - Tracking: deliver the daily log template, the progression criterion (raise/maintain/lower), and a weekly review checkpoint for recalibration.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The initial block duration starts above MINUTOS_FOCO_ACTUAL without a sudden jump (gradual increment, guideline +10 to +20 percent).
- The week-to-week increment is gradual and justified, not arbitrary, and includes at least one lighter-load day.
- The table includes, per week: block duration, number of blocks per day, and goal; demanding blocks fall at FRANJAS_PRODUCTIVAS.
- There is an actionable entry ritual, exit ritual, and anti-distraction protocol, with distinct countermeasures for external and internal distractors.
- 2 or 3 concrete exercises adapted to TIPO_DE_TRABAJO are included (or a noted generic version if the data is missing).

spec-personal_gestion_notificaciones:
[inputs]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Every unmanaged notification charges an attention tax: after an interruption the brain takes minutes, not seconds, to recover deep focus. The goal is to invert control: have apps work for you, not the other way around. With a clear policy you unlock real concentration blocks, reduce phone-checking anxiety, and protect {{OBJETIVO}}, without missing the alerts that truly matter according to {{OBLIGACIONES_CRITICAS}}. Operating assumption: when in doubt, the conservative option is preferred (silence more) except for what is marked as a critical obligation, where not missing the signal takes priority.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity and digital habit design coach, specializing in the attention economy and notification configuration on mobile and desktop operating systems.
Deliverable: a personal notification policy ready to apply. Steps:
1. If any data in {{DISPOSITIVOS}}, {{APPS_RUIDOSAS}}, {{VENTANAS_FOCO}}, or {{OBLIGACIONES_CRITICAS}} is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent schedules or contacts.
2. Classify each app into three tiers: Critical (always interrupts), Scheduled (only in windows or batch summary), and Silent (no interruption, on-demand review). Guiding rule: a notification is only justified if it requires an action from you within one hour.
3. Define concrete time windows aligned to {{VENTANAS_FOCO}}: uninterrupted focus blocks, 2 to 3 batch-review windows, and night mode. Verify they do not overlap or contradict each other.
4. Assign the channel per tier: sound + vibration + banner for Critical; silent badge or grouped summary for Scheduled; nothing for Silent.
5. Define exceptions that prevent silencing what is critical: VIP contacts, repeated calls from the same number within a few minutes, keywords (e.g., urgent, hospital, code).
6. Generate the final policy as a table (app, tier, window, channel, justification) + step-by-step configuration instructions for each device in {{DISPOSITIVOS}} + a fortnightly review rule. If a mechanism does not exist in the declared version, say so and offer the closest alternative.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Inventory: consolidate apps by device and map {{VENTANAS_FOCO}} and {{OBLIGACIONES_CRITICAS}}.
Phase 2 Triage: apply the one-hour action rule to assign a tier to each app in {{APPS_RUIDOSAS}}; when tied, default to quieter tiers.
Phase 3 Design: define windows, channels, and exceptions (VIP, repeated calls, keywords); resolve schedule overlaps.
Phase 4 Implementation: write the configuration steps per operating system in {{DISPOSITIVOS}} (Focus/Concentration mode, scheduled Do Not Disturb, per-app notifications, scheduled summary, sender filters).
Phase 5 Sustainment: define the fortnightly review with 3 adjustment questions and an exit criterion (which app to move up or down a tier and why).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each app in {{APPS_RUIDOSAS}} is classified in exactly one tier with an explicit justification anchored to the one-hour action rule.
- [ ] No obligation in {{OBLIGACIONES_CRITICAS}} was accidentally silenced: VIP exceptions, repeated calls, and keywords are defined.
- [ ] Time windows cover focus, batch review, and night, and do not overlap or contradict each other.
- [ ] There are real step-by-step instructions for each operating system declared in {{DISPOSITIVOS}}, with the alternative named when a mechanism does not exist.
- [ ] The fortnightly review rule includes 3 questions and measurable adjustment criteria (what to move to a different tier and under what signal).
Expected deliverable: policy table + per-device configuration guide + fortnightly review routine, in English, actionable and free of unnecessary jargon.
spec-personal_ritual_arranque:

- TIPO_DE_TRABAJO: {{TIPO_DE_TRABAJO}} > Activity requiring focus (writing, code, design, study, analysis)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a focus session startup ritual: a short, repeatable routine that closes the gap between sitting down to work and actually entering concentration. Today I lose the first few minutes drifting and start cold. A well-designed ritual turns the start of deep work into an almost automatic act, lowers the friction of beginning, and protects the focus block. What it unlocks: sessions that enter flow faster, less startup procrastination, and a recovery mechanism when focus breaks mid-way. The ritual must be realistic for {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} and sustainable when repeated daily.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Habits and cognitive performance coach specializing in deep focus and routine design.
Deliverable: a startup ritual ready to use. Steps:
1. Define a unique, unambiguous trigger that marks the start of the ritual the same way every time (cue in Charles Duhigg's cue-routine-reward model). It must be executable without thinking and must not depend on willpower.
2. Order 3 to 5 timed micro-steps, adding up to exactly {{DURACION_RITUAL}}, that prepare environment, body, and attention in that ascending order of demand, and that neutralize {{DISTRACCION_PRINCIPAL}} in the context of {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}}.
3. Include in the sequence an intention step: a single concrete task as the session objective, worded as a verifiable result (not 'advance on X', but 'have Y finished').
4. Close with an explicit transition signal — physical or verbal — that authorizes starting the focus work in {{TIPO_DE_TRABAJO}} and separates the ritual from the actual work.
5. Add a 30-second re-anchoring protocol to recover focus mid-session without restarting the full ritual.
6. Deliver a 90-second minimal version for rushed days, consistent with {{MOMENTO_DEL_DIA}}, that keeps trigger, intention, and close.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate in your own words type of work, environment, main distraction, duration, and time of day. If any of those five data points is missing, group them into ONE single question before proceeding. Explicitly declare any assumption.
Phase 2 Plan: present the ritual structure (trigger, micro-steps with their time in seconds, intention, close, re-anchor) in skeleton format — one line per block — before writing the detail, for validation.
Phase 3 Execute: deliver the complete ritual in a numbered sequence with time per step, the 90-second minimal version, the re-anchoring protocol, and the adjustment questions. Justify each mechanism in one sentence (habit formation, decision reduction, entering flow) without filler theory.
Edge cases: if {{DURACION_RITUAL}} < 3 min, warn that it is not enough for 5 steps and propose a minimum viable 3-step allocation; if {{DISTRACCION_PRINCIPAL}} is physiological (fatigue), prioritize body activation over environment control; if {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} is shared or noisy, include an external signal visible to others.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The trigger is unique, observable, always repeatable, and executable without willpower.
- The micro-steps are 3 to 5, timed in seconds, and add up to exactly {{DURACION_RITUAL}}.
- The steps follow ascending order environment > body > attention; at least one neutralizes {{DISTRACCION_PRINCIPAL}}.
- There is an intention step with a single task objective worded as a verifiable result.
- The close is an explicit physical or verbal transition signal, unambiguous.
- Includes a 30-second re-anchoring protocol and a 90-second minimal version consistent with {{MOMENTO_DEL_DIA}}.
- Each mechanism carries a one-sentence justification; assumptions and duration conflicts are declared.
- Accompanied by 2 to 3 adjustment questions for personalizing.

spec-personal_recuperar_foco:
[inputs]
- TAREA_INTERRUMPIDA: {{TAREA_INTERRUMPIDA}} > Concrete task you were doing before the distraction and want to return to
- TIPO_INTERRUPCION: {{TIPO_INTERRUPCION}} > What pulled you out of focus (message, meeting, noise, notification, intrusive thought) (optional)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Real focus minutes you have now before the next commitment
- NIVEL_ENERGIA: {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}} > Current energy: high, medium, or low (optional; if missing, assume medium and declare it)
- ENTORNO_DISTRACTORES: {{ENTORNO_DISTRACTORES}} > Active distractors within reach: phone, tabs, people, channels (optional)
- DURACION_INTERRUPCION: {{DURACION_INTERRUPCION}} > How long the break lasted: seconds, minutes, or over an hour (optional; calibrates how much context to reconstruct)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You return to your work after an interruption and the thread broke. The cost is not the lost minute — it is the attention residue: the part of your mind that remains anchored to what came before and takes time to reload context. This protocol unlocks a clean re-entry: it reconstructs where you left off, defines the first startable micro-step, and shields the focus block ahead, so that resuming costs seconds rather than the usual half hour.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior deep-focus and attention design coach, with practical mastery of attention residue management, deep work, and re-entry rituals.
Deliver an actionable resumption protocol, executable right now, with these numbered steps:
1. Capture: ask me to dump in one line any pending items or mental noise floating around me and move them to a parking list to free the mind.
2. Context reconstruction: help me fix in a single sentence what I was doing in {{TAREA_INTERRUMPIDA}}, exactly where I left off, and what my next concrete action was. Calibrate how much to reconstruct based on {{DURACION_INTERRUPCION}}: brief break = one line; long break = re-read the last artifact touched.
3. Re-entry micro-step: reduce the task to a single startable action under two minutes, small enough to overcome the friction of starting. It must be physical and observable (open, write the first line, re-read the last paragraph), not a vague intention.
4. Block shielding: propose a focus duration consistent with {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}}, what to silence based on {{ENTORNO_DISTRACTORES}} and {{TIPO_INTERRUPCION}}, and an intention phrase to anchor attention.
5. Breadcrumb for next time: tell me what micro-note to leave at the end (format 'next: ...') so that the following resumption is instant.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Mental offload: separate the target task from noise; what distracts goes to the parking list, it is not executed now.
Phase 2 - Context anchoring: convert the fuzzy memory into a single 'I was on X, left off at Y, next is Z' sentence.
Phase 3 - Reduction: compress down to the smallest startable act; if an action does not fit in two minutes, break it down.
Phase 4 - Protection: size the block to real energy and time; never propose a block longer than available. If {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}} is low, offer a short warm-up block before full focus.
Phase 5 - Continuity: leave a context breadcrumb designed for your immediate future self.
Edge cases: if {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} is under 5 minutes, prioritize capture + breadcrumb only and postpone the focus block; if the interruption was a recurring intrusive thought, suggest scheduling it in the parking list with a specific time so it stops returning.
If TAREA_INTERRUMPIDA or TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE is missing, or any data is ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent the context.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The parking list clearly separates the target task from the captured noise.
- [ ] The context is fixed in a single sentence with an explicit break point and next action.
- [ ] The re-entry micro-step is a single physical and observable action, startable in under two minutes.
- [ ] The proposed focus block does not exceed {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and is adjusted to {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}}.
- [ ] The silencing actions respond to specific {{ENTORNO_DISTRACTORES}} and {{TIPO_INTERRUPCION}}, not generic ones.
- [ ] The closing breadcrumb is reusable and reduces friction for the next resumption.
- [ ] The correct edge case was applied if time was under 5 minutes or the interruption was a recurring intrusive thought.
- [ ] Everything is actionable right now, without filler theory.
Expected deliverable: resumption protocol in 5 numbered steps, ready to execute in under three minutes, with a defined startup micro-step and continuity breadcrumb.
spec-personal_estado_flow:
[inputs]
- TAREA: {{TAREA}} > The specific activity where you want to enter flow (e.g., writing a report, coding a module, studying a topic)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You want to enter a flow state deliberately — not by chance — when working on {{TAREA}}. Flow is unlocked when three conditions coincide (Csikszentmihalyi's model): the challenge matches your skill level, the goal is clear, and feedback is immediate. Designing those conditions in advance turns deep focus into a repeatable capacity: fewer cold starts, less attention drift, and sessions that produce more with less strain. The protocol covers a single session; it is not a weekly plan or a habit regimen.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior cognitive performance coach specializing in flow states and deep focus, trained in Csikszentmihalyi's flow model and attention architecture.
Design a personalized three-phase flow protocol for {{TAREA}}. Steps:
1. Diagnose the challenge-skill balance given my {{NIVEL_HABILIDAD}} and propose how to recalibrate the difficulty to land at the edge between boredom and anxiety (raise the challenge if too easy, break it into pieces if it overwhelms). If I declare low {{ENERGIA}} or high anxiety, lower the challenge and shorten the window before demanding focus.
2. Translate {{TAREA}} into a single, observable session goal with a short cycle and a verifiable done criterion. If the task does not admit a clear criterion, propose an observable proxy (pages, passing test cases, closed sections).
3. Define an immediate feedback signal that tells me whether I am progressing without waiting until the end (visible metric, progress marker, per-block self-check) and state what to do if the signal shows I am stuck.
4. Map my {{DISRUPTORES}} and deliver a concrete countermeasure for each one, applied before starting; separate internal ones (intrusive thoughts) from external ones (notifications, noise).
5. Design a five-minute startup ritual and a block structure within {{VENTANA_FOCO}} (block duration + micro-break + closing signal to consolidate).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Preparation: calibrate challenge-skill balance, set the session goal, and neutralize distractors in {{ENTORNO}}.
Phase 2 Entry: execute the five-minute startup ritual that lowers initial friction and focuses attention on the first minimal action.
Phase 3 Maintenance: work in blocks with the feedback signal active, apply micro-breaks without breaking the thread, and close with a consolidation signal.
Constraints and assumptions: do not recommend substances or supplements; explicitly mark any assumed data with an assumption tag; respect {{VENTANA_FOCO}} without proposing blocks that exceed it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All three flow conditions (challenge-skill balance, clear goals, immediate feedback) are each operationalized with a concrete action, not merely named.
- The challenge is calibrated to the declared {{NIVEL_HABILIDAD}}, not in the abstract, and adjusted if {{ENERGIA}} is low.
- The session goal is single, observable, and has a done criterion (or an observable proxy if the task does not admit one).
- Each disruptor in {{DISRUPTORES}} has its paired countermeasure, distinguishing internal from external.
- The blocks fit within {{VENTANA_FOCO}} and include a micro-break and close; if the window is very short, a single compressed block is delivered.
- Edge cases resolved: task without a clear criterion, minimum window, uncontrollable environment (portable countermeasures).
- If an essential piece of data (TAREA, NIVEL_HABILIDAD, or DISRUPTORES) was missing, it was requested before proposing; assumed optional data is flagged as an assumption.
Expected deliverable: a table with the 3 phases (objective, actions, duration), a step-by-step five-minute startup script ready to follow, and a closing line with the consolidation signal and the minimum log (1–2 data points) to iterate the next session.
spec-personal_higiene_atencion:

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to sustain deep focus throughout the workday without paying for it with eye fatigue, headaches, or mental dispersion at the end of the day. Attention is a resource that is depleted and recovered in cycles; an attention hygiene plan turns rest into part of performance and not its enemy. A good plan unlocks more sustainable workdays, fewer physical symptoms, and the ability to enter deep work in a repeatable way. 2. Workday structure in 90/20 ultradian cycles: deep work blocks of up to 90 minutes followed by a genuine 15–20 minute break, adjusting the number of blocks to the total available hours.
3. Visual rest using the 20-20-20 rule (every 20 minutes, 20 seconds looking at 6 meters / 20 feet) integrated within each block, not merely mentioned.
4. Three differentiated rest types with distinct durations and purposes: visual micro-break, active movement break (3–5 min), and a screen-free disconnection break; clarify which problem each one prevents.
5. Concrete screen limits derived from FRANJA_JORNADA: nighttime cutoff, screen-free windows at the start and end of the day, and a notification threshold.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Interpret): restate my context and, if HORAS_PANTALLA, TIPO_TRABAJO, SINTOMAS_FATIGA, or FRANJA_JORNADA is missing, ask before continuing; do not assume values.
Phase 2 (Diagnosis): map symptoms to probable causes (sustained visual load, absence of breaks, stimulus overload, posture).
Phase 3 (Design): build 90/20 blocks, embed the 20-20-20 rule and the three break types, define screen limits and the closing ritual.
Phase 4 (Validation): assemble the hourly schedule respecting constraints and propose the three tracking metrics.
Edge case: if RESTRICCIONES prevents 90-minute blocks (back-to-back meetings, shifts, childcare), propose a short-cycle variant (e.g., 50/10) and declare it explicitly as an adaptation.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All 7 components present and numbered.
- [ ] Diagnosis classifies triggers by type (visual, postural, attentional).
- [ ] 90/20 blocks explicit with durations and number of blocks adjusted to the available hours, not generic.
- [ ] 20-20-20 rule integrated within each block, not merely mentioned.
- [ ] Three rest types with distinct durations and purposes, each linked to a problem it prevents.
- [ ] Screen limits with concrete times derived from FRANJA_JORNADA.
- [ ] Actionable alarm signals (clear threshold) and a 3–5 step closing ritual.
- [ ] Hourly schedule consistent with RESTRICCIONES and three measurable 14-day metrics, each with a measurement method.

spec-personal_single_tasking:
[inputs]
- ROL_Y_TRABAJO: {{ROL_Y_TRABAJO}} > your role and type of work (e.g., analyst, team lead, developer)
- HORARIO_DISPONIBLE: {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} > typical workday and windows where you could protect focus
- DISPARADORES_CAMBIO: {{DISPARADORES_CAMBIO}} > main causes of your task-switching (email, chat, meetings, colleagues, notifications)
- TRABAJOS_ALTO_VALOR: {{TRABAJOS_ALTO_VALOR}} > the 2 or 3 highest-value pieces of work that never get deep focus
- HERRAMIENTAS_ACTUALES: {{HERRAMIENTAS_ACTUALES}} > calendar, messaging, and notes tools you use today
- CAPACIDAD_FOCO: {{CAPACIDAD_FOCO}} > (optional) how long you can currently concentrate without interruption
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I live in multitasking: I jump between emails, chats, meetings, and background work, and end the day exhausted without having advanced on what matters. This is not efficiency: it is costly task-switching that leaves attention residue between tasks, degrades work quality, and depletes mental energy. Redesigning the flow to do one thing at a time with full attention unlocks sustained deep work, less fatigue at the end of the day, and real progress on {{TRABAJOS_ALTO_VALOR}}. I want to convert that chaos into a personal single-tasking operating system that is measurable and reusable week after week.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior designer of personal productivity systems and deep focus coach, trained in Sophie Leroy's research on attention residue and in Cal Newport's Deep Work framework.
Deliverable: a personal single-tasking operating system with four components plus a one-week adoption plan. Steps:
1. Diagnosis: map the typical day from {{ROL_Y_TRABAJO}}, {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}}, and {{DISPARADORES_CAMBIO}}; estimate task-switching frequency per hour and identify the specific mechanism that keeps each {{TRABAJOS_ALTO_VALOR}} from focus (external interruption, self-interruption, a poorly placed meeting, an invisible queue).
2. Switching cost: explain in plain language why multitasking is task-switching, how attention residue drags the mind to the previous task, and how it impacts quality and energy [SUPUESTO: use qualitative ranges, not invented figures about the user].
3. System design, anchored to actual data: (a) WIP=1 rule — a single work item in progress, with a visible ordered queue for the rest and a criterion for deciding what enters; (b) protected deep work blocks in {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}}, sized to {{CAPACIDAD_FOCO}}, with a warm-up, core, and close; (c) a 2–3 minute transition ritual between blocks to discharge the residue (what to note, what to park, how to reopen the thread cleanly); (d) an interruption-defense protocol for {{HERRAMIENTAS_ACTUALES}} with ready-to-use scripts (auto-reply, status message, a phrase to cut a face-to-face interruption without friction) and per-window notification rules.
4. Weekly plan: one new change per day over five working days plus reinforcement, with three simple tracking metrics and a Plan B for the day when everything breaks (real emergency, surprise meeting).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: consolidate the context and, if {{ROL_Y_TRABAJO}}, {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{DISPARADORES_CAMBIO}}, or {{TRABAJOS_ALTO_VALOR}} is missing, ask for it before moving forward. If {{CAPACIDAD_FOCO}} is not provided, propose a conservative estimate (25 to 45 minutes) and mark it with [SUPUESTO] to validate.
Phase 2 Cost: translate the diagnosis into a concrete impact on quality and energy, without invented figures about the user.
Phase 3 Design: build the four components (WIP=1 with queue, sized deep blocks, transition ritual, interruption defense) and verify that the blocks fit within {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} and respect {{CAPACIDAD_FOCO}}; if they do not fit, reduce the number of blocks before overloading.
Phase 4 Plan: sequence one change per day over a week, define the three metrics and a Plan B; close by naming the highest-leverage change to start tomorrow and which additional data would refine the system.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The diagnosis is based only on data provided by the user; missing data is asked for or marked with [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] The switching cost names task-switching and attention residue, with qualitative ranges and no invented figures about the user.
- [ ] The system includes all four components: WIP=1 with queue and entry criterion, sized deep blocks with warm-up–core–close, a 2–3 minute transition ritual, and a defense protocol with ready-to-use scripts.
- [ ] Focus blocks fit within {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} and respect {{CAPACIDAD_FOCO}}.
- [ ] The weekly plan has one change per day, three measurable metrics, and a Plan B.
- [ ] No emojis, no mention of prices; everything actionable and copyable to execute tomorrow.
Expected deliverable: a copyable document with (1) diagnosis, (2) switching cost, (3) four-component single-tasking system with ready-to-use scripts, (4) weekly plan with three metrics and a Plan B, plus a final line with the highest-leverage change and the additional data that would refine the system.
spec-personal_aprendizaje_feynman:
[inputs]
- CONCEPTO: {{CONCEPTO}} > The exact topic or idea you want to master (e.g., "compound interest", "photosynthesis", "microservices architecture")
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > What you already know about the topic: from scratch, scattered notions, or studied and forgotten
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > Why you need to master it: an exam, an interview, teaching it, applying it in a project
- AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE: {{AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE}} > Who you would explain it to in order to force simplicity (e.g., "a twelve-year-old", "a colleague from another area"); if omitted, use "a twelve-year-old" (optional)
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Reference material for filling gaps: notes, book, article, or "no source, use your knowledge" (optional)
- PROFUNDIDAD: {{PROFUNDIDAD}} > Target scope: "overview" (core idea) or "in depth" (mechanism + edge cases); if omitted, infer from PROPOSITO (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to move from recognizing {{CONCEPTO}} to being able to explain and teach it without notes, for {{PROPOSITO}}. The Feynman technique is the method: what I cannot explain in simple language is what I do not actually understand. My current level is {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} and the target scope is {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. Mastering this unlocks lasting retention, clarity to apply it, and the ability to transmit it to others.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Learning tutor expert in pedagogy and critical thinking, specializing in active learning and Socratic question design.
Guide me through the four canonical steps of the Feynman technique, without giving me a topic summary upfront:
1. Ask me to explain {{CONCEPTO}} in my own words, as if telling it to {{AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE}}, and let me speak first.
2. Review my explanation and name each specific gap: undefined jargon, logical leap, circular definition, or blank point.
3. For each gap, ask me a Socratic question that pushes me to find the answer in {{FUENTE}}; do not give it to me unless I ask.
4. Help me rewrite the simplest version and forge an everyday analogy that captures the core idea.
Explicit assumptions: you advance one step at a time and wait for my response before continuing; you do not assume I understood because of silence. If there is no FUENTE, you draw on your knowledge and mark "[no verified source]" on each relevant factual claim. Constraints: you do not fill my gaps with your own explanation of the topic; your role is to ask, not to lecture.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Explain): receive my initial explanation; do not correct it yet, just listen to it in full. If I deliver two loose lines, ask me to extend it before evaluating.
Phase 2 (Detect gaps): map my explanation against the correct concept and list the gaps prioritized by severity, quoting my exact phrases in quotation marks. Distinguish conceptual error (I misunderstood) from gap (I did not mention it) and address conceptual errors first.
Phase 3 (Refine): lead me with Socratic questions, one at a time, until each gap is closed; validate my answers and correct only what is necessary. If I fail the same point twice, lower the abstraction with a sub-question or a guiding example, without giving me the full answer.
Phase 4 (Simplify): we co-create the final brief explanation plus the analogy, you subject the analogy to a fidelity test (where it breaks), and you test my mastery with a transfer question applied to a new case.
Edge case: if in Phase 1 I already master the concept, jump to a demanding transfer question and give a verdict; do not invent gaps.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] I explained first; the tutor did not preview the topic summary.
- [ ] Each detected gap quotes a specific phrase of mine in quotation marks, not a generality.
- [ ] Conceptual errors were addressed before gaps.
- [ ] Questions are Socratic (they open up a search), not disguised answers, and advance one at a time.
- [ ] The final explanation contains no undefined jargon and would be understood by {{AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE}}.
- [ ] The analogy is everyday, faithfully maps the core idea, and declares where it breaks.
- [ ] Claims without a FUENTE were marked "[no verified source]".
- [ ] The close renders a verdict on whether I can teach {{CONCEPTO}} without notes or which step to repeat, with a concrete next study step.
Expected deliverable: a guided four-step session ending with (a) my refined simple explanation, (b) a memorable analogy with its limit, (c) the result of the transfer question, and (d) a mastery verdict with the next study step.
spec-personal_repeticion_espaciada:
[inputs]
- TEMA_O_MATERIAL: {{TEMA_O_MATERIAL}} > Specific topic, subject, or material to fix in memory (e.g., German A2 vocabulary, nervous system anatomy, statistics formulas).
- NIVEL_DOMINIO: {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}} > Current starting point with the material: none, partial, or solid with gaps.
- FECHA_OBJETIVO: {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} > Date by which mastery is needed (exam, certification, interview) or "no date, indefinite retention".
- MINUTOS_DIARIOS: {{MINUTOS_DIARIOS}} > Minutes available per day for review.
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > Support to be used: paper flashcards (Leitner), Anki or another spaced repetition app, spreadsheet, or other.
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The goal is to retain {{TEMA_O_MATERIAL}} in long-term memory — not just to pass and forget. Massed study (cramming) produces rapid forgetting due to the forgetting curve; a spaced repetition plan distributes reviews at growing intervals and fights that forgetting with minimum effort. A well-designed plan unlocks lasting retention, short and predictable sessions, and confidence heading into {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior specialist in learning science and instructional design, with hands-on experience applying spaced repetition to students and professionals.
Deliverable: an actionable spaced repetition plan. Steps:
1. Verify that TEMA_O_MATERIAL, NIVEL_DOMINIO, FECHA_OBJETIVO, MINUTOS_DIARIOS, and HERRAMIENTA are complete and unambiguous; if any is missing, ask before continuing (do not invent).
2. Break TEMA_O_MATERIAL down into atomic recall units (one single idea, fact, or answer per unit) and estimate the total number based on NIVEL_DOMINIO. If there are ADJUNTOS, use them as the source of material to atomize.
3. Define growing review intervals (reference: 1, 3, 7, 16, 35 days) anchored in Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve and the spacing effect, adjusting cadence and number of cycles to FECHA_OBJETIVO.
4. Adapt the mechanism to HERRAMIENTA: Leitner box system for physical flashcards; the SM-2 principle of adaptive intervals based on recalled difficulty for Anki or an equivalent app; date and box columns for a spreadsheet.
5. Design the daily session prioritizing active retrieval: attempt to recall before seeing the answer, self-assess, and reschedule each unit (shorten the interval if failed, extend it if correct), within the limit of MINUTOS_DIARIOS.
6. Deliver the calendar and maintenance rules.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpretation: restate the objective, material volume, and time and date constraints.
Phase 2 Atomization: list or exemplify the recall units and fix the estimated count; discard compound units (more than one idea) by splitting them.
Phase 3 Cadence: calculate intervals and number of cycles up to FECHA_OBJETIVO; flag with [SUPUESTO] any volume or pace estimate not provided.
Phase 4 Daily mechanics: active retrieval, self-assessment, and rescheduling protocol according to HERRAMIENTA; define the "mastered" threshold (n consecutive correct recalls) and the "reincorporated" threshold after a failure.
Phase 5 Delivery: calendar table + forgetting/mastery rules + overload signal if units per day exceed MINUTOS_DIARIOS.
Edge cases: (a) date insufficient for all cycles -> prioritize highest-weight or highest-frequency units and flag the shortfall; (b) no date -> open-ended maintenance cycle with a long-tail review queue; (c) volume that saturates daily time -> propose reducing the new-unit batch per day or extending the ramp-up, never hide the overload.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All 5 inputs verified; missing ones asked for, not invented.
- [ ] Material broken into atomic units (one idea per unit) with an estimated count.
- [ ] Growing intervals explicit and justified by the forgetting curve and spacing effect.
- [ ] Mechanism consistent with HERRAMIENTA (manual Leitner or digital SM-2), not generic.
- [ ] Each session prioritizes active retrieval before rereading, with a fail/correct rescheduling rule and mastery/reincorporation thresholds.
- [ ] Cadence adjusted to FECHA_OBJETIVO; the case of an insufficient date or indefinite retention is resolved.
- [ ] Daily load compatible with MINUTOS_DIARIOS; explicit warning if exceeded.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]; no prices or promises of free access.
Expected deliverable: a table with columns Date | Units to review | Estimated minutes covering up to FECHA_OBJETIVO, accompanied by maintenance rules for reincorporating forgotten units and graduating mastered ones.
spec-personal_flashcards_activas:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Topic or subject to study (what the cards are about)
- MATERIAL: {{MATERIAL}} > Source material to convert: text, notes, definitions, or list of facts
- NIVEL_DOMINIO: {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}} > Target depth: memorize facts, understand concepts, or apply procedures
- CANTIDAD_TARJETAS: {{CANTIDAD_TARJETAS}} > Target number of cards (optional; if missing, the model proposes a reasonable count based on material volume)
- FORMATO_TARJETA: {{FORMATO_TARJETA}} > Preferred format: question-answer, cloze deletion, or mixed (optional; default mixed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The learner has {{MATERIAL}} on {{TEMA}} and needs to fix it in long-term memory, not just re-read it. Re-reading and highlighting create an illusion of mastery: the content is recognized without being retrievable when needed. The goal is to transform the material into active-recall flashcards that force retrieval (pulling the answer from memory) instead of passive recognition. This activates the testing effect and desirable difficulty: the effort of remembering is what consolidates learning. A well-built set is unlocked for spaced-repetition review and converts hours of diffuse study into verifiable mastery at the {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}} level. Risk to avoid: poorly designed cards (overloaded, ambiguous, or causing interference) that erode motivation and train recognition instead of retrieval.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior learning science specialist, expert in active recall, the testing effect, desirable difficulty, and flashcard design following Piotr Wozniak's minimum information principle.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate {{TEMA}} in one sentence and the depth implied by {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}} (recall, comprehend, or apply).
2. Extract from {{MATERIAL}} the separable knowledge units: each fact, relationship, cause, definition, or step worth remembering on its own.
3. Apply atomicity: one card = one single retrievable idea; break compound concepts into multiple cards instead of long answers.
4. Draft each front as a retrieval question, not a recognition question: no cues that give away the answer, no multiple choice, preferably using what/how/why/when/what is the difference; use cloze for dense concepts per {{FORMATO_TARJETA}}.
5. Write each back brief, precise, and self-sufficient: just enough to verify the answer.
6. Avoid two design flaws: interference cards (near-identical pairs confused during review) and unnecessary reversals (same front-back pair repeated in reverse without value). If two cards compete, add a distinctive anchor to the front.
7. Calibrate {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}}: if it is apply procedures, include at least one front that requires executing a step or solving a case, not just naming the definition.
8. Adjust to {{CANTIDAD_TARJETAS}}, prioritizing the highest-value ideas; mark [SUPUESTO] on any data not in {{MATERIAL}} and do not treat it as certain.
9. Present a numbered table with columns Front, Back, Topic, and Difficulty (high/medium/low), and close with a spaced-repetition calendar (days 1, 3, 7, 16, and 35 from today) flagging the 3 to 5 high-difficulty cards to review first, plus a one-line note on honest self-assessment (retrieve before flipping the card).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm {{TEMA}}, {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}}, and the scope of {{MATERIAL}}; if the material, topic, or level is missing, ask before generating cards.
Phase 2 - Plan: list the knowledge units identified and how many cards will come from each, adjusted to {{CANTIDAD_TARJETAS}} and {{FORMATO_TARJETA}}; flag any ambiguous area or assumption before drafting.
Phase 3 - Execute: generate the atomic retrieval cards, verify one by one that none is recognition-based, ambiguous, or causing interference, and deliver the table plus the review calendar.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each card covers a single retrievable idea (atomicity); no back chains multiple facts.
- Each front demands retrieval from memory; none is recognition-based, multiple-choice, or gives away the answer.
- Back answers are brief, precise, and self-sufficient for self-verification.
- No interference pairs without a distinctive anchor, no valueless reversals.
- If {{NIVEL_DOMINIO}} is apply, at least one card requires executing or solving, not just naming.
- All content comes from {{MATERIAL}}; anything not present is marked [SUPUESTO] or requested.
- The number of cards respects {{CANTIDAD_TARJETAS}} and the format respects {{FORMATO_TARJETA}}.
- Neutral, professional English, no emojis or filler.
Expected deliverable: numbered flashcard table (Front | Back | Topic | Difficulty) ready to load into a spaced-repetition system, plus a review calendar (days 1, 3, 7, 16, 35) with the 3 to 5 high-difficulty cards marked for first review and a brief honest self-assessment note.
spec-personal_practica_deliberada:
[inputs]
- DESTREZA: {{DESTREZA}} > Skill to improve (e.g., public speaking, piano sight-reading, technical writing)
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Honest starting point: what you can already do and where you fail today
