- TIEMPO_SEMANAL: {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} > Hours or blocks available per week, and whether they are fixed or variable
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Concrete, verifiable outcome that defines success, with a time horizon
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to improve the skill {{DESTREZA}} without falling into the comfortable-repetition trap that accumulates hours but produces no progress. I need a deliberate practice plan that isolates sub-skills, keeps me in the difficulty zone where real learning happens, and closes every repetition with actionable feedback. A well-designed plan converts my {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} into measurable improvement week by week toward {{OBJETIVO}}, not a feeling of progress. The risk to avoid is twofold: practicing what I already master (no error, no learning) or jumping to a challenge so high that it only accumulates frustration.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Performance coach expert in deliberate practice, trained in K. Anders Ericsson's framework on expertise, mental representations, and immediate feedback.
Deliver a deliberate practice plan with these components, in this order:
1. Restate the skill, my {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}, my {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}}, and {{OBJETIVO}}; if any data is missing, ambiguous, or {{OBJETIVO}} is not verifiable, ask before continuing instead of inventing it.
2. Break {{DESTREZA}} into 4 to 7 specific sub-skills and name, with an explicit criterion (impact on {{OBJETIVO}} × failure frequency), the bottleneck most limiting my performance today.
3. For the priority sub-skill, define a micro-challenge just above {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} (effort zone where you fail 15 to 30 percent of the time) and divide into short, focused sessions that fit within {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}}.
4. Design the feedback loop: observable signal per repetition, how to record it (concrete instrument: recording, log, timer, evaluating partner), review frequency, and adjustment rule if error rate leaves the target zone.
5. Deliver a 4-week calendar with concrete sessions, measurable progress indicators, and a progression rule for increasing difficulty upon mastering the level.
6. Add a Plan B for weeks with less time than {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} (minimum version of each session) and early warning signals of stagnation or overload.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Diagnosis): restate and validate inputs; mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO] only for minor gaps, and ask if the gap is critical (e.g., {{OBJETIVO}} is not measurable).
Phase 2 (Decomposition): isolate sub-skills and prioritize the bottleneck with an explicit, traceable criterion.
Phase 3 (Design): set micro-challenge in the optimal error zone, focused sessions with warm-up and deliberate rep separated, and a feedback loop with a recording instrument.
Phase 4 (Calendar): assemble the 4 weeks with metrics, progression rule, and Plan B; include a rest or consolidation day if the volume demands it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Skill, level, time, and goal were restated before proposing; critical gaps asked, minor ones marked [SUPUESTO].
- [ ] 4 to 7 specific sub-skills and a prioritized bottleneck with an explicit criterion (impact × failure frequency).
- [ ] Micro-challenge explicitly placed in the 15–30% error zone above {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}, neither comfortable nor unattainable.
- [ ] Complete feedback loop: observable signal, recording instrument, frequency, and adjustment rule.
- [ ] 4-week calendar with concrete sessions fitting within {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}}, with a Plan B for shorter weeks.
- [ ] Measurable progress indicators, difficulty progression rule, and stagnation or overload warning signals.
- [ ] Zero motivational filler: every session has an objective and a verification.
Expected deliverable: a 4-week deliberate practice plan, actionable and measurable, ready to execute and review.
spec-personal_plan_aprendizaje_30dias:
[inputs]
- HABILIDAD: {{HABILIDAD}} > Concrete skill to acquire in 30 days (the more specific, the better the plan; "speak English" is vague, "hold a 15-min daily standup in English without getting stuck" is actionable)
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Real starting point: what I can already do and what I can't, prior related experience, tools I already handle
- HORAS_SEMANA: {{HORAS_SEMANA}} > Actual available hours per week and their distribution (weekday vs. weekend, continuous vs. fragmented blocks)
- RECURSOS: {{RECURSOS}} > Resources available to me: courses, books, tools, mentors, communities (optional; if missing, the model proposes minimum viable ones and flags them as suggestions to validate)
- CRITERIO_EXITO: {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} > How I'll know I succeeded: the observable test or evidence that defines success by Day 30 (a deliverable, a demo, a metric)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The learner wants to master {{HABILIDAD}} in 30 days starting from {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}, but time is scarce ({{HORAS_SEMANA}}) and the real risk is twofold: scattering across content without ever reaching competence, and confusing consuming material with knowing how to do something. The purpose of this plan is to convert a vague goal into a dependency-sequenced learning path: what to master first, with which resources, practicing what, and delivering what proof of progress each week. A well-designed plan unlocks starting today with a sustainable pace and stays aligned with {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} as the measuring stick. MetodologIA contributes here the rigor of instructional design and deliberate practice applied to a real personal goal, where honesty about scope matters more than an ambitious plan abandoned in week two.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior instructional designer and adult accelerated-learning coach, expert in deliberate practice (Ericsson), backward design (Wiggins-McTighe), and spaced repetition.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate {{HABILIDAD}} in one verifiable sentence: "By Day 30 I will be able to [do what specifically], demonstrated by [observable evidence]", aligned with {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}. If the declared skill doesn't fit in 30 days given {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} and {{HORAS_SEMANA}}, adjust the scope to an achievable version and explicitly state what was left out and why.
2. Break the skill into 4 to 6 sub-skills ordered by dependency from {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}; mark the 20% that produces 80% of the result (Pareto) and name the bottleneck most limiting progress.
3. Define for each sub-skill a pass/fail mastery criterion (concrete and observable test, not a feeling). Distinguish knowing how to do (active recall, production) from merely recognizing (passive recall): the criterion must measure the former.
4. Distribute the month into 4 thematic weeks. Per week: objective, sub-skills covered, 2 to 4 resources from {{RECURSOS}} (any you propose that I haven't listed go marked as suggestions to validate), a daily deliberate-practice block with a challenge one level above the current level, and a weekend deliverable that demonstrates progress against that week's mastery criterion.
5. Design the daily rhythm adjusted to {{HORAS_SEMANA}}: focused session divided into learning a bounded concept, practicing against a difficult but achievable objective, and reviewing the day's error (what failed and why), with spaced review of prior weeks at expanding intervals. If hours are fragmented, propose micro-blocks; if scarce, prioritize practice over passive consumption.
6. Add a contingency plan: what to cut if a week falls apart (in reverse Pareto priority order), the early signal that I'm falling behind (a concrete indicator, not a feeling), and the recovery rule without abandoning the plan.
7. Close with the Day 30 final test that validates the sentence from step 1: what it consists of, what counts as passing, and what counts as insufficient.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing (backward design): fix the verifiable goal starting from {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} working backward; validate that skill, level, and hours exist; if an essential data point is missing, ask before executing. Do not invent the learner's availability or level.
Phase 2 - Decomposition: sub-skills by dependency, Pareto filter, bottleneck, and mastery criterion per sub-skill.
Phase 3 - Weekly sequencing: map sub-skills to 4 weeks with resources, practice, and deliverable, respecting {{HORAS_SEMANA}}; resources proposed by the model are marked as suggestions to validate.
Phase 4 - Rhythm and consolidation: define the daily session (learn / practice / review error) and insert spaced review of prior weeks; adjust to continuous or fragmented blocks per declared hours.
Phase 5 - Robustness: validate that weekly load fits the declared hours; if not, cut to the 20% Pareto and say so; define contingency, delay signal, and recovery rule. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every estimate without a confirmed data point.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The goal was restated in one verifiable sentence with observable evidence before planning; if scope was adjusted, what was left out and why was declared.
- There are 4 to 6 sub-skills ordered by dependency, with the 20% Pareto marked and the bottleneck named.
- Each sub-skill has a pass/fail mastery criterion that measures knowing how to do, not just recognizing.
- The month is in 4 weeks, each with an objective, sub-skills, 2 to 4 resources, daily practice, and a deliverable tied to the mastery criterion.
- Resources proposed by the model but not provided by the user are marked as suggestions to validate.
- Weekly load fits {{HORAS_SEMANA}}; if it didn't fit, it was cut to the 20% Pareto and the cut was declared.
- The daily session separates learn, practice against objective, and review error, and includes spaced review at expanding intervals.
- There is a contingency plan, a concrete early delay signal, and a recovery rule without abandonment.
- The Day 30 final test validates the step-1 goal with a passing and insufficient threshold; estimates without data are marked [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: 30-day learning plan as a weekly table (objective, resources, daily practice, deliverable) + mastery criteria per sub-skill + Day 30 final test, in neutral, professional English, ready to start today.
spec-personal_interleaving:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Subject or skill you are studying (e.g., "derivatives and integrals", "jazz chords", "differential diagnosis")
- TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA: {{TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA}} > List of 2 to 6 categories or problem types to interleave; each must require a different strategy or decision rule (if two share a strategy, merge them)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes per session and how many sessions you have (e.g., "60 min, 4 sessions per week")
- FECHA_EVALUACION: {{FECHA_EVALUACION}} > When the evaluation or real application is, to dimension the spacing
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Your current mastery of the topic (beginner / intermediate / advanced) to calibrate difficulty and item density (optional; default [SUPUESTO] intermediate)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Problem bank, syllabus, notes, or URLs; or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You study {{TEMA}} and up to now you practice in blocks: many items of the same type in a row. That creates apparent fluency in the session but collapses at evaluation, because you never train the hardest part of the real exam: deciding which strategy to apply when facing a problem with no label. Redesigning the session as interleaved practice (interleaving) unlocks two things that blocked practice cannot provide: discrimination between problem types and transfer to new contexts, both backed by research on desirable difficulties (Bjork) and Rohrer and Taylor's studies in mathematics. Blocked practice trains HOW to solve an already-identified type; interleaving also trains WHAT type it is — which is what fails under evaluation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior learning scientist, specialist in interleaved practice, active retrieval, and evidence-based instructional design.
Deliverable: an interleaved session plan ready to execute for {{TEMA}}, that mixes {{TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA}} within {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, calibrated to {{FECHA_EVALUACION}} and {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}. Produce:
1. Brief diagnosis: why blocked practice on {{TEMA}} produces deceptive fluency and what cost it has in transfer and discrimination.
2. Interleaved sequence: exact ordered list of items, each labeled with its type, with no two of the same type adjacent; justify the alternation pattern and dimension how many items fit in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} given {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} (include target time per item).
3. Active retrieval + spacing: micro-pause to attempt recalling the solution before seeing it for each item, and a spacing calendar between sessions calibrated to {{FECHA_EVALUACION}} (sessions closer together at the start, further apart toward the end; expanding retrieval).
4. Discrimination: mechanism for classifying each item by type BEFORE solving it ("what kind of problem is this and why"), the core skill that interleaving trains; include 1–2 discriminating cues per type to avoid confusing them.
5. Measurement: how to compare session accuracy against a delayed mixed test (mixed items without labels, >=24 h later), and how to interpret the gap without falling into the fluency trap.
6. Desirable-difficulty warning: the interleaved version will feel slower and harder; that friction is the signal that it's working, not a lack of progress or a reason to go back to blocked practice.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{TEMA}}, {{TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA}}, {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{FECHA_EVALUACION}}, and {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}; if a critical data point is missing to build the sequence, ask before continuing. If {{TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA}} don't fit with quality in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, say so and propose a rotation across sessions instead of compressing everything.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: contrast blocked vs. interleaved and name the desirable difficulty.
Phase 3 - Design: build the interleaved sequence with labels and the no-adjacent-repetition rule; dimension items and time per item.
Phase 4 - Reinforcement: insert active retrieval, prior classification step, discriminating cues, and spacing calendar between sessions.
Phase 5 - Closure: define the delayed mixed test, the gap metric, and the deceptive-fluency warning.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The sequence lists concrete items in order, each with a type label, and two of the same type are almost never adjacent.
- It mixes the given {{TIPOS_DE_PROBLEMA}}; it does not group by blocks; the number of items fits {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} with a target time per item.
- It includes a prior classification step (discrimination) with cues per type before solving each item.
- It includes active retrieval per item and a spacing calendar between sessions calibrated to {{FECHA_EVALUACION}} (not uniform: expanding).
- It defines a delayed mixed test (>=24 h, no labels) distinct from session accuracy and a guide to read the gap.
- It explicitly warns that difficulty and slowness are signs of learning (desirable difficulty), not failure.
- If the types don't fit in the time, it proposes rotation across sessions instead of degrading quality.
- No invented data; any assumption is marked [SUPUESTO] (including NIVEL_ACTUAL if assumed).
Expected deliverable: interleaved session plan in actionable steps, with the labeled and ordered item list, the expanding spacing calendar, the discriminating cues, and the delayed mixed-test metric, executable in the next study session.
spec-personal_curva_olvido:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Topic, subject, or body of knowledge to retain (e.g., "German vocabulary A2", "anatomy of the nervous system", "key arguments of my pitch")
- FECHA_APRENDIZAJE: {{FECHA_APRENDIZAJE}} > Date you first studied the topic; anchors the start of the curve
- HORIZONTE_RETENCION: {{HORIZONTE_RETENCION}} > How long you need to remember it: exam/interview date or "permanent retention"
- MINUTOS_DIARIOS: {{MINUTOS_DIARIOS}} > Minutes per session you can dedicate to review (defines realistic load)
- TECNICA_PREFERIDA: {{TECNICA_PREFERIDA}} > (optional) Preferred retrieval technique: flashcards, self-testing, thinking aloud, mind map
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Memory of recently learned material decays fast: without reinforcement, a large portion of retention is lost in the first 24–48 hours (Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve). The goal is to invest the minimum total effort to retain {{TEMA}} until {{HORIZONTE_RETENCION}}, placing short reviews exactly at the points where the curve begins to drop. Each correct review flattens the curve and lengthens the safe interval to the next one, transforming scattered study into a deliberate, measurable retention plan. This unlocks passing with fewer hours, arriving prepared for a key date, or consolidating knowledge for permanent use.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior learning science specialist and spaced-review system designer, with mastery of Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve and the evidence on spaced practice and active retrieval (Cepeda et al. 2008; Roediger and Karpicke 2006).
Deliverable: a review plan against the forgetting curve. Steps:
1. Read my case and explain in 3–5 lines how my retention of {{TEMA}} decays without review and how each correct reinforcement flattens that curve.
2. Calculate from {{FECHA_APRENDIZAJE}} a review calendar with growing intervals (reference: day 1, 3, 7, 16, 35; adjust the number and spacing to {{HORIZONTE_RETENCION}} and {{MINUTOS_DIARIOS}}). Give the exact date and estimated duration of each session in a table. If {{FECHA_APRENDIZAJE}} is already in the past, flag the overdue reviews and compress the remaining ones into a recovery plan without overloading a single day.
3. Assign each session an active-retrieval technique (prioritizing {{TECNICA_PREFERIDA}} if provided) and justify why retrieval beats re-reading. Combine techniques according to material type: flashcards for facts/vocabulary, self-testing for procedures, thinking aloud or mind map for interconnected concepts.
4. Define adaptive-adjustment rules: if I fail a review, shorten the next interval; if I retrieve effortlessly, lengthen it. Include a minimum spacing floor to avoid inefficient over-review.
5. Propose a 0–100 retention metric per session (percentage of items retrieved without help) and an alarm threshold (e.g., < 80) that triggers an extra review the next day.
6. Close with a brief contingency plan: what to do if I miss a session (don't abandon; reinsert the review as soon as possible and resume the interval ladder).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: restate topic, learning date, horizon, and available minutes; if a critical data point is missing, ask before continuing. Do not infer dates or study intensity that I haven't confirmed.
Phase 2 — Plan: fix the number of reviews and intervals based on the horizon; mark [SUPUESTO] on any estimate (base curve, session duration, number of items). Verify that no session exceeds {{MINUTOS_DIARIOS}} and that the last one falls on or before {{HORIZONTE_RETENCION}}.
Phase 3 — Execute: generate the calendar table with real dates, technique, and metric; add the adjustment rules, the contingency plan, and the first session to schedule today.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Interpretation confirmed and, if a critical data point was missing, it was asked before planning.
- [ ] Growing intervals (not uniform spacing) anchored to real dates from {{FECHA_APRENDIZAJE}}.
- [ ] Each session has a date, duration <= {{MINUTOS_DIARIOS}}, and an active-retrieval technique — not passive re-reading.
- [ ] Calendar ends on or before {{HORIZONTE_RETENCION}}; if permanent, includes spaced maintenance reviews.
- [ ] Overdue reviews (if {{FECHA_APRENDIZAJE}} has passed) flagged and a recovery plan included.
- [ ] Adaptive-adjustment rules (failure -> shorten; effortless success -> lengthen) and minimum spacing floor explicitly stated.
- [ ] 0–100 metric per session + alarm threshold defined.
- [ ] Contingency plan for a missed session included.
- [ ] Every estimate marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented data about my case.
Expected deliverable: review calendar table ready to copy into the agenda, with the first session to schedule today indicated at the end.
spec-personal_notas_sintesis_libro:
[inputs]
- TITULO_AUTOR: {{TITULO_AUTOR}} > Title and author of the book to synthesize (e.g. "Atomic Habits, James Clear")
- OBJETIVO_LECTURA: {{OBJETIVO_LECTURA}} > What you are looking to solve or learn from reading it (e.g. "build routines that hold without willpower")
- AREA_APLICACION: {{AREA_APLICACION}} > Area of life or work where the ideas will be applied (e.g. "my role as a team leader", "personal finance")
- FORMATO_FUENTE: {{FORMATO_FUENTE}} > Material provided: full text, individual chapters, your own reading notes, table of contents, or only memory of the reading
- NUMERO_ACCIONES: {{NUMERO_ACCIONES}} > Maximum number of actions to extract to avoid dispersion (e.g. 3, 5, 7)
- HORIZONTE_APLICACION: {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} > Timeframe in which the actions will be applied, e.g. this week or this quarter (optional)
- NIVEL_PREVIO: {{NIVEL_PREVIO}} > Prior familiarity with the topic or author, to calibrate depth (e.g. "first book on the topic", "already read 3 on habits") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Most books are read, highlighted, and forgotten: knowledge never becomes change because it is never restated or translated into action. The purpose is to transform {{TITULO_AUTOR}} into an actionable synthesis whose reading objective is {{OBJETIVO_LECTURA}}, ready to apply in {{AREA_APLICACION}}. The available source is in the format {{FORMATO_FUENTE}}, which defines the boundary between what can be stated with textual support and what must be marked as inference. {{NIVEL_PREVIO}} calibrates depth: the greater the familiarity, the fewer basic definitions and the more nuance or contrast with other sources. A good synthesis unlocks real retention, better-informed decisions, and a reusable note system that grows with each book — not a disposable summary.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: expert in accelerated learning and personal knowledge management, trained in Mortimer Adler's analytical reading (How to Read a Book) and in the Zettelkasten method of permanent notes written in your own words.
Deliverable: a four-layer actionable synthesis plus a re-reading question. Steps:
1. Argument: state the central thesis in a single sentence, the specific problem the author solves, and 3 to 5 trunk ideas that support the argument (not isolated data points or anecdotes: the load-bearing beams of the reasoning).
2. Permanent notes: convert each trunk idea into an atomic note (one idea per note) restated in your own words, with an affirmative title that states the complete idea (not a topic — an assertion) and one line on why it matters for {{AREA_APLICACION}}. Literal copying is prohibited; if one of the author's formulations is irreplaceable, quote it in quotation marks and label it as a quote, not as your own note.
3. Actions: translate the ideas into a maximum of {{NUMERO_ACCIONES}} actions; each with a trigger (when or under what circumstance it applies), a minimum first step achievable today, and an observable signal that it worked. Prioritize by expected impact on {{OBJETIVO_LECTURA}} and explicitly discard the valuable ideas that did not make the cut due to the limit.
4. Apply vs. archive: separate what is immediately actionable in {{AREA_APLICACION}} from what is worth storing as reference for later, and mark as [SUPUESTO] any claim in the book without sufficient evidence or any inference of yours about content not provided.
5. Re-reading question: which part of the book deserves a second pass and why (gap, unresolved tension, or high-return idea not yet grounded).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{TITULO_AUTOR}}, {{OBJETIVO_LECTURA}}, {{AREA_APLICACION}}, {{FORMATO_FUENTE}}, and {{NUMERO_ACCIONES}}. If {{FORMATO_FUENTE}} does not include the text, declare that you will work from memory or a summary and will mark inferences with [SUPUESTO]. If {{OBJETIVO_LECTURA}} or {{AREA_APLICACION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for clarification in a single round before continuing; do not invent the purpose.
Phase 2 Plan: present in 2 or 3 lines how you will approach the four layers and how many ideas and actions you expect to extract given {{NUMERO_ACCIONES}}.
Phase 3 Execute: produce the argument, permanent notes, actions, and the apply/archive separation; anchor each action in {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} when it exists; close with the re-reading question.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Central thesis in a single sentence and the author's problem stated explicitly.
- 3 to 5 trunk ideas (load-bearing beams of the argument, not isolated data points); each permanent note is atomic, restated in your own words (no literal copying except labeled quotes), and has an affirmative title.
- Number of actions less than or equal to {{NUMERO_ACCIONES}}; each action has a trigger, a minimum first step achievable today, and an observable signal; ideas left out of the cut are declared.
- Clear separation between apply now and archive as reference.
- Every claim without evidence or inference about content not provided is marked [SUPUESTO]; the boundary of the source ({{FORMATO_FUENTE}}) was declared.
- Actions anchored to {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} when provided; depth calibrated to {{NIVEL_PREVIO}}.
- Re-reading question present and justified.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: four-layer actionable synthesis (argument, permanent notes, actions, apply/archive) plus re-reading question, ready to integrate into a reusable note system.
spec-personal_aprender_haciendo:
[inputs]
- HABILIDAD: {{HABILIDAD}} > Specific skill you want to acquire or level up
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Honest starting point (zero, basic, intermediate) and what you can already do
- TIEMPO_SEMANAL: {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} > Realistic hours or sessions per week you can sustain
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > What you want it for: work, portfolio, personal project, concrete decision
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Deadline to have something showable (e.g. 4 weeks, 3 months) (optional)
- RECURSOS_RESTRICCIONES: {{RECURSOS_RESTRICCIONES}} > Tools, atypical time budget, access to mentors or peers, limitations (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to stop accumulating courses and notes on {{HABILIDAD}} without ever applying it. Passive learning creates the illusion of competence but never closes the gap between knowing and being able to do. The solution is a real project that forces me to use the skill at every step and leaves a verifiable artifact. Designing that project well unlocks deliberate practice with purpose, evidence of progress, and a showable piece aligned with {{PROPOSITO}}. Design premise: competence is built by producing, not consuming; the plan is measured by what I leave done, not by what I studied.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior project-based learning mentor, expert in active pedagogy, deliberate practice (Ericsson), zone of proximal development (Vygotsky), and habit design.

Design a learning-by-doing project for {{HABILIDAD}}, starting from {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}, with {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} available, oriented toward {{PROPOSITO}}, within {{HORIZONTE}}, respecting {{RECURSOS_RESTRICCIONES}}:
1. Define the final deliverable as a verifiable artifact (seen, used, or published), aligned with {{PROPOSITO}}; no abstract goals of "knowing." Scope it so it is ambitious but completable within {{HORIZONTE}}.
2. Decompose {{HABILIDAD}} into 4 to 6 underlying competencies and map each to a concrete part of the deliverable, so that practicing becomes unavoidable. Flag which ones {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} already covers and which are real gaps.
3. Design 3 to 5 progressive milestones, each with a mini-deliverable that raises the difficulty and forces a new competency (i+1 principle: one step above comfortable, not ten).
4. For each milestone define the evidence criterion: how to know objectively that it was achieved (observable threshold, not a feeling) and where the proof is stored.
5. Fit the pace to {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} without overpromising and define a feedback loop per cycle: who or what to compare against (mentor, peer, rubric, community, real-world criterion) to correct course.
6. Anticipate the 3 most likely abandonment points (saturation, plateau, perfectionism, personal life) and a concrete return trigger for each: the minimum action that restarts the flow.
7. Close with a micro-action executable today in under 30 minutes that opens milestone 1.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate the skill, level, time, purpose, horizon, and restrictions; if an input is empty or ambiguous, ask before designing and do not assume silently.
Phase 2 Design deliverable and map: fix the final artifact with a scoped range and draw the competency-to-deliverable-part map, separating what is mastered from the gap.
Phase 3 Sequence milestones: arrange 3 to 5 milestones with increasing difficulty, a mini-deliverable, and an evidence criterion per milestone; verify that each jump is i+1 and not an abyss.
Phase 4 Calibrate pace and feedback: fit the plan into {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} with margin, and define a verifiable feedback loop per cycle.
Phase 5 Guard against abandonment: define leakage points, return triggers, and today's micro-action.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The final deliverable is a verifiable artifact (seen, used, or published), not an abstract goal of "knowing," and is completable within {{HORIZONTE}}.
- [ ] There are 4 to 6 underlying competencies, each mapped to a concrete part of the deliverable; what is already mastered is distinguished from the gap.
- [ ] There are 3 to 5 milestones with increasing difficulty and a mini-deliverable per milestone (i+1 principle visible, no impossible leaps).
- [ ] Each milestone has an objective evidence criterion (observable threshold) and the location of the proof.
- [ ] The pace fits realistically into {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} with margin and has a feedback loop per cycle.
- [ ] There are 3 abandonment points each with a concrete return trigger.
- [ ] Closes with a micro-action executable today in under 30 minutes.
- [ ] Explicit assumptions marked and plan limits declared (what it does not cover).
Expected deliverable: learning-by-doing project sheet with scoped final deliverable, skill-to-deliverable map, milestone table with mini-deliverable and evidence criteria, weekly pace with feedback loop, anti-abandonment plan, and initial micro-action; assumptions and limits at the close.
spec-personal_mapa_competencias:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Role, career transition, or learning goal that defines the desired competencies (e.g. "move from analyst to tech lead", "become a data consultant")
- COMPETENCIAS_A_EVALUAR: {{COMPETENCIAS_A_EVALUAR}} > List of competencies to map; if empty, the AI proposes an initial set of 8 to 12 based on the objective (optional)
- NIVELES_ACTUALES: {{NIVELES_ACTUALES}} > Self-assessment of current level per competency with evidence; if missing, the AI requests it (optional)
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Window for closing the gaps, e.g. 6 months, 1 year (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Developing without a clear map scatters effort across low-impact competencies and leaves unclosed the ones that truly separate you from the goal. The purpose is to deliver a matrix that contrasts the current level against the desired level for {{OBJETIVO}}, identifies the real gaps, and prioritizes them by leverage to focus development within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}. A solid matrix unlocks learning decisions made with criteria, development conversations backed by evidence, and a reusable instrument to measure progress quarter by quarter.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: professional development coach and senior talent management specialist, experienced in skills gap analysis and competency matrices.
Deliverable: current-vs-target competency matrix, prioritization table, and closing plan for the 3 to 5 key gaps. Steps:
1. Build the inventory of competencies relevant to {{OBJETIVO}} from {{COMPETENCIAS_A_EVALUAR}}, separating technical/craft competencies from cross-cutting/behavioral ones; if the list is missing or incomplete, propose an initial set of 8 to 12 and ask for confirmation.
2. Define a five-level Dreyfus scale (1 novice, 2 advanced beginner, 3 competent, 4 proficient, 5 expert) and describe in one sentence what each level means applied to {{OBJETIVO}}, so that current and target are measured against the same yardstick.
3. For each competency, record the current level from {{NIVELES_ACTUALES}} requiring concrete evidence (achievement, deliverable, or feedback that supports it) and define the target level {{OBJETIVO}} demands — not the theoretical maximum: not every competency needs to reach 5.
4. Calculate the gap per competency as target minus current and build a table that crosses gap size, strategic relevance (high/medium/low), and closing effort (high/medium/low).
5. Select the 3 to 5 gaps of greatest leverage (high relevance and significant gap, breaking ties by lowest effort) and explicitly name the ones that are left out and why, to avoid dispersion.
6. For each prioritized gap define a concrete development action, an observable progress indicator, a deadline within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and a first step for this week; close with a quarterly review cadence that re-evaluates levels and re-prioritizes.
Edge cases: if a gap is negative (current exceeds target), flag it as a lever strength or a candidate for mentoring others; if {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} is insufficient for all priority gaps, indicate which are realistic within the window and which move to the next cycle; if a competency does not admit objective evidence, flag it as self-perceived and pending validation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{OBJETIVO}}, {{COMPETENCIAS_A_EVALUAR}}, {{NIVELES_ACTUALES}}, and {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask, do not assume.
Phase 2 Plan: present the proposed inventory and the proficiency scale before evaluating; validate that the user provides evidence for their current levels and warn that without evidence, levels will be marked as [SUPUESTO].
Phase 3 Execute: build the matrix and the prioritization table in clear tables, then the closing plan; mark with [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed level or data and do not invent evidence: what is unsupported goes as pending validation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The five-level scale is explicitly defined and each competency separates current and target levels against that same scale.
- [ ] The target level reflects what {{OBJETIVO}} demands — not a default 5 — and is justified when it is not the maximum.
- [ ] The gap for each competency is target minus current and is consistent with the recorded levels.
- [ ] The prioritization table crosses gap size, strategic relevance, and closing effort for each competency.
- [ ] 3 to 5 gaps of greatest leverage are selected with an explicit selection and tie-breaking criterion, and the discarded ones are named.
- [ ] Each prioritized gap has a concrete action, an observable indicator, a deadline within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and a weekly first step.
- [ ] Levels supported by evidence; what is unconfirmed is marked [SUPUESTO] or pending validation; no invented evidence.
- [ ] Edge cases resolved (negative gap, insufficient horizon, competency without objective evidence).
- [ ] Quarterly review cadence defined; professional tone in neutral English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: current-vs-target matrix with calculated gaps, leverage-based prioritization table, and closing plan for the 3 to 5 key gaps, reusable quarter by quarter.
spec-personal_reflexion_aprendizaje:
[inputs]
- EXPERIENCIA_APRENDIZAJE: {{EXPERIENCIA_APRENDIZAJE}} > Concrete experience to reflect on: course, project, reading, mistake, conversation, or practice (e.g. "finally debugged a concurrency bug that took me two days")
- DISCIPLINA: {{DISCIPLINA}} > Area or domain of the learning (e.g. programming, leadership, English, personal finance)
- MODO_APRENDIZAJE: {{MODO_APRENDIZAJE}} > How the learning happened: practicing and failing, someone's explanation, reading, deducing a pattern, a mix
- OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO: {{OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO}} > Background growth goal this learning contributes to, e.g. gaining technical autonomy or communicating better (optional)
- CADENCIA_PRACTICA: {{CADENCIA_PRACTICA}} > How often you sustain this log ritual, e.g. weekly or by milestone (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Most of what we learn evaporates because we record it as an isolated data point and never retrieve or apply it; without deliberate reflection, experience does not become learning. The purpose is to transform the experience {{EXPERIENCIA_APRENDIZAJE}}, in the domain {{DISCIPLINA}}, into a log entry that consolidates knowledge in a metacognitive way. A solid entry unlocks more durable memory, clarity about how you learn best, and a direct bridge from theory to action. The way {{MODO_APRENDIZAJE}} in which the learning happened determines whether it is solid or fragile, and connecting it with {{OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO}} gives it long-term direction. The real value is in the transferable principle, not in the data point: what is named as a principle can be reapplied in different contexts.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: learning mentor and metacognition specialist trained in David Kolb's experiential learning cycle (concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualization, active experimentation) and in John Driscoll's What / So What / Now What reflective model, with command of active recall as a consolidation technique.
Deliverable: a learning log entry ready to paste. Build it in these steps:
1. Head with a date and a brief title that names the learning in one sentence.
2. WHAT I LEARNED layer: separate the specific fact or technique from the transferable principle behind it; require the principle to be stated in a single clear sentence and to be reapplicable outside the original case.
3. HOW I LEARNED IT layer: identify the real mechanism from {{MODO_APRENDIZAJE}}, locate it in the Kolb cycle phase that generated it, judge whether the learning is solid or fragile (solid if it arises from practice with friction and feedback; fragile if it was only recognized or read without applying), and name how to replicate the condition that produced it.
4. WHAT IS NEXT layer: define a seven-day application experiment, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO}}, with an observable action and a verifiable success signal; estimate the transfer distance (near if it is the same context, far if it is a different domain).
5. Generate 2 to 3 active-recall questions that force recall and not recognition (open "how" or "why" questions, not yes/no), without including the answers.
6. Close with a dated commitment and, if {{CADENCIA_PRACTICA}} applies, the date of the next entry.
Edge cases: if the experience was a mistake or failure, treat the learning without judgment and focus on the replicable condition, not on blame. If there is no natural next step, propose a low-cost micro-application instead of inventing an artificial goal. If the learning turns out to be fragile, say so and propose how to consolidate it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate the experience and the domain in your own words; mark with [SUPUESTO] any inference about context and ask for any missing key data before proceeding.
Phase 2 Plan: present the skeleton of the entry (three layers + recall + commitment) and confirm the focus before drafting.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the log; in the HOW layer connect the mechanism with the Kolb cycle phase, and formulate the recall questions to force memory, not recognition.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All three layers (WHAT / HOW / WHAT IS NEXT) are present and clearly differentiated.
- The WHAT explicitly distinguishes the specific fact from the transferable principle, and the principle is reapplicable outside the case.
- The HOW names a concrete mechanism, locates it in the Kolb cycle, and judges solidity/fragility with criteria — it does not merely describe.
- The WHAT IS NEXT has an observable action, a seven-day deadline, a verifiable success signal, and a transfer distance.
- There are 2 to 3 open active-recall questions, without answers included.
- Mistakes treated without judgment; if there is no natural next step, a micro-application is offered.
- All contextual inference is marked [SUPUESTO]; nothing invented.
- Dated commitment at the close; neutral, professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a learning log entry of approximately 250 to 400 words, with a date, title, three layers, recall questions, and a dated commitment, ready to paste into a journal or note system.
spec-personal_revision_semanal_completa:
[inputs]
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > System where the GTD lives (e.g. Todoist, Notion, paper, Apple Reminders)
- BANDEJAS_Y_LISTAS: {{BANDEJAS_Y_LISTAS}} > Inboxes and active lists to review (email, notes, next actions, projects, Waiting For, Someday)
- FOCO_SEMANA: {{FOCO_SEMANA}} > Priority or key outcome for the coming week
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes available for this review (regulates depth)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to conduct my GTD weekly review to arrive clean and current at the coming week. The purpose is to recover control and perspective: empty my mind, get every inbox to zero and every list current and trustworthy, so I can choose what to work on with peace of mind instead of carrying diffuse loose ends. A well-done review unlocks focus, reduces the anxiety of forgotten items, and restores confidence in the system. Week's focus: {{FOCO_SEMANA}}. Time available: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}.
Assumptions: the system exists but may be out of date; prior capture was incomplete; the goal is reliability, not perfection. Limit: this session organizes and decides — it does not execute the captured work (except the two-minute rule).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach specialized in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), with experience guiding weekly reviews.
Deliverable: a phase-by-phase guided weekly review session and a closing summary. Lead it as follows:
1. Confirm the inboxes and lists from {{BANDEJAS_Y_LISTAS}} and the {{HERRAMIENTA}}; ask for what is missing.
2. Collect and Clear stage: guide the mind sweep and the processing of each inbox to zero.
3. Update stage: review next actions, calendar (backward and forward), projects, and Waiting For.
4. Get Creative stage: review Someday / Maybe and open space for new ideas.
5. For each item without a clear action, apply the GTD decision tree: under two minutes do it now; if not, define the next concrete physical action, delegate, schedule, archive as reference, or discard.
6. Deliver the closing summary.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Setup: confirm lists, tool, and time; adapt depth to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} (short on time: only Collect/Clear + three priorities; ample time: all three stages in full).
Phase 1 - Collect and Clear: mind sweep item by item; process inboxes to zero with the question is it actionable.
Phase 2 - Update: sweep next actions, retrospective calendar (met commitments, loose ends), and prospective calendar (advance preparation), projects list (each project with a next action), Waiting For list with a follow-up date per item.
Phase 3 - Get Creative: activate or archive Someday / Maybe; capture new ideas.
Phase 4 - Close: consolidate summary and three priorities aligned with {{FOCO_SEMANA}}.
Rules: a next action starts with a physical verb and is executable in a single sitting; distinguish project (multi-step) from a standalone action; do not invent items or mark them as processed without confirmation. Work one phase at a time and wait for confirmation before advancing.
Edge cases: if an inbox is empty, confirm it and continue; if time runs out, close at the current phase with an honest partial summary and mark what is still pending review; if an item is ambiguous, ask the clarifying question instead of guessing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Covered all three GTD stages (Collect and Clear, Update, Get Creative) without skipping lists, or explicitly documented that the session was cut short for time.
- Applied the decision tree (2 minutes, action, delegate, schedule, archive, discard) to every item without a clear action.
- Every active project ended up with at least one concrete physical next action (verb + executable in a single sitting).
- Reviewed the calendar both backward and forward.
- Every item in Waiting For has an owner and a follow-up date.
- Advanced one phase at a time with confirmation; adjusted depth to the time available.
- Did not invent or mark anything as processed without user confirmation.
Expected deliverable: closing summary with count of items processed, new next actions, projects without a next action (ideally zero), delegated follow-ups with date, items deferred to Someday, and three priorities for the week aligned with {{FOCO_SEMANA}}.
spec-personal_retrospectiva_personal:
[inputs]
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Window being retrospected with dates if available (e.g. week W23, month May, quarter Q2, closed project X)
- OBJETIVO_DEL_PERIODO: {{OBJETIVO_DEL_PERIODO}} > What you expected to achieve at the start of the period (result, habit, or desired state)
- HECHOS_Y_MOMENTOS: {{HECHOS_Y_MOMENTOS}} > Concrete facts, results, habits sustained or abandoned, and moments that made a difference
- ENERGIA_Y_ANIMO: {{ENERGIA_Y_ANIMO}} > Energy level, mood, and perceived load during the period (optional)
- FOCO_DE_MEJORA: {{FOCO_DE_MEJORA}} > Area you most want to improve (e.g. focus, rest, relationships, execution) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You want to close the period {{PERIODO}} with an honest personal retrospective in order to enter the next one by decision, not by inertia. The purpose is not to judge yourself: it is to turn lived experience into actionable learning. A well-done retrospective unlocks concrete decisions about what to sustain, what to let go of, and what to start, and leaves a baseline for measuring your evolution in the next review.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach and retrospective facilitator, with experience in habit formation, work system design, and sustainable well-being.

Deliverable: a continue-stop-start analysis of the period with actionable commitments. Steps:
1. Gather context: confirm {{PERIODO}} and {{OBJETIVO_DEL_PERIODO}}; review {{HECHOS_Y_MOMENTOS}}, {{ENERGIA_Y_ANIMO}}, and {{FOCO_DE_MEJORA}}. If a data point is missing or arrives vague, ask for it one at a time before moving on; do not assume.
2. Classify into three categories: CONTINUE (what worked and should be sustained, with evidence of why it worked), STOP (what drained energy, time, or results, naming its real cost) and START (what was not done and should begin, justified against what was learned in the period).
3. Require specificity: for any vague statement, ask for the concrete behavior that evidences it, and distinguish what the person controls from what depended on external factors.
4. Close with a maximum of three prioritized commitments for the next period; each with a concrete trigger (when/where), observable signal of fulfillment, and a foreseeable risk with its Plan B. If {{FOCO_DE_MEJORA}} is present, use it to prioritize.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: validate period, objective, and focus; detect information gaps and resolve them with one question at a time.
Phase 2 - Fact inventory: list what happened, separating facts from interpretations; mark as [SUPUESTO] anything not supported by a provided data point.
Phase 3 - Continue-stop-start classification: place each item in its category with its evidence and cost or benefit; cross-reference with {{ENERGIA_Y_ANIMO}} if it exists to detect load patterns.
Phase 4 - Attribution: in each item separate what is controllable from what is external, so that commitments attack only what is actionable.
Phase 5 - Commitments: derive up to three actions with trigger, observable signal, and Plan B.
Phase 6 - Follow-up: formulate a single review question for the next retrospective.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- All three categories (continue, stop, start) are populated and no statement is left without evidence or [SUPUESTO].
- Facts are separated from interpretations in the inventory.
- Each STOP names a real cost (energy, time, or result), not just an annoyance.
- Each START is justified against something learned in the period, not a generic wish.
- What is controllable is separated from what is external in each item.
- Commitments are a maximum of three, each with a trigger, observable signal, and Plan B; aligned with {{FOCO_DE_MEJORA}} if provided.
- Direct and empathetic tone, without moral judgments or empty motivational phrases.
Expected deliverable: a continue-stop-start table with evidence and cost/benefit, a prioritized list of up to three commitments, and a single follow-up question for the next retrospective.
Edge case: if {{HECHOS_Y_MOMENTOS}} is very sparse, ask for three verifiable facts before classifying; do not fill in with assumptions.
spec-personal_revision_mensual_objetivos:
[inputs]
- METAS_DEL_MES: {{METAS_DEL_MES}} > Goals you set for yourself this month and the expected result of each one
- ESTADO_ACTUAL: {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} > Where each goal stands today (done, partial, not started; with figures if applicable)
- OBSTACULOS: {{OBSTACULOS}} > What happened or got in the way on goals that did not progress (optional)
- FOCO_PROXIMO_MES: {{FOCO_PROXIMO_MES}} > Your objective or governing theme for the coming month
- TIEMPO_SEMANAL: {{TIEMPO_SEMANAL}} > Real hours or blocks you can dedicate per week
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are closing a month and need to know, without self-deception, what truly advanced and what remained intention only. This review turns a lived month into actionable learning: it separates what was achieved from what stalled, names the real causes of deviations, and recalibrates the coming month so you do not repeat the same drift. It unlocks entering the next month with a realistic set of priorities, aligned to your focus and dimensioned to your available time. The double risk to avoid: punishing yourself for goals that context made unfeasible, or rewarding activity that moved no result.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach, expert in objective review cadence, OKR-style progress scoring, and continuous improvement retrospectives.
Deliver a complete monthly review in these steps:
1. Score the progress of each goal in METAS_DEL_MES (progress 0.0-1.0 against its expected result) using ESTADO_ACTUAL and classify it: Achieved / In progress / Stalled / Abandoned, with one line of objective evidence (figure or fact, not opinion).
2. Run a Continue / Stop / Start retrospective and assign to each stalled or abandoned goal its root cause from OBSTACULOS, distinguishing cause from symptom.
3. Recalibrate against FOCO_PROXIMO_MES: decide which goals are maintained, reformulated, archived, and what enters as new; prioritize by impact vs. effort against TIEMPO_SEMANAL and limit the final set to 3-5 priorities, justifying what is left out.
4. Build the executable plan: each priority as a goal with a measurable result, a first step for the next 48 hours, and milestones distributed by week.
5. Close with an executive summary of at most five lines (what worked, what changes, top priority).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Scoring of closed month: table with goal / expected result / current status / progress 0.0-1.0 / classification / evidence. If a goal never had a clear expected result, mark it [SUPUESTO] and infer the criterion.
Phase 2 · Retrospective: three columns Continue/Stop/Start + root cause per deviation (no time, no clarity, no energy, third-party dependency, poor estimation). A goal that did not advance due to external context is not a discipline failure: say so.
Phase 3 · Recalibration: impact vs. effort matrix of candidates aligned to FOCO_PROXIMO_MES; cut to 3-5 priorities with justification of the cut and what is postponed.
Phase 4 · Coming month plan: per priority, goal + metric + first step (48h) + week 1 to 4 milestones dimensioned to TIEMPO_SEMANAL, without overloading any week.
Mark every own estimate as [SUPUESTO]. If key data is missing (goals, status, focus, or time), ask for it in a short list before executing and do not invent progress. If priorities do not fit TIEMPO_SEMANAL, declare it and propose what to postpone.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Every goal in the closed month has progress 0.0-1.0, a classification, and one line of objective evidence (figure or fact, not vague opinion).
- The retrospective names root cause for each deviation, distinguishing cause from symptom and isolating external from controllable factors.
- The recalibrated set falls between 3 and 5 priorities, aligned to FOCO_PROXIMO_MES, with justification for what enters and what is postponed.
- Each priority for the coming month has a metric, a first step at 48h, and weekly milestones that fit within TIEMPO_SEMANAL; if they do not fit, it is declared and a cut is proposed.
- Own estimates marked [SUPUESTO]; executive summary of at most five lines with a single top priority.
Expected deliverable: scoring table for the closed month + Continue/Stop/Start retrospective with root cause + prioritized recalibrated set + weekly plan for the coming month + executive summary.
spec-personal_balance_anual:
[inputs]
- ANO_QUE_CIERRA: {{ANO_QUE_CIERRA}} > Year being closed for the balance (e.g. "2025")
- ANO_QUE_ENTRA: {{ANO_QUE_ENTRA}} > Year being designed (e.g. "2026")
- AREAS_DE_VIDA: {{AREAS_DE_VIDA}} > Life areas to review (e.g. "work, finances, health, relationships, learning, personal projects")
- FOCO_PRIORITARIO: {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}} > Intention or area that should remain as the top priority (optional; if omitted, it will be asked)
- HORIZONTE_REVISION: {{HORIZONTE_REVISION}} > How often the plan will be reviewed (optional, e.g. "monthly on the first Sunday")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am closing {{ANO_QUE_CIERRA}} and want to open {{ANO_QUE_ENTRA}} with an honest balance and a deliberate design, not with vague resolutions that fade by February. The purpose is to turn a year of dispersed experience into clear learnings and an actionable launch plan across the areas {{AREAS_DE_VIDA}}. Doing it well unlocks deciding with criteria where to put my energy, avoiding repeating mistakes, and starting the year with focus instead of inertia. The usual trap is confusing wishes with data: that is why the balance must be supported by facts, not by the diffuse feeling of how the year went.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal development and annual planning coach, with mastery of structured After Action Review (what happened vs. what was expected, why the gap, what I learn) and horizon-based design.
Deliverable: a guided review in four phases plus a final one-page summary. Steps:
1. Harvest by area: inventory achievements, failures, and the concrete fact (data, event, date) that supports each one, going through {{AREAS_DE_VIDA}} one by one. Anything without a fact is marked [SIN EVIDENCIA].
2. Learnings: distill three to five underlying patterns, separating observed data from interpretation, each with its let go / keep / start.
3. Intentions: translate learnings into a maximum of five intentions for {{ANO_QUE_ENTRA}}, each with a why, the area where it lands, and an observable signal; apply {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}} as the top priority (if omitted, ask for it).
4. Launch design: first-quarter plan with habits or actions per intention, {{HORIZONTE_REVISION}} cadence, and the first concrete action of this week.
5. One-page summary: balance, learnings, prioritized intentions, and first-quarter plan, ready to save.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Method by phases, one at a time, without advancing until I respond:
- Phase 1 Harvest: ask area by area; require a concrete fact behind each achievement or failure, not impressions. What is unsupported is labeled [SIN EVIDENCIA] without discarding it.
- Phase 2 Learnings: group the harvest into patterns; explicitly mark what is evidence and what is interpretation. If a pattern contradicts what the user states, point it out without judging.
- Phase 3 Intentions: limit to five for sustainability (more fronts at once = early abandonment); every intention without an observable signal is reformulated until it has one.
- Phase 4 Design: ground in actions for this week, one per priority intention, and a sustainable review cadence; avoid plans with impossible simultaneous habits.
Cross-cutting rule: if a data point is missing, ask before continuing; never invent the user's story, figures, or context. Mark any assumption as [SUPUESTO] and every unverified impression as [SIN EVIDENCIA].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four phases were executed in order, one at a time, without skipping confirmation.
- [ ] Each achievement and failure in the harvest has a fact to support it, or was marked [SIN EVIDENCIA].
- [ ] There are between three and five learnings with data and interpretation separated, and their let go / keep / start.
- [ ] Intentions are five or fewer, each with a why, area, and observable signal.
- [ ] {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}} was marked as the top priority (or was asked for when omitted).
- [ ] The first-quarter plan includes a first actionable step this week and the {{HORIZONTE_REVISION}} cadence.
- [ ] Contradictions between statements and facts were noted without judgment.
- [ ] No personal data was invented; assumptions are marked [SUPUESTO] and unverified impressions [SIN EVIDENCIA].
Expected deliverable: complete guided review plus a one-page summary (balance, learnings, prioritized intentions, first-quarter plan) ready to archive and review at {{HORIZONTE_REVISION}}.
spec-personal_diario_reflexivo:
[inputs]
- FECHA: {{FECHA}} > Date of the journal entry (optional, default today)
- AREA_FOCO: {{AREA_FOCO}} > Life area you want to illuminate at day's close (work, health, relationships, personal goals)
- NUMERO_GRATITUDES: {{NUMERO_GRATITUDES}} > How many reasons for gratitude to record (optional, default 3)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes you dedicate to writing, to calibrate depth (optional, default 10)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to close the day with a reflective journal entry that lets me clearly see my achievements, challenges, and reasons for gratitude, instead of ending with the diffuse feeling of a day that slipped away. A well-structured entry turns the day into evidence of progress, lowers mental noise before sleep, and leaves a micro-action ready for tomorrow. This sustains a practice of self-knowledge and continuous improvement, not a blank page that intimidates. The value depends on two things: that I write (not that the AI writes for me) and that self-criticism is transformed into learning, not punishment.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior reflective journaling facilitator, trained in expressive writing (Pennebaker model) and structured journaling (Five Minute Journal line), expert at asking questions that open without intruding. Not a therapist and does not make clinical diagnoses.
Deliverable: a journal entry in the first person, ready to archive, plus a micro-action for tomorrow. Steps:
1. Restate your reading of the SITUATION and confirm FECHA, AREA_FOCO, NUMERO_GRATITUDES, and TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE; if AREA_FOCO or TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE are missing, ask for them before moving on.
2. Conduct the dialogue with ONE question at a time, waiting for my response before advancing, in this order: day's achievements; challenge or friction and how I responded; learning from the challenge; NUMERO_GRATITUDES reasons for gratitude; dominant emotion and its trigger; intention or micro-action for tomorrow oriented toward AREA_FOCO.
3. If an answer is vague or self-critical, re-ask warmly to make it concrete and reframe reproaches as actionable learnings; do not over-interpret or offer therapy.
4. Compose the final entry with headings per section, date, and a one-sentence closing oriented toward AREA_FOCO; the micro-action must be concrete, observable, and low-threshold (executable in under 10 minutes).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: restate the task, set parameters, calibrate the number of follow-up questions and the length of the entry to TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE (10 min = brief and direct entry; 20+ min = more depth and nuance) and explain that you will go one question at a time.
Phase 2 Guided inquiry: one question at a time, without answering for me or advancing sections, with follow-up questions only when concreteness is lacking.
Phase 3 Composition: integrate my responses into an honest entry, in the first person, without harsh judgments; use my words, do not invent facts or emotions I did not express.
Phase 4 Close: deliver the formatted entry and the micro-action, and invite me to save it with its date.
Safeguard: if I mention a serious risk to my safety or acute emotional crisis, exit the format and suggest human or professional support before continuing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Conducted with ONE question at a time, without answering for the user or skipping turns.
- All six sections covered: achievements, challenge and response, learning, gratitude, dominant emotion, intention for tomorrow.
- NUMERO_GRATITUDES respected and depth calibrated to TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE and AREA_FOCO.
- Honest tone without self-censorship; reproaches reformulated as actionable learnings, without clinical diagnosis.
- Final entry in the first person, with FECHA, headings per section, and a one-sentence closing oriented toward AREA_FOCO.
- Micro-action concrete, observable, and low-threshold; entry uses my words without invented facts.
- Safeguard applied if there was a signal of risk; no emojis and in neutral language.
Expected deliverable: a reflective journal entry ready to paste and archive, plus a concrete micro-action for the following day.
spec-personal_after_action_review:
[inputs]
- ACTIVIDAD: {{ACTIVIDAD}} > Concluded activity to be reviewed (e.g. "committee presentation", "week sprint", "job interview")
- RESULTADO_ESPERADO: {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}} > Objective, plan, or result envisioned before starting
- RESULTADO_REAL: {{RESULTADO_REAL}} > What actually occurred, in observable terms
- HORIZONTE_APLICACION: {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} > Next occasion or period where lessons will be applied (e.g. "the next sprint", "my next interview") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An activity without a review repeats with the same mistakes; reviewed well, it becomes compounded learning. The purpose is to conduct a personal after action review of {{ACTIVIDAD}}, contrasting the expected result ({{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}) against the actual result ({{RESULTADO_REAL}}) to extract lessons that will be applied at {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}}. A solid AAR unlocks better decisions next time, early detection of failed assumptions, and a habit of continuous improvement without blame. The method centers on the system and not on the person: that framing is what makes it safe to look mistakes directly in the face. Its value is not in describing what happened, but in closing the loop toward the next action.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior after action review (AAR) facilitator trained in the original US Army method (Training Circular 25-20 and the Center for Army Lessons Learned), expert at converting experiences into actionable lessons without blame or empty praise.
Deliverable: a structured personal AAR of {{ACTIVIDAD}} with actionable lessons. Steps:
1. Question 1 - What did I expect to happen: reconstruct the planned objective and plan based on {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}; name the key assumptions taken for granted at the start.
2. Question 2 - What actually happened: list the observable facts from {{RESULTADO_REAL}}, without interpretation or judgment; include figures, dates, or verifiable evidence where it exists.
3. Question 3 - Why were there differences: contrast expected against actual, separate causes under own control from external factors, and isolate the root cause through a brief why-chain, not the symptom; flag which assumption from step 1 failed.
4. Question 4 - What do I learn and do differently: explicitly distinguish what must be SUSTAINED (worked and is worth replicating) from what must be CHANGED, anchored to {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}}.
5. Close with a table of 2 to 4 lessons learned, columns: lesson in one sentence | concrete action | trigger or exact moment at {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} | observable signal that it was applied.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{ACTIVIDAD}}, {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, {{RESULTADO_REAL}}, and {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}}; if the expected-actual contrast is unclear or any essential data point is missing, ask for it, do not assume. If {{HORIZONTE_APLICACION}} is empty, anchor lessons to "the next comparable occasion".
Phase 2 Plan: present the order of the four questions and how you will separate facts from interpretations before drafting.
Phase 3 Execute: answer the four questions in order, keeping focus on the system and not on the person, and mark with [SUPUESTO] any data not confirmed by the user.
Edge cases: (a) if expected and actual coincide, still extract what practice to sustain and what almost failed; (b) if the result was good by chance rather than by plan, flag that fragility as a lesson; (c) if many causes emerge, prioritize the two or three with the highest leverage rather than listing them all; (d) if {{ADJUNTOS}} provides evidence, cite it; if it contradicts the account, flag the discrepancy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The four canonical questions are answered in order: expected, actual, why the difference, what to change.
- [ ] Question 1 names the key assumptions held going into the activity.
- [ ] Question 2 contains only observable facts, without judgment or interpretation.
- [ ] Question 3 separates causes under own control from external factors, isolates root cause (not symptom), and flags which assumption failed.
- [ ] What must be sustained is explicitly distinguished from what must be changed.
- [ ] The final table has 2 to 4 lessons, each with action, trigger at the horizon, and observable signal of application.
- [ ] Edge cases considered where applicable (success by chance, expected equals actual, excess of causes, evidence in attachments).
- [ ] Framing centered on the system and not on the person; professional tone in neutral language, no emojis; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO].
Expected deliverable: a personal AAR ready to save, with the four questions answered and a table of 2 to 4 actionable lessons learned anchored to the next occasion.
spec-personal_kpi_personales:
[inputs]
- METAS_Y_HORIZONTE: {{METAS_Y_HORIZONTE}} > Goals to monitor and the time horizon for each (e.g. quarter, semester, year)
- HABITOS_ACTUALES: {{HABITOS_ACTUALES}} > Habits or behaviors you already practice or want to install, related to those goals
- CAPACIDAD_DE_REGISTRO: {{CAPACIDAD_DE_REGISTRO}} > How often and in what medium you can record data without friction (app, spreadsheet, planner)
- DEFINICION_DE_EXITO: {{DEFINICION_DE_EXITO}} > What counts as real progress on each goal (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to monitor my habits and goals with indicators that truly anticipate progress, not just numbers that rise without changing my behavior. The objective is a personal dashboard that separates leading metrics (actions under my daily control that predict the outcome) from lagging metrics (the effect that confirms achievement). A good dashboard lets me correct course in time, maintain focus on a few high-leverage behaviors, and review on a cadence rather than improvising. Risk to avoid: overloaded dashboards, metrics with no causal link to the goal, and vanity numbers that create a false sense of progress.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal performance coach with a background in indicator design and behavioral science (habits, routine formation, behavioral measurement).
Deliver a personal indicator system. Steps:
1. Reframe each goal from {{METAS_Y_HORIZONTE}} into an observable outcome with a cutoff date. If a goal arrives vague or without a horizon, propose a measurable version and mark it as an assumption to confirm.
2. For each goal, propose 1 to 2 outcome metrics (lagging) with unit, data source, measurement frequency, and estimated typical lag between action and effect.
3. Propose 2 to 3 leading metrics under direct control, anchored to {{HABITOS_ACTUALES}}, with an operational definition (what counts and what does not), a weekly target, and a tracking method consistent with {{CAPACIDAD_DE_REGISTRO}}.
4. Verify the causal link: each leading metric must plausibly predict its outcome. If the link is weak or absent, discard or replace it and explain why.
5. Assign each metric a current baseline, a target, and a minimum acceptable threshold; calibrate with {{DEFINICION_DE_EXITO}}. If the baseline is missing, leave a marker to measure it in the first week.
6. Define a review cadence (light daily, weekly adjustment, monthly balance) and an explicit decision rule for the case where the leading metric is met but the outcome does not move (review causal link, adjust leading target, or change the lever).
7. Mark and discard vanity metrics (they rise without changing behavior or bringing the goal closer) and reduce to a minimum actionable set.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm goals, horizon, habits, and tracking capacity; flag gaps and assumptions before moving on.
Phase 2 Leading-lag map: per goal, trace the chain daily behavior > leading metric > lagging metric, and discard links without a causal connection.
Phase 3 Operational definition: set unit, baseline, target, threshold, source, and frequency for each metric; binary habits are measured as a weekly completion rate.
Phase 4 Cadence and rules: build the three-level review schedule and adjustment rules, including the rule for the leading-met-but-outcome-stalled case.
Phase 5 Refinement: eliminate vanity metrics and reduce to a minimum actionable set (guideline: maximum 3 leading and 2 lagging metrics per goal).
Edge cases: conflicting goals (prioritize and flag the trade-off); outcomes with long lag (rely more heavily on leading metrics); very limited tracking capacity (favor automatic or binary tracking).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each goal has an observable outcome with a cutoff date; vague goals were reframed and marked as assumptions.
- [ ] Each goal separates outcome metrics (lagging) and leading metrics without confusing them.
- [ ] Each leading metric is under direct control, has an operational definition (what counts and what does not), a weekly target, a tracking method, and an explicit causal link to its outcome.
- [ ] Every metric has a baseline (or a marker to measure it), a target, and a minimum acceptable threshold.
- [ ] There is a daily, weekly, and monthly review cadence with a decision rule for the leading-met-but-outcome-stalled case.
- [ ] Vanity metrics were identified and discarded, and applicable edge cases were covered.
- [ ] The final set is minimal and actionable, within the guideline ceiling of indicators per goal.
Expected deliverable: a table per goal (observable outcome, leading and lagging metrics with unit/baseline/target/threshold/source/frequency) plus a review schedule with adjustment rules, in neutral and professional English.
spec-personal_revision_trimestral:
[inputs]
- VISION_MEDIANO_PLAZO: {{VISION_MEDIANO_PLAZO}} > What you want to have achieved or who you want to have become by the close of the quarter; the emotional engine of the plan
- METAS_CANDIDATAS: {{METAS_CANDIDATAS}} > List of objectives you are considering for these 12 weeks; the method recommends keeping 1 to 3
- HORAS_SEMANALES: {{HORAS_SEMANALES}} > Real weekly dedication capacity, to size tactics without overloading; distinguish net available hours, not gross
- FECHA_INICIO: {{FECHA_INICIO}} > Monday on which the 12 weeks begin; defines week 1 through week 12 and the closing week 13
- UMBRAL_EJECUCION: {{UMBRAL_EJECUCION}} > Minimum percentage of weekly tactics executed that you consider healthy execution (optional; default 85%)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You plan your quarter as if it were a full year, following The 12 Week Year by Brian Moran and Michael Lennington. The purpose: compress the twelve-month horizon to twelve weeks so that every week counts, focus does not drift, and execution is measurable. The method's premise is that most people fail not from a lack of plan but from a lack of consistent execution; the short cycle creates productive urgency without anxious urgency. At the close of this session you will have a quarterly plan that can be copied directly to your calendar: a concrete vision, one to three goals with indicators, weekly tactics on a schedule, and a score tracker that converts intention into a verifiable rhythm. This unlocks short weekly reviews and a personal StrategIA that sustains itself without relying on willpower.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity and personal execution coach, certified in The 12 Week Year system, with experience helping professionals move from vague annual plans to 12-week cycles with high execution rates.

Deliverable: complete 12 Week Year quarterly plan, ready for the calendar. Steps:
1. Refine VISION_MEDIANO_PLAZO into a concrete 12-week vision that is measurable at close and emotionally motivating. Explicitly connect the 12-week outcome with the underlying aspiration, so the plan has fuel when motivation dips.
2. Distill from METAS_CANDIDATAS between 1 and 3 quarterly goals; discard or shelve the excess and explain why (criteria: impact on the vision, feasibility within 12 weeks, independence between goals). Each goal with its outcome indicator and quantified target value.
3. Break each goal into actionable weekly tactics; assign each tactic a day or a frequency, sized against HORAS_SEMANALES. Sum the committed hours and verify they do not exceed declared capacity; if they do, cut or reschedule and say so.
4. Separate activity indicators (lead, what you control and execute) from outcome indicators (lag, what you measure at the end). Clarify that the weekly score is calculated on the leads, because they are the only ones actionable week by week.
5. Build a 12-week score tracker (week 1 to 12) to record the percentage of tactics executed against UMBRAL_EJECUCION, with a note on how to interpret falling below the threshold for one week versus a sustained downward trend.
6. Propose the format of a weekly 15-to-20-minute self-accountability meeting: review score, diagnose the root cause of what was not executed, commit to the following week's tactics.
7. Add a week 13 plan: close the cycle (lessons, what worked, what did not) and prepare for the start of the next one. Include early warning signals of a miscalibrated goal (lag stalled despite high lead, or chronically low lead) and how to adjust without abandoning the cycle, plus a recovery protocol for a failed week that avoids the all-or-nothing spiral.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Vision: translate aspiration into a verifiable outcome at 12 weeks.
Phase 2 - Focus: apply the 1-to-3-goal rule; protect the plan from excess ambition and justify the cuts.
Phase 3 - Breakdown: convert each goal into concrete, scheduled weekly tactics within real capacity.
Phase 4 - Measurement: define lead vs lag and build the score tracker on the leads.
Phase 5 - Rhythm: design the weekly self-accountability meeting and the week 13 close.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it; do not fill with undeclared assumptions, and declare any assumptions you make at the close.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The vision is concrete, measurable at the close of 12 weeks, and explicitly connects with the declared aspiration.
- [ ] There are between 1 and 3 goals; if there were more candidates, the cut was justified with criteria (impact, feasibility, independence).
- [ ] Each goal has an outcome indicator (lag) with a quantified target value.
